definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wort fängt mit A an.

definitions.note: Plural of "Aal".

definitions.note: Often used for stopping an activity or process (e.g., a project, course, procedure).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the cancellation of the course, she got her money back.

definitions.note: Used for tearing down a building or structure.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The demolition of the old house begins tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, the evenings are long.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the evenings, I often read a book.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She goes to an evening school because she works during the day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Abendsonne sieht das Meer golden aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the evening sun, the sea looks golden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir erleben heute ein großes Abenteuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are having a big adventure today.

definitions.note: Often used for scheduled departures (trains/buses/planes) or leaving by car; also used for the start of a ski run ("Abfahrt").

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte wirf den Abfall in den Mülleimer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please throw the trash in the trash can.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the termination, she received severance pay.

definitions.note: Often used for flights/travel (e.g., at the airport).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The departure is at 2:30 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Abfluss in der Küche ist verstopft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen drain is clogged.

definitions.note: Often used for liquids or money (e.g., cash outflow).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The outflow of the water is regulated by a valve.

definitions.note: Often used for an elected representative in a parliament (e.g., the Bundestag).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m talking with a member of parliament.

definitions.note: Usually refers to an elected member of a parliament (e.g., the Bundestag); feminine: Abgeordnete.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Abgeordneter hält eine Rede im Parlament.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The member of parliament is giving a speech in parliament.

definitions.note: Often used both literally (a deep chasm) and figuratively (a hopeless or dangerous situation).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stood at the edge of the abyss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Abhang wachsen viele Bäume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many trees grow on the hillside.

definitions.native: (German) high school diploma, university entrance qualification

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got her Abitur last year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today's schedule is different than usual.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche Ruhe, ohne Ablenkung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need quiet, without distraction.

definitions.note: Often used for changing personnel or shifts, or for replacing something/someone with another.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The relief shift arrives at 6 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Abreise ist für morgen früh geplant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our departure is planned for tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often used for canceling an appointment/event or saying no to an invitation/application.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heel of my shoe is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Abschied fiel mir schwer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got her degree at the university.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hohe Strafen sollen zur Abschreckung dienen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: High penalties are meant to serve as a deterrent.

definitions.note: Often used for shooting down an aircraft or for a hunter’s kill.

definitions.note: Plural of „Absicht“.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please keep your distance.

definitions.note: Often used for accidents (e.g., a plane crash) or when a computer/program crashes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Absätze meiner Schuhe sind zu hoch.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking through the old town in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Also spelled „Aluminium“ in English (especially British English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Dose ist aus Aluminium.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The can is made of aluminum.

definitions.note: Plural of "Amateur".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dem Turnier spielen auch viele Amateure mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many amateurs are also taking part in the tournament.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat große Ambitionen und möchte Karriere machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has big ambitions and wants to have a career.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da läuft eine Ameise über den Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An ant is crawling across the floor.

definitions.note: plural of „Ameise“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Garten sind viele Ameisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many ants in the garden.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a man from the United States; the feminine form is "Amerikanerin".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist Amerikaner und wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an American and lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: female form of „Amerikaner“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist Amerikanerin und lebt jetzt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an American woman and now lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: female form; refers to a woman from the United States
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist Amerikanerin und lebt jetzt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an American woman and now lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: dative plural form of "Amerikaner"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche oft mit Amerikanern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often talk with Americans.

definitions.note: informal; can sound dismissive or mildly derogatory depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Amis feiern Thanksgiving im November.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many Americans celebrate Thanksgiving in November.

definitions.note: A woman paid to breastfeed and care for someone else’s baby (historical/old-fashioned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher hatte die Familie eine Amme für das Baby.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, the family had a wet nurse for the baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: An der Ampel musst du warten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to wait at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Usually refers to an official/public authority or administrative office; also used in set phrases like „im Amt sein“ (to be in office).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss morgen zum Amt, um meinen Ausweis zu verlängern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go to the government office tomorrow to renew my ID.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutsch ist eine Amtssprache in Österreich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: German is an official language in Austria.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt ein Amulett als Glücksbringer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wears an amulet as a good-luck charm.

definitions.note: Usually refers to someone who cannot read and write at all.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist Analphabet und kann keine Briefe lesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is illiterate and can’t read any letters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Analyse zeigt, dass die Preise steigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The analysis shows that prices are rising.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe eine Ananas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm buying a pineapple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Krieg herrschte im Land Anarchie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the war, anarchy reigned in the country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Anblick der Berge ist wunderschön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sight of the mountains is beautiful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein kleines Andenken aus Berlin mitgebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought a small memento from Berlin.

definitions.note: Used as a noun meaning “other people/things.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andere haben das schon ausprobiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Others have already tried that.

definitions.note: Used as a noun meaning “other people” (from the nominalized adjective “andere”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe mit den Anderen nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going home with the others.

definitions.note: Often used after words like „etwas“ (something): „etwas Anderes“ = „something else“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte etwas Anderes bestellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to order something else.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er machte ein paar Andeutungen, aber sagte nichts direkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a few hints, but didn’t say anything directly.

definitions.note: Often used for appreciation/praise for someone’s achievements or work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Für seine Arbeit bekam er viel Anerkennung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He received a lot of recognition for his work.

definitions.note: Often used for medical emergencies (e.g., an epileptic seizure) or sudden physical symptoms (e.g., coughing fit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hatte einen epileptischen Anfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had an epileptic seizure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Anfang war alles schwierig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the beginning, everything was difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Pilot meldete den Anflug auf Frankfurt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pilot reported the approach to Frankfurt.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like „ein Anflug von …“ (e.g., „ein Anflug von Angst“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In seiner Stimme lag ein Anflug von Ärger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a hint of anger in his voice.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., customer service, business, or email).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Anfrage per E-Mail geschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent an inquiry by email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch ein Anfänger in Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still a beginner in German.

definitions.note: Often used for the leader of a group (e.g., a gang, rebels, protesters).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Anführer der Gruppe festgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the leader of the group.

definitions.note: Often used for factual info you provide (e.g., on a form or in an application).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte überprüfen Sie Ihre Angaben im Formular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please check your details in the form.

definitions.note: Informal and usually negative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein Angeber und redet ständig über sein neues Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a show-off and is constantly talking about his new car.

definitions.note: Often used for special prices or promotions in shops/online.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Angebot gilt nur bis Samstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This offer is only valid until Saturday.

definitions.note: Plural of „Angebot“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Supermarkt gibt es diese Woche viele Angebote.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many offers this week at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., hospital, police) for a person’s close family/next of kin.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat die Angehörigen informiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police informed the relatives.

definitions.note: used in a legal/court context; can refer to a female defendant or (as a plural form) multiple defendants
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Angeklagte sagt vor Gericht nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The defendant doesn’t say anything in court.

definitions.note: female defendant (in court); for a male defendant: der Angeklagte
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Angeklagte bestreitet die Vorwürfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The defendant denies the accusations.

definitions.note: court/legal context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Richter befragten die Angeklagten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judges questioned the defendants.

definitions.note: Not the same as English “angel” (in German, that’s “Engel”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Angel im Auto vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my fishing rod in the car.

definitions.note: Often used for practical or official matters (e.g., business, legal, administrative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine private Angelegenheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a private matter.

definitions.note: Plural of "Angelegenheit"; often used for business or personal matters.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch ein paar Angelegenheiten erledigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to take care of a few matters.

definitions.note: Used as a noun meaning the activity of fishing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Angeln macht mir Spaß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fishing is fun for me.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/literary; often used in fixed phrases (e.g., „im Angesicht von“ = „in the face of“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Angesicht der Gefahr blieb sie ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the face of danger, she stayed calm.

definitions.note: Can also mean a single female employee (die Angestellte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Angestellten bekommen heute ihren Lohn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employees get their pay today.

definitions.note: Plural form (often used after prepositions like „mit“, „von“, „bei“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche später mit den Angestellten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll speak with the employees later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mir eine gute Angewohnheit anzutrainieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to develop a good habit.

definitions.note: plural of „Angewohnheit“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gute Angewohnheiten helfen dir beim Lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good habits help you when you’re learning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Angreifer wurde von der Polizei festgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attacker was arrested by the police.

definitions.note: In sports (especially soccer/football).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unser Angreifer hat zwei Tore geschossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our forward scored two goals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Angriff begann in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attack began during the night.

definitions.note: Plural of „Angriff“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Angriffe begannen in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attacks began during the night.

definitions.note: Often used for a strong, anxious fear; in psychology you may also see it translated as “anxiety.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Angst vor Spinnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid of spiders.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used teasingly or as an insult
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm schon, sei kein Angsthase!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, don’t be a scaredy-cat!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Anhalter steht am Straßenrand und wartet auf ein Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A hitchhiker is standing by the side of the road and waiting for a car.

definitions.note: plural of „Anhaltspunkt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat noch keine Anhaltspunkte für ein Verbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police still have no clues that a crime was committed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fahren mit einem Anhänger zum Wertstoffhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re driving to the recycling center with a trailer.

definitions.note: Jewelry that hangs from a necklace or bracelet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt einen Anhänger aus Silber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s wearing a silver pendant.

definitions.note: A person who supports a team, idea, or politician.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein Anhänger dieser Mannschaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a supporter of this team.

definitions.note: Often used in legal or official contexts (e.g., a court hearing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anhörung findet morgen vor Gericht statt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hearing takes place in court tomorrow.

definitions.note: Japanese-style animated shows/films; in German it's a loanword and is treated like a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaue gern Anime.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like watching anime.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Anker liegt auf dem Meeresboden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The anchor is lying on the seabed.

definitions.note: Used in legal/criminal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Staatsanwaltschaft erhebt Anklage gegen den Verdächtigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The public prosecutor brings charges against the suspect.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „ein Anklang an …“ (a hint/echo of …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In seiner Stimme lag ein leiser Anklang von Traurigkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a faint hint of sadness in his voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ankunft des Zuges ist um 18 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train’s arrival is at 6 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ankündigung kommt morgen per E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The announcement is coming tomorrow by email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anlage in Aktien ist riskant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Investing in stocks is risky.

definitions.note: Often used for a larger site or complex (e.g., sports facility, industrial plant).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neue Anlage wird nächstes Jahr eröffnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new facility will open next year.

definitions.note: Common in emails and documents (e.g., "im Anhang" / "in der Anlage").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schicke dir den Vertrag in der Anlage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending you the contract as an attachment.

definitions.note: Often used for a special occasion (e.g., a celebration) or as a reason/motive for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein guter Anlass, um zu feiern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a good occasion to celebrate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zu diesem Anlaß treffen wir uns um 18 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For this occasion, we’re meeting at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Often used for written instructions, e.g. for using or assembling something (like an instruction manual).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Anleitung für den Drucker verloren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost the instructions for the printer.

definitions.note: Often used for something you want to ask for or discuss (e.g., at an office or in customer service).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein Anliegen und brauche bitte Ihre Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a concern and I need your help, please.

definitions.note: Often used for officially registering (e.g., for an event, a course, or at an office).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anmeldung für den Kurs ist bis Freitag möglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Registration for the course is possible until Friday.

definitions.note: Plural of „Anmerkung“. Often used for brief remarks or additional information (e.g., in a document).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte lies die Anmerkungen am Ende des Dokuments.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please read the notes at the end of the document.

definitions.note: Often used for a refined, gentle kind of beauty in someone’s appearance or movement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie bewegte sich mit Anmut über die Bühne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moved across the stage with grace.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Annahme, dass es heute regnet, war falsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The assumption that it would rain today was wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bekomme einen Anruf von meiner Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting a call from my mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche dir eine Nachricht auf den Anrufbeantworter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving you a message on the answering machine.

definitions.note: plural of „Anruf“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute drei Anrufe bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got three calls today.

definitions.note: usually refers to someone calling on the phone
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Anrufer hat einfach aufgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The caller just hung up.

definitions.note: Often used for official/public announcements (e.g., on trains, at airports) or a clear statement of what will happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ansage im Zug war kaum zu verstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The announcement on the train was hard to understand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anschaffung eines neuen Laptops war teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The purchase of a new laptop was expensive.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „den Anschein haben/erwecken“ (= to give the impression).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hatte den Anschein, dass er krank war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It gave the impression that he was ill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Anschlag war die Innenstadt gesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the attack, the city center was closed off.

definitions.note: Often used in compounds like „Aushang/Anschlag am Schwarzen Brett“ for an official notice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Eingang hängt ein Anschlag mit den neuen Öffnungszeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the entrance there is a notice with the new opening hours.

definitions.note: Often used for connections like an electrical/Internet hookup, a phone line, or a train/bus connection.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gibt es hier einen Anschluss für mein Handy-Ladegerät?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is there a connection/plug here for my phone charger?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Kurs habe ich den Anschluss an die Gruppe schnell gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the course, I quickly found my way into the group.

definitions.note: Used for a mailing address (street, city, etc.), not for an email address.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte geben Sie Ihre Anschrift an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please provide your address.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anschuldigung war völlig unbegründet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accusation was completely unfounded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anschuldigungen gegen ihn waren falsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accusations against him were false.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie genießt in der Stadt hohes Ansehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She enjoys high prestige in the city.

definitions.note: Often used for viewpoints/opinions, or for how something is displayed (e.g., in an app or on a screen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meiner Ansicht nach ist das eine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my view, that's a good idea.

definitions.note: Plural of „Ansicht“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben unterschiedliche Ansichten zu diesem Thema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have different views on this topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schicke dir eine Ansichtskarte aus Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending you a postcard from Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor der Prüfung spüre ich große Anspannung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before the exam, I feel a lot of tension.

definitions.note: Often used for indirect references (e.g., in conversation or writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine Anspielung auf seinen letzten Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an allusion to his last mistake.

definitions.note: Often used for a formal speech (e.g., at an event) or the act of addressing someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister hielt eine kurze Ansprache.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor gave a short speech.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or legal contexts (e.g., Anspruch auf = entitlement to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Anspruch auf Urlaubstage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am entitled to vacation days.

definitions.note: Often used for things you believe you are entitled to (e.g., legal or financial claims) or for high expectations/requirements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat Ansprüche auf eine Entschädigung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has claims to compensation.

definitions.note: Often used for places like prisons, psychiatric hospitals, or care facilities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er arbeitet in einer staatlichen Anstalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works in a state institution.

definitions.note: Plural of „Anstalt“; often used for official institutions (e.g., prisons, hospitals, public agencies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dieser Stadt gibt es mehrere staatliche Anstalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are several state institutions.

definitions.note: Often used for polite, socially appropriate behavior (e.g., good manners).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat keinen Anstand und unterbricht ständig andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has no decency and constantly interrupts others.

definitions.note: often means a (paid) position with an employer
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine neue Anstellung bei einer Firma in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a new job at a company in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es kostet mich viel Anstrengung, jeden Tag Deutsch zu lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It takes me a lot of effort to learn German every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: All unsere Anstrengungen waren umsonst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All our efforts were in vain.

definitions.note: Often used for a share/percentage of a whole; also used for a share in a company (e.g., business shares).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Anteil an der Miete ist 400 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My share of the rent is 400 euros.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like „mein herzliches Beileid und meine Anteilnahme“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte Ihnen meine aufrichtige Anteilnahme aussprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to express my sincere sympathy to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Antenne ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The antenna is broken.

definitions.note: Plural form; singular is „das Antibiotikum“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt hat mir Antibiotika verschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed antibiotics for me.

definitions.note: A shop that sells used (often older or rare) books.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe gern alte Bücher im Antiquariat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like buying old books at the secondhand bookshop.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In diesem Laden gibt es viele Antiquitäten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many antiques in this shop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen am Samstag in ein Antiquitätengeschäft und schauen uns alte Möbel an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Saturday we’re going to an antique shop and looking at old furniture.

definitions.note: Often used in official or formal contexts (e.g., filing an application or making a formal request).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Antrag online ausgefüllt und abgeschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filled out the application online and sent it off.

definitions.note: Often used for official or administrative applications (e.g., permits, benefits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte füllen Sie das Antragsformular vollständig aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fill out the application form completely.

definitions.note: Often used for mechanical drive (e.g., a motor or drivetrain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der elektrische Antrieb ist sehr leise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The electric drive is very quiet.

definitions.note: Used for an inner reason or impulse to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was ist dein Antrieb, so hart zu arbeiten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your motivation for working so hard?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe noch keine Antwort bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still haven't gotten an answer.

definitions.note: Plural of „Antwort“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe noch keine Antworten auf meine Fragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still don’t have any answers to my questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Anwalt hilft mir bei dem Vertrag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My lawyer helps me with the contract.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte folgen Sie den Anweisungen des Lehrers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please follow the teacher’s instructions.

definitions.note: Plural of „Anweisung“.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The greatest happiness is time with the family.

definitions.note: Genitive singular of „Glück“; often used to mean “of luck / of happiness.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trotz des Glücks hatte er Angst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the luck, he was afraid.

definitions.note: Something (or sometimes a person) believed to bring good luck.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hufeisen-Anhänger ist mein Glücksbringer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The horseshoe pendant is my lucky charm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dass wir noch Tickets bekommen haben, war ein echter Glücksfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That we still managed to get tickets was a real stroke of luck.

definitions.note: Informal; often used as a friendly (sometimes slightly teasing) remark.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist echt ein Glückspilz!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re really a lucky person!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glücksspiel kann süchtig machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gambling can be addictive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist mein Glückstag!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is my lucky day!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie glaubt, dass 7 ihre Glückszahl ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believes that 7 is her lucky number.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: „Glückwünsche“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Herzlichen Glückwunsch zum Geburtstag!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Happy birthday! (Congratulations on your birthday!)

definitions.note: Plural form (singular: Glückwunsch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Herzlichen Glückwünsche zum Geburtstag!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Congratulations on your birthday!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Glühbirne im Flur wechseln?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please change the light bulb in the hallway?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe zwei Glühbirnen gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two light bulbs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer sehen wir abends Glühwürmchen im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer we see fireflies in the garden in the evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Richter zeigte Gnade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge showed mercy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ring ist aus Gold.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ring is made of gold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Goldfisch schwimmt den ganzen Tag im Aquarium.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My goldfish swims in the aquarium all day.

definitions.note: Plural of "Goldfisch".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Aquarium schwimmen drei Goldfische.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Three goldfish are swimming in the aquarium.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat bei den Olympischen Spielen eine Goldmedaille gewonnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She won a gold medal at the Olympic Games.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Museum liegen alte Goldmünzen in einer Vitrine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the museum, old gold coins are in a display case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Wochenende spiele ich Golf mit Freunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the weekend I play golf with friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Golfball im hohen Gras verloren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost my golf ball in the tall grass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Golfplatz ist heute geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The golf course is closed today.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the traditional Venetian boat.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen eine Fahrt mit der Gondola durch Venedig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking a ride on a gondola through Venice.

definitions.note: Colloquial; also used figuratively for an unpleasant, dirty environment (e.g., “aus der Gosse”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball liegt in der Gosse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball is lying in the gutter.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the God of a monotheistic religion; in the plural (Götter) it can mean 'gods'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glaubst du an Gott?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you believe in God?

definitions.note: Genitive singular of „Gott“ (used to show possession).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is God's will.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a Christian religious service (often in a church).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go to church on Sunday for the service.

definitions.note: Often used in a critical/negative way, especially for religious extremists.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In den Nachrichten war von einem Gotteskrieger die Rede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the news, there was talk of a holy warrior.

definitions.note: often used for the political head of a state/region; also used for the head of a central bank
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gouverneur hält heute eine Rede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The governor is giving a speech today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dem Friedhof steht ein frisches Grab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a fresh grave in the cemetery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Neben der Straße ist ein tiefer Graben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a deep ditch next to the road.

definitions.note: Often used for temperature (degrees) and for angles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute sind es 30 Grad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is 30 degrees.

definitions.note: A noble title; the female equivalent is usually "Gräfin".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Graf wohnt in einem alten Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The count lives in an old castle.

definitions.note: Plural of „Graf“ (a noble title).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Grafen wohnen in einem alten Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The counts live in an old castle.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed phrase „der Heilige Gral“; also used figuratively for a highly sought-after goal.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For many researchers, curing this disease is the Holy Grail.

definitions.note: unit of weight/mass; abbreviation: g

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need 200 grams of flour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch Grammatik lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to study grammar.

definitions.note: Old-fashioned; most commonly used for early record players, especially with a horn.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Museum steht ein altes Grammophon mit großem Trichter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an old gramophone with a big horn in the museum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten fanden eine Granate im Feld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers found a grenade in the field.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten warfen Granaten in den Graben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers threw grenades into the trench.

definitions.note: English loanword; in German, the more common word is "Opa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Grandpa wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa lives in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer ist das Gras ganz grün.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, the grass is completely green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Fluss steht ein Graureiher und wartet auf einen Fisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A grey heron is standing by the river and waiting for a fish.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cruelty in the war shocks many people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durch die Gravitation fallen die Äpfel vom Baum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of gravity, the apples fall from the tree.

definitions.note: Often used for country borders, but also for abstract limits (e.g., personal limits, speed limits).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The border between Germany and France is open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Grenzen zwischen den beiden Ländern sind geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The borders between the two countries are closed.

definitions.note: plural noun; singular: der Grieche

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Griechen wohnen in Griechenland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Greeks live in Greece.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne Griechisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Greek.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children make grimaces in front of the mirror.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, he calls the tourist a gringo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schreiben Sie Ihren Namen in Großbuchstaben.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Großeltern wohnen in der Nähe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents live nearby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Großmutter wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother lives in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Großonkel wohnt in Hamburg.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Berlin ist eine Großstadt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: Plural of „Grundlage“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir lernen die Grundlagen der deutschen Grammatik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are learning the basics of German grammar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen zuerst die Grundregeln erklären.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What sizes do you have?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ein Grübchen auf der linken Wange.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the traffic light, green is lit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grün ist meine Lieblingsfarbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Green is my favorite color.

definitions.note: plural of „Grund“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt viele Gründe dafür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many reasons for that.

definitions.note: dative plural of "Grund"; often used in phrases like "aus ... Gründen" (for ... reasons)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus Sicherheitsgründen ist das Gebäude geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For safety reasons, the building is closed.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like eating gummy bears.

definitions.native: in favor of, for the benefit of

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying cucumbers for the salad.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fasten your seat belt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The good thing about it is that it’s free.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Schluss gab sie ihm noch einen Gutenachtkuss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end she gave him a goodnight kiss.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey, buddy, how’s it going?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have something good for you.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have a 20-euro balance in my account.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister goes to an academic high school.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gardener works in the park every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we have many guests at home.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a guest room for visitors.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Greek mythology, there are many gods.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a belt for these pants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er half ihr aus reiner Güte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helped her out of pure kindness.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you spell the word with H?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need my hairbrush.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my hair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In diesem Zimmer stehen zwei Lampen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two lamps in this room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor der Präsentation hatte ich Lampenfieber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before the presentation, I had stage fright.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland ist ein Land in Europa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany is a country in Europe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Wochenende fahren wir aufs Land.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the weekend we’re going to the countryside.

definitions.note: Dative singular of "Land"; often used in fixed or more formal/older phrases like "im Lande".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Lande herrscht Frieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is peace in the country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug landet auf der Landebahn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The airplane lands on the runway.

definitions.note: Genitive singular form of "Land" (used after words like "des" or to show possession).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Hauptstadt des Landes ist Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The capital of the country is Berlin.

definitions.note: Often refers to a house in the countryside used as a vacation home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verbringen den Sommer in einem Landhaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spend the summer in a country house.

definitions.note: usually means a geographic map (not a city transit map)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir die Landkarte von Deutschland zeigen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me the map of Germany?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen träumen vom Landleben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people dream of country life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Landschaft hier ist wunderschön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The landscape here is beautiful.

definitions.note: plural of „Landschaft“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland hat viele schöne Landschaften.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany has many beautiful landscapes.

definitions.note: Often used for aircraft (and also for boats/spacecraft, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Landung war pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The landing was on time.

definitions.note: Used for traveling or transporting goods by land (as opposed to by sea or air).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir liefern die Ware auf dem Landweg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We deliver the goods by land.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Landwirt arbeitet jeden Tag auf dem Feld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farmer works in the field every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Landwirtschaft ist in dieser Region sehr wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Agriculture is very important in this region.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed phrase „seit Langem“ (= for a long time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne ihn seit Langem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve known him for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist langweilig, ich habe Langeweile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm bored; I'm feeling boredom.

definitions.note: Colloquial; can be mildly insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht mit ihm ausgehen – er ist ein totaler Langweiler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to go out with him—he’s totally boring.

definitions.note: Often used for a (cleaning) cloth or rag.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte den Lappen geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please give me the rag (cloth)?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme meinen Laptop mit zur Uni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking my laptop with me to the university.

definitions.note: In German, "Lasagne" usually refers to the dish (often treated like a singular), even though it looks plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse gern Lasagne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like eating lasagna.

definitions.note: Often used for something heavy to carry or a figurative burden.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Last ist zu schwer für mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The load is too heavy for me.

definitions.note: Common in Austria and Switzerland; in Germany more often: „Lastwagen“ (or „LKW“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Laster liefert morgens die Waren an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A truck delivers the goods in the morning.

definitions.note: Used for harmful habits or moral “vices”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zigaretten sind ein Laster, das schwer aufzuhören ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cigarettes are a vice that is hard to quit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lastwagen liefert heute frisches Gemüse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is delivering fresh vegetables today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lastwagenfahrer liefert heute Gemüse in die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck driver is delivering vegetables to the city today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe in der Schule Latein gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned Latin in school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Laterne vor dem Haus ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street lamp in front of the house is broken.

definitions.note: Plural of "Laterne".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abends gehen die Laternen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the evening, the streetlights turn on.

definitions.note: Most often used for wooden slats/boards; in everyday speech it can also mean a (coffee) latte, but that’s a different word/meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Latte am Zaun ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The slat on the fence is broken.

definitions.note: Usually refers to leaves collectively (especially in autumn), not a single leaf (Blatt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Herbst liegt viel Laub auf den Wegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn, there are a lot of leaves on the paths.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Lauf war ich sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run, I was very tired.

definitions.note: Used as a noun for the activity (often with „das“ or in phrases like „beim Laufen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beim Laufen höre ich Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listen to music while running.

definitions.note: Often used as an activity or sport (e.g., jogging).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe dreimal pro Woche zum Laufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go running three times a week.

definitions.note: informal; often used in the phrase „jemandem den Laufpass geben“ (= to fire someone / to dump someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Streit bekam er den Laufpass.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the argument, he got the sack.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute bin ich guter Laune.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m in a good mood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat oft schlechte Launen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often has bad moods.

definitions.note: As a noun, it means a sound/noise (often a short or noticeable one). Not the same as the adjective/preposition „laut“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen seltsamen Laut gehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a strange sound.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen neuen Lautsprecher für mein Handy gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new speaker for my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Lautstärke leiser machen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn the volume down?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lava fließt den Vulkan hinunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lava flows down the volcano.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem starken Schneefall ging eine Lawine ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the heavy snowfall, an avalanche came down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Leben ist manchmal kompliziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Life is sometimes complicated.

definitions.note: Used as a nominalized adjective (from „lebend“), referring to living people as a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir helfen den Lebenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We help the living.

definitions.note: Genitive singular of „das Leben“; also used as a linking form in many compounds (e.g., „Lebensmittel“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der Sinn des Lebens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the meaning of life.

definitions.note: Often used in serious contexts like medical care, dying, or palliative care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Lebensende möchten viele Menschen nicht allein sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of life, many people don’t want to be alone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei diesem Unfall bestand Lebensgefahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was danger to life in this accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat ein Buch über seine Lebensgeschichte geschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wrote a book about his life story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dieser Stadt sind die Lebenshaltungskosten sehr hoch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city, the cost of living is very high.

definitions.note: Used for a job application; also commonly said as „CV“ in German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schicke Ihnen meinen Lebenslauf per E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending you my résumé by email.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural; in the singular it often refers to a specific food item or a category of food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe Lebensmittel im Supermarkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying groceries at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Dative plural of „Lebensmittel“; often used after prepositions like „in/bei/mit“ and after „von“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe Obst und Gemüse in einem Laden mit frischen Lebensmitteln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy fruit and vegetables in a store with fresh groceries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Lebensmittelvergiftung und mir ist schlecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have food poisoning and I feel sick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein gesunder Lebensstil ist wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A healthy lifestyle is important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verdient genug für seinen Lebensunterhalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He earns enough to cover his living expenses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Lebensversicherung abgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took out a life insurance policy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eine gesunde Lebensweise ist wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A healthy lifestyle is important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit Stunden gab es kein Lebenszeichen von ihm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There had been no sign of life from him for hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Lebensziel ist es, einmal am Meer zu wohnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My life goal is to live by the sea one day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Leber ist ein wichtiges Organ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The liver is an important organ.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als Kind musste ich jeden Morgen einen Löffel Lebertran nehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I had to take a spoonful of cod-liver oil every morning.

definitions.note: Often used as a neutral, general term for any creature (humans, animals, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle Lebewesen brauchen Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All living beings need water.

definitions.note: Usually used for leaks of liquid, gas, or information (e.g., ein Leck im Rohr, ein Datenleck).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Leck im Rohr schnell reparieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to fix the leak in the pipe quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Jacke ist aus Leder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My jacket is made of leather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trägt eine schwarze Lederjacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is wearing a black leather jacket.

definitions.note: Often used for an empty space or an empty feeling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Umzug herrschte in der Wohnung eine seltsame Leere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the move, there was a strange emptiness in the apartment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat eine Legende über einen Drachen erzählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told a legend about a dragon.

definitions.note: In German, this can also mean the explanation of symbols in a map, chart, or diagram.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Legende der Karte sind alle Symbole erklärt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the map key (legend), all the symbols are explained.

definitions.note: Plural of „Legende“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Museum gibt es viele Legenden über die alten Könige.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the museum there are many legends about the old kings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist aus Lehm gebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is built from clay.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Lehrbuch erklärt die Grammatik ganz einfach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This textbook explains the grammar very simply.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Für den Kurs brauche ich zwei Lehrbücher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the course I need two textbooks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Lehre hat viele Menschen beeinflusst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His doctrine has influenced many people.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used for lessons learned (e.g., from experience or history).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus der Geschichte ziehen wir wichtige Lehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We draw important lessons from history.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a male teacher; the female form is "Lehrerin".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer erklärt die Grammatik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the grammar.

definitions.note: Specifically a woman teacher; the male form is "Lehrer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Lehrerin heißt Frau Müller.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our (female) teacher is called Mrs. Müller.

definitions.note: plural form of "Lehrerin"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerinnen sind heute im Lehrerzimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The female teachers are in the teachers' lounge today.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Lehrer“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir danken den Lehrern für ihre Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We thank the teachers for their help.

definitions.note: Genitive singular of „der Lehrer“ (male teacher); also used after genitive prepositions like „während“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das Buch des Lehrers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the teacher's book.

definitions.note: Often used in a more formal or literary way, especially meaning a living body (e.g., in phrases like „mit Leib und Seele“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spürte eine tiefe Wärme in seinem Leib.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a deep warmth in his body.

definitions.note: Dative singular of „Leib“, often used in set phrases like „am eigenen Leibe“ (= personally, from one’s own experience).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe am eigenen Leibe erfahren, wie schwer das ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I experienced firsthand how hard that is.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Leibwächter begleitet die Ministerin überall hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bodyguard accompanies the minister everywhere.

definitions.note: Refers to a human dead body; often used in crime/forensic contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat eine Leiche im Wald gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found a corpse in the forest.

definitions.note: Plural of "Leiche".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei fand zwei Leichen im Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found two corpses in the forest.

definitions.note: More formal than "die Leiche".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Leichnam wurde ins Krankenhaus gebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The corpse was taken to the hospital.

definitions.note: Used as a substantivized adjective (a “thing” that is light/easy), often with etwas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte heute etwas Leichtes essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to eat something light today.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like „Es tut mir leid“ (“I’m sorry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verlust hat großes Leid verursacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loss caused great sorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr Leiden dauerte viele Jahre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her suffering lasted for many years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat eine große Leidenschaft für Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a great passion for music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spielt eine Leier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She plays a lyre.

definitions.native: same old story, same old thing
definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „die gleiche Leier“ (complaining that something is always repeated).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist immer die gleiche Leier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s always the same old story.

definitions.note: Often used for a dog (Hunde-/Hundeleine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist an der Leine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is on a leash.

definitions.note: Plural of „Leine“; can also refer to ropes/lines depending on context. Not to be confused with „Leinen“ meaning “linen” (as a fabric).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nimm die Leinen mit, damit wir die Hunde anleinen können.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take the leashes with you so we can put the dogs on a leash.

definitions.note: Often used for an artist’s canvas or a film/projection screen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Maler arbeitet an einer großen Leinwand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The painter is working on a large canvas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mannschaft hat heute eine starke Leistung gezeigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team showed a strong performance today.

definitions.note: Often used in an administrative/business context (e.g., what a company provides or what’s listed on an invoice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma bietet verschiedene Leistungen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company offers various services.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine sportlichen Leistungen sind beeindruckend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His athletic achievements are impressive.

definitions.note: Masculine noun; refers to a person who is in charge.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Leiter der Abteilung ist heute nicht im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The head of the department isn't in the office today.

definitions.note: Feminine noun in this meaning (die Leiter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Leiter steht in der Garage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ladder is in the garage.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like the management of an organization, department, or facility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Leitung der Schule informiert die Eltern über die Änderungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school's management informs the parents about the changes.

definitions.note: Can refer to an electrical line/cable or a pipe (e.g., water line).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Leitung ist kaputt, deshalb gibt es kein Internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cable is broken, so there is no internet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich ein Glas Leitungswasser haben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I have a glass of tap water?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben heute eine Lektion über das Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we have a lesson about the weather.

definitions.note: Often used for books/articles considered as something to read (e.g., for school, travel, or leisure).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Lektüre ist sehr spannend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This reading material is very exciting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte halte das Lenkrad mit beiden Händen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please hold the steering wheel with both hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Leopard schläft im Schatten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leopard is sleeping in the shade.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (the act/process of learning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beim Lernen höre ich manchmal leise Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I’m studying, I sometimes listen to quiet music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Lerngruppe trifft sich jeden Mittwoch in der Bibliothek.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our study group meets every Wednesday in the library.

definitions.note: Can be offensive depending on context; often more neutral: „lesbische Frau“ or „Lesbe“ used respectfully within the community.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine Lesbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a lesbian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne meine Lesebrille kann ich die Speisekarte nicht lesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without my reading glasses, I can’t read the menu.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lesen macht mir Spaß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Reading is fun for me.

definitions.note: the act of reading
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lesen macht Spaß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Reading is fun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Leser hat das Buch in einem Tag gelesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reader read the book in one day.

definitions.note: Used as a noun for the Latvian language; also used as an adjective (not in this entry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne Lettisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning Latvian.

definitions.note: Used as a noun, usually with an article (e.g. „die Letzte“). Often refers to the last female person, but can also mean the last item/thing in a sequence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war die Letzte, die nach Hause ging.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was the last one to go home.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (capitalized) and typically appears with an article/adjective ending, e.g. „der/die/das Letzte/Letzten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Letzten im Bus gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw the last one on the bus.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning “the last one/person,” especially in rankings or results.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde Letzter im Rennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came in last in the race.

definitions.note: Used for a person/thing that comes last (often with an article: „der Letzte“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin Letzter in der Reihe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am last in the line.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Ferne sahen wir ein Leuchtfeuer an der Küste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the distance we saw a lighthouse on the coast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Leuchtturm zeigt den Schiffen nachts den Weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lighthouse shows the ships the way at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei ihm wurde Leukämie diagnostiziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was diagnosed with leukemia.

definitions.note: Plural-only noun; it usually refers to people in general or a group of people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Leute warten an der Bushaltestelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people are waiting at the bus stop.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Leute“; used after many prepositions (e.g., mit, bei, von, zu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche gern mit Leuten aus anderen Ländern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like talking with people from other countries.

definitions.note: a military rank
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Leutnant gibt den Soldaten neue Befehle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lieutenant gives the soldiers new orders.

definitions.note: Often used in German as a loanword, especially in sports, gaming, work, or education contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Spiel hat viele Level.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This game has many levels.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Bedeutung im Lexikon nachgeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked up the meaning in the dictionary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte das Licht an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn on the light.

definitions.note: plural of „das Licht“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht sehen wir die Lichter der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night we see the lights of the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo ist der Lichtschalter?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is the light switch?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Nachbar ist sehr freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is very friendly.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My (female) neighbor is very friendly.

definitions.note: plural form of "Nachbar" (neighbor)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Nachbarn sind sehr freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our neighbors are very friendly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In unserer Nachbarschaft gibt es einen kleinen Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In our neighborhood there is a small park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach kurzem Nachdenken habe ich eine Lösung gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a short period of thinking, I found a solution.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His successor will take over the leadership starting in January.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Demand for electric cars is increasing.

definitions.note: Used especially in formal contexts (e.g., customer service) for asking for information.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Nachmittag habe ich Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the afternoon I have time.

definitions.note: Used as an adverb meaning “in the afternoon” (often for habitual actions).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the afternoons, I often go for a walk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie ist Ihr Nachname?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your last name?

definitions.note: plural (die Nachnamen)
