definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please write your last names on the form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir eine Nachricht geschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you a message.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: Nachrichten = news.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du die Nachrichten gesehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you see the news?

definitions.note: Plural of „Nachricht“; often used when talking about the news in general or messages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe mir jeden Abend die Nachrichten an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watch the news every evening.

definitions.note: Plural of „Nachricht“; can mean written messages (e.g., texts or app messages).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir drei Nachrichten geschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you three messages.

definitions.note: Usually used when asking for more food (or sometimes a refill of a drink).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich bitte noch einen Nachschlag haben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could I have another helping, please?

definitions.note: Often used for getting more supplies (e.g., food, ammunition, equipment), including in military contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen dringend Nachschub.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We urgently need supplies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin zeigte Nachsicht und gab uns mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher showed leniency and gave us more time.

definitions.note: used especially in school, when a student must stay after class as a punishment
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen seiner Verspätung hat er Nachsitzen bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because he was late, he got detention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Schluss gibt es eine Nachspeise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end, there is a dessert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht ist es still.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night it is quiet.

definitions.note: Used especially for jobs like nursing, hospitals, security, etc.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has the night shift at the hospital this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Nachteil ist, dass der Bus nur einmal pro Stunde fährt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A disadvantage is that the bus only runs once an hour.

definitions.note: Plural of "Nachteil".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The disadvantages are bigger than the advantages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Nachthimmel ist heute besonders klar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The night sky is especially clear today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht hört man die Nachtigall singen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night you can hear the nightingale singing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Nachtisch gibt es Eis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dessert, there is ice cream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Buch liegt auf dem Nachttisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My book is on the nightstand.

definitions.note: Often refers specifically to the back of the neck (nape).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a needle and thread.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a nail for the picture.

definitions.note: Usually used in a more formal/official or general sense (e.g., food products).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie ist dein Name?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your name?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are your friends’ names?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like going out into nature.

definitions.note: historical/political term; often considered offensive or highly sensitive in many contexts.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the film you see Nazis marching in the streets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Morgen liegt oft Nebel über dem Fluss.

definitions.note: usually used for medicine or treatments

definitions.note: Often refers to a separate room next to the main room, especially in a restaurant or pub, used for private groups or meetings.

definitions.native: racial slur for a Black person

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word “Neger” is insulting and is avoided today.

definitions.note: Often used for a personal preference or a tendency toward something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Neigung dazu, alles aufzuschieben.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My nerves are on edge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du gehst mir auf die Nerven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Nervensystem steuert viele wichtige Funktionen im Körper.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nervous system controls many important functions in the body.

definitions.note: Informal/slang; used for a person who keeps annoying you.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein kleiner Bruder ist manchmal eine echte Nervensäge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Nerz lebt oft in der Nähe von Flüssen und Seen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Netz ist kaputt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I write in my blog every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Umzug war es für sie ein Neuanfang.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newcomer starts at the office today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir geben den Neuen am ersten Tag eine kurze Einführung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We give the newcomers a short introduction on the first day.

definitions.note: plural form of the substantivized adjective „der/die Neue“ (a new person/member in a group)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir begrüßen die Neuen in der Klasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We welcome the newcomers in the class.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two vases with flowers on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Vater arbeitet heute von zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is working from home today.

definitions.note: Often used in a patriotic or historical context; in modern everyday German, "Heimat" is more common for "home/homeland."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen fühlen sich stark mit ihrem Vaterland verbunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people feel strongly connected to their fatherland.

definitions.note: Genitive singular of „Vater“ (shows possession).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das Auto meines Vaters.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my father's car.

definitions.note: Informal, affectionate term for "Vater"; used mostly by children or within the family.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Vati holt mich heute von der Schule ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad is picking me up from school today.

definitions.note: Refers to a man; feminine form is "Veganerin".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Bruder ist Veganer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is vegan.

definitions.note: male person; the female form is "Vegetarierin"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Bruder ist Vegetarier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a vegetarian.

definitions.note: Refers specifically to a woman or girl; the masculine form is "Vegetarier".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist Vegetarierin und isst kein Fleisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a vegetarian and doesn’t eat meat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Ventil am Fahrradreifen ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The valve on the bicycle tire is broken.

definitions.note: Usually refers to an electric fan for circulating air.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer läuft der Ventilator die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, the fan runs all night.

definitions.note: Usually means an arranged meeting with someone (often socially).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe morgen eine Verabredung mit einer Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an appointment tomorrow with a friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sitzen abends auf der Veranda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sit on the veranda in the evening.

definitions.note: Often used for organized/public events (e.g., a concert, lecture, festival, or official gathering).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Veranstaltung beginnt um 19 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The event starts at 7 p.m.

definitions.note: Often used in official or workplace contexts for the person who has responsibility for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verantwortliche spricht mit den Eltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The person in charge is talking with the parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage die Verantwortung für das Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take responsibility for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt wechselt den Verband.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor changes the bandage.

definitions.note: Often used for larger groups like professional associations or sports organizations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie arbeitet für einen internationalen Verband.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works for an international association.

definitions.note: plural of „das Verb“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Deutschen sind Verben oft an zweiter Stelle im Satz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In German, verbs are often in second position in the sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen dringend eine Verbesserung der Situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We urgently need an improvement in the situation.

definitions.note: Often used for technical connections (e.g., internet/phone) or transport connections (e.g., train/bus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verbindung ist heute sehr langsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The connection is very slow today.

definitions.note: Used for personal or social ties; also common in the phrase „in Verbindung bleiben“ (to stay in touch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie haben eine enge Verbindung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have a close relationship.

definitions.note: Plural of "Verbindung".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verbindungen zwischen den Städten sind sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The connections between the cities are very good.

definitions.note: Used especially in scientific/chemistry contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Verbindungen sind in Wasser löslich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These compounds are soluble in water.

definitions.note: Often used in a general sense (not naming a specific forbidden thing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als Kind fand ich Verbotenes besonders spannend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I found forbidden things especially exciting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Täter hat ein schweres Verbrechen begangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrator committed a serious crime.

definitions.note: Genitive singular of „das Verbrechen“ (often used after words like „wegen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde wegen eines Verbrechens verhaftet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was arrested because of a crime.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Verbrecher verhaftet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the criminal.

definitions.note: dative plural form of "Verbrecher" (often used after prepositions like mit, von, zu)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei spricht mit Verbrechern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are talking to criminals.

definitions.note: Plural of "Verbrennung".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hatte Verbrennungen an den Händen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had burns on his hands.

definitions.note: Plural of "Verband".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Verbände fordern strengere Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many associations are calling for stricter rules.

definitions.note: Plural of "Verband".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Erste-Hilfe-Kasten sind Verbände und Pflaster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the first-aid kit there are bandages and plasters.

definitions.note: often used in political or military contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sprach mit Verbündeten über den Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke with allies about the plan.

definitions.note: often used in political, military, or strategic contexts; masculine singular (feminine: Verbündete)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland betrachtet Frankreich als wichtigen Verbündeter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany considers France an important ally.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es besteht der Verdacht, dass er gelogen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is suspicion that he lied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Essen beginnt die Verdauung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After eating, digestion begins.

definitions.note: Plural form of „Verdienst“; often used for someone’s accomplishments or contributions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wurde für ihre Verdienste um die Wissenschaft ausgezeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was honored for her achievements in science.

definitions.note: Can refer to one female suspect (singular) or to multiple suspects (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei befragt zwei Verdächtige.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are questioning two suspects.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei befragte Verdächtige.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police questioned suspects.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei befragte die Verdächtigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police questioned the suspects.

definitions.note: Used as a nominalized adjective (neuter) to mean an unspecified suspicious thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat im Auto etwas Verdächtiges gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found something suspicious in the car.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who greatly admires a person (sometimes in a romantic way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat viele Verehrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has many admirers.

definitions.note: Often used for deep respect (sometimes with a religious tone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen empfinden große Verehrung für ihre Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people feel great admiration for their teacher.

definitions.note: Usually an organized group (often for sports or hobbies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Bruder ist in einem Fußballverein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is in a soccer club.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben eine Vereinbarung getroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We made an agreement.

definitions.note: Often used for official, legal, or administrative procedures.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Verfahren dauert mehrere Wochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The procedure takes several weeks.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., on documents, forms, or in academia).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verfasser des Artikels ist unbekannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The author of the article is unknown.

definitions.note: often used for a country's constitution (law); it can also mean someone's physical condition, but the legal meaning is usually the first one learners meet
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verfassung garantiert die Meinungsfreiheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The constitution guarantees freedom of speech.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verfolgung von Minderheiten ist ein schweres Unrecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The persecution of minorities is a serious injustice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Verfolgung gab die Polizei den Täter festgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the pursuit, the police arrested the perpetrator.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/official language, e.g. a decision issued by an authority.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Behörde hat eine Verfügung erlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authority issued an order.

definitions.native: disposal (the ability to use something), availability
definitions.note: Common in fixed phrases like „zur Verfügung stehen“ (to be available) and „zur Verfügung stellen“ (to make available).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto steht dir heute zur Verfügung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is available to you today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Vergangenheit war alles anders.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, everything was different.

definitions.note: a part of some (especially older) gasoline engines
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vergaser ist kaputt, deshalb springt das Auto nicht an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The carburetor is broken, so the car won’t start.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bitte dich um Vergebung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ask you for forgiveness.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts; can refer to revenge (personal) or retribution (as punishment/payment back).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schwor Vergeltung für den Angriff.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swore revenge for the attack.

definitions.note: Very serious and sensitive term; refers to a person who commits rape.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vergewaltiger wurde von der Polizei festgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rapist was arrested by the police.

definitions.note: Strong, legal/medical term.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei ermittelt wegen einer Vergewaltigung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating a rape.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Vergleich zum letzten Jahr ist das Wetter besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Compared to last year, the weather is better.

definitions.note: Common in legal/financial contexts (e.g., reaching an agreement to end a dispute).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Firmen haben einen Vergleich geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two companies reached a settlement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war mir ein Vergnügen, Sie kennenzulernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a pleasure to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war mir ein Vergnügen, dich kennenzulernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a pleasure to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen am Samstag in den Vergnügungspark.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the amusement park on Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du den Text mit dem Vergrößerungsglas lesen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you read the text with the magnifying glass?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verhaftung fand gestern Abend statt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The arrest took place yesterday evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Verhalten war sehr höflich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior was very polite.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach langen Verhandlungen haben sie sich endlich geeinigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After long negotiations, they finally came to an agreement.

definitions.note: Used in a legal/court context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verhandlung vor Gericht beginnt um neun Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The court hearing begins at nine o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verhandlungen zwischen den beiden Firmen dauern noch an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The negotiations between the two companies are still ongoing.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning the act/process of starving (sometimes: starving to death).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durch den Krieg droht vielen Menschen das Verhungern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the war, many people are threatened with starvation.

definitions.note: Usually used as a noun with an article (e.g. „das Verhungern“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durch die Dürre droht vielen Menschen das Verhungern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the drought, many people are at risk of starving.

definitions.note: Often used for personal, social, or professional relationships; can also refer to an affair depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein gutes Verhältnis zu meinen Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a good relationship with my neighbors.

definitions.note: Used for mathematical or comparative relations between quantities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Verhältnis von Jungen zu Mädchen ist drei zu zwei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ratio of boys to girls is three to two.

definitions.note: Plural of "Verhältnis"; often used when talking about someone’s living conditions or the situation in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unter diesen Verhältnissen können wir nicht weiterarbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Under these circumstances, we can’t keep working.

definitions.note: Dative plural of „Verhältnis“; often used in the phrase „unter ... Verhältnissen“ (“under ... circumstances”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unter diesen Verhältnissen können wir nicht arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Under these circumstances, we can’t work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verkauf beginnt morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sale starts tomorrow.

definitions.note: Plural of "Verkaufszahl".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verkaufszahlen sind diesen Monat deutlich gestiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sales figures have risen significantly this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des starken Verkehrs kommen wir zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the heavy traffic, we’re late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verkehrspolizei hat den Unfall aufgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic police recorded the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Germany you have to follow the traffic rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen eines Unfalls gibt es auf der Autobahn einen Verkehrsstau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of an accident, there is a traffic jam on the highway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen eines Verkehrsunfalls ist die Straße gesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of a traffic accident, the road is closed.

definitions.note: Genitive singular form of „Verkehrsunfall“ (e.g., „wegen des Verkehrsunfalls“ = „because of the traffic accident“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des Verkehrsunfalls kam es zu langen Staus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the traffic accident, there were long traffic jams.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Winter gibt es auf dieser Straße oft Verkehrsunfälle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, there are often traffic accidents on this road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zu Karneval trage ich eine bunte Verkleidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For Carnival, I wear a colorful costume.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verkäufer hilft mir bei der Auswahl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salesperson helps me with the selection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verlag veröffentlicht jedes Jahr viele neue Bücher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The publisher releases many new books every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein starkes Verlangen nach Schokolade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a strong desire for chocolate.

definitions.native: reliability, someone/something you can rely on
definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „Auf ihn/sie ist Verlass.“ (= You can rely on him/her.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dich ist immer Verlass.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can always rely on you.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (nominalized verb); often with an article, e.g. „das Verlassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Verlassen der Wohnung ist nach 22 Uhr nicht erlaubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leaving the apartment is not allowed after 10 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde vor allen Leuten rot vor Verlegenheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He blushed with embarrassment in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „in Verlegenheit geraten/kommen“ (to get into a difficult spot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in Verlegenheit, weil ich mein Portemonnaie zu Hause vergessen habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm in a predicament because I forgot my wallet at home.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning “injured person/people” (from the adjective „verletzt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall gab es mehrere Verletzte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, there were several injured people.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural: „die Verletzten“ = the injured (people).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The medics take care of the injured.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got a knee injury while playing soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt behandelt ihre Verletzungen im Krankenhaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor treats her injuries in the hospital.

definitions.note: Plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verleumdungen haben seinem Ruf geschadet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The slanders harmed his reputation.

definitions.note: Often used in the plural to mean "lovers" (a couple in love).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verliebte gehen oft zusammen spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: People in love often go for walks together.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (nominalized verb), usually with an article: „das Verlieren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Verlieren gehört manchmal zum Leben dazu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Losing is sometimes part of life.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult; can also mean the person/team that loses in a competition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende des Spiels waren sie die Verlierer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the game, they were the losers.

definitions.note: Means an engaged person; the gender depends on the article (die Verlobte = fiancée, der Verlobte = fiancé).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Verlobte kommt aus Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My fiancée is from Berlin.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of „Verlobte/Verlobter“ (often used with articles like „den/dem/des“ or in the plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne mit meinem Verlobten zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live together with my fiancé.

definitions.note: the period/state of being engaged to be married
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihre Verlobung haben sie im kleinen Kreis gefeiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They celebrated their engagement in a small circle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verlust meines Handys war sehr ärgerlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loss of my phone was very annoying.

definitions.note: Plural of „der Verlust“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma hat in diesem Jahr hohe Verluste gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company has made big losses this year.

definitions.note: Often used for extending a deadline, contract, or permit; also used in sports for extra time (overtime).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine Verlängerung der Frist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need an extension of the deadline.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unser Vermieter repariert nächste Woche die Heizung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our landlord will repair the heating next week.

definitions.note: female form of "Vermieter" (landlord)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Vermieterin wohnt im Haus nebenan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My landlady lives in the house next door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist nur eine Vermutung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s just an assumption.

definitions.note: Plural of "Vermutung".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt viele Vermutungen darüber, warum der Zug zu spät ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many assumptions about why the train is late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ihr Vermögen in Immobilien investiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She invested her wealth in real estate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Vernichtung der alten Brücke dauerte nur wenige Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The destruction of the old bridge took only a few hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf die Vernunft und nicht nur auf deine Gefühle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Listen to reason and not just to your feelings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte entsorgen Sie die Verpackung im Müll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please throw the packaging in the trash.

definitions.note: Often used for meals provided as part of a service (e.g., at a hotel, event, or on a trip).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Preis ist die Verpflegung inklusive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Food and drink are included in the price.

definitions.note: Plural of "Verpflichtung".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute viele Verpflichtungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many obligations today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Verrat hat alle schockiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His betrayal shocked everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war ein Verräter und hat alles weitererzählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was a traitor and told everyone everything.

definitions.note: female person (a woman)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wurde als Verräterin beschimpft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was insulted as a traitor.

definitions.note: Noun formed from the adjective "verrückt"; often refers to a (specific) woman when used as "die Verrückte".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crazy woman is dancing in the street.

definitions.note: Often colloquial and can be insulting, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Angst vor den Verrückten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid of the crazy people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein Verrückter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a crazy person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe etwas Verrücktes gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did something crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Vers ist schwer zu verstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This verse is hard to understand.

definitions.note: Often used for organized gatherings (e.g., an assembly or a formal meeting).

definitions.note: plural of "Zitrone"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe zwei Zitronen für den Tee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying two lemons for the tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche Zitronensaft für den Tee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need lemon juice for the tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Wasser kann keine Zivilisation lange bestehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, no civilization can last long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten mussten die Zivilisten schützen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers had to protect the civilians.

definitions.note: Used for taxes/fees charged on imported goods; in plural often refers to the customs office/authorities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dieses Produkt musst du Zoll bezahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to pay customs duty on this product.

definitions.note: Unit of length (mainly used for screens, wheels, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fernseher hat 55 Zoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The TV is 55 inches.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Film greifen Zombies die Stadt an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, zombies attack the city.

definitions.note: Plural of "Zombie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dem Film kämpfen sie gegen Zombies.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, they fight against zombies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Zone ist nur für Fußgänger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This zone is only for pedestrians.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Sonntag gehen wir in den Zoo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sunday we’re going to the zoo.

definitions.note: Often used for strong, intense anger; slightly more formal/literary than "Wut".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus Zorn sagte er Dinge, die er später bereute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Out of anger, he said things that he later regretted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme meinen Kaffee ohne Zucker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take my coffee without sugar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durch Zufall habe ich ihn im Supermarkt getroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By chance, I ran into him at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „Zuflucht finden“ (“to find refuge”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Familie fand Zuflucht in einer Kirche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family found refuge in a church.

definitions.note: Plural of „Zufall“; often used for events that happen by chance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind keine Zufälle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those aren’t coincidences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug kommt um 18 Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train arrives at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Often used for an extra song/performance at the end (an “encore”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Publikum klatscht und ruft nach einer Zugabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience claps and calls for an encore.

definitions.note: Can mean access in the sense of permission or the ability to enter/use something (e.g., a building, a service, the internet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinen Zugang zu diesem Konto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have access to this account.

definitions.note: genitive singular of „der Zug“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des Zuges bin ich zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the train, I’m late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zugfahrt nach Berlin dauert zwei Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train journey to Berlin takes two hours.

definitions.note: Often used for access to data, files, systems, or resources (e.g., online access).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinen Zugriff auf diese Datei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have access to this file.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning one’s home; when used adverbially, it commonly appears as „zu Hause“ (at home). Here the example uses the exact form „Zuhause“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute den ganzen Tag Zuhause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m home all day today.

definitions.note: Derogatory; refers to a man who controls and profits from sex workers (often linked to crime).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat einen Zuhälter festgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a pimp.

definitions.note: Often refers to paying attention to what someone says (not just hearing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beim Zuhören lerne ich viel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learn a lot by listening.

definitions.note: often used in the plural (Zuhörer) to mean “the audience.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zuhörer hören aufmerksam zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The listeners are listening attentively.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Zukunft möchte ich in Deutschland leben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the future, I would like to live in Germany.

definitions.note: Often used for official permission/authorization (e.g., university admission, vehicle registration/approval).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Zulassung darf das Auto nicht auf die Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without approval, the car is not allowed on the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie zeigte ihm viel Zuneigung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed him a lot of affection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir auf die Zunge gebissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bit my tongue.

definitions.note: Plural of „Zunge“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zungen der Kinder waren blau vom Eis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children's tongues were blue from the ice cream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gute Zusammenarbeit ist in diesem Team sehr wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good collaboration is very important in this team.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „im Zusammenhang mit …“ (= in connection with …) or „in diesem Zusammenhang“ (= in this context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Zusammenhang mit deiner Bewerbung fehlen noch zwei Dokumente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In connection with your application, two documents are still missing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zusammenstoß auf der Kreuzung hat einen Stau verursacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The collision at the intersection caused a traffic jam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zuschauer klatschen nach dem Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The spectators clap after the game.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun for the act/fact of arriving late.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen seines Zuspätkommens hat er den Zug verpasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because he was late, he missed the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In welchem Zustand ist das Auto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What condition is the car in?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen deine Zustimmung, bevor wir den Vertrag unterschreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need your approval before we sign the contract.

definitions.note: plural of „Zutat“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welche Zutaten brauchen wir für den Kuchen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which ingredients do we need for the cake?

definitions.note: Often used in official or formal contexts (e.g., “Zutritt verboten” = “No entry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zutritt nur für Mitglieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Access only for members.

definitions.note: Often used for a hopeful, trusting attitude about the future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Zuversicht, dass alles gut wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m confident that everything will turn out fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was ist der Zweck dieser Übung?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the purpose of this exercise?

definitions.note: Plural of „Zweck“ (the singular is „der Zweck“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Daten werden nur für bestimmte Zwecke verwendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This data is used only for specific purposes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinen Zweifel daran, dass du das schaffst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no doubt that you can do it.

definitions.note: dative plural of "Zweig"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In den Zweigen sitzt ein Vogel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A bird is sitting in the branches.

definitions.note: Often used to describe finishing position (e.g., in sports/competitions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde Zweiter im Rennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came in second in the race.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen Zweitschlüssel bei meiner Nachbarin hinterlegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left a spare key with my neighbor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dem Märchen hilft ein Zwerg dem Mädchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the fairy tale, a dwarf helps the girl.

definitions.note: plural of „Zwerg“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dem Märchen wohnen sieben Zwerge im Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the fairy tale, seven dwarves live in the forest.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Zwerg“ (used after many prepositions like „mit“, „zu“, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er arbeitet mit den Zwergen in der Mine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works with the dwarves in the mine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schneide eine Zwiebel für die Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m chopping an onion for the soup.

definitions.note: plural of "Zwiebel"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe Zwiebeln für die Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying onions for the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schwester ist ein Zwilling.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a twin.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zwillinge sehen sich sehr ähnlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The twins look very similar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Zwillingsbruder heißt Jonas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My twin brother is called Jonas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Zwillingsschwester und ich sehen uns sehr ähnlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My twin sister and I look very similar.

definitions.note: often used for an unexpected (sometimes minor) event, especially something disruptive or negative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Bahnhof gab es einen kleinen Zwischenfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a small incident at the train station.

definitions.note: Often used for a planned stop during a journey before reaching the final destination.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen einen Zwischenhalt in Köln, bevor wir weiterfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re making a stopover in Cologne before we continue traveling.

definitions.note: plural of „Zahn“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich putze mir jeden Abend die Zähne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brush my teeth every evening.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Zahn“ (often used after prepositions like „mit“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich putze mir mit einer Zahnbürste die Zähne zwischen den Zähnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brush my teeth with a toothbrush, including between my teeth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zeigte ihr viel Zärtlichkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He showed her a lot of tenderness.

definitions.note: Plural of "Zopf".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt heute zwei Zöpfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s wearing two braids today.

definitions.note: Plural of "Zug".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute fahren viele Züge pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today many trains are on time.

definitions.note: dative plural of „der Zug“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit den Zügen komme ich schnell nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the trains, I get to Berlin quickly.

definitions.note: dative plural of „der Zug“ (as in a pull/draw on something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit ein paar Zügen am Seil öffnete er das Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a few pulls on the rope, he opened the gate.

definitions.note: Technical term; often used for a device that triggers an explosion (e.g., in a bomb or grenade).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zünder ist defekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detonator is defective.

definitions.note: Often used for engines/vehicles (e.g., spark ignition).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zündung ist kaputt, deshalb springt das Auto nicht an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ignition is broken, so the car won’t start.

definitions.note: Used with a time or point onward (often with dative): ab Montag, ab jetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ab Montag arbeite ich wieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From Monday on, I’m working again.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „fahren“, „nehmen“, „machen“ to mean leaving/removing (e.g. „abfahren“ = depart).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug fährt um 8 Uhr ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train leaves at 8 o’clock.

definitions.note: Used with time, dates, ages, prices, etc. to mean “starting from”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ab morgen arbeite ich wieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Starting tomorrow, I’ll work again.

definitions.note: Often used with machines/devices, meaning “switch off/turn off.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is off.

definitions.note: Often used as a separable verb particle (Verbpartikel); it typically goes to the end of the clause (e.g., „anmachen“ → „mach … an“, „abmachen“ → „mach … ab“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte das Licht ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn off the light.

definitions.note: Strongly negative; often used to express moral disgust or shock.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde es abartig, wie er über andere Menschen redet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find it disgusting the way he talks about other people.

definitions.native: to turn off; to turn (onto a street)
definitions.note: Often used for turning left/right while driving or walking; separable verb (e.g., „Ich biege ab.“ / „Sie biegen ab.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie müssen an der nächsten Kreuzung rechts abbiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to turn right at the next intersection.

definitions.note: Often used for canceling planned events, appointments, or reservations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Treffen morgen leider abbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, we have to cancel the meeting tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for stopping an activity already in progress (e.g., a conversation, a task, a trip).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Gespräch jetzt abbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to break off the conversation now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das alte Haus kann leicht abbrennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old house can easily burn down.

definitions.note: Often used for getting rid of something by burning, e.g., fat/calories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will die Kalorien wieder abbrennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to burn off the calories again.

definitions.note: Often used with „jemanden von etwas abbringen“ (to dissuade someone from something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann ihn nicht davon abbringen, das Auto zu kaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t dissuade him from buying the car.

definitions.note: Often used for people in official roles (e.g., politicians, leaders) stepping down from a position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Minister musste nach dem Skandal abdanken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The minister had to resign after the scandal.

definitions.note: Usually written with a capital letter as the noun: „der Abend“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Abend habe ich Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the evening I have time.

definitions.native: in the evenings, in the evening
definitions.note: Refers to a habitual or typical time (what you generally do in the evening), not a specific evening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe abends oft spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often go for a walk in the evenings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schwester ist sehr abenteuerlustig und probiert gerne neue Dinge aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very adventurous and likes trying new things.

definitions.note: Often used to contrast what was just said; can also be used to express surprise or objection depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte kommen, aber ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to come, but I don't have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte kommen, aber ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to come, but I don’t have time.

definitions.note: Often used at the start of a sentence to object, correct someone, or express surprise/emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aber das stimmt nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: But that's not true!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte kommen, aber ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to come, but I don't have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr abergläubisch und klopft dreimal auf Holz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very superstitious and knocks on wood three times.

definitions.note: Often used for vehicles (trains, buses, cars) or groups about to leave.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist abfahrbereit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is ready to depart.

definitions.native: to depart; to leave (especially of vehicles, scheduled services)
definitions.note: Common for trains/buses/ships, often with a specific departure time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug wird um 8 Uhr abfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will depart at 8 o'clock.

definitions.native: to drive off; to set off (in a vehicle)
definitions.note: Also used for starting a trip by car/bike, etc.; can be literal ‘drive away’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen jetzt abfahren, sonst kommen wir zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to set off now, otherwise we'll be late.

definitions.native: to fire (a weapon), to shoot off
definitions.note: Used for firing shots or firing a weapon; also for shooting something off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten abfeuern eine Rakete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers fire a rocket.

definitions.native: to launch (e.g., a rocket, missile), to fire off
definitions.note: Common with rockets/missiles; can also be used informally for quickly “firing off” a comment or question.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Raumfahrtbehörde will morgen eine Sonde abfeuern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The space agency wants to launch a probe tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in nautical or technical contexts (e.g., letting out a rope or lowering a load).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Segel langsam abfieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to lower the sail slowly.

definitions.note: Often used for turning in something officially (e.g., homework, an application, a form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst deine Hausaufgaben bis Freitag abgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to hand in your homework by Friday.

definitions.note: Often used when you give something to someone else (sometimes unwillingly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will sein altes Fahrrad nicht abgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t want to give up his old bike.

definitions.note: past participle of "abbiegen"; often used with "sein" in the perfect tense (e.g., "ist abgebogen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist an der nächsten Kreuzung rechts abgebogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned right at the next intersection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist letzte Nacht abgebrannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house burned down last night.

definitions.note: past participle of „abbrennen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist abgebrannt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist letzte Nacht abgebrannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house burned down last night.

definitions.note: past participle of „abbrechen“; often used for ending an activity early
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die Reise abgebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We cancelled (cut short) the trip.

definitions.note: often used with lights, water, gas, etc. (more common in Austrian/Southern German usage)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Wasser abgedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned off the water.

definitions.note: colloquial; describes something unusual or eccentric
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Idee ist total abgedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The idea is totally crazy.

definitions.note: Past participle of "abfahren"; in the present perfect it’s typically used with "sein" (e.g., "ist abgefahren").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist schon abgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train has already left.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used to mean something is surprisingly unusual or impressive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war echt abgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really crazy.

definitions.note: often used about buses/trains that have already left
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist schon abgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train has already left.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense to mean something detached or came off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Knopf ist abgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The button fell off.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to describe values (e.g., temperature, prices) going down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Temperatur ist über Nacht stark abgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The temperature dropped sharply overnight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist schon abgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train has already left.

definitions.native: gone off, exploded (e.g., a bomb, a gun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück ist die Bombe nicht abgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, the bomb didn’t go off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Hausaufgaben abgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned in my homework.

definitions.note: Past participle of „abhalten“ used for events/meetings (often with „werden“ in the passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sitzung wurde gestern abgehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting was held yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of „abhalten“ used with „jemanden von etwas abhalten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nichts hat ihn davon abgehalten, es zu versuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nothing prevented him from trying it.

definitions.note: Colloquial; used as the past participle of the verb „abhauen“ (to run off / take off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nach dem Streit einfach abgehauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the argument, he just took off.

definitions.note: informal; often used to mean someone left suddenly or escaped
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern Abend einfach abgehauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He just ran off last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Ast abgehauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chopped off the branch.

definitions.note: Also used as: „Der Zug geht um 8 Uhr ab.“ (separable verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug wird um 8 Uhr abgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will leave at 8 o’clock.

definitions.native: to go off (e.g., an alarm, fireworks)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Feueralarm kann plötzlich abgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire alarm can suddenly go off.

definitions.note: Common in questions like „Was geht ab?“ = “What’s going on?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was wird hier abgehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s going to happen here? / What’s going on here?

definitions.note: past participle of „abheben“; often used with „sein“ for flights (e.g., a plane taking off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug ist pünktlich abgehoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane took off on time.

definitions.note: often used to describe someone who seems detached or thinks they are better than others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit dem Erfolg wirkt sie ein bisschen abgehoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since the success, she seems a bit aloof.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich vom Bahnhof abgeholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked you up from the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug, der um 8 Uhr vom Gleis 3 abfährt, ist der, der pünktlich abgeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train that leaves from platform 3 at 8 o’clock is the one that departs on time.

definitions.note: Often used in questions like „Was geht ab?“ = “What’s going on?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß nicht, was hier abgeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know what’s going on here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Sprachnachricht abgehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listened to the voice message.

definitions.note: Often used when a phone line or conversation is secretly monitored by the police or another person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Telefon wurde abgehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone was wiretapped.

definitions.note: Colloquial; past participle of „abknallen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Täter wurde von der Polizei abgeknallt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrator was shot (dead) by the police.

definitions.note: Colloquial; used as an adjective meaning someone is acting very crazy/over-the-top.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist ja völlig abgeknallt!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re completely crazy!

definitions.note: Past participle of „abkommen“; often used with „sein“ for something that has detached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Knopf ist abgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The button came off.

definitions.note: often used for best-before dates, tickets, or deadlines
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Joghurt ist abgelaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The yogurt is expired.

definitions.note: used for a person or animal leaving by running
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist abgelaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog ran off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben in einem abgelegenen Dorf übernachtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stayed overnight in a remote village.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Handy auf den Tisch abgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put my phone down on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seine Jacke abgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took off his jacket.

definitions.note: Used for organizing/storing paperwork (e.g., in a folder).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die Unterlagen im Ordner abgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She filed the documents in the folder.

definitions.note: past participle of „ablehnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Antrag wurde abgelehnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My application was rejected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute sehr abgelenkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very distracted today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin beim Lernen leicht abgelenkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get distracted easily while studying.

definitions.note: past participle of „ablenken“; often used with „sein“ to mean being distracted
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute leicht abgelenkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m easily distracted today.

definitions.note: Often used to confirm an agreement, similar to “deal!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns um acht, abgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet at eight, agreed.

definitions.note: Often used with amounts like „fünf Kilo“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe fünf Kilo abgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost five kilos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist hat mir die Fingerabdrücke abgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer took my fingerprints.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zahl der Besucher hat abgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The number of visitors decreased.

definitions.note: past participle; often used with „haben“ when talking about weight loss
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe in den letzten Monaten fünf Kilo abgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve lost five kilos in the last few months.

definitions.note: past participle; used when something has been taken off/removed
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt hat den Verband abgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor removed the bandage.

definitions.note: past participle of "abreisen"; commonly used with "sein" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sind gestern abgereist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „abreißen“; often used with buildings
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das alte Haus wurde abgerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old house was demolished.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert ist abgesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert is canceled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wehrpflicht wurde 2011 abgeschafft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Compulsory military service was abolished in 2011.

definitions.note: Often used for sending mail, packages, or applications.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Paket gestern abgeschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent the package yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for vehicles that are removed (e.g., by a tow truck, sometimes ordered by police).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Auto wurde gestern abgeschleppt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My car was towed away yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Projekt ist abgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is finished.

definitions.note: Often used for doors/rooms/areas that are shut and not accessible.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist abgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is locked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist abgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is locked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Aufgabe abgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completed the task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kabel ist abgeschnitten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cable is cut off.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., in the perfect tense) or as an adjective meaning something has been cut/trimmed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat ein Stück vom Brot abgeschnitten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cut off a piece of the bread.

definitions.note: Usually used with „von“: „abgesehen von …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abgesehen von dem Regen war der Ausflug sehr schön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apart from the rain, the trip was very nice.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „abgesehen davon“ (= aside from that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abgesehen davon ist alles gut gelaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aside from that, everything went well.

definitions.note: Most commonly used in the fixed phrase „abgesehen von …“ (+ dative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abgesehen von dem Regen war der Tag schön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apart from the rain, the day was nice.

definitions.note: Often used for TV/radio programs or events that are discontinued.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Serie wurde nach der zweiten Staffel abgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The series was canceled after the second season.

definitions.note: Often used for someone being removed from a position of power or a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Minister wurde nach dem Skandal abgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The minister was dismissed after the scandal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben das so abgesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed on it like that.

definitions.note: often used for leaving a vehicle somewhere (also: placed/left somewhere)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto ist vor dem Haus abgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is parked in front of the house.

definitions.note: used especially for machines/devices (e.g. heating, motor)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Heizung ist abgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heating is turned off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug ist abgestürzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane crashed.

definitions.note: Often used for accidents (e.g., a person falling, a plane crashing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist von der Leiter abgestürzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell off the ladder.

definitions.note: past participle of „abwaschen“ (used with „haben“ in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Geschirr abgewaschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I washed the dishes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gefahr wurde abgewendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The danger was averted.

definitions.note: Past participle; often used with passive constructions like „wurde abgewiesen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Antrag wurde abgewiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My application was rejected.

definitions.note: past participle of „abwerfen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seine Jacke abgeworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took off his jacket.

definitions.note: past participle of „abwerfen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind hat viele Blätter abgeworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind dropped many leaves.

definitions.native: to have taken off (something), to be not wearing (something)
definitions.note: Used mainly with clothing/accessories. Often appears as separable: „Ich habe die Jacke ab.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann meine Jacke abhaben, weil es hier warm ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can have my jacket off because it’s warm in here.

definitions.note: Often used for cutting something off with an axe; separable verb (hackt ... ab).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Äste abhacken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you chop off the branches?

definitions.native: to prevent, to stop (someone from doing something)
definitions.note: Often used with "jemanden von etwas abhalten" or "jemanden daran abhalten, ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich nicht davon abhalten, das zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stop you from doing that.

definitions.native: to hold (an event, a speech, a meeting)
definitions.note: Often used with events like "eine Rede" or "ein Treffen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister wird eine Rede abhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor will give a speech.

definitions.note: informal; often means leaving suddenly or running away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt abhauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take off now.

definitions.note: Often used for taking cash out of an ATM or bank account.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch schnell Geld abheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still need to quickly withdraw some money.

definitions.note: Used for planes when they leave the ground.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug wird in zehn Minuten abheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane will take off in ten minutes.

definitions.note: Often used for picking up a person (e.g., by car) or collecting something (e.g., an order or package).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mich morgen vom Bahnhof abholen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pick me up from the train station tomorrow?

definitions.note: Often used with „von“: „von etwas/jemandem abhängen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ob wir gehen, kann von der Zeit abhängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whether we go can depend on the time.

definitions.note: For taking something that is hanging (e.g., a picture, curtains).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Gardinen abhängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to take down the curtains.

definitions.note: Colloquial, often with „mit“: „mit Freunden abhängen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Wochenende wollen wir im Park abhängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the weekend we want to hang out in the park.

definitions.note: Often used with „von“ (dependent on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin von meinen Eltern abhängig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am dependent on my parents.

definitions.note: Used especially with „nach“ or „von“ (addicted to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist abhängig von Alkohol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is addicted to alcohol.

definitions.note: colloquial; can sound violent/slang
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dem Film will der Täter den Zeugen abknallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, the perpetrator wants to shoot the witness dead.

definitions.native: to set off (fireworks), to shoot off (fireworks)
definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: An Silvester wollen viele Leute Feuerwerk abknallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On New Year’s Eve, many people want to set off fireworks.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about whether someone has time away from work or duties.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Nachmittag nicht abkömmlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not available this afternoon.

definitions.note: Used for both things (food, weather) and people (to calm down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lass die Suppe erst ein bisschen abkühlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the soup cool down a bit first.

definitions.note: often used for things with a time limit (e.g., contracts, tickets, food)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag kann nächstes Jahr ablaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract can expire next year.

definitions.note: used for how a process or event happens
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besprechen, wie das Treffen ablaufen wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll discuss how the meeting will proceed.

definitions.note: Often used for taking off clothes, glasses, jewelry, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meinen Mantel ablegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take off my coat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss Ihre Anfrage leider ablehnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I have to refuse your request.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of „ablehnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ablehnt das Angebot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rejects the offer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Laute Musik kann mich beim Lernen ablenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Loud music can distract me while I'm studying.

definitions.note: Often used for delivering something (like a package) or handing in work (like an assignment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Paket heute abliefern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to deliver the package today.
