definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte abnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to lose weight.

definitions.note: Often used for taking something off (e.g., clothes, a cover) or removing an item from a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte den Deckel abnehmen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please take the lid off?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Kanal abonniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I subscribed to the channel.

definitions.note: Past participle of „abrasieren“; often used with „sich“ to mean shaving (one’s beard, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich den Bart abrasiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shaved off his beard.

definitions.native: to rain itself out; to stop raining (after a while)
definitions.note: Usually used about the weather, often with „es“ as the subject; separable verb: es regnet ab / es hat abgeregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, es wird gleich abregen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, it’ll stop raining soon.

definitions.note: Used especially for leaving on a trip or journey.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen morgen früh abreisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to leave early tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: tear down, demolish; tear off, rip off
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das alte Haus abreißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to tear down the old house.

definitions.note: Commonly used for canceling appointments, meetings, events, or trips.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Termin absagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to cancel the appointment.

definitions.note: Used when you say you cannot come to something you were invited to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss die Einladung absagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to decline the invitation.

definitions.note: Often used for laws, rules, institutions, or taxes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regierung will die Steuer abschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government wants to abolish the tax.

definitions.native: to turn off, to switch off
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Licht abschalten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn off the light?

definitions.note: Often used about taking a break and not thinking about work or stress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Arbeit will ich einfach abschalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work I just want to relax.

definitions.note: strongly negative; used for something morally repulsive or very unpleasant
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde es abscheulich, wie er sie behandelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find it disgusting how he treats her.

definitions.note: Often used for sending letters/emails or submitting a form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Formular heute abschicken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to send off the form today.

definitions.note: usually used for deporting someone (often a foreigner) from a country
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Behörden wollen ihn abschieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authorities want to deport him.

definitions.native: to shift (blame/responsibility) onto someone, to pass (something) off on someone
definitions.note: often used with „auf jemanden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, die Schuld auf mich abzuschieben, aber ich habe damit nichts zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to shift the blame onto me, but I have nothing to do with it.

definitions.note: often used for bringing down an aircraft
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie haben das feindliche Flugzeug abgeschossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They shot down the enemy aircraft.

definitions.note: used for firing fireworks, rockets, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: An Silvester schießen viele Leute Feuerwerk ab; sie sagen dazu auch: „Wir müssen noch ein paar Raketen abschießen.“
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On New Year’s Eve, many people set off fireworks; they also say: “We still need to shoot off a few rockets.”

definitions.note: Often used for rejecting an offer, invitation, or request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will das Angebot abschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to decline the offer.

definitions.native: to chop off, to cut off
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Metzger muss den Kopf abschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The butcher has to chop off the head.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Tür abschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to lock the door.

definitions.note: Often used for finishing a task/project or concluding a process.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen das Projekt diese Woche abschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to finish the project this week.

definitions.note: Used with things like a contract, subscription, or insurance policy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will eine Versicherung abschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to take out an insurance policy.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of "abschließen"; often used for locking (a door) or closing something off/finishing something (like a contract).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er abschließt die Tür jeden Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He locks the door every evening.

definitions.native: to remove (your) makeup, to take off (your) makeup
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich vor dem Schlafengehen abschminken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to remove my makeup before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde ein Stück Brot abschneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will cut off a piece of bread.

definitions.note: Often used with an adverb like „gut“ (well) or „schlecht“ (badly), especially for results in tests, games, or competitions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird bei dem Wettkampf gut abschneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will do well in the competition.

definitions.note: Often used for copying text (e.g., from the board or from a book).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Vokabeln bitte abschreiben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please copy out the vocabulary words?

definitions.note: Commonly used for cheating by copying someone else’s answers in a test.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wollte in der Prüfung abschreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to cheat on the exam by copying.

definitions.native: off to the side, away from the main road/path
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus liegt abseits der Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is off to the side of the road.

definitions.note: used especially in soccer/football
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stürmer stand abseits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The striker was offside.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used for ending a relationship or getting rid of someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich einfach abserviert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He just dumped me.

definitions.native: to put down, to set down, to drop off
definitions.note: Often used for putting something down somewhere or dropping someone/something off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mich am Bahnhof absetzen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you drop me off at the train station?

definitions.note: Common with taxes/expenses (e.g., Kosten von der Steuer absetzen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich diese Kosten von der Steuer absetzen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I deduct these costs from my taxes?

definitions.note: Used for stopping something like a TV show or an event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sender will die Serie absetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The channel wants to cancel the series.

definitions.note: Often used for making something safer (e.g., a site, a device, a plan) or protecting against risk.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Baustelle absichern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to secure the construction site.

definitions.note: Common in computing for saving a copy of data.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meine Dateien regelmäßig absichern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to back up my files regularly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das absichtlich gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did that intentionally.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong standalone answer meaning “yes, definitely.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ja, das ist absolut richtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, that is absolutely correct.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (weak ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die absolute Wahrheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the absolute truth.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine noun in the accusative case (e.g., after "den").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne den absoluten Grund nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know the absolute reason.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist absoluter Unsinn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is absolute nonsense.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst das Auto hier abstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can park the car here.

definitions.native: turn off (e.g., a device, a machine)
definitions.note: Often used for switching off equipment or systems.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte den Motor abstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn off the engine.

definitions.note: Often used with „über“: „über etwas abstimmen“ = to vote on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen über den Plan abstimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to vote on the plan.

definitions.native: to coordinate, to align (plans, dates, etc.)
definitions.note: Used with a direct object: „etwas abstimmen“ = to coordinate something (e.g., schedules, details).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten die Termine abstimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should coordinate the dates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Erklärung ist mir zu abstrakt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The explanation is too abstract for me.

definitions.note: Often used to deny an accusation, involvement, or responsibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird abstreiten, dass er das Geld genommen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will deny that he took the money.

definitions.note: Often used for computers/phones or vehicles (e.g., a plane).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Computer kann jederzeit abstürzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My computer can crash at any time.

definitions.note: Often used for falling from a height (e.g., off a cliff).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kletterer könnte vom Felsen abstürzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The climber could fall off the cliff.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist doch absurd!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s absurd!

definitions.note: Often implies waiting for something to happen before acting ("wait and see").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen abwarten, was der Arzt sagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to wait and see what the doctor says.

definitions.native: to wash up; to do the dishes
definitions.note: Often refers to washing dishes by hand; separable verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss nach dem Essen noch abwaschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to wash up after eating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen die Hausarbeit abwechselnd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We do the housework in turns.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like „einen Unfall/eine Gefahr abwenden“ (to avert an accident/danger).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärztin konnte die Gefahr abwenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor was able to avert the danger.

definitions.note: Used for physically turning something (or yourself) away, e.g. „den Blick abwenden“ (to look away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er musste den Blick abwenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to look away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Herr Becker ist heute abwesend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mr. Becker is absent today.

definitions.note: Often used for wiping something clean or dry, e.g., a table or a spill.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte den Tisch abwischen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please wipe off the table?

definitions.note: Often used for taking off clothes or removing something stuck on (like tape).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst deine Schuhe abziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to take off your shoes.

definitions.note: Common in math or when deducting costs/taxes from an amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du 10 Euro von dem Preis abziehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you deduct 10 euros from the price?

definitions.native: to dissuade (someone) from, to talk (someone) out of
definitions.note: Used with someone in the accusative + von + dative (e.g., jemanden von etwas abzubringen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, ihn von dieser Idee abzubringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to talk him out of this idea.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „abfahren“, often used after verbs like „planen“, „versuchen“, „vergessen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir planen, um sechs Uhr abzufahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We plan to leave at six o’clock.

definitions.native: to hand in, to hand over
definitions.note: Commonly used for submitting documents/assignments (hand in) or giving something to someone/authorities (hand over).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte vergessen Sie nicht, das Formular heute abzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t forget to hand in the form today.

definitions.note: often used for planned events (e.g., a meeting, a course, an election)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben beschlossen, das Treffen online abzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided to hold the meeting online.

definitions.native: to prevent, to stop (someone from doing something)
definitions.note: often used with "jemanden davon abhalten, ..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nichts kann mich davon abzuhalten, es zu versuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nothing can stop me from trying.

definitions.native: to take off, to lift off
definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „abheben“, used after verbs like „versuchen“, „planen“, „beginnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug versucht gerade abzuheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane is trying to take off right now.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „abheben“, used after verbs like „versuchen“, „planen“, „beginnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe zur Bank, um Geld abzuheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the bank to withdraw money.

definitions.note: Infinitive with „zu“ (used after certain verbs, e.g. „versuchen“, „vergessen“, „planen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergessen, das Paket abzuholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to pick up the package.

definitions.note: often used for taking off clothes (e.g., a jacket, coat, shoes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, meine Jacke abzulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to take off my jacket.

definitions.note: used with exams/tests: eine Prüfung abzulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat nächste Woche noch eine Prüfung abzulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She still has an exam to take next week.

definitions.note: Used especially in formal contexts (e.g., requests, applications).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Antrag ist abzulehnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The application must be rejected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mich mit Musik abzulenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to distract myself with music.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „abnehmen“, often used after verbs like „versuchen“ (to try) or „beginnen“ (to begin).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, abzunehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to lose weight.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „abnehmen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte versuchen, den Deckel abzunehmen, ohne etwas zu verschütten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please try to take off the lid without spilling anything?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe versucht, den Termin abzusagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried to cancel the appointment.

definitions.native: to abolish, to do away with
definitions.note: Often used with laws, rules, or institutions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regierung plant, die Steuer abzuschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government plans to abolish the tax.

definitions.note: used as a zu-infinitive (e.g., after verbs like „vergessen“ or „versuchen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, die Tür abzuschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to lock the door.

definitions.note: used as a zu-infinitive, often with „um … zu“ to express purpose
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche noch einen Kurs, um die Ausbildung abzuschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still need one more course to complete the training.

definitions.note: used with zu (infinitive), often meaning “to wait and see” what happens
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es bleibt abzuwarten, ob das Wetter besser wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It remains to be seen whether the weather will get better.

definitions.native: to wash off, to rinse off
definitions.note: zu-Infinitiv form (e.g., after "versuchen", "Zeit haben", "um ... zu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit, das Geschirr abzuwaschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time to wash the dishes.

definitions.note: Often expresses surprise, disappointment, regret, or sudden realization (depending on context and intonation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ach, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh, I forgot my key!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Acht ist meine Lieblingszahl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eight is my favorite number.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acht ist eine gerade Zahl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eight is an even number.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe acht Äpfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have eight apples.

definitions.note: Used as a (military-style) command; short for „Achtung!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acht! Der Offizier kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Attention! The officer is coming.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" (achte auf ...) to mean "pay attention to".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich achte auf den Verkehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pay attention to traffic.

definitions.note: Used with dates (often with an implied word like „Tag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns am achten Mai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re meeting on May 8th.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ (achten auf + accusative) to mean “pay attention to.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du sollst auf den Verkehr achten!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should pay attention to the traffic!

definitions.note: Can be used with **auf** (to pay attention to) or **jdn./etw.** (to respect, value someone/something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er achtet auf den Verkehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pays attention to the traffic.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „achten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er achtete nicht auf das Schild.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t pay attention to the sign.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" (achtgeben auf + accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst beim Überqueren der Straße gut achtgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to pay close attention when crossing the street.

definitions.note: Often used about being careful and considerate toward people or about paying close attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei bitte achtsam im Umgang mit anderen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be mindful in how you treat others.

definitions.note: Often used as a warning or to get everyone’s attention (e.g., “Achtung!” = “Attention!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Achtung! Da kommt ein Auto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out! A car is coming!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin achtzehn Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am eighteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Oma ist achtzig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma is eighty years old.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned/poetic; often sounds like a final farewell.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Adieu, mein Freund!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Farewell, my friend!

definitions.note: Borrowed from Spanish; used casually (often a bit jokingly) in German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Okay, ich muss los—adios!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, I have to go—bye!

definitions.note: Usually used for legally adopting a child (or sometimes an animal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen ein Kind adoptieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to adopt a child.

definitions.note: past participle of „adoptieren“; often used with „sein“ or „haben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ein Kind adoptiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has adopted a child.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „adoptieren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie adoptierte ein Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She adopted a child.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), used with plural subjects (e.g., „sie“ = they) or formal „Sie“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie adoptierten ein Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They adopted a child.

definitions.note: Often used like a past participle meaning something is addressed to someone (e.g., a letter or email).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die E-Mail ist an dich adressiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The email is addressed to you.

definitions.note: Adjective form; it changes ending depending on case, gender, and whether there is an article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir essen afrikanische Gerichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We eat African dishes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wird aggressiv, wenn er Angst hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog becomes aggressive when it is scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist aggressive.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is aggressive.

definitions.note: comparative form of the adjective "aggressiv"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird aggressiver, wenn er müde ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He becomes more aggressive when he is tired.

definitions.note: used to show realization, understanding, or mild surprise; tone depends on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ah, jetzt verstehe ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ah, now I understand.

definitions.note: Used to show you understand or have realized something; can also sound skeptical depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aha, jetzt verstehe ich das Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aha, now I understand the problem.

definitions.note: Hesitation sound used when thinking or unsure; also commonly written as „ähm“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ahm, ich weiß nicht, ob ich heute Zeit habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Um, I don't know if I have time today.

definitions.note: Often used when you have a vague feeling or premonition about something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ahne, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suspect that something isn’t right.

definitions.note: Often used with a clause introduced by „dass“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ahnt, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suspects that something isn’t right.

definitions.note: Simple past of „ahnen“ (to suspect / have a hunch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ahnte, dass etwas nicht stimmte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suspected that something wasn’t right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war völlig ahnungslos und habe nichts gemerkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was completely clueless and didn’t notice anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bleibe auch im Winter aktiv.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stay active even in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seitdem sie jeden Tag spazieren geht, ist sie aktiver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since she goes for a walk every day, she is more active.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Funktion ist aktiviert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The feature is enabled.

definitions.note: Often used for software, apps, or information (e.g., to bring something up to date).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die App aktualisieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to update the app.

definitions.note: past participle of "aktualisieren"; also used like an adjective (e.g., "eine aktualisierte Version")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die App wurde gestern aktualisiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The app was updated yesterday.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a feminine noun (or before a plural noun in the definite article form, e.g. „die aktuellen …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die aktuelle Situation ist schwierig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The current situation is difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis ist akzeptabel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price is acceptable.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (I accept).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich akzeptiere deine Entschuldigung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accept your apology.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde deine Entscheidung akzeptieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will accept your decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er akzeptiert meine Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepts my decision.

definitions.note: Past participle, often used with "haben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Einladung akzeptiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accepted the invitation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er akzeptierte das Angebot sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepted the offer immediately.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie akzeptierten das Angebot sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accepted the offer immediately.

definitions.note: Used in Swiss German dialect writing; in Standard German this is usually „alle“ (or „all-“ in compounds like „Alltag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist al s Gleiche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s all the same.

definitions.note: Often used to describe childish or not-serious behavior or remarks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein alberner Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a silly joke.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective; here it’s the neuter form (e.g., with das).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte ein alkoholfreies Bier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a non-alcoholic beer.

definitions.note: Used before nouns, like "all the" / "all of the".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: All die Leute sind schon da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the people are already here.

definitions.note: Often used with plural nouns (like “all the …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle Kinder sind müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the children are tired.

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun referring to a whole group (people or things).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle sind schon da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone is already there.

definitions.note: Can also mean “only” in some contexts, but as an adjective it most often means being without other people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Abend allein zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm home alone tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Abend allein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m alone tonight.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something by itself is enough to cause an effect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allein der Gedanke daran macht mir Angst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just the thought of it scares me.

definitions.note: Often used adverbially (e.g., “ich bin alleine” = “I’m alone”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Abend alleine zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm home alone tonight.

definitions.note: Often interchangeable with "allein" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Abend alleine zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m home alone this evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das alleine machen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do that on your own?

definitions.note: Usually describes a person who is not in a relationship (not married/partnered).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist alleinstehend und wohnt in einer kleinen Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is single and lives in a small apartment.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed phrase "vor allem" (= above all, especially).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor allem brauche ich jetzt Ruhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Above all, I need peace and quiet now.

definitions.note: dative singular form (often used after prepositions like „mit“, „von“, „zu“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit allem, was du brauchst, können wir anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With everything you need, we can start.

definitions.note: dative singular form; used after some prepositions (e.g., „nach allem“) and with verbs that take the dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach allem, was passiert ist, sind wir froh, dass du da bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After everything that happened, we’re glad that you’re here.

definitions.note: dative form of „alles“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach allem, was passiert ist, brauche ich eine Pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After everything that happened, I need a break.

definitions.note: dative plural form of "alle" (used before plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe allen Kindern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help all the children.

definitions.note: dative plural form of „alle“ (used with plural nouns or to mean “everyone” in the dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe allen Kindern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help all (the) children.

definitions.note: Genitive plural form of the determiner „all“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das Ende aller Dinge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the end of all things.

definitions.note: Genitive plural form of "alle".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne die Namen aller Kinder in der Klasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the names of all the children in the class.

definitions.note: Used before a noun in the genitive plural (e.g., "aller Kinder").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aller guten Dinge sind drei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All good things come in threes.

definitions.note: Often used to add a contrasting point or limitation; can also mean “indeed” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich würde gern kommen, allerdings habe ich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'd like to come; however, I don't have time.

definitions.note: Used to strongly emphasize that something is the very first one; often used with possessives like „mein/dein…“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war mein allererstes Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was my very first car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin allergisch gegen Nüsse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am allergic to nuts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich reagiere allergisch auf Nüsse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I react allergically to nuts.

definitions.native: all sorts of, all kinds of
definitions.note: Often used before a noun to mean “a variety of” or “a lot of different”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat allerhand Ideen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has all kinds of ideas.

definitions.note: Used to express what you like/prefer best (often with verbs like „machen“, „gehen“, „essen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe allerliebsten mit meinen Freunden ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Most of all, I like going to the movies with my friends.

definitions.native: from all sides, on all sides
definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "von allerseits" (= from all sides) or "allerseits willkommen" (= welcome, everyone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bekomme von allerseits Unterstützung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get support from all sides.

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun/nominalized form meaning “everything” (not as a determiner before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alles ist gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is good.

definitions.note: Used for things/ideas (not people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alles ist gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alles ist gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is good.

definitions.note: Emphasizes that everyone/everything in a group is included; often used with plural nouns or pronouns like „wir/ihr/sie“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen allesamt nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re all going home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Smartphones sind heute fast überall allgegenwärtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smartphones are ubiquitous almost everywhere today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allgemein ist es hier im Winter sehr kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In general, it is very cold here in winter.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (e.g., „allgemeine Informationen“ = general information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben nur allgemeine Informationen über den Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We only have general information about the plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gott gilt in vielen Religionen als allmächtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In many religions, God is considered almighty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Allmählich wird es draußen dunkel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s gradually getting dark outside.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that something is more than desirable; often with adjectives/adverbs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist allzu kompliziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That's far too complicated.

definitions.note: Used to say what role, job, or function someone/something has ("as a …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich arbeite als Lehrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work as a teacher.

definitions.note: Used for past time clauses referring to a single point/period in the past (often with Präteritum); for repeated events or future meaning, German usually uses „wenn“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als ich nach Hause kam, hat es geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I got home, it rained.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned; in modern everyday German you usually say "bald".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme alsbald zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be back soon.

definitions.note: Often used at the start of a sentence meaning “well, then”. False friend: German “also” usually does NOT mean English “also” (= “too”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war müde, also bin ich nach Hause gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was tired, so I went home.

definitions.note: Often used as a discourse marker to start or resume a thought (similar to “so…” in English). Not the same as English “also” (= German „auch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Also, wir gehen jetzt nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Alright, we're going home now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy ist schon alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is already old.

definitions.note: Used as an attributive adjective before a masculine or neuter noun in certain cases (weak/mixed ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besuche meinen alten Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m visiting my old friend.

definitions.note: attributive form of the adjective (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besuche meinen alten Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m visiting my old friend.

definitions.note: Usually used with an article, e.g. "die Alten" (= the elderly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir helfen den Alten im Pflegeheim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We help the elderly people in the nursing home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Laptop ist schon alter als deiner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My laptop is already older than yours.

definitions.note: Informal slang (especially among young people); can sound rude depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alter, das ist ja mega cool!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dude, that’s really super cool!

definitions.note: Not the same as English “to alter” (= to change).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist normal, zu altern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s normal to age.

definitions.note: Used here as the declensed form of the adjective before a neuter noun (e.g., „ein altes Haus“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein altes Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an old house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Kleid sieht altmodisch aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress looks old-fashioned.

definitions.note: Used before superlatives: am + (adjective/adverb)-sten (e.g. am besten = best). Not the same as English “am”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde Mathe am schwierigsten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find math the hardest.

definitions.note: Contraction of "an dem" (dative, masculine/neuter). Often used for locations and for days/dates (e.g. "am Montag").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin am Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am at the train station.

definitions.note: Used at the end of a prayer or to express strong agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Und alle sagten: Amen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: And everyone said: Amen.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „american English“ or „american culture“; more common is the capitalized form „amerikanisch“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag american Music.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like American music.

definitions.note: adjective; inflected form of „amerikanisch“ (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich höre gern amerikanische Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like listening to American music.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak declension (e.g., after a definite article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag den amerikanischen Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the American movie.

definitions.note: masculine nominative singular form (also used after an indefinite article like "ein")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein amerikanischer Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an American movie.

definitions.note: adjective in neuter nominative/accusative singular (used with a neuter noun, often after an article like "ein")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern ein amerikanisches Frühstück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like an American breakfast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärzte müssen sein Bein amputieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors have to amputate his leg.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich amüsant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really amusing.

definitions.note: informal imperative form of „amüsieren“ (often used without the -e: „Amüsier dich!“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amüsier dich gut auf der Party!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have fun at the party!

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich amüsieren = to have fun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film wird dich sicher amüsieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie will surely amuse you.

definitions.note: Used with reflexive pronoun: sich amüsieren.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amüsierst du dich auf der Party?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you having fun at the party?

definitions.note: Often used with „sich“ (e.g., „sich amüsieren“ = to have fun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind amüsiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are amused.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war amüsiert über den Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was amused by the joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film amüsierte mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie amused me.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form; can be used transitively (amuse someone)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Clown und seine Tricks amüsierten die Kinder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The clown and his tricks amused the children.

definitions.note: often used reflexively with „sich“: „sich amüsieren“ = to have fun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir amüsierten uns auf der Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had fun at the party.

definitions.note: Used especially about devices, lights, etc. (opposite: „aus“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is on.

definitions.note: Preposition: uses dative for location (where?), accusative for direction (where to?).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Bild hängt an der Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The picture is hanging on the wall.

definitions.note: Used to say something (like a light, TV, or machine) is switched on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir analysieren die Daten gemeinsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We analyze the data together.

definitions.note: present tense form of "analysieren" (also the past participle "analyzed" in perfect tenses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie analysiert die Daten sehr genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She analyzes the data very carefully.

definitions.note: used for growing plants/crops (e.g., vegetables, grain)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen dieses Jahr Tomaten anbauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to grow tomatoes this year.

definitions.native: to add on (to a building), to build an extension
definitions.note: used for adding an extra part/room onto an existing building
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen an ihr Haus eine Garage anbauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to add a garage onto their house.

definitions.note: Often used for offering something to someone (food, help, a job, a deal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir meine Hilfe anbieten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can offer you my help.

definitions.native: to blow on, to blow at
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht die Kerzen anblasen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t blow on the candles.

definitions.note: Often used with things like a balloon or an air mattress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Ballon anblasen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to inflate the balloon.

definitions.native: to sound (a horn/trumpet), to blow (a signal)
definitions.note: Used for giving a signal with a horn, trumpet, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Musiker wird gleich das Signal anblasen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The musician is about to sound the signal.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „anbieten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er anbot mir seine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He offered me his help.

definitions.note: Often used in cooking when food sticks to the pot/pan and starts to burn.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, sonst kann die Milch anbrennen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful, or the milk might burn!

definitions.note: Rare in modern German; found mainly in older texts or fixed expressions. In everyday German, use “und”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kaufte Brot and Käse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She bought bread and cheese.

definitions.note: often suggests something happening all the time and can sound negative (like “nonstop”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm ist hier andauernd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise here is constant.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning “other people” (in German it’s normally capitalized as „Andere“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andere finden das nicht so wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Others don’t find that so important.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „ander“ (used before a noun, e.g. „eine andere …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme eine andere Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take a different jacket.

definitions.note: often used with a noun: andere Leute = other people
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte andere Schuhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like other shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know others.

definitions.note: Can be used as a pronoun meaning “the other ones” or “others.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die anderen sind schon da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The others are already there.

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun meaning “the other one(s)” or “others” (often with endings like an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme die andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take the other one.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter form of „ander“ (often used when the noun is implied, e.g. „mit anderem“ = “with something else”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit anderem habe ich nicht gerechnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t expect anything else.

definitions.note: This is a declined form of the noun “Andere” (meaning “other person/people”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe den anderen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help the others.

definitions.note: Form of the noun „der/die Andere“ (“the other (one)”). Often used in phrases like „mit den anderen“ (“with the others”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe mit den anderen ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the movies with the others.

definitions.note: Often used as a determiner before a noun (e.g., "die anderen" = "the others").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme den anderen Stuhl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll take the other chair.

definitions.note: declined form of "ander" (e.g., with plural or masculine/neuter dative/accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche mit anderen Leuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m talking with other people.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „die anderen“ (“the others”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche mit anderen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m talking with others.

definitions.note: Form of "andere" used with masculine/neuter dative singular or with plural in several cases (depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es den anderen gesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I told the others.

definitions.note: depends on context: can mean “other” (singular) or “others” (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme den anderen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take the other one.

definitions.note: adjective in masculine nominative singular (e.g. before a masculine noun like „ein anderer Mann“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein anderer Mann hat angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Another man called.

definitions.note: Pronoun form meaning “another/other one” (often used like an adjective before a noun, e.g. „ein anderer Tag“ = “another day”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme anderer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll take another one.

definitions.note: Used like an adjective/pronoun and changes form depending on gender and case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein anderer kommt später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Another one will come later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einerseits möchte ich sparen, andererseits will ich auch reisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the one hand I want to save money; on the other hand I also want to travel.

definitions.note: Neuter singular form of "ander"; often used as a pronoun (e.g. "etwas anderes").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte etwas anderes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want something else.

definitions.note: neuter form of "ander" used on its own as a pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte etwas anderes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want something else.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned; more common today: „ein anderes Mal“, „noch einmal“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm andermal wieder vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come by again another time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beeil dich, andernfalls verpassen wir den Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hurry up, otherwise we’ll miss the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute machen wir es anders.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re doing it differently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beeil dich, sonst ist es anders zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hurry up, otherwise it’ll be too late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mache es anders als du.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do it differently than you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Schlüssel anderswo gelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my keys somewhere else.

definitions.note: Used for quantities; often before a noun with a unit of time/measure (e.g., anderthalb Stunden).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir warten noch anderthalb Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re waiting another hour and a half.

definitions.native: next to each other, against each other
definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „stehen“, „liegen“, „stoßen“ or in phrases like „aneinander denken“ (= think of each other).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bücher stehen aneinander im Regal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are standing next to each other on the shelf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist als Expertin anerkannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is recognized as an expert.

definitions.note: Often used for officially accepting something as valid (e.g., a degree, a certificate, a government).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland wird das neue Zeugnis anerkennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany will recognize the new certificate.

definitions.note: Form of the separable verb "anfangen" used with the prefix attached (common in subordinate clauses, e.g. after "dass", "weil").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass ich morgen früher anfange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that I start earlier tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fangen um acht Uhr an, wenn wir anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We start at eight o’clock when we begin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anfangs war es schwer, aber dann wurde es leichter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At first it was hard, but then it got easier.

definitions.note: Often means touching with your hand; can be used as a command: „Nicht anfassen!“ = “Don’t touch!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht anfassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don't touch it.

definitions.note: Often used for physically touching or handling something; can also be used figuratively (e.g., starting to deal with a problem).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sag ihm, dass er das nicht anfasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell him not to touch that.

definitions.note: Often used for producing something (e.g., clothing, furniture, documents), especially custom-made or made to order.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schreiner wird den Tisch nach Maß anfertigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The carpenter will make the table to measure.

definitions.note: simple past of "anfangen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern anfing der Kurs um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday the course started at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used as a reflexive verb: sich mit jemandem anfreunden.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mich mit meinen neuen Nachbarn anfreunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to make friends with my new neighbors.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "anfangen" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wann anfängst du mit den Hausaufgaben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When do you start your homework?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs anfängt um neun Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course starts at nine o’clock.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich anfühlen“ = “to feel (like)” (e.g., „Es fühlt sich gut an.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß nicht, wie sich das anfühlt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know what that feels like.

definitions.note: past participle of „anbauen“, often used about crops/food
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tomaten werden in Spanien angebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tomatoes are grown in Spain.

definitions.note: past participle of „anbauen“, used for buildings/parts of a building
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: An das Haus ist ein Wintergarten angebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A conservatory has been added onto the house.

definitions.note: past participle of „anbellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat den Postboten angebellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barked at the mail carrier.

definitions.note: Often used for giving information on a form or in an official context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte geben Sie an, wie viele Personen kommen, und geben Sie auch an, ob jemand Vegetarier ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please indicate how many people are coming, and also indicate whether anyone is vegetarian.

definitions.note: Informal; often used negatively.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht immer, mit seinem neuen Auto anzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s always trying to show off with his new car.

definitions.note: Used to report something that is claimed but not confirmed (often with some doubt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat angeblich gestern gekündigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He allegedly quit yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es dir schon angeboten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already offered it to you.

definitions.note: Used for ships or spacecraft; also sometimes figuratively for “connected/plugged in.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff ist im Hafen angedockt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship is docked in the harbor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wurde auf dem Zebrastreifen angefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was hit at the crosswalk.

definitions.note: Often used for vehicles (bus, train, car) when they begin moving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus ist schon angefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus has already pulled away.

definitions.note: past participle of "anfangen"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern mit dem Lernen angefangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I started studying yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „anfassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bildschirm ist ganz fettig, weil ihn alle angefasst haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The screen is really greasy because everyone has touched it.

definitions.note: often used to describe someone’s mood (e.g. „beleidigt/empfindlich“) rather than physical touch
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war sehr angefasst, als er das gesagt hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was very upset when he said that.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “custom-made” (made to order).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schrank wurde nach Maß angefertigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cabinet was custom-made to measure.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" and "mit" + dative: "mit jemandem angefreundet sein".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit meiner Nachbarin angefreundet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m friends with my neighbor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte füllen Sie das Formular wie angegeben aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fill out the form as specified.

definitions.note: colloquial; used like an adjective to describe someone’s attitude
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wirkt manchmal ziemlich angegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sometimes seems pretty conceited.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt wurde angegriffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was attacked.

definitions.note: Past participle of "angucken"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "Ich habe ... angeguckt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir den Film gestern Abend angeguckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the movie last night.

definitions.note: past participle of „anhaben“, used with „haben“ to talk about what someone was wearing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern eine Jacke angehabt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I wore a jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus ist an der Haltestelle angehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stopped at the bus stop.

definitions.note: Often used when the police stop a driver/vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat das Auto angehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police pulled the car over.

definitions.note: Often used with an object: „etwas angehen“ = to start working on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten das Problem morgen angehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should tackle the problem tomorrow.

definitions.note: Also used in phrases like „Das geht mich nichts an“; with „angehen“ it often appears as „jdn. nichts angehen“ (= be none of someone’s business).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das geht dich nichts an, und es muss dich auch nicht angehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s none of your business, and it doesn’t have to concern you either.

definitions.native: to turn on (to switch on, to go on)
definitions.note: Used for lights/devices; commonly as „Das Licht geht an“, but also possible with „angehen“ in the sense of “to switch on/start up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich ist das Licht angegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly the light came on.

definitions.note: Often used with "haben" in the perfect tense; can also mean "signed on" (especially for a ship or a job).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat letzte Woche bei einer neuen Firma angeheuert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was hired at a new company last week.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like „was ... angeht“ (= as far as ... is concerned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was dich angeht, hast du völlig recht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As far as you’re concerned, you’re completely right.

definitions.note: Used for devices/lights when something switches on (e.g., „das Licht geht an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass das Licht gleich angeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the light turns on in a moment.

definitions.note: past participle of „anhängen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat … angehängt“) or like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Datei an die E-Mail angehängt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I attached the file to the email.

definitions.note: past participle of „anhören“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir das Lied angehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listened to the song.

definitions.note: Used mainly in legal/criminal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird wegen Betrugs angeklagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is charged with fraud.

definitions.note: past participle of "ankommen", typically used with "sein" (e.g., "ist/sind angekommen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind gut angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived safely.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert wurde letzte Woche angekündigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was announced last week.

definitions.note: Past participle of „anlangen“; commonly used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist angelangt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist pünktlich in Berlin angelangt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train arrived in Berlin on time.

definitions.note: past participle of „anlassen“; often used for starting a machine/engine or leaving something running
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Motor angelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I started the engine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Jacke angelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my jacket.

definitions.note: Used especially about money (e.g., savings) being invested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sein Geld sicher angelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He invested his money safely.

definitions.note: Usually means fishing with a rod and line (angling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Wochenende gehe ich mit meinem Vater angeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the weekend I go fishing with my father.

definitions.note: past participle of "anlügen" (used with "haben" in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich angelogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lied to me.

definitions.note: past participle, usually used with "haben" (e.g. "hat ... angelogen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich angelogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lied to me.

definitions.note: can also mean “to fish” in the sense of fishing with a rod/line
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er angelt am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fishes at the lake.

definitions.note: past participle of „anmachen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Licht angemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the light.

definitions.note: colloquial; past participle of „anmachen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ihn in der Bar angemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hit on him in the bar.

definitions.note: Often used for being registered for something (e.g., an event) or logged in (online).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch nicht angemeldet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not registered/logged in yet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Kleidung ist für die Feier angemessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your clothes are appropriate for the celebration.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about prices, pay, or behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir möchten einen angemessenen Preis zahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to pay a reasonable price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine angemessene Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an appropriate answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter ist heute angenehm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is pleasant today.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „sein“ (to be) or „finden“ (to find).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter ist heute sehr angenehm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is very pleasant today.

definitions.note: Used as a polite response when being introduced (often as part of “Angenehm, ich bin …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Angenehm, ich bin Laura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pleased to meet you, I'm Laura.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in front of a noun (e.g., with "eine", "die", etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten eine angenehme Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a pleasant trip.

definitions.note: inflected form used before a noun (attributive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünsche dir einen angenehmen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you a pleasant day.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „angenehm“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Hotel ist angenehmer als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This hotel is more pleasant than the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Angenommen, es regnet morgen, dann bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Assuming it rains tomorrow, then we’ll stay at home.

definitions.note: past participle of „annehmen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist angenommen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Antrag ist angenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your application has been accepted.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a hypothetical situation (often with a comma: „Angenommen, …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Angenommen, es regnet morgen, was machen wir dann?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Assuming it rains tomorrow, what will we do then?

definitions.note: often used when an authority (e.g., a boss, government, court) orders something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef hat eine Pause angeordnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss ordered a break.

definitions.note: past participle of „anpassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben den Plan an die neue Situation angepasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We adapted the plan to the new situation.

definitions.note: Often used for a table or food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist schon angerichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is already set.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about something bad you caused.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was hast du denn angerichtet?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What have you done?

definitions.note: past participle of "anrufen"; commonly used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich gestern angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called you yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle, usually used with "haben" (e.g., "Ich habe dich angerufen.")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich gestern Abend angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called you yesterday evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war von deiner Rede sehr angerührt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was very moved by your speech.

definitions.note: Used for food/liquids (e.g., stirring a sauce or batter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe ist schon angerührt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup has already been stirred.

definitions.note: Often used informally to describe something that is currently fashionable or popular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Bar ist gerade sehr angesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bar is very popular right now.

definitions.note: often used in a colloquial way to describe what’s currently “in” (people, places, music, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen heute in die angesagten Clubs der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re going to the trendy clubs in the city.

definitions.note: used more literally for something that has been officially announced or scheduled (e.g., an appointment or event)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den angesagten Termin morgen nicht wahrnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t make the scheduled appointment tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun: „sich (etwas) anschaffen“ = to buy/get oneself (something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir ein neues Handy angeschafft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought myself a new phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir den Film gestern Abend angeschaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the movie last night.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" to describe that something is connected (e.g., to electricity or the internet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Computer ist ans Internet angeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer is connected to the internet.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" (e.g. "Ich bin angeschnallt") and especially about seat belts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle Kinder sind im Auto angeschnallt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the children are buckled up in the car.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “shot and wounded/ hit by a bullet.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde am Bein angeschossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was shot in the leg.

definitions.note: Often used for writing to someone (e.g., by email or direct message).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe sie gestern angeschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I messaged her yesterday.

definitions.native: put on (someone’s) tab, charged to an account
definitions.note: Used when something is added to a bill/account instead of being paid immediately (common in restaurants/bars).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Getränke wurden auf mein Zimmer angeschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drinks were charged to my room.

definitions.note: past participle of "anschreien"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich vor allen Leuten angeschrien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouted at me in front of everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir den Film gestern angesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the movie yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal German; usually followed by the genitive case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Angesichts des schlechten Wetters bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Given the bad weather, we’re staying at home.

definitions.note: Often used for people (feeling tense) or situations/relationships (strained atmosphere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stimmung im Raum war angespannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The atmosphere in the room was tense.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wurde auf der Straße von einer Frau angesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was spoken to by a woman on the street.
