definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Problem wurde in der Sitzung angesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem was mentioned in the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ + dative: „jemanden mit etwas anstecken“ (to infect someone with something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich mit der Grippe angesteckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got infected with the flu.

definitions.note: Common with cigarettes/candles: „eine Zigarette / eine Kerze anstecken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat eine Zigarette angesteckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lit a cigarette.

definitions.note: often used to describe someone who works for an employer (not self-employed)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist bei einer Bank angestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is employed at a bank.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ or with „bei“ to say someone is employed (e.g. „bei einer Firma angestellt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist bei einer Bank angestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is employed at a bank.

definitions.note: Past participle of „sich anstrengen“ (to make an effort).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich wirklich angestrengt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really made an effort.

definitions.note: past participle of „anstreichen“ (to paint/apply paint, e.g., a wall)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wand ist schon angestrichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wall has already been painted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir eine Jacke angetan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on a jacket.

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the dative: „jemandem etwas antun“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was hast du ihm angetan?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What did you do to him?

definitions.note: Past participle of „antreten“; often used with a job, position, or term of office.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat heute seine neue Stelle angetreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He started his new job today.

definitions.note: past participle of „anwenden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Regel richtig angewendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I applied the rule correctly.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative: „auf etwas/jemanden angewiesen sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin auf deine Hilfe angewiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I depend on your help.

definitions.note: Very common in the pattern „auf + Akk. angewiesen sein“ (= to depend on something/someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin auf deine Hilfe angewiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I depend on your help.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative: „auf etwas/jemanden angewiesen sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin auf deine Hilfe angewiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dependent on your help.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively (e.g., traditions or habits that are deeply established).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Tradition ist hier seit Jahrhunderten angewurzelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tradition has been rooted here for centuries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin schon angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m already dressed.

definitions.note: Often used with „von“: „von jemandem angezogen“ = attracted to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fühlt sich von ihr angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels attracted to her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin schon angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m already dressed.

definitions.note: Often used with „von“ or „zu“ (e.g. „von dir angezogen“ / „zu dir angezogen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich von dir angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel attracted to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gut angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is well dressed.

definitions.note: Often used with "von" or "zu" (e.g., "von jemandem angezogen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fühlt sich von ihm angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels attracted to him.

definitions.note: past participle of "anzünden"; often used like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Kerze angezündet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lit the candle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wird den Postboten angreifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog will attack the mail carrier.

definitions.note: Describes someone who is eager to attack or start a conflict (in speech, sports, or behavior).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stürmer spielte heute sehr angriffslustig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The striker played very aggressively today.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often used with an object (e.g., "etwas angucken") or reflexively in the sense of "have a look" (e.g., "sich etwas angucken").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guck dir mal das Bild angucken!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a look at the picture!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte heute etwas Bequemes anhaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to wear something comfortable today.

definitions.native: have on, have switched on (a light/device)
definitions.note: Often used with things like lights: „das Licht anhaben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du beim Lesen das Licht anhaben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you have the light on while reading?

definitions.native: to stop (e.g., a vehicle); to pull over
definitions.note: Commonly used for vehicles or to tell someone (esp. a driver) to stop; separable verb in many tenses (e.g., „hält an“), but the example uses the infinitive exactly as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist fordert den Fahrer auf, sofort anzuhalten, aber er will nicht anhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer tells the driver to stop immediately, but he doesn’t want to stop.

definitions.note: Also used for processes or events that stop temporarily or permanently (e.g., negotiations, bleeding).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt sagt, dass die Blutung bald anhalten sollte, und hofft, dass sie wirklich anhalten wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor says the bleeding should stop soon and hopes that it really will stop.

definitions.note: Intransitive meaning: something continues for a certain time (e.g., rain, pain, cold).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Regen kann noch mehrere Stunden anhalten, und leider wird auch der Wind anhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain may continue for several more hours, and unfortunately the wind will continue too.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive; in everyday German often also with dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anhand der Fotos kann ich mich gut erinnern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Based on the photos, I can remember well.

definitions.note: Often written as one word in subordinate clauses (e.g. „… weil er eine Jacke anhat“). In main clauses it’s typically split: „Er hat eine Jacke an.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe, dass er heute eine rote Jacke anhat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see that he’s wearing a red jacket today.

definitions.note: simple past of "anhaben" (to wear, to have on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er anhatte eine Jacke, obwohl es warm war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was wearing a jacket even though it was warm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Kiste bitte anheben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please lift the box?

definitions.note: Common for attaching a file to an email; also for adding something at the end (e.g., a document or note).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Datei an die E-Mail anhängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will attach the file to the email.

definitions.native: to listen to (something); to hear (something) out
definitions.note: Separable verb; commonly used reflexively in the dative (sich etwas anhören) and often places the prefix at the end in finite clauses (e.g., „Ich höre mir … an.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mir das Lied anhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will listen to the song.

definitions.note: simple past of "ankommen" (ich/er/sie/es kam an → e.g., ich/er/sie/es ankam in subordinate clauses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war erleichtert, als ich endlich in Berlin ankam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was relieved when I finally arrived in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "ankommen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir ankamen spät am Abend am Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived late in the evening at the train station.

definitions.note: Often used with „bei“ + dative for arriving at someone’s place (e.g., „bei mir ankommen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug wird um 18 Uhr ankommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will arrive at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wann ankommst du am Bahnhof?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When do you arrive at the train station?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug kommt um 18 Uhr ankommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train arrives at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Used in the phrase „es kommt auf … an“ (“it depends on …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ankommt darauf an, wie viel Zeit wir haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It depends on how much time we have.

definitions.note: Often used for putting on something specific like a coat, a suit, or gloves.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch meine Jacke anlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to put on my jacket.

definitions.note: Used especially for investing money.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will ihr Geld sicher anlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to invest her money safely.

definitions.note: Often used for creating something planned, like a garden, a file, or a list.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir möchten einen kleinen Garten anlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like to create a small garden.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (jemanden anlügen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum willst du mich anlügen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you want to lie to me?

definitions.note: Commonly used for turning on lights, devices, or a stove.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Licht anmachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn on the light?

definitions.note: Informal; used when someone starts flirting with someone else, often in a forward way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum musst du sie sofort anmachen, wenn wir in einer Bar sind?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you have to hit on her right away when we’re in a bar?

definitions.note: Often used for adding a short comment or correction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dazu noch etwas anmerken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to remark something about that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis ist annehmbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price is acceptable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Angebot annehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will accept the offer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme an, dass er später kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assume that he’ll come later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er annimmt das Angebot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepts the offer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie annimmt, dass der Zug pünktlich ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She assumes that the train is on time.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., reservations, tickets, contracts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meine Reservierung annullieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to cancel my reservation.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can also mean “cancels” (present tense form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Flug wurde annulliert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flight was cancelled.

definitions.note: often used for attaching something to something else (e.g., a button, patch, or label)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Knopf wieder annähen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to sew the button on again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt annähernd 200 Besucher pro Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are approximately 200 visitors per day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hinweis war anonym.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tip was anonymous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man kann hier anonym bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can remain anonymous here.

definitions.native: to tackle, to get started (on something)
definitions.note: Often used for starting a task with energy and determination.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Problem endlich anpacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finally have to tackle the problem.

definitions.note: Used for physically taking hold of something (often with your hands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Kisten anpacken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please pick up the boxes?

definitions.note: Often used with “an” + accusative: sich an etwas anpassen = to adapt to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Plan anpassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to adjust the plan.

definitions.note: Used especially for trying on clothes or shoes in a shop or at home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte die Jacke anprobieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to try on the jacket.

definitions.note: Past participle of "anprobieren" (to try on, e.g., clothes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Jacke schon anprobiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already tried on the jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer will die Diskussion im Unterricht anregen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher wants to stimulate the discussion in class.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like „etwas anregen“ (= to propose an idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte anregen, dass wir früher anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to suggest that we start earlier.

definitions.note: Often used in cooking for arranging food nicely on a plate before serving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Salat noch anrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to arrange/serve the salad.

definitions.note: Very common with „Schaden“ (to cause damage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Sturm kann großen Schaden anrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A storm can cause major damage.

definitions.note: Simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of "anrufen" (to call someone on the phone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern anrief ich meine Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I called my mother.

definitions.note: Present tense (ich): “I call” / “I’m calling” (subjunctive I “I would call” is also possible depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich anrufe dich später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich heute Abend anrufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will call you this evening.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "anrufen" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum anrufst du mich nicht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you call me?

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of „anrufen“ (separable verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er anruft mich später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He calls me later.

definitions.note: often used in cooking (e.g., mixing a sauce or batter)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rühr die Soße kurz an, indem du sie vorsichtig anrührst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stir the sauce briefly by gently stirring it.

definitions.note: often used in the negative: etwas nicht anrühren = not to touch something (including food)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte anrühren Sie das nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t touch that.

definitions.note: Contraction of „an das“ (used with neuter singular „das“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe ans Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the window.

definitions.note: simple past of „ansehen“; often used in subordinate clauses (in main clauses: „sah … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde rot, weil sie ihn so lange ansah.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned red because she looked at him for so long.

definitions.note: Often used for buying/acquiring something (especially something bigger or more permanent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen uns ein neues Auto anschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to buy/get a new car.

definitions.native: to do sex work (as a prostitute)
definitions.note: Colloquial and vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie geht nachts anschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She does sex work at night.

definitions.note: Often used with an accusative object (jemanden/etwas anschauen). Commonly appears as separable verb forms in finite clauses (e.g., schaue … an), but here the example uses the exact word “anschauen” as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mir den Film heute Abend anschauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to watch the movie tonight.

definitions.note: Often used when something seems to be true based on what you know or have heard, but you’re not 100% sure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anscheinend hat der Zug Verspätung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently the train is delayed.

definitions.note: Often used when something seems true based on what you see/hear, but you’re not completely sure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat anscheinend den Zug verpasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently he missed the train.

definitions.note: Often used to say something seems to be true based on what you know, without being completely certain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat anscheinend den Termin vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently he forgot the appointment.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like a device or cable (e.g., „das Gerät anschließen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Kabel bitte anschließen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you connect (plug in) the cable, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir essen jetzt, und anschließend gehen wir spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re eating now, and afterwards we’re going for a walk.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anschließen“; in main clauses it’s often split (e.g. „Er schließt den Drucker an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, dass er den Drucker anschließt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that he’s connecting (plugging in) the printer.

definitions.native: to fasten (a seat belt), to buckle up
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich anschnallen = to buckle up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte anschnallen im Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please buckle up in the car.

definitions.native: to yell at, to shout at
definitions.note: Stronger than just „rufen/schreien“; usually implies anger or scolding.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schrei mich nicht an, sondern hör mir einfach zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don't yell at me; just listen to me.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ansehen“; this form is used when the prefix is attached (e.g., in subordinate clauses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass ich mir den Film heute Abend ansehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that I watch the movie tonight.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (Akkusativ) or reflexively in the pattern: sich etwas ansehen = to have a look at/watch something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mir heute Abend den Film ansehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to watch the movie tonight.

definitions.note: Used to express how someone is viewed or judged (often with „als“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Leute ansehen ihn als Experten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people regard him as an expert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meine Brille ansetzen, um das zu lesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to put on my glasses to read that.

definitions.note: Often used when someone begins a speech or starts to do something: „zu einer Rede ansetzen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wollte etwas sagen und wollte zu einer Erklärung ansetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to say something and wanted to begin an explanation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verkäufer will einen hohen Preis ansetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The seller wants to set a high price.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present of „ansehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum ansiehst du mich so lange?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you looking at me for so long?

definitions.note: Often used in subordinate clauses where the separable prefix stays attached (e.g., „…, dass er mich ansieht.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich merke, dass er mich ansieht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I notice that he is looking at me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute keine Zeit; ansonsten helfe ich dir gern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have time today; otherwise I'd be happy to help you.

definitions.note: Often used for approaching someone directly (e.g., to start a conversation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte ihn kurz ansprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to speak to him briefly.

definitions.note: Used when introducing a topic or issue in conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten das Problem im Meeting ansprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should bring up the problem in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich frage mich, warum er mich so anstarrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wonder why he’s staring at me like that.

definitions.note: Often used with “statt” as “anstatt/statt” + genitive or “von” + dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anstatt Kaffee trinke ich heute Tee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Instead of coffee, I'm drinking tea today.

definitions.note: Often used with a following clause as "anstatt dass" (instead of + verb clause), or with "zu" + infinitive as "anstatt zu" (instead of doing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anstatt dass er anruft, schreibt er eine Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Instead of calling, he writes a message.

definitions.note: Used both literally (illness) and figuratively (e.g., laughter, enthusiasm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Grippe ist sehr ansteckend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flu is very contagious.

definitions.note: Usually used with the genitive (often with dative in spoken German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anstelle eines Autos fährt er mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Instead of a car, he rides his bike to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma will nächste Woche zwei neue Mitarbeitende anstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to hire two new employees next week.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich anstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen uns an der Kasse anstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to line up at the checkout.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „anstellen“; also used in questions/conditionals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum anstellst du ihn nicht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you hire him?

definitions.note: In everyday speech, „anmachen/anschalten“ is also common; here „anstellen“ means to start/turn on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anstellst du bitte den Motor an?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please start the engine?

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ (+ dative) and/or „auf“ (+ accusative): „mit jemandem anstoßen“, „auf etwas anstoßen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wollen wir auf deinen Geburtstag anstoßen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do we want to toast to your birthday?

definitions.native: to bump into, to knock against
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, dass du nicht an den Tisch anstoßen musst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful so you don’t have to bump into the table.

definitions.note: Often used for painting walls, doors, fences, etc. (applying a coat of paint).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Wand heute noch anstreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to paint the wall today.

definitions.native: to make an effort, to try hard
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich anstrengen = to make an effort / try hard.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst dich anstrengen, wenn du die Prüfung bestehen willst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to make an effort if you want to pass the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wanderung war anstrengend, aber schön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hike was tiring, but beautiful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hatte einen anstrengenden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had an exhausting day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein anständiger Mensch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a decent person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich anständig bei ihr entschuldigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He apologized to her properly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine anständige Person.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a decent person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sucht einen anständigen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is looking for a decent job.

definitions.note: Comparative form: „anständiger“ = “more decent/respectable.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist heute anständiger als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is more decent today than yesterday.

definitions.note: adjective used in the neuter form (e.g., with a neuter noun like "ein anständiges ...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sucht ein anständiges Hotel in der Nähe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s looking for a decent hotel nearby.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with feminine nouns (or plural with no article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine antike Vase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an antique vase.

definitions.note: Often used for things from ancient times (e.g., Greece/Rome) or very old historical objects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besichtigen die antiken Ruinen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are visiting the ancient ruins.

definitions.native: to start (a job/position), to take up
definitions.note: Often used for starting a new job, position, or office; separable verb (finite forms split: „tritt … an“), but the infinitive is „antreten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird morgen ihre neue Stelle antreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will start her new job tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object and a person in the dative: „jemandem etwas antun“ (to do something to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dir nichts antun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to do anything to you.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I") of "antworten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich antworte dir später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll answer you later.

definitions.note: Often used with the preposition „auf“ + accusative: „auf eine Frage antworten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte auf meine E-Mail antworten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please reply to my email?

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form of "antworten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum antwortest du nicht auf meine Nachricht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why aren't you answering my message?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "antworten" (he/she/it answers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er antwortet nicht auf meine E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t reply to my email.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „antworten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er antwortete sofort auf meine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He answered my question right away.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (the person you entrust something to) and an accusative object (the thing/secret you entrust).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vertraue dir mein Geheimnis an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entrust you with my secret.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat mir ihr Geheimnis anvertraut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She entrusted me with her secret.

definitions.note: Often used for applying a method, rule, or technique (e.g. in a formal or practical context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst diese Methode in der Praxis anwenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can apply this method in practice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei der Besprechung waren alle Mitarbeitenden anwesend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the employees were present at the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich begrüße die anwesenden Gäste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I greet the guests who are present.

definitions.note: Often used for what a screen/device shows (e.g., a phone, clock, computer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Handy kann die Uhrzeit anzeigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone can display the time.

definitions.note: Used especially for officially reporting a person or a crime.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird den Diebstahl bei der Polizei anzeigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will report the theft to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich schnell anziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get dressed quickly.

definitions.note: Often used for attracting attention or drawing something toward something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das neue Schaufenster soll viele Kunden anziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new shop window display is supposed to attract many customers.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) present tense of „anziehen“; separable verb, often appears split as „ziehst … an“ or as one word „anziehst“ in subordinate clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum glaubst du, dass du heute keinen Mantel anziehst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you think you’re not putting on a coat today?

definitions.note: Infinitive with “zu” (e.g., after certain verbs like „versuchen“, „planen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, dir meine Hilfe anzubieten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to offer you my help.

definitions.native: to dock, to connect (to a docking station)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff versucht, anzudocken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship is trying to dock.

definitions.note: infinitive with „zu“ (used after certain verbs or in constructions like „um … zu“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, pünktlich anzufangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to start on time.

definitions.native: to touch; to handle; to pick up (with the hands)
definitions.note: Infinitive with „zu“ (e.g., „zu versuchen, es anzufassen“). In the perfect tense the verb is „anfassen“: „Ich habe es angefasst.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versuch bitte nicht, die heiße Pfanne anzufassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t try to touch the hot pan.

definitions.note: often used when giving information (e.g., on a form or in instructions)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte vergessen Sie nicht, Ihre Adresse anzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t forget to provide your address.

definitions.note: informal; can sound negative (like bragging)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht immer, mit seinem neuen Auto anzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s always trying to show off with his new car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund versucht, den Postboten anzugreifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog tries to attack the mail carrier.

definitions.note: Often used for vehicles; also used with the meaning “to stop (someone)” (e.g., by the police).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist fordert den Fahrer auf, anzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer tells the driver to pull over.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used after modal verbs, to express purpose, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit, mir das jetzt anzuhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time to listen to that right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte anzuklopfen, bevor du reinkommst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please knock before you come in?

definitions.note: Infinitive with „zu“ (e.g., after certain verbs); main verb is separable „ankommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, pünktlich anzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to arrive on time.

definitions.note: Infinitive with "zu" (e.g., "jemanden anzulügen"). Finite forms include: "du lügst ... an", "er/sie lügt ... an".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast versucht, mich anzulügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You tried to lie to me.

definitions.note: Often used with “Ich habe anzunehmen, …” meaning “I assume …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe anzunehmen, dass der Zug pünktlich ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assume that the train is on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hoffen, das Angebot anzunehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hope to accept the offer.

definitions.note: often used with „sich“ (sich anpassen = to adapt oneself) or with „an“ + accusative (an etwas anpassen = to adapt/adjust something to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, den Plan an die neue Situation anzupassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re trying to adapt the plan to the new situation.

definitions.note: Infinitive with "zu" (used after certain verbs like "versuchen" or after "um ... zu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, dich später anzurufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to call you later.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of "anschauen" (often used after modal verbs or as "um ... zu" / with "haben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vor, mir den Film heute Abend anzuschauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planning to watch the movie tonight.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „anschließen“, often used after another verb (e.g., „versuchen“, „vergessen“, „bitten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, das Ladegerät anzuschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to plug in the charger.

definitions.native: to yell at, to shout at
definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „anschreien“, often used with modal verbs or after certain verbs (e.g. „versuchen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte hör auf, mich anzuschreien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stop yelling at me.

definitions.note: This is the "zu" infinitive form of „ansehen“ (used after certain verbs like „versuchen“, „vergessen“, or with „haben/sein“ + zu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mir den Film anzusehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to watch the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, den Lehrer nach dem Unterricht anzusprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to talk to the teacher after class.

definitions.native: to bring up, to mention (a topic)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist wichtig, das Problem früh anzusprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to bring up the problem early.

definitions.note: Often implies staring in an impolite or uncomfortable way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf, mich so anzustarren!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop staring at me like that!

definitions.note: Often used with the idea of officially starting/setting off or reporting for duty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe morgen früh anzutreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to start/report for duty early tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: to compete, to run (in an election)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hofft, bei der nächsten Wahl erneut anzutreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hopes to run again in the next election.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like threatening or causing harm: „jemandem etwas antun“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drohte, ihr etwas anzutun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threatened to do something to her.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich anziehen“ = to get dressed / to put clothes on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mich warm anzuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to dress warmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma wirbt online, um neue Kunden anzuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company advertises online to attract new customers.

definitions.note: Often used for lighting a cigarette, candle, or fire.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Kerze anzünden?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please light the candle?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Publikum applaudiert laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauds loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Publikum hat lange applaudiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauded for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used in a slightly formal tone, especially in phrases like „apropos + Genitiv“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apropos des Meetings: Wann beginnt es?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: About the meeting: When does it start?

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a related topic or thought; also common in the phrase “Apropos …” (“Speaking of …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apropos, hast du morgen Zeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By the way, do you have time tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann kein Arabisch sprechen, aber ich lerne arabisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't speak any Arabic, but I'm learning Arabic.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich arbeite heute von zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work from home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute lange arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to work late today.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du) form of "arbeiten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du arbeitest heute sehr viel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You work a lot today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „arbeiten“ (er/sie/es arbeitet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er arbeitet heute von zu Hause aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works from home today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „arbeiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr arbeitete ich in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I worked in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „arbeiten“; used especially in writing and formal speech
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzte Woche arbeiteten wir jeden Tag bis spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last week we worked every day until late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Kündigung war er drei Monate arbeitslos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the dismissal, he was unemployed for three months.

definitions.note: Often used in a more formal sense: to present reasons or arguments (e.g., in a discussion or essay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir argumentieren darüber, welche Lösung am besten ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We argue about which solution is best.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sah mich argwöhnisch an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked at me suspiciously.

definitions.note: Not related to the English noun “arm” (body part).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Familie ist arm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family is poor.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun to mean “poor/pitiable” (expressing sympathy), not “poor” in the sense of “not rich.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der arme Mann hat sein Handy verloren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poor man lost his phone.

definitions.note: Not related to the English word “arm” (body part).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir helfen den armen Kindern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We help the poor children.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a masculine singular noun (e.g., „ein armer Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein armer Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a poor man.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with neuter singular nouns (e.g., „ein armes Kind“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein armes Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a poor child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war ein armseliger Versuch, die Situation zu retten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a pathetic attempt to save the situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Treffen für morgen arrangieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you arrange the meeting for tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe alles für die Party arrangiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arranged everything for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wirkt oft arrogant, obwohl er es nicht böse meint.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often seems arrogant, even though he doesn’t mean it badly.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar; used for emphasis (like “fucking freezing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es draußen arschkalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s freezing cold outside today.

definitions.note: Often used about children; in everyday speech commonly with “brav” (e.g., “Sei artig!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei artig und hör deiner Mutter zu!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be good and listen to your mother!

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (declined).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich koche heute asiatische Nudeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm cooking Asian noodles today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aussicht vom Berg ist atemberaubend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view from the mountain is breathtaking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aussicht ist atemberaubend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view is breathtaking.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I breathe") or imperative informal singular ("breathe!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich atme tief durch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a deep breath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte atmen Sie tief durch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take a deep breath.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du atmest tief ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You breathe in deeply.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund atmet schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog breathes quickly.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „atmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Lauf atmete er tief durch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run, he took a deep breath.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund attackiert den Briefträger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog attacks the mail carrier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Angebot ist sehr attraktiv.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The offer is very attractive.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine nouns (e.g., "eine attraktive Frau") or with plural nouns without an article (e.g., "attraktive Angebote")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine attraktive Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an attractive idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen attraktiven Mantel gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought an attractive coat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Kleid ist attraktiver als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is more attractive than the other one.

definitions.note: used as an exclamation of pain (sometimes also sudden surprise)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Au, das tut weh!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ouch, that hurts!

definitions.note: Exclamation used when you feel sudden pain (often said by children, but used by adults too).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aua, das tut weh!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ow, that hurts!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme auch morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm coming tomorrow too.

definitions.note: Often used colloquially instead of „offen“, especially with doors/windows (e.g., „Die Tür ist auf.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is open.

definitions.note: A two-way preposition: with dative for location (on), with accusative for movement/direction (onto).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Handy liegt auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is on the table.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to express movement or position upward (e.g., „aufstehen“, „nach oben schauen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schau bitte auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please look up!

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to urge someone to start or hurry (often repeated: „Auf, auf!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf, wir müssen los!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, we have to go!

definitions.note: Often used as a separable verb particle (e.g., in commands like „Steh auf!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Steh auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stand up!

definitions.note: Often used for building something physically or building something up step by step (e.g., a business, a relationship, confidence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen ein neues Unternehmen aufbauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to build up a new company.

definitions.native: to get open, to manage to open
definitions.note: Used when something is difficult to open (e.g., a jar, bottle, or door).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das Glas nicht aufbekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t get the jar open.

definitions.native: to keep; to store; to keep safe (for later use)
definitions.note: Used for keeping something in a safe/place for later use (e.g., food, documents, valuables).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die wichtigen Dokumente im Safe aufbewahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to keep the important documents in the safe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die wichtigen Dokumente im Safe aufbewahrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kept the important documents in the safe.

definitions.native: to set off, to leave (to start a trip)
definitions.note: Often used for departing on a journey or starting out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden morgen früh aufbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will set off early tomorrow.

definitions.native: to raise, to come up with (money)
definitions.note: Often used for getting the money or resources needed for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen 200 Euro aufbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to come up with 200 euros.

definitions.note: Often used for causing someone to get angry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So eine Bemerkung kann ihn schnell aufbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A remark like that can upset him quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verkäufer war sehr aufdringlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salesman was very pushy.

definitions.native: on each other, on one another
definitions.note: Often used with verbs like liegen/stehen/sitzen (to be positioned) or warten (to wait) to describe people or things being stacked/placed one on top of the other.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bücher liegen aufeinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are lying on top of each other.

definitions.note: Used especially in religious contexts (e.g., Easter) for coming back to life after death.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach drei Tagen soll er von den Toten auferstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After three days, he is said to rise from the dead.

definitions.note: Often used when you finish everything on your plate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte aufessen: Iss dein Gemüse aufessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please eat up your vegetables!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht auffallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to stand out.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative pronoun (e.g., mir, dir).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein kleiner Fehler kann mir sofort auffallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A small mistake can catch my attention right away.

definitions.native: to ask (someone) to do (something), to request (someone) to do (something)
definitions.note: Often used for fairly direct or formal requests (e.g., by an authority).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer fordert die Schüler auf, leise zu sein, und er wird sie erneut auffordern, wenn es weiter laut ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher asks the students to be quiet, and he will ask them again if it stays loud.

definitions.note: Often used for refreshing knowledge or memory (e.g., before an exam).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mein Deutsch vor der Prüfung auffrischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to refresh my German before the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein neues Tattoo ist sehr auffällig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His new tattoo is very noticeable.

definitions.note: Often used when something seems unusual in a way that makes you suspect a problem or wrongdoing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei fand sein Verhalten auffällig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found his behavior suspicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben das Zelt schnell aufgebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We set up the tent quickly.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive I / present (rare outside subordinate clauses) of „aufgeben“: „ich aufgebe“. Commonly used after conjunctions like „dass“, „bevor“, „ohne dass“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass ich nicht aufgebe, auch wenn es schwer ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that I don’t give up, even if it’s hard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht aufgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to give up.

definitions.note: Often used for sending something at the post office.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Brief aufgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to mail the letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern bis zwei Uhr aufgeblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed up until two o’clock yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective to describe someone’s mood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum bist du so aufgebracht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you so upset?

definitions.note: Used for managing to collect or produce something (often money, time, or courage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben genug Geld aufgebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We raised enough money.

definitions.note: often used to describe someone who is annoyed or worked up about something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war sehr aufgebracht, weil der Zug schon wieder verspätet war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was very upset because the train was delayed again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Geld schon aufgebraucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already used up the money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ganze Papier ist schon aufgebraucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the paper is already used up.

definitions.note: Used with sein when it means starting a journey.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind früh aufgebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We set off early.

definitions.note: Often used about doors, locks, etc.; typically with haben or in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür war aufgebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door had been forced open.

definitions.note: Often used for things like the volume, a stove, or a tap/faucet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Musik nicht so laut machen? Du hast sie viel zu laut aufgedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you not make the music so loud? You turned it up way too loud.

definitions.note: Colloquial; describes someone who is very energetic and can’t sit still.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind heute total aufgedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are totally hyper today.

definitions.note: Often used with dative: „jemandem ist etwas aufgefallen“ = “someone noticed something” (literally: “something stood out to someone”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mir sofort aufgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed that immediately.

definitions.note: Past participle of „auffordern“, often used in the passive (e.g., „wurde aufgefordert“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wurde aufgefordert, meinen Ausweis zu zeigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was asked to show my ID.

definitions.note: Often used for animals (or figuratively) in the sense of eating something completely.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat das ganze Fleisch aufgefressen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog devoured all the meat.

definitions.note: past participle of "auffinden"; often used in passive or with "haben" in perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel wurde im Garten aufgefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key was found in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used about plays, operas, or music being put on stage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Stück wurde im Theater aufgeführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The play was performed at the theater.

definitions.note: Often used for items in a list, program, or document.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle Zutaten sind auf der Verpackung aufgeführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All ingredients are listed on the package.

definitions.note: often used with doors/windows or things that open by themselves
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist plötzlich aufgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door suddenly opened.

definitions.note: commonly used with the sun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne ist um sechs Uhr aufgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun rose at six o’clock.

definitions.note: used for plans or ideas that succeed
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück ist unser Plan aufgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, our plan worked out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht aufgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t give up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Brief gestern aufgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mailed the letter yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "aufessen"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Teller schon aufgegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already finished my plate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wurde im Stau aufgehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was delayed by traffic.

definitions.note: Often used intransitively for doors, windows, etc. (i.e., they open).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür will nicht aufgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door won’t open.

definitions.note: Commonly used for the sun (and sometimes the moon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir stehen früh auf, um die Sonne aufgehen zu sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We get up early to see the sun rise.

definitions.note: Past participle of „aufheben“ (often used with „haben“ in the Perfekt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Papier vom Boden aufgehoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked up the paper from the floor.

definitions.note: Often used to mean an event/appointment is canceled: „Der Termin ist aufgehoben.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Termin ist aufgehoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The appointment is canceled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür aufgeht um 8 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door opens at 8 o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used for the sun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne aufgeht um 6 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun rises at 6 o’clock.

definitions.note: past participle of „aufhängen“ (e.g., with „haben“ in the perfect tense, or in the passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Bild an die Wand aufgehängt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hung the picture on the wall.

definitions.note: Past participle of "aufhören"; often used with "haben" to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe aufgehört zu rauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stopped smoking.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used when something is hard to open.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Flasche nicht aufgekriegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn't get the bottle open.

definitions.note: Commonly used about ending a phone call (Partizip II of „auflegen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat plötzlich aufgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suddenly hung up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zucker ist im Wasser aufgelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sugar is dissolved in the water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verein wurde aufgelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The club was disbanded.

definitions.note: Often used for mysteries or unclear situations becoming clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fall ist endlich aufgelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The case has finally been solved.

definitions.note: past participle of „aufmachen“; used with „haben“ or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Tür aufgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I opened the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Gespräch aufgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recorded the conversation.

definitions.note: Often used with places/institutions (e.g., a hospital) in the passive: „wurde aufgenommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde ins Krankenhaus aufgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was admitted to the hospital.

definitions.note: Often used as an interjection/command meaning “Pay attention!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aufgepasst, der Zug kommt gleich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, the train is coming any moment!

definitions.note: Older spelling of „aufgepasst“ (now usually spelled with ss).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe im Unterricht gut aufgepaßt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I paid close attention in class.

definitions.note: Often used for being nervously excited (e.g., before an exam or event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor der Prüfung bin ich sehr aufgeregt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before the exam, I’m very nervous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tüte ist aufgerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bag is torn open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt hat den nächsten Patienten aufgerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor called in the next patient.

definitions.note: Used especially for opening or retrieving something (e.g., a file or webpage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Datei aufgerufen und gespeichert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I opened the file and saved it.

definitions.note: Often used for rooms/homes (clean and in order).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Küche ist endlich wieder aufgeräumt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is finally tidy again.

definitions.note: Describes someone’s mood or demeanor.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute wirkt er sehr aufgeräumt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today he seems very cheerful.

definitions.note: Past participle of „aufräumen“; often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Zimmer aufgeräumt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tidied up my room.

definitions.note: Often used for books, notebooks, or pages (past participle of „aufschlagen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch aufgeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I opened the book.

definitions.note: Often used with cream or egg whites (past participle of „aufschlagen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sahne ist schon aufgeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cream is already whipped.

definitions.note: Often used for something cut open with a knife (can sound graphic/violent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sack war aufgeschlitzt, und das Mehl lag überall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bag had been slit open, and the flour was everywhere.

definitions.note: Often used about a person’s attitude toward new ideas, people, or experiences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr aufgeschlossen und probiert gern neue Dinge aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very open-minded and likes trying new things.

definitions.note: Past participle of „aufschließen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Tür aufgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I unlocked the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe deine Telefonnummer aufgeschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down your phone number.

definitions.native: put on (e.g., a hat), placed on
definitions.note: Often used for putting something on your head (hat, cap, headphones).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Mütze aufgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my cap.

definitions.note: Past participle of „aufstehen“; often used with „sein“ to say someone has gotten up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin schon aufgestanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m already up (out of bed).

definitions.note: past participle of „aufstehen“, usually used with „sein“ in the perfect tense (e.g. „ich bin aufgestanden“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin um sieben Uhr aufgestanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got up at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: past participle of „aufstellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die Stühle im Garten aufgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We set up the chairs in the garden.

definitions.note: past participle of „aufsteigen“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense (e.g. „ist aufgestiegen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist auf den Berg aufgestiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbed up the mountain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Verdächtigen in seiner Wohnung aufgesucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police sought out the suspect at his apartment.

definitions.note: Past participle of „auftauchen“; often used with „sein“ in the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich ist er wieder aufgetaucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly he showed up again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gruppe wurde in drei Teams aufgeteilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The group was divided into three teams.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Creme dünn aufgetragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I applied the cream thinly.

definitions.note: Used with a person as the indirect object (e.g., jemandem eine Aufgabe auftragen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef hat mir eine schwierige Aufgabe aufgetragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss assigned me a difficult task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen wurde pünktlich aufgetragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was served on time.

definitions.note: past participle of "auftreten"; often used with "sein" (e.g., "ist aufgetreten")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Problem ist gestern zum ersten Mal aufgetreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem occurred for the first time yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "auftreten"; often used with "sein" for public appearances (e.g., on stage, on TV)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Band ist gestern Abend in Berlin aufgetreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The band performed in Berlin last night.

definitions.note: past participle of „aufwachsen“, usually used with „sein“ (e.g. „ich bin … aufgewachsen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in Berlin aufgewachsen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grew up in Berlin.

definitions.note: past participle of „aufwachen“; used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute sehr früh aufgewacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up very early today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm hat mich aufgeweckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise woke me up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Suppe aufgewärmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reheated the soup.

definitions.note: Often used for being emotionally unsettled or agitated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Streit war sie sehr aufgewühlt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the argument, she was very upset.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gespräch wurde aufgezeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conversation was recorded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe seine Telefonnummer aufgezeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down his phone number.

definitions.note: Often used about raising children (e.g., Kinder aufziehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ihre Kinder allein aufgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She raised her children on her own.

definitions.note: Common with things like blinds/curtains (e.g., die Jalousien/den Vorhang aufziehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute Morgen die Jalousien aufgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pulled up the blinds this morning.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of **aufgeben** (to give up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er aufgibt nie, auch wenn es schwer ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He never gives up, even when it’s difficult.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of **aufgeben** meaning to submit/hand in (e.g., an assignment, form, package).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie aufgibt das Formular noch heute beim Amt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hands in the form at the office today.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive in formal German; in everyday speech it’s often followed by dative instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aufgrund des Wetters bleiben wir heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the weather, we’re staying at home today.

definitions.note: Often used with a person as the object: jemanden aufhalten = stop/hold someone up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich nicht aufhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to hold you up.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich aufhalten = stay/be located somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen uns hier nicht lange aufhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don't want to stay here long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Papier aufheben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please pick up the paper?

definitions.note: Often used for laws, rules, or decisions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regierung will das Gesetz aufheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government wants to abolish the law.

definitions.note: Often used both intransitively (the mood or weather brightens) and transitively (to cheer someone up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht konnte ihn ein bisschen aufheitern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news could cheer him up a little.

definitions.native: catch up, make up (for lost time/ground)
definitions.note: Often used for catching up to someone/something, or making up for missed work/time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Hausaufgaben aufholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to catch up on the homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass der Stau uns nicht aufhält.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the traffic jam doesn’t delay us.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: sich aufhalten = to stay/spend time somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß, wo er sich aufhält.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know where he is staying.

definitions.note: Often used for hanging something on a wall (e.g., a picture, poster, coat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte das Bild im Wohnzimmer aufhängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to hang up the picture in the living room.

definitions.note: Form of the separable verb „aufhören“ used with the prefix attached (e.g., in subordinate clauses with „dass“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass ich bald aufhöre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that I stop soon.

definitions.note: Commonly used as "aufhören" (infinitive) or conjugated (e.g., "hört auf", "hörte auf"). Also often used with "mit" + dative: "mit dem Rauchen aufhören".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt aufhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to stop now.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „aufhören“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum aufhörst du nicht, so laut zu reden?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you stop talking so loudly?

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive clause (e.g., „aufhörst zu …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass du bald aufhörst zu rauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that you stop smoking soon.

definitions.note: Can be used with „mit“ + noun/pronoun (e.g., „aufhörst mit …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du nicht sofort aufhörst mit dem Lärm, rufe ich die Polizei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t stop the noise immediately, I’ll call the police.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „aufhören“; often used with an activity: „mit etwas aufhören“ = to stop doing something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, dass er sofort aufhört.
