definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that he stops immediately.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „aufhören“ (3rd person singular: „er/sie/es hörte auf“ → also written as one word here: „aufhörte“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er aufhörte sofort, als die Lehrerin hereinkam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stopped immediately when the teacher came in.

definitions.note: often used about the weather (when clouds/fog disappear)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es soll am Nachmittag aufklaren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s supposed to clear up in the afternoon.

definitions.note: often used for misunderstandings or questions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Problem aufklaren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to clear up the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir das bitte aufklären?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please explain that to me?

definitions.native: to educate, to inform (about something important)
definitions.note: Often used for giving people information to raise awareness (e.g., about health, politics, sex education).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schule will die Schüler über gesunde Ernährung aufklären.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school wants to educate the students about healthy nutrition.

definitions.note: often used for problems, questions, or feelings that appear suddenly
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manchmal können Zweifel aufkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes doubts can come up.

definitions.note: usually used with „für“: „für etwas aufkommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss für den Schaden aufkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to pay for the damage.

definitions.note: Often used for charging a battery (phone, laptop, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mein Handy aufladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to charge my phone.

definitions.note: Often used for loading cargo onto a vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Auto mit Koffern aufladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to load the car up with suitcases.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte nicht einfach auflegen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please not just hang up?

definitions.note: Often used for putting on music (e.g., a record, CD, playlist).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde jetzt meine Lieblingsplatte auflegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to put on my favorite record now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Buch bitte auf den Tisch auflegen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please place the book on the table?

definitions.note: often used for something dissolving in a liquid
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte den Zucker im Tee auflösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to dissolve the sugar in the tea.

definitions.note: often used as: sich auflösen (e.g., an organization or group disbands)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verein muss sich auflösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The club has to disband.

definitions.note: used for problems, mysteries, or puzzles
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Problem schnell auflösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to solve the problem quickly.

definitions.note: colloquial contraction of "auf dem" (usually before a masculine or neuter noun in the dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch liegt aufm Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is on the table.

definitions.note: Often used for opening doors, windows, bottles, packages, etc.; also commonly used to mean “to open up” (start) a business/shop for the day.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Fenster aufmachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please open the window?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind im Unterricht sehr aufmerksam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are very attentive in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte hör aufmerksam zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please listen carefully.

definitions.note: comparative form of "aufmerksam"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute bin ich aufmerksamer als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m more attentive than yesterday.

definitions.note: adjective ending (e.g., masculine nominative singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein aufmerksamer Schüler hört gut zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An attentive student listens carefully.

definitions.note: Often used with an object: jemanden aufmuntern.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, meine Freundin aufmuntern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to cheer my friend up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Gespräch aufnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will record the conversation.

definitions.note: often used for picking up a person with a vehicle (e.g., taxi, bus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus wird die Kinder um 8 Uhr aufnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus will pick up the children at 8 o’clock.

definitions.note: can mean taking someone in (e.g., a guest) or accepting something like responsibility or work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Familie wird einen Gast aufnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family will take in a guest.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative („Aufpassen!“) or with „auf + Akk.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst jetzt gut aufpassen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to pay close attention now!

definitions.note: Common with „auf + Akk.“ (e.g., „auf die Kinder aufpassen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute Abend auf die Kinder aufpassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to look after the kids tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for making something look better or shinier (literally or figuratively).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Schuhe aufpolieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to polish up the shoes.

definitions.note: often used to describe posture or position (standing/sitting upright)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte setz dich aufrecht hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sit up straight.

definitions.native: to upset; to agitate; (reflexive) to get upset/angry
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich aufregen = to get upset/angry about something. Also used non-reflexively: jemanden aufregen = to upset someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte reg dich nicht so auf, du musst dich nicht aufregen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t get so worked up; you don’t need to get upset.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich aufregend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really exciting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine aufregende Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an exciting trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke für deine aufrichtige Entschuldigung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your sincere apology.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich danke dir aufrichtig für deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sincerely thank you for your help.

definitions.native: to tidy up; to clean up
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute mein Zimmer aufräumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tidy up my room today.

definitions.note: Contraction of "auf das"; commonly used with movement/direction (accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lege das Buch aufs Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book onto the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Schule muss ich ein Gedicht aufsagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school I have to recite a poem.

definitions.note: Used especially with things like contracts, subscriptions, or agreements (e.g., „den Vertrag aufsagen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will ihre Mitgliedschaft aufsagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to cancel her membership.

definitions.native: to open (a book), to look up (in a book)
definitions.note: Often used with books, notebooks, or dictionaries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Buch aufschlagen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please open the book?

definitions.note: Used for things like waves, balls, or doors hitting/striking a surface.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wellen können heftig aufschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waves can hit hard.

definitions.note: Often used for unlocking a door (e.g., with a key).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Tür aufschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to unlock the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gespräch war sehr aufschlussreich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conversation was very informative.

definitions.native: to write down, to note down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du dir die Adresse aufschreiben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you write down the address?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will meine Brille aufsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to put on my glasses.

definitions.note: Often used with a surface or place: etwas auf etwas aufsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will den Topf auf den Herd aufsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to set the pot on the stove.

definitions.note: Simple past of „aufstehen“; often appears as „stand … auf“ in main clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blieb im Bett, bis er endlich aufstand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed in bed until he finally got up.

definitions.note: Often used for getting out of bed in the morning, or for standing up from a seated/lying position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde jeden Tag um sieben Uhr aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will get up every day at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used for going up stairs/mountains or rising upward (e.g., smoke, balloons).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir steigen langsam auf den Hügel auf und müssen dabei immer wieder aufsteigen, wo es steiler wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We slowly climb up the hill and have to climb further where it gets steeper.

definitions.note: Used for getting onto a vehicle (e.g., train, bus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte aufsteigen: Steigen Sie am nächsten Halt in den Bus ein und dann am Terminal wieder aufsteigen, wenn die zweite Linie kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please board: Get on the bus at the next stop and then board again at the terminal when the second line comes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Stühle im Kreis aufstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to set up the chairs in a circle.

definitions.note: Often used for going to a specific place or person deliberately (e.g., a doctor, an office).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen meinen Arzt aufsuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to visit my doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often implies actively seeking out a place, person, or service (more deliberate than just ‘looking for’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du Hilfe brauchst, solltest du die Beratung aufsuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need help, you should seek out the counseling service.

definitions.native: to surface (come up out of water)
definitions.note: Literal sense: to come up to the surface (e.g., after diving).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Tauchgang wird er bald wieder auftauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the dive, he will soon surface again.

definitions.note: Figurative sense: to appear (often unexpectedly, or after being absent/missing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird heute Abend bestimmt noch auftauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’ll definitely still turn up this evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du plötzlich auftauchst, erschrecken alle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you suddenly show up, everyone gets scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ein Problem auftaucht, ruf mich bitte an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If a problem turns up, please call me.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „auftauchen“ for 3rd person singular: „er/sie/es tauchte auf“ → „er/sie/es auftauchte“ in a subordinate clause (e.g., after „als“, „weil“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich bemerkten wir, dass ein kleines Boot im Nebel auftauchte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly we noticed that a small boat appeared in the fog.

definitions.note: Often used for applying cream, ointment, makeup, paint, etc. onto a surface or skin.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich soll die Creme auftragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m supposed to apply the cream.

definitions.native: to assign, to commission (someone to do something)
definitions.note: Usually used when someone in authority gives someone a task.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wird mir eine wichtige Aufgabe auftragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will assign me an important task.

definitions.note: Often implies finding or getting something that is hard to get (sometimes by searching around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch schnell einen Babysitter auftreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still need to quickly find a babysitter.

definitions.note: used for problems, symptoms, or situations that happen
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht können starke Schmerzen auftreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Severe pain can occur during the night.

definitions.note: used for musicians, actors, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Band wird heute Abend in Berlin auftreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The band will perform in Berlin tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss morgen früh aufwachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: infinitive; separable verb (Präsens often: ich wache ... auf)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte jeden Tag um sieben Uhr aufwachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to wake up every day at seven o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn er morgen früh aufwacht, ruft er dich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he wakes up tomorrow morning, he’ll call you.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „aufwachen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich aufwachte um sechs Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up at six o’clock.

definitions.note: Usually used with a direct object: jemanden aufwecken = to wake someone up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte weck mich morgen um sieben Uhr auf: Bitte weck mich morgen um sieben Uhr aufwecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wake me up tomorrow at seven o’clock: Please wake me up tomorrow at seven o’clock (wake up).

definitions.native: to heat up, to warm up (again)
definitions.note: Often used for reheating food; can also be used for warming up (e.g., muscles) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Suppe in der Mikrowelle aufwärmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to heat up the soup in the microwave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Uhr aufziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to wind up the clock.

definitions.native: pull up, raise (e.g., blinds, a curtain)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Jalousie aufziehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pull up the blinds?

definitions.native: to build up, to set up
definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used after certain verbs, e.g. anfangen, versuchen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, ein neues Regal aufzubauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re trying to set up a new shelf.

definitions.note: Used about not going to bed (often late), e.g., to keep studying or watching something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche heute Nacht aufzubleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to stay up tonight.

definitions.native: to set off, to leave (to start a trip)
definitions.note: Infinitive used here with "müssen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen früh aufzubrechen, um den Zug zu erreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to set off early to catch the train.

definitions.note: Infinitive used here with "versuchen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, die Tür aufzubrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is trying to break the door open.

definitions.note: Used as a "zu"-infinitive form (e.g., after verbs like versuchen, entscheiden, planen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, nicht aufzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying not to give up.

definitions.note: Often used with "zur Post gehen" / "bei der Post" when sending something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe zur Post, um den Brief aufzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the post office to mail the letter.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „aufhalten“ (often used after another verb, e.g. „versuchen, …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, ihn aufzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are trying to stop him.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „aufhalten“ (often used when someone/something is being kept from continuing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stau drohte uns aufzuhalten, aber wir hoffen, bald weiterfahren zu können.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic jam threatened to delay us, but we hope we can continue driving soon.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „aufheben“; used with verbs like „versuchen“, „helfen“, „vergessen“ etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Geld aufzuheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to pick up the money.

definitions.note: Often used for keeping something for later (e.g., a receipt, a ticket, a document).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist wichtig, den Beleg aufzuheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to keep the receipt.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of aufheitern; used after modal verbs or verbs like versuchen/hoffen, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, meine Freundin aufzuheitern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to cheer up my friend.

definitions.native: to catch up, to make up (for lost time/ground)
definitions.note: used with "zu" (e.g., after another verb)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, den verpassten Stoff aufzuholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to catch up on the material I missed.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive of the separable verb „aufhängen“; often used after another verb (e.g., „vergessen“, „versuchen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergessen, meine Jacke aufzuhängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to hang up my jacket.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „aufhören“, used after certain verbs (e.g. „versuchen“, „anfangen“, „aufhören“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mit dem Rauchen aufzuhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to stop smoking.

definitions.note: "aufzumuntern" is the "zu"-infinitive form of "aufmuntern" (used after certain verbs, adjectives, or nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, ihn aufzumuntern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to cheer him up.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „aufnehmen“, often used after another verb (e.g., „versuchen“, „planen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Gespräch aufzunehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to record the conversation.

definitions.native: to pay attention, to be careful
definitions.note: Often used with “auf + accusative” to mean “watch/look after (someone/something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, auf den Verkehr aufzupassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to watch out for the traffic.

definitions.native: to get upset, to get worked up
definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: sich aufzuregen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versuch, dich nicht aufzuregen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try not to get upset.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist leicht, ihn damit aufzuregen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy to upset him with that.

definitions.native: to tidy up, to clean up
definitions.note: zu + infinitive form (e.g., "Ich habe keine Zeit, aufzuräumen.")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Lust, heute aufzuräumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel like tidying up today.

definitions.native: to write down, to note down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, die Telefonnummer aufzuschreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to write down the phone number.

definitions.native: to get up, to stand up
definitions.note: This is the "zu" infinitive form, used after certain verbs (e.g. "versuchen", "vergessen", "anfangen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, früh aufzustehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to get up early.

definitions.native: to set up, to put up
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, das Zelt heute noch aufzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re trying to put up the tent today.

definitions.note: often used with people (sometimes reflexive: sich aufstellen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder haben gelernt, sich in einer Reihe aufzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children learned to line up in a row.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of "aufsuchen" (often used after another verb, e.g. "versuchen", "planen", "müssen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, morgen meinen Arzt aufzusuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to visit my doctor tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er scheint heute doch noch aufzutauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seems to show up after all today.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used after certain verbs like versuchen, anfangen, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, früh aufzuwachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to wake up early.

definitions.note: zu + infinitive form, used after certain verbs (e.g., versuchen), adjectives, or to express purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Baby nicht aufzuwecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying not to wake the baby up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin augenblicklich im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m currently at the office.

definitions.note: Used with the dative after it (e.g., aus Deutschland).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme aus Deutschland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from Germany.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase „… ist aus“ meaning something is off or has ended (e.g., a light is off, a game is over).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is off.

definitions.note: Used to say where someone/something comes from (origin/source); takes the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme aus Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from Berlin.

definitions.note: Used to say what material something is made from; takes the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ring ist aus Gold.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ring is made of gold.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to say something is finished or should end immediately.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus! Schluss jetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop! That's enough now.

definitions.note: As a preposition, it’s used with the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme aus Deutschland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from Germany.

definitions.note: Often used with things like lights, devices, or fires.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is off.

definitions.note: Often used for improving or enlarging something existing (e.g., a network, a road, a business).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt will das Radwegenetz ausbauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city wants to expand the bike-lane network.

definitions.native: to remove (something built in), to dismantle
definitions.note: Can mean taking out installed parts (e.g., a kitchen, a seat, machinery).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die alte Küche ausbauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to remove the old kitchen.

definitions.note: Common in Austrian/Bavarian German; in Standard German you often hear „(sich) ausleihen“ instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich mir dein Buch ausborgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I borrow your book?

definitions.note: Common in Austrian/Bavarian German; means lending something to someone (Standard German: „verleihen“ / „leihen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir 10 Euro ausborgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me 10 euros?

definitions.note: often used for prisoners/animals escaping or someone breaking free from somewhere; infinitive form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gefangene will ausbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner wants to break out.

definitions.native: to break out (start suddenly), to erupt
definitions.note: used for things like a fire, a disease, or a war starting suddenly; also for a volcano erupting; infinitive form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eine Grippe kann im Winter ausbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A flu can break out in winter.

definitions.native: to spread out, to lay out
definitions.note: Used for laying something flat (e.g., a blanket) or spreading something over a surface; separable verb (breitet … aus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will die Decke auf dem Boden ausbreiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to spread the blanket out on the floor.

definitions.note: Often used for news, rumors, ideas, or information spreading.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird das Gerücht im ganzen Dorf ausbreiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will spread the rumor throughout the whole village.

definitions.note: Can describe something extending over an area (e.g., a fire, a smell, an influence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Feuer kann sich bei starkem Wind schnell ausbreiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire can spread quickly in strong wind.

definitions.note: Often used for things like fire, war, panic, or disease starting suddenly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Wald ausbricht ein Feuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A fire breaks out in the forest.

definitions.note: Used for escaping from a place (like prison).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ausbricht aus dem Gefängnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He escapes from prison.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (hypothetical/conditional), often used with „wenn“ (if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ein Feuer ausbräche, würden wir sofort das Gebäude verlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If a fire broke out, we would leave the building immediately.

definitions.native: to think up, to come up with (an idea/story/plan)
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich etwas ausdenken = to think of/come up with something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich denke mir eine gute Ausrede aus, aber eigentlich muss ich mir nichts ausdenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m thinking up a good excuse, but actually I don’t need to come up with anything.

definitions.note: often used for printing a document onto paper
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Dokument bitte ausdrucken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please print out the document?

definitions.native: to express, to put into words
definitions.note: Often used for expressing thoughts or feelings.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann meine Gefühle schwer ausdrücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find it hard to express my feelings.

definitions.native: to squeeze out, to press out
definitions.note: Used for things like toothpaste, juice, or liquid.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Zahnpasta aus der Tube ausdrücken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please squeeze the toothpaste out of the tube?

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“, „fallen“, „nehmen“ or „setzen“ to mean separating into pieces/parts or being separated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Regal fällt auseinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shelf is falling apart.

definitions.note: Often used with separable verbs (e.g., auseinandergehen, auseinandersetzen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Freunde sind auseinandergegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two friends drifted apart.

definitions.note: Used when something is being taken apart or breaks into parts, often with verbs like auseinandernehmen or auseinanderfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Spielzeug ist in tausend Teile auseinandergefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The toy fell apart into a thousand pieces.

definitions.note: often used for people or things that should not be mixed together
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die saubere und die schmutzige Wäsche auseinanderhalten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please keep the clean and the dirty laundry separate?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann die Zwillinge nicht auseinanderhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't tell the twins apart.

definitions.note: Often sounds elevated or formal (e.g., “the chosen one”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wurde für diese Aufgabe auserwählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was chosen for this task.

definitions.note: Used for scheduled things like classes, meetings, or events that don’t take place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unterricht kann heute ausfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The class might be canceled today.

definitions.note: Often used for machines, systems, or transport that stop working (e.g., a train, heating, internet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn die Heizung ausfallen würde, müssten wir ein Hotel nehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the heating were to break down, we’d have to stay in a hotel.

definitions.note: Commonly used with verbs like „machen“ (to track down) or „werden“ (to be found).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Täter ausfindig gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police tracked down the perpetrator.

definitions.note: Usually used with verbs like „machen/werden“: „jdn./etw. ausfindig machen“ = to track someone/something down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Verdächtigen ausfindig gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police tracked down the suspect.

definitions.note: Often used for carrying out plans, tasks, or instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Plan morgen ausführen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to carry out the plan tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das Problem ausführlich erklärt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He explained the problem in detail.

definitions.note: Often used for forms and documents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte ausfüllen Sie dieses Formular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fill out this form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan ist sehr gut ausgearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan is very well worked out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute nicht mehr Geld ausgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to spend any more money today.

definitions.note: Often used for giving out things like flyers, food, tickets, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie werden am Eingang Flyer ausgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will hand out flyers at the entrance.

definitions.note: Used for things like heat, light, sounds, or smells.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lampe kann ein warmes Licht ausgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp can give off a warm light.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective (e.g. „eine ausgebildete Lehrerin“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist als Krankenschwester ausgebildet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is trained as a nurse.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausbreiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Landkarte ist auf dem Tisch ausgebreitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The map is spread out on the table.

definitions.note: Used for things like war, fire, or a disease starting suddenly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Krieg ist ausgebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The war broke out.

definitions.note: Often used for escaping from prison or from captivity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist aus dem Gefängnis ausgebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He escaped from prison.

definitions.note: Often used for hotels, flights, events, or appointments when no places are left.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel ist für das Wochenende komplett ausgebucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is fully booked for the weekend.

definitions.note: Used for something you created in your imagination (e.g., a story, excuse, idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir eine Geschichte ausgedacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made up a story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist schlecht ausgedrückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is poorly phrased.

definitions.note: Used especially for events or services that do not take place (often with sein: „ist ausgefallen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist heute ausgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train was canceled today.

definitions.note: Used especially for machines or systems that stop working (often with sein: „ist ausgefallen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Heizung ist gestern ausgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heating system broke down yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for insects/animals eating something so that holes or damage remain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Motten haben den Pullover ausgefressen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The moths have eaten holes in the sweater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan wurde ausgeführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan was carried out.

definitions.note: Past participle of "ausgehen"; in the perfect tense it usually uses "sein" (e.g., "ich bin ausgegangen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern Abend mit Freunden ausgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went out with friends last night.

definitions.note: Often used when a light goes off or a fire goes out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist plötzlich ausgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light suddenly went out.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausgeben“; often used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat … ausgegeben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern viel Geld ausgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent a lot of money yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausgeben“; used for giving things to people (e.g. flyers, forms, food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin hat die Arbeitsblätter ausgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher handed out the worksheets.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausgraben“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe im Garten eine alte Münze ausgegraben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dug up an old coin in the garden.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausgraben“; used especially when talking about archaeology or construction
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Archäologen haben ein Grab aus der Römerzeit ausgegraben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The archaeologists excavated a grave from Roman times.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Kälte ausgehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I endured the cold.

definitions.native: to go out (leave the house; often to socialize)
definitions.note: Used for leaving home to go somewhere (often in the evening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen heute Abend ausgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to go out this evening.

definitions.native: to go out (with someone) / to date
definitions.note: Can mean going out with someone romantically.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie geht seit zwei Monaten mit ihm aus, und heute wollen sie wieder ausgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been dating him for two months, and today they want to go out again.

definitions.native: to run out / to be used up (supplies)
definitions.note: Often used for things like food, batteries, or tickets: "Die Milch geht aus"; also "uns geht X aus".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Uns ist das Mehl ausgegangen, weil wir so viel gebacken haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ran out of flour because we baked so much.

definitions.native: to go off / to go out (a light, fire, or candle)
definitions.note: Refers to something being extinguished or a light no longer being on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich ist das Licht ausgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly the light went out.

definitions.note: Past participle of „aushelfen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat ausgeholfen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat gestern im Laden ausgeholfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helped out at the shop yesterday.

definitions.note: can mean going out (leaving home, going out in the evening)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn er heute Abend ausgeht, ruf mich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he goes out this evening, call me.

definitions.note: can mean a light/fire stops burning (is extinguished)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sag mir Bescheid, wenn das Licht ausgeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me know when the light goes out.

definitions.note: used when a supply is used up
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen einkaufen, bevor die Milch ausgeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to shop before the milk runs out.

definitions.note: Past participle of "auslachen"; often used with "werden" (passive) or "haben" (perfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde in der Schule ausgelacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was laughed at at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe seinen Namen im Bericht ausgelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left out his name in the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die Luft aus dem Reifen ausgelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She let the air out of the tire.

definitions.note: Often used for people (emotionally/physically) or for things that have been used up (e.g., batteries).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der langen Woche bin ich völlig ausgelaugt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long week, I’m completely exhausted.

definitions.note: Often used for carefully chosen items (e.g., fruit) or selected data/entries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Trauben sind ausgelesen und kommen in den Wein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grapes are selected and go into the wine.

definitions.note: Used to say you have read something all the way to the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch schon ausgelesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already finished reading the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Paket ist schon ausgeliefert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package has already been delivered.

definitions.note: Often used with „jemandem/etwas ausgeliefert sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Handy fühle ich mich völlig ausgeliefert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without my phone, I feel completely helpless.

definitions.note: Used when the subject is the borrower (often with „sich“: „sich etwas ausleihen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir ein Buch ausgeliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I borrowed a book.

definitions.note: Used when the subject is the person who gives something to someone else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir sein Fahrrad ausgeliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lent me his bicycle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle Daten wurden ausgelöscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the data was erased.

definitions.note: Past participle of „auslösen“; often used with „haben/sein“ (perfect tense) or in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Alarm wurde ausgelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The alarm was triggered.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausmachen“ (e.g., lights, devices)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Licht ausgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned off the light.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausmachen“ used for something being agreed on
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben 18 Uhr ausgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed on 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Past participle used with „haben“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Licht ausgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned off the light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fühlt sich ausgenutzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels exploited.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Möglichkeiten sind noch nicht ausgenutzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The possibilities haven’t been used up yet.

definitions.note: past participle of "ausrauben"; used with "sein" or "haben" depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Touristen wurden am Bahnhof ausgeraubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tourists were robbed at the train station.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that something is surprising, annoying, or ironic: “of all people, him!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum muss das ausgerechnet heute passieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why does it have to happen today of all days?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Kosten ausgerechnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I calculated the costs.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative to mean “geared toward / focused on” (e.g., „auf Kunden ausgerichtet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Angebot ist auf Familien ausgerichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The offer is geared toward families.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausrutschen“, often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist auf dem nassen Boden ausgerutscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slipped on the wet floor.

definitions.note: often used in legal contexts (e.g., in court or with the police)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat vor Gericht ausgesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He testified in court.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat klar ausgesagt, dass sie keine Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She clearly stated that she doesn’t have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Handy ist ausgeschaltet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is switched off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fernseher ist ausgeschaltet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The TV is switched off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn ausgeschimpft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I told him off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat das Angebot ausgeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She rejected the offer.

definitions.note: Often used when something is knocked out by a hit, especially a tooth.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihm wurde ein Zahn ausgeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A tooth was knocked out of his mouth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kinder unter 12 Jahren sind ausgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children under 12 are excluded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist vom Wettbewerb ausgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is excluded from the competition.

definitions.note: past participle of „aussehen“; commonly used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat ... ausgesehen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast müde ausgesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You looked tired.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition like „(etwas) ist (etwas) ausgesetzt“ (= exposed to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist oft starkem Wind ausgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is often exposed to strong wind.

definitions.note: Especially used for a child or animal that has been left somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Park wurde ein ausgesetzter Hund gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An abandoned dog was found in the park.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ + dative: „(etwas) ist (jemandem) ausgesetzt“ = to be exposed to something (e.g., weather, danger).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Pflanzen sind der direkten Sonne ausgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plants are exposed to direct sunlight.

definitions.note: Commonly used for children or animals that were left somewhere: „ein Kind/Tier wurde ausgesetzt“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wurde am Straßenrand ausgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was abandoned at the side of the road.

definitions.note: Used for events/activities that are stopped for a time: „Das Spiel/der Unterricht ist ausgesetzt.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des Sturms ist das Spiel ausgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the storm, the game is suspended/postponed.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something is very noticeable or strong (e.g., "ausgesprochen nett" = "particularly nice").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ausgesprochen interessant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is especially interesting.

definitions.note: past participle of „aussprechen“; often used in passive constructions (e.g., „wird … ausgesprochen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Wort wird anders ausgesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word is pronounced differently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Zimmer ist gut ausgestattet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is well equipped.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to describe what something has (e.g., „mit WLAN ausgestattet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Zimmer ist gut ausgestattet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is well equipped.

definitions.note: used for official documents (e.g., passports, certificates, tickets)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Pass wurde gestern ausgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new passport was issued yesterday.

definitions.note: used for objects or artworks shown to the public
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gemälde sind im Museum ausgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The paintings are exhibited in the museum.

definitions.note: past participle of "aussteigen"; often used with "sein" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind an der nächsten Haltestelle ausgestiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got off at the next stop.

definitions.note: Used for species, languages, traditions, etc. that no longer exist.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Tierart ist seit Jahrhunderten ausgestorben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This animal species has been extinct for centuries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch ausgesucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I selected the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Batterie ausgetauscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I replaced the battery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wurde ausgetrickst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was tricked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Boden ist völlig ausgetrocknet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soil is completely dried out.

definitions.note: past participle of „austrinken“; often used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat ... ausgetrunken“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Wasser schon ausgetrunken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already finished my water.

definitions.note: Often used for substituting a player in sports, but also for replacing/changing things in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Trainer hat den Spieler in der zweiten Halbzeit ausgewechselt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coach substituted the player in the second half.

definitions.note: past participle of "auswählen"; often used with "sein" (passive/result) or "haben" (perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gewinner wurden aus allen Teilnehmern ausgewählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The winners were selected from all the participants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen war ausgezeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen hier schmeckt ausgezeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food here tastes excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine ausgezeichnete Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an excellent idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen ausgezeichneten Kaffee getrunken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drank an excellent coffee.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a neuter noun (e.g. "ein ausgezeichnetes ...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein ausgezeichnetes Angebot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an excellent offer.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausziehen“ (to move out of an apartment/house)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist letzten Monat aus der Wohnung ausgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moved out of the apartment last month.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausziehen“ (to take off clothing)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Schuhe ausgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took off my shoes.

definitions.note: past participle of „ausüben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ihren Beruf zehn Jahre lang ausgeübt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She practiced her profession for ten years.

definitions.note: often used with money (Geld)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ausgibt zu viel Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spends too much money.

definitions.note: often used for distributing things like flyers, tickets, food, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ausgibt im Büro die Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hands out the keys in the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben uns ausgiebig über das Problem unterhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked extensively about the problem.

definitions.note: Usually means leaving the house (often to meet people or for entertainment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern Abend ausging ich mit Freunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday evening I went out with friends.

definitions.note: Often used for lights, candles, or fires that stop burning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich ausging das Licht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly the light went out.

definitions.note: Often used for making something equal or compensating for a difference (e.g., costs, disadvantages, accounts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Kosten ausgleichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to balance out the costs.

definitions.native: to endure, to stand (something), to bear
definitions.note: Often used with "nicht" to mean "can't stand" something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Lärm nicht aushalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand the noise.

definitions.note: Used for things like food, batteries, or supplies lasting for a certain time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wasser muss bis morgen aushalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water has to last until tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with “mit” (mit jemandem auskommen = to get along with someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann gut mit meinen Kollegen auskommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can get along well with my colleagues.

definitions.note: Often used with “mit” when talking about money or resources (mit dem Geld auskommen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen mit weniger Geld auskommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to manage with less money.

definitions.note: Often used for making fun of someone in a hurtful way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte lach mich nicht auslachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t laugh at me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst den letzten Satz auslassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can leave out the last sentence.

definitions.note: Often used for letting out air, liquid, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Luft aus dem Reifen auslassen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please let the air out of the tire?

definitions.note: Used with „an“: „etwas an jemandem auslassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du solltest deinen Ärger nicht an mir auslassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn’t take your anger out on me.

definitions.native: to borrow; to check out (from a library)
definitions.note: Used for borrowing something temporarily. With a direct object: etwas ausleihen. With a reflexive pronoun: sich etwas ausleihen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mir ein Buch aus der Bibliothek ausleihen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to borrow (check out) a book from the library.

definitions.note: often used for delivering goods (packages, food, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Paket heute ausliefern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to deliver the package today.

definitions.note: used in legal/political contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Land will den Verdächtigen ausliefern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country wants to extradite the suspect.

definitions.note: Describes something/someone from another country (not domestic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben viele ausländische Gäste im Hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many foreign guests in the hotel.

definitions.note: adjective form used with endings (e.g., in the accusative or dative singular masculine/neuter, or in the plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich treffe mich mit einem ausländischen Studenten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m meeting up with a foreign student.

definitions.note: Often used for fires, flames, cigarettes, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte auslöschen Sie die Kerze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put out the candle.

definitions.note: Used for eliminating people, groups, species, or things completely.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Krankheit könnte ganze Populationen auslöschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The disease could wipe out entire populations.

definitions.note: Commonly used for switching off devices, lights, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Licht ausmachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn off the light?

definitions.note: Often used for making plans or agreeing on a time/place (e.g. einen Termin ausmachen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen noch einen Termin ausmachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still need to arrange a date/appointment.

definitions.note: Form of the separable verb „ausmachen“ (to switch off). In main clauses it often splits: „Er macht das Licht aus.“ In subordinate clauses it stays together: „..., dass er das Licht ausmacht.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, dass er das Licht ausmacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that he turns off the light.

definitions.native: makes up, constitutes; comes to (a sum)
definitions.note: Also used for amounts/totals (e.g., prices).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gesamtbetrag beträgt 30 Euro, was er damit ausmacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The total amount is 30 euros, which is what it comes to.

definitions.note: Often used with „nichts“: „(Das) macht nichts aus.“ = „It doesn’t matter.“ Here forced into a subordinate clause so it contains „ausmacht“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Für mich ist es egal, was du kochst; entscheidend ist nur, dass es für dich nichts ausmacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s fine with me what you cook; the only important thing is that it doesn’t matter to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ausnahmsweise gehe ich heute zu Fuß zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For once, I'm walking to work today.

definitions.native: to take advantage of, to exploit
definitions.note: Often negative when it means exploiting a person; can also be neutral/positive when meaning making full use of an opportunity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will ihre Hilfsbereitschaft ausnutzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to exploit her willingness to help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde meinen Koffer auspacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will unpack my suitcase.

definitions.note: Often used when you want to see how something works or whether you like it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte das neue Spiel ausprobieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to try out the new game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die neue App schon ausprobiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already tried out the new app.

definitions.native: to freak out, to lose it
definitions.note: colloquial; often used when someone suddenly gets very angry or emotional
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann völlig ausrasten, wenn er die Nachricht liest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can totally freak out when he reads the message.

definitions.note: Often used for robbing a person/place by taking valuables (closer to “to loot/ransack” than to steal a specific item).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Täter wollten den Laden ausrauben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrators wanted to rob the shop.

definitions.note: Often used with a person as the object: jemandem etwas ausreden.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, ihm das ausreden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to talk him out of it.

definitions.native: to finish speaking, to say what you want to say
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich ausreden (e.g., „Lass mich ausreden!“ = “Let me finish!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich noch ausreden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still need to finish what I’m saying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Geld wird nicht ausreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The money will not be enough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeit ist ausreichend, um alles zu erledigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The time is sufficient to get everything done.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du ausreichend Zeit für die Hausaufgaben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have enough time for the homework?

definitions.note: Often used before a noun without an article, especially with uncountable nouns or plurals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ausreichend Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have enough time.

definitions.native: to align, to adjust (so it points the right way)
definitions.note: Often used for physically lining something up; separable verb (richtet … aus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Antenne ausrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to align the antenna.

definitions.native: to pass on, to tell (someone a message)
definitions.note: Used for relaying a message to someone; separable verb (richtet … aus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du ihm bitte ausrichten, dass ich später komme?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please tell him that I’m coming later?

definitions.note: Often used as a reflexive verb: sich ausruhen (= to rest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich nach der Arbeit ausruhen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to rest after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dazu nichts aussagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t say anything about that.

definitions.note: Often used in a legal context with witnesses and court cases.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zeuge muss vor Gericht aussagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness has to testify in court.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "aussehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er aussah müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Licht ausschalten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn off the light?

definitions.note: Often used when you sleep longer than usual (e.g., on a weekend) to catch up on sleep.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Samstag kann ich endlich ausschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Saturday I can finally sleep in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rabatt gilt ausschließlich für Studierende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The discount applies exclusively to students.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of "aussehen"; also used as Konjunktiv II for some speakers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, dass ich heute müde aussehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that I look tired today.

definitions.note: Often used with "wie" ("to look like").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wirst müde aussehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will look tired.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective (from the verb „aussehen“) to describe how someone or something looks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine freundlich aussehende Frau kennengelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met a friendly-looking woman.

definitions.note: Often used with an adverb, e.g. „gut aussehender“ = „good-looking“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein gut aussehender Mann steht an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A good-looking man is standing at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Hilfe ist die Situation aussichtslos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without help, the situation is hopeless.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of "aussehen" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du aussiehst heute müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look tired today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „aussehen“; used in subordinate clauses (main clause often: „sieht … aus“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fragt, wie das Haus aussieht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asks what the house looks like.

definitions.note: Used for describing how someone/something looks (appearance), often in phrases like „wie es aussieht …“ (“as it looks/appears …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie sieht dein neues Zimmer aus, und wie aussieht der Schreibtisch?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does your new room look like, and what does the desk look like?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du dieses Wort bitte aussprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please pronounce this word?

definitions.note: Often used for stating something clearly (e.g., an opinion, criticism, thanks, condolences).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie möchte ihre Kritik offen aussprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to express her criticism openly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Lärm nicht ausstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand the noise.

definitions.native: to be pending, to still be outstanding
definitions.note: Often used for things that still haven't happened or been paid yet (e.g., a decision, an appointment, a payment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Entscheidung kann noch lange ausstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision could still be pending for a long time.

definitions.native: get off, get out (of a vehicle)
definitions.note: Often used with public transport (bus, train, tram).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde an der nächsten Haltestelle aussteigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will get off at the next stop.

definitions.native: issue (a document), draw up (a certificate/invoice), display/exhibit (in an exhibition)
definitions.note: Used (1) for issuing official documents (passports, certificates, tickets, invoices) and (2) for exhibiting objects or artworks; separable verb in finite forms: stellt … aus.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Behörde wird einen neuen Reisepass ausstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authority will issue a new passport.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun (e.g., sich aussuchen = choose for oneself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst dir ein Buch aussuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose a book for yourself.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (something being exchanged) or reflexively with „sich“ for exchanging ideas/information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die defekte Glühbirne austauschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to replace the defective light bulb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Batterie austauschen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you replace the battery?

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag australische Filme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Australian films.

definitions.native: to finish drinking, to drink up
definitions.note: Often used with drinks in a glass/cup, meaning to drink it until it’s empty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst dein Glas austrinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to finish your drink (drink your glass empty).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tickets sind ausverkauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets are sold out.

definitions.note: Often used for swapping people or parts (e.g., a player in a game, a battery).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Trainer muss den verletzten Spieler auswechseln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coach has to substitute the injured player.

definitions.note: Often used with “jemandem/etwas ausweichen” = to avoid someone/something (by moving aside or keeping away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dem Auto ausweichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to dodge the car.

definitions.native: to show (your) ID, to identify yourself
definitions.note: Often used with reflexive pronoun: sich ausweisen = to show ID / identify yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie müssen sich am Eingang ausweisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to show your ID at the entrance.

definitions.note: Used for officially forcing someone to leave a place or a country.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei kann Personen ohne gültige Papiere ausweisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police can expel/deport people without valid papers.

definitions.note: Used especially with verbs like lernen, können, wissen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das Gedicht auswendig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the poem by heart.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst ein anderes Thema auswählen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose a different topic.

definitions.note: often used for being away from home/your usual place (e.g., on a trip) or for sports games played away from home
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächste Woche bin ich beruflich auswärts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next week I’ll be away on business.

definitions.note: separable verb; often used reflexively: sich ausziehen
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich ausziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to take off my clothes.

definitions.note: separable verb; used for leaving an apartment/house
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen nächsten Monat ausziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to move out next month.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive of the separable verb „ausbrechen“ (e.g. „zu + auszubrechen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gefangenen versuchten, aus dem Gefängnis auszubrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoners tried to break out of the prison.

definitions.note: This is the 'zu' infinitive form of "ausdenken" (often used in phrases like "nicht auszudenken").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist nicht auszudenken, was alles passieren könnte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to imagine what could happen.

definitions.note: zu + infinitive form (e.g., after verbs like versuchen, lernen, hoffen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist schwer, meine Gefühle auszudrücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to express my feelings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, den Plan heute auszuführen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re trying to carry out the plan today.

definitions.native: to fill out, to complete (a form)
definitions.note: Used especially for forms/documents; often with "ein Formular" or "einen Antrag".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte vergessen Sie nicht, das Formular auszufüllen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t forget to fill out the form.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „ausgeben“, often used after verbs like „haben“ (e.g., „Geld auszugeben“ = to spend money).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute nicht viel Geld auszugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have much money to spend today.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „ausgeben“, used when giving things (like flyers, food, tickets) to people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben viele Flyer auszugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many flyers to hand out.

definitions.note: usually means going out for fun (e.g., to a bar, restaurant, party).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir planen, am Samstag auszugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re planning to go out on Saturday.

definitions.note: used for lights, candles, fires, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kerze scheint nicht auszugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candle doesn’t seem to go out.

definitions.note: Often used for putting up with something unpleasant (pain, noise, heat, stress).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, den Lärm auszuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to endure the noise.

definitions.note: Used with "bei" + dative (e.g., bei der Arbeit) or with "mit" + dative (e.g., mit dem Umzug).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe versprochen, am Samstag im Laden auszuhelfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I promised to help out at the shop on Saturday.

definitions.native: to know one’s way around, to be familiar (with)
definitions.note: Used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich auskennen“ (e.g., „Ich kenne mich hier aus.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mich in der neuen Stadt auszukennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to find my way around in the new city.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ to mean „to get along with“ someone or „to make do with“ something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, mit wenig Geld auszukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re trying to get by with little money.

definitions.note: Often used for fires and lights.
