definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr versucht, das Feuer auszulöschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department is trying to put out the fire.

definitions.note: Often used for traces, memories, or entire groups (in a very strong sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versuchte, alle Spuren auszulöschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to erase all traces.

definitions.native: to turn off, to switch off
definitions.note: Often used for turning off devices, lights, or a stove.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, das Licht auszumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to turn off the light.

definitions.note: Used when making an agreement about a time, place, or plan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben versucht, für morgen um acht ein Treffen auszumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We tried to arrange a meeting for tomorrow at eight.

definitions.note: Often negative when used about people (exploiting someone); can also be neutral/positive when used about opportunities or resources (make full use of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, mich auszunutzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s trying to exploit me.

definitions.note: often used with an object: etwas ausprobieren = to try something out
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vor, das neue Rezept auszuprobieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plan to try out the new recipe.

definitions.native: to talk (someone) out of (something), to dissuade
definitions.note: Used with a direct object (the person) and often something in the accusative (e.g. jemandem etwas ausreden).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, ihm das Rauchen auszureden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to talk him out of smoking.

definitions.note: often used with „sich“: „sich ausruhen“ = to have a rest
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Wanderung versucht er, sich auszuruhen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, he tries to rest.

definitions.native: to switch off, to turn off
definitions.note: Used for turning off devices, lights, machines, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, das Licht auszuschalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to switch off the light.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone's or something's appearance; can be used with an adjective (e.g., „gut aussehen“ = to look good).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du scheinst heute müde auszusehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seem to look tired today.

definitions.note: Used here as a zu-infinitive (e.g., after verbs like beschließen, planen, versuchen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben beschlossen, das Projekt auszusetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided to suspend the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, sich nicht der Kälte auszusetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries not to expose himself to the cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat es nicht übers Herz gebracht, den Hund auszusetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She couldn't bring herself to abandon the dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Wort ist schwer auszusprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word is hard to pronounce.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie traut sich nicht, ihre Meinung auszusprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She doesn't dare to express her opinion.

definitions.native: to die out, to become extinct
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Arten drohen auszusterben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many species are in danger of dying out.

definitions.note: Used with "zu" in constructions like "vorhaben/planen/versuchen, auszuziehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vor, nächstes Jahr auszuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plan to move out next year.

definitions.note: Used with "zu" after another verb (e.g., "vergessen, auszuziehen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat vergessen, seine Schuhe auszuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forgot to take off his shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür schließt automatisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door closes automatically.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Außen ist es heute sehr kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Outside, it’s very cold today.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative (e.g., außer mir/dir/ihm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Außer meinem Bruder kommt niemand zur Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Except for my brother, nobody is coming to the party.

definitions.note: Often used with a noun/pronoun: „außer + dative“ (e.g. „außer mir“ = except me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse alles außer Fisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat everything except fish.

definitions.note: As a subordinating conjunction, it introduces a condition that is an exception.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme morgen, außer ich werde krank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll come tomorrow unless I get sick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit, und außerdem bin ich müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have time, and besides, I'm tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat heute außergewöhnlich gut gespielt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She played extraordinarily well today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine außergewöhnliche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an extraordinary idea.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive (e.g., außerhalb der Stadt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Außerhalb der Stadt ist es nachts sehr dunkel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Outside the city it is very dark at night.

definitions.note: Often used with genitive (e.g., außerhalb der Stadt = outside the city).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Außerhalb ist es heute kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold outside today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen war außerordentlich gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was extraordinarily good.

definitions.note: Usually used with sein + infinitive with zu (rather formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin außerstande, Ihnen heute zu helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am unable to help you today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „essen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern aß ich ein Sandwich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ate a sandwich.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „essen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern aßen wir Pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we ate pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute backen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to bake today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "backen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er backt heute einen Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bakes a cake today.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „backen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern backte ich einen Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I baked a cake.

definitions.note: Used to draw attention to something you’re presenting or revealing (often humorously).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bada! Da ist dein Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ta-da! There’s your present.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bade heute Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking a bath this evening.

definitions.native: to bathe, to take a bath, to swim
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer baden wir im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer we swim in the lake.

definitions.note: Used with „du“ (2nd person singular, present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer badest du oft im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, you often go swimming in the lake.

definitions.note: Can mean either present tense ("bathes") or the imperative plural/formal ("bathe!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er badet gerade im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is bathing in the lake right now.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern badete ich im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I bathed in the lake.

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun: sich (jemandem) den Weg bahnen = to make/clear a way (for oneself/someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bahnte sich einen Weg durch die Menge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paved his way through the crowd.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme bald zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be back soon.

definitions.note: Slightly formal; common in requests (emails, notices).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte antworten Sie baldmöglichst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please reply as soon as possible.

definitions.note: simple past of „binden“ (e.g., ich/er/sie/es band)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er band das Paket mit einer Schnur zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tied up the package with a string.

definitions.note: Often used with „gehen“ (to go bankrupt) or „sein“ (to be bankrupt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma ist bankrott.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is bankrupt.

definitions.note: means paying with cash (not by card)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezahle bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m paying in cash.

definitions.note: a place where you can buy drinks (often alcoholic)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns heute Abend in einer Bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re meeting at a bar this evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer laufe ich oft barfuß am Strand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer I often walk barefoot on the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer laufe ich oft barfuß im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer I often walk barefoot in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used in moral/religious contexts; in everyday speech, "mitfühlend" is also common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Richter war barmherzig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge was merciful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Antwort war ziemlich barsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His answer was pretty curt.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“: „auf etwas basieren“ = to be based on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film soll auf einer wahren Geschichte basieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is said to be based on a true story.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" (e.g., "auf etwas basieren" = "to be based on something").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film basierte auf einer wahren Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was based on a true story.

definitions.note: Often used emphatically to end a discussion or demand that something stops; borrowed from Italian.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Basta! Hör auf damit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enough! Stop it!

definitions.note: simple past of „bitten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bat mich um Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked me for help.

definitions.note: simple past of „bitten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie baten ihn um Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They asked him for help.

definitions.note: Often a shortened, colloquial form of „baue“ (e.g. „ich bau“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bau heute ein Regal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m building a shelf today.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense ("I build").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich baue ein Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am building a house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bauen ein Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are building a house.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anbauen“ (to grow/cultivate crops).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er baut Tomaten im Garten an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grows tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "bauen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er baut ein Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He builds a house.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufbauen“; in a sentence the prefix often comes at the end (… baute … auf).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er baute das Zelt im Garten auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He set up the tent in the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „bauen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr baute er ein kleines Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year he built a small house.

definitions.note: simple past of „bauen“ (for „we/they“ and also polite „you“ plural context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr bauten wir ein kleines Haus am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year we built a small house by the lake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beabsichtige, morgen früher zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I intend to leave earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beabsichtigst du, morgen früher zu gehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you intend to leave earlier tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht beabsichtigt, dich zu verletzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t intend to hurt you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beabsichtigte, früher zu gehen, aber dann kam etwas dazwischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I intended to leave earlier, but then something came up.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “please note” in instructions or announcements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte beachte die Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please note the rules.

definitions.native: pay attention to, take note of, observe
definitions.note: Often used in instructions and formal contexts (e.g., “Bitte beachten Sie …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte beachten Sie die Hinweise auf dem Schild.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pay attention to the notices on the sign.

definitions.note: Often used with an object in the accusative (e.g., Regeln beachten = follow/observe rules).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beachtet die Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He follows the rules.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „beachten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beachtete das Warnschild nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t notice the warning sign.

definitions.note: Used mainly in official or bureaucratic contexts (authorities, applications, permits, benefits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte eine Aufenthaltserlaubnis beantragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to apply for a residence permit.

definitions.native: to file a motion (in a meeting/court context)
definitions.note: Common in formal procedures: e.g., committees, parliaments, courts ("einen Antrag beantragen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Anwalt wird eine Fristverlängerung beantragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer will file a motion to extend the deadline.

definitions.note: Often used in official/bureaucratic contexts (e.g., visas, permits, benefits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ein Visum beantragt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She applied for a visa.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (or imperative) of „beantworten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beantworte deine Frage später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll answer your question later.

definitions.note: Used with a direct object (e.g., a question, an email).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du meine Frage beantworten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you answer my question?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie beantwortet die Frage schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She answers the question quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die E-Mail beantwortet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He answered the email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beantwortete die Frage sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He answered the question immediately.

definitions.note: Often used for editing text/files or for working on/processing a task or topic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Bericht noch bearbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to edit/work on the report.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of „beauftragen“ (e.g., with „haben“ or in the passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe sie beauftragt, den Bericht zu schreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tasked her with writing the report.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "beben" (can also be used for things like the ground, a voice, or a hand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Erde bebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The earth trembles.

definitions.note: Often used for actions, decisions, or speech that are well considered (not impulsive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er traf eine sehr bedachte Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a very thoughtful decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das nicht bedacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't consider that.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „ich bedanke mich (bei dir/Ihnen)“ = “I thank you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bedanke mich für deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich bedanken (e.g., sich bei jemandem für etwas bedanken).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, dich bei ihr für das Geschenk zu bedanken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to thank her for the gift.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of the reflexive verb „sich bedanken“ (often with „bei“ + dative for the person you thank).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich bei ihr bedankt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thanked her.

definitions.note: Formal; usually used in the pattern "es bedarf + Genitive" (e.g., "Es bedarf keiner Erklärung.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es bedarf keiner Erklärung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It requires no explanation.

definitions.note: often used to express polite regret (e.g., in apologies or formal statements)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bedauere, dass ich heute nicht kommen kann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regret that I can't come today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist bedauerlich, dass du nicht kommen kannst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s regrettable that you can’t come.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bedauerlicherweise kann ich heute nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I can’t come today.

definitions.note: Often used in a formal or polite way (e.g., in apologies or official statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bedauere den Fehler sehr; ich kann ihn nur bedauern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really regret the mistake; all I can do is regret it.

definitions.note: Often used to express sympathy or disapproval about an unfortunate person or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine bedauernswerte Situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a regrettable situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bedauert seine Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He regrets his decision.

definitions.note: past participle, often used with "haben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das sehr bedauert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regretted that a lot.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I regret").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bedaure meinen Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regret my mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte bedecken Sie den Topf mit einem Deckel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please cover the pot with a lid.

definitions.note: verb form (3rd person singular present) of „bedecken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schnee bedeckt die Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Snow covers the street.

definitions.note: past participle; often used like an adjective (e.g. about the sky/weather)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Himmel ist bedeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky is covered (overcast).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist mit Papieren bedeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is covered with papers.

definitions.note: Used especially to describe the weather/sky.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist der Himmel bedeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the sky is overcast.

definitions.note: simple past of „bedecken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schnee bedeckte die Straßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snow covered the streets.

definitions.note: subjunctive II (Konjunktiv II) of „bedecken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bedeckte das Essen, wenn Fliegen da wären.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would cover the food if there were flies around.

definitions.note: Often means to take something into account (more careful/formal than just denken).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen auch die Kosten bedenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We also have to consider the costs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bedenkt die möglichen Folgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He considers the possible consequences.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form used with „ihr“ (plural informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bedenkt das bitte, bevor ihr geht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please think about that before you go!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was kann dieses Wort bedeuten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What can this word mean?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein rotes Licht kann Gefahr bedeuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A red light can signify danger.

definitions.note: Often used with "viel" (a lot) to express importance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Unterstützung kann viel bedeuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your support can mean a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Miete ist dieses Jahr bedeutend gestiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rent has increased significantly this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hielt eine bedeutende Rede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave an important speech.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular ("you") present tense of "bedeuten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was bedeutest du damit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you mean by that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was bedeutet dieses Wort?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does this word mean?

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „bedeuten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das bedeutete, dass wir früher gehen mussten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That meant that we had to leave earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Streit war am Ende völlig bedeutungslos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, the argument was completely meaningless.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command to one person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bedien bitte die Maschine vorsichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please operate the machine carefully.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command to one person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bedien die Gäste zuerst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Serve the guests first.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bediene die Kunden im Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I serve the customers in the café.

definitions.note: Often used for serving customers (e.g., in a restaurant or shop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kellnerin wird die Gäste am Tisch bedienen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waitress will serve the guests at the table.

definitions.note: Used for operating a device or machine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Kaffeemaschine bedienen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you operate the coffee machine?

definitions.note: Often used for serving customers (e.g., in a restaurant) or operating a machine/device.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bedient die Maschine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He operates the machine.

definitions.note: past participle of „bedrohen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt ist durch das Hochwasser bedroht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is threatened by the flooding.

definitions.note: often used to describe people, places, or species that are in danger
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Tierarten sind bedroht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many animal species are threatened.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „bedrohen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann bedrohte den Verkäufer mit einem Messer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man threatened the cashier with a knife.

definitions.note: Often used for situations, atmospheres, or feelings that feel heavy or distressing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stimmung im Raum war bedrückend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The atmosphere in the room was oppressive.

definitions.note: Often used about feelings or upsetting news.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht bedrückt mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news depresses me.

definitions.note: Very formal/polite; often used in set phrases like „mit seinem Besuch beehren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir würden uns freuen, wenn Sie uns mit Ihrem Besuch beehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would be happy if you would honor us with your visit.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich beeilen“ (e.g., „Ich beeile mich.“ = “I hurry / I’m hurrying.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beeile mich, sonst verpasse ich den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hurrying, otherwise I’ll miss the bus.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich beeilen = to hurry (up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen uns beeilen, sonst verpassen wir den Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to hurry, otherwise we’ll miss the train.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich beeilen“ = to hurry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beeilt sich, weil der Zug gleich kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hurries because the train is coming soon.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively as the past participle in the perfect tense: „sich beeilen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat sich beeilt und ist pünktlich angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hurried and arrived on time.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich beeilen“ = to hurry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beeilte mich, damit ich den Bus nicht verpasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hurried so that I wouldn’t miss the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aussicht kann viele Menschen beeindrucken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view can impress many people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine beeindruckende Leistung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an impressive achievement.

definitions.note: Past participle of "beeindrucken"; often used with "sein" (e.g., "Ich bin beeindruckt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin sehr beeindruckt von deiner Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very impressed by your work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin wirklich beeindruckt von deiner Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really impressed by your work.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „beeindrucken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film beeindruckte mich sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie impressed me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Meinung kann meine Entscheidung beeinflussen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His opinion can influence my decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist stark von seinen Freunden beeinflusst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is strongly influenced by his friends.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., health, work, performance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm beeinträchtigt meine Konzentration.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise affects my concentration.

definitions.note: Used as a command (imperative) or as “I end/finish” (1st person singular present).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beende bitte das Gespräch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please end the conversation.

definitions.note: Often used for deliberately bringing something to an end (e.g., a meeting, a contract, a relationship).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Meeting jetzt beenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to end the meeting now.

definitions.note: past participle of "beenden"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat beendet") or as an adjective meaning "ended/finished"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer hat den Unterricht beendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher ended the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs ist beendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course is finished.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „beenden“ (often used in writing)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beendete das Gespräch nach fünf Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ended the conversation after five minutes.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural ("we/they")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie beendeten das Gespräch nach fünf Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ended the conversation after five minutes.

definitions.native: to bury (a dead person), to inter
definitions.note: Used specifically for burying someone who has died (a funeral context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Familie wird ihn am Samstag beerdigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family will bury him on Saturday.

definitions.note: used for a person being buried (having a funeral/burial)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde gestern beerdigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was buried yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past of „befehlen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Offizier befahl den Soldaten, stehen zu bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The officer ordered the soldiers to stop.

definitions.note: simple past of "sich befinden" (to be located)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel befand sich in der Nähe des Bahnhofs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel was located near the train station.

definitions.note: simple past of "sich befinden" (to feel; about someone’s condition)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er befand sich nach der Operation besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt better after the operation.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively with „sich“ (e.g. „sie befanden sich …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Toiletten befanden sich im Erdgeschoss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The toilets were located on the ground floor.

definitions.native: deal with, address, concern oneself with
definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich mit etwas befassen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mich heute mit dem Problem befassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to deal with the problem today.

definitions.note: Usually used with „mit“ (often in phrases like „mit etwas befasst sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist mit dem neuen Projekt befasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is dealing with the new project.

definitions.note: Usually used with „mit“ + dative: „mit etwas befasst sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade mit dem Bericht befasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m currently dealing with the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich befehle dir, sofort zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I command you to leave immediately.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (jemandem) and either an infinitive with „zu“ or a clause with „dass“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef befiehlt den Soldaten, zu warten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss orders the soldiers to wait.

definitions.native: to fasten, to attach, to secure
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte befesti­ge das Schild an der Tür und befestigen Sie es gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fasten the sign to the door and secure it well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef befiehlt den Mitarbeitern, pünktlich zu kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss orders the employees to come on time.

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun: „sich befinden“ = to be located / to be (in a place), often in more formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich befinde mich gerade im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m at the office right now.

definitions.note: Usually used with "sich" ("sich befinden") and often sounds formal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Museum wird sich in der Altstadt befinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum will be located in the old town.

definitions.note: Usually used with "sich" ("sich befinden"), often in formal/polite contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie befinden Sie sich heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you feeling today?

definitions.note: Often used (sometimes with „sich“) to state where something is situated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schule befindet sich in der Innenstadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school is located downtown.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively with „sich“ and sounds fairly formal compared to „sich fühlen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er befindet sich heute nicht gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He isn’t feeling well today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef hat mir befohlen, früher zu kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss ordered me to come earlier.

definitions.note: often used for following rules, instructions, or advice
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich befolge die Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I follow the rules.

definitions.note: Often used with rules, instructions, advice, or laws (e.g. Regeln, Anweisungen, Ratschläge, Gesetze).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte befolgen Sie die Anweisungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please follow the instructions.

definitions.note: Used for following rules/instructions/advice, or obeying orders.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er befolgt die Regeln genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He follows the rules exactly.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., police or surveys).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich befrage die Zeugin zu dem Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I question the witness about the accident.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., police, surveys, official questioning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei befragt den Zeugen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are questioning the witness.

definitions.note: Present tense (er/sie/es) of „befragen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Journalist befragt den Zeugen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist questions the witness.

definitions.note: Past participle of „befragen“, often used in passive forms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zeuge wurde befragt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness was questioned.

definitions.note: Often used with an object + „von“ (e.g., jemanden von etwas befreien).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich befreie den Hund aus dem Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I free the dog from the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie befreien den Hund aus dem Käfig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They free the dog from the cage.

definitions.note: past participle of „befreien“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr hat die Katze aus dem Baum befreit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department freed the cat from the tree.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „befreien“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr befreite die Katze aus dem Baum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department freed the cat from the tree.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“: „mit jemandem befreundet sein“ = to be friends with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit Lara befreundet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m friends with Lara.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Antwort ist befriedigend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is satisfactory.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/official contexts, especially with an infinitive clause (e.g., „befugt, etwas zu tun“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nicht befugt, das zu entscheiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am not authorized to decide that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma wird die Pakete jeden Morgen befördern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company will transport the packages every morning.

definitions.note: Usually means being promoted to a higher position at work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef will sie zur Teamleiterin befördern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss wants to promote her to team leader.

definitions.note: Often used for promoting someone at work to a higher position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef befördert sie zur Teamleiterin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss promotes her to team leader.

definitions.note: Commonly used for moving or delivering things (e.g., mail, packages, passengers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma befördert die Pakete jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company transports the packages every day.

definitions.note: Often used for fearing that something bad might happen; commonly followed by a clause with „dass“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich befürchte, dass wir zu spät kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid we’ll be late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er befürchtet, dass der Zug zu spät kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fears that the train will be late.

definitions.note: Often used for being worried that something bad might happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie befürchtete, dass der Zug zu spät kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feared that the train would be late.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., politics, organizations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ausschuss befürwortet den Vorschlag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The committee supports the proposal.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive "sich" ("sich begeben") in more formal or literary language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er begab sich nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr begabt und lernt schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very talented and learns quickly.

definitions.note: comparative form of "begabt"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schwester ist begabter als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is more talented than I am.

definitions.note: often used with crimes or offenses (e.g., a theft, a murder, a mistake)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tat wurde von zwei Männern begangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crime was committed by two men.

definitions.note: used for holidays, anniversaries, or events
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Fest wurde gestern im Dorf begangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The festival was celebrated in the village yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "beginnen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film begann um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie began at eight o'clock.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „beginnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir begannen um acht Uhr mit der Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We began work at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively as „sich begeben“ and sounds formal (e.g. „sich zum Bahnhof begeben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden uns jetzt zum Bahnhof begeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will head to the train station now.

definitions.note: Often used with dative: jemandem begegnen = to meet someone / run into someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich begegne morgen meiner Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will meet my teacher tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du begegnest jeden Tag vielen Menschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You meet many people every day.

definitions.note: Usually used with the dative: jemandem begegnen = to meet/run into someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er begegnet seiner alten Lehrerin auf der Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He runs into his old teacher on the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern begegnete ich meiner alten Lehrerin in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I met my old teacher in town.

definitions.note: Often used with crimes or wrongdoing (e.g., eine Straftat begehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man darf keine Straftaten begehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not commit any crimes.

definitions.native: to celebrate, to observe (a holiday, an anniversary)
definitions.note: Used for marking a special day or event (often in a formal way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen ihren Geburtstag im kleinen Kreis begehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to celebrate her birthday in a small group.

definitions.note: Often used with things like „ein Verbrechen“ (a crime) or „einen Fehler“ (a mistake).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er begeht einen schweren Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He commits a serious mistake.

definitions.note: Often used with holidays or special occasions (e.g. „Weihnachten“, „einen Geburtstag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie begeht ihren Geburtstag im kleinen Kreis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She celebrates her birthday in a small circle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin begeistert von dem Konzert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m excited about the concert.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative (e.g., „begierig auf etwas“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin begierig auf deine Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eager for your answer.

definitions.note: Past tense of „begehen“; often used with crimes or offenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beging einen Diebstahl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed a theft.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich beginne).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beginne heute mit meinen Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I begin my homework today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir beginnen um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We begin at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "beginnen" (used with er/sie/es).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course begins at nine o’clock.

definitions.note: Most often used for bills, debts, or balances (e.g., an invoice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Rechnung noch begleichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to pay the bill.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of „begleiten“ (ich begleite)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich begleite dich nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accompany you home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich zur Haltestelle begleiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will accompany you to the stop.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du begleitest mich zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You accompany me to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er begleitet seine Freundin nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accompanies his girlfriend home.

definitions.note: Past participle, used with auxiliaries like „haben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ihn zum Bahnhof begleitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accompanied him to the train station.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er begleitete sie nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accompanied her home.

definitions.note: Past participle of „beglücken“; often used like an adjective to mean “delighted.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht hat ihn sehr beglückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news made him very happy.

definitions.note: Often means feeling very happy because of something (somewhat formal/literary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war beglückt über die guten Nachrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was delighted about the good news.

definitions.note: Usually used with people (often by a head of state), e.g. in the passive: „wurde begnadigt“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gefangene wurde nach zehn Jahren begnadigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was pardoned after ten years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs hat gestern begonnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course began yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle used as an adjective (from the verb „begraben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schatz ist hier begraben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasure is buried here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen ihn morgen begraben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to bury him tomorrow.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I understand")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich begreife das Problem jetzt besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understand the problem better now.

definitions.note: Often used for really understanding something (getting the idea), not just hearing it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann endlich begreifen, warum das passiert ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can finally understand why that happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Begreifst du, warum ich das so mache?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand why I do it like this?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie begreift die Aufgabe sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She understands the task right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeit ist begrenzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time is limited.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben nur begrenzte Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We only have limited time.

definitions.note: Simple past (ich/er/sie/es) form of "begreifen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er begriff die Frage sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He understood the question immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jetzt habe ich es begriffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Now I’ve understood it.

definitions.note: First-person singular present ("I ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich begrüße dich an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I greet you at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Gäste herzlich begrüßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will warmly greet/welcome the guests.

definitions.note: Used when greeting someone (often in a somewhat formal or polite way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gastgeber begrüßt die Gäste an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The host greets the guests at the door.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „begrüßen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er begrüßte mich an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He greeted me at the door.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural or formal "you"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie begrüßten die Gäste an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They greeted the guests at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das milde Wetter begünstigt das Wachstum der Pflanzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mild weather favors the growth of the plants.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative of „behalten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Behalt das Wechselgeld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep the change.

definitions.note: Often used with „ich“: „ich behalte …“ = “I keep … / I’m keeping …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich behalte das Ticket als Erinnerung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I keep the ticket as a souvenir.

definitions.note: Often used to mean keeping something (not giving it back) or retaining something (like information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst das Buch behalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can keep the book.

definitions.note: Form used with „ihr“ (you plural), and also as an imperative addressed to a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Behaltet das Ticket, ihr braucht es später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep the ticket; you’ll need it later.

definitions.note: Often used for medical treatment, but can also mean to deal with a topic or to treat someone in a certain way; context makes it clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt wird die Patientin morgen behandeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor will treat the patient tomorrow.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du-form): “you” (informal). Often used for treating a patient/condition or dealing with a topic/problem.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie behandelst du diese Wunde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you treat this wound?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt behandelt den Patienten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor treats the patient.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt behandelte den Patienten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor treated the patient.

definitions.note: Often used for treating a patient/illness or dealing with a topic/issue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich behandle heute viele Patienten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I treat many patients today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie arbeitet beharrlich an ihrem Projekt, obwohl es schwierig ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works persistently on her project even though it is difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich behaupte, dass das stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I claim that that's true.

definitions.note: Often used when someone states something as true, sometimes without proof.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird behaupten, dass er nichts davon wusste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will claim that he didn’t know anything about it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du behauptest, dass du keine Zeit hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You claim that you don't have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er behauptet, dass er keine Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He claims that he has no time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das behauptet, aber es stimmt nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He claimed that, but it’s not true.

definitions.note: Simple past form; often used to report what someone said (not necessarily true).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er behauptete, er habe keine Zeit gehabt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He claimed he hadn’t had time.

definitions.note: Often used for fixing a problem/defect (e.g., errors, faults, issues).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Techniker kann den Fehler schnell beheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The technician can fix the error quickly.

definitions.native: to master, to have a good command of
definitions.note: Often used for skills and languages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kann Deutsch sehr gut beherrschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She can master German very well.

definitions.note: Often used for controlling emotions, a situation, or a territory.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er konnte seine Wut nicht beherrschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He couldn’t control his anger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beherrscht die Situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He controls the situation.

definitions.note: Often used for skills and languages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie beherrscht Deutsch sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She knows German very well.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „behalten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich behielt das Buch bis zum Ende der Ferien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kept the book until the end of the vacation.

definitions.note: Often used with “sein” and “bei” (e.g., „bei etwas behilflich sein“ = to help with something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können Sie mir bei der Suche behilflich sein?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me with the search?

definitions.note: As a verb form of „behindern“. Not to be confused with English „behind“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm behindert mich beim Lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise hinders me from studying.

definitions.note: When talking about people, it can sound insensitive as a label; often you’ll hear more respectful phrasing like „Menschen mit Behinderung“ (“people with disabilities”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Museum ist barrierefrei und für behinderte Menschen gut zugänglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum is barrier-free and easily accessible for people with disabilities.

definitions.note: Often used for situations like traffic, work, or progress being held up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verkehr ist durch den Unfall behindert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Traffic is disrupted because of the accident.

definitions.note: Often used for gentle, considerate handling (physically or emotionally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte öffne die alte Kiste behutsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please open the old box carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er behält seinen Pass immer bei sich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always keeps his passport with him.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of „behalten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du behältst das Buch bis morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You keep the book until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich behüte das Kind, bis du zurück bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I protect the child until you are back.

definitions.note: Used with the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin bei meiner Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m at my girlfriend’s place.

definitions.note: Used with the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei Regen bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When it rains, we stay at home.

definitions.note: Used with the dative case; often expresses location or being at someone's place (e.g., bei mir = at my place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin bei meiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m at my sister’s place.

definitions.note: Often used with people/organizations to show association (e.g., bei einer Firma = with/at a company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie arbeitet bei einer Bank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works at a bank.

definitions.note: Often used for keeping something the same (e.g., a rule, plan, price, or habit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir möchten die aktuellen Regeln beibehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like to keep the current rules.

definitions.note: Typically used as: jemandem (Dativ) + etwas (Akkusativ) beibringen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir Deutsch beibringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will teach you German.

definitions.note: Used with a dative person and an accusative thing: jemandem etwas beibringen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Mutter beibringt mir Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother teaches me German.

definitions.note: Often used for confessing sins, especially in a religious (Catholic) context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss beichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to confess.

definitions.note: Often used for confessing sins, especially in a religious context (e.g., to a priest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beichtete seine Sünden in der Kirche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confessed his sins in the church.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beide Kinder spielen im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Both children are playing in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beide sind heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Both are at home today.

definitions.note: dative plural (used with plural nouns, after a dative preposition, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mit beiden Freunden gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I talked with both friends.

definitions.note: dative plural form of "beide"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe beiden Kindern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help both children.

definitions.note: dative plural form of „beide“ (used with plural nouns or „wir/ihr/sie“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe beiden Kindern ein Eis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give both children an ice cream.

definitions.note: used when referring to two things in general (neuter: „beide“ + „-s“), often meaning “both (of them)”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme beides.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take both.

definitions.note: often used to mean people or things are in the same place or close to each other
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sitzen heute alle ganz dicht beieinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re all sitting very close together.

definitions.note: Past participle of „beibringen“, often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat beigebracht“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihm Deutsch beigebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I taught him German.

definitions.note: past participle of „beitragen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat viel zum Erfolg beigetragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He contributed a lot to the success.

definitions.note: past participle of „beitreten“, often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense; commonly used for joining a group/organization
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist dem Verein beigetreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He joined the club.

definitions.note: Contraction of "bei dem" (dative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns beim Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re meeting at the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe beinah den Zug verpasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I almost missed the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Bus beinahe verpasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I almost missed the bus.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „legen“, „stellen“, „schieben“ to mean moving something out of the way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leg bitte das Buch beiseite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put the book aside.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like legen/stellen/schieben to mean moving something out of the way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leg das Buch bitte beiseite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put the book aside.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (jemandem beistehen) and can imply emotional support, help, or being at someone’s side in a difficult situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir in dieser schweren Zeit beistehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will support you in this difficult time.

definitions.note: Often used for joining an organization, party, club, or agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dem Verein beitreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to join the club.

definitions.native: to teach, to show (someone how to do something)
definitions.note: Used with „zu“ + infinitive (from the verb „beibringen“). Often takes a person in the dative (e.g. „jemandem etwas beibringen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, dir Deutsch beizubringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to teach you German.

definitions.note: Zu-infinitive of „beitreten“; often used with organizations/clubs and takes the dative (e.g. „einem Verein beitreten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe beschlossen, dem Verein beizutreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to join the club.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative (command), e.g. “Beiß!” or “Beiß nicht!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beiß nicht in den Apfel, er ist noch heiß!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t bite into the apple, it’s still hot!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund kann beißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog can bite.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "beißen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund beißt den Briefträger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog bites the mail carrier.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „bekommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bekam gestern eine E-Mail von meiner Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got an email from my teacher yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "bekommen" for "wir/sie/Sie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bekamen gestern eine E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got an email yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past of "bekommen" ("you" singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bekamst gestern einen Brief von deiner Oma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You got a letter from your grandma yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Restaurant ist in der Stadt sehr bekannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant is very well-known in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine bekannte Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a well-known story.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „bekennen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bekannte seine Schuld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confessed his guilt.

definitions.note: comparative form of „bekannt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Berlin ist bekannter als Potsdam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Berlin is more well-known than Potsdam.

definitions.note: inflected form of „bekannt“ used before a noun (e.g. „ein bekannter Mann“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein bekannter Schauspieler kommt heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A well-known actor is coming today.

definitions.note: Used attributively before a neuter noun in the nominative or accusative (e.g., „ein bekanntes Lied“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein bekanntes Lied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a well-known song.

definitions.note: past participle of "bekanntgeben"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Termin wurde gestern bekanntgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The date was announced yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss etwas bekennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to confess something.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich zu" (e.g. "sich zu etwas bekennen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will sich zu seinem Glauben bekennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to profess his faith.

definitions.note: Informal slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Joint war er total bekifft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the joint, he was totally stoned.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., something you complain about) or with „sich über … beklagen“ (= to complain about …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen beklagen die hohen Preise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people complain about the high prices.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beklagt sich über den Lärm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He complains about the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat den Verlust lange beklagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lamented the loss for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich beklagen“ = to complain (about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beklagte sich über das laute Geräusch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He complained about the loud noise.

definitions.note: Colloquial; used to mean someone stole from a person (e.g., wallet, phone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wurde in der U-Bahn beklaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was robbed on the subway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Frau ist elegant bekleidet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman is dressed elegantly.

definitions.note: informal; can be mildly insulting or joking depending on tone
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Typ ist total bekloppt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That guy is totally nuts.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (du-form) of „bekommen“; often confused with English “become”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bekomm bitte dein Geld zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please get your money back.

definitions.note: Often used for obtaining something (e.g., a gift, a letter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bekomme heute einen Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get a letter today.

definitions.note: Used with "ein Kind" to mean giving birth.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im April bekomme ich ein Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In April, I am having a baby.

definitions.note: Common false friend: it does NOT mean “to become” (German: werden).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute ein Paket bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to get a package today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden morgen die Tickets bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will get the tickets tomorrow.

definitions.native: to catch (an illness); to come down with
definitions.note: Often used with illnesses (e.g., Fieber, eine Erkältung).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er könnte eine Erkältung bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He might catch a cold.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "bekommen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bekommst heute einen Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You get a letter today.

definitions.note: Often used with the sense of receiving something (e.g., a gift, a letter, an email).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bekommt heute einen Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets a letter today.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of „bekommen“, used for hypothetical or polite statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich mehr Geld hätte, bekäme ich ein besseres Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more money, I would get a better bike.

definitions.note: Often used for actively opposing an enemy, a problem, a disease, or something undesirable (e.g., crime, inflation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr muss den Brand schnell bekämpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department must fight the fire quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm belastet mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise burdens me / puts a strain on me.

definitions.note: means listening in secretly (often intentionally)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er belauscht das Gespräch durch die Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He eavesdrops on the conversation through the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er belegte den Platz am Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He occupied the seat by the window.

definitions.note: Often used with food together with „mit“ (e.g., „ein Brot mit Käse belegen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie belegte das Brötchen mit Käse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She topped the bread roll with cheese.

definitions.native: to instruct; to teach; to inform (often in a corrective, admonishing way)
definitions.note: Often implies correcting someone or telling them what they should know/do; can sound patronizing depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin will die Schüler über die Verkehrsregeln belehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher wants to instruct the students about the traffic rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte beleidigen Sie mich nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t insult me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war wirklich beleidigend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was really insulting.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective/participle meaning someone feels hurt or insulted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin beleidigt, weil du mich nicht eingeladen hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m offended because you didn’t invite me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin beleidigt, weil du mich ausgelacht hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm offended because you laughed at me.

definitions.note: simple past of „beleidigen“ (also used as Konjunktiv II in some contexts)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beleidigte seinen Bruder vor allen Leuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He insulted his brother in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Often used with words like „gut“ or „schlecht“ (e.g. „gut beleumundet“ = well-regarded).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma ist in der Branche gut beleumundet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is well-regarded in the industry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Park ist bei Familien sehr beliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This park is very popular with families.

definitions.note: adjective form of „beliebt“; often used before a noun (e.g., „eine beliebte Sängerin“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine beliebte App.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a popular app.

definitions.note: comparative form of „beliebt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Lied ist beliebter als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This song is more popular than the other one.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter singular noun (or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein beliebtes Restaurant in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a popular restaurant in the city.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "beliebt" (popular). Often used with "die/der/das" (e.g., "die beliebteste"). Not the same as English "beloved".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die beliebteste Serie in Deutschland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the most popular series in Germany.

definitions.note: superlative form of „beliebt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die beliebtesten Bücher in unserer Klasse.
