definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the most popular books in our class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund kann nachts lange bellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog can bark for a long time at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund bellt laut vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barks loudly in front of the door.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „bellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund bellte die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog barked all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wurde belogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was lied to.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wird sie für ihre gute Arbeit belohnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will reward her for her good work.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "belohnen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef belohnt gute Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss rewards good work.

definitions.note: Usually used in a negative sense (e.g., bothering someone or harassing them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich belästige niemanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't bother anyone.

definitions.note: Often used for unwelcome, disturbing behavior (including sexual harassment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte belästigen Sie die anderen Fahrgäste nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t harass the other passengers.

definitions.note: Often used for unwanted or intrusive bothering; can also mean “sexually harass,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum belästigst du mich die ganze Zeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you bothering me all the time?

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like harassment (including sexual harassment) or being bothered/annoyed repeatedly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fühlt sich von ihrem Nachbarn belästigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels harassed by her neighbor.

definitions.note: Transitive verb; usually with a direct object (e.g., jemanden belügen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will mich nicht belügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t want to lie to me.

definitions.note: Used with a direct object for the person being lied to (e.g., „Er belügt mich.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er belügt seine Freunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lies to his friends.

definitions.native: to paint (something), to decorate with paint
definitions.note: Often implies painting on something (e.g., a wall, face, eggs) rather than painting a picture.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder bemalen die Ostereier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are painting the Easter eggs.

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I notice")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bemerke den Unterschied sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I notice the difference immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bemerke, dass du heute sehr müde bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I notice that you’re very tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine bemerkenswerte Leistung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a remarkable achievement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat bemerkenswerte Fortschritte gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has made remarkable progress.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bemerkst sofort den Unterschied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You notice the difference immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bemerkt den Fehler sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He notices the mistake right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Problem zu spät bemerkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed the problem too late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bemerkte, dass ich meinen Schlüssel vergessen hatte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed that I had forgotten my key.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bemerkten den Fehler sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We noticed the mistake immediately.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich bemühen. This entry uses the exact form „bemühen“ in the example sentence as requested (infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mich morgen mehr bemühen, pünktlich zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will make more of an effort to be on time.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive verb: sich bemühen (to make an effort).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich bemüht, pünktlich zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried to be on time.

definitions.note: Often used with an object + “über” (about) or “von” (of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte benachrichtigen Sie mich, wenn das Paket ankommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please notify me when the package arrives.

definitions.note: Often used with a person as the direct object (jemanden benachrichtigen) and optionally with „über …“ (about …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich benachrichtigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I notified you.

definitions.note: Often used with „nach“ to mean “named after”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nach seinem Großvater benannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is named after his grandfather.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich benehmen = to behave (oneself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte benehmen Sie sich in der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please behave at school.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) form, often used as a (firm) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Benehmt euch bitte im Museum ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please behave calmly in the museum.

definitions.note: used with accusative: jemanden beneiden
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beneide dich um deinen neuen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I envy you for your new job.

definitions.note: Used with the accusative: jemanden beneiden; often with „um“ + accusative: jemanden um etwas beneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beneide dich um deinen Mut und ich werde dich dafür immer beneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I envy you for your courage, and I will always envy you for it.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/official contexts (e.g., naming a person, a role, or a cause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können Sie den Grund für Ihre Entscheidung benennen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you name the reason for your decision?

definitions.note: informal (du) imperative form of „sich benehmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Benimm dich in der Schule!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Behave at school!

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form of „benimmen“ (to deprive someone of something / to take something away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Benimm ihm das Messer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the knife away from him!

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "sich benehmen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du benimmst dich heute wirklich gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re behaving really well today.

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun: sich benehmen (“to behave”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er benimmt sich in der Schule gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He behaves well at school.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sich benehmen" (to behave). Often used with "haben" and with "sich".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich in der Schule gut benommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He behaved well at school.

definitions.note: Often used to describe feeling mentally unclear (e.g., from sleep, shock, alcohol, or medication).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Operation war ich noch ganz benommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the operation, I was still completely groggy.

definitions.note: Often used to describe how someone feels (e.g. with „sein“ or „sich fühlen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der langen Nacht fühle ich mich ganz benommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long night, I feel completely dazed.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular): used to tell one person to use something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Benutz bitte meinen Stift.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please use my pen.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich) of „benutzen“; also an imperative form (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich benutze jeden Tag mein Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I use my phone every day.

definitions.note: Often used for using an object or tool; in everyday speech, "verwenden" is also common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich deinen Stift benutzen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I use your pen?

definitions.note: Can also be the past participle meaning “used” (e.g., „hat benutzt“ = “has used”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er benutzt sein Handy jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He uses his phone every day.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „benutzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich benutzte gestern den Computer nur kurz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used the computer only briefly yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in a slightly formal or practical sense (e.g., documents, time, materials).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich benötige deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your help.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of "benötigen"; often used in more formal/official contexts than "brauchen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was benötigst du für die Anmeldung?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you need for the registration?

definitions.note: Often sounds more formal than „braucht“ in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er benötigt Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He needs help.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum); can also be Konjunktiv II (same form for weak verbs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich benötigte dringend Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I urgently needed help.

definitions.note: Common in Austrian and Swiss German; in Germany, "benutzen" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst mein Handy benützen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can use my cell phone.

definitions.note: first-person singular present tense ("I")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beobachte die Vögel im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watch the birds in the park.

definitions.note: Often used for watching carefully or over a period of time (e.g., people, animals, situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir beobachten die Vögel im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We observe the birds in the garden.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du) present tense of "beobachten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du beobachtest die Vögel im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You observe the birds in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beobachtet die Vögel im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He observes the birds in the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "beobachten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beobachtete die Vögel im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watched the birds in the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir beobachteten den Vogel im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched the bird in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Sofa ist sehr bequem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sofa is very comfortable.

definitions.note: comparative form of „bequem“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sessel ist bequemer als der Stuhl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The armchair is more comfortable than the chair.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (jemanden beraten) or reflexively (sich beraten) for discussing and deciding together.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin wird die Schüler bei der Berufswahl beraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher will advise the students on their career choice.

definitions.note: Past participle of „berauben“, often used with „jdn. etw. (Genitiv) berauben“ = to deprive someone of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde seines Geldes beraubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was robbed of his money.

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ (to do something) or „auf“ (to something): „zu + Infinitiv“, „auf + Akk.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist berechtigt, eine Pause zu machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are entitled to take a break.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nur berechtigte Personen dürfen hier rein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Only authorized people are allowed in here.

definitions.note: Often means to discuss something thoroughly or to come to an agreement after talking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Problem noch bereden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still need to discuss the problem.

definitions.note: Used with an object (often a country/region), meaning to travel through it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie möchte nächstes Jahr Kanada bereisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to travel around Canada next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat schon viele Länder bereist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has already traveled to many countries.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" (to be ready) or "bereit für/zu" (ready for/to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin bereit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am ready.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „vorbereiten“; in main clauses the prefix often goes to the end (… „vor“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bereite das Abendessen vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prepare dinner.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „zu“ (zubereiten): „Ich bereite … zu.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bereite das Abendessen zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prepare dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bereiten das Abendessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We prepare dinner.

definitions.note: Often used with the separable prefix „vor-“ (→ „vorbereiten“): „Wir bereiten … vor.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bereiten das Meeting vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are preparing the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bereitet das Abendessen vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prepares dinner.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., with "hat" or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat alles gut bereitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prepared everything well.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „vorbereiten“; the prefix „vor“ often goes to the end of the sentence (e.g. „bereitet … vor“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bereitet das Essen vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prepares the food.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix “zu” (zubereiten): “bereitet … zu”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bereitet das Abendessen zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prepares dinner.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „bereiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie bereitete das Frühstück vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prepared breakfast.

definitions.note: Simple past of the separable verb „vorbereiten“; the prefix often appears at the end of the clause (… „vor“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bereitete die Präsentation sorgfältig vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prepared the presentation carefully.

definitions.note: Simple past form used with the separable verb „zubereiten“ (… bereitete … zu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bereitete das Abendessen zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prepared dinner.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „vorbereiten“; in the simple past, the prefix often goes to the end of the clause (… vor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bereiteten das Abendessen vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We prepared dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe bereits gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already eaten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er half bereitwillig bei den Vorbereitungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He willingly helped with the preparations.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I regret").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bereue, dass ich das gesagt habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regret that I said that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bereuen das, was ich gestern gesagt habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regret what I said yesterday.

definitions.note: Second-person singular informal (du) present tense of "bereuen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bereust es später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You regret it later.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g. „Ich bereue es“ = “I regret it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bereut seine Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He regrets his decision.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „bereuen“ (e.g., ich/er/sie bereute).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bereute meine Entscheidung sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regretted my decision immediately.

definitions.note: Can also be Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form, used for hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bereute es später, wenn ich jetzt nicht hingehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would regret it later if I don’t go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Weg geht hier bergab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The path goes downhill here.

definitions.note: Often used for rescuing/recovering people or things (e.g., from the sea, from rubble).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr konnte den Mann aus dem Auto bergen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department was able to rescue the man from the car.

definitions.note: Common in formal/reporting contexts for retrieving something from a difficult place (water, debris, wreckage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Taucher mussten das Wrack aus dem Fluss bergen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Divers had to salvage the wreck from the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeitung muss heute ausführlich über den Unfall berichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper has to report in detail on the accident today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er berichtet jeden Tag über das Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reports on the weather every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wurde berichtet, dass der Zug verspätet ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was reported that the train is delayed.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „berichten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er berichtete von dem Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reported about the accident.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „berichtigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er berichtigte den Fehler sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He corrected the mistake right away.

definitions.note: Often written with a capital B as a proper adjective: „Berliner“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine berliner Spezialität.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a Berlin specialty.

definitions.note: often used with an object: jemanden (in eine Position) berufen
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Universität will eine neue Professorin berufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The university wants to appoint a new professor.

definitions.native: to cite, to invoke (as a reason or authority)
definitions.note: commonly used reflexively: sich auf etwas berufen (but example uses the exact form „berufen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will sich auf das Gesetz berufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to invoke the law (as his authority).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin beruflich in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am in Berlin for work.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“: „auf etw. beruhen“ = to be based on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Entscheidung wird auf den aktuellen Zahlen beruhen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision will be based on the current figures.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form, used when addressing one person with „du“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beruhig dich, es ist alles in Ordnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down, everything is fine.

definitions.note: Imperative (du-form) of "beruhigen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beruhige dich bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please calm down!

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as „sich beruhigen“ = to calm down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich beruhigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to calm you down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Musik ist sehr beruhigend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music is very calming.

definitions.note: Can mean 'calm' in the sense of becoming calm or making someone calm, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das beruhigt mich ein bisschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That calms me down a little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin jetzt beruhigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m calm now.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „beruhigen“; often used with a direct object (someone you calm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mutter beruhigte ihr Kind schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mother calmed her child quickly.

definitions.note: Usually used with "auf" (on/upon): "beruht auf".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Missverständnis beruht auf einem Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The misunderstanding is based on a mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt berät die Patientin über die Behandlung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor advises the patient about the treatment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen deine Meinung berücksichtigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to take your opinion into account.

definitions.note: past participle of "berücksichtigen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Meinung wird berücksichtigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your opinion is being taken into account.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Berlin ist für seine Geschichte berühmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Berlin is famous for its history.

definitions.note: inflected form used before a noun (e.g., with der/die/das or other determiners)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die berühmte Schauspielerin kommt aus Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The famous actress comes from Berlin.

definitions.note: adjective with ending (e.g., after a definite article or in certain cases)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben den berühmten Schauspieler gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw the famous actor.

definitions.note: comparative form of „berühmt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist noch berühmter als ihr Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is even more famous than her brother.

definitions.note: Superlative form of the adjective „berühmt“; used with a definite article or as a noun (e.g., „die Berühmteste“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die berühmteste Brücke der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the most famous bridge in the city.

definitions.note: First-person singular present subjunctive (or imperative in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte pass auf, dass ich das heiße Blech nicht berühre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please make sure that I don’t touch the hot sheet metal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte berühren Sie das Kunstwerk nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don't touch the artwork.

definitions.note: Often used about feelings or people being emotionally moved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Rede konnte viele Menschen berühren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The speech could move many people.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum berührst du das Bild nicht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you touch the picture?

definitions.note: Can mean literal physical contact or being emotionally moved ("touched").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er berührt den Tisch mit der Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He touches the table with his hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte iss das Brot nicht, es ist schon berührt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t eat the bread; it has already been touched.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin von deiner Nachricht sehr berührt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very moved by your message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er berührte den Knopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He touched the button.

definitions.note: Mostly used in formal/official language (e.g., contracts, rules).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag besagt, dass du bis Ende des Monats zahlen musst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract states that you have to pay by the end of the month.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „besitzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er besaß ein altes Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had an old car.

definitions.note: Often used for getting something you need (e.g., documents, information, supplies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Unterlagen bis morgen beschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to obtain the documents by tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often describes a person who doesn’t show off, or something that is not very large/impressive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr bescheiden und spricht kaum über ihre Erfolge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very modest and hardly talks about her successes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine bescheidene Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a modest apartment.

definitions.note: Used as an inflected adjective form (e.g., after an article or in certain cases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt aus einer bescheidenen Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes from a modest family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein bescheidener Mann spricht nicht viel über seine Erfolge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A modest man doesn’t talk much about his successes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist bescheidener als ihr Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is more modest than her brother.

definitions.native: to cheat, to rip someone off
definitions.note: Vulgar/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich nicht bescheißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to cheat you.

definitions.note: Informal and insulting; can be used jokingly among friends depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine bescheuerte Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a stupid idea.

definitions.note: colloquial and insulting/vulgar
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Lust auf diese bescheuerten Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not in the mood for these stupid rules.

definitions.note: Often implies rude, angry name-calling; typically used with an object (jemanden beschimpfen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann will den Schiedsrichter beschimpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man wants to insult the referee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beschimpft seinen Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He insults his neighbor.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist echt beschissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really shitty.

definitions.note: Very informal/vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich beschissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cheated me / He screwed me over.

definitions.note: very informal and vulgar
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine beschissene Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a shitty idea.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar; often used to complain about something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Lust auf diese beschissenen Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel like dealing with these shitty rules.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/impolite slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein noch beschissener Plan als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s an even shittier plan than yesterday.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein beschissenes Wetter heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is really shitty today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto kann in wenigen Sekunden von 0 auf 100 km/h beschleunigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car can accelerate from 0 to 100 km/h in a few seconds.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „beschleunigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beschleunigte das Auto auf der Autobahn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accelerated the car on the highway.

definitions.note: Simple past of „beschließen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stadtrat beschloss, den Park zu renovieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city council decided to renovate the park.

definitions.note: past participle of „beschließen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben beschlossen, morgen früher zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided to leave earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: Old spelling of „beschloss“ (simple past of „beschließen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stadtrat beschloß, den Park zu renovieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city council decided to renovate the park.

definitions.native: to trim, to prune, to cut back
definitions.note: Often used for cutting back plants/hedges or for cropping an image (e.g., a photo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Frühjahr muss man die Rosen beschneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring you have to prune the roses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt wird das Kind beschneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor will circumcise the child.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I describe") or imperative singular ("describe!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte beschreibe, was passiert ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please describe what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du den Mann beschreiben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you describe the man?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "beschreiben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Artikel beschreibt die Situation sehr genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The article describes the situation very precisely.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „beschreiben“

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat den Mann genau beschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She described the man precisely.

definitions.note: Often used as: „jemanden beschuldigen, etwas getan zu haben“ or „jemanden beschuldigen, etwas zu tun“ (accuse someone of something).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is accused of having taken the money.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you accusing me without evidence?

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the accusative: jemanden beschuldigen (to accuse someone), often with a clause or „wegen“ + Genitive/„für“ + Accusative to say what they’re accused of.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accuses me of having lied.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beschuldigte seinen Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accused his neighbor.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich beschweren (über + Akk.)“ = to complain (about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mich über den Lärm beschweren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to complain about the noise.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: sich beschweren (to complain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beschwert sich über das Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He complains about the food.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach zwei Gläsern Wein war sie schon beschwipst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After two glasses of wine, she was already tipsy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte beschädigen Sie das Buch nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t damage the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy ist beschädigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is damaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beschädigte Ware wird zurückgeschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The damaged goods will be sent back.

definitions.note: In this sense, it takes a direct object (a person or people employed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma wird in der Hochsaison zusätzliches Personal beschäftigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the high season, the company will employ additional staff.

definitions.note: Also common reflexively (sich beschäftigen) meaning ‘to keep oneself busy,’ but here shown with a direct object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Rätsel wird die Kinder den ganzen Nachmittag beschäftigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The puzzle will keep the children occupied all afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (past participle of „beschäftigen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade beschäftigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m busy right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade beschäftigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m busy right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Verhalten war wirklich beschämend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior was really embarrassing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war nach dem Streit sehr beschämt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was very ashamed after the argument.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I protect") or imperative singular ("protect!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beschütze mein Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I protect my child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich beschützen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to protect you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beschützt seine kleine Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He protects his little sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das Kind beschützt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He protected the child.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "beschützen" (e.g., "ich/er/sie/es beschützte").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beschützte das Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He protected the child.

definitions.note: Often used for getting rid of a problem, obstacle, or danger (more formal than "wegmachen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Problem schnell beseitigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to eliminate the problem quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hausmeister beseitigt das Laub vor dem Eingang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The janitor removes the leaves in front of the entrance.

definitions.note: Often used with „von“ + dative: „besessen von (etwas/jemandem)“ = obsessed with (something/someone).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is obsessed with video games.

definitions.note: Used especially in the sense of being controlled by a spirit/demon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Film wirkt sie plötzlich besessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie she suddenly seems possessed.

definitions.note: past participle of „besitzen“ (usually used with „haben“ in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat früher ein kleines Haus besessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used to own a small house.

definitions.note: often used for seats/places, rooms, or positions that are already taken
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Platz ist besetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This seat is taken.

definitions.note: Often used for visiting a place as a sightseer, or viewing a building/object (e.g., a museum, a city, an apartment) to look around.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besichtigen morgen das Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re touring the castle tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er besichtigt das Museum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He visits the museum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die Wohnung besichtigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We inspected the apartment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Deal ist besiegelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The deal is sealed.

definitions.note: Often used for defeating an opponent/enemy (in sports, games, or conflict).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Mannschaft konnte den Gegner endlich besiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team was finally able to defeat the opponent.

definitions.note: Past participle of „besiegen“; also used as the 3rd person singular present form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mannschaft hat den Gegner besiegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team has defeated the opponent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Spiel war die Mannschaft besiegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the game, the team was defeated.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present of „besitzen“ (ich besitze).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besitze kein Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t own a car.

definitions.note: Often used for owning something (property, a car, a house); also for having a quality or ability.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird ein kleines Auto besitzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will own a small car.

definitions.note: Used to describe someone who wants to control another person and doesn’t like them spending time with others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr besitzergreifend und wird schnell eifersüchtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very possessive and gets jealous quickly.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „besitzen“ (er/sie/es).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er besitzt ein altes Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He owns an old house.

definitions.note: colloquial, often a bit crude
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war gestern Abend total besoffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was totally drunk last night.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive form), e.g. feminine singular or plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine besondere Fähigkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a special ability.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive) as an inflected form of "besonders".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen besonderen Wunsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a special wish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein besonderer Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is a special day.

definitions.note: neuter form; often used in phrases like „etwas Besonderes“ (“something special”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute machen wir etwas Besonderes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re doing something special.

definitions.note: Often used with etwas/nichts (e.g., etwas Besonderes = something special).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe etwas Besonderes für dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have something special for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag besonders den Schokoladenkuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I especially like the chocolate cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag besonders den Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I especially like the cake.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative (command), e.g. “Besorg …!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Besorg bitte Milch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please get some milk.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative (command), especially in “Besorg das!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, ich besorg das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, I’ll take care of that.

definitions.note: Often used when you get something for someone or arrange something (e.g., tickets, groceries).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besorge dir die Tickets.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll get you the tickets.

definitions.note: Often used for getting something you need (e.g., buying or picking it up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch Milch besorgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still need to get some milk.

definitions.native: to take care of, to handle
definitions.note: Common in phrases like „Ich besorge das.“ meaning you will do it / handle it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, ich besorge das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, I’ll take care of it.

definitions.note: From „besorgen“: commonly means to get/obtain something or to take care of something (run an errand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er besorgt die Tickets für das Konzert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets the tickets for the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin besorgt, weil du so spät nach Hause kommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m worried because you’re coming home so late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besorgte noch schnell Brot für das Abendessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I quickly got some bread for dinner.

definitions.note: simple past of „besprechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er besprach den Plan mit dem Team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He discussed the plan with the team.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „besprechen“ (used especially in writing and storytelling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besprachen den Plan nach dem Meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We discussed the plan after the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a topic or plan): etwas (Akk.) besprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besprechen morgen den Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll discuss the plan tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of „besprechen“; often used with „haben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben das gestern besprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We discussed that yesterday.

definitions.note: comparative form of „gut“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute geht es mir besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel better today.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „gut“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute geht es mir besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m feeling better.

definitions.note: comparative form of „gut“, used as a declined adjective before a noun (e.g. „eine bessere …“).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a better explanation.

definitions.note: comparative, inflected form of "gut"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche einen besseren Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a better job.

definitions.note: comparative form used with an implied or expressed neuter noun (e.g., „etwas Besseres“, „nichts Besseres“)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to improve my German.

definitions.note: Usually used for passing an exam or test (preterite of „bestehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bestand die Prüfung beim ersten Versuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He passed the exam on the first try.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building already existed in the 18th century.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Prüfung bestanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed the exam.

definitions.note: superlative form of „gut“ (used before a noun, e.g. „die beste …“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die beste Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the best idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unternehmer wollte den Beamten bestechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The businessman wanted to bribe the official.

definitions.note: Often used with exams and tests (e.g., „die Prüfung bestehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Prüfung bestehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pass the exam.

definitions.note: Often used with „aus“ (e.g., „aus drei Teilen bestehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs wird aus fünf Teilen bestehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course will consist of five parts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du so weiterlernst, bestehst du die Prüfung sicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you keep studying like this, you’ll definitely pass the exam.

definitions.note: Often used with „aus“ (e.g., „bestehen aus“ = „to consist of“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Team bestehst du und drei andere Leute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team consists of you and three other people.

definitions.note: Often used with "aus" (e.g., "besteht aus").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs besteht aus zehn Lektionen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Problem besteht schon lange.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He passes the exam on the second try.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to climb the mountain.

definitions.native: to board, to get on (a train/ship/plane)

definitions.note: Informal command form (du imperative) of "bestellen".

definitions.note: Used for ordering food or goods (e.g., in a restaurant or online).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bestelle eine Pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I order a pizza.

definitions.note: Used for ordering goods, food, or services (placing an order).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bestellen eine Pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I order a pizza.

definitions.native: to order (someone) to do something; to assign/appoint

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will order him to come to the office.

definitions.note: past participle of „bestellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Pizza bestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ordered a pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bestellte eine Pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ordered a pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered a pizza.

definitions.note: Plural form used as a noun (often referring to the best people or things in a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Besten gewinnen am Ende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The best win in the end.

definitions.note: superlative form of „gut“; often used as „die besten …“ (the best …) or „am besten“ (best, the best)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die besten Freunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the best friends.

definitions.note: Often used like an adverb, e.g. with verbs such as „klappen“, „gehen“, „verstehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat bestens geklappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That worked out very well.

definitions.note: Used to say something is the maximum you can expect, often with a number or estimate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt heute bestens um acht Uhr nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At best, he'll be home today by eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like „alles bestens“ (“everything’s great”) or „bestens bekannt“ (“well-known”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir geht es bestens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m doing very well.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "bestens bekannt" (well-known) or "bestens vorbereitet" (well-prepared).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin bestens vorbereitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very well prepared.

definitions.note: superlative form of „gut“; often used with masculine singular nouns (e.g., „mein bester Freund“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist mein bester Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is my best friend.

definitions.note: Superlative form of „gut“. „bestes“ is used with neuter singular nouns (e.g., „bestes Essen“, „bestes Ergebnis“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist bestes Essen, das ich je gegessen habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the best food I have ever eaten.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „besteigen“; used for mountains (climb) and vehicles (board).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbed the mountain early in the morning.

definitions.note: Past participle of „besteigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Berg bestiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbed the mountain.

definitions.note: Past participle of „besteigen“, often used for vehicles (e.g., bus, train).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She boarded the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen noch bestimmen, wann wir anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still have to decide when we’ll start.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gesetz bestimmt, wer wählen darf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The law determines who is allowed to vote.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun: „eine bestimmte Sache“ = “a specific thing.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have certain questions.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time on a certain day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche ein bestimmtes Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a specific book.

definitions.note: Past participle of „bestechen“.

definitions.note: past participle of „bestehlen“; often used with „werden“ (passive) to mean someone was robbed.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge will punish the offender.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cannot deny that he took the money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bestreitet die Vorwürfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denies the accusations.

definitions.note: Often used with expenses/costs (e.g., „die Kosten bestreiten“).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supports herself / pays her own living expenses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bestritt, dass er das Geld genommen hatte.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die Vorwürfe bestritten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denied the accusations.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts to mean something happens again and again over time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können Sie den Termin bitte bestätigen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please confirm the appointment?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bestätigt den Termin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confirms the appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Termin bestätigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I confirmed the appointment.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „bestätigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bestätigte den Termin am Telefon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confirmed the appointment on the phone.

definitions.note: Often used to describe being upset or taken aback by unexpected bad news.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was shocked by the news.

definitions.note: Colloquial/short form of the verb „besuchen“ (often used in speech, e.g. „Ich besuch dich morgen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besuch dich morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll visit you tomorrow.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense ("I visit"), or imperative (informal singular: "visit!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besuche meine Großeltern am Wochenende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I visit my grandparents on the weekend.

definitions.note: Used for visiting people or places (including a city, museum, doctor, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will morgen meine Großeltern besuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to visit my grandparents tomorrow.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Besuchst du deine Oma am Sonntag?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you visiting your grandma on Sunday?

definitions.note: present tense: 3rd person singular or 2nd person plural; can also be the past participle (“visited”) depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er besucht seine Großeltern jeden Sonntag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He visits his grandparents every Sunday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Museum ist heute besucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum is visited today.

definitions.note: Often used with "gut" (e.g., "gut besucht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert war gut besucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was well-attended.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „besuchen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr besuchte ich meine Großeltern in Hamburg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I visited my grandparents in Hamburg.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „besuchen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchten gestern unsere Großeltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited our grandparents yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bete jeden Abend vor dem Schlafengehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pray every evening before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Often used with „sich“: „sich an (etw.) beteiligen“ = to participate in / take part in (something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Studierende beteiligen sich an der Diskussion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many students take part in the discussion.

definitions.note: Used with an object (often people) to mean bringing them into a process or decision.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen alle Mitarbeitenden an der Entscheidung beteiligen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to involve all employees in the decision.

definitions.note: Often used with „an“ + dative (e.g. „an etwas beteiligt sein“ = to be involved in something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist an dem Projekt beteiligt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is involved in the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute Abend in der Kirche beten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will pray in church this evening.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „beten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betet jeden Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prays every evening.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „beten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betete jeden Abend vor dem Schlafengehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prayed every evening before going to sleep.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie beteten jeden Abend vor dem Schlafengehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They prayed every evening before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte betonen, dass das sehr wichtig ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to emphasize that this is very important.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „betonen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betonte, wie wichtig das Problem ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He emphasized how important the problem is.

definitions.note: Often a bit more formal than just „ansehen“; can also mean “consider” in the sense of thinking about something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich betrachte das Bild an der Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I look at the picture on the wall.

definitions.note: Often used in a more deliberate or thoughtful way than just "sehen" (to see).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir betrachten das Bild ganz genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We look at the picture very closely.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "betrachten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du betrachtest das Bild ganz genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look at the picture very carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betrachtet das Bild ganz genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks at the picture very closely.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of "betrachten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betrachtete das Bild lange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked at the picture for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir betrachteten das Bild ganz genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We looked at the picture very carefully.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form, usually used with the reflexive pronoun: sich betrinken
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betrank sich auf der Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got drunk at the party.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "betreten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betrat leise das Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He entered the room quietly.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "betreten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir betraten das Gebäude durch den Haupteingang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We entered the building through the main entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie betrauerte den Verlust ihres Großvaters.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She mourned the loss of her grandfather.

definitions.note: Often used for running a business/organization or operating a facility/website (e.g., ein Geschäft/eine Website betreiben).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird in der Innenstadt ein kleines Café betreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will run a small café in the city center.

definitions.note: Often used with a business or institution as the object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie betreibt ein kleines Café in der Innenstadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She runs a small café in the city center.

definitions.note: Common with sports or hobbies (e.g., Sport, Yoga).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betreibt jeden Morgen Sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He does sports every morning.

definitions.note: Often used for entering a place/area (sometimes formally, e.g. on signs: „Nicht betreten!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte betreten Sie den Raum nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please do not enter the room.

definitions.note: Often used for caring for or supervising someone (e.g., children, patients) or being responsible for a group/project.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Kinder am Nachmittag betreuen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will look after the children in the afternoon.

definitions.native: looks after, takes care of, supervises
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betreut die Kinder nach der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks after the children after school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich betreute die Kinder am Nachmittag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked after the children in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Past participle of "betreiben"; often used in passive constructions with "werden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anlage wird mit Solarenergie betrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The facility is operated with solar energy.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts; common in phrases like „Das betrifft …“ / „Was mich betrifft …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das betrifft nur dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That only concerns you.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich betrinken.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich heute Abend nicht betrinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to get drunk tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betritt das Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He enters the room.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du betrittst das Gebäude durch den Haupteingang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You enter the building through the main entrance.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who is affected by something (e.g., an event, a problem) or looks emotionally moved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen sind von den neuen Regeln betroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people are affected by the new rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betrog seine Freunde und nahm das Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deceived his friends and took the money.

definitions.note: past participle of „betrügen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wurde betrogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was cheated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war gestern Abend betrunken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was drunk last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den betrunkenen Mann auf der Straße gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw the drunk man on the street.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine beträchtliche Summe Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a considerable sum of money.

definitions.note: Used for numbers/quantities (e.g., price, distance, total).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gesamtpreis beträgt 25 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The total price comes to 25 euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das betrübt mich sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That saddens me a lot.

definitions.note: Often used for a somewhat formal or serious-sounding “sad.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist betrübt, weil ihr Hund krank ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is sad because her dog is sick.

definitions.native: to cheat; to deceive; to defraud
definitions.note: Used for deceiving someone (e.g., in business) and also for cheating on a partner. In example sentences below, the infinitive is used exactly as „betrügen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will mich nicht betrügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t want to deceive me.

definitions.note: Often used for cheating in a relationship (cheating on someone), or deceiving/scamming someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er betrügt seine Frau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is cheating on his wife.

definitions.note: often used for begging for money or asking insistently for something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss jeden Tag auf der Straße betteln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to beg on the street every day.

definitions.note: simple past of „betteln“ (to beg)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bettelte um Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I begged for help.

definitions.note: (something) to bend; often used with body parts or objects
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beugen das Knie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bend my knee.

definitions.note: to bow (oneself), e.g., out of respect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir beugen uns vor dem Publikum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bow to the audience.

definitions.note: to yield to a rule, pressure, or authority (often: sich beugen + Dativ)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie beugen sich dem Druck.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They yield to the pressure.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „beugen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beugte sich vor, um das Schild besser zu lesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bent forward to read the sign better.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective/participle meaning someone feels worried or something causes worry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin beunruhigt, weil er noch nicht zu Hause ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m worried because he isn’t home yet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin wegen der Prüfung beunruhigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m worried about the exam.

definitions.note: Often used for forming an opinion or evaluation of something (e.g., a situation, performance, or case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das nicht beurteilen, ohne mehr Informationen zu haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't judge that without having more information.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of forming an opinion or evaluation about something/someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin beurteilt die Aufsätze sehr streng.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher judges the essays very strictly.

definitions.note: often used as a conjunction with a following clause: bevor + sentence (e.g., bevor ich gehe …)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich an, bevor ich losfahre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you before I leave.

definitions.note: used to introduce a subordinate clause (often with the verb at the end)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich an, bevor ich losfahre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you before I leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ruf mich an, bevor du losfährst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call me before you leave.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense (ich) of "bevorzugen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bevorzuge Tee statt Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer tea instead of coffee.

definitions.note: often used with: „etw. (Akk.) bevorzugen“ or „etw. gegenüber etw. bevorzugen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde in diesem Fall Tee statt Kaffee bevorzugen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this case, I will prefer tea over coffee.

definitions.note: often used in contexts like hiring, selection, or rules
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma darf keine Bewerber aufgrund ihres Alters bevorzugen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company must not favor any applicants because of their age.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bevorzugst du Tee oder Kaffee?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you prefer tea or coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bevorzugt Kaffee ohne Zucker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He prefers coffee without sugar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Berlin ist nicht die bevölkerungsreichste Stadt Deutschlands.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Berlin is not the most populous city in Germany.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (or imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bewache den Eingang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guard the entrance.

definitions.note: Often used for guarding a person, place, or object (e.g., by police or security).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei muss das Gebäude bewachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have to guard the building.

definitions.note: past participle of "bewachen"; also used like an adjective (e.g., "ein bewachtes Gebäude" = "a guarded building").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gebäude wird rund um die Uhr bewacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building is guarded around the clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei suchte nach einem bewaffneten Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were searching for an armed man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die bewaffneten Männer stehen vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The armed men are standing in front of the door.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bewahre die Briefe in einer Schublade auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I keep the letters in a drawer.

definitions.note: Often used for keeping something safe or keeping it in good condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte bewahren Sie den Kassenbon gut auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please keep the receipt in a safe place.

definitions.note: Can also be used as a past participle (e.g. with "haben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bewahrt das Foto in einer Schublade auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He keeps the photo in a drawer.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of "bewahren"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bewahrte den Brief in einer Schublade auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kept the letter in a drawer.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive: „sich um + Akk.“ (to apply for something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bewarb sich um die Stelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He applied for the position.

definitions.note: Informal imperative (du-form) of "bewegen"; often used as "Beweg dich!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beweg dich, wir müssen los!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move, we have to go!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I move") of "bewegen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bewege den Stuhl näher an den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I move the chair closer to the table.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as „sich bewegen“ (= to move oneself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich mehr bewegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to move more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bewegst den Stuhl ein bisschen nach links.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You move the chair a little to the left.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "bewegen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind bewegt die Blätter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind moves the leaves.

definitions.note: past participle of "bewegen" (used in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Rede hat mich bewegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The speech moved me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wasser ist ständig bewegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is constantly in motion.

definitions.note: Often used about feelings after a meaningful experience or story.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin sehr bewegt von deiner Rede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very moved by your speech.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of "bewegen"; common in written narratives
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind bewegte die Blätter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind moved the leaves.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), typically for „we/they“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bewegten den Tisch in die Ecke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We moved the table into the corner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund lag bewegungslos auf dem Teppich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog lay motionless on the carpet.

definitions.note: Colloquial/contracted form of „beweise“ (standard: „ich beweise“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beweis dir, dass ich recht habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll prove to you that I’m right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beweise dir, dass ich recht habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prove to you that I'm right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das beweisen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you prove that?
