definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "beweisen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das beweist, dass er recht hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That proves that he is right.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively as „sich bewerben“; commonly with „um“ (for a position) and/or „bei“ (at a company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bewerben mich um einen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m applying for a job.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of "beweisen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bewies seine Unschuld vor Gericht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He proved his innocence in court.

definitions.note: Past participle of „beweisen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat es bewiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He proved it.

definitions.note: Often used for causing a (usually concrete) effect or result.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neuen Maßnahmen sollen eine Verbesserung bewirken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new measures are supposed to bring about an improvement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neue Regel bewirkt, dass weniger Müll entsteht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new rule causes less trash to be produced.

definitions.note: Past participle of „bewegen“ often used in a figurative sense (e.g. „sich bewogen fühlen“, „sich zu etwas bewogen sehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fühlte sich durch seine Worte bewogen, zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt persuaded by his words to leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bewohnt eine kleine Wohnung in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in a small apartment in Berlin.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive verb: sich bewerben (um + accusative = for a position; bei + dative = at a company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich um die Stelle beworben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He applied for the position.

definitions.note: Often used in passive: (etwas) wird beworben = (something) is advertised/promoted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das neue Produkt wurde stark beworben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new product was heavily advertised.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich) or imperative (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bewundere deinen Mut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admire your courage.

definitions.note: to feel respect/approval for someone or something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich wirklich bewundern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can really admire you.

definitions.native: to marvel at; to view with admiration
definitions.note: often used when looking at something impressive (e.g., art, scenery)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Touristen bewundern die Kathedrale.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tourists admire the cathedral.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Mut ist wirklich bewundernswert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your courage is really admirable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bewundert ihre Arbeit sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admires her work a lot.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "bewundern"; can mean "admired" or "was admiring" depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bewunderte das Gemälde im Museum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admired the painting in the museum.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural or polite form (Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie bewunderten die Aussicht vom Berg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They admired the view from the mountain.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition like „bewusst sein, dass …“ (to be aware that …) or „sich (etw.) bewusst sein“ (to be aware of something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mir bewusst, dass das schwierig ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aware that this is difficult.

definitions.note: used for a person who has lost consciousness (e.g., after an accident or fainting)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall war er bewusstlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was unconscious.

definitions.note: Spelling note: also written as „bewusstlos“ in modern German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er liegt bewußtlos auf dem Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is lying unconscious on the floor.

definitions.note: Often used for dealing successfully with a difficult situation, task, or emotion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie muss den Stress bei der Arbeit bewältigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to cope with the stress at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es bewölkt, aber es regnet nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s cloudy, but it isn’t raining.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative ("Bezahl!" = "Pay!"). In speech it can also be a shortened form of "bezahle" ("I pay").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bezahl bitte an der Kasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pay at the checkout.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of „bezahlen“ (ich bezahle = I pay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezahle die Rechnung jetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m paying the bill now.

definitions.note: Often used for paying a bill or paying for something in a shop/restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte bitte mit Karte bezahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to pay by card, please.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bezahlst du bar oder mit Karte?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you paying with cash or by card?

definitions.note: past participle of „bezahlen“; also used like an adjective meaning “paid” (e.g., a paid bill)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe schon bezahlt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already paid.

definitions.note: simple past form; in everyday spoken German, people often use the present perfect instead ("habe bezahlt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezahlte gestern die Rechnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I paid the bill yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural (wir/ihr/sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bezahlten die Rechnung sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We paid the bill right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ein bezauberndes Lächeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a charming smile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine bezaubernde Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a charming idea.

definitions.note: Often used with “als” to say what someone/something is called or considered to be.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man kann dieses Verhalten als unfair bezeichnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can describe this behavior as unfair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bezeichnet sie als seine beste Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He calls her his best friend.

definitions.note: Often used for labeling things (e.g., on a map, a bottle, or a form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte bezeichnet die Flaschen mit dem Datum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please label the bottles with the date.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Reporter bezeichnete den Vorfall als Skandal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reporter called the incident a scandal.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts to confirm that something is true or that you witnessed it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zeuge kann bezeugen, dass er den Unfall gesehen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness can testify that he saw the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zeuge bezichtigte ihn des Diebstahls.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness accused him of theft.

definitions.note: Often used with payments/benefits (e.g., salary, pension).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beziehe mein Gehalt am Monatsende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I receive my salary at the end of the month.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase „sich auf etwas beziehen“ (to refer to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich beziehe mich auf deine letzte E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m referring to your last email.

definitions.note: Commonly used with housing: „eine Wohnung / ein Haus beziehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen nächste Woche die neue Wohnung beziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to move into the new apartment next week.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "beziehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Woher beziehst du deine Informationen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you get your information from?

definitions.note: Often used with money/benefits (e.g., „Geld beziehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bezog drei Monate lang Arbeitslosengeld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He received unemployment benefits for three months.

definitions.note: Common in the expression „sich auf etwas beziehen“ (= to refer to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezog mich auf deinen letzten Kommentar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I referred to your last comment.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition like „auf“: „auf etwas bezogen“ = related to / referring to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Frage ist auf das letzte Kapitel bezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The question relates to the last chapter.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „in Bezug auf“ = “regarding / with reference to”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Frage in Bezug auf deine E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a question regarding your email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bezug vom Kissen ist in der Waschmaschine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pillowcase is in the washing machine.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I) of "bezweifeln"; also identical in form to 1st-person singular present indicative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezweifele, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubt that he’s coming today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bezweifelte, dass sie heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doubted that she would come today.

definitions.note: Used with the verb „bezweifeln“ + accusative object or a „dass“-clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezweifle, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubt that he’s coming today.

definitions.note: Often used for overcoming an enemy, an obstacle, or your own feelings (self-control).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie muss ihre Angst bezwingen und vor der Klasse sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to overcome her fear and speak in front of the class.

definitions.note: Often used with the genitive (more formal), but also commonly with "zu" + dative in everyday German: "bezüglich der Sache" / "bezüglich der Sache" / "bezüglich der Sache"; "bezüglich der Rechnung" or "bezüglich der Rechnung"; "bezüglich der Rechnung".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bezüglich Ihrer Anfrage melden wir uns morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Regarding your inquiry, we’ll get back to you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich beängstigend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really frightening.

definitions.note: Often implies looking at something with suspicion or careful scrutiny.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beäugte das Angebot misstrauisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He eyed the offer suspiciously.

definitions.note: Often used with directions when driving (e.g., „links/rechts biege“ = „I turn left/right“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich biege an der nächsten Kreuzung links ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turn left at the next intersection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst links abbiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to turn left.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of „anbieten“ (ich biete … an).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich biete dir meine Hilfe an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offer you my help.

definitions.note: Often used with a separable prefix, e.g. „anbieten“: „Wir bieten Hilfe an.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bieten dir Hilfe an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We offer you help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir einen Kaffee bieten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can offer you a coffee.

definitions.note: From the separable verb "anbieten"; in main clauses the prefix often comes at the end ("bietet ... an").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bietet mir einen Kaffee an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He offers me a coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Café bietet auch vegane Kuchen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The café also offers vegan cakes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schule bietet kostenlose Nachhilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school provides free tutoring.

definitions.note: Informal English loanword; common in fixed phrases like „big deal“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine big Überraschung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a big surprise.

definitions.note: Often used with things like „eine Gruppe/ein Team bilden“ (= to form a group/team). It can look like English “build,” but it usually means “form” rather than build (construction).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bilde mit meinen Freunden eine Gruppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I form a group with my friends.

definitions.note: Usually used as part of the reflexive phrase „sich einbilden“ (e.g. „ich bilde mir ein …“), often meaning to imagine something that isn’t true.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bilde mir ein, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagine that he’s coming today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schülerinnen und Schüler bilden einen Kreis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students form a circle.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like education or training (e.g., sich bilden = to educate oneself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lehrkräfte bilden Kinder und Jugendliche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Teachers educate children and teenagers.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of "bilden"; used with "du".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bildest einen Satz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You form a sentence.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively with „sich“: „sich (etwas) einbilden“ = to imagine something (often wrongly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bildest dir das nur ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re just imagining that.

definitions.note: often used with „sich bilden“ = to form (itself)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus zwei Teilen bildet sich ein Ganzes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Out of two parts, a whole forms.

definitions.note: Often used as the separable, reflexive verb „sich (etwas) einbilden“ (e.g. „Er bildet sich das ein.“ = He imagines/makes that up.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bildet sich das nur ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s just imagining that.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural (“they”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie bildeten einen Kreis um das Feuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They formed a circle around the fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schuhe sind billig, aber sie halten nicht lange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are cheap, but they don’t last long.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (e.g., plural or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben billige Tickets gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought cheap tickets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kaufen billigen Käse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We buy cheap cheese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Ticket ist billiger als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ticket is cheaper than the other one.

definitions.note: Inflected comparative form of „billig“ (e.g., with a definite/indefinite article: „die/eine billigere …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme die billigere Option.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll take the cheaper option.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "sein" (used with "ich").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am tired.

definitions.note: First-person singular present ("I ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich binde meine Schuhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tie my shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst deine Schuhe binden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to tie your shoes.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "binden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bindet seine Schuhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ties his shoes.

definitions.note: sound effect (e.g., a bell/chime or a “ding” sound)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bing! Und schon war die E-Mail da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bing! And the email was already there.

definitions.note: nonstandard spelling of the colloquial contraction „bin’s“ (= „bin es“), used in phrases like „Ich bins.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s me.

definitions.note: Often used on product labels; can also appear as a prefix (e.g., Bio-Milch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe lieber bio Gemüse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer to buy organic vegetables.

definitions.note: Used with times, dates, or limits; often followed by a dative noun phrase (e.g., bis nächsten Montag).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bleibe bis morgen hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll stay here until tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used for time (and sometimes places/limits), often with a specific time/date or with another clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warte bitte, bis ich zurück bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait until I’m back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist bisexuell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is bisexual.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bisher hat es nicht geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So far it hasn’t rained.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bislang habe ich noch keine Antwort bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So far I still haven't gotten an answer.

definitions.note: simple past of „beißen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund biss mich in die Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog bit me on the hand.

definitions.note: Often used in the set phrase "ein bisschen" (= a little).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du ein bisschen langsamer sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you speak a bit more slowly?

definitions.note: Often used with "ein" as "ein bisschen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte ein bisschen langsamer sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak a little more slowly?

definitions.note: Very common in the phrase „ein bisschen“ (= a little/a bit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du ein bisschen langsamer sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you speak a little more slowly?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of "sein" (used with "du")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist heute sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are very tired today.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/literary; in everyday speech, "manchmal" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bisweilen gehe ich nach der Arbeit noch spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I go for a walk after work.

definitions.note: Used to make a request more polite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please help me?

definitions.note: Used as a reply to “Danke”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke! – Bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks! – You're welcome!

definitions.note: Often used to ask someone to repeat what they said (e.g., “Wie bitte?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie bitte? Ich habe dich nicht verstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pardon? I didn’t understand you.

definitions.note: Used to make a request more polite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte, sprechen Sie langsamer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Used as a response to “Danke”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: – Danke! – Bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: – Thanks! – You're welcome!

definitions.note: Used as a polite word when asking for something; also commonly used on its own to mean “please” (e.g., when offering or requesting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte gib mir das Salz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please give me the salt.

definitions.note: Often used with „um“ + accusative + „bitten“: „jemanden um etwas bitten“ = to ask someone for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich dich um einen Gefallen bitten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I ask you for a favor?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kaffee ist bitter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is bitter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lachte bitter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He laughed bitterly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine bittere Wahrheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a bitter truth.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „bitter“ (used with certain endings, e.g. before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag keinen bitteren Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like bitter coffee.

definitions.note: Stronger than just „kalt“; often used for very harsh winter weather.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Draußen ist es heute bitterkalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's bitterly cold outside today.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „weinen“ (to cry) or „klagen“ (to complain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind weinte bitterlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child cried bitterly.

definitions.note: Used politely when handing something to someone or as a response to “thank you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitteschön, hier ist dein Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here you go, here is your coffee.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „bitten“ (you ask/you request).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bittest mich um Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You ask me for help.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "bitten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bittet mich um Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asks me for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich bizarr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really bizarre.

definitions.note: Older spelling; today usually written as „bisschen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte ein bißchen leiser sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak a little more quietly?

definitions.note: Old spelling of "bisschen"; today usually written "bisschen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir ein bißchen helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me a little?

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich blamieren = to embarrass oneself / to make a fool of oneself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich nicht blamieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to embarrass you.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich blamieren“ = to embarrass oneself / make a fool of oneself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blamiert sich vor seinen Freunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He embarrasses himself in front of his friends.

definitions.note: Past participle of „blamieren“, often used with „haben“ and reflexive „sich“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich vor der Klasse blamiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He embarrassed himself in front of the class.

definitions.note: Often used with forms of "sein" (e.g., "ist blank") to mean there’s nothing there.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Seite ist blank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The page is blank.

definitions.note: imperative form, used to tell one person (du) to blow
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Blas die Kerzen aus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Blow out the candles!

definitions.note: Often used with instruments (e.g., a trumpet) or for blowing air (e.g., blowing out candles).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann sehr laut in die Trompete blasen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can blow very loudly into the trumpet.

definitions.note: Often used for people’s skin/face color (e.g., from illness, shock, or lack of sun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du siehst heute sehr blass aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look very pale today.

definitions.note: Verb (archaic/literary). More common today: „erblassen“. Means becoming pale (often from shock, fear, illness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als sie die Nachricht hörte, begann sie zu blassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When she heard the news, she began to pale.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute sehe ich blasser aus als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I look paler than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Himmel ist heute blau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky is blue today.

definitions.note: adjective form used with certain endings (e.g., before a noun or after a determiner)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag das blaue Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the blue car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den blauen Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the blue sky.

definitions.note: Used for masculine nominative singular (and also genitive singular / dative singular after some determiners).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Himmel ist heute blauer als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky is bluer today than yesterday.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a neuter noun (e.g., „ein blaues Auto“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein blaues Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a blue shirt.

definitions.note: colloquial; used to mean not going to work or school on purpose
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern blaugemacht und bin an den See gefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I played hooky yesterday and drove to the lake.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular) of „bleiben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bleib bitte hier!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stay here!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "bleiben" (ich bleibe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bleibe heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m staying home today.

definitions.note: Used for not leaving a place or continuing in the same state; can be followed by an adjective or by a verb in the infinitive with a status meaning (e.g., sitzen, stehen, liegen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will hier bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to stay here.

definitions.native: continue to be; remain (in a state/condition)
definitions.note: Common with adjectives (e.g., ruhig, gesund) to express that a condition does not change.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte bleiben Sie ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remain calm.

definitions.note: Often used with posture verbs to mean “remain seated/standing/lying”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss sitzen bleiben, weil mein Bein weh tut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to remain seated because my leg hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte heute zu Hause bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to stay at home today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „bleiben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bleibst du heute Abend zu Hause?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you staying at home tonight?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "bleiben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bleibt heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stays at home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der langen Krankheit war sie ganz bleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long illness, she was completely pale.

definitions.note: Often used for being temporarily unable to see well because of strong light.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne blendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun dazzles.

definitions.note: Often used for being blinded by bright light.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das helle Licht blendete mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bright light dazzled (blinded) me.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition (e.g., „auf“ = look at; „nach“ = look for) or with an adverbial direction (e.g., „aus dem Fenster“ = out of the window).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann kaum noch klar blicken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can hardly see clearly anymore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blickt aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks out the window.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "blicken"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blickte kurz aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He glanced briefly out the window.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural (or formal “Sie”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie blickten aus dem Fenster und warteten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They looked out the window and waited.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "bleiben"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich blieb gestern Abend zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed at home last night.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II of "bleiben" (used for hypothetical situations or polite phrasing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bliebe zu Hause, wenn ich krank wäre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would stay at home if I were sick.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "bleiben"; used for "we/you(pl)/they" or formal "you" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir blieben zu Hause, weil es den ganzen Tag geregnet hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stayed at home because it rained all day.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „blasen“ (to blow).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind blies die Blätter von den Bäumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind blew the leaves off the trees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann ist blind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man is blind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hilft einer blinden Frau über die Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helps a blind woman cross the street.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "blind" used before a neuter noun (e.g., "ein blindes Kind").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein blindes Kind lernt Braille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A blind child is learning Braille.

definitions.note: Often used for indicator lights or turn signals (e.g., a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das gelbe Licht blinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The yellow light is flashing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss blinzeln, weil die Sonne so hell ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to blink because the sun is so bright.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „blinzeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blinzelte in die Sonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He blinked in the sun.

definitions.note: Colloquial/emphatic: much stronger than just “schnell” (fast).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war blitzschnell fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was done in a flash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lastwagen blockiert die Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is blocking the street.

definitions.note: often used for roads/paths, accounts, cards, or access that can’t be used
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist wegen eines Unfalls blockiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is blocked because of an accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat blondes Haar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has blond hair.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected ending; used before a feminine noun (e.g., „eine blonde Frau“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat blonde Haare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has blond hair.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “just/simply” in the sense of “only” or “all you have to do is…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bloss nicht zu spät!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just don’t be late!

definitions.note: Often used to add emphasis, like “just” in “just tell me!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sag bloß die Wahrheit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just tell the truth!

definitions.note: Adjective ending used before a feminine noun or after certain determiners (e.g., „die bloße Wahrheit“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die bloße Idee macht mir Angst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mere idea scares me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trat mit bloßen Füßen ins Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stepped into the water with bare feet.

definitions.note: Often means being publicly embarrassed or made to look bad.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde vor allen bloßgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was humiliated in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Dialect/rare spelling; in standard German this is usually written "bloß".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist bloû ein Beispiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s just an example.

definitions.note: often used for card games or generally pretending to be more confident/knowledgeable than you are
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blufft beim Poker und gewinnt trotzdem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bluffs in poker and still wins.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich blute am Finger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My finger is bleeding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde kann lange bluten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound can bleed for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du blutest am Finger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are bleeding on your finger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Hand blutet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hand is bleeding.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "bluten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Sturz blutete sein Knie stark.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fall, his knee was bleeding badly.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "blasen"; also used in the phrase "(ein Instrument) blasen" = to play (a wind instrument).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind bläst heute sehr stark.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind is blowing very strongly today.

definitions.note: simple past of „blättern“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blätterte in der Zeitung und trank seinen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He flipped through the newspaper and drank his coffee.

definitions.note: Often sounds blunt or insulting when used about a person; can also mean something is annoying or unfortunate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine blöde Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a stupid idea.

definitions.note: Often used informally; can sound insulting when said about a person. In phrases like „eine blöde Idee“ it can also mean “dumb/annoying.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine blöde Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a stupid idea.

definitions.note: informal; can be insulting
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist blöde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s stupid.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult; can sound rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Lust auf diesen blöden Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t feel like hearing that stupid joke.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often sounds insulting. Here it’s the comparative form ("more").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein blöder Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a stupid mistake.

definitions.note: Often sounds rude or insulting when used about a person; can also describe things like mistakes or situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein blöder Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a stupid mistake.

definitions.note: Used here as an inflected form of the adjective (e.g., before a neuter noun like „blödes Wetter“). Can sound insulting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein blödes Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a stupid problem.

definitions.note: often used for plants/flowers; can also be used figuratively (e.g., business, culture)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Frühling blühen die Blumen im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the flowers bloom in the garden.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (attributive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir spazieren durch blühende Gärten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk through blooming gardens.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „blühen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Frühling blüht der Apfelbaum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the apple tree blooms.

definitions.note: Very informal interjection; expresses strong surprise, amazement, or sometimes annoyance/exasperation (depending on tone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Boah, das ist ja riesig!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, that is huge!

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "abbiegen"; often used with the separable prefix "ab" (e.g., "bog ... ab").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bog an der Ecke ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned at the corner.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „biegen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bog den Draht mit einer Zange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bent the wire with pliers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Flugzeuge bombardieren die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The planes are bombing the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Armee bombardiert die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army bombards the city.

definitions.note: Can also be used figuratively (e.g., with questions, messages, or ads).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mit Fragen bombardiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am bombarded with questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mir Geld borgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to borrow money.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (jemandem etwas borgen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir dein Buch borgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me your book?

definitions.note: Often written with a capital letter in German: „Bostoner“ (as with many place-based adjectives ending in -er).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spricht mit einem bostoner Akzent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks with a Boston accent.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „anbieten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bot mir Hilfe an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He offered me help.

definitions.note: simple past of „bieten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bot mir seine Hilfe an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He offered me his help.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine/neuter dative singular or with plural (e.g., after "im" or before plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen einen Spaziergang im botanischen Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking a walk in the botanical garden.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „anbieten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie boten uns Hilfe an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They offered us help.

definitions.note: Sound effect for a sudden loud noise (e.g., an explosion or something crashing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Und dann: boum!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: And then: boom!

definitions.note: Usually refers to ten-pin bowling (Bowlingbahn).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen heute Abend bowlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going bowling tonight.

definitions.note: simple past form of "abbrechen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er brach das Gespräch ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He broke off the conversation.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „aufbrechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brachen früh am Morgen auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We set off early in the morning.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „aufbrechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb brach die Tür auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief forced the door open.

definitions.note: Used with a place you escape from (often with "aus").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gefangene brach aus dem Gefängnis aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner broke out of the prison.

definitions.note: Used for things like a fire, war, or illness starting suddenly (often with "aus").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Wald brach ein Feuer aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A fire broke out in the forest.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of „brechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er brach das Glas aus Versehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He broke the glass by accident.

definitions.note: Simple past of "einbrechen"; often used with a destination introduced by "in" (e.g., "in die Wohnung").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzte Nacht brach jemand in unsere Wohnung ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night someone broke into our apartment.

definitions.note: Simple past of „zusammenbrechen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem langen Lauf brach er plötzlich zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long run, he suddenly collapsed.

definitions.note: simple past (wir/sie) of „ausbrechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie brachen aus dem Gefängnis aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They broke out of the prison.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „bringen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er brachte mir ein Glas Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brought me a glass of water.

definitions.note: Past tense of the separable verb „einbringen“; the prefix often appears later in the sentence (… brachte … ein).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er brachte einen Vorschlag ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He introduced a proposal.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „bringen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie brachten das Essen nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They brought the food home.

definitions.note: simple past (du-form) of "bringen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du brachtest mir gestern das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You brought me the book yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „brennen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Feuer brannte die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire burned all night.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form, used especially in writing; can mean either an ongoing past action or a completed one depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kerzen brannten die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candles were burning all night.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a feminine noun (e.g., die brasilianische Küche) or in the plural (e.g., brasilianische Filme)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die brasilianische Musik ist sehr bekannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Brazilian music is very well-known.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command (imperative) meaning “(you) roast/fry!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Brate das Gemüse kurz in der Pfanne!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fry the vegetables briefly in the pan!

definitions.note: often used for cooking in a pan with fat/oil (fry) or in the oven (roast)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute Abend Kartoffeln braten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to fry potatoes this evening.

definitions.note: colloquial short form of „brauche“ (common in spoken German)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauch Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need help.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of „brauchen“ (ich brauche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your help.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of needing something (sometimes more formal than “need”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I require more time.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (Ich brauche Wasser.) or with „zu“ + infinitive (Du brauchst nicht zu kommen. = You don't need to come).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche deine Hilfe, weil ich sie dringend brauche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your help because I urgently need it.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form of "brauchen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Brauchst du Hilfe?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you need help?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "brauchen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er braucht mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He needs more time.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of "brauchen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauchte gestern Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I needed help yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "brauchen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchten mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We needed more time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person singular: “you needed”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du brauchtest gestern Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You needed help yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), used with „ihr“ (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr brauchtet gestern viel Zeit für die Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You needed a lot of time for the homework yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist braun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is brown.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with some nouns (e.g., feminine or plural, or after certain articles)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage heute eine braune Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm wearing a brown jacket today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den braunen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the brown dog.

definitions.note: Neuter adjective ending (e.g., before a neuter noun like „das Auto“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein braunes Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a brown car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er braut sein eigenes Bier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brews his own beer.

definitions.note: Often used about children or pets meaning they behave properly; can also mean polite/obedient.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist heute ganz brav.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is very well-behaved today.

definitions.note: Often used about children behaving properly; not the same as English "brave".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sitzen brav am Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are sitting nicely at the table.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „brav“ (often used for children: behaving well, obedient). Not the same as English “brave”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist der Hund braver als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the dog is better behaved than yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used about children; not the same as English “brave” (= mutig).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein braves Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a well-behaved child.

definitions.note: used to praise someone after a performance or achievement
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bravo, das war wirklich toll!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bravo, that was really great!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I break")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich breche das Glas aus Versehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accidentally break the glass.

definitions.note: Used as the split-off verb stem of the separable verb „aufbrechen“ (e.g. „Wir brechen … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brechen morgen früh auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re setting off tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: To break (physically); also used in fixed expressions like „ein Gesetz brechen“ (to break a law).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst das Glas leicht brechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can easily break the glass.

definitions.note: Often used to describe waves, light, or a voice as it breaks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wellen rollen brechend ans Ufer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waves roll up to the shore, breaking.

definitions.note: Used with „ihr“ (you plural) in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr brecht das Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are breaking the bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist hier sehr breit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is very wide here.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (attributive): „eine breite Straße“ = “a wide street.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine breite Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wide street.

definitions.note: comparative form of "breit"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist hier breiter als dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is wider here than there.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "ausbreiten"; also used with "sich" ("sich ausbreiten" = to spread).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Feuer breitet sich schnell aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire spreads quickly.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „ausbreiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er breitete die Decke auf dem Boden aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spread the blanket out on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst hier bremsen, weil die Straße glatt ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to brake here because the road is slippery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus bremst plötzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus suddenly brakes.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "bremsen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus bremste plötzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus braked suddenly.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich). Can mean being on fire or causing something to burn; context decides.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brenne mir die Finger am heißen Topf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I burn my fingers on the hot pot.

definitions.note: Can mean to be on fire, to burn something, or to have a burning sensation (e.g., eyes, skin).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Kamin kann Holz lange brennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the fireplace, wood can burn for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr löschte die brennenden Autos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department put out the burning cars.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus brennt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is burning.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anbrechen“; the prefix „an“ may appear later in the sentence (e.g. „bricht … an“). Often used with „Der Tag“ (the day).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tag bricht an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The day is beginning.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix: „bricht … aus“ (e.g., a fire, war, fight, panic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Küche bricht ein Feuer aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A fire breaks out in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix: „bricht … aus“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dem Kind ist schlecht, und es bricht plötzlich aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child feels sick and suddenly throws up.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "brechen"; can mean breaking something or a thing breaking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ast bricht im Wind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The branch breaks in the wind.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „braten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er briet die Kartoffeln in der Pfanne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fried the potatoes in the pan.

definitions.note: Often used to praise someone’s performance or an idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine brillante Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a brilliant idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine brillante Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a brilliant idea.

definitions.note: Often used for something that looks glossy or gleaming (e.g., a surface).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine brillante Oberfläche poliert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She polished a shiny surface.

definitions.note: also commonly used to mean “take” (e.g. bringing something to a place)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bringe dir das Buch morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll bring you the book tomorrow.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of „bringen“ (ich bringe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bringe dir morgen das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll bring you the book tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte ein Glas Wasser bringen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please bring me a glass of water?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "bringen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bringst du mir bitte ein Glas Wasser?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring me a glass of water, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bringt mir einen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brings me a coffee.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively for topics or information that could cause trouble or strong reactions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeitung hat über die brisanten Details berichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper reported on the explosive details.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine nouns (nominative/accusative singular) or with plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag britische Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like British music.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak ending form (e.g., after “die/der/das” or similar determiners)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die britischen Serien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the British TV series.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine nouns in the nominative case (and in some other contexts)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein britischer Schauspieler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a British actor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war brutal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was brutal.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech as an intensifier (like “really” or “super”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war brutal teuer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was really expensive!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der zweite Film ist brutaler als der erste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The second movie is more brutal than the first.

definitions.note: Subjunctive II form of "bringen"; used for hypotheticals or polite/indirect statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brächte dir etwas zu essen, wenn ich Zeit hätte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would bring you something to eat if I had time.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) of "brauchen"; often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bräuchte bitte ein Glas Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would need a glass of water, please.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form; often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bräuchten mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would need more time.

definitions.note: Used for loud animal sounds and also for loud shouting (often in anger or across a distance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Löwe kann sehr laut brüllen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lion can roar very loudly.

definitions.note: Often used for booking travel, hotel rooms, tables, appointments, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte ein Hotelzimmer buchen und buche es für zwei Nächte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to book a hotel room and I’m booking it for two nights.

definitions.note: Used for spelling a word letter by letter.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du deinen Nachnamen bitte buchstabieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you spell your last name, please?

definitions.note: used when saying the letters of a word (e.g., a name) out loud
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er buchstabiert seinen Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spells his name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe buchstäblich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I literally have no time.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „backen“ (used mainly in writing and in some regions; in speech often „hat ... gebacken“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern buk sie einen Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday she baked a cake.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen nicht im Auto bumsen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They don’t want to have sex in the car.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine bunte Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a colorful bag.

definitions.note: comparative form of "bunt"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Bild ist bunter als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This picture is more colorful than the other one.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "buono"; used with feminine singular nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ho una buona idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a good idea.

definitions.note: Informal; used when leaving (often borrowed from English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Okay, ich muss los—bye!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, I have to go—bye!

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (or imperative: “bake!”) of „backen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bäckt heute Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bakes bread today.

definitions.note: past subjunctive (Konjunktiv II), 2nd person singular; used for hypotheticals or polite/indirect speech
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du mich bätest, würde ich dir helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you asked me, I would help you.

definitions.note: Older/archaic 3rd person singular simple past of "bitten"; in modern German you’ll usually see "bat".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bätet um Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nicht böse auf dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not mad at you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist nicht böse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog isn’t mean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der böse Zauberer wohnt im Turm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The evil wizard lives in the tower.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sah ihn böse an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looked at him angrily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich böse verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got badly hurt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder haben Angst vor dem bösen Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are afraid of the evil man.

definitions.note: Often describes an angry mood or expression (e.g., a look).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sah ihren bösen Blick.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw her angry look.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein böser Mann drohte uns.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An evil man threatened us.

definitions.note: Often used for an angry or hostile attitude (e.g., a “böser Blick” = an angry/mean look).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein böser Blick reichte schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An angry look was enough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein böses Wort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an evil word.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "bücken"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bückte sich, um den Schlüssel aufzuheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bent down to pick up the key.

definitions.note: usually means ironing clothes (removing wrinkles with an iron)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute Abend noch ein Hemd bügeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to iron a shirt this evening.

definitions.note: usually used for ironing clothes; can also mean "to smooth out" (e.g., problems) in a figurative sense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bügelt sein Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He irons his shirt.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „bügeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern bügelte ich mein Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ironed my shirt.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „bürsten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bürstete den Hund nach dem Spaziergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brushed the dog after the walk.

definitions.note: Often used with „für“ + accusative (e.g. „für einen Fehler büßen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss für seinen Fehler büßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to pay for his mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir campen dieses Wochenende am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re camping by the lake this weekend.

definitions.note: Informal; often used as a friendly toast or to say thanks (especially in Austria and Bavaria).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Case, dass du mir geholfen hast!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cheers, thanks for helping me!

definitions.note: Not Standard German; common in Swiss German/Alemannic as a form of "können" ("can").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich chan heute nöd cho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't come today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kellner war sehr charmant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter was very charming.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with feminine singular nouns (or as a nominalized adjective for a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine charmante Gastgeberin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a charming hostess.

definitions.note: Refers to the Chinese language or something from China.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche ein bisschen chinesisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak a little Chinese.

definitions.note: adjective inflected form; used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular, plural, or after certain determiners)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse gern chinesische Nudeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like eating Chinese noodles.

definitions.note: adjective in a declined form (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse heute in einem chinesischen Restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm eating at a Chinese restaurant today.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a masculine noun in the nominative singular (and also after words like „ein“ in some cases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein chinesischer Tee ist sehr beliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Chinese tea is very popular.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a neuter noun (e.g., with "ein").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir suchen ein chinesisches Restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for a Chinese restaurant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In vielen Ländern sind christliche Feiertage wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In many countries, Christian holidays are important.

definitions.note: informal greeting; also used when saying goodbye
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ciao, wie geht’s?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi, how are you?

definitions.note: Often used with numbers, dates, or times; also common in the abbreviation „ca.“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Reparatur kostet circa 200 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The repair costs around 200 euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schwester ist sehr clever.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very smart.

definitions.note: Not a standard German verb form; in German the verb is usually „kommen“ (e.g. „ich komme“). You may see „come“ only as an English word used in German contexts (e.g. in quotes or code-switching).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Chat-Nachricht stand: „Come quickly!“
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chat message said: “Come quickly!”

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; can mean “cool” in the sense of “awesome” or “calm.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist echt cool!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really cool!

definitions.note: Informal; used as a reaction to show approval or agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cool! Dann machen wir das so.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cool! Then we'll do it that way.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "cool" (used before a noun or after words like "eine").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine coole Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a cool idea.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein cooles Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a cool car.

definitions.note: Often used to say you are (or will be) present/available, e.g. when arriving: „Ich bin gleich da.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gleich da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be right there in a moment.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to point something out or to hand something to someone (like “there you go!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da! Das ist mein Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There! That’s my key.

definitions.note: Used at the start of a subordinate clause to give a reason; often interchangeable with "weil" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da es heute regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since it’s raining today, we’re staying at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da ist mein Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is my key.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a reason (often at the beginning of a clause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da es regnet, bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since it’s raining, we’re staying at home.

definitions.note: Often used to say someone/something is present ("there") or included/along with something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Handy dabei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have my phone with me.

definitions.note: Often written as two words: „da bleiben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dableiben, bis du zurückkommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to stay there until you come back.

definitions.note: simple past of "denken" (used with ich/er/sie/es)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich dachte, du bist schon zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought you were already at home.

definitions.note: Simple past of „nachdenken“ (to think; to think about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich dachte lange nach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought for a long time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „denken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir dachten, der Zug kommt pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We thought the train would arrive on time.

definitions.note: Simple past (du-form) of "denken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du dachtest, es wäre schon zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You thought it was already too late.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form used with "ihr" (you all) or as a polite/plural form in some dialects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr dachtet, der Zug kommt pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You thought the train would arrive on time.

definitions.note: Dialect/colloquial demonstrative pronoun (roughly like standard German „das“). Not related to English „dad“ (= father).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dad habe ich schon gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already seen that.

definitions.note: Often used to express cause and effect: “dadurch” = “because of that / thereby.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat viel geübt und dadurch die Prüfung bestanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He practiced a lot and as a result passed the exam.

definitions.note: Refers back to something previously mentioned (e.g., a thing, idea, or situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezahle dafür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll pay for it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hilfst mir, und dafür helfe ich dir morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You help me, and in return I’ll help you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often refers back to something mentioned earlier; also commonly used as "dagegen sein" = to be against it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin dagegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m against it.

definitions.note: Past participle of the separable verb „dalassen“ (“to leave there”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Schlüssel zu Hause dagelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my key at home.

definitions.note: past participle of „dasein“ (used e.g. with „sein“ in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern nicht dagewesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wasn’t there yesterday.

definitions.note: More common in southern Germany, Austria, and Switzerland; in standard German often replaced by „zu Hause“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Abend daheim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m at home this evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnet stark; daher bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining heavily; therefore we’re staying at home.
