definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kommen aus Berlin und fahren daher weiter nach Leipzig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re coming from Berlin and going on from there to Leipzig.

definitions.note: often used with verbs of movement (going/coming) to indicate a destination
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen nach der Arbeit dahin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going there after work.

definitions.native: back there, over there (in the back)
definitions.note: Refers to a place farther away, often behind something or toward the back of a room.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jacken hängen dahinten an der Garderobe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jackets are hanging back there on the coat rack.

definitions.note: Refers to a specific thing or place already mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Garten ist groß; dahinter steht ein altes Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden is big; behind it there is an old house.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“: „jemandem/etwas dahinterkommen“ = to discover the truth (often about a trick or secret).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind dem Betrug dahintergekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We figured out the fraud.

definitions.native: to figure out, to find out
definitions.note: Often used for discovering how something works or uncovering a secret/trick.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dahinterkommen, wie das funktioniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to figure out how that works.

definitions.native: to be behind (something), to be responsible for (something), to be the reason behind (something)
definitions.note: Often used to identify who/what is responsible for an event or situation, sometimes with a suspicious tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wer könnte dahinterstecken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who could be behind it?

definitions.note: Often used to say who/what is responsible for something (sometimes implying a hidden reason or plan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaube, dass er dahintersteckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think he’s behind it.

definitions.note: Refers to a time in the past (often contrasted with now).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Damals hatte ich kein Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Back then I didn't have a cell phone.

definitions.note: Refers back to something previously mentioned (a thing, situation, or idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann damit nicht arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t work with it.

definitions.note: Introduces a purpose clause and sends the verb to the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne Deutsch, damit ich in Deutschland arbeiten kann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning German so that I can work in Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen zuerst einkaufen und danach ins Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First we’re going shopping, and after that we’re going to the café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel liegt daneben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key is next to it.

definitions.note: Often used to say something is incorrect or missing the point.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Antwort ist leider daneben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, your answer is wrong.

definitions.note: Used with the dative case; often followed by a noun (e.g., dank dem Regen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dank deiner Hilfe haben wir es geschafft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks to your help, we managed it.

definitions.note: Often used together with "danke" (e.g., "Danke, dank!") or as part of fixed phrases like "Gott sei Dank".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dank, das ist sehr nett von dir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks, that’s very nice of you!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin dir sehr dankbar für deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very grateful to you for your help.

definitions.note: Common short form of "danke schön" / "danke sehr".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke, das ist sehr nett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks, that’s very nice.

definitions.note: Commonly used on its own to mean “thank you”; literally “(I) thank.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke für deine Hilfe!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your help!

definitions.note: Often used with dative for the person being thanked and with “für” + accusative for what you thank for.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir danken dir für deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We thank you for your help.

definitions.note: present participle of „danken“; often used to mean doing something while expressing thanks
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dankend nahm er das Geschenk an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanking them, he accepted the gift.

definitions.note: Often written as two words: „danke schön“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dankeschön für deine Hilfe!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your help!

definitions.note: third-person singular present of „danken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er dankt dir für deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thanks you for your help.

definitions.note: Simple past of „danken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich dankte ihr für die Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thanked her for the help.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about what happens next in time or in a sequence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war zuerst im Supermarkt und dann zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was at the supermarket first and then at home.

definitions.note: Often used as the first part of words like darauf, daran, damit (meaning roughly “there-/it-” + preposition). As a standalone word, it’s literary/old-fashioned and similar to da.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dar kommt er!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There he comes!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs/prepositions that take "an" (e.g. denken an, arbeiten an) to refer back to something previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich denke oft daran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often think about it.

definitions.note: Often refers back to something mentioned before; also common with verbs that take a preposition like „warten auf“ (to wait for).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte darauf, dass du anrufst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm waiting for you to call.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die E-Mail gelesen und daraufhin sofort geantwortet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He read the email and after that replied immediately.

definitions.note: Refers back to something previously mentioned; often used with making/creating/learning something from it (e.g., „daraus machen“, „daraus lernen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können daraus viel lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can learn a lot from it.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „dürfen“; used for permission (and sometimes polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er darf heute länger aufbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is allowed to stay up later today.

definitions.note: Used to ask for or give permission, or to say what is allowed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst hier nicht rauchen, aber ich darf draußen rauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re not allowed to smoke here, but I’m allowed to smoke outside.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „dürfen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst hier nicht parken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are not allowed to park here.

definitions.note: Refers back to something previously mentioned (a container, place, text, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Tasche ist ein Schlüssel; darin ist ein roter Anhänger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the bag there is a key; in it there is a red keychain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war krank, darum bin ich zu Hause geblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was sick, therefore I stayed at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel liegt darunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key is underneath (it).

definitions.note: Used with numbers or groups to mean that something/someone is included in that group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unter den Gästen waren fünf Kinder, darunter auch meine Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Among the guests were five children, including my sister.

definitions.note: Often used after verbs/prepositions that take „über“ (e.g. sprechen über).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sprechen später darüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll talk about it later.

definitions.note: Refers to a position or movement higher than something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lampe hängt darüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp is hanging above it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das gefällt mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like that.

definitions.note: This is the subordinating conjunction meaning “that” (often spelled “dass”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaube, das stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that’s true.

definitions.note: definite article for neuter singular (nominative/accusative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reading the book.

definitions.note: as a demonstrative determiner (often stressed) for neuter singular
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus dort ist sehr alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That house over there is very old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist sehr wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is very important.

definitions.note: used as a relative pronoun to refer back to a noun (like “the thing that …”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das Buch, das ich gerade lese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the book that I’m reading right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst morgen pünktlich dasein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to be there on time tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a subordinate clause (often after verbs like denken, sagen, wissen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich denke, dass es heute regnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that it’s raining today.

definitions.note: subordinating conjunction introducing a subordinate clause (often after verbs like sagen/denken/wissen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaube, dass er heute keine Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that he doesn't have time today.

definitions.note: Refers to a neuter noun (das); often used on its own to mean “the same thing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dasselbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want the same thing.

definitions.note: Used to refer back to the same thing as a neuter noun (“das”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme das blaue Hemd, und er nimmt dasselbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take the blue shirt, and he’ll take the same one.

definitions.note: Neuter form of „derselbe“; refers to the exact same item, not just something similar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben dasselbe Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same problem.

definitions.note: neuter form of „derselbe“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht dasselbe wie gestern essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to eat the same thing as yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund bleibt vor der Tür dastehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog stays standing there in front of the door.

definitions.native: to look, to appear (in a certain way)
definitions.note: Often used with an adverb or phrase like „gut/schlecht dastehen“ or „als … dastehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte nicht als Lügner dastehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to appear as a liar.

definitions.note: Often used with a time expression (e.g., zwei Stunden) or with "lange".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie lange wird das Meeting dauern?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How long will the meeting last?

definitions.note: Often implies something happens too often or is annoying.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist dauernd am Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He's constantly on his phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film dauert zwei Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie lasts two hours.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „dauern“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film dauerte zwei Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie lasted two hours.

definitions.native: from it, from that; of it, of that
definitions.note: Pronominal adverb (da- + von); usually refers to things or ideas, not people (for people: von ihm/ihr/ihnen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe zwei Äpfel und esse jetzt einen davon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two apples and I’m eating one of them now.

definitions.note: Often used with "mit + noun" to mean "got away with (something)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück ist niemand verletzt davongekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, nobody got away injured.

definitions.note: past participle of „davonrennen“, often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist plötzlich davongerannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog suddenly ran away.

definitions.note: Often used with "mit + Dativ" to mean "to get away with (something)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will mit der Lüge davonkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to get away with the lie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund will nicht hören und könnte gleich davonlaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog won’t listen and could run away any moment.

definitions.note: Often used with a following clause introduced by „dass“ (e.g., „davor, dass …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Angst davor, dass ich zu spät komme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm afraid that I'll be late.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „kommen“ or „gehören“ to mean “to be added/come along (with it)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme ein Wasser und dazu einen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a water and also a coffee.

definitions.note: Refers back to something already mentioned (like “to that/for that”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit dazu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time for it.

definitions.native: to add (to that), to throw in
definitions.note: often used when adding something extra (e.g., money, ingredients, information)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können noch etwas Geld dazugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can add a bit more money.

definitions.note: often used with a clause starting with „dass“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hatte Angst, dazugeben, dass er gelogen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was afraid to admit that he lied.

definitions.native: to belong (to a group), to be included
definitions.note: Often used with “zu” (e.g., „zu einer Gruppe dazugehören“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehöre zu diesem Team nicht nur dazu, ich will wirklich dazugehören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't just belong to this team; I really want to belong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sitze zwischen Anna und Ben, und Paul sitzt dazwischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sitting between Anna and Ben, and Paul is sitting in between.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something happens during that time or interrupts something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben gegessen, und dazwischen hat es angefangen zu regnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ate, and in the meantime it started to rain.

definitions.note: Old spelling of "dass" (modern standard spelling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, daß er heute keine Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that he doesn’t have time today.

definitions.note: Not standard German; mostly appears in foreign names/titles (e.g., French/Spanish/Portuguese) where it means “of/from”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er heißt Jean de la Fontaine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His name is Jean de la Fontaine.

definitions.note: Often used for settings, accounts, or functions (e.g., in apps/devices).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst die Benachrichtigungen in den Einstellungen deaktivieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can disable notifications in the settings.

definitions.note: Present tense form of „decken“ (ich decke = I cover).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich decke den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wolken decken den Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Clouds cover the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen noch den Tisch decken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still need to set the table.

definitions.note: can also mean “sets (the table)” depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Deckel deckt den Topf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lid covers the pot.

definitions.note: Often used for things/devices that don’t work properly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy ist defekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is broken.

definitions.note: Often used in sports, politics, or discussions to describe a cautious, protective style or attitude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mannschaft spielte sehr defensiv.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team played very defensively.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Wort bitte definieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please define the word?

definitions.note: Common in spoken German to strongly agree (like “for sure”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme definitiv morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m definitely coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: informal singular (used with du); used before masculine/neuter nouns in nominative (and neuter accusative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das dein Hund?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that your dog?

definitions.note: informal (used with du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das deine Tasche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that your bag?

definitions.note: Used with feminine singular nouns (and with plural nouns) in the nominative or accusative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das deine Tasche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that your bag?

definitions.note: informal (used with du); feminine singular or plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das deine Jacke?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that your jacket?

definitions.note: informal (used with du); feminine singular or plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das deine Tasche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that your bag?

definitions.note: Dative singular form of „dein“ (informal „you“); used with masculine or neuter nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe deinem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping your brother.

definitions.note: dative masculine or dative/neuter singular form (informal “du” possessive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe deinem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping your brother.

definitions.note: informal singular; used before a noun (a declined form of "dein")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe deinen Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see your brother.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular (e.g., deinen Bruder) or accusative plural (e.g., deine Kinder) form of "dein".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe deinen Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see your brother.

definitions.note: genitive masculine/neuter or genitive feminine plural form of "dein" (often used with "wegen" + genitive or in set phrases like "einer deiner ...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen deiner Hilfe sind wir pünktlich angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your help, we arrived on time.

definitions.note: genitive singular feminine form used as a pronoun (meaning "of yours")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine Freundin deiner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a friend of yours.

definitions.note: Genitive singular (masculine/neuter) of "dein"; used after certain prepositions (e.g., wegen, trotz) or in fixed phrases.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen deiner Hilfe bin ich jetzt fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your help, I'm finished now.

definitions.note: informal singular possessive form (from „dein-“); used with certain case/gender endings (e.g., dative feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe deiner Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping your mother.

definitions.note: Genitive singular form of "dein" (informal "your"); used with masculine or neuter nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen deines Autos komme ich zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your car, I’m coming late.

definitions.note: genitive singular form of "dein" (used with masculine or neuter nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen deines Autos bin ich zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your car, I’m late.

definitions.note: informal (used with du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deinetwegen komme ich zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of you, I'm late.

definitions.native: because of you, on your account
definitions.note: informal (addresses one person with du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin deinetwegen früher gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came earlier because of you.

definitions.note: possessive pronoun (used without a following noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das deins?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that yours?

definitions.note: present tense (3rd person singular) of "dekorieren"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er dekoriert den Raum für die Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decorates the room for the party.

definitions.note: past participle of "dekorieren"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Raum ist schön dekoriert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is nicely decorated.

definitions.note: “del” is not used as a German preposition/adposition. It may be a typo or a word from another language (e.g., Spanish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: „del“ ist kein deutsches Wort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “del” is not a German word.

definitions.note: dative singular form of the definite article for masculine and neuter nouns (der/das)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe dem Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help the man.

definitions.note: Dative form of "der" (masculine/neuter singular); used when something is given/shown/said to someone or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wem gibst du das Buch? – Dem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who are you giving the book to? – To him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich demnächst an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll call you soon.

definitions.note: adjective inflected form (e.g., with a feminine noun, or plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir unterstützen eine demokratische Regierung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We support a democratic government.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak inflection form (e.g., after a definite article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir unterstützen die demokratischen Werte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We support the democratic values.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter singular form of „derselbe“; used to emphasize it’s the exact same person/thing (stronger than „der/die/das gleiche“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es demselben Mann gesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I told it to the same man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist nicht in Ordnung, jemanden vor anderen zu demütigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is not okay to humiliate someone in front of others.

definitions.note: Form of the definite article used mainly for masculine accusative singular (e.g. "den Hund") and also for dative plural (e.g. "den Kindern").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the dog.

definitions.note: used for masculine singular in the accusative (object)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see him over there.

definitions.note: used for plural in the dative (indirect object)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe den, die Hilfe brauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help those who need help.

definitions.native: to those; to whom, to which
definitions.note: Dative plural form of "der/die/das" (used for people or things, often in relative clauses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die Leute, denen ich gestern geholfen habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the people whom I helped yesterday.

definitions.note: Accusative form of "derjenige"; often used to point to a specific person/thing, frequently followed by a relative clause (e.g., "denjenigen, der …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne denjenigen, der hier wohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the one who lives here.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Denk an mich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think of me!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of „denken“ (also used in polite requests like „Ich denke, …“ = „I think …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich denke, das ist eine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that is a good idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir denken jeden Tag darüber nach, wie wir besser lernen können, aber ich muss jetzt ausdrücklich das Wort denken benutzen: denken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We think every day about how we can learn better, but now I must explicitly use the word denken: denken.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-Form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was denkst du darüber?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you think about that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er denkt oft an seine Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often thinks about his family.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „zurückdenken“; in a sentence it’s often split: „denkt … zurück“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er denkt oft an seine Kindheit zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often thinks back to his childhood.

definitions.note: Often used as a modal particle in questions to sound more natural/curious (like “then”, “so”, or “anyway” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was machst du denn?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So what are you doing then?

definitions.note: Used as a coordinating conjunction (followed by main-clause word order), unlike "weil" which triggers verb-final word order.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe nach Hause, denn ich bin müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going home because I'm tired.

definitions.note: Used to give a reason (often like a more written/formal “because”); unlike “weil”, it doesn’t send the verb to the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn es regnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m staying at home because it’s raining.

definitions.note: Often used in questions as a modal particle to add emphasis/interest; it may be untranslated in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was machst du denn?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing then?

definitions.note: Introduces a reason and does not send the verb to the end (word order stays like a main clause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe nach Hause, denn ich bin müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going home because I’m tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnet, dennoch gehen wir spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining; nevertheless, we’re going for a walk.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular form of "derselbe"; used before a noun or as a pronoun to mean exactly the same one.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern denselben Mann im Park gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw the same man in the park yesterday.

definitions.note: Describes a mood/state; also used in medical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich in letzter Zeit oft depressiv.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lately I often feel depressed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachrichten sind heute wirklich deprimierend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news is really depressing today.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective to describe how someone feels.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute ziemlich deprimiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m pretty depressed today.

definitions.note: Commonly used for feeling low/sad (can be temporary and not necessarily a medical diagnosis).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der schlechten Nachricht war sie ganz deprimiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bad news, she was really depressed.

definitions.note: definite article (one form of “the”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is sleeping.

definitions.note: relative pronoun (often masculine nominative singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne den, der dort steht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the one who is standing over there.

definitions.note: demonstrative pronoun (often masculine nominative singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der dort ist meiner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That one over there is mine.

definitions.native: like that, in such a way
definitions.note: Often used to intensify: „derart + adjective“ = “so/that (adjective)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war derart laut, dass ich nicht schlafen konnte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was so loud that I couldn’t sleep.

definitions.note: Often used before a plural noun (as in this form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Derartige Probleme treten selten auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such problems occur rarely.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun, meaning “of this/that kind.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben mit derartigen Problemen keine Erfahrung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have no experience with such problems.

definitions.note: relative determiner for feminine singular or plural nouns (genitive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die Frau, deren Auto vor dem Haus steht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s the woman whose car is parked in front of the house.

definitions.note: relative determiner referring to something feminine singular or plural (e.g., "deren Hund" = "whose dog")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die Frau, deren Hund immer bellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the woman whose dog always barks.

definitions.native: such a thing, something like that
definitions.note: Usually used after an indefinite word like „nichts“, „etwas“, „alles“ or „was“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas Derartiges habe ich noch nie gesehen, nichts dergleichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never seen anything like that, nothing of the sort.

definitions.note: Used to refer back to a specific male person/thing; often followed by a relative clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Derjenige, der zuerst ankommt, bekommt den Preis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The one who arrives first gets the prize.

definitions.note: Emphasizes degree; often stronger than "so" in English and common in spoken language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war dermaßen müde, dass ich im Sitzen eingeschlafen bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was so tired that I fell asleep sitting up.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that it is exactly the same person or thing as previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben derselbe Lehrer wie letztes Jahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same teacher as last year.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun meaning “the same person/thing”; it inflects like the definite article + adjective (der/die/das + -selbe) for case and gender.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist derselbe, den wir gestern getroffen haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is the same one we met yesterday.

definitions.note: Genitive singular or dative plural form of "derselbe"; used with a noun to mean "the same (one)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen derselben Idee haben wir uns gestritten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We argued because of the same idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Derzeit habe ich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I currently don't have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit den derzeitigen Preisen kann ich mir das nicht leisten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the current prices, I can't afford that.

definitions.note: Genitive singular form of the definite article (used with masculine and neuter nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des Wetters bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the weather, we’re staying at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnet, deshalb bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's raining, therefore we're staying at home.

definitions.note: genitive masculine/neuter singular relative determiner/pronoun (refers back to a masculine or neuter noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der Mann, dessen Auto gestohlen wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the man whose car was stolen.

definitions.note: Relative pronoun (masculine/neuter singular, genitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der Mann, dessen Auto gestohlen wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the man whose car was stolen.

definitions.note: Used for masculine/neuter singular in genitive (meaning “of whom/which”); often followed by a noun (e.g., „dessen Auto“ = “whose car”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der Mann, dessen Auto gestohlen wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the man whose car was stolen.

definitions.note: Used in the correlative comparative structure „je … desto/umso …“ (e.g., „Je mehr…, desto besser…“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je länger ich warte, desto ungeduldiger werde ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The longer I wait, the more impatient I get.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hatte keine Zeit, deswegen bin ich nicht gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t have time, that’s why I didn’t come.

definitions.note: Often used like an adverb meaning “in a detailed way.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Plan detailliert erklärt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He explained the plan in detail.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (attributive); often with a noun like „Beschreibung“ (description) or „Informationen“ (information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine detaillierte Beschreibung geschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrote a detailed description.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen einen detaillierten Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a detailed plan.

definitions.note: Past tense (simple past) of "deuten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie deutete seine Worte als Warnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She interpreted his words as a warning.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is easy to see/hear/understand.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unterschied ist deutlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The difference is clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich deutlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak clearly.

definitions.note: Often used to mean that a difference or change is easy to see or recognize.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist deutlich kälter als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s noticeably colder than yesterday.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "deutlich"; can be used as an adjective or an adverb depending on the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich deutlicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak more clearly.

definitions.note: comparative form of the adverb „deutlich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte deutlicher sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak more clearly?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak German.

definitions.note: Adjective form of „deutsch“ used with certain endings (e.g., before plural nouns or feminine singular nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese deutsche Bücher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read German books.

definitions.note: adjective form used with nouns (inflected), e.g. „die deutschen …“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die deutschen Lieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the German songs.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a masculine noun (e.g., „ein deutscher …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein deutscher Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a German film.

definitions.note: Adjective used with a neuter noun in nominative or accusative (e.g., „ein deutsches Auto“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein deutsches Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a German car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt diagnostiziert eine Grippe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor diagnoses the flu.

definitions.note: accusative (direct object) form of the informal singular pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see you.

definitions.note: informal singular direct-object form (accusative) of „du“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see you.

definitions.note: Often used for things like doors, windows, lids, and clothing that fit without gaps.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte das Fenster dicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please close the window tightly.

definitions.note: Used for things that have many things close together (e.g., fog, traffic, forest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute Morgen war der Nebel sehr dicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This morning the fog was very thick.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „zumachen“ or „schließen“ to mean „shut tightly/securely“; and with distance to mean „close by“ (e.g., „dicht daneben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte das Fenster dicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please close the window tightly.

definitions.note: adjective form of „dicht“ with an -en ending (e.g., after „den“, „die“, „mit“ + plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch den dichten Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking through the dense forest.

definitions.note: comparative form of „dicht“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Wald stehen die Bäume hier dichter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the forest, the trees stand closer together here.

definitions.note: Often describes physical thickness (e.g., a book, a wall) or a person/animal being fat.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist sehr dick geworden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog has gotten very fat.

definitions.note: When used to describe a person, it can sound rude; for people, alternatives like „kräftig“ or „übergewichtig“ are often more polite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine dicke Jacke im Winter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a thick jacket in winter.

definitions.note: Adjective form with -en ending (often used after words like "die", "diese", "meine" in plural, or in some other cases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage die dicken Bücher nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m carrying the thick books home.

definitions.note: comparative form of „dick“ (used to compare: thicker/fatter than)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch ist dicker als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is thicker than the other one.

definitions.note: definite article form used with feminine singular nouns and with plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Frau liest ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman is reading a book.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a relative clause (refers back to a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die Frau, die neben mir sitzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s the woman who is sitting next to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die sind sehr teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are very expensive.

definitions.note: Feminine form of „derjenige“; used to point out a specific person/thing (often with a relative clause, e.g. „diejenige, die …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist diejenige, die den Schlüssel hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the one who has the key.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (e.g., „Ich diene dir.“ = “I serve you.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich diene meinem Land.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I serve my country.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (e.g., jemandem dienen = to serve someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will meinem Land dienen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to serve my country.

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ + noun (e.g., zu etwas dienen = to be used for something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel kann dazu dienen, die Tür zu öffnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key can be used to open the door.

definitions.note: means regularly/habitually on that weekday (every Tuesday)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dienstags habe ich einen Deutschkurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Tuesdays I have a German class.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „dienen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er dient in der Armee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He serves in the army.

definitions.note: Colloquial/short form of "dieses"; used with nouns (not as a standalone pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag dies Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this book.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun meaning “this (one/thing)” (can also be used like “that” depending on context). Not the verb “dies” in English (= stops living).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dies ist mein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my book.

definitions.note: Refers back to something already mentioned (often used in formal writing/speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe diesbezüglich noch eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have a question regarding this.

definitions.note: used before a noun; meaning depends on gender/number/case
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag diese Schuhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like these shoes.

definitions.note: feminine singular or plural form (depending on context) of "dieser".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Tasche ist neu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is new.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "derselbe" (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme dieselbe Jacke wie gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking the same jacket as yesterday.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "derselbe"; used to point to the very same person/thing (not just a similar one).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist dieselbe Frau, die ich gestern gesehen habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the same woman that I saw yesterday.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben dieselben Bücher gelesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We read the same books.

definitions.note: Dative masculine or neuter singular form of „dieser“; often used after prepositions like „mit“, „zu“, „bei“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit diesem Buch lerne ich Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning German with this book.

definitions.note: dative masculine or neuter singular form of "dieser"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe diesem Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm helping this man.

definitions.note: Form of "dieser" used especially as accusative masculine singular (e.g., „diesen Mann“) and also as dative plural (e.g., „mit diesen Leuten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne diesen Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this man.

definitions.note: masculine accusative singular form of “dieser” (also used with masculine accusative singular nouns like “diesen Mann”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne diesen Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this man.

definitions.note: Demonstrative determiner; this form is commonly used with masculine nouns in the nominative (e.g., „dieser Mann“ = “this man”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Hund ist sehr freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dog is very friendly.

definitions.note: demonstrative pronoun used for masculine nominative singular ("this one")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser ist meiner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This one is mine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe dieses Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying this book.

definitions.note: neuter nominative/accusative form of „dieser“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch ist sehr spannend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very exciting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diesmal komme ich pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This time I’m coming on time.

definitions.note: Old-fashioned/literary; in modern German usually "weil" or "da".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieweil es spät ist, gehen wir nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since it’s late, we’re going home.

definitions.note: dative form of informal singular “du” (used for an indirect object, often translated as “to you”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe dir das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving you the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine direkte Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a direct question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme direkt zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be right back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich direkt nach dem Essen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you right after eating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine direkte Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a direct answer.

definitions.note: comparative form of "direkt"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte direkter sagen, was du meinst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please say more directly what you mean?

definitions.note: Usually used for conducting an orchestra or choir.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird heute Abend das Orchester dirigieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will conduct the orchestra tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for being tactful or keeping something private/confidential.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sei diskret und erzähl es niemandem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be discreet and don’t tell anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich diskret mit ihr darüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak discreetly with her about it.

definitions.note: often used with „über“ + accusative (about) or „mit“ + dative (with someone)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir diskutieren über den neuen Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re discussing the new plan.

definitions.note: present tense (er/sie/es) of „diskutieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er diskutiert gerade mit seiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is discussing things with his sister right now.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural or formal "you"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern diskutierten wir lange über das Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we discussed the problem for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used to contradict a negative statement or assumption ("But it is!"), or to emphasize that something is true despite what was said before.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt doch heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is coming today after all.

definitions.note: Often used to contradict or correct what was just said ("but actually...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte kommen, doch ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to come, but I don’t have time.

definitions.note: Used to contradict a negative statement or assumption (like “yes it is!” / “it does!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Du kommst heute nicht. — Doch!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — You're not coming today. — Yes, I am!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte kommen, doch ich muss arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to come, but I have to work.

definitions.note: Often used as a modal particle to encourage or soften a request; it may not translate literally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm doch mit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just come along!

definitions.note: Used to contradict a negative question or statement ("Yes, on the contrary").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du keine Zeit? – Doch, ich habe Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t you have time? – Yes, I do have time.

definitions.note: informal/colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war doll von dir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was really great of you!

definitions.note: means “(every) Thursday” as a recurring time expression
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Donnerstags gehe ich nach der Arbeit ins Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Thursdays, I go to the gym after work.

definitions.note: An exclamation of surprise or annoyance; can be mild or stronger depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Donnerwetter, das ist ja teuer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, that’s really expensive!

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech; can be insulting depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine doofe Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a stupid idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute kostet das Ticket doppelt so viel wie gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the ticket costs twice as much as yesterday.

definitions.note: Used with a noun; here it’s the inflected form of the adjective “doppelt”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme die doppelte Menge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take the double amount.

definitions.note: refers to a place away from the speaker (often contrasted with „hier“ = here)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus hält dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stops there.

definitions.note: indicates movement toward a place (destination), not location
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe morgen dorthin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going there tomorrow.

definitions.note: Commonly used with verbs like „sein“/„kommen“ in expressions like „du bist dran“ (= it's your turn) or „ich bin dran“ (= I'm next).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist dran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's your turn.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „daran“; often used with verbs like „sein“, „arbeiten“, „denken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade dran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m on it right now.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ or „kommen“ to say whose turn it is.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist dran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s your turn.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „darauf“ (common in spoken German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leg das Buch drauf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on it.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „darauf“ when talking about what happens next.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat gelacht, und drauf ist er gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He laughed, and then he left.

definitions.note: colloquial shortening of „darauf“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leg das Buch drauf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on it (on top).

definitions.note: Colloquial form of "darauf"; often used with verbs like "legen" (put) or "stehen" (be on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leg das Buch bitte drauf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put the book on it.

definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht draufgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to die.

definitions.native: to be used up, to be spent (e.g., money)
definitions.note: often used with money, time, or resources
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Für die Reparatur kann das ganze Geld draufgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the money could be used up for the repair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin aus Versehen auf die Brille draufgetreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accidentally stepped on the glasses.

definitions.note: Colloquial shortened form of „daraus“. Often used with verbs like „machen“ (e.g., „etwas draus machen“ = make something of it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach was draus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Make something of it!

definitions.native: out of it, from it, out of that
definitions.note: Colloquial shortened form of "daraus".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was machst du draus?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What will you make out of it?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist kalt draußen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold outside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schuhe sind ganz dreckig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are really dirty.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with certain cases/genders/numbers (e.g., before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ziehe die dreckige Jacke aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take off the dirty jacket.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (attributive); ending depends on case/gender/number
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht auf dem dreckigen Boden sitzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to sit on the dirty floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Schuhe sind dreckiger als meine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your shoes are dirtier than mine.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a neuter noun in the nominative or accusative singular (e.g., „ein dreckiges Zimmer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein dreckiges Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a dirty room.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal imperative: „Dreh …!“ (= “Turn …!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dreh bitte den Schlüssel im Schloss!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn the key in the lock!

definitions.note: first-person singular present tense of „drehen“ (ich drehe)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich drehe mich um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turn around.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du dich bitte umdrehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn around?

definitions.note: Used with films/videos (e.g., einen Film drehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie drehen morgen einen Film in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are filming a movie in Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (you) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Drehst du bitte die Musik leiser?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you turn the music down, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er dreht das Rad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turns the wheel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drehte den Schlüssel im Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned the key in the lock.

definitions.note: Used with movies/TV: „einen Film drehen“ = to film/shoot a movie.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie drehte gestern eine Szene für den Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She filmed a scene for the movie yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "drehen" for "we/they" and formal "you" (Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie drehten sich um und gingen zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They turned around and went back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe drei Geschwister.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have three siblings.

definitions.note: dative plural form of the numeral "drei"; used after certain prepositions (e.g., "mit") or in fixed phrases
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe mit dreien meiner Freunde ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the cinema with three of my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kostet dreihundert Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That costs three hundred euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn dreimal angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called him three times.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used like hinein/herein (e.g., reingehen = gehen + drein).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh nicht einfach drein!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t just go in!

definitions.note: Usually describes behavior that is rude or shamelessly bold.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war wirklich dreist von ihm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was really cheeky of him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto kostet dreitausend Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car costs three thousand euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin dreizehn Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am thirteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin dreißig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am thirty years old.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often used instead of "drinnen" or "darin".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel ist drin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key is inside.

definitions.note: Informal/short for „drinnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin schon drin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m already inside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche dringend deine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I urgently need your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte ruf mich dringend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please call me urgently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist dringender als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is more urgent than yesterday.

definitions.note: Can be used literally (e.g., water, light, noise) or figuratively (insisting, pressing a point).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wasser dringt durch das Dach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water is getting through the roof.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist kalt draußen, aber drinnen ist es warm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold outside, but inside it’s warm.

definitions.note: Most commonly used in the phrase „zu dritt“ (= three people together).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen heute Abend zu dritt ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The three of us are going to the cinema tonight.

definitions.note: Usually used with "zu": "zu dritt" = "as a group of three".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen zu dritt ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The three of us are going to the movies.

definitions.note: Used as an ordinal number; often appears with feminine nouns (e.g., „die dritte …“) or as a nominalized form (e.g., „die Dritte“ = the third person/one).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die dritte Frage ist leicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The third question is easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am dritten Tag sind wir nach Berlin gefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the third day we drove to Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist drogenabhängig und braucht Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is drug-addicted and needs help.

definitions.note: Often used with “jemandem” (to someone) and/or “mit” + dative (with something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird mir mit der Polizei drohen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will threaten me with the police.

definitions.note: Used when something bad is about to happen (e.g., danger, a storm).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Unwetter wird drohen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A severe storm will be looming.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) present tense of „drohen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum drohst du mir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you threatening me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er droht mir mit der Polizei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threatens me with the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drohte, die Polizei zu rufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threatened to call the police.

definitions.note: Often used for printing documents or photos (e.g., from a computer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Dokument bitte drucken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please print the document?

definitions.note: colloquial shortening of „darum“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin müde, drum gehe ich jetzt nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m tired, so I’m going home now.

definitions.note: Often used in spoken German to explain a reason or consequence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe morgen frei, drum gehe ich heute früher ins Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have tomorrow off, therefore I'm going to bed earlier today.

definitions.note: colloquial form of „darunter“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze liegt drunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is lying underneath.

definitions.native: to push in, to shove, to cut in line
definitions.note: Often used for pushing past others in a crowd or at a line/queue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte drängeln Sie nicht, alle kommen gleich dran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t push in line; everyone will get their turn soon.

definitions.note: Often used when there is pressure (physical or metaphorical), e.g., in a crowd or to urge someone to act.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Leute drängen sich vor dem Eingang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: People are crowding in front of the entrance.

definitions.note: Can mean to push physically or to press/urge someone to do something; often used with "jemanden zu etwas drängen" (to pressure someone into something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drängt mich, schneller zu arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He urges me to work faster.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „drängen“; often used for telling stories or in written narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drängte sich durch die Menge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushed his way through the crowd.

definitions.native: over there, on the other side
definitions.note: Refers to a place at some distance from the speaker, often across something (e.g., a street, river, border).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Supermarkt ist drüben auf der anderen Straßenseite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supermarket is over there on the other side of the street.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „darüber“; often refers back to something previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben gestern drüber gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked about it yesterday.

definitions.note: colloquial form of „darüber“; often used with verbs of motion or position (e.g., drübergehen, drübersetzen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen gleich drüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll go over there in a moment.

definitions.note: Informal command form (du imperative) of „drücken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Drück bitte den Knopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Press the button, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich drücke den Knopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I press the button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht drücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please do not press.

definitions.note: Often used for pressing a button or pushing something down/in.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte drücken Sie den Knopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please press the button.

definitions.note: In this sense, it’s commonly used as jemanden drücken (to hug someone), often in contexts like saying hello/goodbye or comforting someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dich drücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to hug you.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ausdrücken“; often used with „aus“ at the end of the clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie drückt ihre Gefühle klar aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She expresses her feelings clearly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drückt den Knopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He presses the button.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „drücken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drückte den Knopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pressed the button.

definitions.note: informal singular (used with friends, family, children, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist sehr nett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are very nice.

definitions.note: informal singular (used with friends, family, children, or people your age); not used in formal situations
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist mein Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are my friend.

definitions.native: to smell nice, to be fragrant
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Rosen duften im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roses smell nice in the garden.

definitions.note: Usually used for pleasant scents (e.g., flowers, food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kaffee duftet frisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee smells fresh.

definitions.note: Often used for tolerating something unpleasant or undesirable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Lärm nicht länger dulden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t tolerate the noise any longer.

definitions.note: Often insulting; use carefully. For objects/decisions it can also mean “silly” or “a bad idea.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine dumme Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a dumb idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat dumm gelacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He laughed stupidly.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive adjective); its exact ending depends on gender/case and whether there is an article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine dumme Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a stupid idea.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „dumm“ (e.g., after „den/dem/die“ or in plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den dummen Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the stupid mistake.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „dumm“ (e.g. „dummer als …“ = „stupider than …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Test ist dummer als der letzte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This test is stupider than the last one.

definitions.note: Often used to mean that something happened because of a stupid mistake; similar to “stupidly” in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dummerweise habe ich den Termin vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I forgot the appointment.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun (e.g. "ein dummes Kind").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein dummes Missverständnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a stupid misunderstanding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Wald ist es nachts sehr dunkel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the forest it’s very dark at night.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., after a definite article like „den“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag den dunkelblauen Pullover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the dark blue sweater.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "dunkel" (used before a noun, e.g. "eine dunkle Nacht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Stadt gibt es viele dunkle Gassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the city there are many dark alleys.

definitions.note: Used here in a declined form (e.g., after an article or in certain cases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der dunklen Nacht habe ich nichts gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the dark night I didn’t see anything.

definitions.note: comparative form of "dunkel"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Blau ist dunkler als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This blue is darker than the other one.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter noun (e.g. „ein dunkles Zimmer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ein dunkles Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see a dark room.

definitions.note: Preposition; usually takes the accusative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch den Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking through the park.

definitions.note: Often takes the accusative case (e.g., durch den Park).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch den Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking through the park.

definitions.note: Used with accusative in the sense of cause/reason (e.g., durch den Regen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Flug fällt durch den Sturm aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flight is canceled because of the storm.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs (e.g., „durchgehen“ = to go through) or as a separable prefix; also common as a preposition, but here it’s used as an adverb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind durch und können nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re through and can go home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch den Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking through the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es durch einen Freund erfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found out about it through a friend.

definitions.native: take a deep breath, breathe deeply
definitions.note: Often used to mean “pause to calm down / recover” after stress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Gespräch musste ich erst einmal durchatmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the conversation, I first had to take a deep breath.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something is possible or true (sometimes like “quite” in “quite possible”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist durchaus möglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is definitely possible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein durchdachter Plan.
