definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a well-thought-out plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Umzug ist alles durcheinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the move, everything is all mixed up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir durchfahren den Tunnel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drive through the tunnel.

definitions.note: Often used for plans, tasks, projects, tests, or events.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden morgen die Umfrage durchführen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will carry out the survey tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used when you finish working through material (e.g., a book, exercises, a topic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Übungen komplett durchgearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked through the exercises completely.

definitions.note: Often used for working without a break, e.g., through the night.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die ganze Nacht durchgearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We worked straight through the whole night.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used to mean someone has lost control or is acting irrationally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der schlechten Nachricht ist er völlig durchgedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bad news, he totally freaked out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin durch die Prüfung durchgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I failed the exam.

definitions.note: Often used when a plan or proposal doesn’t succeed or is rejected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan ist durchgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan fell through.

definitions.note: past participle of „durchführen“ (often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die Umfrage letzte Woche durchgeführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We carried out the survey last week.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object, meaning to check or review something (e.g., a list, notes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind die Liste noch einmal durchgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went through the list one more time.

definitions.note: Used for physically going through a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist durch den Park durchgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walked through the park.

definitions.native: held out, endured, stuck it out
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe bis zum Ende durchgehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I held out until the end.

definitions.note: Often used for going through something step by step (e.g., a text, plan, or contract).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Vertrag noch einmal durchgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to go through the contract one more time.

definitions.note: Used especially when a horse (or sometimes a person) bolts and can’t be controlled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Pferd kann durchgehen, wenn es erschrickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The horse can bolt if it gets startled.

definitions.note: informal/colloquial; can be insulting depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Typ ist völlig durchgeknallt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That guy is completely crazy.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense (e.g. „Ich bin … durchgekommen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind trotz des Schnees gut durchgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got through fine despite the snow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Bericht durchgelesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read through the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe viel durchgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been through a lot.

definitions.native: pulled an all-nighter, stayed up all night
definitions.note: Often used with „die Nacht“ (e.g., „die Nacht durchmachen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die Nacht durchgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stayed up all night.

definitions.native: got through, made it through, endured
definitions.note: Past participle of "durchstehen"; often used with "haben" (hat ... durchgestanden).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die schwierige Zeit zum Glück durchgestanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, she got through the difficult time.

definitions.native: to keep going; to persevere; to hold out
definitions.note: often used for continuing despite difficulty, or lasting until the end of a demanding period
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht mehr, aber ich werde durchhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't go on anymore, but I will keep going.

definitions.note: Often used for getting through a difficult situation or getting through (e.g., by phone, through traffic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann gerade nicht durchkommen, die Leitung ist besetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t get through right now; the line is busy.

definitions.native: to let through; to allow through
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Türsteher wird nur Gäste mit Ticket durchlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bouncer will only let guests with a ticket through.

definitions.note: Often used for difficult experiences (e.g., a crisis, a hard time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine schwere Zeit durchmachen müssen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had to go through a hard time.

definitions.native: stay up all night, pull an all-nighter
definitions.note: Colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute Nacht durchmachen, um für die Prüfung zu lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to stay up all night tonight to study for the exam.

definitions.note: often used to describe being wet all the way through (e.g., from rain)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Spaziergang im Regen waren meine Schuhe völlig durchnässt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the walk in the rain, my shoes were completely soaked.

definitions.note: Often used for crossing a larger area or distance (e.g., a country, a forest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir durchqueren den Wald zu Fuß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We cross the forest on foot.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „durchqueren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er durchquerte die Straße bei Grün.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He crossed the street when the light was green.

definitions.note: contraction of "durch das" (usually with a neuter noun: "das ...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durchs Fenster rein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go in through the window.

definitions.note: Often means recognizing a trick, lie, or hidden intention (not being fooled).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann deinen Plan durchschauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can see through your plan.

definitions.note: Often used for seeing through a lie, trick, or someone's intentions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er durchschaut die Lüge sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sees through the lie immediately.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle (e.g., with "haben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat seinen Plan schnell durchschaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She quickly figured out his plan.

definitions.note: Often used as a separable verb in a sentence: „… schneidet … durch“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Seil durchschneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to cut through the rope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eine große Straße kann ein Wohngebiet durchschneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A big road can run through (cut across) a residential area.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verdiene durchschnittlich 2.500 Euro im Monat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On average, I earn 2,500 euros a month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Regeln konsequent durchsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to enforce the rules consistently.

definitions.note: Often used for making it through a difficult time or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen diese schwere Zeit gemeinsam durchstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get through this difficult time together.

definitions.native: to search (through); to rummage through; to comb through
definitions.note: means to search thoroughly within/through something (e.g., a room, bag, files, a website); separable: ich durchsuche, du durchsuchst, er/sie/es durchsucht; Perfekt: hat durchsucht
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei wird das Haus morgen durchsuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police will search the house tomorrow.

definitions.note: often used for systematically searching large amounts of information
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Datenbank nach dem Namen durchsuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to search the database for the name.

definitions.native: to search (someone) for weapons/contraband; to frisk
definitions.note: can be used for searching a person (e.g., by security or police)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sicherheitsdienst darf dich am Eingang durchsuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Security is allowed to search you at the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei durchsucht das Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police search the car.

definitions.note: past participle (used with auxiliaries like „hat“ or in passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat das Auto durchsucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police searched the car.

definitions.note: often implies a thorough search, e.g., by police or security
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei durchsuchte das Haus nach Beweisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police searched the house for evidence.

definitions.native: to pull through, to thread through
definitions.note: Often used for pulling something like a cable, string, or ribbon through an opening or loop.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Kabel durchziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pull the cable through.

definitions.note: Used when something (like a smell, feeling, or theme) spreads through a place or is present throughout something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein starker Duft kann die ganze Wohnung durchziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A strong smell can permeate the whole apartment.

definitions.note: Simple past of "dürfen"; often used for permission (was allowed to) or, in context, possibility (could).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich durfte gestern länger aufbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was allowed to stay up longer yesterday.

definitions.native: were allowed to, were permitted to, could
definitions.note: Past tense plural (Präteritum) of „dürfen“; often expresses permission or having the right to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir durften gestern länger aufbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were allowed to stay up later yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Lauf bin ich sehr durstig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run, I am very thirsty.

definitions.note: verb form of „duschen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Sport dusche ich schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After sports, I shower quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt duschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to shower now.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „duschen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er duscht jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He showers every morning.

definitions.note: simple past of „duschen“ (to shower)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern duschte ich nach dem Sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I showered after sports.

definitions.note: Used when speaking informally to someone (using “du” instead of “Sie”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir duzen uns im Team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We address each other with “du” on the team.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of „denken“ (ich/er/sie). Often used to sound tentative; commonly replaced by „würde denken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich dächte, das ist eine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would think that's a good idea.

definitions.note: Informal and insulting; use with care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine dämliche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a stupid idea.

definitions.note: Insulting/impolite; use with care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine dämliche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a stupid idea.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected form (e.g., after a definite article or as a weak ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen dämlichen Fehler gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a stupid mistake.

definitions.note: Often insulting; used to describe a person or thing as very foolish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein dämlicher Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a stupid mistake.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "dämlich"; often insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war dämlicher als nötig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was dumber than necessary.

definitions.note: Used for daybreak getting light, or figuratively for a realization starting to become clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Langsam dämmerte es, und wir gingen nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was slowly getting light, and we went home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen das Gemüse dämpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to steam the vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Teppiche dämpfen den Schall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Carpets dampen (muffle) the sound.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "dösen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Zug döste er kurz ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the train, he dozed off briefly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Test ist dümmer als der letzte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This test is dumber than the last one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Eis ist dünn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ice is thin.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., after "eine")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine dünne Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a thin jacket.

definitions.note: comparative form of „dünn“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Jacke ist dünner als die andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This jacket is thinner than the other one.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form (Konjunktiv I), often used in reported speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich dürfe heute früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that I may leave earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used to ask for permission or to say what is permitted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich darf hier sitzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am allowed to sit here.

definitions.note: Often used with another verb in the infinitive (e.g., „Ich darf gehen.“ = “I’m allowed to go.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich darf hier sitzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am allowed to sit here.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) form of "dürfen"; often used to ask for permission or give/deny permission.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr dürft hier nicht rauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) are not allowed to smoke here.

definitions.note: Often used to express a polite assumption/guess (similar to “probably”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das dürfte stimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is probably true.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II of "dürfen" used to express a guess/probability; also the plural form (sie/wir/ihr) in this usage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es dürfte heute regnen, und die Straßen dürften nass werden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will probably rain today, and the streets will likely get wet.

definitions.note: Often used for weather, places, moods, or a dark/ominous atmosphere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Himmel sieht heute düster aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky looks gloomy today.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something happened a moment ago, or to add emphasis like “just/simply.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn eben gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just saw him.

definitions.native: equal (in rank/status), on an equal footing
definitions.note: Often used for people/partners or groups being of the same rank, status, or standing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist ihm ebenbürtig und lässt sich nichts gefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is his equal and doesn’t let herself be pushed around.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme ebenfalls morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m also coming tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme ebenso morgen vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m also stopping by tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to say something is just as acceptable as an alternative (like “might as well”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst ebensogut morgen kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can come tomorrow just as well.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that a negative statement applies equally (frequently with „wie“: „ebensowenig wie …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ebensowenig Zeit wie du.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have just as little time as you do.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das eine echte Goldkette?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that a real gold chain?

definitions.note: Often used in spoken German to emphasize an adjective or statement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist echt schön!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really nice!

definitions.note: Commonly used as an intensifier in spoken German (like “really”/“totally”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist echt schön!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really nice!

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to show surprise or to ask for confirmation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echt? Das wusste ich nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Really? I didn’t know that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine echte Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a real story.

definitions.note: Accusative masculine singular / dative plural inflected form of „echt“ (used before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche einen echten Diamanten, aber ich will keinen echten Diamanten aus Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for a real diamond, but I don't want a "real" diamond made of glass.

definitions.native: to authenticate; to certify as genuine (rare, formal)
definitions.note: Verb „echten“ can mean to authenticate/verify something as genuine; relatively uncommon compared with „echt“ (adj.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gutachter musste das Dokument echten, bevor es vor Gericht verwendet werden durfte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The expert had to authenticate the document before it was allowed to be used in court.

definitions.note: Used as an attributive adjective before a masculine noun in nominative or accusative (e.g., „ein echter …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein echter Diamant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a real (genuine) diamond.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (e.g., "ein echtes ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein echtes Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a real problem.

definitions.note: Often used to describe people, character, or origin; can also describe something of high quality or refined style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist edel und gerecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is noble and just.

definitions.note: Common for materials (e.g., metals) and products; suggests something valuable or refined.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Stoff ist edel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fabric is fine/high-quality.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of the adjective used before a noun (e.g., with feminine nouns or in the plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine edle Geste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a noble gesture.

definitions.note: Often used as an inflected form of the adjective „edel“ before a noun (e.g. „ein edler Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein edler Mensch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a noble person.

definitions.note: Can also be the comparative form of „edel“ in predicate position (meaning “more noble/finer”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Wein ist edler als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This wine is finer than the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein edles Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a noble, fine gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Methode ist sehr effektiv.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method is very effective.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Maschine ist sehr effizient und spart Energie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This machine is very efficient and saves energy.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“: „Das ist mir egal“ = “I don’t care / It doesn’t matter to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist mir egal, was du machst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It doesn’t matter to me what you do.

definitions.note: Often used to say something is unimportant or that you don't care which option is chosen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist mir egal, was du machst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It doesn't matter to me what you do.

definitions.note: Often used to say you don't care or that something is unimportant; can sound dismissive depending on tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Egal, wir machen einfach weiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whatever, we'll just keep going.

definitions.note: Often used with „ob“: „egal, ob …“ = “whether … or not”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Egal, ob es regnet, wir gehen spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whether it rains or not, we’re going for a walk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist egoistisch von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s selfish of you.

definitions.note: Colloquial filler particle; often signals impatience, a mild objection, or that something is obvious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eh nicht so wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That isn't important anyway.

definitions.note: Used as a subordinating conjunction meaning “before” (often with the verb at the end).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wasch dir die Hände, ehe du isst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wash your hands before you eat.

definitions.note: often used before a noun (e.g., „meinen ehemaligen Lehrer“ = “my former teacher”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen ehemaligen Kollegen gestern getroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met my former colleague yesterday.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine singular noun in the nominative case (e.g., "ehemaliger Präsident").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein ehemaliger Chef wohnt jetzt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My former boss lives in Berlin now.

definitions.note: Often used to express a preference or that something is more likely.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte eher Tee als Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would rather have tea than coffee.

definitions.native: to honor, to pay tribute to
definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts or for showing respect (e.g., to people, achievements, traditions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir ehren die Sieger nach dem Rennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We honor the winners after the race.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr ehrgeizig und lernt jeden Tag Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very ambitious and learns German every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei bitte ehrlich zu mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be honest with me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir eine ehrliche Antwort gegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a frank answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ehrlich gesagt, habe ich heute keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Honestly, I don't have time today.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected form; used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article/case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine ehrliche Person.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an honest person.

definitions.note: comparative form of „ehrlich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ehrlicher als sein Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is more honest than his brother.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/ceremonial contexts to show respect (e.g., a respected person or institution).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchten die ehrwürdige Kirche im Stadtzentrum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited the venerable church in the city center.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchten den ehrwürdigen Dom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited the venerable cathedral.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist eifersüchtig auf ihren neuen Kollegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is jealous of her new coworker.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie arbeitet eifrig an ihrem Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is working diligently on her project.

definitions.note: comparative form of the adverb/adjective "eifrig"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du eifriger lernst, bestehst du die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you study more diligently, you’ll pass the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wirkt ein bisschen eigenartig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man seems a bit strange.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein eigenartiger Geruch liegt in der Luft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A strange smell is in the air.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "eigenartig".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der zweite Film war eigenartiger als der erste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The second movie was stranger than the first.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with feminine singular or plural nouns, or after a definite article (weak ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine eigene Meinung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have my own opinion.

definitions.note: dative singular (masculine or neuter) form of "eigen" (used with a dative masculine/neuter noun after a dative article like "dem/meinem/deinem")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe meinem eigenem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping my own brother.

definitions.note: Form of "eigen" used with a noun (attributive), e.g. after a determiner like "meinen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen eigenen Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have my own key.

definitions.note: Often used with possessive words to emphasize that something belongs to someone (e.g. „mein eigener …“ = “my own …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mein eigener Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my own key.

definitions.note: Used with a neuter noun (e.g., „ein eigenes Zimmer“ = „a room of one’s own“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein eigenes Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have my own room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr eigensinnig und macht alles auf ihre Weise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very stubborn and does everything her own way.

definitions.note: Often used to soften a question or to correct/clarify something (similar to “actually” or “to be honest”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eigentlich wollte ich heute zu Hause bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Actually, I wanted to stay at home today.

definitions.note: Most often used reflexively: „sich eignen (für)“ = to be suitable (for).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch eignet sich gut für Anfänger, weil es die Grundlagen klar erklärt und sich dafür sehr gut eignet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is well suited for beginners because it explains the basics clearly and is very suitable for that.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" (e.g., „Es eignet sich …“) to mean “it is suitable …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Raum eignet sich gut für Besprechungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is very suitable for meetings.

definitions.note: Often used in a slightly formal or written style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss zur Arbeit eilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to hurry to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es eilig und muss jetzt los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm in a hurry and have to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es eilig und muss jetzt los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in a hurry and have to leave now.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „eilen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er eilt zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hurries to the train station.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „eilen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er eilte zum Bahnhof, weil der Zug gleich abfuhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hurried to the train station because the train was leaving soon.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „eilen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir eilten zum Bahnhof, aber der Zug war schon weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hurried to the train station, but the train was already gone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nur ein Ticket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have one ticket.

definitions.note: Used as an indefinite article ("a/an") or as the number "one"; which meaning it has depends on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a book.

definitions.note: Indefinite article used before some singular nouns (not the same as English “in”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a book.

definitions.note: Used before a noun to mean “one”; the standalone form of the number is usually “eins”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nur ein Kaffee, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just one coffee, please.

definitions.note: Used like an indefinite article before masculine/neuter singular nouns, and also as the number “one” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a book.

definitions.note: Used when the action is mutual/reciprocal (often after a preposition: miteinander, füreinander, voneinander, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir helfen einander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We help each other.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte einatmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please breathe in.

definitions.note: usually means entering a building illegally (burglary)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand wollte letzte Nacht in die Wohnung einbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone tried to break into the apartment last night.

definitions.note: often used for roofs, floors, or ice
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Dach kann bei starkem Schnee einbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof can collapse in heavy snow.

definitions.note: used especially with „Die Nacht bricht ein.“; the infinitive is „einbrechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn die Nacht einbricht, scheint es, als würde die Welt verstummen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When night falls, it seems as if the world goes quiet.

definitions.native: to bring in, to carry in
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Einkäufe einbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to bring the groceries in.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., politics, meetings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Partei will einen Gesetzesentwurf einbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party wants to introduce a draft law.

definitions.note: Used for flights, hotels, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen am Flughafen einchecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to check in at the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Antwort ist eindeutig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eindeutig zu teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is clearly too expensive.

definitions.note: feminine form of the indefinite article (used with feminine nouns in nominative/accusative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cat.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of the indefinite article/number "ein" (used in nominative and accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cat.

definitions.note: Used before feminine nouns (and sometimes in set phrases) as the indefinite article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cat.

definitions.note: feminine form of the indefinite article
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a question.

definitions.note: feminine form of the indefinite article/number (used with feminine nouns in nominative/accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cat.

definitions.note: indefinite article/pronoun used with feminine nouns (nominative or accusative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cat.

definitions.note: Used mainly to describe twins ("eineiige Zwillinge" = identical twins).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sind eineiige Zwillinge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are identical twins.

definitions.note: Also commonly written as „anderthalb“ in many contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte noch eineinhalb Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll wait another hour and a half.

definitions.note: Dative masculine or neuter form of "ein"; used after certain prepositions/verbs or as an indirect object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe einem Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping a friend.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter form of "ein"; used before masculine/neuter nouns in the dative case
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe einem Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping a friend.

definitions.note: dative singular of the indefinite article (masculine/neuter); often translated as “to a” or “for a” depending on the verb/preposition
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe einem Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping a friend.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter form of "ein" (often translated as "to a" / "for a" depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe einem Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping a friend.

definitions.note: dative singular (masculine/neuter) form of «ein»
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe einem Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping a friend.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular form of "ein"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a dog.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular form of the indefinite article "ein"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe einen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see a dog.

definitions.note: masculine accusative form of the indefinite article/pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a dog.

definitions.note: accusative form of the pronoun „einer“ (refers to one person/one of them)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne einen, der in Berlin wohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know someone who lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun meaning “one (of them)”; this form is accusative masculine singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme einen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take one.

definitions.note: Used as the masculine nominative or neuter genitive form of the indefinite article/pronoun "ein".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einer der Studenten kommt aus Kanada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One of the students comes from Canada.

definitions.note: Indefinite pronoun for a (male) person; often used like “one of (them/us/you) …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einer von euch hat seinen Schlüssel vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One of you forgot his key.

definitions.note: Genitive singular form (usually masculine or neuter) of „ein“; often used like “of a”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen eines Unfalls ist die Straße gesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of an accident, the road is closed.

definitions.note: Genitive singular form of "ein" (masculine/neuter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das Ende eines Films.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the end of a movie.

definitions.note: Often used in partitive expressions like „eines davon“ = “one of them/one of those.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eines davon ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One of them is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aufgabe ist einfach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The task is simple.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “just” when giving a simple suggestion or instruction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm einfach morgen vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just come by tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die Aufgabe einfach gelöst, ohne Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He solved the task easily, without help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine einfache Aufgabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a simple task.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine accusative or plural dative (weak or mixed declension), depending on the article
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen einfachen Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a simple plan.

definitions.note: comparative form of „einfach“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Aufgabe ist einfacher als die letzte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This task is easier than the last one.

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adverb „einfach“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte einfacher erklären?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please explain that more simply?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein einfaches Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a simple problem.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "einfach"; often used with "der/die/das" as a noun phrase meaning "the simplest/easiest (one/solution)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die einfachste Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the simplest solution.

definitions.native: to drive in, to enter (by vehicle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug wird gleich in den Bahnhof einfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will pull into the station shortly.

definitions.native: to occur to (someone), to come to mind
definitions.note: Often used with a dative person (e.g., mir, dir): "Mir fällt etwas ein."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir kann gerade nichts einfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nothing is coming to mind right now.

definitions.note: Used for buildings/roofs, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn es weiter regnet, kann das Dach einfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it keeps raining, the roof could collapse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine einflussreiche Politikerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an influential politician.

definitions.note: Often used for putting food in the freezer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Brot einfrieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will freeze the bread.

definitions.note: often used with a dative pronoun (e.g., mir, dir): „Mir fällt etwas ein.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir einfällt gerade keine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No good idea is coming to mind right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn die Decke nachgibt, einfällt sie plötzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the ceiling gives way, it suddenly caves in.

definitions.note: Often negative: implies someone is not very intelligent or is easily fooled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war so einfältig, dass er jeden Trick glaubte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was so simple-minded that he believed every trick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr einfühlsam und versteht, wie andere sich fühlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very empathetic and understands how other people feel.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive verb "sich einbilden" (e.g., "sich etwas einbilden" = to imagine something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir das nur eingebildet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only imagined that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist so eingebildet, dass er nie Fehler zugibt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is so conceited that he never admits mistakes.

definitions.note: Often used for something someone thinks is real, but it isn’t (e.g., an illness or fear).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärztin sagt, seine Schmerzen sind nur eingebildet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor says his pains are only imaginary.

definitions.note: Past participle of „einbrechen“ meaning to break into a building (e.g., burglary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In die Wohnung wurde letzte Nacht eingebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment was broken into last night.

definitions.note: Past participle of „einbrechen“ meaning something collapses or gives way (e.g., a roof, ice, ground).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Dach ist unter dem Schnee eingebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof collapsed under the snow.

definitions.note: past participle of „eindringen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist eingedrungen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wasser ist in den Keller eingedrungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water has entered the basement.

definitions.note: Past participle of "einfallen"; commonly used with "sein" and often with "mir/dir/ihm..." (dative) for ideas or thoughts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist ein guter Name eingefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A good name occurred to me.

definitions.note: past participle of „einfangen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die Katze eingefangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We caught the cat.

definitions.note: Often used for payments, emails, or applications (e.g. „Die Zahlung ist eingegangen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zahlung ist eingegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The payment has been received.

definitions.note: past participle of „einhalten“; often used in the perfect tense or in the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regeln wurden eingehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rules were followed.

definitions.native: to address, to go into (a topic)
definitions.note: Often used with „auf“: „auf etwas eingehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer wird auf meine Frage eingehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher will address my question.

definitions.note: Often used for plants (and sometimes animals/businesses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Blumen werden ohne Wasser eingehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flowers will die off without water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Läufer hat seinen Gegner eingeholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The runner caught up with his opponent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Ball eingeholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fetched the ball.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eingekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went shopping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle eingeladenen Gäste sind schon da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the invited guests are already here.

definitions.note: Past participle of „einladen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „Ich bin eingeladen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin zu Marias Geburtstagsparty eingeladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m invited to Maria’s birthday party.

definitions.note: Past participle of "einlassen"; often used for being allowed to enter (e.g., in passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde nicht eingelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wasn’t let in.

definitions.note: Usually used with reflexive „sich einleben“ (to get used to a new place/situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach zwei Wochen hat sie sich in der neuen Stadt gut eingelebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After two weeks, she had settled in well in the new city.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like being admitted or committed to an institution (especially a hospital).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall wurde er ins Krankenhaus eingeliefert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was admitted to the hospital.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g., „Ich bin eingeloggt.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin schon eingeloggt und kann das Formular ausfüllen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m already logged in and can fill out the form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kräuter sind in die Soße eingemischt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The herbs are mixed into the sauce.

definitions.note: Often used with „sich“: „sich in etwas eingemischt“ = to interfere/get involved in something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich in das Gespräch eingemischt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He interfered in the conversation.

definitions.note: Often used for taking medicine (e.g., tablets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Tablette eingenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have taken the tablet.

definitions.note: past participle of "einpacken"; often used like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Geschenke schon eingepackt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already wrapped the gifts.

definitions.note: past participle of „einreichen“; commonly used with „haben“ (perfect tense) or in the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Antrag gestern eingereicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I submitted the application yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das alte Fahrrad ist total eingerostet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old bicycle is completely rusty.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively for skills you haven't used in a long time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin beim Sprechen noch etwas eingerostet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm still a bit out of practice when speaking.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., with „sein“: „ist eingeschaltet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist eingeschaltet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is switched on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist im Unterricht eingeschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell asleep in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind ist schon eingeschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is already asleep.

definitions.note: Often used for lightning (“Der Blitz hat eingeschlagen.”) or for hitting/knocking something into something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Blitz hat in den Baum eingeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lightning struck the tree.

definitions.note: Used with things like Weg, Richtung, Kurs, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben einen neuen Weg eingeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took a new path.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Preis ist das Frühstück eingeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Breakfast is included in the price.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to mean that something is part of a price/offer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Preis ist das Frühstück eingeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Breakfast is included in the price.

definitions.note: Often used about children when they begin primary school (die Einschulung).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Tochter ist dieses Jahr eingeschult worden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My daughter started school this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schaden wurde auf 5.000 Euro eingeschätzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The damage was estimated at 5,000 euros.

definitions.note: Often used in passive constructions like „wird eingesetzt“ (= is used/deployed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Software wird in vielen Firmen eingesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The software is used in many companies.

definitions.note: Common when talking about people being assigned/appointed to a role (often with „als“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde als Teamleiter eingesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was appointed as team leader.

definitions.note: past participle of „einsetzen“; often used in passive ("wird eingesetzt" = "is used")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Computer wird in der Schule eingesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer is used at school.

definitions.note: Often used for people/animals being kept somewhere and not allowed to leave.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist im Keller eingesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is locked up in the basement.

definitions.note: past participle of „einsperren“; used with „sein“ (state/result) or „werden“ (passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist im Garten eingesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is locked up in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde gestern eingestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was hired yesterday.

definitions.note: used for products, services, or production that is stopped permanently
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Produktion wurde eingestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Production was discontinued.

definitions.note: used for settings on a device or system
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wecker ist auf sieben Uhr eingestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The alarm clock is set for seven o’clock.

definitions.note: Used especially for getting into a vehicle (bus, train, car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern in den Bus eingestiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got on the bus yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „einsteigen“, often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in den Bus eingestiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got on the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die alte Brücke ist letzte Woche eingestürzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old bridge collapsed last week.

definitions.note: past participle of „eintreffen“, often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist eingetroffen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist pünktlich eingetroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train arrived on time.

definitions.note: Past participle of „einwandern“; in the perfect tense it is usually used with „sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Großeltern sind in den 1960er-Jahren nach Deutschland eingewandert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents immigrated to Germany in the 1960s.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Geschenk ist schon eingewickelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The present is already wrapped.

definitions.note: often used with „in + Akk.“ (e.g. „in den Vertrag einwilligen“ = to consent to the contract)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat in die Bedingungen eingewilligt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She consented to the terms.

definitions.note: Literally “thrown in”; commonly used for putting a letter into a mailbox.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Brief gestern eingeworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I posted the letter yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine Münze in den Automaten eingeworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She put a coin into the machine.

definitions.note: past participle of „einziehen“ (to move in)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzte Woche sind wir in die neue Wohnung eingezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last week we moved into the new apartment.

definitions.note: past participle of „einziehen“ in the sense of taking something away officially (e.g., by the police)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat seinen Führerschein eingezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police confiscated his driver’s license.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern in die neue Wohnung eingezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moved into the new apartment yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used when money is taken automatically (e.g., taxes, fees, direct debit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gebühr wird jeden Monat automatisch eingezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fee is automatically collected every month.

definitions.note: Separable verb: in the present tense you often see it split (e.g. „ich hole dich ein“), but it remains the same verb „einholen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Läufer will den Führenden einholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The runner wants to catch up with the leader.

definitions.native: to bring in, to collect (e.g. laundry)
definitions.note: Often used for bringing something inside from outside (e.g. laundry before it rains).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Wäsche einholen, bevor es regnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to bring in the laundry before it rains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kostet einhundert Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That costs one hundred euros.

definitions.note: Most often used with „(sich) einig sein“ (to agree).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind uns einig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agree.

definitions.note: Used with plural nouns (and sometimes with uncountable nouns) to mean an unspecified small number or amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einige Leute warten schon draußen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some people are already waiting outside.

definitions.note: Used for an indefinite number (more than one). Often used with plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einige Freunde kommen heute Abend vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some friends are coming over this evening.

definitions.note: Dative form of „einig-“ (often used after prepositions like „mit“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit einigem Glück bekommen wir heute noch einen Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With some luck, we’ll still get a table today.

definitions.note: dative plural form of "einige"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mit einigen Freunden gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I talked with some friends.

definitions.note: Dative plural form of "einige" (often used after prepositions like "mit", "von", "zu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mit einigen Freunden gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I talked with some friends.

definitions.note: Most often used reflexively: „sich einigen“ = to reach an agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen uns einigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to come to an agreement.

definitions.note: Genitive form of "einige" (often used after genitive prepositions like "trotz").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trotz einiger Probleme hat alles gut funktioniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite some problems, everything worked well.

definitions.note: Refers to an unspecified amount or number; often used to mean “some things” or “a lot (of stuff)” in a general way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe noch einiges zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have quite a bit to do.

definitions.note: neuter form of "einige"; often used as a pronoun meaning “some (things)” or as a quantity meaning “quite a bit.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe noch einiges zu erledigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have some things to do.

definitions.native: quite a few things, some things
definitions.note: Often implies “a fair amount” rather than just a little.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe noch einiges zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have quite a bit to do.

definitions.note: Refers to an unspecified amount; often suggests more than just „etwas“ (“something”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einiges gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned quite a bit.

definitions.note: Often used with “sich” (sich einigen = to agree/reach an agreement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach langen Verhandlungen einigten sie sich auf einen Preis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After long negotiations, they agreed on a price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute nach der Arbeit einkaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going shopping after work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich morgen zu meiner Party einladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will invite you to my party tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Café sieht sehr einladend aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The café looks very inviting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen Gurken einlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to pickle cucumbers.

definitions.note: Usually used with "eine Pause": "eine Pause einlegen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss eine Pause einlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take a break.

definitions.note: Often used with tickets, vouchers, coupons, points, or a promise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte diesen Gutschein einlösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to redeem this voucher.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “one time” in general, or “once/at some point” (e.g., in requests or suggestions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war einmal in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was once in Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich einmischen (in + Akk.)“ = to get involved (in a way that isn’t wanted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich nicht in eure Diskussion einmischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to interfere in your discussion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst die Tablette morgens einnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to take the tablet in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used for revenue/earnings (e.g., a shop, event, or company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Laden kann an einem guten Tag viel Geld einnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shop can bring in a lot of money on a good day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht zwei Sitze einnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t occupy two seats.

definitions.note: Often used for packing things into a bag/suitcase or wrapping something (e.g., a gift).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch meine Sachen einpacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to pack my things.

definitions.note: Often used for putting a picture or photo in a frame.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dieses Foto einrahmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to frame this photo.

definitions.note: Often used for officially submitting documents (e.g., an application or request).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Antrag heute einreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to submit the application today.

definitions.native: to set up, to furnish, to arrange
definitions.note: Used for furnishing/setting up a room or home, setting up devices/accounts, or arranging something so it works as intended.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die neue Wohnung noch einrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still need to furnish/set up the new apartment.

definitions.note: Used as a standalone number (e.g., counting or as a noun); before a noun it usually becomes „ein/eine“ depending on gender and case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have one.

definitions.note: used as a pronoun (often meaning “one” as a standalone number, not before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme eins.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich heute einsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel lonely today.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a noun (e.g., feminine nominative/accusative or plural, depending on context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine einsame Frau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a lonely woman.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine or neuter nouns in accusative singular (e.g., after "den" or "ein")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den einsamen Mann am Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the lonely man by the window.

definitions.note: often used as an adjective ending (e.g., masculine nominative singular) before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein einsamer Mann sitzt am Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A lonely man is sitting by the window.

definitions.note: comparative form of „einsam“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit dem Umzug ist er einsamer als früher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since the move, he is lonelier than before.

definitions.note: Often used for collecting scattered things or gathering items/money/signatures from multiple places.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Konzert haben wir den Müll einsammeln müssen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, we had to collect the trash.

definitions.note: Often used for devices, lights, TVs, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Licht einschalten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn on the light?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann heute Abend nicht einschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't fall asleep this evening.

definitions.native: to hit, strike; to smash in
definitions.note: Often used for hitting forcefully (e.g., smashing a window) or when something hits (e.g., lightning strikes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball wird gleich in die Scheibe einschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball is about to smash into the window.

definitions.note: Used when turning onto a street or choosing a direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen hier rechts einschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to turn right here.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of "einschlafen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind einschlief sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child fell asleep right away.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive, often also with the dative in everyday German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis ist einschließlich Steuern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price is including taxes.

definitions.note: Often used with a clause: „Ich sehe ein, dass …“ (= I realize/understand that …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann einsehen, dass du recht hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can see (realize) that you’re right.

definitions.note: Often used for official documents or records you are allowed to view.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst die Unterlagen morgen im Büro einsehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can inspect (look at) the documents tomorrow at the office.

definitions.note: Separable verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die SIM-Karte einsetzen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please insert the SIM card?

definitions.note: Often used with tools, methods, or resources.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können diese Methode im Unterricht einsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can use this method in class.

definitions.note: Often used for weather (e.g., rain, frost) starting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Abend kann Regen einsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the evening, rain can set in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma einsetzt neue Software ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company uses new software.

definitions.note: Often used for putting a person or animal in a closed place so they can’t get out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei wird den Mann für zwei Jahre einsperren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police will imprison the man for two years.

definitions.note: Somewhat literary/old-fashioned; often refers to the past ("back then").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einst lebte er in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Once he lived in Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something into a pocket, bag, or socket.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst den Schlüssel einstecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to put the key in (e.g., into your pocket).

definitions.note: Common when someone takes money and keeps it instead of giving it to someone else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will das Geld einstecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to pocket the money.

definitions.note: Used for getting into a car/taxi and for boarding public transport (bus/train/tram/plane).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden an der nächsten Haltestelle in den Bus einsteigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will get on the bus at the next stop.

definitions.note: Often used for hiring staff (e.g., a company hires someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma will nächstes Jahr zehn neue Leute einstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to hire ten new people next year.

definitions.note: Often used for adjusting a device or settings (e.g., set the temperature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Heizung auf 20 Grad einstellen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you set the heating to 20 degrees?

definitions.note: simple past of „eintreten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als ich ankam, eintrat er gerade in den Raum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, he was just entering the room.

definitions.note: Often used for arriving at a place or for something (e.g., a letter, news) arriving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug soll um 18 Uhr eintreffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is supposed to arrive at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Often used with a place/building (e.g. ein Zimmer, ein Haus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie möchte jetzt in den Raum eintreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She would like to enter the room now.

definitions.note: Used for events or situations (e.g. ein Fall, eine Veränderung).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn dieser Fall eintritt, kann eine Verzögerung eintreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If this case occurs, a delay can occur.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“: „Ich bin einverstanden.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit dem Plan einverstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree with the plan.

definitions.note: Often used to mean that something works correctly or is in good condition (no faults).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Computer funktioniert einwandfrei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer works perfectly.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “without any faults/problems,” e.g., when something works properly or is in good condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Computer funktioniert einwandfrei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The computer works flawlessly.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/legal contexts; commonly with „in + Akk.“ (einwilligen in etw.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde in die Verarbeitung meiner Daten einwilligen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will consent to the processing of my data.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nennen Sie die Namen einzeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please say the names one by one.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective meaning “individual” in phrases like „einzelne Personen“ (“individual people”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einzelne Schüler haben die Aufgabe schon fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Individual students have already finished the task.

definitions.note: Often used after a definite article (e.g., „die einzelnen …“) meaning “the individual …” (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die einzelnen Schritte genau erklärt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We explained the individual steps in detail.

definitions.note: used for moving into a new home/apartment
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen nächsten Monat in die neue Wohnung einziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to move into the new apartment next month.

definitions.native: to pull in, to draw in
definitions.note: often used for things like curtains, awnings, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte die Vorhänge einziehen, es wird dunkel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pull in the curtains; it’s getting dark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einzig diese Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have only this question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Gemälde ist wirklich einzigartig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painting is truly unique.

definitions.note: adjective in a declined form (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine einzigartige Gelegenheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a unique opportunity.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (usually with an article, e.g. „die/der/das Einzige“) meaning ‘the only one’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die Einzige, die heute Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the only one who has time today.

definitions.note: Usually used with a definite article (e.g., „die einzige …“) to mean “the only …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die einzige Person, die mir geholfen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the only person who helped me.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective “einzig”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nur einen einzigen Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have one brother.

definitions.note: Declined form of „einzig“ used before a masculine noun (e.g., „mein einziger Bruder“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist mein einziger Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is my only brother.
