definitions.note: Often used to mean the only one (not necessarily “unique” in the sense of being special).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mein einziges Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my only problem.

definitions.note: Used with „auf“ + accusative: „auf etwas eingehen“ = to respond to / address something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit, auf diese Frage einzugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have time to go into this question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Pflanze droht einzugehen, wenn du sie nicht gießt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plant might die if you don't water it.

definitions.note: used as the 'zu' infinitive form of the verb „eingestehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er weigert sich, den Fehler einzugestehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He refuses to admit the mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, dich einzuholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to catch up with you.

definitions.note: Often used with "Informationen/Auskünfte einzuholen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen erst Informationen einzuholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We first have to obtain some information.

definitions.note: Infinitive with „zu“, often used after another verb (e.g. „gehen“, „versuchen“, „Zeit haben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe in den Supermarkt, um einzukaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the supermarket to shop.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „einladen“ (used after certain verbs, e.g. „versuchen“, „vergessen“, „bitten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergessen, meine Nachbarn einzuladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to invite my neighbors.

definitions.note: Used with "zu" (e.g., after verbs like "vergessen", "versuchen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergessen, den Hund einzulassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to let the dog in.

definitions.note: often used in medical instructions (e.g., tablets, drops)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, die Tablette nach dem Essen einzunehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to take the tablet after eating.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive of „einpacken“ (often used with „um ... zu“ or after verbs like „vergessen“, „versuchen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergessen, das Geschenk einzupacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to wrap the present.

definitions.note: Often used for formal submissions (e.g., documents, applications, proposals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte vergessen Sie nicht, den Antrag bis Freitag einzureichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don't forget to submit the application by Friday.

definitions.native: to turn on, to switch on
definitions.note: zu-Infinitiv form (used after verbs like versuchen, vergessen, planen, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, das Licht einzuschalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to turn on the light.

definitions.note: This is the "zu" infinitive form (used after certain verbs and in some constructions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, früh einzuschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to fall asleep early.

definitions.note: often used with vehicles (bus, train, car)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss an der nächsten Haltestelle aussteigen, und du kannst dann einzusteigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get off at the next stop, and then you can get on.

definitions.native: to start, to begin (talking about something)
definitions.note: often used when starting a topic or beginning a discussion
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bevor wir einzusteigen, möchte ich noch eine Frage stellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before we start, I’d like to ask one more question.

definitions.note: often used for hiring employees
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir planen, nächstes Jahr drei neue Leute einzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We plan to hire three new people next year.

definitions.note: used for ending an activity, service, or production
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma hat beschlossen, die Produktion einzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company decided to stop production.

definitions.note: used for setting or adjusting a device or setting
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, die Heizung richtig einzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to set the heating correctly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das alte Gebäude droht einzustürzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old building is in danger of collapsing.

definitions.native: to object, to raise an objection
definitions.note: used as a "zu"-infinitive (e.g., "nichts dagegen einzuwenden haben")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nichts dagegen einzuwenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no objection to that.

definitions.note: Often also used figuratively to mean “iron/unyielding” (e.g., strict discipline).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben eine eiserne Tür im Keller.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have an iron door in the basement.

definitions.note: Often used literally (very cold) or figuratively (emotionally cold, unfriendly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wasser ist eiskalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is ice-cold.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective "eiskalt" (used before a noun or after "sein/werden").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trank einen Schluck eiskalte Limonade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drank a sip of ice-cold lemonade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist eitel und spricht ständig über sein Aussehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is vain and constantly talks about his appearance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Geruch in der Küche ist ekelhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smell in the kitchen is disgusting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Geruch ist echt eklig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smell is really disgusting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt ein elegantes Kleid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing an elegant dress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug fährt elektrisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train runs electrically.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (e.g., before a feminine singular noun like „elektrische Lampe“ or with certain plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die elektrische Lampe ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The electric lamp is broken.

definitions.note: adjective ending used here for accusative masculine or dative/genitive plural (weak declension, e.g. after "den" or "die")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich repariere den elektrischen Motor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m repairing the electric motor.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong negative feelings (e.g., about a situation, illness, weather, or someone's condition).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine elende Erkältung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a miserable cold.

definitions.note: Often expresses strong negative emotion; can also be used as an insult (like “you miserable …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe diesen elenden Fehler gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made this miserable mistake.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong disapproval (e.g. about a person, situation, or thing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein elender Trick.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a miserable trick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin elf Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am eleven years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mannschaft wurde im Halbfinale eliminiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team was eliminated in the semifinals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war sehr emotional.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very emotional.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular nouns or plural nouns, depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine emotionale Rede.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an emotional speech.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „empfehlen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt empfahl mir mehr Schlaf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor recommended that I get more sleep.

definitions.note: Simple past of "empfinden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich empfand große Erleichterung nach dem Gespräch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt great relief after the conversation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich empfange heute ein Paket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I receive a package today.

definitions.note: Often used for receiving guests/visitors (e.g., officially), or receiving something like a letter or a signal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir empfangen morgen Besuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are receiving visitors tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir dieses Buch empfehlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can recommend this book to you.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „empfehlen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welches Restaurant empfiehlst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which restaurant do you recommend?

definitions.note: Often used for feelings or sensations (including how you react to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich empfinde große Dankbarkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel great gratitude.

definitions.note: Often used for how something feels or is experienced (e.g., pain, cold, something as pleasant/unpleasant).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann große Freude empfinden, wenn ich meine Familie sehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel great joy when I see my family.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form). Often used for feelings, impressions, or sensations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie empfindest du das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you feel about that?

definitions.note: Often used for feelings or reactions (e.g., finding something pleasant/unpleasant).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er empfindet große Freude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels great joy.

definitions.note: Often used for people (sensitive) or things/technology (sensitive, delicate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Haut ist sehr empfindlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My skin is very sensitive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte wasch die empfindliche Bluse nur im Schonwaschgang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wash the delicate blouse only on the gentle cycle.

definitions.note: past participle of "empfehlen"; often used in the passive ("wurde empfohlen") or perfect tense ("hat empfohlen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Restaurant wurde mir empfohlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This restaurant was recommended to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das als ungerecht empfunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt that was unfair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er empfängt heute ein wichtiges Paket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He receives an important package today.

definitions.note: often used for receiving guests or visitors (e.g., at the door or at a reception).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gastgeberin empfängt ihre Gäste an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hostess welcomes her guests at the door.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion to mean moving upward (e.g., „emporsteigen“, „emporheben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball flog hoch empor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball flew high up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war empört über die ungerechte Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was outraged about the unfair decision.

definitions.note: Intransitive or transitive; often used as „enden“ (intransitive: to come to an end) or „etw. enden“ (transitive: to end sth.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film kann heute früher enden, aber ich möchte ihn richtig enden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie can end earlier today, but I want it to end properly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du endest den Brief mit deinem Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You end the letter with your name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film endet um 20 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie ends at 8 p.m.

definitions.note: Simple past of "enden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film endete um zehn Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie ended at ten o'clock.

definitions.note: Often used for decisions, results, or deadlines that cannot be changed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Entscheidung ist endgültig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision is final.

definitions.note: often used for decisions or results that can’t be changed
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Entscheidung ist endgültig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision is final.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a feminine noun (or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir warten noch auf die endgültige Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are still waiting for the final decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Endlich bin ich mit der Arbeit fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally, I’m done with the work.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective (e.g., before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten eine endlose Diskussion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had an endless discussion.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in declined forms (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben einen endlosen Strand entlangspaziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked along an endless beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schuhe sind mir zu eng.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are too tight for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist hier sehr eng.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is very narrow here.

definitions.native: to hire, to engage (someone for a job/role)
definitions.note: Used with a direct object, often in formal contexts (e.g., hiring an artist, speaker, expert).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma will für das Projekt eine Expertin engagieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to hire an expert for the project.

definitions.note: Commonly reflexive: sich engagieren (e.g., for a cause/organization).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er möchte sich ehrenamtlich engagieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to get involved as a volunteer.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive „sich engagieren“ + „für“ (a cause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie engagiert sich für den Umweltschutz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is committed to environmental protection.

definitions.native: hires, books (e.g. an actor or musician)
definitions.note: Used especially in cultural/work contexts (theater, film, events).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Theater engagiert einen neuen Schauspieler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The theater hires a new actor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr engagiert und hilft jede Woche im Tierheim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very committed and helps at the animal shelter every week.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with feminine singular nouns (and sometimes after certain determiners).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schuhe sind zu enge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are too tight.

definitions.note: Form of the adjective „eng“ used before a noun (e.g., plural or with certain case endings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch die engen Straßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk through the narrow streets.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "eng".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Schuhe sind enger als meine alten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are tighter than my old ones.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like "enger Kontakt" (close contact).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir arbeiten jetzt enger zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We work together more closely now.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to the English language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann ein bisschen Englisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can speak a little English.

definitions.note: often used with a verb like „sprechen“ (to speak) or as an adjective before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche nicht so gut englisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t speak English that well.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese englische Bücher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read English books.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak declension (used after a determiner), e.g. "den englischen ..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne den englischen Wortschatz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning English vocabulary.

definitions.note: adjective in masculine nominative singular (e.g., before a masculine noun like „Tee“ or „Text“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist englischer Tee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is English tea.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun in the nominative or accusative singular (e.g., „ein englisches Buch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese ein englisches Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm reading an English book.

definitions.native: to do without, to go without
definitions.note: Somewhat formal; often used in the sense of not needing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das entbehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can do without that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden morgen entdecken, wie das Gerät funktioniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will discover how the device works.

definitions.note: present tense (er/sie/es) or imperative (ihr); also used as a past participle meaning “discovered,” depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entdeckt einen Fehler in der Rechnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He discovers a mistake in the bill.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „entdecken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie entdeckte einen Fehler im Bericht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She discovered a mistake in the report.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural or formal “you” (Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie entdeckten einen Fehler in der Rechnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They discovered a mistake in the bill.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entehrt seine Familie mit dieser Tat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dishonors his family with this act.

definitions.note: Past participle/adjectival use.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fühlte sich entehrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She felt dishonored.

definitions.note: Used literally for starting a fire and figuratively for starting emotions, debates, conflicts, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Funke kann ein Feuer entfachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A spark can ignite a fire.

definitions.note: Often figurative: to set off or intensify anger, unrest, debate, or conflict.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Worte können einen Streit entfachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His words can spark a quarrel.

definitions.note: Frequently used with abstract nouns like Hass, Begeisterung, Diskussion, Konflikt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Artikel kann eine hitzige Diskussion entfachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The article can spark a heated debate.

definitions.native: to be omitted, to be dropped
definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts to say something is no longer necessary or is left out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der letzte Punkt kann entfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The last item can be omitted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Karte bitte entfalten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you unfold the map, please?

definitions.note: Often used in a more abstract sense (e.g., talents, potential, a situation) to mean something gradually becomes visible or grows.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie konnte ihr Talent in der neuen Firma richtig entfalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was able to really develop her talent in the new company.

definitions.note: Often used as “ich entferne …” (“I remove …”); can also be used as an imperative (“remove!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich entferne den Fleck aus dem T-Shirt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remove the stain from the T-shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte entfernen Sie den Fleck aus dem Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remove the stain from the shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Möbel von der Wand entfernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to move the furniture away from the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entfernt den Fleck aus dem Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He removes the stain from the shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärztin hat den Zahn entfernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor removed the tooth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Dorf ist weit entfernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village is far away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bahnhof ist nur zehn Minuten entfernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train station is only ten minutes away.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „entfernen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entfernte den Fleck aus dem Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He removed the stain from the shirt.

definitions.note: Often used for escaping from a place or situation (sometimes more formal/literary than "fliehen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gefangene konnte aus dem Gefängnis entfliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was able to escape from the prison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wollte das Kind entführen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man wanted to kidnap the child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann entführt das Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man kidnaps the child.

definitions.note: past participle of „entgehen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist entgangen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb ist der Polizei entgangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief escaped the police.

definitions.note: often used with a dative pronoun (e.g. „ist mir entgangen“ = I missed it / it slipped my notice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mir völlig entgangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completely missed that.

definitions.note: Often used after a noun or pronoun (postposition), especially with dative: "mir entgegen" = "toward me".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt mir entgegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is coming toward me.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like "entgegen dem Rat" (= contrary to the advice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entgegen dem Rat ihres Arztes arbeitet sie weiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Contrary to her doctor's advice, she keeps working.

definitions.note: Often used with dative (e.g., jemandem/etwas entgegen) and frequently as a separable verb prefix (e.g., entgegenkommen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ging ihr entgegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walked toward her.

definitions.note: Often used with dative (e.g., entgegen der Regeln = contrary to the rules).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist entgegen den Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is contrary to the rules.

definitions.note: Often used with abstract nouns like Respekt (respect), Verständnis (understanding), Vertrauen (trust).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dir mehr Verständnis entgegenbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to show you more understanding.

definitions.note: Often used with dative + "entgehen": jemandem entgehen = to escape someone / to evade someone (e.g., punishment, attention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb konnte der Polizei entgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was able to evade the police.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (e.g. "Mir entgeht etwas" = "Something escapes me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir entgeht ein wichtiges Detail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An important detail escapes me.

definitions.note: simple past of „entgehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb entging der Polizei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief escaped the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Preis sind Getränke enthalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Drinks are included in the price.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: etwas enthalten.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Liste kann alle Namen enthalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This list can contain all the names.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „enthalten“ (to contain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Liste enthielt drei Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The list contained three names.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „enthalten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Produkt enthält Zucker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product contains sugar.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „enthüllen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Journalist enthüllte die Wahrheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist revealed the truth.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "entkommen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gefangene entkam in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner escaped during the night.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative (e.g., einer Sache/jemandem entkommen = escape from something/someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb konnte der Polizei entkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was able to escape from the police.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „entkommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb entkommt durch die Hintertür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief escapes through the back door.

definitions.note: Used for taking goods off a vehicle (unload) or for releasing electricity (discharge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den LKW entladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to unload the truck.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative after the noun (e.g., „den Fluss entlang“) or placed before the noun with the genitive (more formal, e.g., „entlang des Flusses“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen den Fluss entlang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking along the river.

definitions.note: Often used with a noun phrase (e.g., „den Fluss entlang“ = along the river).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen die Straße entlang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking along the street.

definitions.note: simple past of „entlanggehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entlangging den Fluss bis zur Brücke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went along the river up to the bridge.

definitions.note: Usually used for being fired from a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma hat ihn letzte Woche entlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fired him last week.

definitions.note: Used for letting someone go (e.g., from prison or from the hospital).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt hat sie heute aus dem Krankenhaus entlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor discharged her from the hospital today.

definitions.note: Often used for emptying containers (e.g., bins, bottles, pockets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte entleeren Sie den Mülleimer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please empty the trash can.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der schlechten Nachricht war sie völlig entmutigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bad news, she was completely discouraged.

definitions.note: Depending on context, this form can mean “I decide” (present tense) or be used as the informal singular imperative “decide!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich entscheide heute, was wir essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decide today what we’re going to eat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht entscheiden, welches Buch ich kaufen soll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't decide which book I should buy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist entscheidend für unseren Erfolg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is decisive for our success.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective before a noun (inflected form of „entscheidend“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die entscheidende Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the decisive question.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du), present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du entscheidest heute, was wir essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You decide today what we eat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entscheidet heute, ob er mitkommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decides today whether he’s coming along.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "entscheiden"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entschied sich für das blaue Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided on the blue shirt.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „entscheiden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entschied sich für das blaue Hemd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided on the blue shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich für den Zug entschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to take the train.

definitions.note: past participle of „entscheiden“; often used with „haben“ (Perfekt)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich entschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided.

definitions.note: past participle of „entscheiden“, often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich für das blaue Hemd entschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided on the blue shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr entschieden und gibt nicht so schnell auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very determined and doesn’t give up so quickly.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „entschließen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich entschloss mich, heute früher nach Hause zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to go home earlier today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist entschlossen, Deutsch zu lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is determined to learn German.

definitions.note: Past participle of the reflexive verb „sich entschließen“ (usually used with „sich“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich entschlossen, heute früher nach Hause zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to go home earlier today.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive verb “sich entschließen” (to decide / make up one’s mind).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich entschlossen, Deutsch zu lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to learn German.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist entschlossen, Deutsch zu lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is determined to learn German.

definitions.note: informal (du) form; often used as a quick apology or to get someone’s attention
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldige, kannst du mir bitte sagen, wie spät es ist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, can you please tell me what time it is?

definitions.note: Common as an informal (du) way to apologize or get someone’s attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldige, ich bin zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I'm too late.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich entschuldigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich entschuldigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to apologize.

definitions.note: Often used to politely ask to be excused or to forgive a mistake.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können Sie mich bitte entschuldigen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you please excuse me?

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich entschuldigen = to apologize.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mich entschuldigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to apologize.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: jemanden entschuldigen = to excuse someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können Sie mich bitte entschuldigen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you please excuse me?

definitions.note: Informal (du) form: “you apologize”. Often used with “dich” (sich entschuldigen) = “to apologize”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum entschuldigst du dich nicht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you apologize?

definitions.note: Informal (du) form; 2nd person singular present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum entschuldigst du dich nicht bei ihr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you apologize to her?

definitions.note: Often used as a polite plural/informal imperative to address more than one person ("you all").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigt bitte die Verspätung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry about the delay.

definitions.note: Used with "sich" ("sich entschuldigen" = to apologize).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entschuldigt sich sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He apologizes right away.

definitions.note: Used when speaking to more than one person (informal “you all”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigt bitte die Störung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry to disturb you (all).

definitions.note: Used to apologize or to politely get someone's attention (e.g., in public or when interrupting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigung, können Sie mir helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, can you help me?

definitions.note: Used literally for defusing a bomb, and figuratively for defusing tension or a conflict.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei muss die Bombe entschärfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have to defuse the bomb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unfall war entsetzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident was horrible.

definitions.note: Used to intensify an adjective or adverb; expresses something very negative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war entsetzlich laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was terribly loud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin entsetzt über das, was passiert ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m shocked about what happened.

definitions.note: Often used for getting rid of trash or waste properly (e.g., recycling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du den Müll bitte entsorgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please dispose of the trash?

definitions.note: Often used for throwing something away properly (e.g., recycling, trash disposal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den alten Computer entsorgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I disposed of the old computer.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I relax") or imperative ("relax!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Arbeit entspanne ich auf dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I relax on the sofa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mich am Wochenende entspannen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to relax on the weekend.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: sich entspannen (to relax).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entspannt sich nach der Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He relaxes after work.

definitions.note: Past participle of entspannen; commonly used with haben in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich schnell entspannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He relaxed quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Urlaub bin ich ganz entspannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the vacation, I’m completely relaxed.

definitions.note: simple past form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Arbeit entspannte ich auf dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I relaxed on the sofa.

definitions.note: Often used for devices, accounts, or blocked access (e.g., phone, screen, SIM card).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du dein Handy entsperren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you unlock your phone?

definitions.note: Used when access is blocked or restricted (e.g., a card, an account, or a road).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bank kann deine Karte entsperren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank can unblock your card.

definitions.note: Used with the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entsprechend den Regeln ist das nicht erlaubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the rules, that is not allowed.

definitions.note: Often used to refer back to something mentioned before: “entsprechend” = “in line with that / as a result.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat den ganzen Tag geregnet, und entsprechend sind die Straßen nass.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained all day, and accordingly the streets are wet.

definitions.note: Often used with a noun to mean “the matching/appropriate one” (e.g., the corresponding form, document, number).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte füllen Sie das entsprechende Formular aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fill out the corresponding form.

definitions.note: Often used with "entsprechen + dative" (e.g., "Das entspricht dem Plan.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das entspricht nicht meinen Erwartungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That doesn't match my expectations.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative noun/pronoun to mean “to have its origin in / to stem from.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Probleme können Missverständnissen entspringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many problems can arise from misunderstandings.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "entstehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Laufe der Zeit entstand ein neues Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over time, a new problem arose.

definitions.note: past participle of "entstehen"; commonly used with "sein" (e.g., "ist entstanden")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Problem ist gestern entstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem arose yesterday.

definitions.native: to arise, to come into being
definitions.note: Used for something beginning to exist or developing (an idea, a problem, a situation, a work of art).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie kann eine neue Idee entstehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How can a new idea arise?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich nicht enttäuschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to disappoint you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich enttäuschend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really disappointing.

definitions.note: past participle of „enttäuschen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin wirklich enttäuscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really disappointed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin enttäuscht, weil du nicht gekommen bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m disappointed because you didn’t come.

definitions.note: Often used with "oder" (either...or).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entweder gehen wir zu Fuß, oder wir nehmen den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Either we go on foot, or we take the bus.

definitions.note: Usually used with "oder" (entweder ... oder ...) to present two alternatives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entweder bleibst du zu Hause, oder du kommst mit uns.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Either you stay at home, or you come with us.

definitions.note: Often used for creating an initial plan or drawing (e.g., a building, a logo, a text draft).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie entwerfen ein neues Logo für die Firma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are designing a new logo for the company.

definitions.note: Used for developing products/ideas/plans, and also for something (a situation, ability, person) developing over time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma kann eine neue App entwickeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company can develop a new app.

definitions.note: Often used when you come up with a concept, method, or strategy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen eine neue Strategie entwickeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to devise a new strategy.

definitions.note: More literal meaning: to unfold something that is rolled up or wrapped.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will die Karte entwickeln, um den Weg zu sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to unfold the map to see the way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma entwickelt eine neue App.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company develops a new app.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., with "sein" or "haben") or like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Produkt ist gut entwickelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The product is well developed.

definitions.note: simple past form of „entwickeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er entwickelte eine neue App.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He developed a new app.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), used with plural subjects (e.g., wir/sie) or formal Sie
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie entwickelten eine neue App.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They developed a new app.

definitions.native: to slip away, to sneak off
definitions.note: Often used when someone leaves quietly or quickly without being noticed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schnell entwischen, bevor jemand ihn gesehen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slipped away quickly before anyone saw him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze entwischt durch die offene Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat escapes through the open door.

definitions.note: Often used when someone or an animal gets away quietly or quickly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze ist entwischt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat has escaped.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Architektin hat ein neues Haus entworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The architect designed a new house.

definitions.native: to take away, remove; to withdraw
definitions.note: Often used with a direct object + dative person/thing: jemandem etwas entziehen (e.g., a license, money, trust).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Staat kann ihm den Führerschein entziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The state can take away his driver's license.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du diese Handschrift entziffern?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you decipher this handwriting?

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts, especially for rights/permissions (e.g., a driver’s license) being taken away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihm wurde der Führerschein entzogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His driver’s license was taken away.

definitions.note: Often used in a somewhat formal or old-fashioned way (similar to “charming”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein entzückendes kleines Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a delightful little café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war entzückt über das Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was delighted with the gift.

definitions.note: Often used transitively: etwas entzünden = to ignite something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Funke kann trockenes Gras schnell entzünden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A spark can quickly ignite dry grass.

definitions.note: Used for a male person; can also refer to a masculine noun (often translated as “it” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne Paul, und er ist sehr nett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know Paul, and he is very nice.

definitions.note: Rather formal; often used with "für" + accusative (e.g. etwas für wichtig erachten).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erachte diese Entscheidung für richtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I consider this decision to be right.

definitions.note: past participle of „erbauen“, often used in passive constructions (e.g. „wurde erbaut“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schloss wurde 1880 erbaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle was built in 1880.

definitions.note: often used in formal/written notices (e.g., “wird erbeten” = “is requested”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rückmeldung wird bis Freitag erbeten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Feedback is requested by Friday.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal; often used with a direct object (something) and the person asked in the dative (jemandem etwas erbitten).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hiermit erbitte ich Ihre Unterstützung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hereby request your support.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "erblassen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als er die Nachricht hörte, erblasste er sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he heard the news, he turned pale immediately.

definitions.note: Often used in a more formal/literary way than plain „sieht“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erblickt plötzlich einen Fuchs im Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suddenly catches sight of a fox in the forest.

definitions.note: More formal/literary than "sah".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als sie um die Ecke bog, erblickte sie das Meer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When she turned the corner, she caught sight of the sea.

definitions.note: Used for someone losing their sight (often in the past tense in narratives).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall erblindete er auf einem Auge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he went blind in one eye.

definitions.note: Formal/old-fashioned; often used as „sich erbieten“ = to offer to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erbot sich, uns zu helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He offered to help us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat nach dem Essen erbrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He vomited after eating.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „erben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erbte das Haus von ihrer Großmutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She inherited the house from her grandmother.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong negative judgment (about a person, behavior, or situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Verhalten war wirklich erbärmlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior was really pathetic.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „alles Erdenkliche“ (= everything imaginable).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat alles Erdenkliche versucht, um das Problem zu lösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tried everything imaginable to solve the problem.

definitions.note: Often used in passive or as a past participle adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wurde erdrosselt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was strangled.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively as „sich ereignen“ (impersonal: something happens).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas kann sich überall ereignen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something like that can happen anywhere.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich ereignen“ (something happens).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unfall ereignet sich am frühen Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident happens early in the morning.

definitions.note: Used with the reflexive form: sich ereignen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unfall ereignete sich gestern Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident happened yesterday evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr erfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very experienced.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte erfahren, was passiert ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to find out what happened.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „am eigenen Leib erfahren“ (= experience something firsthand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er musste am eigenen Leib erfahren, wie hart die Arbeit ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to experience firsthand how hard the work is.

definitions.note: comparative form of the adjective „erfahren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine erfahrenere Ärztin als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a more experienced doctor than I am.

definitions.note: weak ending (-er) before a masculine noun (e.g., „der erfahrene Mann“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein erfahrener Lehrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is an experienced teacher.

definitions.note: Simple past of „erfinden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erfand eine neue Maschine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He invented a new machine.

definitions.note: Often used for entering or collecting information (e.g., data) in a system.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das System erfasst alle Daten automatisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The system records all data automatically.

definitions.note: Used when someone quickly comprehends an idea or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erfasst sofort, worum es geht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She immediately understands what it's about.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „erfassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei erfasste alle Daten im System.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police recorded all the data in the system.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „erfassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erfasste sofort, was passiert war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She immediately understood what had happened.

definitions.native: to invent; to make up (a story, excuse, lie)
definitions.note: In the example, the infinitive is used to match the exact form "erfinden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will eine neue Geschichte erfinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to make up a new story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr erfinderisch und findet immer eine Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very inventive and always finds a solution.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suche nach dem Schlüssel war erfolglos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The search for the key was unsuccessful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist in ihrem Beruf sehr erfolgreich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very successful in her job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die Prüfung erfolgreich bestanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She passed the exam successfully.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „erfolgreich“, used before a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir suchen einen erfolgreichen Manager.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are looking for a successful manager.

definitions.note: comparative form of „erfolgreich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Team ist erfolgreicher als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This team is more successful than the other one.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/official language (e.g., announcements, instructions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lieferung erfolgt morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delivery takes place tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Für die Anmeldung ist ein Ausweis erforderlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An ID is required for registration.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das wird Zeit und Geduld erfordern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That will require time and patience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das erfordert viel Geduld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That requires a lot of patience.

definitions.note: Often used for exploring unknown areas/topics (e.g., space, the ocean, or a scientific question).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wissenschaftler erforschen die Ursachen des Klimawandels.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Scientists research the causes of climate change.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich (an etwas) erfreuen“ = to enjoy, to take pleasure in something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wird dich erfreuen, das zu hören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will please you to hear that.

definitions.note: Often used in polite/formal phrases like „Ich bin erfreut, …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erfreut, Sie kennenzulernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am pleased to meet you.

definitions.note: Often used in polite/formal phrases like „Sehr erfreut!“ (= ‘Pleased to meet you!’) or „Ich bin erfreut, dass …“ (= ‘I’m pleased that …’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erfreut, dass du heute Zeit hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m pleased that you have time today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wasser ist an heißen Tagen wirklich erfrischend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is really refreshing on hot days.

definitions.note: Often used for people/body parts that are very cold; can also imply freezing to death in other contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Hände sind erfroren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hands are frozen.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „erfahren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erfuhr erst später, dass sie umgezogen ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only found out later that she moved.

definitions.note: past participle of „erfinden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine Geschichte erfunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made up a story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Geschichte ist erfunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The story is made up.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form) of „erfahren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du erfährst die Wahrheit morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You find out the truth tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "erfahren"; also used for getting information/news (often with "von" or in "erfährt, dass …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erfährt, dass der Zug Verspätung hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finds out that the train is delayed.

definitions.note: Subjunctive II form of „erfahren“ (used for hypotheticals, wishes, or polite/indirect statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich die Wahrheit erführe, wäre ich sehr überrascht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I found out the truth, I would be very surprised.

definitions.note: Used for requirements, conditions, expectations, promises, wishes, duties.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann alle Voraussetzungen für den Job erfüllen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can meet all the requirements for the job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Wunsch hat sich erfüllt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My wish has come true.

definitions.note: often used with a preposition like „mit“ (filled with).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Raum ist mit Rauch erfüllt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is filled with smoke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Konzert fühlte sie sich erfüllt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, she felt fulfilled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erfüllte alle Bedingungen für das Stipendium.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He met all the requirements for the scholarship.

definitions.note: Simple past of "ergeben"; commonly used with "sich" as "sich ergeben" (= to result, to turn out), but here it can also mean "gave".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Rechnung ergab am Ende 42 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, the bill came to 42 euros.

definitions.note: Used mostly in formal/legal language, especially about decisions or rulings (e.g., a judgment) being issued.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Urteil ist gestern ergangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judgment was issued yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich ergeben“ = to surrender.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ergebe mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I surrender.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object: „jemandem ergeben sein“ = to be devoted/loyal to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ihr ergeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is devoted to her.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" as "sich ergeben" (to result, to turn out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Untersuchung kann neue Erkenntnisse ergeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The investigation can yield new insights.

definitions.note: Usually reflexive: "sich ergeben" = to surrender.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten mussten sich ergeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers had to surrender.

definitions.note: Used with numbers: "Das ergibt ..." = "That makes ..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zwei und drei ergeben fünf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two and three make five.

definitions.note: Often used with “zusammen”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr ergebt zusammen ein gutes Team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Together, you make a good team.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like „Das ergibt Sinn“ (“That makes sense”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du 2 und 2 addierst, ergibt das 4.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you add 2 and 2, that results in 4.

definitions.note: Often used with „sich“: „sich ergeben“ = to surrender.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ergibt sich der Polizei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He surrenders to the police.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts; also common in set phrases like „die Gelegenheit ergreifen“ (to seize the opportunity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde deine Hand ergreifen und dich zur Seite ziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will grab your hand and pull you aside.

definitions.note: Used for something that strongly affects you emotionally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war sehr ergreifend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very moving.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal/literary contexts (e.g., to seize an opportunity or to take hold of something firmly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ergreift meine Hand und zieht mich mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grabs my hand and pulls me along.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „ergreifen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ergriff meine Hand und zog mich weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seized my hand and pulled me away.

definitions.note: past participle of „ergreifen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat … ergriffen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Täter schnell ergriffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police quickly seized the perpetrator.

definitions.note: often used to describe being emotionally affected (e.g., „Ich war sehr ergriffen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war von ihrer Rede sehr ergriffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was very moved by her speech.

definitions.note: Often used for adding missing information or completing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Liste bitte ergänzen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you add to the list, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erhalte heute eine E-Mail von meiner Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I receive an email from my teacher today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit Sport und guter Ernährung erhalte ich meine Gesundheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With exercise and good nutrition, I maintain my health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute eine E-Mail von meiner Lehrerin erhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received an email from my teacher today.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of keeping something in good condition or preserving something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das alte Gebäude erhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to preserve the old building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erhebe mein Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I raise my glass.

definitions.note: Often used with nouns like „Gebühr“ (fee) or „Steuer“ (tax).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erhebe eine Gebühr für den Service.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I charge a fee for the service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte erheben Sie die Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please raise your hand.

definitions.note: Often used with things like Gebühren (fees) or Steuern (taxes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt will eine Gebühr erheben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city wants to charge a fee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erhebt die Hand und stellt eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She raises her hand and asks a question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel erhebt eine Gebühr für das Parken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel charges a fee for parking.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „erhalten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erhielt gestern eine E-Mail von meiner Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received an email from my teacher yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „erhalten“ (wir/ihr/sie/Sie).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erhielten gestern eine E-Mail von der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They received an email from the school yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „erheben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer erhob die Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher raised his hand.

definitions.note: past participle of "erheben"; often used with "haben/sein" or in the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die Hand erhoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He raised his hand.

definitions.note: used especially with Gebühren/Steuern in the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wurden keine Gebühren erhoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No fees were charged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit erhobenen Händen ging er aus dem Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With raised hands, he left the house.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (he/she/it hopes for)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erhofft eine schnelle Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hopes for a quick answer.

definitions.note: past participle (used with auxiliaries like „hat“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat einen Erfolg erhofft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hoped for success.

definitions.note: Most often used reflexively: „sich erholen“ (to recover / to rest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich nach der Arbeit erholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to rest after work.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: sich erholen = to recover / to rest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Arbeit erholt er sich ein bisschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, he rests a bit.

definitions.note: Past participle; often used with haben/sein and usually with sich (sich erholen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich nach der Krankheit schnell erholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He recovered quickly after the illness.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "erholen"; often used in written narratives. In everyday speech, German often prefers the perfect tense: "hat sich erholt."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Grippe erholte sie sich schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the flu, she recovered quickly.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „erhalten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erhält heute einen Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He receives a letter today.

definitions.note: often used with „sein“ + an optional place/source (e.g., online, im Laden).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Ticket ist online erhältlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket is available online.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as „sich erhängen“ = to hang oneself (suicide).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wollte sich nicht erhängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t want to hang himself.

definitions.note: Usually used for a person being executed (or hanging oneself). For hanging up objects, German typically uses „aufhängen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wurde am Marktplatz erhängt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was hanged in the marketplace.

definitions.note: Usually means to kill someone by hanging (a person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Henker erhängte den Verurteilten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The executioner hanged the convicted man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Preise erhöhen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to increase the prices.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis erhöht sich jedes Jahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price increases every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt hat die Steuern erhöht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city has raised the taxes.

definitions.note: Often used in a formal or religious context (e.g., prayers being answered).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Wunsch wurde erhört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My wish was granted.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I remember") or imperative singular ("remember!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erinnere mich an deinen Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remember your name.

definitions.note: Transitive use: „jemanden an etwas erinnern“ = to remind someone of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte erinnere mich morgen an den Termin—erinnern ist wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remind me about the appointment tomorrow—reminding is important.

definitions.note: Commonly used reflexively as „sich erinnern“; includes the verb „erinnern“ in the expression.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mich erinnern, und ich werde mich erinnern, wenn du mich daran erinnern kannst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to remember, and I will remember if you can remind me of it.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erinnerst du dich an unseren Ausflug?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you remember our trip?

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich erinnern (an)“ = to remember (something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erinnert sich an den Termin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He remembers the appointment.

definitions.note: Often used with an object: „jemanden an etwas erinnern“ = to remind someone of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erinnert mich an die Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reminds me of the rules.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive form: „sich an etwas erinnern“ = to remember something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erinnerte mich an deinen Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remembered your birthday.

definitions.note: Used with a direct object: „jemanden an etwas erinnern“ = to remind someone of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erinnerte mich an den Termin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reminded me about the appointment.

definitions.note: past participle of „erkennen“; often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn sofort erkannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recognized him right away.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "erkennen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erkannte ihn sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recognized him immediately.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form; often used in writing or formal speech
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erkannten den Fehler sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They recognized the mistake immediately.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present: “I recognize / I realize”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erkenne dich sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recognize you immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich auf dem Foto erkennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can recognize you in the photo.

definitions.note: Often used when you come to understand something after noticing it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann erkennen, dass ich einen Fehler gemacht habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can see/realize that I made a mistake.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „erkennen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erkennt ihn sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She recognizes him immediately.

definitions.note: Often used for climbing something difficult (like a mountain or peak); can sound a bit literary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben den Gipfel erklommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We climbed the summit.

definitions.note: imperative (informal singular): used when telling one person “you” to explain something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erklär mir bitte, wie das funktioniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please explain to me how that works.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense ("I explain") or imperative ("explain!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erkläre dir die Regel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I explain the rule to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir das bitte erklären?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please explain that to me?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du), present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum erklärst du mir nicht, warum du so spät bist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you explain to me why you’re so late?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin erklärt die Aufgabe noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the task one more time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „erklären“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer erklärte die Grammatik noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explained the grammar once again.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form; used with wir/sie/Sie
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erklärten den Plan Schritt für Schritt.
