definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They explained the plan step by step.

definitions.native: to inquire, to ask for information
definitions.note: Usually used as "sich erkundigen" (to inquire).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mich bei der Rezeption erkundigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will inquire at the reception.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich erkundigen (nach …)“ = to ask/inquire (about …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erkundigt sich nach dem Weg zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asks about the way to the train station.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich erkundigen (nach …)“ = to ask/inquire (about …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich nach den Öffnungszeiten erkundigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I inquired about the opening hours.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich erkundigen (nach)“ = to inquire/ask about something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erkundigte mich nach dem Weg zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked for directions to the train station.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich erkälten (e.g., sich erkälten = to catch a cold).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich ohne Jacke rausginge, erkälte ich mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I went outside without a jacket, I would catch a cold.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich erkälten = to catch a cold.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich nicht erkälten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to catch a cold.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du), present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du ohne Jacke rausgehst, erkältest du dich schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you go outside without a jacket, you’ll catch a cold quickly.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“: „Ich bin erkältet.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erkältet und bleibe heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cold and I'm staying home today.

definitions.note: Used with „sein“: „Ich bin erkältet.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erkältet und bleibe heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a cold and I'm staying home today.

definitions.note: Simple past form of "erliegen"; often used with "einer Krankheit / Versuchung" (to succumb to an illness/temptation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach langer Krankheit erlag er schließlich seiner Krankheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a long illness, he finally succumbed to his illness.

definitions.note: More formal than "bekommen"; often used in official or academic contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie konnte endlich die Genehmigung erlangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was finally able to obtain the permit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erlangt endlich die nötige Erfahrung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finally attains the necessary experience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat den Titel erlangt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She obtained the title.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "erlangen"; often used in more formal contexts (e.g., rights, recognition, fame).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erlangte die deutsche Staatsbürgerschaft nach fünf Jahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She obtained German citizenship after five years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erlaube dir heute, länger aufzubleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m allowing you to stay up later today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Eltern erlauben mir, heute Abend länger aufzubleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents allow me to stay up later tonight.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erlaubst du mir eine Frage?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you allow me a question?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier ist Fotografieren nicht erlaubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Photography is not allowed here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier ist das Fotografieren erlaubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Photography is allowed here.

definitions.note: Often used as simple past (Präteritum) of „erlauben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer erlaubte uns, früher zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher allowed us to leave early.

definitions.note: First-person singular present ("I experience"); can also be used as a command ("experience!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erlebe jeden Tag etwas Neues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I experience something new every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte einmal den Sonnenaufgang in den Bergen erleben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to experience the sunrise in the mountains once.

definitions.note: Past participle of „erleben“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat erlebt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat in ihrem Leben viel erlebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has experienced a lot in her life.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I …") of "erledigen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erledige das gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll take care of that right away.

definitions.native: to take care of; to get done; to deal with (so it’s no longer an issue)
definitions.note: Common for completing tasks/errands or handling a matter so it’s settled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das heute noch erledigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take care of that today.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle or like an adjective (e.g. "Das ist erledigt.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das schon erledigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already taken care of that.

definitions.note: often means something has been taken care of (a task, paperwork, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aufgabe ist erledigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The task is done.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „erledigen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erledigte die Aufgabe schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He completed the task quickly.

definitions.note: Often used in hunting contexts (e.g., wild game).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Jäger wird morgen einen Hirsch erlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunter will kill a deer tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Jäger erlegt ein Reh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunter kills a deer.

definitions.note: Fairly formal; used with things like fees, taxes, or costs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erlegt die Gebühr sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pays the fee immediately.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like "etwas" (something): "etwas erleichtern" = to make something easier.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Werkzeug kann die Arbeit erleichtern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tool can make the work easier.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like relieving pain, worries, or stress: "Schmerzen/Sorgen erleichtern".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tabletten können die Schmerzen erleichtern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tablets can relieve the pain.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to describe how someone feels after a worry is gone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erleichtert, dass alles gut gegangen ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m relieved that everything turned out well.

definitions.note: Often used for learning something thoroughly, especially a skill or craft.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will einen Beruf erlernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to learn a profession.

definitions.note: Often used for skills or abilities that are learned through practice or training.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat den Beruf in einer Ausbildung erlernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She learned the profession in a training program.

definitions.note: Often used for people (spiritually/intellectually enlightened).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie gilt als sehr erleuchtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is considered very enlightened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Raum ist hell erleuchtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is brightly lit.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „erleiden“ (to suffer, to undergo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erlitt bei dem Unfall schwere Verletzungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suffered severe injuries in the accident.

definitions.note: past participle of „erleiden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat bei dem Unfall schwere Verletzungen erlitten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suffered serious injuries in the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können Sie das bitte noch einmal erläutern?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you please explain that again?

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „erläutern“; often used in writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer erläuterte die Aufgabe noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explained the task once again.

definitions.note: Often used in a religious or dramatic sense (e.g., to redeem or deliver someone from sin, suffering, or a curse).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erlöse dich von diesem Versprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I free you from this promise.

definitions.note: Often used in a religious sense (“redeem”) or for ending someone’s suffering.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt konnte den Patienten von seinen Schmerzen erlösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor was able to free the patient from his pain.

definitions.note: Used with amounts, especially for the money you get from selling something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen für das alte Fahrrad noch 50 Euro erlösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still want to get 50 euros for the old bicycle.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts for a serious reminder or warning about behavior or rules.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer ermahnte die Schüler, leise zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher admonished the students to be quiet.

definitions.native: to investigate; to ascertain/determine (officially, by inquiry)
definitions.note: Used especially in official/police contexts (to investigate) and in formal contexts for finding out facts, figures, or results (to determine/ascertain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei muss die Ursache des Brandes ermitteln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police must investigate the cause of the fire.

definitions.note: Stronger and more specific than just „töten“ (to kill); implies an intentional killing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand wollte den Journalisten ermorden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone wanted to murder the journalist.

definitions.note: Used for intentional killing (murder); often in passive contexts like “was murdered.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Journalist wurde in der Nacht ermordet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was murdered during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Täter ermordete das Opfer in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrator murdered the victim at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ermunterte ihn, weiterzumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She encouraged him to keep going.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer will die Schüler ermutigen, mehr zu sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher wants to encourage the students to speak more.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „ermutigen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ermutigte ihn, weiterzumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She encouraged him to keep going.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das neue Gesetz soll es den Menschen ermöglichen, schneller Hilfe zu bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new law is supposed to enable people to get help faster.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neue Software ermöglicht schnellere Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new software enables faster work.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of „ernennen“, often in passive constructions (e.g. „zu … ernannt“ = appointed as …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wurde zur Teamleiterin ernannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was appointed as team leader.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ernannten ihn zum Vorsitzenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They appointed him as chairperson.

definitions.note: Often used for renewing documents, subscriptions, or contracts; for buildings/things it can mean renovate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meinen Pass erneuern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to renew my passport.

definitions.note: often used in a more formal or written style than "wieder"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Antrag erneut ausfüllen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to fill out the application again.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of „erniedrigen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erniedrigt seinen Bruder vor der Klasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He humiliates his brother in front of the class.

definitions.note: past participle of „erniedrigen“ (often used like an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Gespräch war sie völlig erniedrigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the conversation, she was completely humiliated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine ernste Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a serious question.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „im Ernst?“ (seriously?) or „im Ernst“ (seriously, for real).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meinst du das ernst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you mean that seriously?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine ernste Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a serious question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sprach mit einem ernsten Ton.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke in a serious tone.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „ernst“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lage wird ernster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is getting more serious.

definitions.note: Can also be an inflected form of „ernst“ (e.g. „ein ernster Mann“, „ein ernster Fehler“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein ernster Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a serious mistake.

definitions.note: comparative form of the adverb "ernst"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst ernster darüber nachdenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to think about it more seriously.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meinst du das ernsthaft?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you mean that seriously?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine ernsthafte Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a serious question.

definitions.note: comparative form of „ernsthaft“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist heute viel ernsthafter als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is much more serious today than yesterday.

definitions.note: Used mainly for crops or fruit; can also be used figuratively (e.g., to reap benefits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Herbst ernten die Bauern die Kartoffeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn the farmers harvest the potatoes.

definitions.note: third-person singular present tense of „ernten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erntet im Herbst die Äpfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He harvests the apples in autumn.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive pronoun: „sich ernähren“ = to eat (a certain way), to live on (a certain food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit diesem Job kann ich meine Familie ernähren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With this job I can feed my family.

definitions.note: Often used for taking control of a place or territory (sometimes also used figuratively, e.g., "a heart").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Armee will die Stadt erobern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army wants to capture the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Armee erobert die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army conquers the city.

definitions.note: Usually used with "auf" + accusative (e.g. "auf etwas erpicht sein").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist auf Anerkennung erpicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is eager for recognition.

definitions.note: Common patterns: jemanden erpressen; etwas erpressen; jemanden mit etwas erpressen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will mich erpressen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to blackmail me.

definitions.native: to force (something) through threats; to coerce
definitions.note: Also used more generally for forcing a result through pressure or threats (often with an object like ein Geständnis/ein Geldbetrag).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie versuchten, ein Geständnis zu erpressen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to coerce a confession.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erpresst seinen Chef mit Fotos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He blackmails his boss with photos.

definitions.note: Often used for correctly guessing (e.g., an answer, a number, a word).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du erraten, wie alt sie ist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you guess how old she is?

definitions.note: Often used with abstract things like attention, interest, suspicion, or feelings (e.g., „Aufsehen erregen“ = attract attention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Verhalten konnte großes Misstrauen erregen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior could arouse great suspicion.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „Aufmerksamkeit erregen“ = “to attract attention.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Video erregt viel Aufmerksamkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The video attracts a lot of attention.

definitions.note: Can also mean “sexually aroused” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war nach der Nachricht ganz erregt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was very excited after the news.

definitions.note: Often used for being available by phone/email (e.g., erreichbar sein).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute den ganzen Tag telefonisch erreichbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can be reached by phone all day today.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erreiche den Bahnhof in zehn Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reach the train station in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen unser Ziel erreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to reach our goal.

definitions.note: Usually means getting to a place/level (reach) or accomplishing a goal (achieve).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug erreicht um 18 Uhr Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train reaches Berlin at 6 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erreichte das Ziel nach drei Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reached the goal after three hours.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „erreichen“ (used with we/they/you plural/formal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erreichten das Ziel vor Sonnenuntergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They reached the goal before sunset.

definitions.note: Often used for constructing buildings/structures or establishing something officially (e.g., an institution).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt will eine neue Schule errichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city wants to build a new school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt errichtet eine neue Brücke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is building a new bridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie begann zu erröten vor Scham.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She began to blush with shame.

definitions.note: Often used for blushing from embarrassment or emotion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie errötet, als er sie lobt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She blushes when he praises her.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "erröten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als er das Kompliment hörte, errötete er sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he heard the compliment, he blushed right away.

definitions.note: Often used for creating something new in a deliberate or elevated sense (e.g., art, worlds, humanity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Künstler hat ein neues Werk erschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The artist created a new work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich konnte man einen Mann vor der Tür erscheinen sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly you could see a man appear in front of the door.

definitions.native: to be published, to come out
definitions.note: Used for books, newspapers, albums, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch soll nächstes Jahr erscheinen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is supposed to be published next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erscheint heute zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shows up too late today.

definitions.note: Used for books, newspapers, magazines, films, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Roman erscheint im März.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new novel is published in March.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "erscheinen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich erschien ein Mann an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly a man appeared at the door.

definitions.note: past participle of erscheinen; used with sein in the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern nicht zur Arbeit erschienen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t show up at work yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of erscheinen; often used for books, newspapers, articles, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch ist letztes Jahr erschienen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was published last year.

definitions.note: Usually used as an informal command (du-imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erschieß ihn nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t shoot him!

definitions.note: very strong/violent; used for killing with a gun, often in contexts like executions or hunting
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du näher kommst, erschieße ich dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you come closer, I'll shoot you dead.

definitions.note: Usually means killing someone by shooting (not just firing a gun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Soldat wollte den Gefangenen erschießen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldier wanted to shoot the prisoner dead.

definitions.note: Used for killing someone by shooting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist erschießt den Angreifer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer shoots the attacker dead.

definitions.native: to beat to death, to kill
definitions.note: Usually means killing someone by hitting them.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wollte den Mann nicht erschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t want to beat the man to death.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of „erschlagen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Räuber erschlug den Mann mit einem Stock.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The robber beat the man to death with a stick.

definitions.note: Usually implies that someone was killed by shooting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist erschoss den Täter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer shot the perpetrator dead.

definitions.note: past participle of „erschießen“ (to shoot dead)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wurde erschossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was shot dead.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „erschrecken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erschrak, als das Telefon plötzlich klingelte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got startled when the phone suddenly rang.

definitions.native: to get scared; to be startled
definitions.note: Commonly used reflexively: „sich erschrecken“ = to get scared/startled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erschrecke jedes Mal, wenn das Telefon plötzlich klingelt, und es ist wirklich erschrecken für mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get startled every time the phone suddenly rings, and it really is frightening for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich erschreckend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really frightening.

definitions.note: Used when someone/something causes another person/animal to be scared.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund erschreckt die Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog scares the cat.

definitions.note: Simple past form often used in the meaning “to frighten (someone)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund erschreckte das Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog frightened the child.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (past participle) with „sein“: „Ich bin erschrocken.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erschrocken, als ich den lauten Knall gehört habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got scared when I heard the loud bang.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective meaning someone is suddenly scared or surprised.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war erschrocken, als es plötzlich laut geknallt hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was startled when there was suddenly a loud bang.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „erschaffen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Künstler erschuf ein neues Gemälde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The artist created a new painting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der langen Wanderung war ich völlig erschöpft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long hike, I was completely exhausted.

definitions.note: Often used to describe an emotional reaction to bad news or a disturbing event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war erschüttert, als ich die Nachricht hörte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was shocked when I heard the news.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (what is being replaced) and sometimes with „durch“ + accusative (what it’s replaced with).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ersetze den Zucker durch Honig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I replace the sugar with honey.

definitions.note: Often used with the accusative for what is replaced and with „durch“ for what it is replaced with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die alte Batterie durch eine neue ersetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to replace the old battery with a new one.

definitions.note: Often used with an object in the accusative (e.g., etwas) and sometimes with „durch“ + accusative (by/with).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Chef ersetzt den alten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new boss replaces the old one.

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the dative + a thing in the accusative (jdm etw ersparen) or reflexively (sich etw ersparen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dir die Details ersparen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to spare you the details.

definitions.note: Present tense (er/sie/es).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erspart jeden Monat 50 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He saves 50 euros every month.

definitions.note: Past participle (used with haben).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat genug Geld erspart.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has saved up enough money.

definitions.note: Often used with time expressions to mean something happens later than expected or not until a certain time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme erst morgen zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm only coming back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to mark the first step in a sequence (often with „dann“ later).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erst essen wir, dann gehen wir los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First we eat, then we set off.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/old-fashioned; often used for getting something (often at a good price).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Fahrrad günstig erstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought the bicycle for a good price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma wird mir die Kosten erstatten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company will reimburse (refund) my costs.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „Anzeige erstatten“ (to file a police report/complaint).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte eine Anzeige erstatten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to file a police report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wirklich erstaunlich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is really astonishing!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erstaunlich schnell hat sie die Aufgabe gelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Surprisingly quickly, she solved the task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erstaunt über die Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am amazed by the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war erstaunt, wie schnell er die Aufgabe gelöst hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was astonished at how quickly he solved the task.

definitions.note: Used as a noun meaning “the first one/person.” Often appears in phrases like „als Erste“ (“as the first [one]”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin als Erste angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived first.

definitions.note: ordinal adjective form (e.g., feminine or with certain endings)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist meine erste Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my first apartment.

definitions.note: Simple present, 3rd person singular of „erstellen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Software erstellt jeden Morgen einen Bericht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The software creates a report every morning.

definitions.note: Past participle of „erstellen“ (often used with „haben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein neues Konto erstellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I created a new account.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „erstellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erstellte eine Liste für den Einkauf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He created a list for the shopping.

definitions.note: colloquial spelling of „(das) erste Mal“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute erstemal in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm in Berlin for the first time today.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the ordinal number/adjective meaning “first” (used with nouns, e.g. in “am ersten Tag”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am ersten Tag war ich sehr nervös.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the first day I was very nervous.

definitions.note: Colloquial spelling; in standard German you usually write it as "zum ersten Mal" (two words).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erstenmal in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in Berlin for the first time.

definitions.note: Used to introduce the first point in a list or argument; often followed by „zweitens“ (secondly), „drittens“ (thirdly), etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erstens müssen wir einen Termin finden, und zweitens brauchen wir ein Budget.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First, we need to find a date, and second, we need a budget.

definitions.note: Ordinal form used before a noun (e.g., “mein erster Tag”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mein erster Tag in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my first day in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective ending (e.g., before a neuter noun: „erstes Mal“ = „first time“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mein erstes Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my first car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rauch war so dicht, dass er fast ersticken musste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke was so thick that he almost had to suffocate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rauch ist so dicht, dass man fast erstickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke is so thick that you almost choke.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „ersticken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann erstickte im Rauch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man suffocated in the smoke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel ist erstklassig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is first-class.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often used to mean “let’s do this first / for now”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke erstmal einen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For now, I’ll have a coffee.

definitions.note: Past participle of „erstechen“; often used with „werden/sein“ in passive or perfect constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde im Park erstochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was stabbed to death in the park.

definitions.note: Formal/polite; often used in official letters or legal language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Anwalt ersuchte das Gericht um eine Fristverlängerung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer requested an extension of the deadline from the court.

definitions.note: Often used when someone is caught doing something wrong or secret.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde beim Schummeln ertappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was caught cheating.

definitions.note: Formal/official verb used for permissions, orders, instructions, information, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Behörde kann eine Genehmigung erteilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authority can grant a permit.

definitions.native: to give (e.g., instructions, an order, information)
definitions.note: Common collocations: Anweisungen erteilen, einen Auftrag erteilen, Auskunft erteilen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wird klare Anweisungen erteilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will give clear instructions.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., issuing a permit or granting permission).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Behörde erteilt eine Genehmigung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The authority issues a permit.

definitions.note: Often used with negatives like "Ich ertrage das nicht" (I can't stand that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ertrage den Lärm nicht mehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand the noise anymore.

definitions.note: Often used for tolerating something difficult (pain, stress, an unpleasant situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Lärm nicht mehr ertragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't bear the noise anymore.

definitions.note: simple past of „ertrinken“ (to drown, intransitive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann ertrank im Fluss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man drowned in the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ertrinken kann man auch in flachem Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can drown even in shallow water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Hilfe ertrinkt er im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without help, he drowns in the lake.

definitions.note: past participle of „ertrinken“; used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann ist im Fluss ertrunken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man drowned in the river.

definitions.note: Often used in a more formal or literary way than aufwachen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erwache jeden Morgen um sechs Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up every morning at six o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin erwachsen und entscheide das selbst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m an adult and I decide that myself.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (e.g., „erwachsene Menschen“). Capitalized „Erwachsene“ is the noun meaning “adults.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nur erwachsene Personen dürfen Alkohol kaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Only adult people are allowed to buy alcohol.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein erwachsener Mensch muss Verantwortung übernehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An adult has to take responsibility.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erwacht jeden Morgen um sechs Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wakes up every morning at six o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used with “sein” in the perfect tense (e.g., „ist erwacht“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist plötzlich erwacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suddenly woke up.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „erwachen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erwachte mitten in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She woke up in the middle of the night.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I expect").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erwarte heute einen wichtigen Anruf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I expect an important call today.

definitions.note: Used for expecting something to happen or someone/something to arrive; also for what is demanded/required in a role or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erwarte heute einen Anruf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I expect a call today.

definitions.note: Slightly more formal; often used when you think something is likely to occur.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir erwarten morgen starken Regen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We anticipate heavy rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Emphasizes waiting for something (often news, results, a person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erwarten gespannt die Ergebnisse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are eagerly awaiting the results.

definitions.note: Refers to what you consider reasonable to demand from someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erwarte von dir, dass du pünktlich bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I expect you to be on time.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form of "erwarten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was erwartest du von dem Kurs?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you expect from the course?

definitions.note: Can be the 3rd person singular present form of „erwarten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erwartet heute Besuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He expects visitors today.

definitions.note: Can be the past participle of „erwarten“, often used with „haben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich schon erwartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already expected you.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „erwarten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erwartete dich um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I expected you at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form used with wir/sie/Sie.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir erwarteten dich um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We expected you at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (someone/something that is awakened); can also be used figuratively (e.g., to arouse interest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das laute Geräusch erweckt mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loud noise wakes me up.

definitions.note: Often used in somewhat formal contexts; also appears in set phrases meaning to show (e.g., „jemandem die Ehre erweisen“ = to do someone the honor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er konnte seine Unschuld erweisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was able to prove his innocence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Vertrag erweitern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to expand the contract.

definitions.note: often used for “expanded/extended” in the sense of making something bigger or adding more content/features
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma erweitert ihr Angebot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is expanding its range of products/services.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., acquiring property, rights, or skills).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie möchte ein Haus erwerben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She would like to purchase a house.

definitions.note: Often used for replying to what someone just said (a rather formal word).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erwidert ruhig: „Ich sehe das anders.“
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He replies calmly: “I see that differently.”

definitions.note: Past participle form, used with auxiliaries like „hat“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sofort erwidert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He replied immediately.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal or written German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: „Ich komme gleich“, erwiderte er ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “I’ll be right there,” he replied calmly.

definitions.note: Past participle of "erweisen"; often used with "haben" (perfect tense) or in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seine Unschuld erwiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He proved his innocence.

definitions.note: Often used for catching someone doing something wrong or unexpectedly; also used for catching something like a bus/train.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erwische den Bus gerade noch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just barely catch the bus.

definitions.note: Commonly used for catching someone (often in the act) or managing to get/spot someone at a particular moment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei konnte den Dieb erwischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were able to catch the thief.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Dieb erwischt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police caught the thief.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „erwischen“; often means catching someone doing something or catching/grabbing someone unexpectedly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist erwischte den Dieb auf frischer Tat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer caught the thief in the act.

definitions.note: simple past of „erwägen“ (often used in more formal contexts, like „to weigh/consider an option“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erwog kurz, ob er das Angebot annehmen sollte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He briefly considered whether he should accept the offer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vorschlag ist erwägenswert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The proposal is worth considering.

definitions.note: first-person singular present subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I); also the (formal) singular imperative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erwähne das nur kurz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll just mention that briefly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte noch etwas Wichtiges erwähnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to mention something important as well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat meinen Namen im Gespräch erwähnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mentioned my name in the conversation.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „erwähnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erwähnte meinen Namen im Gespräch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mentioned my name in the conversation.

definitions.note: Often used for making something warmer (e.g., food, a room) or for warming yourself up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Suppe in der Mikrowelle erwärmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will warm up the soup in the microwave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Täter erwürgt sein Opfer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrator strangles his victim.

definitions.note: past participle, often used with "hat" or "wurde".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Opfer wurde erwürgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The victim was strangled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Maschine erzeugt Strom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The machine generates electricity.

definitions.note: often used about raising/bringing up children; can also mean educating in the sense of training someone’s behavior
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erziehe meine Kinder zu selbstständigen Menschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am raising my children to be independent people.

definitions.note: Used especially for raising children; can also mean to educate in the sense of shaping someone’s behavior and values.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie müssen ihre Kinder liebevoll erziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They must raise their children with love.

definitions.note: Commonly used with results like goals, successes, profits, or agreements (e.g., ein Ergebnis/einen Erfolg/einen Gewinn erzielen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Unternehmen will nächstes Jahr einen höheren Gewinn erzielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to achieve a higher profit next year.

definitions.note: often used for achieving a result, goal, or success
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erzielt gute Ergebnisse in Mathe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She achieves good results in math.

definitions.note: Past participle of „erziehen“; often used in the perfect tense or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist von seinen Großeltern erzogen worden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was raised by his grandparents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind sehr gut erzogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are very well-brought-up.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative: “Erzähl!” = “Tell (me)!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erzähl mir davon!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me about it!

definitions.note: imperative (informal singular) of „erzählen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Erzähl mir bitte die Geschichte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell me the story!

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present (ich). Also used for the imperative to one person (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erzähle dir eine Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m telling you a story.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I tell"); also used as the informal imperative ("tell!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erzähle dir später eine Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll tell you a story later.

definitions.note: Often used with someone as a dative object (e.g. jemandem etwas erzählen = to tell someone something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir eine Geschichte erzählen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you tell me a story?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum erzählst du mir nicht die ganze Geschichte?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you tell me the whole story?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense (er/sie/es) of „erzählen“; can also be the informal plural imperative („erzählt!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erzählt eine Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tells a story.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "erzählen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er erzählte mir eine lustige Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told me a funny story.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „erzählen“ (they/we told)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern erzählten sie mir eine lustige Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they told me a funny story.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/literary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Bemerkung erzürnte sie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His remark angered her.

definitions.note: Can mean opening something (like a door or an account) or starting something (like a meeting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich eröffne ein neues Konto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I open a new account.

definitions.note: Often used for opening something officially or for the first time (e.g., an account, a business, an event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte ein Konto eröffnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to open an account.

definitions.note: Used for officially starting a new business, building, event, or exhibition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt wird das neue Museum nächste Woche eröffnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city will inaugurate (open) the new museum next week.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense (he/she/it opens).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister eröffnet das Festival.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor opens the festival.

definitions.note: past participle; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist eröffnet“ = has been opened / is open).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Museum ist offiziell eröffnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum is officially opened.

definitions.note: Often used in announcements or signs (e.g., that a shop, exhibition, or event is now open).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Geschäft ist eröffnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shop is open.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of „eröffnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister eröffnete das neue Schwimmbad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor opened the new swimming pool.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural/formal “you”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie eröffneten das neue Geschäft im Mai.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They opened the new shop in May.

definitions.note: Often used when you can manage to set aside or make available something extra.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann etwas Zeit für dich erübrigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can spare some time for you.

definitions.note: Common in the reflexive form: „sich erübrigen“ (= to become unnecessary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn wir alles online finden, wird sich die Frage erübrigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we can find everything online, the question will be unnecessary.

definitions.note: Often used as a “dummy” subject, like English “it” in “it is raining.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnet heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining today.

definitions.note: Command (informal) to one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ess dein Gemüse!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat your vegetables!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Beeren sind essbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The berries are edible.

definitions.note: First-person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of "essen"; common in reported speech and fixed phrases like "Es sei denn...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er esse kein Fleisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that he doesn't eat meat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen heute Pizza essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to eat pizza today.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) present tense of „essen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr esst jeden Morgen Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) eat bread every morning.

definitions.note: Used mainly in plural, often in more formal German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Etliche Leute warten schon seit einer Stunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Several people have already been waiting for an hour.

definitions.note: Used to give an approximate number or amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme in etwa zehn Minuten zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be back in about ten minutes.

definitions.note: Often used in questions to suggest a possibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du etwa meinen Schlüssel gesehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you maybe seen my key?

definitions.note: often used to mean “a bit / somewhat” before adjectives or adverbs
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe etwas vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot something.

definitions.note: used to soften statements, especially before adjectives/adverbs
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist etwas teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a little expensive.

definitions.note: Often used as an indefinite pronoun: something/anything (depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte etwas essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to eat something.

definitions.note: Used before adjectives/adverbs to mean “somewhat/a bit”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist etwas schwierig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is somewhat difficult.

definitions.note: Often used like English “somewhat/a bit” with adjectives and adverbs (e.g., etwas müde = somewhat tired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche etwas Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some water.

definitions.note: informal; object form (accusative or dative) of „ihr“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe euch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping you.

definitions.note: accusative or dative form; used for addressing more than one person
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe euch das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving you (all) the book.

definitions.note: Plural or formal (Sie) possessive determiner (2nd person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das euer Auto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that your car?

definitions.note: plural or feminine form of “euer” (used with plural nouns or feminine singular nouns in the nominative/accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sind das eure Schuhe?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are those your shoes?

definitions.note: Possessive pronoun for “you” (plural) or polite “you” (Sie); “eure” is used with feminine singular nouns (and with plural nouns in some cases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das eure Jacke?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that your jacket?

definitions.note: Plural or feminine singular form of "euer" (informal 2nd-person plural "you"), used with a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo ist eure Jacke?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is your jacket?

definitions.note: dative masculine or neuter singular form of the informal plural possessive determiner (used with ihr: “you all”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe eurem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm helping your brother.

definitions.note: used when talking to more than one person (plural “you”); dative masculine or neuter singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe eurem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping your brother.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular form of „euer“ (used with masculine nouns in the accusative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe euren Hund im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see your dog in the park.

definitions.note: masculine accusative plural (e.g., with a masculine noun in the accusative case, or with plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe euren Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see your father.

definitions.note: used when addressing more than one person (plural “you”); this form is used with masculine nouns in the accusative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe euren Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see your father.

definitions.note: Genitive singular (masculine/neuter) or dative plural form of "euer" (informal plural "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen eurer Hilfe sind wir pünktlich angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your help, we arrived on time.

definitions.note: Genitive form of "euer" (2nd person plural "you all" or formal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen eurer Hilfe haben wir es geschafft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your help, we managed to do it.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner for informal plural “you” (ihr).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe eurer Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m helping your mother.

definitions.note: genitive singular or genitive plural form of „euer“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen eures Lärms konnte ich nicht schlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your noise, I couldn't sleep.

definitions.note: Genitive form of „euer“ (2nd person plural / formal „Sie“); used to show possession, often in phrases like „wegen eures …“ or „trotz eures …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen eures Lärms kann ich nicht schlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of your noise, I can’t sleep.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a feminine noun or in the plural (depending on the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die europäische Union hat neue Regeln beschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The European Union has adopted new rules.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak/strong ending form used with certain articles/pronouns (e.g., „die europäischen …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die europäischen Länder arbeiten oft zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The European countries often work together.

definitions.note: Often used for evacuating people from a place (e.g., after a fire or flood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei muss das Gebäude evakuieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have to evacuate the building.

definitions.note: past participle of „evakuieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gebäude wurde evakuiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was evacuated.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “if necessary” or “as the case may be,” not “eventually.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können uns eventuell morgen treffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can possibly meet tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often also used informally to mean “a very long time.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich ewig lieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will love you forever.

definitions.note: Adjective in a declined form (e.g., before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die ewige Liebe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is eternal love.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wünschen sich den ewigen Frieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wish for eternal peace.

definitions.note: This is the masculine nominative singular form (e.g., before a masculine noun like „ewiger Frieden“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hoffen auf ewiger Frieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hope for eternal peace.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (often with a hyphen) to mean someone/something from the past (e.g., an ex-partner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Ex-Freundin wohnt jetzt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ex-girlfriend lives in Berlin now.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present ("ich existiere")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich existiere, also bin ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exist, therefore I am.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einhörner existieren nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unicorns do not exist.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Existierst du wirklich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you really exist?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Regel existiert schon seit Jahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This rule has existed for years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher existierte hier ein kleines Dorf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A small village used to exist here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bombe kann jederzeit explodieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bomb can explode at any time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ballon explodiert plötzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon suddenly explodes.

definitions.note: Past participle used with an auxiliary (e.g., „ist“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bombe ist explodiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bomb has exploded.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „explodieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bombe explodierte mitten in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bomb exploded in the middle of the night.

definitions.note: Often used in business/economics contexts; also used in computing for exporting data/files.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland muss viele Autos exportieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany has to export many cars.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma exportiert Autos nach Kanada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company exports cars to Canada.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something is in addition to what is usual or expected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche ein extra Handtuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need an extra towel.

definitions.note: Often means “in addition” or “separately/on the side,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich die Soße extra bekommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I get the sauce on the side?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist heute extrem kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is extremely cold today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine extreme Situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an extreme situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen in diesem Restaurant ist exzellent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food in this restaurant is excellent.

definitions.note: colloquial; used to get someone’s attention or to express surprise/annoyance
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ey, hör auf damit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey, stop that!

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) present tense of „essen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was eßt ihr heute Abend?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you eating this evening?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen war einfach fabelhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was simply fabulous.

definitions.note: Used before a noun; often expresses enthusiastic praise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten eine fabelhafte Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a fabulous idea.

definitions.note: Informal singular command form of "fahren" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fahr bitte langsam!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please drive slowly!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "fahren" ("ich fahre" = "I drive/ride").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fahre morgen mit dem Zug nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking the train to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.native: to drive; to ride; to travel (by vehicle)
definitions.note: Often used for traveling by vehicle (car, bus, train, etc.); with a direct object it can mean to drive something (e.g., ein Auto fahren = to drive a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen mit dem Zug nach Berlin fahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will travel to Berlin by train tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used especially for public transport (trains, buses, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug fährt heute fahrplanmäßig um 18:05 Uhr ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train departs today at 6:05 p.m. according to the schedule.

definitions.note: Used with ihr (you all) in the present tense, and also as the plural imperative (“Drive!/Go!”). Not related to English “fart”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr fahrt morgen nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) are driving to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “just” or “reasonable.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein fairer Preis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a fair price.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “quite” or “pretty” (degree), especially in informal speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin fair müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m fairly tired.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like rules, behavior, or competition (e.g., „ein faires Spiel“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine faire Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a fair decision.

definitions.note: German noun: der Fall = case/instance; not the verb „fallen“ (to fall).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In diesem Fall rufe ich dich morgen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this case I’ll call you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich falle vom Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fall off the bicycle.

definitions.note: Infinitive form (used after modal verbs, with "zu", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, sonst wirst du fallen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful, or you’ll fall!

definitions.note: Past participle (often used with "sein": "ist gefallen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern auf der Treppe gefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell yesterday on the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst das Glas nicht fallenlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not drop the glass.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a condition (often similar to „wenn“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ruf mich an, falls du Hilfe brauchst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call me in case you need help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist falsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Antwort ist falsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answer is wrong.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine singular nouns (and sometimes in plural, depending on case/article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die falsche Adresse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the wrong address.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular (weak ending) after a determiner, e.g. "den falschen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den falschen Schlüssel genommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the wrong key.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "falsch" (e.g., masculine nominative singular in strong declension).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war falscher Alarm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a false alarm.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter singular noun (or as a nominalized adjective in neuter singular), e.g. „ein falsches Bild“ or „etwas Falsches“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein falsches Bild.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wrong picture.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "falten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er faltete den Brief und steckte ihn in den Umschlag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He folded the letter and put it into the envelope.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a warm, friendly atmosphere (e.g. „familiäre Atmosphäre“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir mögen die familiäre Atmosphäre im Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We like the familiar, informal atmosphere in the café.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „finden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fand den Schlüssel unter dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found the key under the sofa.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "finden"; used with plural subjects or formal "Sie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fanden den Schlüssel unter dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found the key under the sofa.

definitions.note: simple past (du-form) of "finden"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du fandest den Schlüssel unter dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You found the key under the sofa.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of „finden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr fandet den Schlüssel unter dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You found the key under the sofa.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „anfangen“; as an imperative it is usually followed by „an“ (e.g., „Fang an!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fang jetzt an!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Start now!

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative: “Fang …!” = “Catch …!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fang den Ball!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Catch the ball!

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix: „Ich fange … an.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fange um acht Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I start at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix in the verb „anfangen“ (e.g. „Wir fangen an.“ = „We start.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fangen um acht Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We start at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: infinitive form; often used with a direct object (e.g., a ball, a fish)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Torwart muss den Ball fangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goalkeeper has to catch the ball.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anfangen“; the prefix often appears at the end of the clause (…fangt … an).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr fangt morgen mit dem Kurs an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) start the course tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with "ihr" (you all) in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr fangt den Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) catch the ball.

definitions.note: Usually used with the separable particle "an" ("fangt ... an").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr fangt um acht Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) start at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war fantastisch!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was fantastic!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein fantastischer Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a fantastic movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Film ist fantastischer als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is more fantastic than the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Opa ist farbenblind und kann Rot und Grün schwer unterscheiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa is color-blind and has difficulty telling red and green apart.

definitions.note: Often used as the (informal) singular imperative of „fassen“ (e.g., giving someone a command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fass meine Hand!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grab my hand!

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (du) of „fassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fass meine Hand!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold my hand!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fasse das Geländer, weil es glatt ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grab the railing because it’s slippery.

definitions.note: Often used for taking hold of something firmly (more formal than „nehmen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Geländer fassen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please grab/hold the railing?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anfassen“; in many sentences the prefix appears at the end (e.g., „fasst … an“).
