definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fasst das Glas nicht an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't touch the glass.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., someone’s hand): „Er fasst meine Hand.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fasst meine Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grabs my hand.

definitions.note: Simple past of „fassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fasste meine Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grabbed my hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin fast fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm almost finished.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich faszinierend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really fascinating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin von dem Film fasziniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fascinated by the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin fasziniert von deinem Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m fascinated by your project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute zu faul, um zu kochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm too lazy to cook today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die faule Katze schläft den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lazy cat sleeps all day.

definitions.note: Often used for food/fruit that has gone bad.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die faule Banane liegt im Müll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rotten banana is in the trash.

definitions.native: to rot, to go bad (esp. food/organic material)
definitions.note: Verb; often used with ‘lassen’ or ‘anfangen zu’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Äpfel faulen im Keller.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apples are rotting in the cellar.

definitions.note: Verb; can also be used figuratively for things deteriorating.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Pflege faulen die Holzbalken schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without care, the wooden beams rot quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute bin ich fauler als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m lazier than yesterday.

definitions.note: Form of **faul** used e.g. with neuter singular nouns (*ein faules Kind*) or in the accusative after an indefinite article (*Ich sehe ein faules Kind*).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein faules Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a lazy child.

definitions.note: Often used for food (e.g., fruit); **faules** is the neuter form (e.g., *faules Obst*).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werfen faules Obst weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We throw away rotten fruit.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "faul"; used with "der/die/das" or after "am" (e.g., "der faulste", "am faulsten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist der faulste Schüler in der Klasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is the laziest student in the class.

definitions.note: informal/colloquial short form of „fege“ (e.g., as an informal command)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Feg bitte die Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sweep the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute die Küche fegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to sweep the kitchen today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "fegen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fegt den Boden in der Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sweeps the floor in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Mostly used in fixed expressions like „hier fehl sein“ or „fehl am Platz“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tut mir leid, Sie sind hier fehl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, you're in the wrong place here.

definitions.note: Mostly used in set phrases like „fehl am Platz“ (= out of place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Bemerkung ist hier völlig fehl am Platz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That remark is completely out of place here.

definitions.note: Often used with a person/thing as the subject to mean it isn’t there (e.g., someone is absent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fehle heute in der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m absent from school today.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative person: „Mir fehlt …“ = “I’m missing … / I don’t have …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir fehlen heute die Zeit und die Energie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m lacking time and energy.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with a definite/indefinite article); it means something is not there
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte füllen Sie die fehlenden Angaben aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fill in the missing information.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative pronoun/person: „Mir fehlt …“ = “I’m missing/lacking …” (literally “To me … is missing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir fehlt heute die Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time today (literally: Time is missing to me today).

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „fehlen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel fehlte auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key was missing from the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Regal fehlten zwei Bücher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two books were missing from the shelf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich feiere heute meinen Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m celebrating my birthday today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Musik klang feierlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music sounded solemn.

definitions.note: Often used with an event (e.g., birthday) or a holiday; in informal contexts it can also mean to party.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir feiern heute deinen Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re celebrating your birthday today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "feiern" (used with "du")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum feierst du heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you celebrating today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er feiert heute seinen Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He celebrates his birthday today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "feiern" for "we/you (plural)/they"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Wochenende feierten wir seinen Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last weekend we celebrated his birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war feige von ihm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was cowardly of him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war zu feige, um die Wahrheit zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was too cowardly to tell the truth.

definitions.note: Often used for taste (subtle), texture, or something very small/precise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen schmeckt fein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake tastes fine.

definitions.note: Common in fixed phrases like „Das ist fein.“ meaning something like “That’s nice/great.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist fein, danke!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s nice, thanks!

definitions.note: As an adverb, often means “fine” in the sense of “okay / all right.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alles ist fein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is fine.

definitions.note: Used as a short interjection to express approval or agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fein, dann machen wir das so.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fine, then we'll do it that way.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (attributive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten beobachteten die feindliche Bewegung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers observed the hostile movement.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with masculine/neuter dative singular or with plural (all genders) in certain case contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir begegneten keinen feindlichen Soldaten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We didn’t encounter any enemy soldiers.

definitions.note: Adjective form of „fein“ used with a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article/case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt eine feine Bluse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a fine blouse.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine accusative or plural dative nouns (weak/mixed declension), depending on the article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte den feinen Käse probieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to try the fine cheese.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective ending (e.g., before a noun) or as a nominalized adjective depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern etwas Feines zum Nachtisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like something fine for dessert.

definitions.note: often used with „von“ (e.g., „fern von …“ = „far from …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen fern von der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live far from the city.

definitions.note: Usually used with a form of “sein” (e.g., „es ist nicht fern“ = “it’s not far”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bahnhof ist nicht fern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train station is not far.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "fern" (e.g., in phrases like "in fernen …" = "in distant …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat in fernen Ländern gelebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lived in distant countries.

definitions.note: past participle of „fernsehen“; used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern Abend ferngesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched TV yesterday evening.

definitions.native: keep away, keep at a distance
definitions.note: Separable verb: (etw./jdn.) von + Dat. fernhalten; Perfekt: hat ferngehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte fernhalten Sie die Kinder vom Herd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please keep the children away from the stove.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form (often used in reported/indirect speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er fernsehe jeden Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he watches TV every evening.

definitions.native: to watch TV; to watch television
definitions.note: Verb: fernsehen (separable: ich sehe fern / ich habe ferngesehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fernsehen abends oft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We often watch TV in the evening.

definitions.native: to stay away, to keep away
definitions.note: Often used with "von" (e.g., "von der Schule fernbleiben" = to stay away from school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat beschlossen, der Party fernzubleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided to stay away from the party.

definitions.native: to keep away, to keep (someone/something) at a distance
definitions.note: Often used with „von“ + dative (e.g., „jemanden von etwas fernhalten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte versuchen Sie, die Kinder vom Feuer fernzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please try to keep the children away from the fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern Abend beschlossen, fernzusehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday evening I decided to watch TV.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" (e.g., "fertig sein" = to be finished/ready).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit meinen Hausaufgaben fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m finished with my homework.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g., „Ich bin fertig.“ = I’m finished / I’m done).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bist du schon fertig?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you finished already?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Hausaufgaben fertiggemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finished my homework.

definitions.note: Often used about how something/someone makes a person feel (e.g. a stressful day).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der lange Tag hat mich fertiggemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The long day wore me out.

definitions.note: Past participle of „fertigstellen“; often used with „haben“ or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Brücke ist endlich fertiggestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bridge has finally been completed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Bericht heute noch fertigmachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to finish the report today.

definitions.native: put someone down, wear someone down
definitions.note: informal; often used as „jemanden fertigmachen“ (to bully/tear someone down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf, ihn fertigmachen zu wollen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop trying to put him down!

definitions.note: Often used for finishing a task, project, or piece of work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Bericht bis morgen fertigstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to finish the report by tomorrow.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used with verbs like „versuchen“, „planen“, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, das Projekt bis Freitag fertigzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re trying to finish the project by Friday.

definitions.note: Used literally for physically restraining someone, and figuratively for captivating/holding someone’s attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei muss den Verdächtigen fesseln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have to shackle the suspect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schraube sitzt fest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The screw is tight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch steht fest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table stands firmly.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like halten, drücken, ziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hält meine Hand ganz fest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She holds my hand very tightly.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „halten“ or „drücken“ to mean holding/pressing strongly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Halt dich fest!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on tight!

definitions.note: Often used for something stable or not easily moved/changed (e.g., feste Regeln, feste Schuhe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche feste Schuhe für die Wanderung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need sturdy shoes for the hike.

definitions.native: firm, solid, tight (attributive form of „fest“ in masculine accusative / masculine dative / plural dative)
definitions.note: Form used before a noun, e.g., „den festen…“ (masc. acc.), „mit festem…“ (masc./neut. dat.; not „festen“), „mit den festen…“ (pl. dat.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trägt den festen Gürtel beim Wandern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wears the tight belt while hiking.

definitions.native: to celebrate / to feast (verb: „fasten“ in some contexts; but „festen“ is uncommon as a verb form in standard German—usually „feiern“ for celebrating)
definitions.note: As a verb, „festen“ is rare/archaic; most learners will encounter „festen“ as an inflected adjective form of „fest“ (e.g., „den festen…“, „die festen…“, „mit den festen…“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie dekorierten den Saal und begannen, mit den festen Traditionen des Dorfes zu feiern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decorated the hall and began celebrating with the village’s established traditions.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „fest“; can also appear with an adjective ending before a masculine noun (e.g., „fester Boden“ = firm ground).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Griff wird fester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grip becomes firmer.

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adverb “fest”. Also a false friend with English “to fester” (= to rot/infect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Halt dich fester am Geländer fest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on tighter to the railing.

definitions.note: past participle of „festhalten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich am Geländer festgehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I held on to the railing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Termin ist festgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The date is set.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wurde gestern festgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was arrested yesterday.

definitions.native: to hold on to; to hold tight
definitions.note: Used literally (gripping something) and figuratively (sticking to an idea, plan, or record).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Halte dich gut fest und bleib ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on tight and stay calm.

definitions.native: to stick to; to maintain (an opinion/plan)
definitions.note: Figurative: keeping to a decision, belief, or course of action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde an meinem Plan festhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will stick to my plan.

definitions.native: to record; to note down; to capture (in writing/pictures)
definitions.note: Often used with “schriftlich” or in contexts like documenting facts or capturing moments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die wichtigsten Ergebnisse schriftlich festhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to record the most important results in writing.

definitions.note: used especially in a police/legal context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei wird den Mann morgen festnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police will arrest the man tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for finding out or officially stating a fact (e.g., in reports, by police, doctors).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei konnte schnell feststellen, wer das Auto gefahren hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were able to quickly determine who drove the car.

definitions.native: to hold on to, to hold tight
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, den Ball festzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to hold on to the ball.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form, often used after expressions like „um … zu“ or verbs like „versuchen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Um die Ursache festzustellen, müssen wir noch ein paar Tests machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To determine the cause, we still need to do a few tests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Pommes sind zu fett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fries are too greasy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag keine fette Wurst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like fatty sausage.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective "fett" (e.g., before a plural noun or after an article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, nicht so viele fetten Pommes zu essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try not to eat so many greasy fries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte kein fettes Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want any fatty/greasy food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Luft im Keller ist feucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The air in the basement is damp.

definitions.note: Often used for air/weather meaning “humid.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die feuchte Luft klebt auf der Haut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The humid air sticks to your skin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme einen feuchten Lappen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a damp cloth.

definitions.note: to dismiss someone from a job
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef will ihn feuern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss wants to fire him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten feuern auf das Ziel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers shoot at the target.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Soldat feuert zweimal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldier fires twice.

definitions.note: Informal in this meaning; often used when someone loses their job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma feuert den Mitarbeiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fires the employee.

definitions.note: Often used with "an" ("jemanden anfeuern" = to cheer someone on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie feuert ihr Team laut an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cheers her team on loudly.

definitions.note: Often used with things like firing a gun or lighting a fire; can also mean firing someone from a job depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Soldat feuerte dreimal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldier fired three times.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/offensive sexual verb; often used in insults (e.g., “Fick dich!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fick dich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fuck you!

definitions.note: Very vulgar/sexually explicit; often used as an insult (e.g., “Fick dich!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fick dich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fuck you!

definitions.note: Very vulgar and offensive; use with extreme caution.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ficke niemanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fuck nobody.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/explicit; often used as an insult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich soll mich ficken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says I should go fuck myself.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/explicit; refers to having sex, and can also be used as an insult in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fickt seine Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fucks his girlfriend.

definitions.note: Often used in German to mean “fiction” in general (as opposed to non-fiction), especially in publishing or libraries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese gerade ein Buch aus der Abteilung Fiction.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m currently reading a book from the fiction section.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „einfallen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir fiel sofort eine gute Idee ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A good idea immediately occurred to me.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „fallen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern fiel das Buch vom Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday the book fell off the table.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „fallen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern fielen die Blätter von den Bäumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday the leaves fell from the trees.

definitions.note: Often used for people or behavior; can be fairly informal/colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war fies von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was mean of you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir filmen das Konzert mit dem Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re filming the concert with a phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können das Projekt finanziell nicht stemmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can't manage the project financially.

definitions.note: Used in contexts about money, funding, or finances; here it’s the inflected form before a noun (e.g., „finanzielle Hilfe“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen finanzielle Unterstützung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need financial support.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with masculine accusative, masculine/neuter dative, or plural genitive nouns (weak/strong/mixed endings depend on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben wegen der finanziellen Probleme um Hilfe gebeten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We asked for help because of the financial problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bank wird das neue Haus finanzieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank will finance the new house.

definitions.note: past participle of „finanzieren“; often used with „werden/sein“ (e.g., „wird finanziert“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Projekt wird von der Stadt finanziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is funded by the city.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „finden“ (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Findest du den Schlüssel?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you find the key?

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I") of "finden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde den Schlüssel nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find the key.

definitions.note: often used with an opinion (e.g., "ich finde, dass …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde das gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that's good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann meinen Schlüssel nicht finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t find my key.

definitions.note: Often used to give an opinion (e.g., with “gut/schlecht zu finden”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er scheint den Film gut zu finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seems to think the movie is good.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "finden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Findest du den Schlüssel?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you find the key?

definitions.note: Used with an object or clause to mean "to think" (e.g., "ich finde, dass...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie findest du das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you think about that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er findet seine Schlüssel nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can’t find his keys.

definitions.note: Often used to give an opinion: „Ich finde …“ = “I think …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie findet den Film langweilig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She thinks the movie is boring.

definitions.note: simple past of "anfangen"; in sentences the separable prefix often appears at the end ("fing … an")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fing gestern mit dem Deutschkurs an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He started the German course yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „fangen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fing den Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He caught the ball.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „anfangen“; often used in narratives and written German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fingen um acht Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They began at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „fangen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fingen den Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They caught the ball.

definitions.note: Often used for places/rooms or the weather; can also describe a person’s mood or expression.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Wald war es schon am Nachmittag finster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the forest it was already dark in the afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fischen am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fish at the lake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fischt jeden Samstag im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fishes in the lake every Saturday.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „fit sein“ (= to be fit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nach dem Training wieder fit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm fit again after training.

definitions.note: Colloquial (especially in southern Germany/Austria); means “quickly,” not “to fix/repair.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme fix nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll come home quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Teller ist ganz flach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plate is completely flat.

definitions.note: often used for water (lakes, pools, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Pool ist hier sehr flach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pool is very shallow here.

definitions.note: inflected form of „flach“ (used before a noun, e.g. with „den/die/das“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stelle die Teller auf den flachen Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the plates on the flat table.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used when an illness (or sometimes an incident) makes someone unable to do anything for a while.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Grippe hat mich für drei Tage flachgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flu knocked me out for three days.

definitions.native: to put out of action, to knock (someone) flat
definitions.note: Colloquial; often used when an illness leaves someone unable to work or do much.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Grippe kann mich für eine Woche flachlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flu can put me out of action for a week.

definitions.note: Often a shortened/colloquial form of "flehe" ("I beg/plead").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fleh dich an: Hilf mir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I beg you: help me!

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „flehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er flehte sie um Hilfe an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He begged her for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr fleißig und lernt jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very hardworking and studies every day.

definitions.note: Often also used as an adjective meaning “hard-working.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lernt fleißig für die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studies diligently for the exam.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine fleißige Studentin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a hard-working student.

definitions.note: comparative form of the adjective „fleißig“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist fleißiger als sein Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is more diligent than his brother.

definitions.note: comparative form of "fleißig" when used as an adverb
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du fleißiger lernst, bestehst du die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you study more diligently, you’ll pass the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche flexibel gestaltete Arbeitszeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need flexibly arranged working hours.

definitions.note: comparative form of "flexibel"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Lösung ist flexibler als die alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This solution is more flexible than the old one.

definitions.note: Often used for repairing clothes, shoes, or other items with holes or tears.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meine Jeans flicken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to patch my jeans.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal (du) imperative: “Flieg!” = “Fly!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Flieg bitte nicht so schnell!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t fly so fast!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fliege morgen nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m flying to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht fliegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't fly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sahen eine fliegende Untertasse am Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a flying saucer in the sky.

definitions.note: adjective inflected form (often used with a noun, e.g. „die fliegenden Vögel“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe die fliegenden Vögel am Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the flying birds in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein fliegender Teppich ist nur in Märchen möglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A flying carpet is only possible in fairy tales.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „fliegen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du fliegst morgen nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You fly to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense (3rd person singular) of „fliegen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vogel fliegt über den See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird flies over the lake.

definitions.note: Often used in serious contexts (e.g., war, danger, persecution).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Familie musste aus dem Land fliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family had to flee the country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb flieht aus dem Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief flees from the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Regen kann man sehen, wie das Wasser schnell fließen kann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, you can see how the water can flow quickly.

definitions.note: Often used about language ability (e.g., fließend Deutsch sprechen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spricht fließend Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks fluent German.

definitions.note: Used for liquids or movement that goes smoothly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fluss ist hier breit und fließend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river is wide and flowing here.

definitions.note: often used with languages (e.g., „fließend Deutsch sprechen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spricht fließend Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks German fluently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fluss fließt durch die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flows through the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist sehr flink.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is very quick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird auf der Party mit vielen Leuten flirten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will flirt with many people at the party.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „flirten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er flirtet mit ihr auf der Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He flirts with her at the party.

definitions.note: simple past of „fliegen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern flog ich nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I flew to Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „fliegen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzte Woche flogen wir nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last week we flew to Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „fliehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er floh aus dem brennenden Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fled from the burning house.

definitions.note: simple past of „flüchten“ (often used in written narratives)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er floh aus der Stadt, bevor die Polizei ankam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fled the city before the police arrived.

definitions.note: Often means using offensive/strong language out of anger or frustration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er beginnt zu fluchen, weil der Bus schon wieder zu spät ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He starts to swear because the bus is late again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum fluchst du so viel?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you curse so much?

definitions.note: This form is normally spelled with an umlaut: „flüchtet“ (from „flüchten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er flucht aus dem brennenden Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He flees from the burning house.

definitions.note: past tense (simple past) of "fluchen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fluchte leise, als der Zug wieder Verspätung hatte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cursed quietly when the train was delayed again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind flussabwärts bis zur Brücke gefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drove downstream as far as the bridge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fahren flussaufwärts bis zum nächsten Dorf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going upstream to the next village.

definitions.note: often used with „vor“ + dative to mean fleeing from something (e.g. danger, war)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen flüchten vor dem Krieg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people flee from the war.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er flüchtete aus dem brennenden Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fled from the burning house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eindruck war nur flüchtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The impression was only fleeting.

definitions.note: used to describe someone who is逃 running away from the police or authorities
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der flüchtige Täter wurde später gefasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fugitive offender was caught later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nur einen flüchtigen Eindruck bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only got a fleeting impression.

definitions.note: Used to describe a person who is escaping or hiding from the police.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei sucht den flüchtigen Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are looking for the fugitive man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wasser ist noch flüssig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is still liquid.

definitions.note: Used especially about speaking a language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spricht flüssig Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks fluent German.

definitions.note: Used especially with languages and speaking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spricht flüssig Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks German fluently.

definitions.note: Describes something happening without problems or interruptions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alles läuft flüssig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is running smoothly.

definitions.note: Used here as an adjective ending (-es), e.g. before a neuter noun like „Wasser“ or as a nominalized adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte gib mir flüssiges Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please give me liquid water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte flüstern, das Baby schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please whisper; the baby is sleeping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er flüstert mir ein Geheimnis ins Ohr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He whispers a secret in my ear.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er flüsterte mir ein Geheimnis ins Ohr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He whispered a secret in my ear.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural (they / we)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie flüsterten im Kino, damit niemand sie hörte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They whispered in the movie theater so that nobody would hear them.

definitions.note: often means “I follow” (1st person singular, present tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich folge dir auf Instagram.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I follow you on Instagram.

definitions.note: can also be an informal command: “follow!” (imperative, to one person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Folge mir bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please follow me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte folgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please follow me?

definitions.note: Often used before a noun in set phrases like „die folgende Frage“ (“the following question”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte beantworten Sie die folgende Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please answer the following question.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective "folgend"; often used before a noun (e.g. "in den folgenden Tagen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In den folgenden Tagen habe ich viel gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the following days, I learned a lot.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal or written German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat die ganze Nacht geregnet, folglich bleiben wir heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained all night, therefore we’re staying home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund folgt mir nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog follows me home.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „folgen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er folgte ihr nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He followed her home.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie folgten dem Hund nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They followed the dog home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man darf niemanden foltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not torture anyone.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of „fordern“; also used as a polite/less direct way to express a demand/request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er fordere mehr Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he demands more money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Arbeiter fordern höhere Löhne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The workers are demanding higher wages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef fordert mehr Konzentration.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss demands more concentration.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef forderte mehr Konzentration im Team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss demanded more focus in the team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Frage bitte anders formulieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you phrase the question differently, please?

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion in expressions like „fortgehen“ (to go away) or „fortfahren“ (to drive away/continue).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte fort!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go away!

definitions.note: Used with verbs of motion to mean going away/continuing on; often seen as in „fortgehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er geht fort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes away.

definitions.native: to continue, to carry on (with something)
definitions.note: Often used with "mit" + dative: "mit etwas fortfahren" = to continue with something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fortfahren mit der Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We continue with the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schon fortgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has already left.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving a place (sometimes for going out in the evening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt fortgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave now.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "fortgehen"; common in writing and in subordinate clauses (e.g., "weil er fortging").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war müde, weil er früh fortging.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was tired because he left early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Gespräch morgen fortsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to continue the conversation tomorrow.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used after certain verbs, adjectives, or as a purpose clause)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Gespräch fortzusetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to continue the conversation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Darf ich dich fotografieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: May I photograph you?

definitions.note: Can be used as a present-tense form (e.g., “he/she photographs,” “you all photograph”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fotografiert den Sonnenuntergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He photographs the sunset.

definitions.note: Can be used as the past participle (e.g., with “haben” or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Gebäude fotografiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I photographed the building.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „fotografieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fotografierte das alte Gebäude bei Sonnenuntergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She photographed the old building at sunset.

definitions.note: Command form (informal singular): used when telling one person you know well to ask (e.g., a friend, child).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Frag den Lehrer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask the teacher!

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present of „fragen“ (ich frage = I ask).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich frage den Lehrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ask the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Darf ich etwas fragen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: May I ask something?

definitions.note: Often used to say that something is uncertain or not likely to be true (e.g., „Es ist fraglich, ob …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist fraglich, ob er heute noch kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s doubtful whether he will still come today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form) of „fragen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fragst du mich oder ihn?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you asking me or him?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "fragen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fragt nach deinem Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asks for your name.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „fragen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fragte mich nach meinem Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He asked me my name.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „fragen“ for „we/you(pl)/they“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fragten nach dem Weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They asked for directions.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form used with informal singular du: "you asked".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum fragtest du mich das gestern?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you ask me that yesterday?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Verhalten ist ziemlich fragwürdig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His behavior is pretty questionable.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective (e.g., "French cheese") or for the language (e.g., "in French").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann ein bisschen Französisch, aber nicht sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can speak a little French, but not very well.

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine nouns or plural nouns (with a determiner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne die französische Sprache.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning the French language.

definitions.note: weak ending used after a determiner (e.g., der/die/das, ein/eine) in masculine accusative or dative singular, or in plural dative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir lernen den französischen Wortschatz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re learning the French vocabulary.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a masculine noun in the nominative case (e.g., „ein französischer Film“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein französischer Film läuft heute Abend im Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A French movie is playing at the cinema tonight.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a neuter noun in the nominative or accusative singular (e.g., „ein französisches Buch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein französisches Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a French book.

definitions.note: Simple past of „fressen“; usually used for animals, and can sound rude/coarse if used about people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund fraß das Fleisch schnell auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog ate the meat quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist aber frech!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really cheeky!

definitions.note: Can mean either “not occupied/available” (e.g., a seat, time) or “not restricted” (e.g., free access).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist dieser Platz noch frei?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is this seat still free?

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “available / not occupied” (e.g., a seat, a table, a time slot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist der Platz noch frei?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is the seat still free?

definitions.note: Often used with "haben" to mean you don’t have to work or go to school (e.g., "Ich habe heute frei.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen habe ich frei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m off.

definitions.note: Used before a feminine noun or with plural nouns (inflected form of "frei").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du noch eine freie Minute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you still have a free minute?

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter singular form of „frei“ (e.g., after „mit“, „zu“, „in“ + dative, or with dative adjectives)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit freiem Eintritt dürfen Kinder heute ins Museum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With free admission, children may enter the museum today.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „frei“ (e.g., „freien Eintritt“ = free admission).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben freien Eintritt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have free admission.

definitions.note: comparative form of „frei“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier bin ich freier als zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Here I am freer than at home.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a neuter singular noun (e.g. freies WLAN).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier gibt es freies WLAN.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is free Wi‑Fi here.

definitions.note: often used for granting permission (e.g., a payment, a request, access).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Antrag wurde freigegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The application was approved.

definitions.note: often used for publishing or making something accessible (e.g., information, files, seats).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Datei ist für alle freigegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The file is shared/made available for everyone.

definitions.note: past participle of „freilassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Mann nach der Befragung freigelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police released the man after the questioning.

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun in German (e.g., "Ich habe mir ... freigenommen" = "I took ... off").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir heute freigenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took today off.

definitions.note: Used in a legal/court context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist vor Gericht freigesprochen worden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was acquitted in court.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „sagen“ or „fragen“ to mean speaking openly and directly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sage dir freiheraus, dass ich keine Zeit habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m telling you frankly that I don’t have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sprach freimütig über ihre Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spoke candidly about her mistakes.

definitions.note: often used to mean taking a day (or days) off work/school
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Freinehmen ist manchmal nötig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Taking time off is sometimes necessary.

definitions.note: means this happens regularly every Friday (habitual)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Freitags gehe ich nach der Arbeit ins Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Fridays I go to the gym after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Teilnahme ist freiwillig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Participation is voluntary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mache das freiwillig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m doing that voluntarily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt ist mir fremd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is unfamiliar to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Stadt fühle ich mich manchmal fremd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the city, I sometimes feel strange (like I don't belong).

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (e.g. „eine fremde Stadt“ = “a foreign/strange city”). Not related to English “friend”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine fremde Sprache für mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a foreign language for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen fremden Mann gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a strange man.

definitions.note: Used about being unfaithful in a romantic relationship.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist ihrem Freund fremdgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cheated on her boyfriend.

definitions.note: Used mainly for animals; when used about people it sounds rude/insulting (like “to stuff one’s face”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund kann nicht aufhören zu fressen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog can't stop eating.

definitions.native: to stuff one’s face; to eat greedily (about people, insulting)
definitions.note: Colloquial and disparaging when referring to people; implies eating in an uncouth/greedy way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf, so zu fressen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop stuffing your face like that!

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „freue“ (e.g. „ich freu mich …“). Often used with „mich“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich freu mich, dich zu sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm happy to see you.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „freue“ (usually with „mich“ and „auf“ + accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich freu mich auf das Wochenende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking forward to the weekend.

definitions.native: am happy, am glad; look forward (to)
definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „(ich) freue mich …“, often with „auf“ + accusative to mean “look forward to.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich freue mich auf das Wochenende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking forward to the weekend.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich freuen = to be happy, to be glad (often about something that will happen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Musik kann mich sehr freuen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music can make me very happy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verkäuferin ist sehr freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The saleswoman is very friendly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lächelt freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She smiles kindly.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine nouns or in some plural/genitive contexts (e.g., 'eine freundliche Frau', 'die freundlichen Leute')
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine freundliche Kollegin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a friendly colleague.

definitions.note: adjective in a declined form (e.g., after “einen”, “den”, “mit dem”, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen freundlichen Lehrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a friendly teacher.

definitions.note: comparative form of „freundlich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist sie viel freundlicher als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today she is much friendlier than yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used to sound polite when making a request or describing someone doing something helpful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Könnten Sie mir freundlicherweise helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you kindly help me?

definitions.note: Adjective in the form used before a neuter noun (or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schreibe ein freundliches E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m writing a friendly email.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "sich freuen"; often used with "dich" (reflexive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du freust dich über das Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are happy about the gift.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich freuen“ (= to be happy/glad about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er freut sich über das Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is happy about the gift.

definitions.note: Often used like: „Das freut mich.“ (= That makes me happy / I’m glad to hear that.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das freut mich sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That makes me very happy.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive verb „sich freuen“ (e.g., „er freute sich“ = he was happy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie freute sich sehr über die guten Nachrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was very happy about the good news.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "sich freuen" (to be happy/glad).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir freuten uns über die guten Nachrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were happy about the good news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist hier sehr friedlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is very peaceful here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Demonstration verlief friedlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The demonstration went peacefully.

definitions.note: Used to say you feel cold (not that something is turning to ice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich friere, kannst du das Fenster schließen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m freezing—can you close the window?

definitions.note: Often used about a person feeling cold ("I’m freezing"), not just water turning to ice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Jacke muss ich frieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without a jacket I have to freeze / I’m freezing without a jacket.

definitions.note: Used for “to be cold” (a person/animal) or “to freeze” (water, etc.), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir friert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm freezing.

definitions.note: Can describe food (not old/spoiled) or air/weather (cool and fresh).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Brot ist noch frisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread is still fresh.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kaffee ist frisch gemahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is freshly ground.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe frische Brötchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying fresh rolls.

definitions.note: dative singular (masculine or neuter) adjective ending; also used after certain prepositions like „mit“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse Brot mit frischem Käse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat bread with fresh cheese.

definitions.note: used before a noun with an adjective ending
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe frischen Fisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying fresh fish.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "frisch".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Salat ist frischer als der von gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This salad is fresher than yesterday’s.

definitions.note: Used when the adjective ending is "-es" (e.g., with neuter nouns like "frisches Brot").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte frisches Brot kaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to buy fresh bread.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) of „fressen“; used for animals, and can sound rude if said to a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Friss dein Futter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat your food!

definitions.note: Used mainly for animals; can also be rude/insulting when used about people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund frisst sein Futter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog eats his food.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g. „Ich bin froh …“) and commonly with „über“ + accusative or „dass“ + clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin froh, dass du da bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m glad that you’re here.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „frieren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir fror, obwohl ich eine Jacke trug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was freezing even though I was wearing a jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Boden ist hier sehr fruchtbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soil is very fertile here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin frustriert, weil es nicht klappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m frustrated because it isn’t working.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind heute fröhlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are happy today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder lachen fröhlich im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are laughing happily in the garden.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective (e.g., used before a noun or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine fröhliche Stimme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a cheerful voice.

definitions.note: comparative form of „fröhlich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute bin ich fröhlicher als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m happier than yesterday.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a neuter noun (e.g., "ein fröhliches Kind").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein fröhliches Lied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a cheerful song.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stehe heute früh auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting up early today.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „früh“ (used before a noun, e.g. „am frühen Morgen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns am frühen Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet early in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used to compare times (earlier than something else) or to talk about the past (formerly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher habe ich in Berlin gewohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to live in Berlin.

definitions.note: Can refer to an earlier time today or to the past in general, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher habe ich in Berlin gewohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to live in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive) to refer to someone/something from an earlier time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine frühere Schule war in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My former school was in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich erinnere mich an meinen früheren Chef.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I remember my former boss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe frühmorgens joggen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go jogging early in the morning.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I); also identical in form to 1st person singular present indicative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich frühstücke jeden Morgen um sieben Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have breakfast every morning at seven o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich frühstücke jeden Morgen um sieben Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have breakfast every morning at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular informal (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du frühstückst jeden Morgen um sieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have breakfast every morning at seven.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense (he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er frühstückt jeden Morgen um sieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has breakfast every morning at seven.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "frühstücken"; common in writing and storytelling
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern frühstückte ich um sieben Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I had breakfast at seven o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben frühzeitig gemerkt, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We noticed early on that something was wrong.

definitions.note: Very informal/colloquial and emphatic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war fuchsteufelswild, als er die Nachricht hörte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was furious when he heard the news.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/strong swear word; used as an exclamation of anger, frustration, or surprise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fuck, ich habe den Bus verpasst!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fuck, I missed the bus!

definitions.note: Simple past of „fahren“ (used for ‘to drive’ or ‘to travel/go by vehicle’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern fuhr ich mit dem Auto zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I drove to work by car.

definitions.note: simple past of „fahren“ (used with wir/sie/Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fuhren gestern nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drove to Berlin yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sterne funkeln am Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stars twinkle in the sky.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „funkeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sterne funkelten am klaren Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stars twinkled in the clear sky.

definitions.note: Often used for machines, devices, systems, or plans when they operate properly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy kann nicht funktionieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone can’t work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy funktioniert nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone doesn't work.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "funktionieren"; often used in written German or storytelling, while spoken German often prefers "hat ... funktioniert".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fernseher funktionierte gestern nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The TV didn’t work yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used informally just to mean “very” (e.g., “furchtbar nett” = “really nice”), not only something scary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter ist heute furchtbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is terrible today.

definitions.note: Often used informally as an intensifier meaning “very” (e.g., furchtbar nett = really nice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich furchtbar geärgert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was terribly annoyed.

definitions.note: Adjective form; often used before a noun (e.g., "eine furchtbare Idee").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine furchtbare Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a terrible idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten einen furchtbaren Streit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a terrible argument.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein furchtbarer Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a terrible mistake.

definitions.note: Neuter form used before a noun (often with an article like „etwas“ or „ein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist etwas Furchtbares.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is something terrible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war so furchteinflößend, dass ich das Licht anlassen musste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was so frightening that I had to leave the light on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie blieb auch in der Krise furchtlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She remained fearless even during the crisis.

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ + infinitive (e.g., „fähig, etwas zu tun“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nicht fähig, das alleine zu machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not able to do that alone.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „fähig“; often used with „als“ (than).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist heute viel fähiger als früher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is much more capable today than before.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "fahren" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fährst du heute mit dem Bus zur Schule?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to school by bus today?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „fahren“ (he/she/it drives).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fährt jeden Morgen mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the bus to work every morning.

definitions.note: Used especially for cutting down trees.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arbeiter will den Baum fällen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The worker wants to fell the tree.

definitions.note: Often used for payments, deadlines, or something that is required at a certain time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Miete ist am ersten Tag des Monats fällig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rent is due on the first day of the month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, sonst fällst du!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, or you'll fall!

definitions.note: From the separable verb „auffallen“; often used with „jemandem auffallen“ = to be noticed by someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das fällt mir sofort auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I notice that right away.

definitions.note: Often used for events, classes, appointments, or trains that do not take place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unterricht fällt heute aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Class is canceled today.

definitions.note: Often used for machines, systems, or power that stop working.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Aufzug fällt schon wieder aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elevator breaks down again.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „einfallen“. Often used with a dative pronoun: „Mir fällt … ein.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir fällt gerade kein gutes Beispiel ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No good example is coming to mind right now.

definitions.note: 3rd-person singular present tense of „fallen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Herbst fällt das Laub von den Bäumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn, the leaves fall from the trees.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „fällen“ (to fell/cut down), used especially in writing and narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bauer fällte den alten Baum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farmer felled the old tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fälscht die Unterschrift.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forges the signature.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of „finden“ (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fände das eine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would find that a good idea.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (would + verb), used for hypothetical/conditional situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fänden das Restaurant schnell, wenn wir eine Karte hätten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would find the restaurant quickly if we had a map.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du), subjunctive II (Konjunktiv II).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du fändest den Weg leichter, wenn du eine Karte hättest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You would find the way more easily if you had a map.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "anfangen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du fängst heute um acht Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You start today at eight o'clock.
