definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "fangen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du fängst den Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You catch the ball.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „anfangen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs fängt um neun Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course starts at nine o'clock.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „fangen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Torwart fängt den Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goalkeeper catches the ball.

definitions.note: Used with „an“ as „anfangen“ (separable verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film fängt um acht Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie starts at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used with hair or fabric (e.g., Haare, Stoff).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich färbe meine Haare blond.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dye my hair blonde.

definitions.note: Often used for changing the color of hair, fabric, or eggs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will ihre Haare blond färben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to dye her hair blond.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of „färben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tinte färbt das Papier blau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ink dyes the paper blue.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "färben"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie färbte ihre Haare blond.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dyed her hair blonde.

definitions.note: Often used for encouraging or helping something/someone develop or progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schule fördert begabte Schüler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school supports talented students.

definitions.note: Can look like English “formerly,” but it means “formally,” not “in the past.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich förmlich bei uns entschuldigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He formally apologized to us.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize something that feels almost physical or very intense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor Freude ist sie förmlich in die Luft gesprungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She practically jumped into the air with joy.

definitions.note: Often used with „hinzu“ (as in „hinzufügen“ = to add).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich füge noch ein paar Details hinzu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I add a few more details.

definitions.note: Often used in formal instructions (e.g., on forms or in emails).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte fügen Sie Ihre Adresse in das Formular ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please enter your address into the form.

definitions.note: Usually used as „sich fügen“ (to comply/submit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende musste er sich fügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he had to comply.

definitions.note: Often used with „hinzu“ (separable), as in „etwas hinzufügen“ = to add something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fügt noch einen Satz hinzu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She adds another sentence.

definitions.note: Simple past of „fügen“ (to add/insert).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fügte am Ende noch eine Bemerkung hinzu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He added a remark at the end.

definitions.note: Imperative (du-form): used to tell one person to feel/touch something (often as „Fühl mal …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fühl mal, wie kalt das Wasser ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Feel how cold the water is.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present ("I feel").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich heute müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel tired today.

definitions.note: Commonly used with a reflexive pronoun (mich/dich/sich) to describe how someone feels; also used transitively for sensing by touch.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich heute müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel tired today.

definitions.note: Often used with an object in the accusative when physically feeling something with your hands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt muss den Knoten fühlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor has to feel the lump.

definitions.note: Basic verb form „fühlen“ (not the conjugated „fühle“/„fühlst“ etc.); can also appear as reflexive „sich fühlen“ in conjugated forms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann fühlen, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel that something isn’t right.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form) of „fühlen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie fühlst du dich heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you feel today?

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun and particle: „sich … anfühlen“ = to feel (like), to feel to the touch.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stoff fühlt sich weich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fabric feels soft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fühlt sich heute besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels better today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „fühlen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühlte mich nach dem langen Tag müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt tired after the long day.

definitions.note: simple past (wir/ihr/sie/Sie) of „fühlen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fühlten uns nach dem langen Tag müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We felt tired after the long day.

definitions.note: Usually used as an informal command (imperative) of „führen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Führ mich bitte zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please lead me to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich führe die Gruppe durch die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lead the group through the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich führe ein kleines Café in der Nähe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I run a small café nearby.

definitions.note: Often used for leading people or guiding someone somewhere; also used in contexts like leading a team or a discussion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du uns zum Bahnhof führen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lead us to the train station?

definitions.note: Used especially with things like documents or weapons (e.g., einen Ausweis führen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss immer meinen Ausweis führen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always have to carry my ID.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „führen“ (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du führst das Team heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You lead the team today.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of „führen“ (also used for formal „you“: „Sie führt…“ is rare; usually „Sie führen…“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er führt die Gruppe durch die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leads the group through the city.

definitions.note: simple past of "führen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Guide führte die Gruppe durch die Altstadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide led the group through the old town.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „führen“ (they/we led; also formal „you“ led).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie führten die Gruppe durch das Museum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They led the group through the museum.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular): used to tell one person to fill something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Füll bitte das Glas mit Wasser!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fill the glass with water!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fülle die Flasche mit Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fill the bottle with water.

definitions.note: Used as the main verb part of the separable verb „ausfüllen“ (the prefix „aus“ can appear elsewhere in the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir füllen das Formular aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fill out the form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Glas mit Wasser füllen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please fill the glass with water?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er füllt die Flasche mit Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fills the bottle with water.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "füllen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er füllte das Glas mit Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He filled the glass with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe fünf Äpfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have five apples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kostet fünfhundert Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That costs five hundred euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn fünfmal angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called him five times.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto kostet fünftausend Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car costs five thousand euros.

definitions.note: ordinal number; used with feminine nouns (or as a nominalized form in some contexts)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wohnt im fünften Stock.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives on the fifth floor.

definitions.note: Dative singular (masculine/neuter) or genitive plural form of the ordinal adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am fünften Tag fahren wir nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the fifth day we’re going to Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin fünfunddreißig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am thirty-five years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin fünfzehn Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fifteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin fünfzig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fifty years old.

definitions.note: Takes the accusative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein Geschenk für meine Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a gift for my mother.

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I fear")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fürchte mich vor Spinnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m afraid of spiders.

definitions.native: to fear; to be afraid of
definitions.note: Often used with an object (etw./jdn. fürchten). Reflexive ‘sich fürchten’ is also common, but the example below uses the exact word form ‘fürchten’ as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Kinder fürchten die Dunkelheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many children fear the dark.

definitions.note: Often used to intensify something negative (similar to “really” or “very”): e.g. „fürchterlich kalt“ = “terribly cold.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine fürchterliche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a terrible idea.

definitions.note: Often used as an intensifier in everyday speech (like “really” or “very”), not only to describe something frightening.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist heute fürchterlich kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is terribly cold today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine fürchterliche Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a terrible night.

definitions.note: Strong negative; often used in everyday speech to mean “awful.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten einen fürchterlichen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a terrible day.

definitions.note: comparative form of „fürchterlich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm war fürchterlicher als wir erwartet hatten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm was more terrible than we had expected.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum fürchtest du dich vor der Prüfung?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you afraid of the exam?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „fürchten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fürchtet die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fears the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fürchtete sich vor dem Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was afraid of the dog.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „fürchten“; often used in written narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fürchteten den Sturm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They feared the storm.

definitions.native: for each other, for one another
definitions.note: Used for mutual actions or relationships; often with verbs like da sein, sorgen, kämpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind immer füreinander da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are always there for each other.

definitions.note: Contraction of „für das“; used with neuter singular „das“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe fürs Wochenende keine Pläne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any plans for the weekend.

definitions.note: Present tense (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich füttere den Hund jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feed the dog every morning.

definitions.note: often used for feeding animals (giving them food)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jeden Morgen muss ich die Katze füttern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning I have to feed the cat.

definitions.note: Used with “du” (2nd person singular, present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du fütterst den Hund jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You feed the dog every morning.

definitions.note: used for feeding animals (or figuratively: giving someone information)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie füttert den Hund jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feeds the dog every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fütterte den Hund jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fed the dog every morning.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „abgeben“; the prefix often appears later in the sentence as „... ab“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gab die Hausaufgaben pünktlich ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He handed in the homework on time.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „aufgeben“ (often with „auf“ later in the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gab das Rauchen auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave up smoking.

definitions.note: Past tense form of „ausgeben“; the separable prefix „aus“ usually appears at the end of the clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gab gestern viel Geld aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spent a lot of money yesterday.

definitions.note: Past tense form of „ausgeben“; the separable prefix „aus“ usually appears at the end of the clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin gab die Blätter aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher handed out the sheets.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „geben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gab mir das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me the book.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „nachgeben“ (Präteritum); often appears as „gab … nach“ in a sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gab schließlich nach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finally gave in.

definitions.note: Past tense form of the separable verb „zugeben“; it is often used with „zu“ later in the sentence (e.g. „Er gab es zu.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gab zu, dass er das Fenster kaputt gemacht hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admitted that he broke the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gabelt die Nudeln auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forks up the noodles.

definitions.note: Often used with “sich”: „Der Weg gabelt sich.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Weg gabelt sich nach dem Dorf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The path forks after the village.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach einer Stunde gaben wir auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After an hour, we gave up.

definitions.note: Often used for turning in homework or an assignment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie gaben ihre Hausaufgaben pünktlich auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They handed in their homework on time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie gaben mir gestern ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me a book yesterday.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix of „zugeben“: „gaben … zu“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie gaben zu, dass sie einen Fehler gemacht hatten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They admitted that they had made a mistake.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person singular (du-form) of „geben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du gabst mir gestern dein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You gave me your book yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past of "gelten"; often used in phrases like "als etwas gelten" (to be considered as something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher galt dieses Gesetz nur für Erwachsene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, this law was valid only for adults.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Film ganz gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the whole movie.

definitions.note: Often used before adjectives to mean “quite/pretty,” usually not as strong as “very.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ganz schön teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s quite expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die ganze Zeit auf dich gewartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited for you the whole time.

definitions.note: Used as an inflected form of „ganz“ before a noun (e.g., after „den“, „die“, „das“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den ganzen Tag gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked the whole day.

definitions.note: Masculine nominative form of „ganz“ used with masculine nouns (e.g., „ein ganzer Tag“ = „a whole day“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein ganzer Tag reicht dafür nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A whole day isn’t enough for that.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter singular noun (e.g. „ein ganzes Jahr“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein ganzes Jahr in Berlin gelebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lived in Berlin for a whole year.

definitions.note: Often used with negation (e.g., „gar nicht“ = “not at all”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gar keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no time at all.

definitions.note: Used for emphasis, often before adjectives/adverbs (e.g., „gar nicht so schlecht“ = “not even that bad”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist gar nicht so schwer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That isn’t even that hard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich garantiere dir, dass ich pünktlich bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guarantee you that I’ll be on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir das Ergebnis nicht garantieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't guarantee you the result.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich garantiere dir: Er kommt pünktlich; das garantiert er.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guarantee you: He’ll be on time; he guarantees it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das klappt garantiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That will definitely work.

definitions.note: Often used with „werden“: „geachtet werden“ = to be respected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird in seiner Gemeinde sehr geachtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very respected in his community.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht geahnt, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t suspect that he was coming today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben am See geangelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fished at the lake.

definitions.note: past participle of "antworten"; used with "haben" in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir gestern nicht geantwortet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t answer you yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „arbeiten“; often used with „haben“ to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern lange gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked for a long time yesterday.

definitions.note: colloquial short form of „gebe“ (e.g. „ich geb …“ instead of „ich gebe …“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich geb dir das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll give you the book.

definitions.note: past participle of „backen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist schon gebacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is already baked.

definitions.note: Past participle of „baden“, used with „haben“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben gestern im See gebadet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went for a swim in the lake yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past of „gebären“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie gebar ein gesundes Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave birth to a healthy child.

definitions.note: past participle of „bauen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus wurde 1900 gebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house was built in 1900.

definitions.note: Often used like a past participle adjective (e.g., describing how something is built).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist gut gebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is well built.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „auf“ (e.g., „Ich gebe nicht auf.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe nicht auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't give up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe dir das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give you the book.

definitions.note: past participle of "beichten" (often used with "haben" in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat dem Priester gebeichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He confessed to the priest.

definitions.note: General meaning: to give (someone something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe dir das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give you the book.

definitions.note: Often interchangeable with “to give” in everyday contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte den Stift geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you hand me the pen, please?

definitions.note: Used for offering/providing something (often abstract or service-like).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schule will den Kindern mehr Unterstützung geben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school wants to provide the children with more support.

definitions.note: “geben” can mean “to produce/amount to” in math/logic or outcomes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zwei und zwei geben vier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two and two make four.

definitions.note: Idiomatic: “eine Party / ein Konzert / einen Empfang geben”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie geben am Samstag eine Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re having a party on Saturday.

definitions.note: Used with the separable-prefix verb „aufgeben“ (e.g. „aufgeben“ → „wir geben auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir geben nicht auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don't give up.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative (indirect object) and an accusative (direct object): jemandem etwas geben.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte das Buch geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please give me the book?

definitions.note: past participle of "bitten"; often used with "haben" in the present perfect (Perfekt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich um Hilfe gebeten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked you for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe für dich gebetet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prayed for you.

definitions.note: Past participle of "bilden"; used in the perfect tense or in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder haben einen Kreis gebildet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children formed a circle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr gebildet und liest viel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very educated and reads a lot.

definitions.note: past participle of „beißen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat mich gebissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog bit me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind hat die ganze Nacht stark geblasen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind blew strongly all night.

definitions.note: Often used with „von“ + a cause (e.g., light): „vom Licht geblendet“. Can be literal or figurative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin vom grellen Licht geblendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am dazzled by the bright light.

definitions.note: Past participle of „bleiben“, typically used with „sein“ in the perfect tense (e.g. „ist geblieben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist zu Hause geblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed at home.

definitions.note: past participle of "bleiben"; often used with "sein" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern zu Hause geblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed at home yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat gestern Nacht stark geblitzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a lot of lightning last night.

definitions.note: past participle of „bluten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde hat stark geblutet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound bled a lot.

definitions.note: Most often used with „sein“ to say when/where someone was born.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in Berlin geboren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was born in Berlin.

definitions.note: past participle of „gebären“; commonly used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist geboren“ = „was born“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in Berlin geboren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was born in Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used before a feminine noun (e.g., “eine geborene …”). In names, “geborene” can mean “née” (maiden name).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine geborene Berlinerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a born Berliner.

definitions.note: Often used with a place name (e.g. „geborener Berliner“ = born in Berlin).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist geborener Berliner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was born in Berlin.

definitions.note: past participle of „borgen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „ich habe … geborgt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir ein Buch geborgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I borrowed a book.

definitions.note: In some contexts, „borgen“ can also mean „to lend“ (giving something to someone temporarily).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir zehn Euro geborgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lent me ten euros.

definitions.note: past participle of "bringen"; used with "haben" to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir einen Kaffee gebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought you a coffee.

definitions.note: Often used about lights/candles to mean they were on (e.g., „Das Licht hat gebrannt.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht hat die ganze Nacht gebrannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light was on all night.

definitions.note: past participle of „braten“; often used like an adjective (e.g. „gebratener Fisch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fisch ist in der Pfanne gebraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fish is fried in the pan.

definitions.note: Usually used to describe cooked food (from the verb „braten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse gern gebratenes Hähnchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like eating fried chicken.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of using something (up) or making practical use of it; less common than "benutzen" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann diesen Schlüssel noch gebrauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can still use this key.

definitions.note: Often used a bit more formally than "benutzen"; common in phrases like "können ... gebrauchen" (= could use).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann deine Hilfe gut gebrauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I could really use your help.

definitions.note: Often used with „werden“: „gebraucht werden“ = to be needed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde hier gebraucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am needed here.

definitions.note: Common when talking about items that are not new.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Fahrrad ist gebraucht, aber noch gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bike is used, but still good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein gebrauchtes Fahrrad gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a used bicycle.

definitions.note: Often used with things you buy (e.g., a used car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine gebrauchte Jacke gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a used jacket.

definitions.note: past participle of „brechen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir den Arm gebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I broke my arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Arm ist gebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My arm is broken.

definitions.note: often used as an adjective (from the verb „brechen“ = to break)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die gebrochene Vase liegt auf dem Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The broken vase is lying on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kam mit gebrochenem Arm ins Krankenhaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came to the hospital with a broken arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich den gebrochenen Arm eingegipst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had his broken arm put in a cast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein gebrochener Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a broken man.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) present tense of „geben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gebt ihr mir bitte das Buch?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you (plural) please give me the book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein Hotelzimmer gebucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I booked a hotel room.

definitions.note: Slang/vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie haben gestern Nacht gebumst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They banged last night.

definitions.note: Past participle of „binden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Paket mit einer Schnur fest gebunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tied the package tightly with a string.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist am Baum gebunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is tied to the tree.

definitions.note: Used for books: „ein gebundenes Buch“ = a hardcover book.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe das Buch lieber gebunden als als Taschenbuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer to buy the book in hardcover rather than as a paperback.

definitions.note: past participle of „bügeln“, usually about clothes
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Hemd schon gebügelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already ironed my shirt.

definitions.native: is due (to someone), is owed (to someone)
definitions.note: Often used in fairly formal phrases like „Dir gebührt Dank/Respekt.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dir gebührt unser Dank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are owed our thanks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe an dich gedacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought of you.

definitions.note: Often used to say something was (not) intended, e.g. "So war das nicht gedacht."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So war das nicht gedacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s not how it was meant/intended.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g. „Das ist so nicht gedacht.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist nicht so gedacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s not intended like that.

definitions.note: past participle of „danken“, used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir für deine Hilfe gedankt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thanked you for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat länger gedauert als erwartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That took longer than expected.

definitions.note: Past participle of „decken“; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist gedeckt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist schon gedeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is already set (covered).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist mit einem Tuch gedeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is covered with a cloth.

definitions.note: Often used to describe colors or lighting that are not bright.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt heute eine gedeckte Farbe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s wearing a muted color today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Vorfall fühlte sie sich gedemütigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the incident, she felt humiliated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fühlte sich vor allen Leuten gedemütigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt humiliated in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Often used in formal language (e.g., ceremonies); commonly with the genitive (e.g., „der Opfer“) or with „an + Akk.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gedenke heute der Opfer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we commemorate the victims.

definitions.note: Formal/literary; often used with an infinitive clause (e.g., „… zu gehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gedenke morgen früher zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I intend to leave earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (memorials, ceremonies) and commonly takes the genitive case (e.g., „der Opfer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gedenken der Opfer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We commemorate the victims.

definitions.note: Rather formal/literary; often used with „an“ (e.g. „gedenkst du an …?“) or with the genitive in more formal German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gedenkst du an die Opfer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you remember the victims?

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts; commonly with the genitive (e.g. „der Opfer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gedenkt der Opfer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He commemorates the victims.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das habe ich anders gedeutet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I interpreted that differently.

definitions.note: Past participle of „dienen“. Often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat gedient“), and commonly in the sense of serving in the military.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat in der Armee gedient.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He served in the army.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Schlüssel im Schloss gedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned the key in the lock.

definitions.note: Used for making a film/video (e.g., a movie scene).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Szene wurde in Berlin gedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The scene was filmed in Berlin.

definitions.note: Past participle of „drohen“, often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir gedroht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has threatened me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch ist schon gedruckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is already printed.

definitions.note: past participle of „drücken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Knopf gedrückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pressed the button.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „sich gedulden“ (= to be patient / to wait).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann so ein Verhalten nicht gedulden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t tolerate that kind of behavior.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin geduldig und warte hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am patient and I’ll wait here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte warte geduldig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait patiently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss geduldiger sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to be more patient.

definitions.note: Past participle of "duschen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "Ich habe geduscht.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute Morgen geduscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I showered this morning.

definitions.note: Very formal; often used in polite address in letters/speeches (e.g., „Geehrter Herr …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geehrter Herr Müller, vielen Dank für Ihre Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Mr. Müller, thank you very much for your message.

definitions.note: Often used with „für“ (for) or „zu“ (for/to) to say something is suitable for a purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Schuhe sind nicht für den Winter geeignet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes aren't suitable for winter.

definitions.note: inflected form used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine geeignete Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a suitable solution.

definitions.note: Often used with „sich“: „sich auf etwas einigen“ = to agree on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben uns auf einen Termin geeinigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed on a date.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Haus von meiner Oma geerbt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I inherited the house from my grandma.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Äpfel sind schon geerntet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apples have already been harvested.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form, used with plural subjects and with formal "Sie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fuhren gestern nach Berlin, aber sie sind nicht mitgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drove to Berlin yesterday, but they didn’t come along.

definitions.note: Past participle (Partizip II), used to form the perfect tense (usually with "sein").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch nie so schnell gefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have never driven that fast.

definitions.note: Used with a dative pronoun (mir/dir/ihm …): e.g. „Ich gefalle dir“ literally means “I please you,” i.e. “you like me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, ich gefalle dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like me.

definitions.note: past participle of "fallen" (used with "sein")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern die Treppe hinunter gefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell down the stairs yesterday.

definitions.note: Literally “to please”; the person who likes something is in the dative (e.g. „Das gefällt mir.“ = “I like that.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das könnte dir gefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You might like that.

definitions.note: often used to refer to soldiers who died in war (e.g., „gefallene Soldaten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gedenken der gefallenen Soldaten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We commemorate the fallen soldiers.

definitions.note: Usually written with an umlaut: „gefällt“. Often used with a dative pronoun (mir/dir/ihm …): „Das gefallt mir.“ = “I like that.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kleid gefallt mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the dress.

definitions.note: past participle of „fangen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Ball gefangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I caught the ball.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g., „gefangen sein“ = to be trapped).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vogel ist im Käfig gefangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird is trapped in the cage.

definitions.note: past participle of "fassen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Ball gefasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He caught the ball.

definitions.note: often used with "bleiben/sein" (e.g. "gefasst bleiben")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie blieb trotz der schlechten Nachricht gefasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She stayed calm despite the bad news.

definitions.note: Often used with „bleiben“ or „sein“ to mean staying calm in a difficult situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trotz der schlechten Nachricht blieb sie gefasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the bad news, she stayed calm.

definitions.note: often used to describe someone staying in control, especially in a difficult situation
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trotz der schlechten Nachricht blieb er gefasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the bad news, he remained composed.

definitions.note: past participle of "fegen"; used with "haben" (e.g., "hat ... gefegt") or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern die Küche gefegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swept the kitchen yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "fehlen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "Du hast mir gefehlt" = "I missed you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast mir sehr gefehlt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really missed you.

definitions.note: past participle of "feiern"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "Wir haben ... gefeiert").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben gestern ihren Geburtstag gefeiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We celebrated her birthday yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „fertigen“ (often used with „haben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma hat die Teile in Deutschland gefertigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company manufactured the parts in Germany.

definitions.note: Past participle of "fesseln"; often used like an adjective meaning someone is physically restrained.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann war an den Stuhl gefesselt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was tied to the chair.

definitions.note: Often used literally for someone whose hands/feet are tied; also used figuratively meaning “captivated/fascinated.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann war an Händen und Füßen gefesselt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was tied up hand and foot.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean someone was dismissed from their job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef hat ihn gestern gefeuert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss fired him yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat in die Luft gefeuert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police fired into the air.

definitions.note: Very vulgar. Can refer to sex or (more often in everyday speech) being in serious trouble.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Geld sind wir echt gefickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without money, we're really screwed.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative pronoun (e.g., mir/dir/ihm): something ‘pleased’ someone = someone liked something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film gefiel mir sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the movie a lot.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of "gefallen" (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das würde mir besser gefallen, aber das hier gefiele mir auch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like that better, but I would like this one too.

definitions.note: Used with dative (e.g., „Das gefiel mir“ = “I liked that,” literally “That pleased me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Farben gefielen mir sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the colors a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film wurde in Berlin gefilmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was filmed in Berlin.

definitions.note: past participle of „fischen“ (often used with „haben“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben gestern im See gefischt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fished in the lake yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of „flicken“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Hose geflickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I patched/mended the pants.

definitions.note: past participle of "fliegen"; used with "sein" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind nach Berlin geflogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have flown to Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist aus dem Land geflohen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fled the country.

definitions.note: past participle of „fliehen“, usually used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist geflohen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist aus dem Land geflohen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fled the country.

definitions.note: past participle of „folgen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist … gefolgt“) or in phrases like „gefolgt von …“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist mir nach Hause gefolgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog followed me home.

definitions.note: past participle of "foltern"; often used with "werden" (passive) or "haben" (perfect)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde im Gefängnis gefoltert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was tortured in prison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn gefragt, ob er morgen Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked him whether he has time tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Schuhe sind gerade sehr gefragt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are very much in demand right now.

definitions.note: Usually used for animals (for people it can sound rude or joking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat das Fleisch gefressen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog ate the meat.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive verb "sich freuen" (e.g., "Ich habe mich gefreut" = "I was glad").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich sehr gefreut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was very glad.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of „gefrieren“; often used for weather or liquids turning to ice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dieser Kälte gefriert das Wasser sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this cold, the water freezes immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht gefror der See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the night, the lake froze.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der See ist über Nacht gefroren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lake froze overnight.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to describe something that has frozen (e.g. water, ground).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der See ist komplett gefroren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lake is completely frozen.

definitions.note: past participle of „frühstücken“; commonly used with „haben“ in the Perfekt tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe schon gefrühstückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already had breakfast.

definitions.note: past participle of „finden“; often used with „haben“ to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Schlüssel gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys.

definitions.note: colloquial/vulgar
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat im Aufzug gefurzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He farted in the elevator.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Rauchen kann deine Gesundheit gefährden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoking can endanger your health.

definitions.note: often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist gefährdet“) to say someone/something is at risk
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die kleine Firma ist durch die Krise gefährdet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The small company is endangered because of the crisis.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Weg ist nachts sehr gefährlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This path is very dangerous at night.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (weak/mixed/strong declension depending on context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine gefährliche Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a dangerous street.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (weak/mixed/strong declension, depending on the article and case)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben den gefährlichen Hund gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw the dangerous dog.

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adjective „gefährlich“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Weg ist nachts gefährlicher als am Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This path is more dangerous at night than during the day.

definitions.note: Used here as an inflected form of the adjective before a neuter noun (e.g., „ein gefährliches Tier“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein gefährliches Tier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a dangerous animal.

definitions.note: superlative form of „gefährlich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die gefährlichste Straße in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the most dangerous street in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die gefährlichsten Straßen der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the most dangerous streets in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Musik ist gefällig, aber nicht besonders spannend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music is pleasant, but not especially exciting.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „Wärst du so gefällig …?“ to make a request sound very polite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wärst du so gefällig und machst das Fenster zu?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you be so kind as to close the window?

definitions.note: Often used in polite or formal language (e.g. in polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kellner war sehr gefällig und hat uns sofort geholfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter was very helpful and helped us right away.

definitions.note: Used to make a strong, often annoyed or commanding request; can sound rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm gefälligst sofort her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here right now, please!

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "gefallen"; the thing that is liked is the grammatical subject in German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du gefällst mir sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like you a lot.

definitions.note: past participle of „fällen“, used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat … gefällt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann hat den Baum gefällt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man cut down the tree.

definitions.note: Used in the pattern „X gefällt mir“ = “I like X” (literally “X pleases me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film gefällt mir sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the movie a lot.

definitions.note: Used with a dative person: „Mir gefällt …“ = “I like …” (literally: “... pleases me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir gefällt das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the book.

definitions.note: Used for things like documents, money, or branded goods that are not genuine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Pass ist gefälscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The passport is forged.

definitions.note: often used for goods, documents, money, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine gefälschte Uhr gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a counterfeit watch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wolle ist blau gefärbt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wool is dyed blue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich heute besser gefühlt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt better today.

definitions.note: past participle of „führen“, often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat geführt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die Gruppe durch die Stadt geführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He led the group through the city.

definitions.note: past participle of „füllen“; often used with „sein“ to describe something as filled
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Flasche ist mit Wasser gefüllt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is filled with water.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (it’s the past participle of "füllen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Flasche ist mit Wasser gefüllt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is filled with water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein gefürchteter Gegner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a feared opponent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze ist schon gefüttert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat has already been fed.

definitions.note: Used especially for clothing (e.g., a jacket lined with warm material).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jacke ist warm gefüttert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jacket is warmly lined.

definitions.note: Past participle of "gehen"; used with "sein" to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nach Hause gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have gone home.

definitions.note: past participle of gehen; typically used with sein to form the present perfect (e.g., ich bin gegangen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern früh nach Hause gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went home early yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „geben“; used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir das Buch gegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have given you the book.

definitions.note: Often used with the accusative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind gegen den Vorschlag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are against the proposal.

definitions.note: Used to give an approximate time; typically with the accusative (e.g., gegen 8 Uhr).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme gegen acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll come around eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Mannschaften spielen heute gegeneinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two teams are playing against each other today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir helfen uns gegenseitig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We help each other.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gegenwärtig arbeite ich in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m currently working in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used with the dative case and can come before or after the noun/pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bank ist gegenüber der Post.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank is opposite the post office.

definitions.note: Used for position/location; often with dative (e.g. „gegenüber dem Haus“ = opposite the house).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Supermarkt ist gegenüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supermarket is opposite (across from here).

definitions.note: used for something located across from something else (e.g., on the other side of the street)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf der gegenüberliegenden Straßenseite ist ein Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a café on the opposite side of the street.

definitions.note: past participle of "essen"; used with "haben" to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe schon gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already eaten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir geglaubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believed you.

definitions.note: past participle of „graben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern ein Loch gegraben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dug a hole yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma wurde 1998 gegründet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company was founded in 1998.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ihn freundlich gegrüßt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We greeted him kindly.

definitions.note: past participle of "gucken" (often used with "haben"); informal/colloquial for "sehen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen Film geguckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched a movie.

definitions.note: Imperative form (informal singular) of „gehen“: used to tell one person to go.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh nach Hause!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go home!

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (telling one person: “go!”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte nach Hause!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go home!

definitions.note: past participle of "haben"; used with "haben" to form the present perfect and past perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit gehabt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I haven't had any time.

definitions.note: Often used for computers/accounts (e.g., a website or account was hacked).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein E-Mail-Konto wurde gehackt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My email account was hacked.

definitions.note: Used for food (e.g., nuts, herbs, onions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zwiebel ist schon gehackt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The onion is already chopped.

definitions.note: past participle of "halten"; often used with "haben" to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Tür für sie gehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I held the door for her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat schnell gehandelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He acted quickly.

definitions.note: Used when talking about trading (e.g., stocks, goods): „mit etw. handeln“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat mit Aktien gehandelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She traded stocks.

definitions.note: past participle of „hassen“; used in the present perfect and as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn lange gehasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have hated him for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Ball zu fest gehauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hit the ball too hard.

definitions.note: often used for chopping wood or cutting down a tree
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie haben den Baum im Garten gehauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They chopped down the tree in the garden.

definitions.note: Older spelling with ß; modern spelling is usually "gehasst".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fühlte sich von allen gehaßt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt hated by everyone.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ausgehen“; the prefix „aus“ usually comes at the end: „Ich gehe … aus.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe heute Abend aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going out tonight.

definitions.note: first-person singular present tense of „gehen“ (ich gehe)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe heute zu Fuß zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to work on foot today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde ist geheilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound is healed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück ist die Wunde schnell geheilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, the wound healed quickly.

definitions.note: often used with „(ein) geheimer …“ or „im Geheimen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein geheimer Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a secret plan.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., "eine geheime ...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie arbeitet an einer geheimen Mission.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is working on a secret mission.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie treffen sich an einem geheimen Ort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They meet in a secret place.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun (or nominalized form) in this inflected form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat ein geheimes Treffen geplant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He planned a secret meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die Überraschung lange geheimgehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept the surprise secret for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fremde wirkt geheimnisvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stranger seems mysterious.

definitions.note: adjective inflected form of "geheimnisvoll"; often used before a noun (e.g., "eine geheimnisvolle Person")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eine geheimnisvolle Frau steht vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A mysterious woman is standing at the door.

definitions.note: Used as an infinitive with „zu“ (e.g. after verbs like „versuchen“, „bitten“, „vergessen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, den Plan geheimzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to keep the plan secret.

definitions.note: past participle of „heiraten“; used with „sein“ in the Perfekt (e.g., „Ich bin … geheiratet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind letztes Jahr geheiratet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got married last year.

definitions.note: Past participle of „heißen“; commonly used to talk about what someone/something was called (e.g. in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat früher Hans geheißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used to be called Hans.

definitions.note: Often used for going somewhere on foot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go now.

definitions.note: Common, basic verb; often used for going somewhere on foot, but also broadly for ‘go’ in many contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to go now.

definitions.native: to function; to work (of devices, systems)
definitions.note: Used especially in questions/negations about whether something works.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy will nicht gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone won’t work.

definitions.note: Often used when someone is about to head out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go (I have to leave).

definitions.native: to be acceptable; to be okay (that works)
definitions.note: Colloquial: expresses that something is fine/acceptable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Für mich kann das so gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That can work for me / That’s fine with me.

definitions.note: In phrases like ‘Wie geht es weiter?’ (How does it continue?).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie wird es weiter gehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How will it go on? / What happens next?

definitions.note: Often implies going on foot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to go now.

definitions.note: Most commonly used in the phrase „nicht geheuer“ (= something doesn’t seem right).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sache ist mir nicht geheuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something about it seems suspicious to me.

definitions.note: often implies crying loudly or for a long time
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die ganze Nacht geweint und dann noch mehr geheult.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cried all night and then howled/wailed even more.

definitions.note: used for animals (e.g., wolves) or the wind
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind hat die ganze Nacht geheult.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind howled all night.

definitions.note: colloquial/spoken short form of „gehen“ (often used in speech and informal writing)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt gehn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Koffer vom Boden gehoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lifted the suitcase off the floor.

definitions.note: past participle of "hoffen"; often used with "haben" to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gehofft, dass du heute kommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hoped that you would come today.

definitions.note: past participle of "helfen"; commonly used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir gestern geholfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I helped you yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "holen"; often used with "haben" to form the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich vom Bahnhof geholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked you up from the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehorche dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I obey you.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative (jemandem gehorchen = to obey someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder müssen ihren Eltern gehorchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children have to obey their parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gehorcht seiner Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He obeys his mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat gehorcht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He obeyed.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative (jemandem gehorchen = to obey someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund gehorchte seinem Besitzer sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog obeyed its owner immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist gehorsam und hört auf seinen Besitzer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is obedient and listens to its owner.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „gehen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gehst du heute zu Fuß zur Schule?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you walking to school today?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „angehen“: the prefix „an“ often appears later in the sentence (e.g. „geht … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht geht an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light turns on.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufgehen“; in a sentence, „auf“ often comes at the end (e.g., „geht … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür geht auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door opens.

definitions.note: From the verb „aufgehen“ (used for the sun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne geht auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun rises.

definitions.note: From the verb „ausgehen“ (e.g., to go out in the evening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er geht heute Abend mit Freunden aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s going out with friends this evening.

definitions.note: Used with „eingehen“ for things like letters, orders, applications, payments, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zahlung geht heute ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The payment is received today.

definitions.note: Often seen in common phrases like „Wie geht’s?“ (“How are you?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er geht heute zur Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes to school today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er geht nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is going home.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „los“ (e.g., „geht … los“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug geht um 8 Uhr los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train leaves at 8 o'clock.

definitions.note: With the separable verb „umgehen“ (um-): „... geht ... um“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Gerücht geht in der Stadt um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A rumor is going around in the city.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix: „geht … unter“ (from „untergehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne geht um 20 Uhr unter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun sets at 8 p.m.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix of „vorgehen“ (e.g. „geht … vor“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er geht Schritt für Schritt vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He proceeds step by step.

definitions.note: Colloquial contraction of „geht es“ (often written „geht's“), used in phrases like „Wie gehts?“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie gehts dir heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die ganze Nacht gehustet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He coughed all night.

definitions.note: Past participle of „hängen“ when used with an object (e.g., hanging something up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Bild an die Wand gehängt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hung the picture on the wall.

definitions.note: past participle of „hänseln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Schule wurde er oft gehänselt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school, he was often teased.

definitions.note: Not standard in written German; a colloquial/dialect shortening of „gehört“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas gehör nicht hierher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something like that doesn’t belong here.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "gehören" (often used with "zu" or a dative pronoun to express belonging/being part of something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch gehört mir nicht; es ist nicht meins, also gehöre ich nicht dazu, es zu behalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book doesn’t belong to me; it’s not mine, so I’m not meant to keep it.

definitions.note: Often used with "zu" + dative: "zu mir/dir/ihm/ihr/uns/euch/ihnen gehören".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch kann nur dir gehören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book can only belong to you.

definitions.native: be one of, be part of
definitions.note: Often used with "zu" + dative to say someone/something is part of a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss zu unserem Team gehören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He must be part of our team.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "gehören".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du gehörst zu unserer Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You belong to our family.

definitions.note: Used to express that something belongs to someone (e.g., "Das gehört dir" = "That is yours").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch gehörst du aber nicht, oder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: But that book isn’t yours, is it?

definitions.note: Often used with "zu" + dative (e.g., "Das gehört mir." / "Das gehört zu ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch gehört meiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book belongs to my sister.

definitions.note: Past participle of "hören" (to hear), not "gehören".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Geräusch schon gehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already heard the noise.

definitions.note: past participle of hören (used to form the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du das schon gehört?
