definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you heard that already?

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „gehören“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch gehörte mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book belonged to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bücher gehörten meiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books belonged to my sister.

definitions.note: Informal; can also mean “horny” depending on context, so be careful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war echt geil!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really awesome!

definitions.note: Informal; can sound crude in many situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist total geil auf sie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is really horny for her.

definitions.note: Informal/slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein geiles Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s an awesome game.

definitions.note: Vulgar/sexual meaning; can be offensive in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schreibt ihr ständig geiles Zeug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s constantly texting her horny stuff.

definitions.note: often used with „gegen“ + accusative (e.g., gegen Grippe) or „gegen“ + disease name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gegen Grippe geimpft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am vaccinated against the flu.

definitions.note: Past participle of "impfen"; often used with "sein" (e.g., "Ich bin geimpft") or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gegen Grippe geimpft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am vaccinated against the flu.

definitions.note: Past participle of „irren“; often used with „sich“ (e.g., „sich geirrt haben“ = to have been mistaken).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich geirrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was mistaken.

definitions.note: Often perceived as old-fashioned or offensive; in modern German, more neutral terms like "psychisch krank" are common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gilt als geisteskrank und braucht Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is considered mentally ill and needs help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute geistig müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m mentally tired today.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “spiritual” rather than “religious.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fühlt sich geistig mit der Natur verbunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels spiritually connected to nature.

definitions.note: Can also mean “spiritual” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Regelmäßiger Schlaf ist wichtig für die geistige Gesundheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Regular sleep is important for mental health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine geistreiche Antwort gegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gave a witty answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist so geizig, dass er nicht einmal Trinkgeld gibt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is so stingy that he doesn’t even leave a tip.

definitions.note: past participle of „jagen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat die Katze gejagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chased the cat.

definitions.note: past participle of "kennen" (to know someone/something, be familiar with)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn schon lange gekannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had known him for a long time.

definitions.note: Past participle of "kaufen"; often used with "haben" to form the past (perfect) tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern ein neues Fahrrad gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new bike yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „kauen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das Brot lange gekaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He chewed the bread for a long time.

definitions.note: Used mainly for boats/ships (also possible for small craft like canoes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Boot ist im Sturm gekentert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat capsized in the storm.

definitions.note: past participle of „kidnappen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind ist gestern gekidnappt worden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child was kidnapped yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “Es hat geklappt” = “It worked (out).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, es hat geklappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, it worked out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stuhl ist schon zusammengeklappt, aber die Tür hat nicht richtig geklappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair is already folded up, but the door didn’t fold/close properly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Konzert haben alle laut geklatscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, everyone clapped loudly.

definitions.note: past participle of "klauen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat ... geklaut").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand hat mein Fahrrad geklaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone stole my bike.

definitions.note: Often used with an adverb like „gut/schlecht/elegant gekleidet“ (well/poorly/elegantly dressed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war elegant gekleidet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was dressed elegantly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind auf den Baum geklettert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We climbed up the tree.

definitions.note: Past participle of „klingeln“, often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat an der Tür geklingelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone rang the doorbell.

definitions.note: past participle of „klopfen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand hat an der Tür geklopft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone knocked on the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Situation ist jetzt geklärt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is clarified now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Problem ist geklärt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem is resolved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nuss ist schon geknackt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nut is already cracked open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Passwort geknackt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cracked the password.

definitions.note: past participle of „kneifen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der kleine Junge hat mich in den Arm gekniffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little boy pinched me on the arm.

definitions.note: colloquial; past participle of „kneifen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat am Ende doch gekniffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, he chickened out.

definitions.note: past participle of „kochen“; often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern Pasta gekocht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cooked pasta yesterday.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective with neuter singular endings (e.g., before a neuter noun like „Gemüse“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse gekochtes Gemüse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat cooked vegetables.

definitions.note: Past participle of „kommen“, usually used with „sein“ in the perfect tense (e.g., „ist gekommen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern spät gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came late yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "können", used with "haben" (e.g., "hat gekonnt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es nicht gekonnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn’t do it.

definitions.note: past participle of „kosten“ (used in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat mich viel Zeit gekostet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That cost me a lot of time.

definitions.note: Informal/vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist im Auto schlecht geworden, und ich habe gekotzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got sick in the car, and I threw up.

definitions.note: Past participle of „kratzen“ (to scratch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich am Arm gekratzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I scratched my arm.

definitions.note: Past participle of "kriegen"; in everyday German it’s very common, often instead of "bekommen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen Brief von ihr gekriegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a letter from her.

definitions.note: Often used for feeling emotionally hurt (e.g., by a remark or behavior).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war gekränkt, weil er sie nicht eingeladen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was offended because he didn’t invite her.

definitions.note: past participle of „kämpfen“; used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben lange für unsere Rechte gekämpft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fought for our rights for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive verb phrase „sich kümmern (um)“ (= to take care of / look after).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich um die Kinder gekümmert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took care of the children.

definitions.note: Past participle of „kündigen“; often used with „haben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern gekündigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I quit yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of „kündigen“; often used in passive sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag wurde gekündigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract was terminated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich geküsst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kissed you.

definitions.note: past participle of "küssen" (used in perfect tenses and passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe sie gestern geküßt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kissed her yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „lachen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben viel gelacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We laughed a lot.

definitions.note: Often used like a past participle adjective (from „laden“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der LKW ist schon geladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is already loaded.

definitions.note: Past participle of „laden“; used in the present perfect and as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der LKW ist schon geladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck is already loaded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug ist pünktlich gelandet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane landed on time.

definitions.note: Simple past of "gelingen"; often used with "es" as the subject ("Es gelang mir, ..." = "I managed to ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gelang mir, das Problem schnell zu lösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I managed to solve the problem quickly.

definitions.native: to reach; to get to; to come to (a place/state)
definitions.note: Often used with “zu” (to) or set phrases like “zur Ansicht gelangen” (to come into view) and “in die Hände gelangen” (to fall into someone’s hands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie kann dieses Foto in die Zeitung gelangen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How can this photo get into the newspaper?

definitions.note: Often used with a destination or goal (e.g. „gelangt nach …“, „gelangt zu …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie gelangt man am schnellsten zum Bahnhof?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you get to the train station the fastest?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute im Unterricht total gelangweilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m totally bored in class today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute im Unterricht sehr gelangweilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very bored in class today.

definitions.note: adjective in an inflected form (e.g., after an article or with plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die gelangweilten Schüler schauen auf die Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bored students are looking at the clock.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who stays composed and doesn’t get stressed easily.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trotz des Stresses blieb sie gelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the stress, she stayed calm.

definitions.note: past participle of „lassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Schlüssel zu Hause gelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my key at home.

definitions.note: Past participle of „laufen“, usually used with „sein“ in the present perfect (e.g. „ich bin … gelaufen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern nach Hause gelaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran home yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used with an adverb like „gut“ or „schlecht“ (e.g., „gut gelaunt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute bin ich gut gelaunt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm in a good mood.

definitions.note: Past participle of "lauschen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat gelauscht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe an der Tür gelauscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listened at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Banane ist gelb.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The banana is yellow.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with a feminine singular noun: „die gelbe …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage heute die gelbe Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing the yellow jacket today.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a masculine noun in the accusative (e.g., „den gelben …“), or after certain determiners (e.g., „keinen gelben …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den gelben Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the yellow bus.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a masculine noun, often without an article (e.g., „gelber Wagen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gelber Sand liegt am Strand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yellow sand lies on the beach.

definitions.note: comparative form of „gelb“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Banane ist gelber als die andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This banana is more yellow than the other one.

definitions.note: Past participle of "leben"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe zehn Jahre in Berlin gelebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lived in Berlin for ten years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat meine Hand geleckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog licked my hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Flasche geleert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I emptied the bottle.

definitions.note: often used in phrases like „gut gelegen“ (well located)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wohnung ist sehr zentral gelegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment is very centrally located.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" to say where something is (e.g. "Das Hotel ist zentral gelegen.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel ist zentral gelegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is centrally located.

definitions.note: past participle of „liegen“; very commonly used with „sein“ to describe where something is (e.g. „Das Hotel ist zentral gelegen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel ist zentral gelegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is centrally located.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe gelegentlich ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I occasionally go to the movies.

definitions.note: past participle of „legen“, often used with „haben“ (perfect tense) or in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch auf den Tisch gelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book on the table.

definitions.note: past participle of „lehren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das wird in der Schule gelehrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is taught in school.

definitions.note: Past participle of "leisten"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat ... geleistet").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat hervorragende Arbeit geleistet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She accomplished excellent work.

definitions.note: past participle of "lernen"; commonly used with "haben" to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute viel gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned a lot today.

definitions.note: past participle of "lernen"; used with "haben" in the perfect tense and as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe viel gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned a lot.

definitions.note: past participle of „lesen“ (used for the perfect tense and passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch schon gelesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already read the book.

definitions.note: past participle of „lieben“; used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense, and as an adjective meaning “beloved.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich lange geliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I loved you for a long time.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (e.g., feminine nominative/accusative: „meine geliebte Schwester“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine geliebte Schwester wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My beloved sister lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective before a noun; often means “dear” in an affectionate sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besuche meinen geliebten Bruder am Wochenende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m visiting my beloved brother this weekend.

definitions.note: Used as an inflected form of the adjective/participle meaning “beloved.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besuche meinen geliebten Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m visiting my beloved brother.

definitions.note: past participle of „liefern“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat geliefert“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Paket wurde gestern geliefert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package was delivered yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir ein Buch geliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I borrowed a book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihm mein Fahrrad geliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lent him my bike.

definitions.note: Intransitive verb; commonly used with a dative person (e.g., "Mir gelingt es ..."), or as a noun phrase (e.g., "Das Gelingen ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gelingt mir, den Termin zu verschieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I manage to reschedule the appointment.

definitions.note: Used to say that something succeeds/works out (often with “es”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gelingt mir heute nicht, pünktlich zu kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t manage to arrive on time today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sehr gelitten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suffered a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer hat sie für ihre Arbeit gelobt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher praised her for her work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gelobte, vorsichtiger zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He promised to be more careful.

definitions.note: Often used about rules/restrictions being made less strict.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regeln wurden gelockert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rules were relaxed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anzeige hat viele Kunden gelockt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ad lured many customers.

definitions.note: Literally the past participle of „lügen“ (“to lie”), often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine gelogene Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a made-up (false) story.

definitions.note: past participle of „lügen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich angelogen und dann gesagt, er habe nicht gelogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lied to me and then said he hadn’t lied.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich lohnen" (e.g. "Das hat sich gelohnt." = "That was worth it.")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Aufwand hat sich gelohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The effort was worth it.

definitions.note: Often used with time limits ("bis" + date/time) or in rules/agreements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fahrschein kann nur gelten, wenn er entwertet wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket can only be valid if it has been validated.

definitions.note: Often used with "für" in the pattern "Das kann für ... gelten" (That can apply to ...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Regel kann auch für Kinder gelten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This rule can also apply to children.

definitions.note: Past participle of "gelingen" (used like “turned out well”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan ist gelungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan was successful.

definitions.note: Past participle of „lächeln“; used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat mich angelächelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She smiled at me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall war sein Bein gelähmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, his leg was paralyzed.

definitions.note: past participle of „läuten“; used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat geläutet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Telefon hat die ganze Nacht geläutet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone rang all night.

definitions.note: past participle of „löschen“; often used for files, messages, or data
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die E-Mail gelöscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deleted the email.

definitions.note: past participle of „löschen“; used for fires, candles, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr hat das Feuer gelöscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department extinguished the fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Problem ist gelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem is solved.

definitions.note: Often used with „in“ (e.g., „im Wasser gelöst“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Salz ist im Wasser gelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salt is dissolved in the water.

definitions.note: Describes a person’s mood/attitude (calm, not tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Urlaub bin ich ganz gelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the vacation I feel completely relaxed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Problem ist gelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem is solved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Knoten ist gelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knot is loosened/untied.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective; it’s also the past participle of "machen" (to do/make).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Hausaufgaben sind schon gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The homework is already done.

definitions.note: Past participle of „machen“, used in the present perfect (with „haben“) and in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das schon gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already done that.

definitions.note: past participle of "malen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat gemalt")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern ein Bild gemalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I painted a picture yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s behavior as nasty or unkind.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war gemein von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was mean of you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine gemeine Bemerkung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a mean remark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine gemeine Pflanze in dieser Region.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a common plant in this region.

definitions.note: Used to describe someone’s behavior or words as unkind or nasty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag seine gemeinen Kommentare nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like his mean comments.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „gemein“ when describing someone’s unkind behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist heute gemeiner als sonst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is meaner than usual today.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive) to mean “common” in the sense of “typical/ordinary.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein gemeiner Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a common mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen das gemeinsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll do that together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir lernen gemeinsam für die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re studying together for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben viel gemeinsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a lot in common.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (declined); often appears in phrases like „gemeinsame Freunde“ (mutual friends).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben gemeinsame Freunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have mutual friends.

definitions.note: used before a noun (inflected form of „gemeinsam“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben einen gemeinsamen Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a mutual friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ein gemeinsames Ziel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a common goal.

definitions.note: Often used like a predicate, e.g. "so gemeint" = "meant like that"; from the verb "meinen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war nicht so gemeint.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That wasn’t meant like that.

definitions.note: past participle of "meinen"; often used with "sein" (e.g., "ist gemeint")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie ist das gemeint?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How is that meant?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vorfall wurde der Polizei gemeldet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The incident was reported to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich für den Kurs gemeldet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I signed up for the course.

definitions.note: Past participle of „merken“, often used with „haben“ (e.g., „ich habe … gemerkt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe sofort gemerkt, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed right away that something isn't right.

definitions.note: past participle of "messen"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Temperatur gemessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I measured the temperature.

definitions.note: Past participle of „mieten“; often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern ein Auto gemietet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rented a car yesterday.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „gemischt“ (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern eine gemischte Pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a mixed pizza.

definitions.note: past participle of „mögen“ (used with „haben“ in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Film wirklich gemocht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really liked the movie.

definitions.note: past participle of „melken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Kuh heute Morgen gemolken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I milked the cow this morning.

definitions.note: Past participle of "morden". In everyday German, "ermorden/ermordet" is more common when talking about murdering a specific person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Täter hat drei Menschen gemordet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrator murdered three people.

definitions.note: past participle of "mähen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rasen ist schon gemäht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawn has already been mowed.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative (e.g., gemäß dem Gesetz).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gemäß dem Vertrag müssen wir bis Freitag liefern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the contract, we have to deliver by Friday.

definitions.note: Often describes a warm, relaxed, friendly atmosphere (e.g., a room, café, evening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die kleine Wohnung ist sehr gemütlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The small apartment is very cozy.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a warm, relaxed, pleasant atmosphere (not just physical comfort).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sitzen gemütlich auf dem Sofa und trinken Tee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re sitting comfortably on the sofa and drinking tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Café ist gemütlicher als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This café is cozier than the other one.

definitions.note: Used with the dative, often in fixed phrases (e.g., gen Norden). Somewhat formal or literary compared to "nach".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fahren gen Süden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re driving south.

definitions.note: Past participle of "nennen"; often used like an adjective (e.g., "so genannt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird Thomas genannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is called Thomas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die genaue Adresse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the exact address.

definitions.note: Often used as a short answer to mean “exactly/that’s right.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Genau, so machen wir das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Exactly, that’s how we’ll do it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist genau das, was ich meine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s exactly what I mean.

definitions.note: Often used as a short response to agree or confirm something (like “right!” / “exactly!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: — Du kommst um acht Uhr, oder? — Genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: — You’re coming at eight o’clock, right? — Right.

definitions.note: Often used as an interjection to confirm or agree with what someone just said (like “exactly” or “that’s right”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: „Du meinst morgen um acht?“ – „Genau!“
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “You mean tomorrow at eight?” – “Exactly!”

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., feminine or plural, depending on the context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne die genaue Adresse nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know the exact address.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „genau“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte genauer erklären?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you explain that more precisely, please?

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adverb „genau“; often used to correct or уточнить what was just said.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns am Freitag, genauer gesagt um 18 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We'll meet on Friday—more precisely, at 6 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das genauer erklären?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you explain that more exactly?

definitions.note: Used to clarify or correct what was just said.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Genaugenommen habe ich es nicht gekauft, sondern geschenkt bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Strictly speaking, I didn’t buy it; I got it as a gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich denke genauso wie du.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think just like you do.

definitions.note: Often used in official or formal contexts (e.g., permits, requests, budgets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wird den Antrag genehmigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will approve the request.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle, especially with „sein“ in the passive/perfect sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Antrag ist genehmigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The application has been approved.

definitions.note: Present tense form (3rd person singular) of „genehmigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef genehmigt meinen Urlaub.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss approves my vacation.

definitions.note: Common in everyday speech; often used to mean “fed up” in a mild way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute richtig genervt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really annoyed today.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective with „sein“ (e.g. „Ich bin genervt.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin von dem Lärm total genervt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm really annoyed by the noise.

definitions.note: Usually used for recovering from an illness (more formal than „sich erholen“ in everyday speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nach der Grippe schnell genesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He recovered quickly after the flu.

definitions.note: Often used informally to express enthusiasm, like “awesome!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Idee ist genial!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The idea is awesome!

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with feminine nouns (and sometimes in other adjective declensions, depending on article/case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine geniale Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a brilliant idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat genickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He nodded.

definitions.note: Informal singular command (du-imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Genieß deinen Urlaub!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enjoy your vacation!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich genieße den Kaffee am Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I enjoy the coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a meal, a moment) or with "es" in phrases like "Genieß es!".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann es wirklich genießen, morgens Kaffee zu trinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can really enjoy drinking coffee in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er genießt die Ruhe am Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He enjoys the quiet in the evening.

definitions.note: past participle of „nehmen“; often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Zug um acht Uhr genommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the train at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: simple past of „genießen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er genoss das ruhige Wochenende zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He enjoyed the quiet weekend at home.

definitions.note: past participle of „genießen“; often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Essen sehr genossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really enjoyed the food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe genug gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have eaten enough.

definitions.note: Used before or after a noun to mean “enough” (e.g. genug Zeit / Zeit genug).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du genug Zeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have enough time?

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to tell someone to stop or that something is sufficient.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Genug! Hör bitte auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enough! Please stop!

definitions.note: Can also be used as an adverb meaning “enough” (e.g. “Das ist genug.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe genug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have enough.

definitions.note: past participle of „nutzen“; often used in the present perfect (Perfekt) with „haben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe diese App jeden Tag genutzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used this app every day.

definitions.note: past participle of „nähen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Knopf wieder angenäht, und jetzt ist alles fest genäht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sewed the button back on, and now everything is sewn on tightly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein kurzer Anruf kann genügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A short phone call can be enough.

definitions.note: used before a noun to mean “enough (of)”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du genügend Zeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have enough time?

definitions.note: Often used with dummy subject “es” (e.g., “Es genügt …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es genügt, wenn du mir kurz Bescheid gibst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s enough if you let me know briefly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat viel geopfert, um seiner Familie zu helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has sacrificed a lot to help his family.

definitions.note: past participle of "packen"; used in perfect tenses and the passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Koffer gepackt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I packed my suitcase.

definitions.note: past participle of "parken"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "Ich habe geparkt.")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe hier schon einmal geparkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have parked here before.

definitions.note: Past participle of "pellen"; commonly used for things like eggs or potatoes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Eier sind schon gepellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The eggs are already peeled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen Baum gepflanzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted a tree.

definitions.note: Past participle of „pflegen“; often used with „haben“ to say someone has cared for someone (e.g., in a nursing context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Vater zu Hause gepflegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cared for my father at home.

definitions.note: past participle of „pflücken“, usually used for picking flowers or fruit
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe frische Erdbeeren gepflückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I picked fresh strawberries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Reise ist für nächste Woche geplant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trip is planned for next week.

definitions.note: past participle of „planen“; often used like an adjective or in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Reise ist gut geplant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trip is well planned.

definitions.note: Past participle of „platzen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist geplatzt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ballon ist geplatzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon has popped.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Orangensaft frisch gepresst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pressed the orange juice fresh.

definitions.note: Often used in a formal or literary way (e.g., "Gepriesen sei ..." = "Blessed be ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde für seine Arbeit gepriesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was praised for his work.

definitions.note: Past participle of „prüfen“; often used in the perfect tense or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Unterlagen geprüft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the documents.

definitions.note: Colloquial; refers to hitting someone repeatedly (violent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde auf dem Heimweg geprügelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was beaten up on the way home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Küche geputzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cleaned the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wurde gequält.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was tortured.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “straight (not curved)” or “upright/even.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist hier ganz gerade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is completely straight here.

definitions.note: Used to say something is happening at the moment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich koche gerade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cooking right now.

definitions.note: Used for something that happened very recently.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gerade nach Hause gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has just come home.

definitions.note: Used to describe doing something in a straight line (not crooked).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schneid das Papier gerade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please cut the paper straight.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis ("exactly this/that").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gerade das macht mir Sorgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s exactly what worries me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte geradeaus bis zur Ampel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go straight ahead to the traffic light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe geradewegs nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going straight home.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that something is very much the case; often expresses surprise or strong judgment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist geradezu unglaublich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s downright unbelievable!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fahrer hat das Auto gerammt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The driver rammed the car.

definitions.note: past participle of "rennen"; used with "sein" in the perfect tense (e.g., "Ich bin gerannt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin so schnell gerannt, wie ich konnte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran as fast as I could.

definitions.note: Often used with "in" + accusative (e.g., in Schwierigkeiten geraten).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht in Schwierigkeiten geraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to get into trouble.

definitions.note: Often used to say how something turned out (e.g., "gut geraten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist gut geraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake turned out well.

definitions.note: past participle of "raten" (used with "haben")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihm geraten, zum Arzt zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advised him to go to the doctor.

definitions.note: past participle of "raten" (used with "haben")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die richtige Antwort geraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guessed the correct answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schmuck wurde geraubt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jewelry was robbed.

definitions.note: past participle of "rauchen"; often used in the perfect tense (e.g., "hat geraucht")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat gestern Abend geraucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He smoked last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Kosten schon gerechnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already calculated the costs.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like laws, decisions, or treatment of people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist nicht gerecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That isn’t fair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine gerechte Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a just decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Kritik ist gerechtfertigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your criticism is justified.

definitions.note: past participle of "reden"; used in the perfect tense (with "haben") and in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben lange geredet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “taken care of” in phrases like “Das ist geregelt.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, das ist schon geregelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, that’s already taken care of.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat die ganze Nacht geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained all night.

definitions.note: Past participle of "reichen"; often used with "haben" in phrases like "Es hat gereicht".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat gereicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was enough.

definitions.note: Past participle of "reichen"; used when food or drinks are brought/handed out (often in passive: "wird gereicht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Nachtisch wurde Obst gereicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fruit was served for dessert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist letztes Jahr nach Italien gereist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She traveled to Italy last year.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s mood or tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem langen Tag war er ziemlich gereizt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long day, he was pretty irritated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück sind alle gerettet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, everyone is saved.

definitions.note: past participle of "retten"; often used with "sein" or "haben" in the perfect tense, and also as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wurde gerettet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was rescued.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition (e.g., „auf“) to mean directed/aimed at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Werbung ist auf junge Leute gerichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advertising is aimed at young people.

definitions.note: often used with „in“ + noun to mean coming into a (usually sudden, often negative) state (e.g. trouble, danger, panic)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er geriet in Panik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He panicked (he got into a panic).

definitions.note: simple past form of „geraten“ (used with plural subjects like „sie“ = they / you formal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie gerieten in Schwierigkeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They got into trouble.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., „in geringem Maße“ = „to a small extent“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kosten sind zum Glück gering.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fortunately, the costs are small.

definitions.note: Dative masculine/neuter singular form of "gering".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei geringem Wind gehen wir segeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the wind is low, we go sailing.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "gering".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die geringste Sorge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s the least worry.

definitions.note: Superlative form of „gering“; often used in phrases like „die geringsten Zweifel“ (= the slightest doubts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht die geringsten Zweifel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have the slightest doubts.

definitions.note: Past participle of "reißen"; often used with "sein" to mean something has snapped/torn.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Seil ist gerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rope has snapped.

definitions.note: Past participle of „reiten“; typically used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist geritten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern geritten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rode yesterday.

definitions.note: Adjective; this form is used before a noun (e.g., with a feminine noun or in the plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die germanische Sprache hat viele Ähnlichkeiten mit dem Englischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Germanic language has many similarities with English.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean you like doing something ("gern"), or to respond politely to thanks ("Gern.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe dir gern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll gladly help you.

definitions.note: Often used to express that you like doing something or that you accept an offer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe dir gerne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d be happy to help you.

definitions.note: past participle of „riechen“; used in the perfect tense (e.g., „hat gerochen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen hat komisch gerochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food smelled strange.

definitions.note: Past participle of „rufen“, used as an adjective (e.g. „die gerufene Nummer“ = the number called/dialed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die gerufene Nummer ist besetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The number called is busy.

definitions.note: past participle of „rufen“; used with auxiliaries like „haben/sein“ (e.g., „hat … gerufen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich gestern Abend gerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called me yesterday evening.

definitions.native: gets into (a situation), ends up in
definitions.note: Often used with „in + Akk.“ (e.g. „in Schwierigkeiten geraten“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gerät in Schwierigkeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets into trouble.

definitions.note: Often used with an adverb like „gut“ or „schlecht“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan gerät gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan turns out well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wohnung ist hell und geräumig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment is bright and spacious.

definitions.note: Usually used to describe being emotionally moved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war sehr gerührt von deiner Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was very touched by your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe wird ständig gerührt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is stirred constantly.

definitions.note: often used to describe being emotionally affected
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war sehr gerührt von deiner Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was very touched by your message.

definitions.note: Often used with „für“ to mean ready/prepared for something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind gut gerüstet für den Winter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are well prepared for the winter.

definitions.note: past participle of „sagen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g. „ich habe … gesagt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das schon gesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already said that.

definitions.note: past participle of „sammeln“, often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe alle Quittungen gesammelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have collected all the receipts.

definitions.note: Used before a noun to mean the whole of something (e.g. „die gesamte Zeit“ = the whole time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die gesamte Klasse wartet vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The whole class is waiting in front of the door.

definitions.note: Often used with a definite article or a possessive (e.g., „der gesamte Tag“, „meine gesamte Familie“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den gesamten Tag gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked the entire day.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive), often with an -en ending (e.g., after „den“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den gesamten Tag gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked the entire day.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective; often used with nouns like „der/die/das gesamte …“ (the entire …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den gesamten Tag gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked the entire day.

definitions.note: used to refer to something in its complete extent (e.g., “ein gesamtes Jahr” = “a whole year”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ein gesamtes Jahr in Berlin gelebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We lived in Berlin for a whole year.

definitions.note: past participle of „senden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir gestern eine Nachricht gesandt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you a message yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "schaden"; commonly used with "haben" (e.g., "hat geschadet")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat ihm sehr geschadet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That harmed him a lot.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „Voraussetzungen sind geschaffen“ = “the conditions have been created/put in place.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Voraussetzungen sind geschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conditions have been created (put in place).

definitions.note: past participle of "schaffen" in the sense of creating something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Künstler hat ein neues Werk geschaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The artist created a new work.

definitions.note: Often used with "es" in the phrase "es geschafft" meaning to succeed at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es geschafft!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did it!

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „geschehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern geschah ein Unfall auf der Autobahn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday an accident happened on the highway.

definitions.note: past participle of "schauen"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern Abend einen Film geschaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched a movie last night.

definitions.note: Subjunctive form of „geschehen“; often used in set phrases like „So geschehe es.“ (= “So be it.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So geschehe es.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So be it.

definitions.note: Often used in questions like „Was ist geschehen?“ (“What happened?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was ist hier geschehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What happened here?

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech; can mean “sensible” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist wirklich gescheit und löst das Problem schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is really smart and solves the problem quickly.

definitions.note: past participle of „scheitern“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan ist gescheitert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan failed.

definitions.note: past participle of "schenken" (used in the present perfect and passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir das Buch geschenkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave you the book as a gift.

definitions.note: Often used for practical ability (e.g., with your hands). In other contexts, it can also be the past participle of „schicken“ (= sent), but here it’s used as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr geschickt mit den Händen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very skillful with her hands.

definitions.note: past participle of „schicken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir eine Nachricht geschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you a message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine geschickte Handwerkerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a skillful craftswoman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist geschickter als ihr Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is more skillful than her brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist seit zwei Jahren geschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been divorced for two years.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective (e.g. „geschieden sein“ = to be divorced).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sind seit 2019 geschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been divorced since 2019.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was geschieht hier?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is happening here?

definitions.note: Very vulgar/strong language; can be offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat auf den Gehweg geschissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog pooped on the sidewalk.

definitions.note: past participle of „schlafen“; used with „haben“ (e.g. „ich habe geschlafen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute Nacht gut geschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I slept well tonight.

definitions.note: past participle of „schlagen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich geschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hit me.

definitions.note: past participle of "schleppen"; often implies carrying something heavy with effort
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den schweren Koffer die Treppe hochgeschleppt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dragged/hauled the heavy suitcase up the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is closed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is closed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte benutzen Sie die geschlossene Tür nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t use the closed door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Tablette geschluckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swallowed the pill.

definitions.note: Can describe food (no flavor) or something inappropriate/offensive (e.g., a joke).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Witz war echt geschmacklos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The joke was really in bad taste.

definitions.note: Past participle of "schmecken"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat ... geschmeckt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe hat sehr gut geschmeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup tasted very good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin wirklich geschmeichelt von deinem Kompliment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really flattered by your compliment.

definitions.note: past participle of „schmieden“; often used to describe something made by forging (especially metal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schwert ist aus Stahl geschmiedet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sword is forged from steel.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (e.g., with „sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist heute dezent geschminkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing subtle makeup today.

definitions.note: Colloquial past participle meaning “thrown” (often used instead of the standard form “geworfen”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Ball weit geschmissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has thrown the ball far.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schokolade ist geschmolzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate has melted.

definitions.note: Past participle of "schmücken"; often used with "sein" (to be) to describe something that is decorated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Saal ist mit Blumen geschmückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hall is decorated with flowers.

definitions.note: Often used about catching someone (e.g., police catching a thief).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Dieb geschnappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police caught the thief.

definitions.note: past participle of „schnarchen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die ganze Nacht geschnarcht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He snored all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern hat es den ganzen Tag geschneit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it snowed all day.

definitions.note: past participle of „schneiden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Brot schon geschnitten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already cut the bread.

definitions.note: past participle of „schnitzen“; often used like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Figur ist aus Holz geschnitzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The figurine is carved from wood.

definitions.note: past participle of „schieben“; used in the perfect tense (usually with „haben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Tisch zur Seite geschoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pushed the table to the side.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech to mean very surprised or upset by something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war total geschockt, als ich das gehört habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was totally shocked when I heard that.

definitions.note: Past participle of „scheren“; often used for shearing sheep or shaving hair.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schaf ist schon geschoren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sheep has already been shorn.

definitions.note: past participle of „schießen“; used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat zweimal geschossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shot twice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Brief ist geschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter is written.

definitions.note: past participle of "schreiben"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen Brief geschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote a letter.

definitions.note: often used as an adjective (from the verb „schreiben“) to describe something that is in writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die geschriebenen Notizen noch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have the written notes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat laut geschrien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouted loudly.

definitions.note: Often used in the pattern „etwas ist (jemandem/etwas) geschuldet“ = “something is due to / attributable to someone/something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verzögerung ist dem Wetter geschuldet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delay is due to the weather.

definitions.note: past participle of „schummeln“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat bei der Prüfung geschummelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cheated on the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Knöchel ist geschwollen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ankle is swollen.

definitions.note: past participle of „schwimmen“, used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern im See geschwommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swam in the lake yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „schwören“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat geschworen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir geschworen, dass er die Wahrheit sagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swore to me that he was telling the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Krankheit bin ich noch geschwächt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the illness, I’m still weakened.

definitions.note: Used for skipping school or a class on purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat heute die Schule geschwänzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He skipped school today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Nachbar ist sehr geschwätzig und erzählt jedem alles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is very talkative and tells everyone everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto ist bei dem Unfall stark geschädigt worden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car was badly damaged in the accident.

definitions.note: Often used for things done in a professional context (not private).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin diese Woche geschäftlich in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in Berlin this week for work.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) of „geschehen“, used for hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn das noch einmal geschähe, würde ich sofort gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If that happened again, I would leave immediately.

definitions.note: past participle of "schälen"; often used like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kartoffeln sind schon geschält.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The potatoes are already peeled.

definitions.note: Often used with numbers/amounts to mean an approximate value.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kosten werden auf etwa 200 Euro geschätzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The costs are estimated at about 200 euros.

definitions.note: Used to say someone/something is held in high regard.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein geschätzter Kollege.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a valued colleague.

definitions.note: past participle of „schütteln“; often used like an adjective or in perfect tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Saft ist gut geschüttelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The juice is well shaken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gebiet ist geschützt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The area is protected.

definitions.note: Often used in religious contexts, but also figuratively to mean “fortunate.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind gesegnet, so gute Freunde zu haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are blessed to have such good friends.

definitions.note: past participle of "sehen"; used to form the perfect tense (e.g., "habe gesehen" = "have seen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Film schon gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already seen the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir gestern eine Nachricht gesendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you a message yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "sitzen" (used with "haben")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den ganzen Tag am Schreibtisch gesessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sat at the desk all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist gesetzlich verboten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is legally forbidden.

definitions.note: past participle of „setzen“ (used in the perfect tense and in the passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Glas auf den Tisch gesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the glass on the table.

definitions.note: Often used for data/files meaning they have been saved safely (made a backup).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Daten sind gesichert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The data is backed up.

definitions.note: Often used in reports/news when someone or something is seen (e.g., ships, animals, a suspect).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the morning, a wolf was spotted near the village.

definitions.note: Used for organizing or sorting through things (e.g., documents, files, photos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fotos wurden nach Datum gesichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photos were sorted by date.

definitions.note: Colloquial and often crude; past participle of „saufen“ (to drink alcohol heavily).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat gestern zu viel gesoffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drank too much yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used with „für“ or „dafür“ (e.g., „für alles gesorgt“, „dafür gesorgt, dass …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, ich habe schon für alles gesorgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, I’ve already taken care of everything.

definitions.note: Often used with „sich um + Akk.“ (e.g., „sich um jemanden gesorgt“). More commonly you also hear „sich Sorgen machen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben uns sehr um dich gesorgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were very worried about you.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" + accusative (e.g., "gespannt auf ...") to mean looking forward to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gespannt auf das Wochenende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m excited about the weekend.

definitions.note: past participle of „sparen“, usually used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat gespart“).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have saved enough money.

definitions.note: past participle of "speichern"; often used with "sein" or as an adjective

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The file is saved on the computer.

definitions.note: Past participle of „speisen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „Wir haben … gespeist“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben gestern Abend im Restaurant gespeist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ate (dined) at the restaurant last night.

definitions.note: Often used in technical contexts with „mit“ (e.g., „mit Strom gespeist“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gerät wird mit Strom gespeist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The device is powered with electricity.

definitions.note: Past participle of „spenden“; often used with „haben“ (Perfekt) or in the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat 50 Euro gespendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She donated 50 euros.

definitions.note: Often used for roads/areas that are closed to traffic or for accounts/cards that can’t be used.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is blocked because of construction work.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (e.g. a road or account being blocked/closed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist wegen Bauarbeiten gesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is closed because of construction work.

definitions.note: past participle of „spielen“; used in the perfect tense and the passive

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I played with my friends yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „sprechen“; also used as an adjective

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spoke with each other for a long time yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „springen“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist über den Zaun gesprungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He jumped over the fence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein neuer Kollege ist sehr gesprächig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My new colleague is very talkative.

definitions.note: past participle of „spucken“; used in the perfect tense with „haben“.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spit on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Geschirr schon gespült.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already washed the dishes.

definitions.note: past participle of "spüren"; used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den kalten Wind auf meiner Haut gespürt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt the cold wind on my skin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gestalten den Garten neu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re redesigning the garden.

definitions.note: Can mean creating/designing something (e.g., a product or poster) or shaping/structuring something (e.g., a process or lesson).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She designs a new logo for the company.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "gestehen"

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat lange vor der Tür gestanden.

definitions.note: past participle of „starten“; often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense
