definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss allows us a short break.

definitions.note: Often used in formal signs and notices.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Entry is permitted only with an ID.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of "gestatten"

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher allowed us to go home early.

definitions.note: past participle of „stecken“

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dir etwas gestehen: Ich habe einen Fehler gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to confess something to you: I made a mistake.

definitions.note: Often used for questions (“a posed question”) or photos/scenes (“staged”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine gestellte Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a posed question.

definitions.note: past participle of „stellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Vase auf den Tisch gestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the vase on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern war ich zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I was at home.

definitions.note: past participle of „steigen“, often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist/sind gestiegen“)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bee stung me.

definitions.note: past participle of „stehlen“; often used with „haben“ to form the present perfect

definitions.note: attributive form (used before a noun)

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin auf dem Gehweg gestolpert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tripped on the sidewalk.

definitions.note: past participle of "stoppen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat gestoppt")

definitions.note: used for text or items removed from a list.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knitted a scarf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat das Gebäude gestürmt.

definitions.note: past participle of „singen“ (often used with „haben“ to form the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern im Chor gesungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sang in the choir yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „sinken“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wasserstand ist gesunken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water level has fallen.

definitions.note: past participle of „säubern“; often used with „sein“/„werden“ (e.g., „ist/werden gesäubert“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Küche ist schon gesäubert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen has already been cleaned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat schwer gesündigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has sinned gravely.

definitions.note: past participle of „tun“; often used with „haben“ to form the present perfect

definitions.note: past participle of „täuschen“

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bet that he would be late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch ist meiner Mutter gewidmet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is dedicated to my mother.

definitions.note: Past participle of „widmen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist … gewidmet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch ist meiner Mutter gewidmet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is dedicated to my mother.

definitions.note: Past participle of "weisen"; often used with an object (e.g., someone) and a direction or something being indicated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich in die richtige Richtung gewiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pointed me in the right direction.

definitions.note: Often used with „ich“ to mean “I win” (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gewinne das Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I win the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Mannschaft will heute gewinnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team wants to win today.

definitions.note: Used for gaining time, distance, confidence, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen Zeit gewinnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to gain time.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du trainierst, gewinnst du das Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you practice, you win the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gewinnt das Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wins the game.

definitions.note: often used with things like medicine: „Das hat (nicht) gewirkt.“ = it (didn’t) work / it had (no) effect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Medikament hat schnell gewirkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The medicine worked quickly.

definitions.note: less common than „gestrickt“ in everyday German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schal ist von Hand gewirkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The scarf is hand-knitted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Tisch gewischt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wiped the table.

definitions.note: Often used to express agreement or confirmation (similar to “certainly”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mir gewiss, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sure that he’s coming today.

definitions.note: Often used to express agreement or emphasis; can sound a bit formal in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gewiss hast du recht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Surely you are right.

definitions.note: Often means “certain” in the sense of specific but not named or not exactly defined.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gewisse Zweifel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have certain doubts.

definitions.note: Used to refer to things or people that are not specified in detail (often: “certain” in the sense of “particular”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt gewisse Risiken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are certain risks.

definitions.note: Used before a noun with an adjective ending (e.g. „einen gewissen …“ = „a certain …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen gewissen Verdacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a certain suspicion.

definitions.note: Often used with an article, e.g. „ein gewisser …“ = “a certain …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein gewisser Herr Müller hat angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A certain Mr. Müller called.

definitions.native: in a way, so to speak
definitions.note: Often used to soften or qualify a statement (similar to “in a sense”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verstehe dich gewissermaßen, aber ich bin nicht ganz einverstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understand you in a way, but I don’t completely agree.

definitions.note: often used with an indefinite article (e.g., „ein gewisses …“) to mean “a certain …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein gewisses Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a certain problem.

definitions.note: Often used with „an + Akk.“ (e.g., „an etwas gewohnt sein“) or in the phrase „wie gewohnt“ = “as usual”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin das frühe Aufstehen gewohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m used to getting up early.

definitions.note: Past participle of „wohnen“, commonly used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat gewohnt“ = „lived“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe zwei Jahre in München gewohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lived in Munich for two years.

definitions.note: past participle of "wollen"; often used like an adjective (e.g. "Das ist so gewollt.")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist so gewollt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s intended that way.

definitions.note: past participle of "gewinnen"; used with "haben" in the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben das Spiel gewonnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We won the game.

definitions.note: past participle of the auxiliary verb "werden"; used with "sein" to form the perfect tense (e.g., "ist ... geworden")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schnell wütend geworden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has quickly become angry.

definitions.note: past participle of "werden", usually used with "sein" (e.g. "ist ... geworden")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin müde geworden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got tired.

definitions.note: past participle of „werfen“; used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Ball weit geworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the ball far.

definitions.note: past participle of "wissen"; often used with "haben" to form the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das nicht gewusst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't know that.

definitions.note: Older spelling of modern standard German „gewusst“ (past participle of „wissen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das nicht gewußt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t know that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein anderes Buch gewählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chose a different book.

definitions.note: Used in the context of elections or voting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie haben gestern einen neuen Bürgermeister gewählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They elected a new mayor yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., rights, permissions, requests, loans).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt wird dem Verein eine Förderung gewähren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city will grant the association a subsidy.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., rights, permission, support, or assistance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt gewährt den Familien finanzielle Unterstützung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city provides financial support to the families.

definitions.native: to accustom; to get used to
definitions.note: Commonly used reflexively as „sich an + Akk.“ (to get used to something), or transitively as „jemanden an + Akk. gewöhnen“ (to accustom someone to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich daran gewöhnen, früh aufzustehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get used to getting up early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe gewöhnlich um acht Uhr zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually go to work at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a feminine noun (or in some plural contexts), e.g. „die gewöhnliche Sache“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die gewöhnliche Route zur Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the usual route to school.

definitions.note: Adjective in an inflected form (e.g., after “die/der/das”, “einen”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns zur gewöhnlichen Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We meet at the usual time.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „gewöhnlich“ (often used before a noun: „ein gewöhnlicher Tag“ = „a more usual day“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute war es ein gewöhnlicherer Tag als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today was a more usual day than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein gewöhnliches Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an ordinary problem.

definitions.note: Often used with "an" + accusative: "an etwas gewöhnt (sein)" = "to be used to something."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin an den Lärm gewöhnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am used to the noise.

definitions.note: Often used with "an" (an etwas gewöhnt) or in the phrase "(ich) bin es gewohnt".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin es nicht gewöhnt, so früh aufzustehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm not used to getting up so early.

definitions.native: got used to, became accustomed to
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich an + Akk. gewöhnen“ = to get used to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gewöhnte mich schnell an den neuen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got used to the new job quickly.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „wie gewünscht“ (= as desired/as requested).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist genau so, wie ich es mir gewünscht habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s exactly how I wished it would be.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe ist gut gewürzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is well seasoned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe schon gezahlt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already paid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Bild ist von meiner Tochter gezeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The picture is drawn by my daughter.

definitions.note: Often used with documents like contracts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag ist schon gezeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract is already signed.

definitions.note: past participle of „zeigen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir das Foto gezeigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I showed you the photo.

definitions.note: past participle of „zelten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben am See gezeltet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We camped by the lake.

definitions.note: Past participle of „ziehen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat gezogen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Koffer über den Boden gezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pulled the suitcase across the floor.

definitions.note: Past participle of „ziehen“; in the sense of moving to a new place it’s commonly used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist gezogen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind letztes Jahr nach Berlin gezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We moved to Berlin last year.

definitions.note: past participle of „zucken“; often used with „hat“ in the Perfekt (e.g. „hat gezuckt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Auge hat den ganzen Tag gezuckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My eye twitched all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nie daran gezweifelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I never doubted it.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something that doesn’t feel natural (e.g., a forced smile).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Lächeln wirkte gezwungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His smile seemed forced.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zwingen“; often used with „haben“ (has forced) or „werden“ (was forced).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich gezwungen, zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forced me to go.

definitions.note: past participle used as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die gezählten Stimmen wurden noch einmal überprüft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The counted votes were checked again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe bis zehn gezählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I counted to ten.

definitions.note: Used especially for animals (and sometimes plants) that are bred/cultivated by humans.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Hunde wurden in Deutschland gezüchtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dogs were bred in Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Termin geändert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed the appointment.

definitions.note: Past participle of „ärgern“; often used with „sich“ to mean ‘got annoyed’ / ‘was annoyed’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich über die Verspätung geärgert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was annoyed about the delay.

definitions.note: past participle of „äußern“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat … geäußert“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seine Meinung klar geäußert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He expressed his opinion clearly.

definitions.note: often used to say something is open/has been opened (e.g., a door, a store)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist geöffnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is open.

definitions.note: past participle of „öffnen“; often used with „haben“ (I have opened) or „sein“ (it is open)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Fenster geöffnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I opened the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe viel geübt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I practiced a lot.

definitions.note: Imperative (du) form used with separable verbs like „abgeben“ (often appears with „ab“ elsewhere in the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gib das Formular bitte ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please hand in the form.

definitions.note: Used as the informal singular imperative with separable verbs like „aufgeben“ (e.g., „Gib … auf!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gib nicht auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t give up!

definitions.note: informal singular command (imperative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gib mir bitte das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please give me the book.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative of „geben“ (used when speaking to one person you address as „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gib mir bitte das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please give me the book.

definitions.note: Usually used with the separable prefix „zu“ (as in „gib … zu“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gib es zu: Du hast das vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admit it: you forgot that.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „ab“ (e.g. „du gibst ... ab“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du gibst deine Hausaufgaben morgen ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You hand in your homework tomorrow.

definitions.note: From the separable verb "aufgeben"; you usually say "du gibst ... auf" ("auf" goes at the end of the clause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum gibst du so schnell auf?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you giving up so quickly?

definitions.note: used with money (e.g., Geld ausgeben)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du gibst zu viel Geld aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You spend too much money.

definitions.note: used for distributing things to people
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du gibst die Flyer am Eingang aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You hand out the flyers at the entrance.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „geben“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gibst du mir bitte das Buch?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me the book, please?

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „angeben“: „gibt … an“ (e.g., gives/provides information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gibt seine Adresse an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He states/provides his address.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gibt nie auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He never gives up.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb prefix: gibt … aus.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gibt viel Geld aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spends a lot of money.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb prefix: gibt … aus.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin gibt die Arbeitsblätter aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher hands out the worksheets.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "geben"; also used in the expression "es gibt" = "there is/there are".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gibt mir das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives me the book.

definitions.note: Used as "es gibt" to say that something exists or is available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt hier ein gutes Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a good café here.

definitions.note: colloquial contraction of "gibt es" (often written without an apostrophe)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier gibts Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is coffee here.

definitions.note: Often used negatively (about wanting too much money, food, attention, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gierig und will immer mehr Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is greedy and always wants more money.

definitions.note: Informal imperative (du-form) of „gießen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gieß die Blumen bitte heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please water the flowers today.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of „gießen“ (ich gieße).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gieße Wasser in das Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pour water into the glass.

definitions.note: Often used with liquids (pouring) or with plants (watering).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte ein Glas Wasser eingießen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pour me a glass of water, please?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular (er/sie/es) of „gießen“; often used for pouring liquids, or for watering plants.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gießt Wasser in das Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pours water into the glass.

definitions.note: Often used for substances, animals, or plants that contain poison.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Beeren sind giftig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These berries are poisonous.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "gelten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Fahrschein gilt nur heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ticket is only valid today.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „abgehen“ (e.g. „ging … ab“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ging pünktlich ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train left on time.

definitions.note: Past tense of the separable verb „angehen“; the prefix „an“ often comes at the end of the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ging an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light came on.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „aufgehen“ in the simple past (Präteritum), e.g. „ging … auf“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne ging um sechs Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun rose at six o’clock.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „aufgehen“ in the simple past (Präteritum), e.g. „ging … auf“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ging plötzlich auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door suddenly opened.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of the separable verb „ausgehen“; the „aus“ often appears later in the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ging gestern Abend aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went out last night.

definitions.note: Used for lights, fires, or devices when they go off by themselves.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ging plötzlich aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light suddenly went out.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „eingehen“ (often said about plants or a business failing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Pflanze ging ein, weil sie kein Wasser bekam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plant died because it didn’t get any water.

definitions.note: simple past of gehen
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern ging ich nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I went home.

definitions.note: simple past (er/sie/es) of „untergehen“ (often used with the separable prefix „unter“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne ging um 8 Uhr unter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun set at 8 o’clock.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of „gehen“, often used for hypothetical situations or polite suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ginge heute mit dir ins Kino, aber ich muss arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would go to the cinema with you today, but I have to work.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „ausgehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern Abend gingen wir mit Freunden aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday evening we went out with friends.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "gehen" for "we/you (plural)/they"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern gingen wir zusammen nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we went home together.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) simple past; more common in writing/storytelling than in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern gingst du nach der Schule nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you went home after school.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person plural (ihr) of „gehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr gingt gestern zusammen nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You went home together yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist ganz glatt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is completely smooth.

definitions.note: Often used to say something went easily or without issues.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Vorstellungsgespräch lief glatt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The job interview went smoothly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine glatte Oberfläche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a smooth surface.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative (“Believe!”), and also in spoken German as a shortened form of “glaube” (e.g. “ich glaub …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glaub mir, das stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Believe me, that's true.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaube, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think (that) he’s coming today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie glauben, dass er die Wahrheit sagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believe that he is telling the truth.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “think” when giving an opinion or guess (like “I think so”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glauben, dass das eine gute Idee ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that is a good idea.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glaubst du mir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you believe me?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "glauben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er glaubt dir nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t believe you.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „glauben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaubte dir, aber ich hatte keine Beweise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believed you, but I had no proof.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural or formal “you” (Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie glaubten, dass der Zug pünktlich kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They believed that the train would be on time.

definitions.note: Simple past (du-form): used with "you" (singular, informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du glaubtest ihm, aber er hat gelogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You believed him, but he lied.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Erklärung klingt glaubwürdig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His explanation sounds credible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die gleiche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same idea.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like „bis gleich“ (see you soon) or „gleich!“ meaning “right away!”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm coming right away.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “in a moment” (not necessarily instantly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be right there.

definitions.note: Used in comparisons (e.g., “gleich alt” = “the same age”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Kinder sind gleich alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two children are the same age.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Kinder sind gleichaltrig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two children are the same age.

definitions.note: Often used with a definite article (e.g., "der/die/das gleiche") to mean "the same".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die gleiche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same idea.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „gleich“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen im gleichen Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in the same house.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „gleich“ used before a masculine noun (or as a predicate adjective in some set phrases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein gleicher Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the same mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind gleichermaßen überrascht und erleichtert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are equally surprised and relieved.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite reply meaning “you too” (e.g., after “Guten Appetit!” or “Schönen Tag!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke! Gleichfalls!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks! Same to you!

definitions.note: Often used with "(jdm/etw) gleichgültig sein" = to not care about someone/something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist mir gleichgültig, was du wählst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t care what you choose.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte verteile die Farbe gleichmäßig auf der Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please spread the paint evenly on the wall.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative: jemandem gleichen = to resemble someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gleicht seinem Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He resembles his father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind gleichzeitig angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived at the same time.

definitions.note: Often used for smooth, effortless movement (e.g., on ice, through air, over a surface).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vogel kann lange gleiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird can glide for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used for surfaces (ice, wet floors, mud) that you can easily slip on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, der Gehweg ist heute Morgen glitschig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful, the sidewalk is slippery this morning.

definitions.note: Informal; often sounds rude (like “to gawk”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf zu glotzen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop staring!

definitions.note: Often sounds rude or impolite; used when someone is staring in an obvious way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum glotzt du mich so an?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you staring at me like that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dem Wasser kann man die Sonne glänzen sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the water you can see the sun shining.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (attributive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt eine glänzende Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is wearing a shiny jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stern glänzt heute besonders hell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The star shines especially brightly today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „glänzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stern glänzte in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The star shone in the night.

definitions.note: Usually refers to believing in God/a religion (not just believing a fact).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Großeltern sind sehr gläubig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are very religious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute sehr glücklich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very happy today.

definitions.note: Often also used as an adjective meaning "happy"; as an adverb it means "happily" or "luckily" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glücklich habe ich noch einen Parkplatz gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, I still found a parking space.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with a feminine noun like „eine glückliche Frau“ or plural like „glückliche Kinder“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine glückliche Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a happy mother.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „glücklich“, typically used before a noun (attributive), e.g. „einen glücklichen …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünsche dir einen glücklichen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you a happy day.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „glücklich“ (happy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit dem Umzug bin ich viel glücklicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since the move, I’m much happier.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used before a masculine noun (e.g. „ein glücklicher Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein glücklicher Mann wartet vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A happy man is waiting in front of the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glücklicherweise hat es heute nicht geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, it didn’t rain today.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter noun (e.g., ein glückliches Kind).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein glückliches Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a happy child.

definitions.note: superlative form of „glücklich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist heute die glücklichste Person im Raum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the happiest person in the room today.

definitions.note: superlative form of „glücklich“ used before a noun (e.g., „die glücklichsten …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die glücklichsten Kinder in der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the happiest children in the school.

definitions.note: Often used as a short, standalone phrase (like “Congrats!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Glückwunsch zu deinem neuen Job!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Congratulations on your new job!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef war gnadenlos und entließ mehrere Mitarbeiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss was merciless and fired several employees.

definitions.note: Often used in formal, religious, or old-fashioned contexts (e.g., about God, a ruler, or in polite set phrases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei gnädig und vergib ihm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be merciful and forgive him.

definitions.note: Often formal or old-fashioned; common in fixed phrases (e.g., with "Blick", "Urteil", "Bescheid").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der König schenkte dem Verurteilten einen gnädigen Blick.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king gave the condemned man a merciful look.

definitions.note: Weak adjective ending often used before a noun (e.g., after der/die/das, this/that, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage die goldene Kette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm wearing the golden necklace.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in weak/mixed declension (e.g., after an article or possessive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt den goldenen Ring jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wears the golden ring every day.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter noun (or as a nominalized adjective) in certain cases.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ein goldenes Armband gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought a golden bracelet.

definitions.note: simple past form of "gießen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er goss Wasser in das Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He poured water into the glass.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation (often capitalized as "Gott"), e.g., to show surprise, frustration, or emphasis.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oh Gott, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh God, I forgot my key!

definitions.note: simple past of „gießen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er goß Wasser in das Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He poured water into the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir graben ein Loch im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We dig a hole in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund grabt ein Loch im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog digs a hole in the garden.

definitions.note: colloquial short form of „gerade“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe grad keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just don't have time right now.

definitions.note: colloquial (short for "gerade")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin grad unterwegs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m on my way right now.

definitions.note: colloquial spelling of „gerade“ (common in informal writing/speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme grade nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m just getting home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Satz ist grammatisch korrekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sentence is grammatically correct.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “fantastic/awesome” in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert war grandios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was magnificent.

definitions.note: Used especially for animals (e.g., cows, sheep) eating grass in a field.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kühe grasen auf der Wiese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cows are grazing in the meadow.

definitions.note: Means “at no cost” (not “free” as in “not restricted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eintritt ist heute gratis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.note: Often used in ads and everyday speech to mean you don’t have to pay.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eintritt ist heute gratis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense: “I congratulate” (also used in “I congratulate you!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gratuliere dir zum Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I congratulate you on your birthday.

definitions.note: Usually used with dative for the person (jemandem) and often with „zu“ for the occasion (zu etwas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gratuliere dir zum Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I congratulate you on your birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gratuliert dir zum Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He congratulates you on your birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gratulierte ihr zum Geburtstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He congratulated her on her birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Himmel ist heute grau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky is gray today.

definitions.note: adjective ending; used before a noun or after certain determiners (e.g., die graue Jacke)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage heute die graue Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm wearing the gray jacket today.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „grau“ (e.g., before a plural noun: „die grauen …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe die grauen Wolken am Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the gray clouds in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen war grauenhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was horrible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war grauenvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was terrible.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with neuter singular nouns (e.g., ein graues Auto)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ein graues Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see a gray car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wäre grausam, ihn allein zu lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It would be cruel to leave him alone.

definitions.note: adjective used with a noun (weak/strong/mixed ending), e.g., before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine grausame Tat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a cruel act.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hörten grausame Geschichten aus dem Krieg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They heard horrible stories from the war.

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Chef ist grausamer als der alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new boss is crueler than the old one.

definitions.note: Usually used impersonally: „Mir/dir/ihm … graut (vor …)“ = “I/you/he … dread (…)/am terrified (of …)”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir graut vor der Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dreading the exam.

definitions.note: Imperative (du-form): used to tell one person to grab something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Greif den Ball!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grab the ball!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde nach dem Glas greifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will reach for the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte greifen Sie nach dem Geländer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please reach for the railing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb wollte nach der Tasche greifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief wanted to grab the bag.

definitions.native: to take effect; to kick in (measures, rules, etc.)
definitions.note: often used with abstract subjects: Maßnahmen/Gesetze/Regeln greifen
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neuen Regeln greifen ab Montag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new rules take effect starting Monday.

definitions.note: often: eingreifen = to intervene; but greifen can appear in set phrases like 'zu Maßnahmen greifen'
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regierung muss zu Maßnahmen greifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government has to take measures.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "greifen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er greift nach dem Glas Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reaches for the glass of water.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "greifen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund greift den Mann an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog attacks the man.

definitions.note: Usually used with „an“: „an + accusative“ (e.g., „an Frankreich“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland und Frankreich grenzen aneinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany and France border each other.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected form; used before a noun (or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die griechische Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Greek cuisine.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective (used with nouns in certain cases/genders/numbers)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse heute in einem griechischen Restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eating at a Greek restaurant today.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „angreifen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund griff den Mann an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog attacked the man.

definitions.note: Simple past of „greifen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er griff nach dem Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grabbed for the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Griff der Tür ist locker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door handle is loose.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) plural form of „angreifen“; usually used with the separable prefix: „griffen … an“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie griffen den Mann in der Nacht an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They attacked the man at night.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural form (e.g. “we/they grabbed”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie griffen nach der Tasche und liefen weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They grabbed for the bag and ran away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er grinst, weil er den Witz verstanden hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grins because he understood the joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er grinste und sagte nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grinned and didn’t say anything.

definitions.note: Can also mean “approximate” in contexts like a rough estimate (eine grobe Schätzung).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein grober Stoff.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a coarse fabric.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war sehr grob von ihm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was very rude of him.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective “grob”, often used before a noun (e.g. with a masculine accusative noun after “einen”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein groben Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a crude mistake.

definitions.note: Often used for people to mean “tall.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist groß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is big.

definitions.native: in a big way, on a large scale
definitions.note: Often used to mean something is done with a lot of effort, attention, or celebration. Not the same as English “gross”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das wurde groß gefeiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was celebrated in a big way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein großartiger Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a great movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hast du großartig gemacht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You did that great!

definitions.note: adjective; used here in an inflected form (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine großartige Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a great idea.

definitions.note: Adjective in a declined form (e.g., after der/die/das, ein-, or in plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke für deinen großartigen Tipp!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for your great tip!

definitions.note: Used as an adjective with a neuter noun in nominative or accusative singular (e.g., with "ein ..." or without an article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein großartiges Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a great gift.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „groß“, typically used before a noun (e.g., with feminine or plural nouns, depending on the article). Not the same as English “gross” (= disgusting).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a big city.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „groß“ (used before a noun).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a big bag.

definitions.note: Dative singular (masculine or neuter), or dative plural after a determiner (e.g., dem/einem, den).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in a big house.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with masculine accusative singular (and in some contexts also with plural dative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den großen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the big dog.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "groß" (e.g., with "den" or in plural/dative contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den großen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the big dog.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a big dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein großer Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a big dog.

definitions.note: Used with a neuter noun (strong declension) or after an article/pronoun (mixed declension), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ein großes Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see a big house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist sehr großzügig von dir.
