definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She founded a start-up in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), “they founded/established” or “(you) founded/established” (plural, formal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: 1920 gründeten sie eine kleine Firma in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In 1920, they founded a small company in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die Unterlagen gründlich geprüft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She checked the documents thoroughly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Wohnung gründlich geputzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cleaned the apartment thoroughly.

definitions.note: adjective form (inflected); used before a noun or with a definite article (e.g., "die grüne Jacke")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die grüne Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the green jacket.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with plural nouns after “die”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die grünen Äpfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the green apples.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a masculine noun (e.g. „ein grüner Apfel“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein grüner Apfel liegt auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A green apple is lying on the table.

definitions.note: neuter nominative/accusative singular form (and also genitive singular or dative plural, depending on context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte ein grünes T-Shirt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a green T-shirt.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative of „grüßen“ (like “Say hi!”). Common in phrases like „Grüß Gott!“ in southern Germany/Austria.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grüß deine Eltern von mir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Say hi to your parents from me!

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular) of "grüßen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grüß bitte deine Eltern von mir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please say hello to your parents from me!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (or subjunctive I) of „grüßen“: „I greet“ / „(that) I greet“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich grüße meine Nachbarn jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I greet my neighbors every morning.

definitions.native: to greet; to say hello to
definitions.note: Often used with an accusative object (jemanden grüßen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich morgen früh grüßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will greet you tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „grüßen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er grüßt seine Nachbarn jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He greets his neighbors every morning.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "grüßen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er grüßte seine Nachbarin freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He greeted his neighbor in a friendly way.

definitions.note: informal; often used as an imperative (like “Look!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guck mal, da drüben ist ein Hund!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look, over there is a dog!

definitions.note: colloquial (especially in northern Germany); often used like “schauen”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gucke aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking out the window.

definitions.note: Informal; common in spoken German (more formal: „sehen“, „schauen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute Abend einen Film gucken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to watch a movie tonight.

definitions.note: colloquial; 2nd person singular present of „gucken“ (du guckst)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du guckst gerade aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re looking out the window right now.

definitions.note: Colloquial/informal for "schaut"; often used in spoken German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er guckt aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks out the window.

definitions.note: Colloquial for „schaute/ansah“; simple past (ich/er/sie/es guckte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er guckte aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked out the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein guter Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a good plan.

definitions.note: Not the English noun “gut” (meaning intestines).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche gut Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak German well.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to show agreement or to move on to the next point.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gut, dann gehen wir jetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, then we'll go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr gutaussehend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very good-looking.

definitions.note: Used attributively before a noun; can refer to people of any gender, depending on the noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der gutaussehende Mann wartet vor dem Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The good-looking man is waiting in front of the café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mit dem gutaussehenden Mann gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with the good-looking man.

definitions.note: attributive form (used before a noun), usually masculine singular (e.g. „ein gutaussehender Mann“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein gutaussehender Mann wartet vor dem Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A good-looking man is waiting in front of the café.

definitions.note: Feminine (or plural) form of "gut"; often used before a noun (e.g., "eine gute Idee").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a good idea.

definitions.note: Dative singular (masculine or neuter) of "gut".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit gutem Essen und guter Musik wird der Abend perfekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With good food and good music, the evening becomes perfect.

definitions.note: Used mainly with masculine/neuter nouns in the accusative case (e.g., after a direct-object article like „den“), and in set phrases like „Guten Morgen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünsche dir einen guten Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you a good day.

definitions.note: Masculine nominative singular form (e.g., with a masculine noun like „Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein guter Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a good movie.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "gut"; often used with neuter nouns (e.g., "gutes Wetter") or as a nominalized adjective (e.g., "etwas Gutes").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute gibt es etwas Gutes zu essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today there is something good to eat.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form, often used in reported speech or in clauses with "dass".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hofft, dass ich gutgehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hopes that I'm doing well.

definitions.note: Often written as two words: „gut gehen“ (e.g., „Alles wird gut gehen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, alles wird gutgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, everything will go well.

definitions.native: is doing well, is going well
definitions.note: Used in expressions like „Wie geht es dir?“ – „Mir geht es gut.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass es dir gutgeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you’re doing well.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object or with “für” + noun (e.g., einen Fehler gutmachen, etwas für jemanden gutmachen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meine Verspätung gutmachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to make up for my lateness.

definitions.native: do good, be good for (someone), benefit
definitions.note: Often also written separately as „gut tun“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Spaziergang kann guttun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A walk can do you good.

definitions.native: to be doing well, to be well
definitions.note: Used with people/animals (often with „es scheint/du scheinst …“ or after verbs like „hoffen“, „wünschen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dir geht es gut, und dass es dir bald wieder gutzugehen beginnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you're doing well, and that you’ll start to feel well again soon.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive II), used for hypothetical/conditional situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gäbe dir gern mehr Zeit, aber ich muss jetzt los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would gladly give you more time, but I have to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss gähnen, weil ich müde bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to yawn because I'm tired.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum gähnst du so oft im Unterricht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you yawn so often in class?

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „gähnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gähnte, weil er sehr müde war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He yawned because he was very tired.

definitions.note: Often a bit formal; similar to "völlig".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist gänzlich unmöglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is completely impossible.

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the dative and a thing in the accusative (e.g., „Ich gönne dir eine Pause.“). With „nicht“ it can mean „to begrudge“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gönne dir eine Pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll grant you a break.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative person + an object: sich/jemandem etwas gönnen. Common: „Ich gönn(e) dir das“ = I’m happy for you / you deserve it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mir heute ein Stück Kuchen gönnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to treat myself to a piece of cake today.

definitions.note: Used in religious contexts and also figuratively (e.g., describing something extremely good).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine göttliche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a divine idea.

definitions.note: Often used in official contexts (tickets, IDs, contracts) and with time limits ("gültig bis" = "valid until").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Ausweis ist noch gültig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ID is still valid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wohnung ist günstig, aber sehr klein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment is inexpensive, but very small.

definitions.note: Often used for conditions, situations, or timing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bedingungen sind günstig für einen Ausflug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conditions are favorable for an outing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Flug war sehr günstig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flight was very cheap.

definitions.note: Often used for conditions or circumstances (e.g., a favorable time or situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bedingungen sind heute günstig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conditions are favorable today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen günstigen Flug gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a cheap flight.

definitions.note: often used for conditions, opportunities, or times (e.g., a favorable moment)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir warten auf den günstigen Moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re waiting for the favorable moment.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „günstig“ (often used for price).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Ticket ist günstiger als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This ticket is cheaper than the other one.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „günstig“ (often used for conditions, timing, or outcomes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen wäre ein günstigerer Zeitpunkt für das Gespräch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow would be a more favorable time for the conversation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine gütige Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a kind teacher.

definitions.note: An interjection used to express sudden realization, recognition, or triumph.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha, jetzt verstehe ich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aha, now I understand!

definitions.note: informal short form of „habe“ (1st person singular, present)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hab keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no time.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of „haben“ (ich hab = I have); common in speech and informal writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hab heute keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time today.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute viel gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have learned a lot today.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense (ich habe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute viel zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot to do today.

definitions.note: Common verb meaning to possess or to have something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ein neues Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a new car.

definitions.note: Auxiliary used to form the present perfect (Perfekt) with many verbs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben schon gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have already eaten.

definitions.note: Also used as an auxiliary verb to form the perfect tense (e.g., „Ich habe gearbeitet.“ = “I have worked.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte ein neues Fahrrad haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to have a new bike.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „vorhaben“; often used with separated „vor“ (e.g. „Wir haben viel vor.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben am Wochenende viel vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re planning a lot for the weekend.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I (used especially in reported speech/quotations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er behauptet, du habest das Geld nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He claims you don’t have the money.

definitions.note: archaic/older form of modern German "habt" (2nd person plural: "ihr habt")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr habet es gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have seen it.

definitions.note: colloquial contraction of „hab’s“ (= „habe es“), often used in informal speech/writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habs schon gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already done it.

definitions.note: 2nd-person plural (ihr) present form; often used as an auxiliary to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr habt das schon gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) have already seen that.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural present tense (ihr).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr habt heute viel Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have a lot of time today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hacke die Zwiebel klein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chop the onion into small pieces.

definitions.note: Usually means gaining access illegally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hacke nicht in fremde Computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't hack into other people's computers.

definitions.note: Often used for chopping wood or cutting something into small pieces.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen heute noch Holz hacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still have to chop wood today.

definitions.note: Used for gaining unauthorized access to computers or online accounts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand hat versucht, meinen Account zu hacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone tried to hack my account.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hackt das Gemüse klein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He chops the vegetables into small pieces.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hackt das Passwort in wenigen Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hacks the password in a few minutes.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like „halb so schlimm“ (not so bad) or with time expressions like „halb drei“ = 2:30.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin halb fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m half done.

definitions.note: Used as a noun mainly in sports to mean a half (of a game/match).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im ersten Halb haben wir zwei Tore geschossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the first half we scored two goals.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "halb" (e.g., used with feminine nouns like "eine halbe Stunde").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte noch eine halbe Stunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll wait another half hour.

definitions.note: inflected form of „halb“, used e.g. in the plural after certain cases (like dative after „mit“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fangen mit halben Portionen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll start with half portions.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter singular noun (e.g., „ein halbes Jahr“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte noch ein halbes Jahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll wait another half a year.

definitions.note: simple past of „helfen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er half mir gestern bei den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helped me with the homework yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „helfen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie halfen mir beim Umzug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They helped me with the move.

definitions.note: Used as a greeting; can also be used to get someone’s attention (like “hello?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hallo, wie geht's?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hello, how are you?

definitions.note: Often used as a filler word to soften or explain what you’re saying (common in spoken German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin halt müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m just tired.

definitions.note: Common German filler word used to soften or explain what you mean; often hard to translate directly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß halt nicht, was ich sagen soll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just don't know what to say.

definitions.note: Common filler particle in spoken German that softens or emphasizes what you’re saying; often hard to translate directly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dann mach es halt morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Then just do it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form of „halten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Halt! Das ist gefährlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop! That’s dangerous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich halte das Buch in der Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m holding the book in my hand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich halte an der Ampel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stop at the traffic light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich halte das Buch in der Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m holding the book in my hand.

definitions.note: Often used with „an“: „anhalten“ = to stop (e.g., a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich halte an der Ampel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stop at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Often used with specific constructions, e.g. "halten für" = to consider (someone/something as).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Tür halten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please hold the door?

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) form of "halten"; also used as the informal plural imperative ("hold! / stop!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Haltet bitte die Tür fest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold the door firmly, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen jetzt handeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to act now.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ + dative: „mit etwas handeln“ = to trade/deal in something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will mit gebrauchten Möbeln handeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to trade in used furniture.

definitions.note: Often used with "nach" to mean "acts according to" (e.g., "Er handelt nach den Regeln.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er handelt schnell und entschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He acts quickly and decisively.

definitions.note: Used for buying and selling goods (commerce).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie handelt mit Kleidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She trades in clothing.

definitions.note: Used when describing the topic of a book/film/story, often with "von".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film handelt von einer Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is about a family.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of „handeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er handelte schnell und entschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He acted quickly and decisively.

definitions.note: Often used with „von/über etw. handeln“ = “be about something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film handle von einer Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The film is about a family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, der Hund ist ganz harmlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, the dog is completely harmless.

definitions.note: Also used figuratively (e.g., a “hard” test or a “hard” time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Brot ist schon ganz hart.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread is already completely hard.

definitions.note: Often used for people, rules, or situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Prüfung war hart.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam was tough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie arbeitet hart für ihre Prüfungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works hard for her exams.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine harte Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a hard decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag keine harten Kekse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like hard cookies.

definitions.note: often used before a masculine noun (e.g., „harter Käse“ = „hard cheese“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Harter Käse schmeckt mir gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like hard cheese.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "hart" used before a noun (e.g., with neuter nouns like "Brot").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist hartes Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is hard bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fleck ist hartnäckig und geht nicht raus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stain is stubborn and won’t come out.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich hasse).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hasse es, zu spät zu kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hate being late.

definitions.note: Strong negative feeling; stronger than „nicht mögen“ (to not like).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sagen, dass sie ihren Chef hassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say that they hate their boss.

definitions.note: 2nd/3rd person singular present tense of "hassen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum hasst du ihn so sehr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you hate him so much?

definitions.note: simple past (du/er/sie/es form) of "hassen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum hasste er die Schule so sehr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did he hate school so much?

definitions.note: simple past (ihr) of „hassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum hassten ihr ihn so sehr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you hate him so much?

definitions.note: Used with „du“ (informal singular “you”) as an auxiliary, especially to form the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast das schon gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have already done that.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of "haben" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du Zeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have time?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schrieb die E-Mail hastig und machte viele Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wrote the email hastily and made many mistakes.

definitions.note: Auxiliary form of „haben“, used to form the present perfect (Perfekt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat heute viel gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has learned a lot today.

definitions.note: Often used as an auxiliary verb to form the present perfect (e.g. „hat gemacht“ = „has done“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat ein Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a car.

definitions.note: Used as the past tense form of „haben“ and often as an auxiliary in the past perfect (Plusquamperfekt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hatte schon gegessen, als sie ankam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already eaten when she arrived.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had no time yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person plural (ihr)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had no time yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hammer the nail into the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He whispered something into her ear.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used for hitting someone

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop hitting him!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen noch Holz hauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still have to chop wood.

definitions.note: Used to say what matters most, often in the sense of “as long as …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hauptsache, du bist gesund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The main thing is that you're healthy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich arbeite hauptsächlich von zu Hause aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work mainly from home.

definitions.note: Often used informally; can sound rough depending on context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hits the door.

definitions.note: From „hauen“; often colloquial for hitting/striking (can sound a bit rough).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slams his fist on the table.

definitions.note: From the verb „hauen“ (to hit/whack/chop), not the noun „die Haut“ (skin).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er haut den Nagel in die Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hits the nail into the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you hate him so much?

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „hassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als Kind haßte ich Spinat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child I hated spinach.

definitions.note: Used to get someone's attention; can also express mild surprise or a protest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He, warte mal!

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form of „heben“ (used to tell one person to lift/pick something up).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please lift the suitcase up!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hebe das Kind hoch.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please lift the box?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "heben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hebt die Kiste hoch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lifts the box up.

definitions.note: Often used for strong emotions, arguments, pain, or weather.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnet heute heftig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining heavily today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat gestern Abend heftig geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained heavily last night.

definitions.note: Often used for strong reactions or emotions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat heftig protestiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She protested strongly.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine nouns (e.g. „eine heftige …“) or in the plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine heftige Diskussion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an intense discussion.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine/neuter singular or plural nouns in certain cases (e.g., accusative masculine/neuter, dative plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat einen heftigen Streit mit seinem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had an intense argument with his brother.

definitions.note: comparative form of "heftig".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm wird heute Abend noch heftiger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm will get even more intense this evening.

definitions.note: Often used with feelings, thoughts, or plans (e.g. „einen Verdacht hegen“ = to harbor a suspicion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hege den Verdacht, dass er lügt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I harbor the suspicion that he’s lying.

definitions.note: Often used with feelings or thoughts (e.g., hope, suspicion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann keinen Verdacht hegen, dass sie gelogen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can harbor no suspicion that she lied.

definitions.note: Often used with feelings or attitudes (e.g., doubts, hatred, hopes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hegt große Zweifel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has serious doubts.

definitions.note: often used for sensitive topics or difficult situations that need careful handling
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine heikle Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a delicate question.

definitions.note: Often used after accidents or trips to mean someone arrived without injury.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück ist sie heil nach Hause gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily she got home safe.

definitions.note: Used as an old-fashioned or ideological salute; today strongly associated with Nazi usage ("Sieg Heil").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Einige riefen „Heil!“ und streckten den Arm aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some shouted “Heil!” and held out their arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich heile zum Glück schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, I heal quickly.

definitions.note: Often used for wounds/illnesses or emotional healing; can also be used transitively (“etwas/jemanden heilen” = to heal/cure something/someone) or reflexively (“sich heilen” = to heal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ärzte können viele Krankheiten heilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Doctors can cure many diseases.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die heilende Salbe hilft bei kleinen Wunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The healing ointment helps with small wounds.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein heiliger Ort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a holy place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine heilige Stätte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a holy place.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (e.g., „eine heilige Kirche“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine heilige Stätte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a holy place.

definitions.note: Often used in religious contexts; can also mean “saintly” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchen die heiligen Stätten der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are visiting the holy sites of the city.

definitions.note: Often confused with English “healing” (it does not mean that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchten den heiligen Ort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited the holy place.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „heilig“ (holy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Gebäude ist uns heiliger als alles andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This building is holier to us than anything else.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde heilt schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound heals quickly.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion (e.g., gehen/fahren) to mean “(go) home.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe jetzt heim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going home now.

definitions.note: Used for going back home by some means of transportation (car, bus, train, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt heimfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go home now.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving (e.g., from work, school, a party) to go home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde jetzt heimgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to go home now.

definitions.note: Past participle of „heimkehren“, typically used with „sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist nach vielen Jahren endlich heimgekehrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After many years, she finally returned home.

definitions.note: past participle of "heimkommen"; often used with "sein" (e.g., "ist heimgekommen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist spät heimgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came home late.

definitions.note: Slightly formal/literary compared to simply saying „nach Hause kommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Urlaub heimkehren wir wieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the vacation, we return home again.

definitions.note: Separable verb: ich komme heim, ich bin heimgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute spät heimkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will come home late today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat heimlich Schokolade gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He secretly ate chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir trafen uns in einem heimlichen Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We met in a secret café.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I marry / I’m getting married"); also used as an imperative ("marry!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächstes Jahr heirate ich meinen Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next year I’m going to marry my boyfriend.

definitions.note: Can be used both for “to marry someone” (jemanden heiraten) and “to get married” (heiraten).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen nächstes Jahr heiraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to get married next year.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heiratest du mich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you marry me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er heiratet nächstes Jahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s getting married next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er heiratete im Juni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got married in June.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "heiraten"

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They married in the summer of 2010.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute heiser und kann kaum sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hoarse today and can barely speak.

definitions.note: Swiss spelling of standard German „heißt“.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does that mean in English?

definitions.note: Often used both for people/moods (cheerful) and for weather/sky (bright, clear).

definitions.note: can describe temperature, weather, or food/drinks

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is hot.

definitions.note: Used about temperature (e.g., weather, food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es sehr heiß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is very hot.

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine nouns or with plural nouns depending on the article (e.g., „eine heiße Suppe“, „heiße Tage“). Not to be confused with „heiße“ from the verb „heißen“ (“am called”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a hot soup.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "heißen" (used to give your name).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich heiße Anna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My name is Anna.

definitions.note: dative singular masculine/neuter or after a definite/indefinite article (weak/mixed adjective ending)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir trinken Tee mit heißem Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drink tea with hot water.

definitions.native: to be called, to be named
definitions.note: Often used about what someone/something is called (name/designation).
