definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to be called Anna.

definitions.note: Used to say what a word, sign, or expression means.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was kann „Danke“ heißen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What can “Danke” mean?

definitions.native: to be called, to be named
definitions.note: Used to state or ask someone’s name (e.g., „Ich heiße …“, „Wie heißt du?“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie heißen du und dein Bruder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you and your brother called?

definitions.native: to mean (i.e., to signify; said of words, expressions, signs)
definitions.note: Used to explain what something means (e.g., „Das heißt …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was heißt dieses Wort auf Englisch?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does this word mean in English?

definitions.note: comparative form of „heiß“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es heißer als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is hotter than yesterday.

definitions.note: Neuter singular form (e.g., with "ein" or "das").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern ein heißes Getränk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a hot drink.

definitions.note: superlative form of „heiß“ (hot)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist der heißeste Tag des Jahres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is the hottest day of the year.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „heißen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie heißt du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your name?

definitions.note: Archaic spelling of modern German „heißt“ (3rd person singular of „heißen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das heiût „Willkommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That means “welcome.”

definitions.note: Common colloquial/spoken form of „helfe“ (dropping the -e).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, ich helf dir gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, I’ll help you in a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe dir mit den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help you with your homework.

definitions.note: Usually used with the dative: jemandem helfen = to help someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dir helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to help you.

definitions.note: Used with ihr (2nd person plural) in the present tense, and also as the plural imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr helft mir mit den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You help me with the homework.

definitions.note: Also used for sound: „hell“ = high-pitched/clear (e.g., a bright voice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Zimmer ist sehr hell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is very bright.

definitions.note: Not related to English "hell" (it means "bright"/"light").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne scheint hell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun is shining brightly.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine/neuter nouns in the dative singular, or with plural nouns in the genitive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit dem hellblauen Hemd siehst du sehr gut aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look very good in the light-blue shirt.

definitions.note: Used as an attributive adjective before a feminine noun (or as a weak ending after a determiner like "die").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die helle Lampe macht das Zimmer freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bright lamp makes the room feel welcoming.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of the adjective „hell“ (with an adjective ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die hellen Farben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the bright colors.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "hell".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Zimmer ist heller als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is brighter than yesterday.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun in the nominative or accusative (e.g., „ein helles Zimmer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein helles Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a bright room.

definitions.note: Used as a greeting or to get someone’s attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hello, wie geht's?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hello, how are you?

definitions.note: simple past of „hellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne hellte den Himmel auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun brightened the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin schon seit sechs Uhr hellwach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been wide awake since six o’clock.

definitions.note: Used with a point in time (often with a date or event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne seit 2020 hier, und sie wohnt schon länger her.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve lived here since 2020, and she has been living here since even earlier.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement or to indicate direction (toward the speaker/place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, please!

definitions.note: Used to get someone’s attention; can sound a bit abrupt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Her, komm mal her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey, come over here!

definitions.native: from here, from there (toward the speaker)
definitions.note: Used with verbs of motion to mean movement toward the speaker/this place (e.g., come here).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come here!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to express movement from a higher place to a lower place (e.g., herabfallen, herabkommen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Blatt fällt vom Baum herab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leaf is falling down from the tree.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion (e.g., herabfallen = to fall down) or in the phrase „von … herab“ (= from … down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Apfel fällt vom Baum herab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apple falls down from the tree.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to show movement toward the speaker or a point of reference (e.g., herankommen, heranholen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte heran!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come over here!

definitions.note: often used with „zu“ + dative: „zu jemandem/etwas heranzukommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, näher an die Bühne heranzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to get closer to the stage.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion to indicate movement upward in the direction of the speaker (as opposed to “hinauf,” which is away from the speaker).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm schnell herauf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come up here quickly!

definitions.note: Often used to describe movement from inside to outside, sometimes emphasizing direction toward the speaker; can be used on its own or together with "aus".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm aus dem Haus heraus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come out of the house!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs and separable prefixes (e.g., herauskommen = come out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte heraus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come out!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean movement from inside to outside (e.g., herauskommen = come out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte heraus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come out!

definitions.note: Often used for discovering information or solving something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch herausbekommen, wann der Zug abfährt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still need to find out when the train leaves.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „herausfinden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich herausfand gestern, dass das Museum montags geschlossen ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I found out that the museum is closed on Mondays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss herausfinden, wann der Zug abfährt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to find out when the train leaves.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie herausfindet, wo der Schlüssel ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She finds out where the key is.

definitions.note: Past participle of "herausbringen"; often used with "haben" (e.g. "hat ... herausgebracht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ein neues Buch herausgebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She published a new book.

definitions.note: past participle of „herausfordern“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn zu einem Rennen herausgefordert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I challenged him to a race.

definitions.note: past participle of „herausfinden“; commonly used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es endlich herausgefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finally found out.

definitions.note: past participle of „herausgeben“; often used with „werden“ in the passive (e.g. „wurde herausgegeben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch wurde 2020 herausgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was published in 2020.

definitions.note: past participle of „herausgeben“; used for giving things out to people (e.g. flyers, forms).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Flyer wurden am Eingang herausgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flyers were handed out at the entrance.

definitions.note: Often used with sein in the perfect tense (e.g., „ist herausgekommen“). Can also mean „was released/published“ for books, movies, music, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Film ist gestern herausgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new movie came out yesterday.

definitions.note: Used to talk about the result of a situation or how something ended up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende ist alles gut herausgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, everything turned out well.

definitions.native: to take out, to get out
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Milch aus dem Kühlschrank herausholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take the milk out of the fridge.

definitions.native: to bring out (the best), to get the most out of
definitions.note: Often used in a figurative sense, especially with "das Beste" (the best).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kann das Beste aus dem Team herausholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She can bring out the best in the team.

definitions.note: Often used for something becoming visible/known (e.g., information, results).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende wird die Wahrheit herauskommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, the truth will come out.

definitions.note: Used to say how something ends up or what the result is.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wird oft anders herauskommen, als man denkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will often turn out differently than you think.

definitions.note: zu-Infinitiv form (used after verbs like versuchen, planen, vergessen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche herauszufinden, warum der Zug zu spät ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to find out why the train is late.

definitions.note: Often used for coming out of a place (e.g., a building) or for something being released/published.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, aus dem Zimmer herauszukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is trying to get out of the room.

definitions.native: here (English word used in German contexts; means „hier“ )
definitions.note: Used in spoken/written German when switching to English (code-switching) or quoting English; not the standard German word (standard: „hier“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte hier bleiben—oder, wie du immer sagst, "stay here"?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please stay here—or, as you always say, "stay here"?

definitions.native: HERE (proper name/brand, e.g., the map service)
definitions.note: Often written in all caps as a brand name (HERE Technologies / HERE WeGo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Route in HERE gespeichert und schicke sie dir gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved the route in HERE and I’ll send it to you in a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte herein!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come in!

definitions.note: Often formal or written; refers to something being contained within a document, container, or text (“herein” = within this/inside here).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hierin stehen alle wichtigen Informationen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the important information is written in here.

definitions.note: past participle of „hereinkommen“; commonly used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gerade hereingekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He just came in.

definitions.note: past participle of „hereinlassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Türsteher hat uns nicht hereingelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bouncer didn’t let us in.

definitions.note: Simple past of "hereinkommen" (often used in storytelling or written narration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als ich gerade telefonierte, kam er plötzlich hereinkam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As I was just on the phone, he suddenly came in.

definitions.note: Often used for entering a room or building; also common as an invitation (e.g., "Kommen Sie bitte herein!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er möchte hereinkommen, aber die Tür ist abgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to come in, but the door is locked.

definitions.note: Often used for letting someone enter a room/building.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mich bitte hereinlassen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please let me in?

definitions.note: A friendly, polite-sounding invitation to enter (often used by shopkeepers or hosts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hereinspaziert, bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come in, please!

definitions.native: to let in, to allow in
definitions.note: often used with an object/pronoun: jemanden hereinlassen = to let someone in
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mich bitte hereinzulassen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please let me in?

definitions.note: Past participle of „herbringen“ (to bring here).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Kisten aus dem Auto hergebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought the boxes here from the car.

definitions.note: Past participle of "herfahren"; indicates movement toward the speaker (often used with "sein" in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist mit dem Auto hergefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came here by car.

definitions.note: past participle of „herführen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Verdächtigen zur Wache hergeführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police brought the suspect to the station.

definitions.note: Past participle of "herkommen"; typically used with "sein" (e.g., "ist hergekommen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gerade hergekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He just came over here.

definitions.note: Past participle of the separable verb „herschicken“ (to send someone/something here).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir die Unterlagen hergeschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you the documents here.

definitions.note: Past participle of „herschicken“; often used with „haben“ (e.g. „hat … hergeschickt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir die Unterlagen hergeschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sent me the documents over.

definitions.note: past participle of „herstellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto wurde in Deutschland hergestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car was manufactured in Germany.

definitions.note: Often used as a separable verb, especially in the imperative: „Hör her!“ = “Listen up!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst jetzt gut herhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to listen closely now.

definitions.note: Simple past of „herkommen“ (to come here).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern herkam er erst spät nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he didn’t come home until late.

definitions.note: often used to ask about the origin of something (e.g. “Woher kommt das?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Woher soll das Geld herkommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is the money supposed to come from?

definitions.note: with the particle “her-”, it means moving toward the speaker/this place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst nicht extra herkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t have to come here специально (just for that).

definitions.note: Often used in questions like: „Woher kommst du?“ (= Where are you from?)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Woher herkommst du eigentlich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you come from, actually?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „herkommen“; often used with a separated prefix (e.g., „kommt … her“), but here the example keeps the exact form „herkommt“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fragt, wo er herkommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asks where he comes from.

definitions.note: Often used as an exclamation to show annoyance, surprise, or impatience.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Herrgott, das dauert ja ewig!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh my God, this is taking forever!

definitions.note: Expresses surprise, annoyance, or worry (mild exclamation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Herrje, ich habe schon wieder meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh dear, I forgot my key again!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten einen herrlichen Tag am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a wonderful day at the lake.

definitions.note: adjective inflected form; often used before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten herrliche Ferien am Meer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had wonderful holidays by the sea.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "herrlich" (often used to express strong positive feeling, like "wonderful").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ausblick ist heute herrlicher als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view is more wonderful today than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten herrliches Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had wonderful weather.

definitions.note: often used for ruling over a country/area or being in control
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der König will über das Land herrschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king wants to rule over the country.

definitions.note: used for situations, feelings, weather, conditions, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Stadt kann große Aufregung herrschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There can be great excitement in the city.

definitions.note: Often used for a person ruling (a king/queen) or for something being prevalent (e.g., silence, chaos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In diesem Land herrscht ein König.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A king rules in this country.

definitions.note: Simple past of „herrschen“; used for a person or government ruling over a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der König herrschte viele Jahre über das Land.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king ruled over the country for many years.

definitions.note: Simple past of „herrschen“; used for conditions or situations (e.g., silence, chaos, peace).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Raum herrschte plötzlich Stille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, silence prevailed in the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Firma kann Autos in Deutschland herstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This company can manufacture cars in Germany.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like "wiederherstellen" (restore) or "Kontakt/Ordnung/Verbindung herstellen" (establish contact/order/a connection).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen den Kontakt zu unseren Nachbarn herstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to establish contact with our neighbors.

definitions.note: Often used together with „um … herum“ (“around …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sitzen um das Feuer herum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are sitting around the fire.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean moving/being around without a clear direction (e.g., walking around, lying around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder laufen im Park herum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are running around in the park.

definitions.note: Often used in separable verb forms (e.g., „herumlaufen“ = to walk around) or with movement/location to mean being somewhere without a clear direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir laufen den ganzen Tag herum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk around all day.

definitions.note: past participle of „herumführen“; often used with „werden“ (passive) for guided tours.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wurden durch das Museum herumgeführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were shown around the museum.

definitions.note: past participle of "herumreisen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist letztes Jahr durch Europa herumgereist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She traveled around Europe last year.

definitions.native: to fool around, to mess around
definitions.note: colloquial; often implies wasting time by being silly instead of doing something seriously
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf, herumzualbern, und mach bitte deine Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop fooling around and please do your homework.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean movement downward (e.g., herunterkommen, herunterfallen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte die Treppe herunter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come down the stairs!

definitions.native: to fall down; to fall off
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch ist vom Tisch herunterfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book fell off the table.

definitions.note: past participle of „herunterfallen“ (usually used with „sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas ist heruntergefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass fell down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Datei heruntergeladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I downloaded the file.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean “out/into view” (e.g., hervorkommen = come out, stand out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus dem Nebel trat plötzlich eine Gestalt hervor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A figure suddenly emerged from the fog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Entscheidung hervorbringt viele Probleme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This decision brings about many problems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen war hervorragend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was excellent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen schmeckt hervorragend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food tastes excellent.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine hervorragende Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an excellent idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein hervorragender Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an excellent film.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt eine Kette mit einem herzförmigen Anhänger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s wearing a necklace with a heart-shaped pendant.

definitions.note: Often used in greetings, welcomes, and thanks (e.g., „herzlich willkommen“, „herzlichen Dank“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich begrüße Sie herzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I greet you warmly.

definitions.note: Describes a person or action as lacking compassion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine herzlose Bemerkung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a heartless remark.

definitions.native: to come here, to come over
definitions.note: Used as a 'zu'-infinitive form of the verb (e.g., after another verb like hoffen, versuchen, vergessen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, bald herzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to come here soon.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used with another verb, e.g. to express purpose or necessity)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma plant, neue Batterien in Deutschland herzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company plans to manufacture new batteries in Germany.

definitions.note: Indicates movement or direction toward the speaker/this side (often used with verbs like kommen, gehen, rufen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte herüber!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come over here!

definitions.note: often used for driving/chasing someone or an animal (sometimes with dogs)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Hunde hetzen den Hasen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dogs chase the hare.

definitions.note: often used about stirring people up against someone (e.g., spreading hate)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man darf nicht gegen andere Menschen hetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not incite hatred against other people.

definitions.note: Often used for inciting people against someone or something (e.g., in politics or propaganda).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hetzt die Leute gegeneinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He incites people against each other.

definitions.note: Used for driving an animal (or someone) to chase another.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hetzt die Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chases the cat.

definitions.note: Often used as colloquial 1st-person singular present without the -e (instead of „ich heule“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich heul gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm about to cry.

definitions.note: Often used for loud, intense crying (especially by children).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind fängt an zu heulen, weil es sein Spielzeug verloren hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child starts to cry because it lost its toy.

definitions.note: Used for animals, wind, or sirens making a long, loud sound.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht heulen die Wölfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night the wolves howl.

definitions.note: often used for crying loudly (like a child) or for animals howling
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum heulst du schon wieder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you crying again?

definitions.note: Often used for loud crying (e.g., a child) or animals howling; can also be used figuratively for things like wind or sirens.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby heult die ganze Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is crying the whole time.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „heulen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund heulte die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog howled all night.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „heulen“; often used for loud crying.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind heulte vor Schmerz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child cried in pain.

definitions.note: Colloquial/short form of „heute“ (common in speech and informal writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heut habe ich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I don’t have time.

definitions.note: colloquial/poetic short form of „heute“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heut habe ich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I don't have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute habe ich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I don’t have time.

definitions.note: Used before a noun; this is an inflected form of the adjective "heutig".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die heutige Sitzung beginnt um neun Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today's meeting starts at nine o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der heutigen Sitzung sprechen wir über das neue Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In today's meeting, we're talking about the new project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heutzutage arbeiten viele Menschen von zu Hause aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nowadays, many people work from home.

definitions.note: informal; used to greet someone or to get someone's attention
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hey, kannst du mir kurz helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey, can you help me for a moment?

definitions.note: informal greeting
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hi, wie geht's?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi, how’s it going?

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „halten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hielt das Baby ganz vorsichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He held the baby very carefully.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of "halten", used for hypothetical/conditional situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hielte dich fest, wenn ich könnte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would hold you tight if I could.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of "halten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hielten die Tür für mich offen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They held the door open for me.

definitions.note: simple past (du-form) of "halten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hieltest mir die Tür auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You held the door open for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am here.

definitions.native: in doing so, in the process, in this context
definitions.note: Often used to refer back to what was just mentioned (e.g., an action, procedure, or situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hierbei musst du besonders vorsichtig sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In doing so, you have to be especially careful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst hierbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to stay here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du müde bist, hierbleibst du einfach zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re tired, you just stay here at home.

definitions.note: Often used to refer back to something just mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hierfür brauchst du ein Passwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For this, you need a password.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern Abend hiergeblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed here last night.

definitions.note: Indicates movement toward the speaker or current location.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte hierher!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come over here!

definitions.native: asked to come here, requested to come here
definitions.note: Used as the past participle (Partizip II) meaning someone was asked/requested to come to this place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Sie hierhergebeten, weil ich mit Ihnen sprechen möchte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I asked you to come here because I want to talk to you.

definitions.note: past participle of „hierherbringen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das Paket hierhergebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brought the package here.

definitions.note: Past participle of „hierherführen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Guide hat uns hierhergeführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide led us here.

definitions.note: Past participle of "hierherkommen"; used with "sein" in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern Abend hierhergekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came here last night.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" to form the perfect tense (e.g. "Wir sind hierhergezogen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind vor zwei Jahren hierhergezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We moved here two years ago.

definitions.note: simple past tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum hierherkamst du so spät?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you come here so late?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst sofort hierherkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to come here right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn er heute hierherkommt, können wir alles besprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he comes here today, we can discuss everything.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „hierherkommen“, used after verbs like „versuchen“, „hoffen“, „vergessen“, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke, dass du versucht hast, hierherzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for trying to come here.

definitions.note: refers to movement/direction toward the speaker’s location
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte hierhin!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come here!

definitions.note: Often used with an object: etwas hierlassen = to leave something here.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du sollst den Schlüssel hierlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should leave the key here.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or written language (letters, emails, official statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hiermit bestätige ich den Termin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hereby confirm the appointment.

definitions.note: As a verb, it’s typically written as two words („hier sein“). If you require the exact form „hiersein“, it may appear as a nonstandard/merged spelling (e.g., for tagging, wordplay, or emphasis).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss morgen um acht hiersein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to be here at eight tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually written as two words: „hier sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst hiersein, wenn der Arzt kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to be here when the doctor comes.

definitions.note: Refers back to something nearby or already mentioned; often used with amounts or parts (e.g., “two of these/from this”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme drei Äpfel, und zwei hiervon sind für dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take three apples, and two of these are for you.

definitions.note: Common in more formal writing and speech; often refers back to something just mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hierzu habe ich noch eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have another question about this.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, hierzubleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to stay here.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „heißen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher hieß er Peter, aber jetzt heißt er Paul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used to be called Peter, but now he is called Paul.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher hießen sie anders.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They used to be called something else.

definitions.note: Slang; means being intoxicated/under the influence (often cannabis).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin high.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m high.

definitions.note: imperative (command) form, used to tell one person to help
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hilf mir bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help me, please!

definitions.note: Used as an urgent call for assistance (like “Help!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hilfe! Ich kann meine Tasche nicht finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help! I can't find my bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne meinen Pass bin ich im Ausland völlig hilflos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without my passport, I’m completely helpless abroad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke, das war sehr hilfreich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks, that was very helpful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Nachbarin ist sehr hilfsbereit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our neighbor is very helpful.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „helfen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hilfst mir mit den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You help me with the homework.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „helfen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hilft seiner Freundin bei den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helps his girlfriend with the homework.

definitions.note: Used as a mild exclamation to show surprise, annoyance, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Himmel, das ist ja teuer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Heavens, that’s expensive!

definitions.native: to there, there (away from the speaker)
definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement to show direction away from the speaker (e.g., hingehen, hinfahren).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe jetzt hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going there now.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement to indicate direction away from the speaker or toward a place that’s being pointed out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte hin und frag ihn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go over there and ask him.

definitions.note: Often used with a verb of motion to show movement away from the speaker (e.g., hingehen = go there).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe jetzt hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going there now.

definitions.note: Indicates movement/direction downwards; often used with verbs like gehen, steigen, fallen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stieg die Treppe hinab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went down the stairs.

definitions.note: Indicates movement from a higher place to a lower one; often used with verbs like „gehen“, „steigen“, „blicken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir stiegen den steilen Weg hinab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went down the steep path.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement to emphasize direction upward (e.g., hinaufgehen = go up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm schnell hinauf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come up quickly!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion to indicate direction away from the speaker (e.g., going up stairs/mountain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen die Treppe hinauf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go up the stairs.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement (e.g., gehen, kommen) or with the preposition „nach“: „nach draußen hinaus“ = out (to the outside).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte hinaus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go out!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion (e.g., gehen, schauen) or in separable verbs like „hinausgehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte hinaus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go out!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion (e.g., gehen, laufen) or in phrases like „nach draußen / hinaus“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte hinaus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go outside!

definitions.note: Used for going from inside to outside; separable verb (e.g., ich gehe hinaus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde jetzt hinausgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to go outside now.

definitions.native: to go outside, to go out
definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of „hinausgehen“ (often used after verbs like „versuchen“, „planen“, „vergessen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, jeden Tag hinauszugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to go outside every day.

definitions.native: to manage (to do something), to get done
definitions.note: Common in everyday speech; often means managing to do something (sometimes despite difficulty).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, wir hinbekommen das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, we’ll manage to do it.

definitions.note: Means bringing something to a place away from the speaker (often translated with “there/over”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Paket morgen hinbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take the package there tomorrow.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German: “Das bringe ich hin!” = “I can manage that / I’ll get that done.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, ich kann das schon hinbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, I can manage that.

definitions.note: Often used with: „jemanden/etwas an etwas hindern“ (to stop someone/something from doing something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das schlechte Wetter kann uns daran hindern, spazieren zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bad weather can prevent us from going for a walk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stau hinderte uns daran, pünktlich anzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic jam prevented us from arriving on time.

definitions.note: often used with verbs of motion (e.g., gehen, fahren) to emphasize passing from one side to the other
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch den Park hindurch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk through the park.

definitions.note: Often used with a verb of motion (e.g., gehen, kommen) to emphasize movement inward; can also be used as a separable prefix (e.g., hineingehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte hinein!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come in!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion to mean “(go/come) in/inside,” and commonly paired with another word like „hineingehen“ or „hinein in …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte hinein!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come in!

definitions.note: Often used with movement (e.g., with verbs like gehen/kommen/werfen) and can be used as a separable prefix (e.g., hineingehen = go in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte hinein!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come in!

definitions.note: past participle of „hineingehen“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist schnell hineingegangen, weil es draußen kalt war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went in quickly because it was cold outside.

definitions.note: Infinitive of a separable verb (hinein + gehen). In many conjugated forms, the parts split (e.g., „Ich gehe hinein.“), but here the example keeps the full infinitive „hineingehen“ exactly as written.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen jetzt hineingehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to go in now.

definitions.native: get into (a situation), end up in
definitions.note: Often used for getting into trouble or a difficult situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist in Schwierigkeiten hineingeraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got into trouble.

definitions.native: go there, drive there (travel there by vehicle)
definitions.note: Means traveling/going to a place (often contrasted with "herfahren" = come here by vehicle). Used with a destination or context that implies “there/to that place.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hinfahren morgen mit dem Zug nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to Berlin by train tomorrow.

definitions.native: to lead there, to guide there
definitions.note: "hin-" emphasizes movement to a place away from the speaker ("there").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich zum Bahnhof hinführen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can lead you to the train station.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively for a result or conclusion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zu viel Stress kann zu Problemen hinführen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Too much stress can lead to problems.

definitions.note: simple past of „hängen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Bild hing früher über dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The picture used to hang above the sofa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Kuchen zur Party hingebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought the cake to the party.

definitions.note: Past participle of „hinfahren“; typically used with „sein“ (e.g., „Ich bin ... hingefahren.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern mit dem Bus zur Schule hingefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I went to school by bus.

definitions.note: Past participle of „hinfallen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin auf der Treppe hingefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell down on the stairs.

definitions.note: Past participle of „hingehen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist hingegangen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist zu ihr hingegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went over to her.

definitions.note: Used to contrast two statements; often appears after the topic being contrasted (e.g., „Ich …, du hingegen …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag Kaffee; Tee hingegen trinke ich selten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like coffee; on the other hand, I rarely drink tea.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form, often used in reported speech (e.g. ‘he says that I go/that I’m going’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich hingehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that I’m going (there).

definitions.note: Often used with a specific destination or person: „zu + Dativ“ (e.g., zu ihm/zu der Party hingehen). Emphasizes the direction/going to that place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute Abend zu der Party hingehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to go to the party tonight.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „hingehen“; „hin-“ emphasizes going away from the speaker to a place (often “over there”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum hingehst du nicht einfach zu ihm?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you just go over to him?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "hingehen"; often used with a destination (e.g., to an event or place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hingeht jeden Freitag zum Training.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes to practice every Friday.

definitions.note: Used to say that someone/something is (or is not) in the correct place; often implies ‘this is where it should be’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bücher gehören ins Regal; dort gehören sie hin, dort gehören sie hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books belong on the shelf; that’s where they belong.

definitions.native: belonged (there), was meant to be there
definitions.note: Past participle of "hingehören"; often used with "hat" (e.g., "Das hat hier nicht hingehört").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat hier nicht hingehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That didn’t belong here.

definitions.note: colloquial; past participle often used with „haben“ (e.g. „Ich habe es hingekriegt.“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es endlich hingekriegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finally managed to do it.

definitions.note: past participle of "hinlegen"; often used with "haben" (Perfekt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch auf den Tisch hingelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book down on the table.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „hängen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bilder hingen früher im Flur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pictures used to hang in the hallway.

definitions.note: Usually used for carrying out a death sentence (capital punishment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gefangene wurde hingerichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was executed.

definitions.note: Often used for an execution as a death penalty; also used for a brutal killing in a war/crime context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gefangene wurde am Morgen hingerichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner was executed in the morning.

definitions.note: past participle of "hinsetzen"; often used with "sich" ("sich hinsetzen" = to sit down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich auf die Bank hingesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sat down on the bench.

definitions.note: past participle of „hinstellen“ (separable verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Tasche vor die Tür hingestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the bag down in front of the door.

definitions.note: Past participle, used with "haben" (e.g., "hat ... hingetan").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch auf den Tisch hingetan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative: „jemanden auf etwas hinweisen“ = to point something out to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn darauf hingewiesen, dass der Termin heute ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pointed out to him that the appointment is today.

definitions.note: Usually used with „sein“ or „sich fühlen“ + „zu“ (dative): „zu jemandem/etwas hingezogen sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich zu dieser Stadt hingezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel drawn to this city.

definitions.note: Colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, er will dich gleich hinhauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, he’s about to hit you.

definitions.native: to work out, to be alright
definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „Das muss hinhauen“ / „Das haut hin“ (= that should work out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das muss heute hinhauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That has to work out today.

definitions.native: to get there, to reach (a place)
definitions.note: Often used with a destination (e.g., „dort/da“ or a place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen vor 8 Uhr dort hinkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get there before 8 o’clock.

definitions.note: Informal; often used for successfully handling something difficult or complicated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das heute noch hinkriegen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you manage to get that done today?

definitions.note: often used literally (walking with a limp) and also figuratively to mean something is flawed or doesn’t quite work
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall hinkt er noch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he still limps.

definitions.native: to put down, to lay down
definitions.note: Often used with objects; separable in finite forms (e.g. „Ich lege es hin.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will das Buch auf den Tisch hinlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to put the book down on the table.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich hinlegen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich kurz hinlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to lie down for a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert war hinreißend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was delightful.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich hinsetzen = to sit down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte hinsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sit down.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (something you put somewhere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Tasche bitte dort hinstellen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please put the bag there?

definitions.native: in the back, at the back
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sitzen hinten im Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are sitting in the back of the car.

definitions.note: Can be used as a preposition (takes dative for location, accusative for movement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stuhl steht hinter dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair is behind the table.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive) to mean farther back/at the back.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte benutzen Sie die hintere Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please use the rear door.

definitions.native: one after another, in a row
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder standen hintereinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were standing one after another (in a row).

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of critically examining or challenging something (e.g., an assumption or decision).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hinterfragt die Entscheidung des Chefs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She questions the boss’s decision.

definitions.note: past participle of „hintergehen“; used with „haben/sein“ or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich hintergangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He betrayed me.

definitions.note: Often used for betraying someone’s trust; can also mean being unfaithful to a partner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich nicht hintergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to betray you.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „kommen“ or „laufen“ in the sense of doing something later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir essen erst und gehen hinterher ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll eat first and then go to the movies afterwards.

definitions.note: Often used to mean following someone/something, e.g. „jemandem hinterherlaufen“ (run after someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund läuft dem Ball hinterher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog runs after the ball.

definitions.note: Describes someone’s behavior as deceitful in a mean way (not just quietly clever).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde es hinterhältig, hinter jemandes Rücken schlecht über ihn zu reden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think it’s underhanded to speak badly about someone behind their back.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving something behind or leaving a message for someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hinterlasse dir eine Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll leave you a message.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving something after you go (e.g., a message, traces, an inheritance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir eine Nachricht hinterlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left me a message.

definitions.note: Second-person plural form (you all); often used as an imperative in requests or instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte hinterlasst eure Telefonnummer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please leave your phone number.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „hinterlassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hinterließ eine Nachricht auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left a message on the table.

definitions.note: Used for leaving something behind physically or leaving a trace/impact (e.g., marks, an impression).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hinterlässt Pfotenabdrücke im Schnee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog leaves paw prints in the snow.

definitions.note: contraction of „hinter dem“ (dative, masculine/neuter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund liegt hinterm Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is lying behind the house.

definitions.note: Contraction of “hinter das” (used with neuter nouns with “das”, often in spoken German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lege das Kissen hinters Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the pillow behind the sofa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hintrittst ans Fenster und schaust hinaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You step up to the window and look outside.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used as the separable verb phrase „hin tun“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wohin soll ich die Tasche hintun?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where should I put the bag?

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion to mean movement down away from the speaker (e.g., going downstairs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe die Treppe hinunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going down the stairs.

definitions.note: indicates movement away from the speaker (as opposed to "herunter")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er geht die Treppe hinunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He goes down the stairs.

definitions.note: Implies movement away from the speaker, often to a lower place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh die Treppe hinunter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go down the stairs!

definitions.note: Often used as a separable verb in finite forms: "Ich gehe hinunter."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen jetzt hinuntergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to go downstairs now.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „hinweggehen“ (go away) or in the pattern „über … hinweg“ meaning “over/across …” in a figurative or literal sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ging ohne ein Wort hinweg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went away without a word.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“ and fixed expressions like „über etw. hinweg“ (= over/across something, figuratively also ‘to get over something’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schmerz geht langsam hinweg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pain slowly goes away.

definitions.native: to overlook, to ignore (something), to turn a blind eye (to something)
definitions.note: Often used with „über“ + accusative: „über etwas hinwegsehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir dürfen über diese Fehler nicht hinwegsehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must not overlook these mistakes.

definitions.native: to get over (something), to move on
definitions.note: Often used with „über + Akk.“ (e.g. „über etwas hinwegkommen“ = to get over something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, bald darüber hinwegzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to get over it soon.

definitions.note: “hin-” indicates movement away from the speaker (toward that place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollte unbedingt hinwollen, aber ich hatte keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really wanted to go there, but I didn’t have time.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „kommen“, „fügen“, or „addieren“ (e.g., „hinzukommen“, „hinzufügen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zu den Kosten kommen noch Steuern hinzu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Taxes are added on top of the costs.

definitions.note: Often used with an object you add something to: „etwas (zu etwas) hinzufügen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte noch Zucker hinzufügen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please add some more sugar?

definitions.note: past participle of „hinzufügen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat hinzugefügt“) or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe noch ein Foto hinzugefügt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I added another photo.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of "hingehen"; often used with another verb (e.g., "versuchen, hinzugehen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Lust, heute Abend hinzugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel like going there tonight.

definitions.native: to be added, to come in addition
definitions.note: often used to say that something extra is added on top of what already exists (e.g., extra costs, tasks, people)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zu den Kosten kann noch eine Gebühr hinzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An additional fee may be added to the costs.

definitions.note: often used with an object like „etwas hinzufügen“ (to add something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, dem Dokument noch ein Foto hinzuzufügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to add another photo to the document.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion to mean going/moving to the other side (e.g., hinübergehen, hinüberschwimmen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen jetzt hinüber zur anderen Straßenseite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going over to the other side of the street now.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected form; used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben heute eine historische Rede gehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We heard a historical speech today.

definitions.note: Adjective in the weak ending form (e.g., after a definite article: „den historischen …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchen morgen den historischen Marktplatz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re visiting the historical market square tomorrow.

definitions.note: often used for arguments, discussions, or debates
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten eine hitzige Diskussion über Politik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a heated discussion about politics.

definitions.note: Used to show you are thinking, uncertain, or not fully convinced (like “hmm” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hm, ich weiß nicht, ob das eine gute Idee ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hmm, I don't know if that's a good idea.

definitions.note: Used to show hesitation, thinking, or doubt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hörst dir das Lied an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You listen to the song.

definitions.note: Used with „auf“ as part of the separable verb „aufhören“ (e.g., „Du hörst auf.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hörst jetzt auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stop now.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „hören“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hörst du die Musik?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you hear the music?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufhören“; it’s often used with „auf“ at the end of the clause (e.g., „hört … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hört jetzt auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stops now.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "hören".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hört die Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hears the music.

definitions.note: From the verb „zuhören“ (to listen). Often used with „zu“ (e.g., „hört zu“ / „hört mir zu“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hört dir aufmerksam zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She listens to you attentively.

definitions.note: Simple past of „anhören“; the particle „an“ is often separated (e.g., „hörte … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hörte mir das Lied gestern Abend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listened to the song yesterday evening.

definitions.note: Simple past of „aufhören“; often used with „auf“ (e.g., „hörte auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hörte sofort auf zu reden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stopped talking right away.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "hören"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hörte ein Geräusch im Flur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a noise in the hallway.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufhören“; in a sentence, „auf“ is often separated (e.g. „hörten … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hörten um Mitternacht auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stopped at midnight.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "hören" for "we/you (plural)/they".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hörten die Musik ganz leise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They heard the music very quietly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ein hübsches Kleid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a pretty dress.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective too (meaning “pretty”); as an adverb it describes how something is done.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat sich hübsch angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dressed nicely.

definitions.note: Adjective ending form of „hübsch“ (e.g., with a feminine noun or after an article like „die/eine“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine hübsche Blume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a pretty flower.

definitions.note: adjective ending form of "hübsch" (e.g., with masculine accusative or plural dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den hübschen Jungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the handsome boy.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "hübsch".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Mantel ist hübscher als der alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new coat is prettier than the old one.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a neuter noun (e.g., „ein hübsches Kleid“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein hübsches Kleid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a pretty dress.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "hübsch".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die hübscheste in der Klasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the prettiest in the class.

definitions.note: Subjunctive (Konjunktiv II) form of „helfen“; often replaced in everyday speech by „würde helfen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hülfe dir gern, aber ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would gladly help you, but I don’t have time.

definitions.note: Often used for small, light jumps (e.g., like a rabbit or a child).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder hüpfen im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are hopping in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hase hüpft über die Wiese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rabbit hops across the meadow.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „hüpfen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hase hüpfte über die Wiese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rabbit hopped across the meadow.

definitions.note: Often used for looking after children or animals (e.g., sheep).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hüte heute die Kinder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking after the children today.

definitions.note: Often used for taking care of someone/something (e.g., children, animals) or keeping something safe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Kinder hüten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please watch the children?

definitions.note: Often used for watching over animals (e.g., a shepherd watching sheep).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hütet die Schafe auf der Wiese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watches over the sheep in the meadow.

definitions.note: A brand name (Apple smartphone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein iPhone zu Hause vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my iPhone at home.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular subject pronoun (used for the speaker)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Wohnung ist ideal für eine kleine Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This apartment is ideal for a small family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der ideale Zeitpunkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the ideal time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei konnte den Täter schnell identifizieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were able to identify the perpetrator quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei identifiziert den Täter anhand von Fingerabdrücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police identify the perpetrator using fingerprints.

definitions.note: often used as the past participle in the present perfect (e.g. „hat ... identifiziert“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Täter identifiziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have identified the perpetrator.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei identifizierte den Täter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police identified the perpetrator.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Fotos sind identisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two photos are identical.

definitions.note: Used to express disgust.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Igitt, das ist eklig!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eww, that’s gross!

definitions.note: Commonly used as the informal imperative (du) form in commands (e.g., "Ignorier das!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ignorier das bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please ignore that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ignoriere die Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ignore the message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte ignorieren Sie die E-Mail von gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please ignore yesterday’s email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum ignorierst du meine Nachrichten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you ignoring my messages?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ignoriert meine Nachrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ignores my messages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ignorierte meine Nachricht den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ignored my message all day.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ignorierten die Warnungen und gingen trotzdem weiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ignored the warnings and kept going anyway.

definitions.note: dative form of „er“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe ihm das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give him the book.

definitions.note: accusative (direct object) form of „er“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ihn jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see him every day.

definitions.note: dative plural form of „sie“ (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe ihnen das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give them the book.

definitions.note: possessive determiner; meaning depends on context (singular feminine = “her”, plural = “their”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anna findet ihr Handy nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Anna can’t find her phone.

definitions.note: informal second-person plural pronoun (used to address more than one person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr seid heute sehr leise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) are very quiet today.

definitions.note: possessive (shows something belongs to a woman/girl)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ihr Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is her book.

definitions.note: possessive (shows something belongs to them)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ihr Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is their house.

definitions.note: dative object pronoun (often used after verbs like helfen/geben)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe ihr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help her.

definitions.note: Dative form of „sie“ (she).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe ihr das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give her the book.

definitions.note: possessive determiner for „sie“; can mean “her” (she) or “their” (they), depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihre Kinder sind schon in der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their children are already at school.

definitions.note: Possessive pronoun/determiner form used with feminine singular nouns (e.g., ihre Tasche) and with plural nouns (e.g., ihre Freunde).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sucht ihre Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is looking for her keys.

definitions.note: Dative singular masculine/neuter or dative plural form of the possessive determiner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe ihrem Bruder.
