definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help her brother.

definitions.note: Dative singular masculine/neuter or dative plural form of "ihr" (used for “to/for her” or “to/for them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe ihrem Bruder das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving the book to her brother.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner form used with masculine accusative singular nouns (e.g. „ihren Bruder“) or plural dative nouns (e.g. „mit ihren Freunden“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ihren Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see her brother.

definitions.note: Possessive form of „ihr“ used before a noun (e.g., accusative masculine singular: „ihren Bruder“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ihren Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see her brother.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner form of „ihr“ used with dative feminine singular or genitive (feminine singular / plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche mit ihrer Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m talking to her/their mother.

definitions.note: Form of "ihr" used for feminine singular in dative/genitive (and also for plural in some cases); often means "her" or "their" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mit ihrer Mutter gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with her/their mother.

definitions.note: dative (plural) form of the personal pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe ihrer das Geld morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll give them the money tomorrow.

definitions.note: genitive form of the personal pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gedenken ihrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We remember her/them.

definitions.note: Genitive singular feminine or genitive plural form of the possessive determiner “ihr”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen ihres Autos kommt sie heute zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of her car, she is late today.

definitions.note: Genitive singular feminine or genitive plural form of the possessive pronoun/determiner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen ihres Autos kommt sie heute zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of her car, she is late today.

definitions.native: because of her/them, for her/their sake
definitions.note: Refers to either “her” (feminine singular) or “them” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind ihretwegen zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of her/them, we’re late.

definitions.note: used as the Roman numeral for 3 (often written as “III”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kapitel III ist sehr kurz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Chapter III is very short.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist illegal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is illegal.

definitions.note: Contraction of "in dem"; used with the dative (often before masculine/neuter nouns, e.g. "im Park", "im Sommer").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet in the park.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., in nominative/accusative feminine singular or plural without an article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine imaginäre Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an imaginary friend.

definitions.note: Adjective in a declined form (e.g., after a determiner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind hat einen imaginären Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has an imaginary friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kinder imitieren oft die Erwachsenen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children often imitate adults.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin immer pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am always on time.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned/literary; more common today: „für immer“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich immerdar lieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will love you forever.

definitions.note: Often used to point out a positive aspect or minimum in a situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat den ganzen Tag geregnet, aber immerhin ist es jetzt trocken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained all day, but at least it’s dry now.

definitions.note: Often used to complain that something keeps happening or someone keeps doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er redet immerzu über die Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He talks about work all the time.

definitions.note: Often used with "gegen" + accusative for what you’re vaccinating against (e.g., gegen Grippe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt impft die Kinder gegen Grippe, um sie zu impfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor vaccinates the children against the flu in order to vaccinate them.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland muss jedes Jahr viel Kaffee importieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany has to import a lot of coffee every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutschland importiert viel Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Germany imports a lot of coffee.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to mean powerless or ineffective; can also refer to sexual impotence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Unterstützung fühlte er sich der Situation gegenüber impotent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without support, he felt powerless in the face of the situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen improvisieren, weil der Plan nicht funktioniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to improvise because the plan isn't working.

definitions.note: Usually used with „sein“ + „zu“ + infinitive: „imstande sein, etwas zu tun“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nicht imstande, das allein zu machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not able to do that alone.

definitions.note: Used with dative for location (in/inside) and with accusative for motion or direction (into).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am in the school.

definitions.note: Common preposition. With dative it often means location (“in”); with accusative it often means movement/direction (“into”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am in the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Verhalten ist inakzeptabel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This behavior is unacceptable.

definitions.note: often used after a noun phrase, like “(something) included”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Frühstück ist im Preis inbegriffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Breakfast is included in the price.

definitions.note: Introduces a subordinate clause that explains the means/method (how something is done).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verbessert sein Deutsch, indem er jeden Tag liest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He improves his German by reading every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Hände verschränkten sich ineinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two hands clasped into each other.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde ist infiziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound is infected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde ist infiziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound is infected.

definitions.native: as a result of, due to
definitions.note: Used with the genitive (often + von + dative in spoken German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Infolge des Sturms sind viele Flüge ausgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a result of the storm, many flights were canceled.

definitions.note: Depending on context, this form can mean “I inform” (present tense) or “inform!” (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich informiere dich morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll let you know tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with: jemanden (über etwas) informieren (= to inform someone about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich morgen über die Änderungen informieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will inform you about the changes tomorrow.

definitions.note: present tense form (e.g., „er/sie/es informiert“; also „ihr informiert“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer informiert die Eltern über den Ausflug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher informs the parents about the trip.

definitions.note: past participle; often used with „haben“ or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich gestern informiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I informed you yesterday.

definitions.note: describes someone who knows the relevant facts or is well-informed
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist gut informiert über das Thema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is well informed about the topic.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „informieren“ (e.g., „ich informierte“, „er/sie informierte“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich informierte sie sofort über die Änderung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I informed her immediately about the change.

definitions.note: Usually used in the phrase „nicht infrage kommen“ (= not to be an option).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eine Entschuldigung kommt nicht infrage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An apology is out of the question.

definitions.note: Often used in news/legal contexts; commonly with "werden" (e.g., "wurde inhaftiert").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde wegen Betrugs inhaftiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was imprisoned for fraud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wirkt manchmal ziemlich inkompetent.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss sometimes seems pretty incompetent.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used with verbs like „sein“ (to be) or „bleiben“ (to stay)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bleib bitte inne!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stay inside!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist warm drinnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s warm inside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich höre auf meine innere Stimme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I listen to my inner voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die inneren Organe sind sehr wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The internal organs are very important.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive (often with dative in everyday speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Innerhalb einer Woche bekommst du eine Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Within a week, you’ll get an answer.

definitions.note: Often used for feelings or reactions you don’t show outwardly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Innerlich war ich sehr nervös.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Internally, I was very nervous.

definitions.note: Often used about strong feelings or close relationships; also common in the phrase „innig lieben“ (“to love deeply”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie umarmte ihn innig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hugged him tightly.

definitions.note: Contraction of „in das“ (used with neuter singular „das“ and usually indicates movement/direction).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going into the movie theater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war insgeheim froh, dass das Treffen abgesagt wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was secretly glad that the meeting was canceled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Insgesamt habe ich drei Geschwister.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Overall, I have three siblings.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + dative (e.g., „auf etwas insistieren“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich insistiere auf einer Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I insist on an answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch kann mich jeden Tag inspirieren, mehr zu schreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book can inspire me every day to write more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin von ihrer Arbeit inspiriert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am inspired by her work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Turm ist instabil und könnte umfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tower is unstable and could fall over.

definitions.note: Used for installing software/apps, or setting up equipment so it’s ready to use.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Programm auf meinem Laptop installieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to install the program on my laptop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe instinktiv zurückgezuckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I instinctively recoiled.

definitions.note: This is the adjectival ending -e (e.g., with a feminine noun or after certain determiners).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie liest gern intellektuelle Bücher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes reading intellectual books.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr intelligent und lernt schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very intelligent and learns quickly.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (attributive adjective); the ending changes depending on gender/case/article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine intelligente Studentin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an intelligent student.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen intelligenten Kollegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an intelligent colleague.

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Bruder ist intelligenter als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is more intelligent than I am.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used here as a declension (e.g., before a neuter noun like „Kind“ or as a nominalized form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein intelligentes Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an intelligent child.

definitions.note: superlative form used with endings (e.g., after articles like „die“, „den“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die intelligentesten Schüler lösen die Aufgabe schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The most intelligent students solve the task quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe diese Woche einen intensiven Kurs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an intensive course this week.

definitions.note: Often used to mean working/studying with a lot of effort or focus.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe intensiv für die Prüfung gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I studied intensively for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich interessant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really interesting.

definitions.note: Used before a noun or after an article (weak declension).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine interessante Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an interesting idea.

definitions.note: This is the declined form of the adjective (used before a noun, or after certain determiners/prepositions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen interessanten Film gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw an interesting movie.

definitions.note: comparative form of "interessant"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch ist interessanter als der Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is more interesting than the movie.

definitions.note: Adjective in neuter form (e.g., with a neuter noun like „etwas“ or „ein Buch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist etwas Interessantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is something interesting.

definitions.note: superlative form; can be used with or without an ending depending on what it describes (e.g., der/die/das interessanteste …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das interessanteste Buch, das ich je gelesen habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the most interesting book I have ever read.

definitions.note: Often used with „sich … für“: „Ich interessiere mich für …“ = “I’m interested in …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Thema kann mich wirklich interessieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This topic can really interest me.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „du interessierst dich (für …)“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Interessierst du dich für Musik?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you interested in music?

definitions.note: Often used with „an“ + dative: „interessiert an …“ = interested in …
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin an Kunst interessiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am interested in art.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin sehr an Musik interessiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very interested in music.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich für etwas interessieren“ = to be interested in something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich interessierte mich schon als Kind für Sterne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was interested in stars even as a child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein internationales Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an international project.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with feminine nouns (nominative/accusative singular) or with plural nouns in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine internationale Konferenz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an international conference.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with certain cases/genders/numbers (e.g., weak/mixed declension)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir arbeiten an einem internationalen Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are working on an international project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man kann diese Aussage auf verschiedene Weise interpretieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can interpret this statement in different ways.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er interpretiert die Frage anders als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He interprets the question differently than I do.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Text ist falsch interpretiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The text is interpreted incorrectly.

definitions.note: Often used in journalism/media; also common in job contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Journalistin wird den Schauspieler interviewen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist will interview the actor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Journalist interviewt die Schauspielerin nach der Premiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist interviews the actress after the premiere.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist eher introvertiert und spricht nicht gern vor vielen Leuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is rather introverted and doesn't like speaking in front of many people.

definitions.note: present tense (3rd person singular) of „investieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er investiert jeden Monat etwas Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He invests a bit of money every month.

definitions.native: to what extent, in what way
definitions.note: Often used in indirect questions to ask for clarification or specifics.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können Sie erklären, inwiefern das für uns wichtig ist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you explain to what extent that is important for us?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich koche, und inzwischen deckst du den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cooking, and meanwhile you set the table.

definitions.note: Usually used with other words (e.g., „irgendwo“, „irgendwie“, „irgendwann“, „irgendein“) to mean “some-/any-” in an unspecified way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das irgendwo gesehen, aber ich weiß nicht mehr, wo genau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw that somewhere, but I don't remember exactly where.

definitions.note: Used mostly in combination with question words, e.g. "irgendwo" (somewhere/anywhere), "irgendjemand" (someone/anyone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendetwas gehört?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you heard anything?

definitions.note: Used when the exact person/thing doesn’t matter or is unknown; often with a noun (like “some kind of …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendein Buch über Berlin?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any book about Berlin?

definitions.note: Used with feminine nouns in nominative or accusative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendeine Frage?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any question?

definitions.note: used for an unspecified person or thing (dative masculine/neuter singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mit irgendeinem Kollegen darüber gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I talked about it with some colleague.

definitions.note: Dative masculine or neuter singular form of „irgendein“ (used when the noun is in the dative case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte irgendeinem Kollegen geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please give that to some colleague?

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular form of "irgendein".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir irgendeinen Stift geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me some/any pen?

definitions.note: Accusative masculine singular form of "irgendein" (used with masculine nouns in the accusative case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendeinen Stift für mich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any pen for me?

definitions.note: Used when the noun is omitted (like “anyone/someone”); this form is masculine nominative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann mir irgendeiner helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can someone help me?

definitions.note: Indefinite pronoun meaning an unspecified person; this form is masculine singular (e.g., 'irgendeiner kommt').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Irgendeiner hat an der Tür geklopft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Somebody knocked on the door.

definitions.note: means an unspecified thing; often used when it doesn’t matter what exactly
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche irgendetwas zu essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need something to eat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist irgendjemand zu Hause?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is someone home?

definitions.note: Dative form of "irgendjemand" (someone/anyone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte irgendjemandem erklären?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please explain that to someone?

definitions.note: accusative form of "irgendjemand" (used for a direct object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du heute irgendjemanden gesehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you see anyone today?

definitions.note: Refers to an unspecified time (in the past or future).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich irgendwann an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you sometime.

definitions.note: informal; often used when you don’t know or don’t want to specify what it is
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendwas zu trinken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have something to drink?

definitions.note: Plural form; used with plural nouns or as a pronoun meaning “any (ones)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendwelche Fragen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any questions?

definitions.note: used with plural nouns; means it doesn’t matter which ones / unspecified ones
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendwelche Fragen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any questions?

definitions.note: Used in questions/negatives to mean “any”; often implies “some kind of / any kind of.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du irgendwelchen Zucker?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any sugar?

definitions.note: refers to an unknown or unspecified person
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hat irgendwer meinen Schlüssel gesehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Has anyone seen my key?

definitions.note: Often used when something is hard to explain or when you're not sure exactly how.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das irgendwie schaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to manage that somehow.

definitions.note: Used when the exact place is unknown or not important.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Handy irgendwo im Haus liegen lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my phone somewhere in the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind kommt irgendwoher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind is coming from somewhere.

definitions.note: Refers to movement/direction (where to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen irgendwann irgendwohin fahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to go somewhere sometime.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a sarcastic or mocking tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Kommentar war ironisch gemeint.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His comment was meant ironically.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ironisch gesagt war der Tag am Ende doch ganz schön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ironically, in the end the day turned out to be quite nice after all.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist irre vor Wut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is crazy with anger.

definitions.note: colloquial/informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aussicht ist irre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view is amazing.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech; can also mean "awesome/amazing" in a positive, colloquial way depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist doch irre!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s crazy!

definitions.note: From the verb „irren“ (often used reflexively: „sich irren“ = to be mistaken).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich irre mich selten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m rarely mistaken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Werbung ist irreführend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advertisement is misleading.

definitions.native: to be mistaken; to be wrong
definitions.note: Often used in the construction „sich irren“ (= to be mistaken).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich irre, wenn ich glaube, dass das die richtige Lösung ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m mistaken if I think that’s the right solution.

definitions.note: More literary/poetic usage; refers to moving about without a clear direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nachts irre ich durch die leeren Straßen der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night I wander through the city’s empty streets.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular informal (du) form of the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du irrst dich, das ist nicht mein Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re mistaken; that isn’t my key.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "irren"; used when someone is mistaken (often in statements like "Wer das glaubt, irrt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er irrt, wenn er glaubt, das sei einfach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is mistaken if he thinks that’s easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich irrte mich bei der Adresse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was mistaken about the address.

definitions.note: Often used in a literary context for moving around without a clear direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er irrte stundenlang durch die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wandered through the city for hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe irrtümlich die falsche Datei gelöscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mistakenly deleted the wrong file.

definitions.note: Nonstandard/dialect spelling of standard German “ist”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er is heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is at home today.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech for insulating a building (heat/sound) as well as for separating something from others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Dach besser isolieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to insulate the roof better.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Dorf ist im Winter oft isoliert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village is often isolated in winter.

definitions.note: Often used for materials or buildings that keep heat/noise/electricity from passing through.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wasserleitung ist nicht gut isoliert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water pipe is not well insulated.

definitions.note: informal singular command (imperative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iss dein Gemüse!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat your vegetables!

definitions.note: Nonstandard/dialect spelling of „ist“ (from „sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das iss gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is good.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form of „essen“ (used when telling one person to eat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iss deinen Apfel!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat your apple!

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „essen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er isst jeden Morgen Müsli.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He eats muesli every morning.

definitions.note: Used as the auxiliary verb in the present perfect with certain verbs (especially movement or change of state).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nach Hause gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has gone home.

definitions.note: can refer to the Italian language or to something from Italy (e.g., Italian food, an Italian restaurant)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne Italienisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning Italian.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a noun (declined form of "italienisch")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag italienische Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Italian music.

definitions.note: adjective in accusative masculine/neuter singular or dative plural (weak/mixed endings), depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte einen italienischen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like an Italian coffee.

definitions.note: Used with a neuter noun in nominative or accusative singular (e.g., "italienisches Essen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte heute italienisches Essen kochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to cook Italian food today.

definitions.note: Old spelling of the imperative; today usually written "iss".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iß bitte dein Gemüse!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please eat your vegetables!

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „essen“ (he/she/it eats).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ißt einen Apfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He eats an apple.

definitions.note: Also used to confirm or agree with what someone said (like “yeah”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ja, ich komme morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, I’m coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: Also used to agree or confirm something (like “yeah”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ja, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, I’m coming right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ja, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, I'll come in a moment.

definitions.note: imperative (du-form) of "jagen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jag die Katze nicht vom Sofa!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t chase the cat off the sofa!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "jagen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich jage im Herbst im Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hunt in the forest in autumn.

definitions.note: Often used for pursuing someone or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich jage dem Bus hinterher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chase after the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Herbst gehen sie in den Wald, um zu jagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In autumn they go into the forest to hunt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder versuchen, einander im Park zu jagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children try to chase each other in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund jagt die Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chases the cat.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „jagen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund jagte die Katze durch den Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chased the cat through the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie jagten den Dieb durch die Straßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They chased the thief through the streets.

definitions.note: means over a long period of several years
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat jahrelang in Berlin gelebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lived in Berlin for years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Burg stand jahrhundertelang auf dem Hügel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle stood on the hill for centuries.

definitions.native: yeah, yeah; sure (said dismissively or impatiently)
definitions.note: Often expresses impatience, skepticism, or that you’re not really listening (not an enthusiastic “yes”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jaja, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yeah, yeah, I’ll be right there.

definitions.note: Often implies annoying or self-pitying complaining.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf zu jammern und fang an zu helfen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop whining and start helping!

definitions.note: Often used for complaining in an annoying way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er jammert schon wieder über das Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s whining about the weather again.

definitions.note: can describe the language or something from Japan
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne japanisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Japanese.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a noun (weak ending, e.g., after “die/diese/meine”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die japanische Küche ist sehr beliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Japanese cuisine is very popular.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak/mixed declension (e.g., after an article like „den/die/das“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne den japanischen Ausdruck.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning the Japanese expression.

definitions.note: adjective in masculine nominative singular, used before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein japanischer Film läuft heute Abend im Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Japanese film is playing at the cinema tonight.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun in the nominative or accusative singular (e.g. „japanisches Essen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte japanisches Essen probieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to try Japanese food.

definitions.note: Often used for firm agreement or acknowledgment (e.g., to an order); can sound formal or military.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jawohl, ich komme sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, I’m coming right away.

definitions.note: Used in the correlative construction “je …, desto/umso …” to show that one thing changes as another changes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mehr ich lerne, desto besser wird mein Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The more I learn, the better my German gets.

definitions.note: An interjection expressing discomfort, mild disgust, or dismay; often used like “jeez” (from “Jesus”) in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je, das stinkt ja furchtbar!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh dear, that smells awful!

definitions.note: Used in correlative comparisons (often with „desto/umso“ in the main clause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je früher wir losfahren, desto besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The earlier we leave, the better.

definitions.note: feminine nominative/accusative form of "jeder" (e.g., "jede Frau", "jede Woche")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jede Woche gehe ich dreimal ins Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every week I go to the gym three times.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of „jeder“ (used before a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jede Woche gehe ich schwimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every week I go swimming.

definitions.note: Dative masculine/neuter singular form of "jeder".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe jedem Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help every child.

definitions.note: Dative singular form of "jeder" (masculine/neuter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe jedem, der mich darum bittet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help everyone who asks me to.

definitions.note: Masculine accusative singular form of "jeder".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe jeden Tag meine Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see my neighbors every day.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular form of „jeder“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe jeden Tag meine Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see my neighbors every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme morgen vorbei; jedenfalls versuche ich es.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll come by tomorrow; anyway, I’ll try.

definitions.note: Often changes ending depending on case and gender (e.g., jeder/jede/jedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jeder Tag ist anders.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every day is different.

definitions.note: Means “everyone/each” when used by itself; it can also be used like “each/every” before a singular noun (with endings: jeder/jede/jedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jeder kann Deutsch lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone can learn German.

definitions.note: More formal than "jeder"; often used in official language (e.g., rules, laws).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jedermann muss sich an die Regeln halten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone has to follow the rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst mich jederzeit anrufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can call me anytime.

definitions.note: Neuter nominative/accusative form of "jeder" (used with neuter nouns like "Kind", "Auto", "Buch").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jedes Kind hat ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every child has a book.

definitions.note: neuter singular form of "jeder"; used before a neuter noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jedes Kind bekommt ein Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every child gets a present.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jedesmal, wenn ich Kaffee trinke, kann ich nachts nicht schlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every time I drink coffee, I can’t sleep at night.

definitions.note: Often also written as two words: „jedes Mal“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jedesmal, wenn ich ihn sehe, muss ich lachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every time I see him, I have to laugh.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollte kommen, jedoch hatte ich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to come; however, I didn’t have any time.

definitions.note: More formal than "jede"; often used in official or written language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jedwede Form von Gewalt ist inakzeptabel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Any form of violence is unacceptable.

definitions.note: more formal than "jeder"; often used in legal/official language
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jedweder Versuch, die Regeln zu umgehen, ist verboten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Any attempt to get around the rules is forbidden.

definitions.note: Used in more formal German; often interchangeable with "jede" in meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir akzeptieren jegliche Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We accept any help.

definitions.note: Used in formal or legal language; it means “any kind of / any” in a very general sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte vermeiden Sie jeglichen Kontakt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please avoid any contact.

definitions.note: Often used in questions or negatives; very common in the phrase „wie auch immer / was auch immer / wann auch immer“ is different from „jemals“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warst du jemals in Berlin?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you ever been to Berlin?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand hat an der Tür geklopft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone knocked at the door.

definitions.note: dative form of „jemand“ (used after verbs/prepositions that take the dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe jemandem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help someone.

definitions.note: accusative form of „jemand“ (used for the direct object)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne jemanden in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know someone in Berlin.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "jener" (more formal/literary than "diese" in everyday speech)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jene Kinder spielen im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those children are playing in the park.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "jener" (rather formal; contrasts with "diese" = these)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jene Bücher gehören mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those books belong to me.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of “jener” (used like “those” and often contrasted with “diese” = “these”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jene Bücher sind sehr interessant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those books are very interesting.

definitions.note: dative singular (masculine or neuter) of "jener"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit jenem Mann habe ich gestern gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with that man yesterday.

definitions.note: Accusative masculine singular or dative plural form of the demonstrative determiner/pronoun „jener“; more formal/literary than „der/die/das“ or „dieser“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme jenen Stuhl dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take that chair over there.

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular or dative plural form of "jener" (rather formal; often replaced by "der/die/das").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe jenen Mann gestern gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw that man yesterday.

definitions.note: More formal/literary than "der/dieser"; used to point out something farther away or previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jener Mann dort ist mein Lehrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That man over there is my teacher.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun meaning “that/those over there” or “the former”; less common than “dieser” in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jener ist mein Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That one is my brother.

definitions.note: Form of "jener"; used more for something farther away or previously mentioned, and sounds more formal/literary than "dieser".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jenes Haus dort gehört meiner Tante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That house over there belongs to my aunt.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun/determiner; refers to something more distant (in space, time, or context) than "dies-" (this).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme jenes Buch dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll take that book over there.

definitions.note: Points to something more distant (in space, time, or context) than "dieses"; can sound formal or literary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jenes Haus dort ist sehr alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That house over there is very old.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive in careful/formal German; in everyday speech it’s often used with von + dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jenseits des Flusses liegt ein kleines Dorf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Beyond the river there is a small village.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jep, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yep, I’m coming right away.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (attributive), especially in phrases like "die jetzige Situation".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die jetzige Situation ist schwierig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The current situation is difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit meinem jetzigen Job bin ich zufrieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy with my current job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go now.

definitions.note: Often used with plural nouns or numbers to show distribution (e.g., “two each”) or to match items one-to-one (“respectively”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tickets kosten jeweils 15 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets cost 15 euros each.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often sounds a bit casual. It can also express agreement or confirmation (like “right”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jo, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yeah, I’ll be there in a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich jogge jeden Morgen im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I jog every morning in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe jeden Morgen joggen im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go jogging every morning in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er joggt jeden Morgen im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He jogs in the park every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann mit drei Bällen jonglieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can juggle with three balls.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fans jubeln nach dem Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fans cheer after the goal.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „jubeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fans jubelten nach dem Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fans cheered after the goal.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "jubeln"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fans jubelten laut nach dem Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fans cheered loudly after the goal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Arm juckt schon den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My arm has been itching all day.

definitions.note: Often used with negation: „Das juckt mich nicht.“ = “I don’t care / That doesn’t matter to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das juckt mich nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t care.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schwester ist noch sehr jung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is still very young.

definitions.note: Often also used as an adjective (e.g., „ein junges Mädchen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist noch jung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is still young.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „jung“ (used before a noun, e.g. „der junge Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der junge Mann wohnt hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The young man lives here.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (declined form of „jung“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe die jungen Hunde im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the young dogs in the park.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a masculine singular noun (e.g., „ein junger Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein junger Mann wartet vor dem Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A young man is waiting in front of the café.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun (e.g., after "ein": "ein junges Kind").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein junges Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a young child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir zahlen die Versicherungsprämie jährlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We pay the insurance premium annually.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who gets angry suddenly and easily.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist manchmal sehr jähzornig und schreit schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is sometimes very quick-tempered and starts shouting quickly.

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine singular nouns or with plural nouns (depending on case)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie besucht eine jüdische Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She attends a Jewish school.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine/neuter in the accusative, or with masculine/neuter in the dative/with genitive, depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er besucht den jüdischen Friedhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He visits the Jewish cemetery.

definitions.note: comparative form of „jung“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schwester ist jünger als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is younger than me.

definitions.note: comparative form of „jung“; can be used before a noun (e.g. „der jüngere Bruder“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine jüngere Schwester wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My younger sister lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: comparative form of „jung“; commonly used with a noun (e.g., „die jüngeren Leute“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche mit meinem jüngeren Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m talking with my younger brother.

definitions.note: Superlative form of „jung“; often used with feminine nouns (e.g., „die jüngste Tochter“) or as a noun meaning „the youngest (female person/thing)“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die jüngste Tochter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the youngest daughter.

definitions.note: Used especially with nouns like „Nachrichten“, „Entwicklungen“, „Ereignisse“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du die jüngste Nachricht gelesen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you read the latest news?

definitions.note: Adjective form used in neuter singular (e.g., before a neuter noun like „Lied“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich höre ein kabylisches Lied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m listening to a Kabyle (Kabylian) song.

definitions.native: to poop, to take a dump
definitions.note: Very informal / vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat auf den Gehweg kacken müssen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog had to poop on the sidewalk.

definitions.note: Often used for a bald head or for trees/landscapes without leaves or vegetation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schon mit dreißig kahl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is already bald at thirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cold.

definitions.note: Often used adverbially (e.g., in fixed phrases like „jmdn. kalt lassen“ = not to affect someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das lässt mich kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That leaves me cold.

definitions.note: Usually means acting without emotion or mercy (not literally having cold blood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Mann kaltblütig getötet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He killed the man in cold blood.

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine singular nouns or with plural nouns after “die”/“meine” etc. (weak/mixed declension)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke eine kalte Cola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m drinking a cold cola.

definitions.note: dative singular (masculine or neuter) or genitive singular (masculine or neuter) form of "kalt"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei kaltem Wetter bleibe ich lieber zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In cold weather, I prefer to stay at home.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „kalt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mit kalten Händen die Tür geöffnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He opened the door with cold hands.

definitions.note: comparative form of "kalt"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es kalter als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is colder than yesterday.

definitions.note: neuter singular form (used with a noun like "kaltes Wasser")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte kaltes Wasser, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like cold water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Bier kaltmachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you chill the beer?

definitions.note: colloquial; often means to kill someone intentionally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollten ihn kaltmachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wanted to kill him.

definitions.note: Simple past form of "ankommen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kam gestern spät nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came home late yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past of „herauskommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kam erst nach dem Film heraus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He only came out after the movie.

definitions.note: simple past of „kommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kam heute zu spät zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came to work too late today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „ankommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kamen gestern Abend spät an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived late last night.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „kommen“ used with „wir/sie/Sie“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern kamen wir spät nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we came home late.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person singular (du-form) of "kommen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kamst gestern sehr spät nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You came home very late yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person plural (ihr) of „kommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr kamt gestern Abend sehr spät nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You came home very late last night.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a following noun (weak/mixed inflection, e.g. after an article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine kanadische Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a Canadian friend.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected form; used with masculine/neuter dative singular or plural nouns (e.g., mit dem kanadischen Pass; die kanadischen Städte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich reise mit dem kanadischen Pass.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m traveling with the Canadian passport.

definitions.note: Masculine nominative singular form; used before a masculine noun (e.g., „kanadischer Pass“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein kanadischer Pass liegt auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Canadian passport is on the table.

definitions.note: Also used to ask/give permission (“can/may”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann gut schwimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can swim well.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „können“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann heute nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can’t come today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „können“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please help me?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please help me?

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „kennen“; often used in writing or storytelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kannte ihn schon aus der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already knew him from school.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural (we/you/they) of „kennen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kannten ihn schon aus der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We already knew him from school.

definitions.note: simple past (informal singular “du”) of “kennen”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kanntest meinen Bruder schon, oder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already knew my brother, right?

definitions.note: simple past form used with “ihr” (you all)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr kanntet ihn schon seit der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You all knew him since school.

definitions.note: colloquial/informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kapieren das nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't understand that.

definitions.note: Informal; often used to check if someone understands ("Do you get it?").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kapierst du das jetzt?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you get it now?

definitions.note: Colloquial/informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du das kapiert?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you understand that?

definitions.native: to surrender; to capitulate; to give up
definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., war, negotiations, debates).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach stundenlangen Verhandlungen musste die Armee kapitulieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After hours of negotiations, the army had to surrender.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean something doesn’t work anymore.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is broken.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean something doesn’t work anymore (can also be used about people being very tired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy ist kaputt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone is broken.

definitions.note: used before a noun (inflected form of „kaputt“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die kaputte Lampe funktioniert nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The broken lamp doesn’t work.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich repariere die kaputten Schuhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m repairing the broken shoes.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun (e.g. ein kaputtes Handy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein kaputtes Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a broken phone.

definitions.note: Past participle of „kaputtgehen“, often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist kaputtgegangen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy ist kaputtgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone broke (stopped working).

definitions.note: past participle of "kaputtmachen"; used with auxiliaries like "haben" (e.g., "hat ... kaputtgemacht")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Handy kaputtgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I broke my phone.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often means to damage something so it no longer works.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, dass du das Handy nicht kaputtmachen wirst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful you won’t break the phone.

definitions.note: Often used for collecting payment (e.g., at a register or for bills).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kellner kassiert am Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter collects the payment at the table.

definitions.note: usually refers to the Roman Catholic Church (can also mean “universal” in some contexts, but that’s uncommon for beginners)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Großeltern sind katholisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are Catholic.

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine nouns or (in some cases) plural nouns, depending on the article/case
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie besucht eine katholische Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She attends a Catholic school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst gut kauen, bevor du schluckst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to chew well before you swallow.

definitions.note: imperative (du-form) of „kaufen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kauf bitte Brot!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please buy bread!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of „kaufen“ (ich kaufe = I buy / I’m buying).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe heute Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying bread today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen will ich ein Auto kaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I want to buy a car.

definitions.note: second-person singular present tense (du-form) of "kaufen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was kaufst du im Supermarkt?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you buying at the supermarket?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „einkaufen“ (often used for doing the grocery shopping); the prefix „ein“ may appear later in the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kauft nach der Arbeit ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shops after work.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „kaufen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kauft heute Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He buys bread today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „kaufen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufte gestern ein neues Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new phone yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "kaufen" for "we/you(pl)/they"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern kauften wir ein neues Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we bought a new phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich kaum hören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can hardly hear you.

definitions.note: Used to express a very small amount; often used with nouns like "kaum Zeit" (hardly any time) or with "ein": "kaum ein ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe kaum Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have hardly any time.

definitions.note: Can mean “(he/she/it) chews” or “chew!” when speaking to a group (ihr).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kaut Kaugummi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is chewing gum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kehre die Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sweep the kitchen.

definitions.note: Usually means sweeping with a broom; also used in set phrases like „zurückkehren“ (to return), but here it’s the basic verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kehren jeden Morgen die Treppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sweep the stairs every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kehrst die Küche nach dem Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You sweep the kitchen after the meal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kehrt den Küchenboden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sweeps the kitchen floor.

definitions.note: Often used with „zurück“: „kehrt zurück“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kehrt morgen nach Berlin zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She returns to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with a direction or around (e.g., „kehrte um“ = turned around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kehrte um und ging nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned around and went home.

definitions.note: Common with „zurück“ (e.g., „kehrte zurück“ = returned).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kehrte spät zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She returned late.

definitions.note: simple past form of "zurückkehren"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kehrte gestern Abend nach Hause zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came back home yesterday evening.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "kehren"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Urlaub kehrten wir nach Hause zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the vacation, we returned home.

definitions.note: Used to negate a noun (like “not a/any”). It changes endings like “ein” (e.g., kein/keine/keinen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe kein Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have a car.

definitions.note: Used to negate a noun (like "no" / "not any").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no time.

definitions.note: Used with feminine singular nouns or with plural nouns (nominative/accusative), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no time.

definitions.note: dative singular (masculine or neuter) form of „kein“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe keinem Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not helping any neighbor.

definitions.note: Dative masculine/neuter form of "kein"; used with masculine or neuter nouns in the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mit keinem Freund darüber gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t talk about it with any friend.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter form of «kein» (used with masculine/neuter nouns in the dative case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinem Mann geholfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t help any man.

definitions.note: Accusative masculine singular or accusative plural form of „kein“ (used to negate nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinen Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no brother.

definitions.note: Accusative masculine singular of „kein“, and also accusative plural for all genders.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinen Hunger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not hungry.

definitions.note: masculine nominative (also used for 'not a' with masculine nouns in nominative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keiner hat Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No one has time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keiner hat Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No one has time.

definitions.note: Often refers back to a group mentioned or implied (e.g., “none of them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe drei Schlüssel, aber keiner passt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have three keys, but none of them fits.

definitions.note: Used before a noun, often without an article, to emphasize “none at all.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinerlei Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no time at all.

definitions.note: Genitive singular form of "kein"; used with neuter nouns and to mean "of no ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt keines dieser Bücher mehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are none of these books left.

definitions.native: under no circumstances, by no means
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst keinesfalls zu spät kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Under no circumstances are you allowed to be late.

definitions.native: by no means, not at all
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist keineswegs sicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is by no means certain.

definitions.note: Used to refer back to a neuter noun (das) or when the gender isn’t specified.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe drei Bücher, aber keins ist spannend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have three books, but none is exciting.

definitions.note: colloquial short form of „kenne“ (1st person singular of „kennen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenn ihn nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know him.

definitions.note: Used for knowing people/places/things by experience or familiarity (not for knowing facts—German often uses "wissen" for that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne diese Stadt gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this city well.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of "kennen"; used for knowing people/places/things (being familiar with), not for knowing facts ("wissen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne diese Stadt sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this city very well.

definitions.note: Used for knowing people/places/things through familiarity; compare with "wissen" for knowing facts/information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne diese Stadt gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this city well.

definitions.note: Used for knowing people, places, or things (being acquainted with), not for knowing facts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne diese Stadt gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know this city well.

definitions.note: past participle of „kennenlernen“, often used with „haben“ in the present perfect (Perfekt)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern meine neuen Nachbarn kennengelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met my new neighbors yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for meeting someone for the first time and getting acquainted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte deine Eltern kennenlernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to get to know your parents.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „kennenlernen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo hast du ihn kennengelernt, und wann kennenlernst du seine Familie?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where did you meet him, and when are you going to get to know his family?

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of "kennenlernen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kennenlernte letztes Jahr meine neuen Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met my new neighbors last year.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form, used especially in writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kennenlernten uns in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We met in Berlin.

definitions.note: used with other verbs (e.g., after "um" or "ohne"), like "to get to know" in English
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dich bald kennenzulernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to get to know you soon.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kennst meinen Bruder, oder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You know my brother, right?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular (er/sie/es) present tense of „kennen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kennt meinen Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knows my brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder kichern im Unterricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children giggle in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kicherte leise über den Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She giggled softly at the joke.

definitions.note: informal; often used in gaming or slang contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will den Endgegner endlich killen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to finally kill the boss.

definitions.note: informal; often used like English “to kill,” especially in gaming/slang contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er killt den Boss in zwei Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kills the boss in two minutes.

definitions.note: describes a distance that stretches over many kilometers (often: as far as the eye can see)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stau ist kilometerweit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic jam stretches for kilometers.

definitions.note: Often used negatively to criticize immature behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er benimmt sich kindisch, wenn er verliert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He behaves childishly when he loses.
