definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, dass das Glas nicht kippen kann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful that the glass can't tip over.

definitions.note: Often used for pouring something somewhere (sometimes carelessly), e.g. into a drain or trash.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst kein Öl in den Abfluss kippen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not pour any oil into the drain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin an den Füßen sehr kitzelig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm very ticklish on my feet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feder kitzelt an meiner Nase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The feather tickles my nose.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin an den Füßen sehr kitzlig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very ticklish on my feet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Leute klagen über das Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people complain about the weather.

definitions.note: legal context (often: gegen jemanden klagen = to sue someone)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will die Firma wegen Betrugs klagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to sue the company for fraud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er klagt ständig über den Lärm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He complains all the time about the noise.

definitions.note: Used in a legal context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma klagt gegen den ehemaligen Mitarbeiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company sues the former employee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er klagte über die laute Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He complained about the loud music.

definitions.note: In legal contexts, it can mean to sue (to bring a case to court).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie klagte gegen die Firma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sued the company.

definitions.note: simple past of „klingen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Musik klang wunderschön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music sounded wonderful.

definitions.note: Very informal and rude; used to tell someone to stop talking (often written/said as “Klappe!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Klappe! Ich versuche zu schlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shut up! I’m trying to sleep.

definitions.note: Often used with "es" ("es klappt") to mean something works out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass es morgen klappen wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it will work out tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used for folding something with a hinge (e.g., a seat, a table).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst den Sitz nach vorne klappen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can fold the seat forward.

definitions.note: Often used as “Es klappt.” = “It works.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, das klappt schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, it’ll work out.

definitions.note: Often used with an extra word like „auf/zu“ (e.g., „klappt auf/zu“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Deckel klappt zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lid flips shut.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan klappte am Ende doch noch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, the plan worked after all.

definitions.note: Often also used to mean “of course/sure” in conversation, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Erklärung ist klar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The explanation is clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte klar sagen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please say that clearly?

definitions.note: Often used on its own to agree or confirm (like “sure”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Klar, ich helfe dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of course, I'll help you.

definitions.note: informal; used to show agreement or confirmation
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Klar, ich komme morgen mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sure, I’ll come along tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine klare Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a clear answer.

definitions.note: Dative singular masculine/neuter or genitive singular masculine/neuter form of „klar“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit klarem Wasser schmeckt der Kaffee besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With clear water, the coffee tastes better.

definitions.note: adjective ending (inflected form of "klar")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen einen klaren Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a clear plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es ein klarer Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is a clear day.

definitions.note: comparative form of „klar“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit der Karte ist der Weg klarer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the map, the way is clearer.

definitions.note: Very common in everyday speech; often used with "mit" to mean coping with something, or getting along with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mit dem Stress gerade nicht klarkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't cope with the stress right now.

definitions.note: Used especially in the phrase "mit jemandem klarkommen" = to get along with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme mit meinem neuen Chef nicht gut klarkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t get along well with my new boss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass er allein klarkommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that he can manage on his own.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ (e.g., „mit jemandem klarkommen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sagt, dass sie gut mit ihrer neuen Chefin klarkommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She says that she gets along well with her new boss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir das gleich klarmachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll make that clear to you in a moment.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun (e.g., „sich etwas klarmachen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mir klarmachen, dass das Zeit braucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to realize that this takes time.

definitions.note: Often used when correcting a misunderstanding or stating something explicitly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte klarstellen, dass ich damit nicht einverstanden bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to make it clear that I don't agree with that.

definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war klasse!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was great!

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine singular nouns (and with plural nouns) in certain contexts, depending on the article/determiner
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich höre gern klassische Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like listening to classical music.

definitions.note: Adjective form with -er ending (often used with masculine singular nouns, e.g. „ein klassischer …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein klassischer Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a classic mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zuschauer klatschen laut nach dem Konzert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience claps loudly after the concert.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of „klatschen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Publikum klatschte laut nach dem Konzert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience clapped loudly after the concert.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), used for “they/we clapped” depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende des Konzerts klatschten alle laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the concert, everyone clapped loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich klaue kein Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t steal money.

definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand will mein Fahrrad klauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone wants to steal my bike.

definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er klaut mein Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He steals my phone.

definitions.note: Used both transitively (something sticks something) and intransitively (something sticks). Common with "an" + dative (to be stuck to) or "auf" + dative (to stick on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Aufkleber kann gut an der Tür kleben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sticker can stick well to the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Poster klebt an der Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poster is stuck to the wall.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „kleben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Aufkleber klebte am Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sticker was stuck to the window.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich kleiden“ = to get dressed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kleidet sich für die Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets dressed for the party.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „kleiden“; often used with „sich“ (sich kleiden = to dress oneself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kleidete sich schnell, bevor sie das Haus verließ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dressed quickly before she left the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist klein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is small.

definitions.note: Used here in the weak form (often after a definite article like "der/die/das" or words like "dieser").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe die kleine Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the small cat.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used in certain cases/genders (e.g., after 'einen': 'einen kleinen ...').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen kleinen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a small dog.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „klein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Bruder ist kleiner als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is smaller than me.

definitions.note: comparative form of „klein“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme die kleinere Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking the smaller bag.

definitions.note: comparative form of "klein"; used with an adjective ending (e.g., before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme den kleineren Koffer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take the smaller suitcase.

definitions.note: Used with a neuter noun (e.g., "ein kleines Haus").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ein kleines Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a small problem.

definitions.note: superlative form of „klein“ (used with a noun or after an article, e.g. „der/die/das kleinste …“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das kleinste Zimmer in der Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the smallest room in the apartment.

definitions.note: superlative form of "klein"; often used with "am" (am kleinsten = the smallest) or with a definite article (die kleinsten …)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Von allen Kindern ist Mia am kleinsten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of all the children, Mia is the smallest.

definitions.note: often used for things like drawers, doors, zippers, or machines when they don’t move smoothly
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schublade klemmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drawer is stuck.

definitions.note: informal imperative (command): “climb!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kletter nicht auf das Geländer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t climb on the railing!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich klettere jeden Samstag in der Halle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I climb in the gym every Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir klettern am Wochenende in der Halle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We climb at the gym on the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze klettert auf den Baum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat climbs up the tree.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "klettern"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kletterte schnell auf den Baum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He climbed quickly up the tree.

definitions.note: Often used for doorbells or phone calls.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte an der Tür klingeln?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please ring the doorbell?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „klingeln“ (used for bells, phones, doorbells).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Telefon klingelt gerade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is ringing right now.

definitions.note: Simple past of „klingeln“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es klingelte an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone rang the doorbell.

definitions.note: Used for how something sounds (often about a tone, voice, or bell).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich höre die Glocken klingen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hear the bells ringing.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "klingen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du klingst heute müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You sound tired today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "klingen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das klingt gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That sounds good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich klopfe an die Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I knock on the door.

definitions.note: Often used for knocking on a door; also used for tapping/knocking sounds (e.g., heart pounding).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte an die Tür klopfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please knock on the door?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand klopft an die Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone is knocking on the door.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „klopfen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jemand klopfte an die Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone knocked on the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine kluge Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a smart decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast klug entschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You decided wisely.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine kluge Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a smart decision.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a masculine singular noun (e.g., „ein kluger Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein kluger Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a clever plan.

definitions.note: Used with a neuter noun in nominative or accusative singular (or as a nominalized adjective: “a smart one/thing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein kluges Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a smart child.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kläre das später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll clarify that later.

definitions.note: Often used with something like „eine Frage/ein Problem/ein Missverständnis klären“ (to clarify/resolve a question/problem/misunderstanding).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Missverständnis klären.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to clear up the misunderstanding.

definitions.note: comparative form of „klug“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist klüger als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is smarter than I am.

definitions.note: superlative form of "klug"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die klügste Person in unserer Klasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the smartest person in our class.

definitions.note: Often used for making a cracking/crunching noise (e.g., nuts, joints, ice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beim Kauen kann man das Eis im Getränk knacken hören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While chewing, you can hear the ice in the drink crack.

definitions.note: Used for solving/breaking something like a code, password, or case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Hacker versuchen, das Passwort zu knacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hackers are trying to crack the password.

definitions.native: to bang, to pop (make a loud sudden noise)
definitions.note: Used for loud sudden noises (e.g., a door, firecracker, gunshot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn der Wind kommt, kann die Tür laut knallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the wind comes, the door can bang loudly.

definitions.note: informal/intensifying; means a very strong, striking red color
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt heute ein knallrotes Kleid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s wearing a bright red dress today.

definitions.note: used for a loud sudden noise (e.g., a door slamming)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür knallt zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door slams shut.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür knallte laut zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door slammed shut loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben den Zug nur knapp erreicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We barely caught the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wasser ist in dieser Region knapp.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Water is scarce in this region.

definitions.note: Often used for time/quantity to mean “just about enough” or “only just.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe knapp genug Geld für das Ticket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I barely have enough money for the ticket.

definitions.note: Often used about clothing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trägt eine knappe Shorts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She’s wearing skimpy shorts.

definitions.note: Often used about time, money, or resources.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben nur eine knappe Stunde Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We only have a limited hour of time.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "knapp".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unser Zeitplan ist heute noch knapper als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our schedule is even tighter today than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür knarrte laut, als ich sie öffnete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door creaked loudly when I opened it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schuh kann ganz schön kneifen, besonders am kleinen Zeh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoe can really pinch, especially on the little toe.

definitions.note: Informal; often used with "vor" + noun (e.g., "vor Angst kneifen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wollte zur Prüfung gehen, aber am Ende hat er gekniffen und ist zu Hause geblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to go to the exam, but in the end he chickened out and stayed home.

definitions.note: Can also look like English “knee” (a noun), but here it’s a verb form of „knien“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich knie vor dem Bett und bete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kneel in front of the bed and pray.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kniet vor dem Bett und betet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kneels in front of the bed and prays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kniete vor dem Altar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knelt in front of the altar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kniff mich in den Arm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pinched me in the arm.

definitions.note: colloquial, figurative meaning (to avoid something because you're scared or don't want to do it)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als es ernst wurde, kniff er.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When it got serious, he chickened out.

definitions.note: simple past of "knuffen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er knuffte mich in die Seite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He nudged me in the side.

definitions.note: Often used for animals (e.g., dogs); can also describe a person speaking in an irritated, low voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund knurrt, weil er Angst hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog growls because it is scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund knurrte, als der Fremde näher kam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog growled when the stranger came closer.

definitions.note: usually used for food (e.g., bread, crust, fried foods)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Brot ist außen knusprig und innen weich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside.

definitions.note: Informal; usually means kissing passionately.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden knutschen im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two are making out in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er knöpfte seine Jacke zu, weil es kalt war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He buttoned up his jacket because it was cold.

definitions.note: Used as the verb form with the pronoun “ich” (I): “ich koch(e) …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich koch heute Abend Pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cooking pasta tonight.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense: “I cook / I am cooking.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich koche heute Abend Pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm cooking pasta tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute Abend kochen und eine Suppe machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to cook this evening and make a soup.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present tense of "kochen" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kochst heute Abend Pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re cooking pasta tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kocht heute Abend Pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cooks pasta tonight.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „kochen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern kochte er eine Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he cooked a soup.

definitions.native: to collide, to crash (into each other)
definitions.note: often used for vehicles or objects; figuratively also for plans/ideas that conflict
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zwei Autos kollidieren an der Kreuzung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two cars collide at the intersection.

definitions.note: used for interests, schedules, plans, or opinions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Termine kollidieren, deshalb können wir nicht beide Treffen wahrnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The appointments conflict, so we can’t attend both meetings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Sofa ist sehr komfortabel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sofa is very comfortable.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech to say something feels odd or not quite right.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Irgendwie ist das komisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Somehow, that's strange.

definitions.note: Often means “strange/weird” rather than “funny” in the humorous sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine komische Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a strange question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erzählt einen komischen Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tells a funny joke.

definitions.note: Often used for something that seems odd or suspicious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen komischen Geruch bemerkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed a strange smell.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "komisch"; depending on context it can mean "strange" or "funny."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist noch komischer als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s even stranger than yesterday.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used in contexts like neuter nominative/accusative singular (e.g., „ein komisches Ding“) or as a nominalized adjective (e.g., „etwas Komisches“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute etwas Komisches gehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard something strange today.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative of „kommen“ (used when speaking to one person you address with „du“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, please!

definitions.note: Informal singular command (imperative) of "kommen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte hierher!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, please!

definitions.note: From the separable verb „auskommen“; the prefix „aus“ goes to the end in a main clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme mit meinen Kollegen gut aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get along well with my colleagues.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "kommen" (ich komme).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming in a moment.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ankommen“: in main clauses the prefix „an“ often comes at the end (e.g. „Wir kommen … an.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kommen um 18 Uhr am Bahnhof an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrive at the train station at 6 p.m.

definitions.note: Basic meaning: movement toward the speaker or a reference point.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme morgen nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with a destination or time; focuses on reaching a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kommen um acht Uhr am Bahnhof an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrive at the station at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Used with prepositions like „zu“ to indicate reaching someone/somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme gleich zu dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming to you in a moment.

definitions.note: Used in expressions like „Wie kommt das?“ to ask how something happened.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie kommt das, dass du so spät bist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How come you’re so late?

definitions.note: Used with „aus“ to indicate origin.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme aus Kanada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from Canada.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen morgen kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used before a noun in the accusative masculine or genitive plural, often with time expressions (e.g. „den kommenden Montag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nächsten Monat in den kommenden Wochen wenig Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won’t have much time in the coming weeks next month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du den Artikel bitte kommentieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please comment on the article?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of "kommen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du heute Abend zu mir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming to my place tonight?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ankommen“; in many sentences you’ll also see „an“ at the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug kommt um 8 Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train arrives at 8 o’clock.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „auskommen“; often used with „mit“ + dative (e.g. „mit wenig Geld“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt mit wenig Geld aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets by with little money.

definitions.note: From „auskommen“; often used with „mit“ + dative to mean getting along with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kommt gut mit ihren Kollegen aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gets along well with her colleagues.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „herauskommen“; in the present tense it often appears as „kommt … heraus“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fleck kommt nicht heraus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stain doesn’t come out.

definitions.note: Often used with a destination or origin, e.g. "kommt aus ..." = "is from ..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus kommt gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is coming soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen besser kommunizieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to communicate better.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr kompetent und hilft mir immer weiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very competent and always helps me make progress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das komplett vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completely forgot that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Thema ist komplex, aber wir erklären es Schritt für Schritt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The topic is complex, but we explain it step by step.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine komplexe Aufgabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a complex task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aufgabe ist kompliziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The task is complicated.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (attributive), e.g. “eine komplizierte Frage”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine komplizierte Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a complicated question.

definitions.note: comparative form of "kompliziert"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die zweite Aufgabe ist komplizierter als die erste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The second task is more complicated than the first.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „komponieren“ (also used as subjunctive II in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mozart komponierte viele berühmte Stücke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mozart composed many famous pieces.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “not abstract” (a concrete example or specific details).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du konkrete Pläne für morgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any specific plans for tomorrow?

definitions.note: Simple past form of "können"; often used in writing and storytelling (in speech, "konnte" is also common).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich konnte gestern nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn't come yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past of „können“ (ich/er/sie/es konnte)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich konnte gestern nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn’t come yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "können"; often used in writing and narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir konnten gestern nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We couldn’t come yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „können“; often used in writing and formal speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir konnten gestern nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We couldn’t come yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person singular (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du konntest gestern nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You couldn’t come yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past, 2nd person singular (du) of „können“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du konntest gestern nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You couldn’t come yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for political views or for a traditional/cautious attitude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Eltern sind politisch eher konservativ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents are politically rather conservative.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., consult a doctor, a lawyer, or a reference book).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sollten bei starken Schmerzen einen Arzt konsultieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have severe pain, you should consult a doctor.

definitions.note: Depending on context, this form can mean “I contact” (present tense) or “contact!” (imperative, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kontaktiere dich später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll contact you later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich morgen per E-Mail kontaktieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll contact you tomorrow by email.

definitions.note: Past participle or 3rd person singular present of „kontaktieren“; often used with „hat“ as an auxiliary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich gestern kontaktiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He contacted me yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kontrolliere am Eingang die Tickets und kontrollieren ist heute meine Aufgabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I check the tickets at the entrance, and checking is my job today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist kontrolliert meinen Ausweis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer checks my ID.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist kontrollierte meinen Ausweis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer checked my ID.

definitions.note: Often used for converting files or data formats; can also mean converting (changing) to a different religion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Datei in ein anderes Format konvertieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to convert the file into a different format.

definitions.note: informal (du) command/imperative form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Konzentrier dich bitte auf die Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please concentrate on the homework.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively with „sich“: „sich auf etwas konzentrieren“ = to focus on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich auf meine Hausaufgaben konzentrieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to concentrate on my homework.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular form; can also be used with reflexive verbs (sich konzentrieren).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er konzentriert sich auf seine Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He concentrates on his homework.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective to describe someone’s state (e.g., being focused).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wirkt heute sehr konzentriert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She seems very focused today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute sehr konzentriert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very focused today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er konzentrierte sich auf die Aufgabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He concentrated on the task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere neuen Kolleginnen sind sehr kooperativ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our new colleagues are very cooperative.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen mit der Polizei kooperieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to cooperate with the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kooperiert mit der Polizei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cooperates with the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind rutschte kopfüber die Rutsche hinunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child slid down the slide headfirst.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Datei bitte kopieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please copy the file?

definitions.note: Can be present tense (er/sie/es kopiert) or past participle (kopiert).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kopiert die Datei auf den USB-Stick.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She copies the file onto the USB drive.

definitions.note: Past participle, often used with "haben" to form the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Text kopiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I copied the text.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter singular noun (often after an article like „ein“), e.g., „ein koreanisches Restaurant“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir essen heute in einem koreanisches Restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re eating at a Korean restaurant today.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is factually right or done in the right way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Antwort ist korrekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is correct.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast die Aufgabe korrekt gelöst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You solved the task correctly.

definitions.note: Often used for correcting mistakes (e.g., text, homework, or an error).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte meinen Text korrigieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please correct my text?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (he/she/it corrects).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer korrigiert die Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher corrects the homework.

definitions.note: past participle, often used with an auxiliary verb (e.g., hat/ist).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Fehler korrigiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I corrected the mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er korrigierte den Fehler sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He corrected the mistake right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Politiker ist korrupt und nimmt Bestechungsgeld an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The politician is corrupt and takes bribes.

definitions.note: adjective form with an ending (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei untersucht die korrupten Politiker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating the corrupt politicians.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonde misst die kosmischen Strahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The probe measures the cosmic rays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Uhr ist sehr kostbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This watch is very valuable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein kostbares Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a precious book.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv (often used in indirect speech) or a hypothetical statement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eintritt koste 8 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The admission costs 8 euros.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative in cooking ("Taste it!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Koste die Soße und sag mir, ob sie gut ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Taste the sauce and tell me if it’s good.

definitions.note: Infinitive verb form; often appears conjugated (kostet), but here shown as 'kosten' to match the headword exactly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tickets kosten zehn Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets cost ten euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eintritt ist heute kostenlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.note: means no cost (not “free” as in “not restricted”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eintritt ist heute kostenlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.note: Means free as in no cost (not “free” in the sense of available or unrestricted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt kostenlose Parkplätze hinter dem Gebäude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are free parking spaces behind the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kostet zehn Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That costs ten euros.

definitions.note: Simple past of „kosten“ (to cost).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Ticket kostete 20 Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket cost 20 euros.

definitions.note: Very informal/vulgar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist so schlecht, ich muss gleich kotzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel so sick, I’m going to throw up any second.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal; often used as an insult or to express strong disgust (e.g., „Du kotzt mich an.“ = „You disgust me.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist schlecht, ich kotzt gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel sick; I’m going to throw up in a moment.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "krachen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ast krachte auf den Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The branch crashed onto the ground.

definitions.note: Also used (especially with „sein“) to mean being unwell; not the same as English “cranky”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin krank und bleibe heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sick and I’m staying home today.

definitions.note: Used as a declined form of the adjective „krank“ before a noun (e.g. with „die“, „der“, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die kranke Frau bleibt heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sick woman is staying at home today.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „krank“ (used with certain case/gender/number endings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchen den kranken Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re visiting the sick neighbor.

definitions.note: comparative form of „krank“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute fühle ich mich kranker als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I feel sicker than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein krankes Kind braucht viel Ruhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A sick child needs lots of rest.

definitions.note: Often used in informal spoken German to express strong surprise or emphasis (can be positive or negative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist krass!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s intense!

definitions.note: Informal; used to react to something surprising or extreme (positive or negative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Krass, das hätte ich nicht erwartet!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Crazy, I wouldn't have expected that!

definitions.note: Colloquial/slang; used to react to something surprising, extreme, or impressive (can be positive or negative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Krass, das ist ja riesig!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, that's huge!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze kann mich kratzen, wenn ich sie erschrecke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat can scratch me if I scare her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze kratzt mich am Arm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat scratches me on the arm.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „kratzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze kratzte mich am Arm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat scratched me on the arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr kreativ und hat viele gute Ideen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very creative and has many good ideas.

definitions.note: Used especially in banking/finance contexts for people or companies that are likely to repay a loan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist kreditwürdig und bekommt den Kredit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is creditworthy and gets the loan.

definitions.note: Often used for circling in the air (e.g., birds, planes) or thoughts “circling” around a topic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Adler kann stundenlang über dem Tal kreisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The eagle can circle over the valley for hours.

definitions.note: Simple past of "krempeln", often used with "hoch" (e.g., sleeves).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er krempelte die Ärmel hoch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rolled up his sleeves.

definitions.note: Colloquial and often crude; commonly used for animals or as an insult, not in polite contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fliegen krepieren nach ein paar Tagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flies die after a few days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kreuzen die Straße an der Ampel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We cross the street at the traffic light.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „kriechen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schnecke kriecht langsam über den Weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snail crawls slowly across the path.

definitions.note: Colloquial spoken short form of „kriege“ (1st person singular of „kriegen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich krieg das schon hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll manage that.

definitions.note: colloquial; in writing, you’ll often see "bekommen" instead
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich krieg das schon hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll manage that (I’ll get it done).

definitions.note: colloquial; often used like "bekommen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kriege morgen das Paket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m getting the package tomorrow.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; in more formal contexts, “bekommen” is often preferred.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte ein Glas Wasser kriegen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please get me a glass of water?

definitions.note: informal; 2nd-person singular (du) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kriegst du das Paket heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you getting the package today?

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used like „bekommt“ (to get/receive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kriegt heute ein Paket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s getting a package today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine kriminelle Handlung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a criminal act.

definitions.note: Often means evaluating or judging something carefully (sometimes with disapproval).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr kritisch gegenüber neuen Apps.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very critical of new apps.

definitions.note: Can describe a dangerous or very serious situation (e.g., health or safety).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Zustand ist kritisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His condition is critical.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wird meinen Bericht kritisieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will criticize my report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kritisiert den Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He criticizes the plan.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "kritisieren".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kritisierte den Bericht im Meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He criticized the report in the meeting.

definitions.note: simple past of „kriechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze kroch leise unter das Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat crept quietly under the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist kräftig genug, um die Kiste zu tragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is strong enough to carry the box.

definitions.note: Often used for food or drink with a strong, rich taste or that is quite substantial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Wanderung essen wir eine kräftige Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, we’re eating a hearty soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schüttelte ihr kräftig die Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shook her hand firmly.

definitions.note: Adjective form (e.g., before a noun): can describe people, flavors, colors, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern eine kräftige Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a hearty soup.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „kräftig“ (e.g., before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche einen kräftigen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a strong coffee.

definitions.note: used especially for a rooster’s sound
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hahn kann morgens sehr laut krähen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rooster can crow very loudly in the morning.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person’s manners, taste, or education (similar to “cultured”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr kultiviert und spricht mehrere Sprachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very refined and speaks several languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film ist kurz, aber sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is short, but very good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war nur kurz im Laden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was only in the shop for a short time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nur eine kurze Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have a short question.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "kurz" (often used after dative prepositions like "mit"; also common in the phrase "seit kurzem" = "recently").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trägt ein Hemd mit kurzem Ärmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is wearing a shirt with a short sleeve.

definitions.note: Usually used in the phrase „vor kurzem“ (= recently).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn vor kurzem gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him recently.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with 'den', 'dem', 'des').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir nehmen den kurzen Weg nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking the short way home.

definitions.note: attributive form of „kurz“ (used before a masculine noun, e.g. „ein kurzer …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein kurzer Moment, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One short moment, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche ein kurzes Video.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a short video.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du kurzfristig einspringen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you fill in on short notice?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir kuscheln auf dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We cuddle on the sofa.

definitions.note: comparative form of „kalt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es kälter als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is colder than yesterday.

definitions.note: superlative form of „kalt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der kälteste Tag des Jahres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the coldest day of the year.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of "kommen", often used for hypotheticals or polite phrasing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wäre froh, wenn du morgen früher käme(st).
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d be happy if you came earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of "kommen"; often used for hypotheticals or polite suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn sie früher kämen, könnten wir zusammen essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they came earlier, we could eat together.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II, 2nd person singular; sounds old-fashioned/poetic in modern German (more common: „kämmst“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du früher kämest, hätten wir mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you came earlier, we would have more time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jeden Morgen kämmen wir die Haare, bevor wir aus dem Haus gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning we comb our hair before we leave the house.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kämpf weiter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep fighting!

definitions.note: Often used as 1st person singular present with "ich" ("ich kämpfe" = "I fight / I am fighting").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kämpfe für meine Träume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fight for my dreams.

definitions.note: Can be used both literally (in a battle) and figuratively (struggle for/against something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kämpfen gegen das Unrecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fight against injustice.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kämpfst jeden Tag für deine Ziele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You fight every day for your goals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kämpft jeden Tag für seine Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fights every day for his family.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "kämpfen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kämpfte bis zum Ende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fought until the end.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural / formal “you” plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kämpften bis zum Ende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fought until the end.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a feminine noun (or in plural) depending on the sentence
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die königliche Familie wohnt im Palast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The royal family lives in the palace.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form of "können" (often used in reported speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er könne heute nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he can't come today.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I) form of „können“, often used in reported speech or in formal statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er könne heute nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he can’t come today.

definitions.note: modal verb used with another verb in the infinitive (usually without „zu“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, morgen kommen zu können.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to be able to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Modal verb; often used with a second verb in the infinitive (e.g., „Ich kann schwimmen.“ = “I can swim.”). The dictionary form is „können“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss morgen weniger arbeiten können, sonst werde ich krank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to be able to work less tomorrow, otherwise I’ll get sick.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (ihr) form of the modal verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Könnt ihr mir bitte helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please help me?

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) form of "können".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr könnt heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) can go home earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about possibilities or to make polite requests (Konjunktiv II of „können“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich könnte dir morgen helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I could help you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II of "können"; often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Könnte ich bitte ein Glas Wasser bekommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could I please get a glass of water?

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form; often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Könnten Sie mir bitte helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you please help me?

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) Konjunktiv II (would/could).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du könntest morgen früher kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You could come earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr), subjunctive II; often used for polite suggestions or hypotheticals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr könntet heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You could go home earlier today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute körperlich sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I am physically very tired.

definitions.note: Used before a noun in the adjective ending form (e.g., „körperliche Arbeit“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall braucht er körperliche Ruhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he needs physical rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist köstlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is delicious.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine accusative, neuter genitive, or plural dative forms (depending on the context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern den köstlichen Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like the delicious cake.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter noun (often with an article like „ein“ or „das“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein köstliches Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a delicious meal.

definitions.note: often used for temperature (cool to the touch/weather); can also describe a person's manner as reserved/distant
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es ziemlich kühl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s pretty cool.

definitions.note: adjective form often used before a feminine noun (e.g. „eine kühle Nacht“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist eine kühle Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is a cool night.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective meaning “cool” (not “cold”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es kühlen im Schatten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s cool in the shade.

definitions.note: comparative form of „kühl“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es kühler als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is cooler than yesterday.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (du-form), usually used with "dich" and "um" (e.g., "Kümmer dich um …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kümmer dich um die Kinder, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take care of the kids, please.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal singular command with „dich“: „Kümmere dich (um ...)!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kümmere dich um die Kinder!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take care of the kids!

definitions.note: Usually used with "sich" + "um" + accusative: "sich um etwas/jemanden kümmern".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mich morgen um meine kleine Schwester kümmern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take care of my little sister tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „du kümmerst dich um …“ = you take care of / look after …
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kümmerst dich um die Kinder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You take care of the children.

definitions.note: Used with a reflexive pronoun (sich kümmern) and often with „um“ + accusative: „sich um etwas/jemanden kümmern“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kümmert sich um seine Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes care of his sister.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich um + accusative“ (to take care of someone/something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kümmerte sich um seine kleine Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took care of his little sister.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive form „sich kümmern (um)“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kümmerten sich um die Kinder, während wir gearbeitet haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took care of the children while we worked.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present ("I ..."); used for quitting a job or ending/canceling something (e.g., a contract).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kündige meinen Job zum Monatsende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I quit my job at the end of the month.

definitions.note: Used for leaving a job (often formally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde meinen Job zum Monatsende kündigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to quit my job at the end of the month.

definitions.note: Used for contracts/services (e.g., phone plan, membership, lease).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden den Vertrag nächste Woche kündigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to cancel the contract next week.

definitions.note: Past tense form (simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kündigte gestern seinen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He quit his job yesterday.

definitions.note: Past tense form (simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kündigte den Vertrag sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cancelled the contract immediately.

definitions.note: Past tense form (simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Trainer kündigte eine große Veränderung an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coach announced a big change.

definitions.native: in the future, from now on
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Künftig werde ich mehr Wasser trinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the future, I will drink more water.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a feminine noun or in a plural noun phrase (weak/mixed declension), depending on the article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine künstlerische Begabung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an artistic talent.

definitions.note: comparative form of „kurz“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Weg ist kürzer als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This path is shorter than the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn kürzlich in der Stadt gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him in town recently.

definitions.note: Informal command (du imperative) of „küssen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Küss mich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Kiss me!

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular): used when telling one person you know well to kiss.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Küss mich bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Kiss me, please.

definitions.note: First-person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of "küssen"; also the (rare) first-person singular past subjunctive (Konjunktiv II).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich küsse sie nur aus Höflichkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that I kiss her only out of politeness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie küssen sich zum Abschied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They kiss each other goodbye.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "küssen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er küsst sie zum Abschied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kisses her goodbye.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „küssen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er küsste sie zum Abschied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He kissed her goodbye.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "küssen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie küssten sich zum Abschied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They kissed each other goodbye.

definitions.note: Informal; often suggests talking too much without saying anything important.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf zu labern und sag endlich, was passiert ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop rambling and finally say what happened.

definitions.note: Informal; can sound a bit rude/annoyed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du laberst schon wieder über dasselbe Thema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re rambling about the same topic again.

definitions.note: colloquial; often implies talking a lot without saying anything useful
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er labert die ganze Zeit, aber niemand hört ihm zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He babbles the whole time, but nobody listens to him.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (to one person: “du”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lach doch mal!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, laugh!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lache über den Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I laugh at the joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder lachen laut im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are laughing loudly in the garden.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „lachen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum lachst du so laut?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you laughing so loudly?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (er/sie/es lacht).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lacht über den Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He laughs at the joke.

definitions.note: simple past of „auslachen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die anderen Kinder lachten ihn aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The other children laughed at him.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lachen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lachte über den Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He laughed at the joke.

definitions.note: Past tense form of the separable verb „auslachen“; often used with the prefix separated (e.g. „Sie lachten ihn aus.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lachten ihn aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They laughed at him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern lachten wir über den Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we laughed at the joke.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „einladen“; in the present tense it’s used like: „Ich lade dich ein.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lade dich morgen zu meiner Party ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m inviting you to my party tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „ein“ (einladen); in main clauses the „ein“ often comes at the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir laden dich morgen ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re inviting you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Auto laden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to load the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mein Handy laden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to charge my phone.

definitions.note: simple past of „liegen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch lag auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book lay on the table.

definitions.note: simple past (plural) of „liegen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schlüssel lagen auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys were lying on the table.

definitions.note: Can describe a person/animal (unable to walk well) or, figuratively, something weak or ineffective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall war sein Bein lahm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, his leg was lame.

definitions.note: Used for planes, birds, spacecraft, etc.; also figuratively for ending up somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug wird gleich landen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane will land soon.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "landen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du landest in Frankfurt um 18 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You land in Frankfurt at 6 p.m.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug landet pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane lands on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug landete pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane landed on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film ist sehr lang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is very long.

definitions.note: Used as a postposition (it usually comes after the noun or time expression).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den ganzen Tag lang gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked all day long.

definitions.note: Often used with time expressions (e.g., „lange“ / „lang“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich lang nicht gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I haven’t seen you in a long time.

definitions.note: often used in speech as a shorter form of „lange“ (e.g. „schon lang“ = „schon lange“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte schon lang auf den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been waiting a long time for the bus.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with masculine nominative singular nouns after articles/possessives, etc. (e.g., „der lange Tag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der lange Weg ist anstrengend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The long way is exhausting.

definitions.note: Often used with a negation to mean “for a long time” (e.g., “nicht lange”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich lange nicht gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I haven’t seen you in a long time.

definitions.note: Used to talk about distance, often with “fahren/gehen/laufen” etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind lange gelaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked a long way.

definitions.native: for a long time, a long while
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe lange auf den Bus gewartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited for the bus for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean duration (e.g. warten, dauern).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte schon lange auf den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been waiting for the bus for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe die langen Straßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the long streets.

definitions.note: used before a masculine noun (e.g., «ein langer …»)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein langer Weg liegt vor uns.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A long road lies ahead of us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein langes Seil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a long rope.

definitions.note: Often used with an accusative object to mean going along a route (e.g., a street, path, corridor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie langgeht langsam den Weg zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She walks slowly along the path to the station.

definitions.note: As an adjective it means “slow”; as an adverb it often means “slowly” (same form in German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich langsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak slowly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich langsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak slowly.

definitions.note: adjective with weak ending (e.g., after a definite article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der langsame Zug kommt erst um acht Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The slow train doesn’t arrive until eight o’clock.

definitions.note: comparative form of "langsam"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte langsamer sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak more slowly?

definitions.note: comparative form of "langsam"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte langsamer sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you speak more slowly, please?

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun: sich langweilen = to be bored (e.g. Ich langweile mich.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich langweile mich zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m bored at home.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., „Der Film langweilt mich.“ = “The movie bores me.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solche langen Vorträge können mich langweilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such long lectures can bore me.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich langweilen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mich ohne Musik schnell langweilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can get bored quickly without music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war total langweilig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was totally boring.
