definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „langweilig“ (e.g., with a feminine noun or plural nouns depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine langweilige Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a boring story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film langweilt mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie bores me.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Unterricht langweilte ich mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class I was bored.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "lesen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern las ich ein interessantes Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I read an interesting book.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural ("we/they")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern lasen wir ein spannendes Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we read an exciting book.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (du-form) of „lassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lass mich in Ruhe!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave me alone!

definitions.note: Often used with an object + adjective/adverb to mean “leave (something) (like this)” (e.g., leave it open).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lasse das Fenster offen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave the window open.

definitions.note: Used to give permission or not prevent something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lasse dich heute länger aufbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m letting you stay up later today.

definitions.note: Common causative construction: lassen + infinitive (often with an object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lasse meinen Bruder das Auto waschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having my brother wash the car.

definitions.note: Meaning to not take something along / to leave something somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lasse meinen Regenschirm im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving my umbrella at the office.

definitions.note: Often in the sense of refraining from an action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lass das!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop that!

definitions.note: Can mean to refrain from interfering or to stop insisting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lasse es dabei bewenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll let it rest at that.

definitions.note: Often used with another verb in the infinitive (e.g., jemanden gehen lassen = let someone go).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst mich gehen lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to let me go.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst dein Fahrrad hier lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can leave your bike here.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural present of "lassen" (ihr lasst).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lasst mich bitte kurz erklären.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please let me explain briefly.

definitions.note: adjective form (e.g., before a feminine noun in the nominative/accusative, or after certain determiners in other cases)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lernt die lateinische Sprache in der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is learning the Latin language at school.

definitions.note: weak adjective ending; used before a noun with a definite article or similar determiner
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne die lateinischen Wörter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning the Latin words.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze lauert im Gras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is lurking in the grass.

definitions.note: Most commonly used as the informal singular imperative: “Run!”. It can also be a colloquial short form of “ich laufe” (“I run”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lauf schneller!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Run faster!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "laufen" (ich laufe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich laufe jeden Morgen zur Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I run to school every morning.

definitions.note: Basic meaning: to run (on foot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe joggen, aber heute will ich einfach nur laufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go jogging, but today I just want to run.

definitions.note: In everyday speech, "laufen" can mean simply going somewhere on foot, depending on region/context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können zum Supermarkt laufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can walk to the supermarket.

definitions.native: to work; to be running (machines, processes)
definitions.note: Used for things like programs, engines, business operations, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Programm muss im Hintergrund laufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The program has to be running in the background.

definitions.native: to be going well/badly; to proceed
definitions.note: Common with "gut/schlecht laufen" to describe how something is going.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie läuft es? Bei mir läuft alles gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How’s it going? Everything’s going well for me.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “ongoing/current” (e.g., projects, costs, work).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Während der laufenden Arbeiten ist der Eingang geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the ongoing work, the entrance is closed.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) present tense or imperative form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr lauft jeden Morgen zur Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You run to school every morning.

definitions.note: Often used for people whose mood changes quickly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist heute sehr launisch und reagiert schnell genervt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very moody today and gets annoyed quickly.

definitions.note: Often used for listening attentively, sometimes secretly (eavesdropping), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lauscht an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He listens at the door.

definitions.note: simple past of "lauschen"; often implies listening attentively (sometimes secretly)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lauschte an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He listened at the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Musik ist zu laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music is too loud.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive in more formal German; often with the dative in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Laut dem Wetterbericht soll es morgen regnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the weather report, it's supposed to rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte lies den Satz laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please read the sentence out loud.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (declined), e.g. „laute Musik“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich höre laute Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m listening to loud music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich höre die lauten Geräusche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hear the loud noises.

definitions.note: Used mainly for the wording of texts, signs, questions, titles, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Satz muss genau so lauten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sentence has to read exactly like this.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte lauter sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak louder?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte lauter sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you speak louder, please?

definitions.note: Often used before a plural noun to mean “nothing but …”. Not related to English “louder” (that’s German: „lauter“ = comparative of „laut“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Kiste sind lauter alte Fotos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the box there are nothing but old photos.

definitions.note: Colloquial; used before a plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier stehen lauter Autos vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are lots of cars parked out front.

definitions.note: comparative of „laut“ in the sense of speaking/playing more loudly
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sprich bitte lauter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak louder.

definitions.note: adjective in a declined form (e.g., before a neuter noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hört lautes Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is listening to loud music.

definitions.note: Used to state the exact wording or content of something (a rule, a message, a title, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Frage lautet: Wie spät ist es?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The question is: What time is it?

definitions.note: Used to report the wording of something (e.g., a question, headline, rule).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Frage lautete: „Wie heißt du?“
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The question was: “What’s your name?”

definitions.native: at the top of one’s voice, loudly
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lachte lauthals über den Witz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He laughed loudly at the joke.

definitions.note: often implies speaking or reacting in a noticeably loud way (e.g., complaining or arguing)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fans protestierten lautstark vor dem Stadion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fans protested loudly in front of the stadium.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tee ist nur lauwarm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tea is only lukewarm.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular imperative of „lassen“; also written „lass“ in modern spelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Laß uns gehen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go!

definitions.note: Older spelling of „lasst“ (imperative, plural "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Laßt uns nach Hause gehen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go home!

definitions.note: Not used as a determiner in standard German; this is the French masculine singular definite article, sometimes seen in German contexts when quoting French.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf Französisch heißt „der Hund“: le chien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In French, “the dog” is: le chien.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) and imperative (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich lebe jetzt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says I live in Berlin now.

definitions.note: Imperative (du-form), used to tell one person to live (e.g., in the sense of enjoying life).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lebe dein Leben!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Live your life!

definitions.note: infinitive verb (dictionary form)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte in Berlin leben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to live in Berlin.

definitions.note: often used in fixed expressions (e.g., „das Leben“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das Leben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That's life.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist noch lebend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is still alive.

definitions.note: Declined form of "lebend" used before a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine lebende Pflanze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a living plant.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective/adjective-like participle "lebend" (e.g., after an article or other determiner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne den lebenden Künstler persönlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the living artist personally.

definitions.note: attributive form used before a masculine noun (e.g., „ein lebender Mensch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein lebender Fisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a living fish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt ist nachts sehr lebendig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is very lively at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie erzählt die Geschichte lebendig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tells the story vividly.

definitions.note: Often used to describe places, stories, or events as full of life and activity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Berlin ist eine lebendige Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Berlin is a lively city.

definitions.note: dative singular masculine/neuter form of the adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit lebendigem Interesse fragte sie nach dem Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With lively interest, she asked about the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir schützen die lebendigen Tiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We protect the living animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein lebendiger Markt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a lively market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt ist nachts lebendiger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is livelier at night.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., a prison sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde zu lebenslänglich verurteilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sentenced to life in prison.

definitions.note: A serious term often used to describe someone who feels they no longer want to live.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der schlechten Nachricht fühlte er sich lebensmüde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bad news, he felt suicidal.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal or old-fashioned; often used in written or solemn contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lebewohl, mein Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Farewell, my friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Diskussion war lebhaft und interessant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The discussion was lively and interesting.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with feminine nouns in the nominative or accusative (e.g., „eine lebhafte Diskussion“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten eine lebhafte Diskussion im Unterricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a lively discussion in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo lebst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you live?

definitions.note: third-person singular present tense of „leben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lebt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „leben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lebte früher in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lived in Berlin before.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 1st/3rd person plural (wir/sie/Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher lebten wir in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We used to live in Berlin.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „leben“ for „du“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du lebtest damals in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You lived in Berlin back then.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund kann meine Hand lecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog can lick my hand.

definitions.note: Often used about food and drinks; can also be used more generally to mean something is enjoyable (e.g., "Das war lecker!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist richtig lecker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is really delicious.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive form) with an adjective ending.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern eine leckere Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a delicious soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern den leckeren Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like the delicious cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund leckt meine Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog licks my hand.

definitions.note: Used for liquids/gases escaping from something (like a pipe or container).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Rohr leckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pipe is leaking.

definitions.note: Used mainly in official/formal contexts (e.g., on forms) to mean not married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dem Formular steht, dass ich ledig bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form it says that I am single.

definitions.note: Often used to downplay or limit something (similar to "just").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe lediglich eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have one question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Flasche ist leer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is empty.

definitions.note: weak ending; used before a noun (e.g., "eine leere Flasche")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werfe die leere Flasche weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m throwing away the empty bottle.

definitions.note: Often used for emptying out a container (a glass, bottle, box, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leere das Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I empty the glass.

definitions.note: Strong adjective (inflected form of „leer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich räume die leeren Flaschen weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put away the empty bottles.

definitions.note: Used for emptying out a container (e.g., bin, bottle, pocket); infinitive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen den Mülleimer leeren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will empty the trash can tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Eimer ist leerer als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bucket is emptier than the other one.

definitions.note: Used here as an adjective ending for neuter singular (e.g., „ein leeres Glas“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ein leeres Glas auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see an empty glass on the table.

definitions.note: simple past form of „leeren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er leerte das Glas in einem Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He emptied the glass in one go.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ablegen“; „ab“ usually comes at the end of the sentence (e.g. „Ich leg … ab.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leg meine Jacke ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take off my jacket.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „lege“ (from separable verb „anlegen“), often used in speech and informal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leg meinen Mantel an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my coat.

definitions.note: Often a colloquial shortened form of „lege“ (1st person singular), especially in spoken German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warte kurz, ich leg gleich auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a second, I’ll hang up in a moment.

definitions.note: Often a colloquial shortened form of „lege“ (1st person singular), especially in spoken German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leg noch ein Lied auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll put on another song.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative of „legen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leg das Buch auf den Tisch!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the book on the table!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist völlig legal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is completely legal.

definitions.note: used when ending a phone call (from separable verb „auflegen“: „ich lege … auf“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lege jetzt auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hanging up now.

definitions.note: used for starting music (e.g., putting on a CD/record)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lege die CD auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m putting on the CD.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Often used with an object and a place (e.g., something onto a table). Not related to the English word “leg”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte legen Sie das Buch auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put the book on the table.

definitions.native: to lay; to put (down); to place
definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: to place something somewhere (e.g., onto a surface).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Buch auf den Tisch legen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will put the book on the table.

definitions.note: 2nd-person singular present tense of "legen" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du legst das Buch auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put the book on the table.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anlegen“; in the present tense the prefix often goes to the end: „legt … an“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er legt seine Jacke an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts on his jacket.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of "legen" (he/she/it puts/lay)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er legt das Buch auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts the book on the table.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ablegen“; in the simple past the prefix often splits off: „legte … ab“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er legte gestern die Prüfung ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took the exam yesterday.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ablegen“; in the simple past the prefix often splits off: „legte … ab“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie legte ihre Jacke ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took off her jacket.

definitions.note: Past tense form of the separable verb „anlegen“ (e.g. „legte … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er legte seine Jacke an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put on his jacket.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „auflegen“ (e.g., „legte … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er legte auf und ging nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hung up and went home.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „auflegen“ (e.g., „legte … auf den Tisch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie legte das Buch auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She put the book on the table.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „einlegen“ (… legte … ein).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er legte die Karte in den Umschlag ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put the card into the envelope.

definitions.note: Often used with „eine Pause“: „eine Pause einlegen“ (… legte … ein).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir legten eine kurze Pause ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took a short break.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of "legen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er legte das Buch auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put the book on the table.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „legen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie legten die Bücher auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put the books on the table.

definitions.note: From the separable verb "ablehnen"; in a main clause the prefix usually goes to the end ("lehne ... ab").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lehne das Angebot ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reject the offer.

definitions.note: Often used with „an“ (e.g., „sich an etw. lehnen“ = to lean against sth.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann sich nicht lange an die Wand lehnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can’t lean against the wall for long.

definitions.note: Commonly in the separable verb „ablehnen“ (to reject/decline).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird das Angebot ablehnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will reject the offer.

definitions.note: simple past of „ablehnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lehnte das Angebot ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He declined the offer.

definitions.note: Simple past of „lehnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lehnte an der Wand und wartete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leaned against the wall and waited.

definitions.note: Simple past of „lehnen“ (often used with „ablehnen“ meaning to refuse something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lehnte das Angebot ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She declined the offer.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "ablehnen" (used with plural subjects or formal "Sie").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lehnten das Angebot ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They refused the offer.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lehre Deutsch an einer Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I teach German at a school.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts; for everyday situations, "unterrichten" is also common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: An der Universität lehren sie Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the university they teach German.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (er/sie/es lehrt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lehrt Deutsch an der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He teaches German at the school.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lehren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lehrte Deutsch an der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He taught German at the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Hausaufgaben sind heute leicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The homework is easy today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Tasche ist leicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das leicht erklären.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can explain that easily.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected form of „leicht“; the ending depends on gender/case and whether there is an article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine leichte Aufgabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an easy task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage einen leichten Koffer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m carrying a light suitcase.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir schreiben heute einen leichten Test.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re writing an easy test today.

definitions.note: comparative form of „leicht“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Koffer ist leichter als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This suitcase is lighter than the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit einem Plan geht es leichter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a plan, it goes more easily.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „leicht“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme den leichteren Koffer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take the lighter suitcase.

definitions.note: Neuter nominative/accusative singular form of the adjective "leicht" (often used before a neuter noun like "ein leichtes Gepäck").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme ein leichtes Gepäck mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm taking light luggage with me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Vertrag leichtfertig unterschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He signed the contract carelessly.

definitions.note: Past participle of the verb "leichtfallen"; commonly used with "sein" (e.g., "ist mir leichtgefallen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Prüfung ist mir leichtgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam was easy for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr leichtgläubig und glaubt alles, was man ihm erzählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very gullible and believes everything people tell him.

definitions.note: Usually describes behavior that ignores risks or consequences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war leichtsinnig von ihm, ohne Helm Motorrad zu fahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was reckless of him to ride a motorcycle without a helmet.

definitions.note: Used with forms of „sein“: „Es tut mir leid“ = “I’m sorry.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es tut mir leid, ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sorry, I don’t have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leide unter Rückenschmerzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suffer from back pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen leiden still.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people suffer silently.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „nicht leiden können“ = “can’t stand”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann es nicht leiden, wenn man zu spät kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand it when people arrive late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie singt leidenschaftlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sings passionately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leider habe ich heute keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I don’t have time today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "leiden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er leidet unter Rückenschmerzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suffers from back pain.

definitions.note: Often used as the phrase „Es tut mir leid“ (“I’m sorry”). In many sentences it appears split: „tut … leid“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wird dir leidtun, dass du das gesagt hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’ll regret that you said that.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form of „leihen“, addressed to one person; often written with an apostrophe as „leih’“ in informal writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leih mir bitte deinen Stift!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please lend me your pen!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leihe dir mein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lend you my book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leihe mir ein Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I borrow a bicycle.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" (e.g. "sich etwas leihen" = to borrow something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich mir dein Buch leihen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I borrow your book?

definitions.note: In some contexts "leihen" can also mean "to lend" (giving something for someone else to use); in everyday German, "ausleihen" or "verleihen" are also common for this meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir mein Fahrrad leihen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will lend you my bike.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "leihen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er leiht mir sein Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lends me his bicycle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sei leise, das Baby schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be quiet; the baby is sleeping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich leise, das Baby schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak quietly; the baby is sleeping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte leiser sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you speak more quietly, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte leiser sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak more quietly?

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „gute Arbeit leisten“ (do good work) or „Hilfe leisten“ (give help).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leiste heute gute Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m doing good work today.

definitions.note: Often used with „mir“ (e.g., „Ich leiste mir das nicht“ = I can’t afford that / I won’t treat myself to that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So ein Auto leiste ich mir nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t afford a car like that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen heute viel leisten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to accomplish a lot today.

definitions.note: Often used as: sich etwas leisten (to be able to afford something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mir das nicht leisten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't afford that.

definitions.note: Often used with nouns like „Arbeit“ (work) or „Hilfe“ (help), meaning to carry out or provide something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er leistet gute Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He does good work.

definitions.note: Past tense (Präteritum) of „leisten“; often used in fixed phrases like „(gute) Arbeit leisten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er leistete gute Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did good work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leite das Projekt bis zum Ende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lead the project until the end.

definitions.native: to lead; to manage; to be in charge of
definitions.note: Used for leading people/organizations or being in charge of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird das Team seit zwei Jahren leiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been going to lead the team for two years.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "leiten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie leitet das Projekt seit Januar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been leading the project since January.

definitions.note: Often used for steering (e.g., a car) or guiding/directing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lenk das Auto vorsichtig durch die Kurve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Steer the car carefully through the curve.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of „lenken“ (ich lenke).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lenke das Auto vorsichtig durch die enge Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I steer the car carefully through the narrow street.

definitions.note: Often used for steering a vehicle; also used more generally for directing something (e.g., attention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lenkt das Auto vorsichtig durch die enge Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He steers the car carefully through the narrow street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lenkt das Auto durch die enge Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He steers the car through the narrow street.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lenken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lenkte das Auto vorsichtig um die Kurve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He steered the car carefully around the curve.

definitions.note: Used as a verb stem in conjugated forms (e.g., ich lern(e), du lernst, er/sie/es lernt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lern Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning German.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present ("I learn").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learn German.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will jeden Tag lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to learn every day.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „lernen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du lernst gerade Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re learning German right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lernt heute für die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is learning for the exam today.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb "kennenlernen"; in the past tense it often appears as "lernte ... kennen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lernte ihn letztes Jahr kennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got to know him last year.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lernen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lernte gestern viel für die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned a lot for the exam yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural (wir/ihr/sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir lernten gestern viel Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We learned a lot of German yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schrift ist sehr klein, aber noch lesbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The writing is very small, but still readable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist lesbisch und lebt mit ihrer Freundin zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is lesbian and lives together with her girlfriend.

definitions.note: first-person singular present tense of "lesen" ("I read")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese jeden Abend ein Kapitel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read a chapter every evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute Abend ein Buch lesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will read a book this evening.

definitions.note: present participle (describes someone/something that is reading)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein lesendes Kind sitzt am Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A child who is reading is sitting by the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch ist wirklich lesenswert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is really worth reading.

definitions.note: Form of „lesen“ used with „ihr“ (you all) in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr lest jeden Abend ein Kapitel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You all read a chapter every evening.

definitions.note: As a noun it’s usually written with an article and capitalized (e.g., „die Letzte“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war die Letzte in der Schlange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was the last person in the line.

definitions.note: Often used with a definite article or possessive (e.g. „die letzte Woche“, „mein letzter Tag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die letzte Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the last question.

definitions.note: often used in phrases like „in den letzten …“ = “in the last …” (referring to the most recent past period).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe in den letzten Tagen viel gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve worked a lot in the last few days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztendlich haben wir uns für den Zug entschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ultimately, we decided to take the train.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used in everyday speech instead of the more formal "kürzlich"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztens war ich mit Freunden im Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The other day I went to the cinema with friends.

definitions.note: used with masculine singular nouns in the nominative case (e.g., „letzter Tag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist letzter Tag der Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is the last day of the trip.

definitions.note: Often used with time expressions (e.g., letztes Jahr = last year).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr habe ich Deutsch gelernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I learned German.

definitions.note: Usually written as two words: „letztes Mal“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztesmal war ich schon um acht zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last time I was already home by eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztlich müssen wir eine Entscheidung treffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ultimately, we have to make a decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sterne leuchten heute besonders hell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stars are shining especially brightly today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe die leuchtenden Sterne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the shining stars.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „leuchten“ (it/he/she shines).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht leuchtet hell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light shines brightly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich leugne, dass ich das gesagt habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deny that I said that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird alles leugnen, wenn man ihn fragt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will deny everything when you ask him.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „leugnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er leugnete, dass er das Geld genommen hatte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denied that he had taken the money.

definitions.note: formal (polite) form; intended as dative case (often used after prepositions like „mit“, „von“, or as an indirect object); note: standard spelling is „Ihnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich lhnen helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I help you?

definitions.native: (nonstandard) likely intended as “ihr”: her, their, your (plural, informal)
definitions.note: “lhr” is not a standard German word; it often appears as a typo/OCR error for “ihr” (lowercase i). In correct German, “ihr” can mean “her” (possessive), “their,” or “your” when addressing multiple people informally; compare “Ihr” (capital I) for formal “your.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist lhr Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is her car.

definitions.note: Not standard German spelling; likely intended “Ihr” (capital I). Used to address more than one person (informal plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: lhr seid heute sehr pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) are very punctual today.

definitions.note: Not standard German spelling; likely intended “ihr”. Dative pronoun meaning “to/for her”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe lhr das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give her the book.

definitions.note: Not standard German spelling; likely intended “ihr”. Possessive determiner; meaning depends on context (her = of one woman, their = of several people, your = belonging to “you” plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist lhr Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is her car.

definitions.native: (likely a typo for) her, their; (capitalized: Ihre) formal “your”
definitions.note: German normally uses "ihre/Ihre" with the letter i. "lhre" with an l is not standard; it may appear due to a font/reading error or OCR mistake.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe lhre Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see her sister.

definitions.note: When written with a capital I ("Ihrem"), it usually means formal "your."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe lhrem Vater das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving her father the book.

definitions.note: „lhren“ is not standard German; it is almost certainly a typo for „Ihren“ (formal/polite ‘your’) or „ihren“ (their/her, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe lhren Brief bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received your letter.

definitions.note: Likely an OCR/typo variant of „Lehrer“ (standard spelling). Used for a male teacher; the feminine form is „Lehrerin“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein lhrer ist sehr streng.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is very strict.

definitions.note: Likely intended as „Lehrer“; in German the plural is „Lehrer“ (same form as masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele lhrer arbeiten auch nachmittags.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many teachers also work in the afternoons.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone as kind/pleasant; also used as a polite form of address ("Liebe/r ..." = "Dear ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Nachbarin ist sehr lieb.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is very kind.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s friendly or caring behavior (e.g. “Das ist lieb von dir”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke, das ist sehr lieb von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks, that’s very kind of you.

definitions.note: feminine/plural form of the adjective „lieb“; often used before names or feminine nouns (e.g. „Liebe Anna …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine liebe Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a dear (kind) sister.

definitions.note: Used as a greeting in letters/emails before a name (e.g., “Liebe Anna,”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Liebe Anna, danke für deine Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Anna, thanks for your message.

definitions.note: Often used as the 1st person singular present form: „ich liebe“ = “I love”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich liebe dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love you.

definitions.note: often used as a friendly/polite form of address before a noun (especially in the plural), e.g. "meine lieben …"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine lieben Eltern wohnen in Hamburg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dear parents live in Hamburg.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich immer lieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will always love you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sah ihn liebend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looked at him lovingly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind ist wirklich liebenswert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is really lovable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr liebenswürdig und hilft allen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very kind and helps everyone.

definitions.note: Comparative of „gern“, used to express a preference (often with two options: „lieber … als …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke lieber Tee als Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d rather drink tea than coffee.

definitions.note: Comparative of "gern"; often used in the pattern "lieber ... als ..." ("rather ... than ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke lieber Tee als Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d rather drink tea than coffee.

definitions.note: Often used with „… lieber als …“ to express preference (similar to “prefer … to …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist Kaffee lieber als Tee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer coffee to tea.

definitions.note: Often used to express a preference (e.g., with „Ich möchte lieber …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe heute lieber zu Fuß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d rather walk today.

definitions.note: Often used to express a preference (e.g., “Ich hätte lieber …” = “I’d rather have …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke lieber Tee als Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d rather drink tea than coffee.

definitions.note: Often used before a neuter noun (e.g. „Kind“) as a friendly, affectionate description.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein liebes Kind, komm bitte her.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dear child, please come here.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form) of "lieben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du liebest mich wirklich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You really love me.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form, often used in reported/indirect speech (from "liebhaben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er liebhabe sie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he loves her.

definitions.native: to love (affectionately), to be fond of
definitions.note: Used for affectionate, often less romantic love (e.g., family members, children, pets, close friends).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich liebhaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love you (in an affectionate way).

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense form of "lieben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du liebst Musik, oder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You love music, right?

definitions.note: Superlative form of "lieb"; used like "my dearest ..." or "the dearest ..." depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist meine liebste Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my dearest friend.

definitions.note: Often used with "am" as in "am liebsten" = "most / most of all" (talking about preferences).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse Pizza am liebsten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like eating pizza the most.

definitions.note: Often used as a term of endearment (especially when addressing a man), e.g. at the start of a letter/message.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Liebster Paul, ich vermisse dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dearest Paul, I miss you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er liebt seine Familie sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He loves his family very much.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lieben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er liebte sie sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He loved her very much.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural or polite "Sie" form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher liebten sie lange Spaziergänge am Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, they loved long evening walks.

definitions.note: Simple past (du-form) of „lieben“; used for one person you address as „du“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als Kind liebtest du Märchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, you loved fairy tales.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „laufen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern lief ich nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ran home.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „laufen“ (plural: we/they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern liefen wir schnell nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we ran home quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir liefern die Bestellung morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll deliver the order tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Online-Shop liefert das Paket morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The online shop delivers the package tomorrow.

definitions.note: Means being in a lying position (e.g., on a bed); not usually “to tell a lie” in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich liege im Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m lying in bed.

definitions.note: Despite the POS given, this word is normally used as a verb in German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will im Bett liegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to lie in bed.

definitions.native: to be located, to be situated
definitions.note: Despite the POS given, this word is normally used as a verb in German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel soll am Strand liegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is supposed to be located on the beach.

definitions.native: to lie (be lying); to be located
definitions.note: Used for people/objects lying in a horizontal position, and for describing where something is located.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch muss flach liegen, damit es nicht beschädigt wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book has to lie flat so it doesn’t get damaged.

definitions.note: Used especially for vehicles or machines that stop working unexpectedly (often with "sein": "ist liegengeblieben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Auto ist auf der Autobahn liegengeblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My car broke down on the highway.

definitions.note: Past participle of „liegenlassen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „Ich habe … liegengelassen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Schlüssel zu Hause liegengelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my key at home.

definitions.native: to leave (something) behind, to leave (something) lying around
definitions.note: Often used when you forget something somewhere (e.g., on the train) or don’t pick it up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Handy im Zug liegenlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left my phone on the train.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du), present tense of "liegen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du liegst im Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are lying in bed.

definitions.note: Often used for location ("to be located"): "Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch." = "The book is on the table."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Handy liegt auf dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is lying on the couch.

definitions.note: Simple past of „leihen“. With a reflexive pronoun (e.g., „ich lieh mir …“) it can also mean „borrowed“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lieh meiner Freundin mein Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lent my friend my bike.

definitions.note: Simple past of „leihen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie liehen sich ein Auto für das Wochenende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They borrowed a car for the weekend.

definitions.note: informal singular command (imperative) of „lesen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lies bitte die E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please read the email.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "lesen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er liest jeden Abend ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reads a book every evening.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „lassen“ (ich/er/sie/es ließ)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ließ ihn gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I let him go.

definitions.note: Subjunctive II form of "lassen" (used for hypothetical/conditional statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ließe dich gehen, wenn ich könnte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would let you go if I could.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „lassen“ (plural or formal „you“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ließen die Kinder draußen spielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They let the children play outside.

definitions.note: Can also be Konjunktiv II (subjunctive II) plural of „lassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn es sicher wäre, ließen sie dich allein gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it were safe, they would let you go alone.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (simple past) form of „lassen“, used for hypothetical/contrary-to-fact situations (often in „wenn“-clauses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du mich gehen ließest, wäre ich dir dankbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you would let me go, I would be grateful to you.

definitions.note: Usually stays the same for all genders and cases (often used without endings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tasche ist lila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bag is purple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Medikament kann die Schmerzen lindern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This medication can relieve the pain.

definitions.note: Adjective form of „links“ used with a noun (e.g., feminine singular or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nimm die linke Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the left hand.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „links“ (e.g., after „mit“: „mit der linken Hand“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schreibe mit der linken Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I write with my left hand.

definitions.note: Used for something on the left side (e.g., body parts, directions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein linker Arm tut weh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My left arm hurts.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (e.g., „linkes Knie“ = “left knee”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein linkes Knie tut weh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My left knee hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Apotheke ist links neben dem Supermarkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pharmacy is on the left next to the supermarket.

definitions.note: simple past of „leiden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er litt lange unter starken Kopfschmerzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suffered from severe headaches for a long time.

definitions.note: Used for events happening in real time (e.g., TV/radio/internet) or experienced in person (not recorded).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert wird heute Abend live im Fernsehen übertragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert will be broadcast live on TV this evening.

definitions.note: Used especially for live broadcasts/streams (e.g., TV, radio, online).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind jetzt live.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are live now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lobe dich für deine gute Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I praise you for your good work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer will die Klasse für ihre gute Arbeit loben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher wants to praise the class for their good work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Einsatz für das Team ist wirklich lobenswert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your commitment to the team is truly praiseworthy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lobt seine Tochter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He praises his daughter.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „loben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer lobte die Klasse für ihre gute Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher praised the class for their good work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Duft von frischem Brot kann viele Menschen in die Bäckerei locken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smell of fresh bread can lure many people into the bakery.

definitions.note: Often used for clothing or objects that are not tight; also for a relaxed atmosphere or attitude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schraube ist locker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The screw is loose.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verband sitzt locker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bandage is sitting loosely.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech to mean something is done without much effort.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das schaffe ich locker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can do that easily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Duft von frischem Brot lockt viele Kunden an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smell of fresh bread attracts many customers.

definitions.note: simple past of „lügen“ (to lie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er log mich an und sagte, er hätte keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lied to me and said he didn't have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist logisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is logical.

definitions.note: Often used colloquially to mean “of course” or “sure,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Logisch komme ich morgen mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of course I'll come along tomorrow.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die logische Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the logical answer.

definitions.native: to be worth it, to pay off
definitions.note: Often used in the reflexive form „sich lohnen“ (e.g., „Es lohnt sich …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früh aufzustehen kann sich lohnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Getting up early can be worth it.

definitions.note: Often used with “sich” (as in “es lohnt sich”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das lohnt sich nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s not worth it.

definitions.note: Often used predicatively (with „sein“), e.g. „Der Knopf ist los.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Knopf ist los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The button is loose.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „sein“ or „werden“ to mean something is detached or no longer fixed in place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Knopf ist los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The button is loose.

definitions.note: Often used as an exclamation to start, hurry, or set off (e.g. „Los!“, „Los geht’s!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los, wir müssen jetzt gehen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, we have to go now!

definitions.note: Often used to get things started or encourage someone to begin; also common in the phrase "Na los!" (= "Come on!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los, wir müssen jetzt gehen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go, we have to leave now!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „losfahren/losgehen/loslassen“ and in the phrase „Was ist los?“ (= What’s going on?).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was ist los?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s going on?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schrauben sind lose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The screws are loose.

definitions.native: to set off; to depart (by vehicle); to drive off
definitions.note: Separable verb: present tense often appears as "fährt ... los"; the infinitive is "losfahren". Used for starting a trip or departing in a vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen um sieben Uhr losfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to set off at seven o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen morgen früh losfliegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to take off early tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Past participle of „losgehen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist losgegangen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert ist um acht losgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert started at eight.

definitions.note: Past participle of „losgehen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist losgegangen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind früh losgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We set off early.

definitions.note: Often used for starting a trip or leaving somewhere; also used for something beginning (e.g., an event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen jetzt losgehen, sonst verpassen wir den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to set off now, otherwise we'll miss the bus.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „losgehen“; often used with „es“ (e.g. „Es geht los.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film losgeht um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie starts at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: past participle of „loswerden“, often used with „sein“ (e.g., „Ich bin … losgeworden“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin den alten Kühlschrank endlich losgeworden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finally got rid of the old fridge.

definitions.native: to start bawling, to burst into loud crying
definitions.note: Colloquial; emphasizes loud, sudden crying.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als er das gehört hat, hat er sofort losheulen müssen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he heard that, he immediately had to start bawling.

definitions.note: Used both literally (release your grip) and figuratively (stop holding on emotionally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst meine Hand loslassen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to let go of my hand!

definitions.note: Often used when starting an activity right away ("Let’s get going!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können jetzt loslegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can get started now.

definitions.note: Often used with an object in the accusative (e.g., etwas/jemanden loswerden).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss diese alten Sachen loswerden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to get rid of these old things.

definitions.native: to set off, to start driving
definitions.note: Infinitive with "zu" (used after verbs like "versuchen" and after "um ... zu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, pünktlich loszufahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We try to set off on time.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of "loswerden" (often used with another verb, e.g. "versuchen, ... loszuwerden").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, meine schlechten Gewohnheiten loszuwerden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to get rid of my bad habits.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „einladen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lud mich zu seiner Geburtstagsparty ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He invited me to his birthday party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lugte durch das Schlüsselloch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He peeked through the keyhole.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film ist wirklich lustig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is really funny.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., "lustige Geschichte" = "funny story").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine lustige Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a funny story.

definitions.note: Usually used with a noun in the weak declension (e.g., after der/die/das, dieser, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag den lustigen Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the funny movie.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "lustig".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der zweite Film ist lustiger als der erste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The second movie is funnier than the first.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with neuter singular nouns like „ein lustiges Spiel“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein lustiges Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a funny game.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form, often used in reported speech (e.g. after verbs like „sagen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagte, er lächele nur aus Höflichkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said he was only smiling out of politeness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie muss lächeln, als sie die Nachricht liest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to smile as she reads the message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stand lächelnd in der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stood in the doorway, smiling.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stand lächelnd an der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She stood at the door, smiling.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum lächelst du so?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you smiling like that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lächelt und sagt nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He smiles and doesn’t say anything.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lächeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lächelte, als er die gute Nachricht hörte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He smiled when he heard the good news.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lächelten und winkten mir zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They smiled and waved to me.

definitions.note: Often expresses strong disapproval or that something isn’t to be taken seriously.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist lächerlich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s ridiculous!

definitions.note: First-person singular present subjunctive I; also used as a polite/soft command (“(you should) smile”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sagt, ich lächle zu wenig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She says I smile too little.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "einladen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lädt seine Freunde zur Party ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He invites his friends to the party.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „herunterladen“; in a sentence it’s usually „lädt … herunter“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lädt die Datei herunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He downloads the file.

definitions.note: Weak adjective ending; often used after a definite article or similar word.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen einen Spaziergang in der ländlichen Gegend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking a walk in the rural area.

definitions.note: comparative form of "lang"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film ist länger als ich gedacht habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is longer than I thought.

definitions.note: comparative form of "lang"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte länger bleiben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please stay longer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte länger bleiben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please stay longer?

definitions.note: comparative form of „lang“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bleibe heute länger im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m staying longer at the office today.

definitions.note: comparative form of "lang" (long); used before a noun (declined adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen eine längere Pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking a longer break.

definitions.native: a long time ago, long since
definitions.note: Often used with the present tense to mean that something happened earlier and is still true now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es längst vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot it a long time ago.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "lang" used with endings (e.g., with articles: der/die/das längste).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der längste Weg nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the longest way home.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "lassen"; often used with an infinitive (e.g., "lässt ... machen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lässt mich heute früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lets me leave earlier today.

definitions.note: 3rd-person singular present tense of "lassen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lässt mich in Ruhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leaves me alone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die ständigen Fragen sind wirklich lästig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The constant questions are really annoying.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) present tense of "laufen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum läufst du so schnell?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you running so fast?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „laufen“ (he/she/it runs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund läuft schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog runs fast.

definitions.note: Usually used for bells (e.g., church bells, doorbells) or phones.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Glocken läuten jeden Sonntagmorgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bells ring every Sunday morning.

definitions.note: Used for bells, doorbells, phones, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Telefon läutet schon wieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is ringing again.

definitions.note: simple past of „läuten“ (used for bells, doorbells, church bells)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich läutete das Telefon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly the phone rang.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of „lassen“ (often written „lässt“ in modern spelling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er läßt mich heute früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lets me leave earlier today.

definitions.note: informal singular command (du imperative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lösch die Datei, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Delete the file, please.

definitions.note: informal singular command (du imperative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lösch das Feuer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put out the fire!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of „löschen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lösche die Datei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I delete the file.

definitions.note: Common for deleting files/messages or removing text/data.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du diese Datei bitte löschen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please delete this file?
