definitions.note: Used for stopping a fire, flame, or a light.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr konnte das Feuer schnell löschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department was able to put out the fire quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er löscht die E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deletes the email.

definitions.note: Used for fires, candles, and similar things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr löscht das Feuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department puts out the fire.

definitions.note: simple past of „löschen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich löschte die E-Mail aus Versehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deleted the email by mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du diese Aufgabe lösen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you solve this problem?

definitions.note: Often used for undoing something that is tied (e.g., a knot) or making something less tight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Knoten lösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to untie the knot.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „auflösen“; in the present tense the prefix „auf“ often goes to the end of the sentence (e.g., „löst … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tablette löst sich im Wasser auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tablet dissolves in the water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie löst das Problem schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She solves the problem quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er löst den Knoten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He unties the knot.

definitions.note: Simple past of the separable verb „auslösen“; the particle „aus“ often comes at the end of the clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rauch löste den Alarm aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke triggered the alarm.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lösen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie löste das Problem in wenigen Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She solved the problem in a few minutes.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „lösen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mechaniker löste die Schraube vorsichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mechanic loosened the screw carefully.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal (du) imperative: „Lüg!“ (= „Lie!“). It can also appear as a colloquial form of „lüge“ (“I lie”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lüg nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't lie!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lüge nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht lügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t lie.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du lügst mich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are lying to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er lügt nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He isn’t lying.

definitions.note: Used as an informal command (imperative) with the separable verb "aufmachen"; "auf" usually comes later in the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte das Fenster auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please open the window!

definitions.note: Usually the informal singular imperative of „machen“ (as in „Mach das!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte die Tür zu!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please close the door!

definitions.note: Informal command (imperative) form of „machen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte die Tür zu!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please close the door!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist machbar, wenn wir heute anfangen.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He closed the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Unterstützung fühlte er sich machtlos.

definitions.note: From "mögen"; often used with a direct object or with "gern".

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective; used before a noun (attributive)

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Magst du Kaffee?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like coffee?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of „mögen“; often used to express liking or preference.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like coffee?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr Deutsch ist makellos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her German is flawless.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like „ein Mal“ (once) or „das nächste Mal“ (next time).

definitions.note: Often used as a particle to make a request sound more casual or friendly (common in imperatives).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dem Hemd ist ein Mal.

definitions.note: Often used as a modal particle to soften a request or suggestion (similar to “just” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm mal her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here for a moment!

definitions.note: Often used as “ich male …” (“I paint/draw …”); can also be the informal imperative “Male!” (“Paint!/Draw!”).

definitions.note: Impersonal pronoun used for general statements (similar to English “one,” “people,” or generic “you”). Not the same as the noun “Mann” (= man).

definitions.note: Used with plural nouns (and sometimes with uncountable nouns); often means “some (people/things),” “a few.”

definitions.note: often used for people or things in the plural (e.g., "Manche Leute ...")

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some people don’t drink coffee.

definitions.note: Used to refer to an unspecified subset of people or things; often implies “some (but not all)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manche Leute trinken keinen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some people don't drink coffee.

definitions.note: Accusative masculine singular (or accusative plural) form of the determiner "manch".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know some mistake in this text.

definitions.note: used as an indefinite pronoun; refers to several unspecified things

definitions.note: Used as a pronoun meaning “some things” or “a few things.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manchmal gehe ich nach der Arbeit noch spazieren.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally: „es mangelt an + dative“ (there is a lack of …).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Foto ist manipuliert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo is manipulated.

definitions.note: colloquial exclamation to show surprise, annoyance, or emphasis

definitions.note: often used for physically marking something or indicating/highlighting it (e.g., in a document or on a map)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The physiotherapist massaged my back.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to mean something is perfectly suited to a person or purpose.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She needs medical help.

definitions.note: Often used with an article, e.g. „die meisten“ = “most (people/things)” in the plural.

definitions.note: superlative form of „viel“ (used with plural nouns, e.g. „die meisten …“)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Most people come by bus.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually walk to work.

definitions.note: Often used for successfully handling or coping with a difficult task or situation.

definitions.note: Often used for reporting information (to the police, a teacher, etc.) or registering/announcing yourself (e.g., at a hotel or for an event).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du merkst sofort, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You notice right away that something isn’t right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er merkt sofort, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He notices right away that something isn’t right.

definitions.note: Often used with “sich merken” (to memorize/remember something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie merkt sich seinen Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She remembers his name.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "merken"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich merkte, dass ich meinen Schlüssel vergessen hatte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed that I had forgotten my key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir merkten sofort, dass etwas nicht stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We noticed right away that something was wrong.

definitions.note: Often used neutrally (“unusual”) or with mild suspicion (“something’s not right”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wirklich merkwürdig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is really strange.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “strange/odd” (not “remarkable” in a positive sense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verhält sich heute merkwürdig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is behaving strangely today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine merkwürdige Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a strange story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen merkwürdigen Traum gehabt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a strange dream.

definitions.note: Often means "strange" rather than "remarkable" (German "bemerkenswert").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein merkwürdiger Geruch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a strange smell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute etwas Merkwürdiges gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw something strange today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Länge des Tisches messen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to measure the length of the table.

definitions.note: Interjection used to show hesitation, thinking, or agreement (depending on intonation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mh, ich weiß nicht, ob das eine gute Idee ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hmm, I don't know if that's a good idea.

definitions.note: informal; used to show agreement or that you’re listening (often like “yes”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: „Kommst du mit?“ – „Mhm.“
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “Are you coming with?” – “Mm-hmm.”

definitions.note: Common abbreviation for „Mittwoch“, used in calendars and schedules.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Mi habe ich frei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m off on Wed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze beginnt laut zu miauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat starts to meow loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze miaut vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat meows in front of the door.

definitions.note: accusative form of "ich" (I)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mich hören?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you hear me?

definitions.note: Accusative form of „ich“ (also used reflexively: „mich“ = myself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sieht mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sees me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er mied den Konflikt und ging nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He avoided the conflict and went home.

definitions.note: Often used in informal speech to describe something unpleasant or of poor quality (e.g., weather, mood, situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter ist heute mies.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is lousy today.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used to describe something unpleasant or of poor quality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine miese Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a lousy idea.

definitions.note: Often used in casual speech to describe something unpleasant (weather, mood, situation, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dem miesen Wetter bleiben wir lieber zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this lousy weather, we'd rather stay at home.

definitions.note: comparative form of "mies".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist das Wetter noch mieser als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the weather is even lousier than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mieses Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s lousy weather.

definitions.note: Used when you pay to use something temporarily (e.g., an apartment, a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir mieten eine Wohnung in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We rent an apartment in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „mieten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr mietete ich eine kleine Wohnung in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I rented a small apartment in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir mieteten ein Auto für das Wochenende.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We rented a car for the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Winter ist dieses Jahr mild.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The winter is mild this year.

definitions.note: comparative form of "mild"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist das Wetter milder als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the weather is milder than yesterday.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a noun (e.g., with a feminine noun in nominative or accusative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die militärische Ausbildung dauert sechs Monate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The military training lasts six months.

definitions.note: Used for people who have not yet reached the legal age (e.g., 18).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist noch minderjährig und darf keinen Alkohol kaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is still underage and is not allowed to buy alcohol.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst mindestens 18 Jahre alt sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must be at least 18 years old.

definitions.note: Used with a number or amount to subtract it (common in math and prices).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kostet 50 Euro minus 10 Euro Rabatt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That costs 50 euros minus a 10-euro discount.

definitions.note: often used with numbers and in math (e.g., “minus zehn” = “minus ten”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe minus zehn Grad gemessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I measured minus ten degrees.

definitions.note: Dative form of "ich"; often means "to me" or is used as an indirect object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help me?

definitions.note: dative form of „ich“; often used reflexively (e.g. „ich wasche mir …“ = I wash … for myself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wasche mir die Hände.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my hands.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular) of "mischen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Misch die Zutaten gut!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mix the ingredients well!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense ("I").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mische Mehl und Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mix flour and water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Zutaten gut mischen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you mix the ingredients well?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "mischen" (he/she/it mixes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er mischt Zucker in den Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mixes sugar into the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir geht es heute miserabel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel miserable today.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "miserabel".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter ist heute miserabler als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is more miserable today than yesterday.

definitions.note: Command form (informal singular) of "messen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Miss die Länge des Tisches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Measure the length of the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er missbraucht seine Macht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He abuses his power.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of „missbrauchen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Trainer missbrauchte seine Macht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coach abused his power.

definitions.note: Often used like: "etwas missfällt jemandem" (the thing is the subject; the person is in the dative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es kann dir missfallen, aber ich finde den Plan gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It may displease you, but I think the plan is good.

definitions.note: Used with dative for the person who is displeased: „Das missfällt mir.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Ton missfällt mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your tone displeases me.

definitions.note: Often refers to physical or serious abuse (e.g., of a person or animal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wurde jahrelang misshandelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was abused for years.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of „messen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt misst meinen Blutdruck.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor measures my blood pressure.

definitions.note: Verb; used with the dative case (jemandem/etwas misstrauen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich misstraue ihm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I distrust him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist misstrauisch und glaubt nicht alles, was man ihm erzählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is suspicious and doesn't believe everything people tell him.

definitions.note: Also commonly used as an adjective meaning “suspicious/distrustful.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaute mich misstrauisch an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked at me suspiciously.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich missverstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I misunderstood you.

definitions.note: mild swear word used to express annoyance or frustration
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mist, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn, I forgot my key!

definitions.note: Usually used with the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe mit meiner Freundin ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the movies with my girlfriend.

definitions.note: Used as an adverb, often in phrases like “Komm mit!” (= come along).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du mit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming along?

definitions.note: Used as a particle with verbs like "mitkommen"; often in questions/commands (e.g., "Kommst du mit?" = "Are you coming along?").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du mit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming along?

definitions.note: Often used meaning you learn or realize something (sometimes by overhearing or catching it indirectly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gar nicht mitbekommen, dass du schon da bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t even notice that you were already here.

definitions.note: often used when bringing something to a place/meeting (e.g., “Bring your ID along.”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte deinen Ausweis mitbringen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please bring your ID along?

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize interaction/doing something jointly, not just being in the same place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir arbeiten gut miteinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We work well together.

definitions.native: ride along, come along (in a vehicle)
definitions.note: Means traveling together with someone in a car, bus, train, etc.; often used when you join someone else’s trip (e.g., in their car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich morgen mit dir mitfahren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I ride along with you tomorrow?

definitions.note: past participle of "mitbringen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir ein Buch mitgebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought you a book.

definitions.native: to come along, to go along (with)
definitions.note: Often used informally to mean joining someone as they go somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du mit? Ich kann nicht, aber du kannst mitgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming along? I can’t, but you can come along.

definitions.note: past participle of „mitkommen“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern mitgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came along yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "mitkriegen"; commonly used in spoken German meaning "to become aware of" or "to catch" (information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht mitgekriegt, dass du schon da bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t notice that you were already here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe beim Spiel mitgemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I participated in the game.

definitions.note: past participle of "mitnehmen"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Regenschirm mitgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took my umbrella with me.

definitions.note: Often used to describe being emotionally caught up or strongly influenced by something (e.g., music, a mood, an event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war von der Musik mitgerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was carried away by the music.

definitions.note: Often used to mean joining in (e.g., in a game or activity) or cooperating.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat bei dem Spiel mitgespielt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She played along in the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat mitgeteilt, dass die Straße gesperrt ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police informed us that the road is closed.

definitions.note: Often used with “mit” + dative or “bei” + dative to say you can keep up with someone/something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann beim Joggen nicht mithalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't keep up while jogging.

definitions.note: Often used in sentences where the separable prefix stays attached, e.g. in a subordinate clause: „…, dass ich mitkomme.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass ich morgen mitkomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that I can come along tomorrow.

definitions.note: Separable verb: *mitkommen* → *ich komme mit*, *komm mit!*; in the example sentence below the infinitive *mitkommen* is used explicitly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Willst du morgen mitkommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to come along tomorrow?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of „mitkommen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du mit, oder mitkommst du später?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming along, or are you coming later?

definitions.note: Often used for participating in an activity, event, or game.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Machst du bei dem Spiel mitmachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you joining in the game?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form) of „mitmachen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du bei dem Spiel mitmachst, macht es mehr Spaß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you join in the game, it’s more fun.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "mitmachen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er mitmacht beim Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He joins in the game.

definitions.note: used when you bring someone/something with you to another place
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde meinen Regenschirm mitnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take my umbrella with me.

definitions.native: play along; take part (in a game)
definitions.note: Often used for participating in a game or activity with others; can also mean cooperating/going along with something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spielst du heute Abend mitspielen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you playing along tonight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mittags esse ich oft eine Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At noon I often eat soup.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal or written contexts (e.g., announcements, official messages).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte Ihnen mitteilen, dass der Termin verschoben wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to inform you that the appointment has been postponed.

definitions.note: Often expresses mild criticism (not very good).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war mittelmäßig, aber die Musik war gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was mediocre, but the music was good.

definitions.note: Formal; used with the genitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir lösen das Problem mittels eines neuen Programms.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We solve the problem by means of a new program.

definitions.note: Often used with a noun phrase in the dative: „mitten in + Dativ“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir stehen mitten im Regen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are standing in the middle of the rain.

definitions.native: right in the middle (of it), in the middle
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich standen wir mittendrin im Gedränge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly we were right in the middle of the crowd.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „mittel“ used before a noun (e.g., „im mittleren Stockwerk“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wohnt im mittleren Stockwerk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives on the middle floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mittlerweile habe ich keine Zeit mehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By now I don’t have any time anymore.

definitions.note: Slightly more formal than "manchmal".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mitunter regnet es hier sogar im Sommer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes it even rains here in summer.

definitions.native: to bring along, to bring with (you)
definitions.note: zu-Infinitive form of "mitbringen" (often used after verbs like "vergessen" / "versuchen" / "bitten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergessen, meinen Ausweis mitzubringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to bring my ID with me.

definitions.note: Used with another verb (e.g., "versuchen, mitzukommen"); the separable verb is "mitkommen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versuch bitte, mitzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please try to come along.

definitions.native: to join in, to take part
definitions.note: Used with another verb after a verb like „versuchen“, „bitten“, etc. (zu-infinitive form of „mitmachen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Lust, mitzumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel like joining in.

definitions.native: to take along, to bring along
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, deinen Regenschirm mitzunehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to take your umbrella with you.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of "mitteilen" (often used after verbs like "bitten", "versprechen", "hoffen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte rufen Sie mich an, um mir die Entscheidung mitzuteilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please call me to let me know the decision.

definitions.note: Spelling: modern German usually writes this as „misstrauisch“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr mißtrauisch gegenüber Fremden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very suspicious of strangers.

definitions.note: Older spelling; today it’s usually written "missverstanden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich mißverstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I misunderstood you.

definitions.note: An informal sound used to show agreement or that you’re thinking/considering something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mm, das klingt gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mm-hmm, that sounds good.

definitions.note: colloquial/regionally used (especially in parts of northern and western Germany)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mo, ich bin gleich fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hang on, I'll be finished in a moment.

definitions.note: simple past of „mögen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als Kind mochte ich Spinat nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I didn’t like spinach.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "mögen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als Kinder mochten wir Eis sehr gern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As kids, we really liked ice cream.

definitions.note: simple past (du-form) of „mögen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du mochtest den Film sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You liked the movie a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Schule ist sehr modern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our school is very modern.

definitions.note: Declined form of the adjective (used before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen in einer modernen Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a modern apartment.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine/neuter dative singular or plural (e.g., after articles like „den“, „die“, „mit den“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen in einem modernen Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a modern house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Handy ist moderner als mein altes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cellphone is more modern than my old one.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a neuter singular noun (e.g., "ein modernes ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein modernes Gebäude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a modern building.

definitions.note: Used to ask someone to wait briefly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Moment, ich bin gleich da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One moment, I'll be right there.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a temporary situation right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe momentan keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have time at the moment.

definitions.note: Emphasizes a long duration; often used with a sense of “for months on end.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe monatelang auf einen Termin gewartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited for months for an appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bezahle die Miete monatlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pay the rent monthly.

definitions.note: used to talk about something that regularly happens on Mondays
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Montags gehe ich nach der Arbeit ins Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Mondays I go to the gym after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist moralisch nicht vertretbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That isn’t morally justifiable.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with "die", "eine"); the ending changes depending on case/gender/number.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine moralische Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a moral question.

definitions.note: As a noun, it’s usually capitalized in German: „der Morgen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Morgen trinke ich Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the morning I drink coffee.

definitions.note: Often used with the preposition „bis“: „bis morgen“ (= see you tomorrow).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sehen uns morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll see each other tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sehen uns morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll see each other tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to talk about the time of day (often contrasted with “abends” = in the evening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin morgen oft müde, aber abends habe ich viel Energie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m often tired in the morning, but in the evening I have a lot of energy.

definitions.note: Used as a greeting, often as a short form of "Guten Morgen!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen! Wie geht’s?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good morning! How are you?

definitions.note: Used as a noun meaning the time of day; not the adverb “tomorrow” (which is usually “morgen” without “am”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen früh habe ich einen Termin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow morning I have an appointment.

definitions.note: Refers to the morning in general or as a habitual time (not usually to one specific morning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe morgens joggen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go jogging in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute sehr motiviert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very motivated today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute sehr motiviert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very motivated today.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally with "es" ("es munkelt, dass ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es munkelt, dass die Firma bald verkauft wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is rumored that the company will be sold soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind heute besonders munter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are especially cheerful today.

definitions.note: Often used for being well-rested or not sleepy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Kaffee bin ich wieder munter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the coffee, I'm awake again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er murmelte etwas Unverständliches vor sich hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He muttered something unintelligible to himself.

definitions.note: Used here as an adjective with a neuter noun (e.g., „ein musikalisches Kind“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ein musikalisches Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a musical child.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „müssen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss heute arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go now.

definitions.note: 1st/3rd person singular present tense of „müssen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to work today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "müssen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to go now.

definitions.note: simple past of „müssen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich musste heute früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to get up early today.

definitions.note: simple past of „müssen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich musste gestern lange arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to work for a long time yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "müssen"; used mainly in writing and formal speech (in conversation often replaced by "haben ... müssen" in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir mussten früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to get up early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musstest gestern lange arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to work for a long time yesterday.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr), simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr musstet gestern früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to get up early yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr mutig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very brave.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with a feminine noun like „die mutige Frau“ or in plural like „mutige Menschen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die mutige Frau hilft dem Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The brave woman helps the child.

definitions.note: comparative form of "mutig"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist heute mutiger als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is braver today than yesterday.

definitions.note: Old spelling; today usually written as „muss“ (from „müssen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muß jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go now.

definitions.note: Old spelling of „muss“ (from „müssen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muß heute arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to work today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of the auxiliary verb "müssen"; old spelling—today usually written "musst".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du mußt heute früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to get up early today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "müssen" (older spelling; today usually written "musst").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du mußt jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must go now.

definitions.note: Older spelling of „musste“ (pre-1996 spelling reform).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mußte heute länger arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to work longer today.

definitions.note: Old spelling of „mussten“ (modern). Past tense form of „müssen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir mußten gestern lange warten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to wait a long time yesterday.

definitions.note: past tense form of „müssen“ (used with an infinitive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du mußtest gestern lange warten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to wait a long time yesterday.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural simple past of "müssen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr mußtet gestern früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You had to get up early yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der König ist sehr mächtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king is very powerful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der König herrschte mächtig über sein Reich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king ruled his kingdom powerfully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine mächtige Armee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a powerful army.

definitions.note: comparative form of „mächtig“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Land ist mächtiger als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This country is more powerful than the other one.

definitions.note: Superlative form of "mächtig" (powerful).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die mächtigste Person im Unternehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the most powerful person in the company.

definitions.note: Usually refers to mowing grass (e.g., with a lawnmower).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute den Rasen mähen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to mow the lawn today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er mäht heute den Rasen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mows the lawn today.

definitions.note: often used for people or animals; also used in forms/records to indicate sex/gender
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Welpe ist männlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The puppy is male.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with nouns (e.g., before a noun); often means “male” in the sense of gender/sex.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir suchen einen männlichen Bewerber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are looking for a male applicant.

definitions.note: Often used to make polite requests (from the verb "mögen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Common polite way to say what you want; from the verb „mögen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: polite way to say you want something (often used for requests)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte einen Kaffee, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Polite way to express a wish or request; often followed by an infinitive (e.g., „Ich möchte gehen.“) or a noun (e.g., „Ich möchte einen Kaffee.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchten einen Kaffee, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Used to express a polite wish or request (common in questions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möchtest du einen Kaffee?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form, used mainly in polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möchtest du einen Kaffee?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like a coffee?

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr). Often used to make polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möchtet ihr etwas trinken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like something to drink?

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr); polite-sounding form used for wishes/requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möchtet ihr etwas trinken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you (all) like something to drink?

definitions.note: Used mainly in formal/literary wishes (subjunctive), often at the start of a sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möge dir das Glück hold sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: May fortune be with you.

definitions.note: Used mainly in formal or literary wishes/benedictions (Konjunktiv I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möge das Glück mit dir sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: May luck be with you.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or literary wishes and formulas (Konjunktiv).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möge er in Frieden ruhen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: May he rest in peace.

definitions.note: Commonly used to express liking or preference; often with an object or infinitive (e.g., „Ich mag …“, „Ich mag es, … zu …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like coffee.

definitions.note: As a modal verb, it can express possibility (often in constructions like „Es mögen …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mögen heute Gewitter auftreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thunderstorms might occur today.

definitions.native: to be fond of; to like (someone/something)
definitions.note: Can also be used for people/things you are fond of (informal/common).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir mögen unsere Nachbarn sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We like our neighbors a lot.

definitions.note: Infinitive form; in many everyday sentences you’ll see conjugated forms like „mag“, but this example uses the exact word „mögen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss gestehen, dass ich Schokolade mögen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to admit that I like chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist es morgen möglich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is it possible tomorrow?

definitions.note: adjective form (declined)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gibt es eine mögliche Lösung?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is there a possible solution?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möglicherweise kommt sie morgen zu Besuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maybe she will come to visit tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize making something the maximum degree possible (often with adjectives/adverbs like „schnell“ or „bald“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte komm möglichst bald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come as soon as possible.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural form (ihr): “you (all) like”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr mögt Schokolade, oder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) like chocolate, right?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am very tired today.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of the adjective „müde“ (e.g., after „einen/den/die/das“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den müden Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the tired man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die Prüfung mühelos bestanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She passed the exam effortlessly.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" (reflexive): "sich mühen" = to struggle/try hard.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mühte mich, die Aufgabe zu verstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I struggled to understand the task.

definitions.note: Used especially for rivers/streams flowing into a larger river, a lake, or the sea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fluss mündet in den Rhein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flows into the Rhine.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to describe a process or action ending in a result.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gespräch mündet in einen Streit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conversation leads to an argument.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist heute mürrisch und will nicht reden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is grumpy today and doesn’t want to talk.

definitions.native: would have to (if I/he/she/it were to), might have to
definitions.note: Konjunktiv I (subjunctive I) form of „müssen“ (1st/3rd person singular), common in reported speech and indirect statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagte, er müsse heute länger arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said that he would have to work longer today.

definitions.note: Often used to convey someone else’s claim or statement in indirect speech (Konjunktiv I), sometimes with a distancing/neutral tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie behauptet, ich müsse sofort gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She claims that I must leave immediately.

definitions.note: Modal verb used to express necessity or obligation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich denke, dass wir morgen arbeiten müssen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that we have to work tomorrow.

definitions.note: Modal verb; expresses necessity or obligation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen heute früher anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to start earlier today.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural present (ihr) of „müssen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr müsst jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) have to go now.

definitions.native: would have to, would need to
definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of "müssen"; often used for polite suggestions or hypothetical necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich müsste heute früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have to leave earlier today.

definitions.native: would have to, would need to
definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of "müssen"; often used for polite suggestions or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssten jetzt losfahren, sonst kommen wir zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have to leave now, otherwise we’ll be late.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II of "müssen"; used for hypothetical situations or polite suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du müsstest morgen früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You would have to get up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: Older spelling of modern "müsst" (2nd person plural: "you" as in "you all").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr müßt jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to go now.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) present tense of „müssen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr müßt jetzt nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to go home now.

definitions.native: would have to, would need to
definitions.note: Subjunctive II form of "müssen"; often used to make something sound less direct or to talk about a hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich müßte heute früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have to leave earlier today.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II of "müssen". Old spelling; modern spelling is usually "müsste".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich müßte morgen früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have to get up early tomorrow morning.

definitions.native: would have to, would need to
definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form (often used for hypothetical situations or polite suggestions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müßten jetzt gehen, sonst verpassen wir den Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have to go now, otherwise we'll miss the train.

definitions.note: Very common interjection; meaning depends on tone and context. Often used to start a question or conversation, like “well?” or “so?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Na, wie geht's dir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So, how are you?

definitions.note: used for direction to cities/countries (usually with dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fliegen morgen nach Spanien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re flying to Spain tomorrow.

definitions.note: used for time (usually with dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Schule gehe ich nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After school I go home.

definitions.note: often used with reports, rules, or someone’s opinion (usually with dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Wetterbericht wird es morgen kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the weather report, it will be cold tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with a time expression (e.g., nach dem Essen = after eating / after the meal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Essen gehe ich spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the meal, I go for a walk.

definitions.note: Commonly used with destinations (e.g., nach Berlin). Not used before most countries with an article (e.g., in die Schweiz).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I'm going to Berlin.

definitions.note: Used with a dative noun/pronoun to indicate direction or destination.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fahren nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to Berlin.

definitions.note: Used with a dative noun/pronoun to mean “after” in time (later than).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Essen gehen wir spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the meal, we go for a walk.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a subordinate clause; often followed by past tense (Perfekt/Präteritum) for a completed earlier action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nachdem ich gegessen hatte, bin ich spazieren gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After I had eaten, I went for a walk.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of „nachdenken“; also identical in form to 1st person singular present indicative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich nachdenke und dann antworte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says I think about it and then answer.

definitions.note: Often used with „über“ + accusative: „über etwas nachdenken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss über deine Frage nachdenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to think about your question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sieht heute sehr nachdenklich aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looks very thoughtful today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder gehen nacheinander in die Klasse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children go into the classroom one after another.

definitions.note: Often used for giving in during an argument or negotiation, or for something physically/materially yielding under pressure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende hat er nachgeben müssen und ihr recht gegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end he had to give in and agreed that she was right.

definitions.note: Past participle of „nachdenken“, usually used with „haben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe lange nachgedacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about it for a long time.

definitions.note: Often used with "haben" in the perfect tense ("hat nachgegeben") to mean someone stopped resisting or pressure was reduced.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende hat er nachgegeben und zugestimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end he gave in and agreed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund versucht, der Katze nachgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is trying to follow the cat.

definitions.native: to follow up on, to investigate
definitions.note: Often used with a dative object like „einer Sache nachgehen“ (= to look into something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei wird dem Hinweis nachgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police will follow up on the tip.

definitions.note: Often used with things like pain, pressure, intensity, or wind/rain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schmerz hat nachgelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pain has let up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Angaben noch einmal nachgeprüft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rechecked the details once again.

definitions.note: Used with „haben“ in the perfect tense; often with „in/bei“ (e.g., im Wörterbuch) or with a direct object (e.g., die Adresse).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe im Wörterbuch nachgesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked it up in the dictionary.

definitions.note: Often used as „jemandem etwas nachsehen“ (= to forgive/overlook something in someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ihm den Fehler nachgesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She forgave him for the mistake.

definitions.note: often used after verbs of motion (e.g., gehen/kommen/fahren) in the sense of “(to) home”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe jetzt nachhause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going home now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich nachher an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you later.

definitions.native: to catch up (on something), to make up (for something)
definitions.note: Often used for making up missed work, classes, appointments, or sleep.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Unterricht nachholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to make up the class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund nachjagt der Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is chasing after the cat.

definitions.note: Often used with a noun in the dative, e.g. „einer Bitte / einer Aufforderung nachkommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde deiner Bitte nachkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will comply with your request.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder werden ihren Eltern nachkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children will follow their parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Akku nachladen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to recharge the battery.

definitions.note: Often used for not paying enough attention or being sloppy with duties/tasks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nachlässig mit seinen Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is careless with his homework.

definitions.note: Often used for copying someone’s actions, behavior, or an example (e.g., in school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte nachmachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please copy/imitate that?

definitions.note: Usually capitalized in German: „der Nachmittag“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Nachmittag gehe ich oft spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the afternoon, I often go for a walk.

definitions.note: Often used for habitual actions or general time of day (e.g., “nachmittags” = in the afternoons).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nachmittags mache ich oft einen Spaziergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the afternoon, I often go for a walk.

definitions.note: often means to check again or confirm something by looking it up or testing it
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Zahlen noch einmal nachprüfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to check the numbers again.

definitions.note: often used for looking up information in a dictionary or online
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Wort im Wörterbuch nachschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to look up the word in the dictionary.

definitions.note: Often used with "nachsehen" + "in" to mean checking information in a source (e.g., a book, an email, online).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde schnell im Wörterbuch nachsehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll quickly look it up in the dictionary.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase "etwas jemandem nachsehen" (= forgive someone for something, overlook a fault).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir den Fehler nachsehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can forgive you for the mistake.

definitions.note: Usually written with a capital letter in German: Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht ist es oft sehr still.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night it is often very quiet.

definitions.note: Often used with time expressions (e.g., nachts um drei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nachts ist es hier sehr ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night it is very quiet here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das nicht nachvollziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't understand that.

definitions.native: to think about it, to reflect
definitions.note: Used after verbs like „vergessen“, „versuchen“, „anfangen“ (zu + infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, darüber nachzudenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to think about it.

definitions.native: to give in, to give way, to yield
definitions.note: often used with „zu“ (as here) after verbs like „versuchen“, „aufhören“, „bereit sein“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat versucht, nicht nachzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried not to give in.

definitions.native: to catch up, to make up for (something missed)
definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used after another verb, e.g. "versuchen", "haben", "planen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, den Stoff von letzter Woche nachzuholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to catch up on last week’s material.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nackt im Badezimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is naked in the bathroom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schlafe nackt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sleep naked.

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine singular or plural nouns, or as a weak/strong ending in a noun phrase (e.g., 'die nackte Haut', 'nackte Füße')
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie bedeckte ihre nackte Haut mit einem Handtuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She covered her naked skin with a towel.

definitions.note: inflected form of "nackt" used before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei suchte nach dem nackten Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were looking for the naked man.

definitions.note: often used with "bei" (near) or "an" (close to/next to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Supermarkt ist ganz nah bei meiner Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supermarket is very near my apartment.

definitions.note: Often used with a form of "sein" (e.g., "Es ist nah.")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bahnhof ist ganz nah.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train station is very close by.

definitions.note: Often used with prepositions like "bei" or "an" (e.g., "nahe bei/nahe am" = near).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne nahe am Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live near the park.

definitions.note: Often used with "bei" or "an" (e.g., "nahe bei ...", "nahe an ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel ist nahe am Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is near the train station.

definitions.note: Used as a preposition with the dative case (often in more formal written German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen nahe dem Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live near the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne ganz nahe bei der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live very close to the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nahezu fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m almost finished.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „annehmen“; often used with the separable prefix „an“ (e.g., „nahm … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nahm das Angebot an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepted the offer.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „nehmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nahm den Bus zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took the bus to work.

definitions.note: Past tense (Präteritum) form of „annehmen“; in a sentence the prefix often splits off: „nahmen … an“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie nahmen das Angebot an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They accepted the offer.

definitions.note: Past tense (Präteritum) form of „annehmen“; in a sentence the prefix often splits off: „nahmen … an“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir nahmen an, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We assumed (supposed) that he would come today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie nahmen den Bus nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the bus home.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „teil“ (e.g. „nahmen … teil“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Studierende nahmen an dem Kurs teil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many students took part in the course.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe ist nahrhaft und schmeckt gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is nutritious and tastes good.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "nahen" (e.g., "er/sie/es naht" or "ihr naht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Herbst naht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Autumn is approaching.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist naiv zu glauben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s naive to believe.

definitions.note: Often used to show hesitation, mild doubt, or resignation (similar to “well…” or “oh well”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Naja, ich weiß nicht, ob das eine gute Idee ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, I don’t know if that’s a good idea.

definitions.native: on behalf of, in the name of
definitions.note: Used with the genitive, often in formal contexts (e.g., in letters or announcements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Namens der ganzen Klasse danke ich Ihnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On behalf of the whole class, I thank you.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „nennen“ (ich/er/sie/es nannte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nannte seinen Hund Max.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called his dog Max.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 1st/3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie nannten ihn einen Helden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called him a hero.

definitions.note: Expresses surprise or curiosity; often used when something is unexpected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nanu, wo ist denn mein Schlüssel?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Huh, where is my key then?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schuhe sind ganz nass.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are completely wet.

definitions.note: inflected form of „nass“, used (for example) before feminine nouns like „Straße“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die nasse Jacke ausgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took off the wet jacket.

definitions.note: used before a noun (inflected form of „nass“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ziehe die nassen Schuhe aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take off the wet shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine natürliche Reaktion.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a natural reaction.

definitions.note: Often used as a reply to mean “of course/sure” in conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Natürlich helfe ich dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of course I’ll help you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Natürlich komme ich heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of course I'm coming today.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (attributive); ending changes with gender/case
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche natürliche Zutaten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for natural ingredients.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in some cases (e.g., after articles/determiners)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir besuchen den natürlichen Park am Stadtrand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re visiting the natural park on the edge of the city.

definitions.note: Neuter singular form of the adjective (used before a neuter noun or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir suchen ein natürliches Shampoo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for a natural shampoo.

definitions.note: colloquial shortened form of "eine" (used mainly in spoken German)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ne Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an idea.

definitions.note: Colloquial sentence tag used to seek agreement; common in speech (especially in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kommst morgen, ne?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re coming tomorrow, right?

definitions.note: colloquial (spoken); used like a tag question (similar to „nicht wahr?“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kommst morgen, ne?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're coming tomorrow, right?

definitions.note: Used with the dative for location (where?), and with the accusative for direction/movement (where to?).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lampe steht neben dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp is next to the sofa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Nachbarn wohnen nebenan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors live next door.

definitions.native: on the side, by the way
definitions.note: Often used for something done in addition to the main activity or mentioned as an aside.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mache das nebenbei, wenn ich Zeit habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do that on the side when I have time.

definitions.native: next to each other, side by side
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Häuser stehen nebeneinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two houses stand next to each other.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute Morgen ist es sehr neblig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This morning it is very foggy.

definitions.note: Often used for light, playful teasing (not serious bullying).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will seine Schwester nur necken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He just wants to tease his sister.

definitions.note: informal; often used in spoken language
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nee, ich habe heute keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No, I don't have time today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ergebnisse sind leider negativ.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, the results are negative.

definitions.note: Adjective ending of "negativ" (e.g., after "eine").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine negative Erfahrung gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a negative experience.

definitions.note: Common spoken shortening of „nehme“ (as in „ich nehm“ = „ich nehme“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehm einen Kaffee, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have a coffee, please.

definitions.note: From the separable verb "annehmen"; in many sentences it appears split as "nehme … an".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme das Angebot an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accept the offer.

definitions.note: From the separable verb "annehmen"; often used as "Ich nehme an, dass …".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme an, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assume (that) he’s coming today.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I") of "nehmen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme den Bus zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take the bus to work.

definitions.note: Basic sense: to take (physically take/grab).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will das Buch nehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to take the book.

definitions.note: Common with public transport: take the bus/train, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen den Zug nehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will take the train.

definitions.native: to take (time) / to take a moment
definitions.note: Used in phrases about time: take time, take a moment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nimm dir Zeit; ich möchte dich etwas fragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take your time; I want to ask you something.

definitions.note: Used for taking medication.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst die Tabletten jeden Abend nehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to take the tablets every evening.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) command/imperative form of „nehmen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nehmt bitte eure Schuhe aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take off your shoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist neidisch auf seinen Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is jealous of his brother.

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ + noun/infinitive to mean “tends to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er neigt dazu, alles zu spät zu machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tends to do everything too late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nein, ich habe heute keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No, I don’t have time today.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „einen“ (masculine accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nen neuen Laptop gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new laptop.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative of „nennen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nenn mich bitte Anna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please call me Anna.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative (du) of „nennen“; also used colloquially as a shortened form of „nenne“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nenn mir bitte deinen Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell me your name.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present of "nennen" (ich nenne).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nenne meinen Hund Bruno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I call my dog Bruno.

definitions.note: Often used with two objects: jemanden (Akk.) + etwas (Akk.), e.g. „Ich nenne ihn Tom.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie nennen wir das Kind?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do we name the child?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of „nennen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie nennst du deinen Hund?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you call your dog?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "nennen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nennt seinen Hund Bruno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He calls his dog Bruno.

definitions.note: Imperative (du-form) of „nerven“; used in informal commands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nerv mich nicht!
