definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't annoy me!

definitions.native: to annoy, to get on someone’s nerves
definitions.note: Commonly used informally to mean “to bug/annoy (someone)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du solltest aufhören, mich zu nerven.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should stop annoying me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die laute Musik ist wirklich nervig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loud music is really annoying.

definitions.note: Informal; 2nd person singular (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du nervst mich gerade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're annoying me right now.

definitions.note: Commonly used in spoken German; can sound a bit blunt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das laute Geräusch nervt mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loud noise annoys me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin vor der Prüfung nervös.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m nervous before the exam.

definitions.note: Also commonly used as an adjective meaning “nervous.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war nervös, bevor ich die Prüfung geschrieben habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was nervous before I took the exam.

definitions.note: Often used for people or behavior; can also mean “pleasant” about things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist sehr nett von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s very nice of you.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone/something is pleasant or friendly; can also be used politely when making requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte nett sein und mir helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please be nice and help me?

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine singular nouns (e.g. „eine nette Frau“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine nette Nachbarin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a nice neighbor.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine accusative singular (e.g., "einen netten ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich treffe heute einen netten Kollegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m meeting a nice colleague today.

definitions.note: comparative form of "nett"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Bruder ist netter als du denkst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your brother is nicer than you think.

definitions.note: Form of the adjective "nett" used with a neuter noun (or as a nominalized adjective), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein nettes Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a nice gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein neues Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a new phone.

definitions.note: Often used adverbially to mean “again/from scratch” (e.g. etwas neu machen = to do something again/from scratch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Computer neu starten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to restart the computer.

definitions.note: Feminine singular or plural form of „neu“ (also used with nouns with no article, e.g. „Neue Bücher“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine neue Jacke gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new jacket.

definitions.note: Form of the adjective „neu“, used before feminine singular nouns (and also before plural nouns in some cases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine neue Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a new bag.

definitions.note: dative masculine or neuter singular form of "neu" (also used after certain prepositions like "mit")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit meinem neuem Handy kann ich besser Fotos machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With my new phone, I can take better photos.

definitions.note: inflected form of „neu“, used before a noun (e.g., „einen neuen …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe einen neuen Laptop.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying a new laptop.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (nominalized adjective) to refer to people who are new in a group, class, job, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sprechen mit den Neuen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re talking with the new people.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a masculine noun (e.g., „ein neuer …“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein neuer Lehrer kommt morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A new teacher is coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: comparative form of „neu“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Modell ist neuer als das alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This model is newer than the old one.

definitions.note: Used here as an adjective with a neuter noun (e.g., „ein neues Auto“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein neues Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a new phone.

definitions.note: As a noun it’s usually capitalized: „Neues“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gibt es etwas Neues?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is there anything new?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die neueste Version.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the latest version.

definitions.note: superlative form of „neu“; often used after a definite article (e.g., „die neuesten …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die neuesten Nachrichten gelesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the latest news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin neugierig, was passiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m curious what happens.

definitions.note: refers to a time not long ago (often within the last few days or weeks)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe neulich Anna in der Stadt getroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into Anna in town the other day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe neun Bücher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have nine books.

definitions.note: ordinal number (can be used as an adjective, e.g. with a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist der neunte Januar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is the ninth of January.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin neunzehn Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am nineteen years old.

definitions.note: Colloquial/informal pronunciation/spelling of „nicht“ (common in speech and chats).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute nich' viel Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have much time today.

definitions.note: Used to negate verbs, adjectives, or whole sentences (different from „kein“, which negates nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme heute nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not coming today.

definitions.note: Colloquial spelling of „nicht mal“ (also written „nichtmals“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nichtmal Zeit für einen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't even have time for a coffee.

definitions.note: Used as an indefinite pronoun meaning “nothing / not anything.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nichts verstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood nothing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see nothing.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „nicken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nickte und sagte nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He nodded and said nothing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das noch nie gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have never done that before.

definitions.note: Used as a cry or call (e.g., in slogans) meaning that something/someone should be brought down or overthrown.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nieder mit dem Krieg!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Down with the war!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean “down to the ground” (e.g. jemand fällt nieder = someone falls down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er fiel nieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell down.

definitions.native: to burn down (to the ground); to set fire to and destroy
definitions.note: Often used for deliberately burning something down completely.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Angreifer wollten das Dorf niederbrennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attackers wanted to burn the village down.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive verb "sich niederlassen" meaning to settle in a place (often permanently).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Studium hat sie sich in Hamburg niedergelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After her studies, she settled in Hamburg.

definitions.note: describes a person’s mood
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der schlechten Nachricht war sie völlig niedergeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bad news, she was completely depressed.

definitions.note: often used for teams or opponents in sports/competition
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mannschaft kehrte niedergeschlagen nach Hause zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team returned home defeated.

definitions.note: Describes feeling emotionally very upset (often after bad news).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als sie die Nachricht hörte, war sie völlig niedergeschmettert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When she heard the news, she was completely devastated.

definitions.note: Often used to mean stabbed badly or stabbed to death, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wurde vor dem Bahnhof niedergestochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was stabbed in front of the train station.

definitions.note: Very often used reflexively: sich niederlassen = to settle (somewhere), take up residence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Studium will er sich in Hamburg niederlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After his studies, he wants to settle down in Hamburg.

definitions.note: often used for small children, animals, or things that look sweet/charming
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist wirklich niedlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is really cute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist zu niedrig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is too low.

definitions.note: Often used for things like temperature, salary, prices, or numbers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Temperaturen sind heute sehr niedrig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The temperatures are very low today.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in weak/mixed declension (often after an article like „den“, „einen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben den niedrigen Tisch ins Wohnzimmer gestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put the low table in the living room.

definitions.note: comparative form of „niedrig“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Temperatur ist heute niedriger als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The temperature is lower today than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das niemals vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will never forget that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Niemand ist zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No one is home.

definitions.note: dative form of „niemand“ (used as an indirect object, often after certain prepositions)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe niemandem geholfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t help anyone.

definitions.note: Accusative form of „niemand“, used as a direct object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne niemanden in dieser Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know anyone in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss niesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to sneeze.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er niest schon den ganzen Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been sneezing all morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nieste gestern im Unterricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sneezed yesterday in class.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (du-form)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nimm bitte meinen Stift.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take my pen.

definitions.note: Very emphatic and poetic/old-fashioned; often used for dramatic effect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das nimmermehr tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will never do that again.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „nehmen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nimmst du heute den Bus zur Arbeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you taking the bus to work today?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „annehmen“; in main clauses, „an“ often goes to the end (e.g., „nimmt … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nimmt das Angebot an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accepts the offer.

definitions.note: Often used with „dass …“ or a question word clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie nimmt an, dass der Zug pünktlich ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She assumes that the train is on time.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „nehmen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nimmt jeden Morgen den Bus zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the bus to work every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann meine Schlüssel nirgends finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find my keys anywhere.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann meinen Schlüssel nirgendwo finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t find my key anywhere.

definitions.note: Used for direction: not going to any place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute nirgendwohin gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to go anywhere today.

definitions.note: informal (spoken); short for „nichts“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nix verstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood nothing.

definitions.note: Often used to say something continues (still) or hasn’t happened up to now (yet), especially with negation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still tired.

definitions.note: Commonly used before a noun with an article: „noch ein/eine …“ = “another …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche noch ein Glas Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need another glass of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still tired.

definitions.note: Often used with negatives (e.g., “noch nicht” = “not yet”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind noch nicht fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re not finished yet.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often interchangeable with „noch einmal“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das nochmal sagen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you say that again?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte nochmals sagen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please say that again?

definitions.note: Adjective in neuter nominative/accusative singular (strong or mixed declension), often used before a neuter noun (e.g., „nordisches Licht“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Himmel sehen wir nordisches Licht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the sky we see northern lights.

definitions.note: very informal; short for „normal“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du morgen? – Norm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming tomorrow? – Sure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ganz normal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s completely normal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Normal gehe ich nach der Arbeit noch einkaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Normally I go shopping after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine normale Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a normal question.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in some contexts (e.g., with accusative masculine/neuter after certain determiners, or plural in some cases)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinen normalen Kaffee mehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have any normal coffee left.

definitions.note: comparative form of "normal"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es normaler als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is more normal than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Normalerweise gehe ich um acht Uhr zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually go to work at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: adjective used in neuter nominative/accusative singular (e.g., with a neuter noun like „ein normales Auto“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein normales Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a normal problem.

definitions.note: Used to express a last resort or fallback option.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können notfalls ein Taxi nehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If necessary, we can take a taxi.

definitions.native: to note (something) down; to write (something) down
definitions.note: Used especially for quickly writing information down so you don’t forget it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich notiere die Adresse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I write down the address.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er notiert die wichtigsten Punkte im Heft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He notes down the most important points in the notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La notte è molto silenziosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The night is very quiet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist notwendig, dass du heute kommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is necessary that you come today.

definitions.note: Looks like English “null”, but in everyday German it’s the number 0.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist null Grad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is zero degrees.

definitions.native: to number; to label/mark with numbers
definitions.note: Often used for pages, seats, items, or steps in instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte numerieren Sie die Seiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please number the pages.

definitions.note: Often used to move a story or explanation forward (like “now,” “well then”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nun gehen wir nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Now we’re going home.

definitions.note: Often used as a conversational filler to introduce what comes next (e.g., a question, conclusion, or new point).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nun, was machen wir jetzt?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, what do we do now?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nur fünf Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have five euros.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I use").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nutze mein Handy nur am Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only use my phone in the evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann die App gut nutzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can use the app well.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., "etwas nutzen") or with "für" to indicate purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können das Angebot nutzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can benefit from the offer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Passwort ist das Konto nutzlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without a password, the account is useless.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „nutzen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nutzt sein Handy nur abends.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He uses his phone only in the evenings.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "nutzen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nutzte die Zeit, um Deutsch zu lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He used the time to learn German.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher nutzten wir ein Wörterbuch aus Papier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, we used a paper dictionary.

definitions.note: As a noun it’s usually capitalized: der/die Nächste (the next one/person). Often used when calling someone (e.g., in a line).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nächste, bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next, please!

definitions.note: Used with feminine nouns (e.g., die nächste Woche) and also with plural nouns (e.g., die nächsten Tage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächste Woche habe ich Urlaub.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next week I have vacation.

definitions.note: Often used with a definite article (e.g., „die nächste …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die nächste Station ist Hauptbahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The next stop is Central Station.

definitions.note: Colloquial spelling; more standard is „nächstes Mal“ (two words).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächstemal komme ich pünktlicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next time I'll be more punctual.

definitions.note: Often used in time expressions (e.g., with days, weeks, months).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme nächsten Dienstag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming next Tuesday.

definitions.note: Used with certain cases/articles (e.g., “nächsten Montag”, “in den nächsten Wochen”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme nächsten Montag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming next Monday.

definitions.note: Used to call the next person in a line (often without an article), e.g. at a counter or in a waiting room.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächster, bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next, please!

definitions.note: often used before a masculine noun (e.g., „nächster Halt“ = “next stop”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächster Halt: Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next stop: Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used with time expressions (e.g., „nächstes Jahr“ = “next year”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächstes Jahr besuche ich meine Großeltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next year I’m visiting my grandparents.

definitions.note: Used as the neuter form of „nächste“ (e.g., with „Jahr“, „Mal“, „Wochenende“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächstes Jahr fahre ich nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next year I’m going to Berlin.

definitions.note: often used to refer to the closest place/location (e.g., the nearest pharmacy, station, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo ist die nächstgelegene Apotheke?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is the nearest pharmacy?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute Abend nähen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to sew this evening.

definitions.note: comparative form of "nah"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte näher!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come closer!

definitions.note: comparative form of "nah" (near)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte näher!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come closer!

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich nähern + dative (e.g., sich dem Ziel nähern).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir nähern uns dem Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are approaching the train station.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of „nehmen“, used for hypothetical situations or polite suggestions/requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nähme ein Taxi, wenn es regnen würde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would take a taxi if it were going to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie näht einen Knopf an die Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sews a button onto the jacket.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „nähen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Oma nähte früher ihre Kleider selbst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma used to sew her clothes herself.

definitions.note: Used to specify or clarify something (often giving more detail after a statement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann heute nicht kommen, nämlich weil ich arbeiten muss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't come today, namely because I have to work.

definitions.note: In informal speech, it’s often used to introduce a reason (similar to “because”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin müde, ich habe nämlich schlecht geschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm tired because I slept badly.

definitions.note: Used to specify or explain something you just mentioned; often introduces more detail (can be like “that is” or “because,” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann heute nicht kommen, nämlich weil ich krank bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t come today, namely because I’m sick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Dorf liegt nördlich von Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village is north of Berlin.

definitions.note: Usually means complaining in an annoying, repetitive way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nörgelt ständig über das Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is constantly complaining about the weather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist nötig, dass wir jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is necessary that we leave now.

definitions.native: to force; to compel (someone to do something)
definitions.note: Usually used with an object + „zu“ + infinitive: „jemanden zu etwas nötigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef hat ihn dazu genötigt, am Wochenende zu arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss forced him to work on the weekend.

definitions.note: Implies strong pressure rather than a polite request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Umstände nötigen uns, sofort zu handeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The circumstances compel us to act immediately.

definitions.native: to oblige (someone); to make (someone) feel compelled
definitions.note: Can be used when someone feels compelled by a situation or social pressure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Worte nötigen mich, mich zu entschuldigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His words oblige me to apologize.

definitions.note: Often used for not being drunk; also commonly used for not having eaten yet (e.g., before a blood test).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nüchtern und kann noch fahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sober and can still drive.

definitions.note: Used when you haven’t eaten (e.g., before a medical test or when taking medicine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst für die Blutabnahme nüchtern sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to be fasting for the blood draw.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (jemandem): „Das nützen mir (nichts).“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Tipps können dir wirklich nützen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tips can really help you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch ist sehr nützlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very useful.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine singular nouns or plural nouns (e.g., „eine nützliche App“, „nützliche Tipps“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine nützliche App.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a useful app.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „nützlich“ (e.g., used before a noun after „einen“, „den“, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke für den nützlichen Tipp!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for the useful tip!

definitions.note: Nominalized adjective: used as a noun meaning “something useful” (often with an article, e.g. „etwas Nützliches“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir etwas Nützliches zeigen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me something useful?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „nützen“; often used with „(nichts)“ as in „Das nützt nichts.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das nützt mir sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That helps me a lot.

definitions.note: Often used in poetic or emotional language (e.g., addressing someone or expressing strong feeling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: O Gott, was ist passiert?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh God, what happened?

definitions.note: Used to introduce an indirect yes/no question (often translated as “whether”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß nicht, ob er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know whether he is coming today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Brand war die Familie obdachlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the fire, the family was homeless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tassen stehen oben im Schrank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cups are up in the cupboard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nimm bitte die obere Schublade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take the upper drawer.

definitions.note: used as an inflected form of the adjective „ober“ (e.g., after a definite article or in certain cases)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen im oberen Stockwerk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live on the upper floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Interesse an Politik ist eher oberflächlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His interest in politics is rather superficial.

definitions.note: Superlative form used before a noun (e.g., with feminine nouns or in plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die oberste Etage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the top floor.

definitions.note: often used with nouns like "Etage" (floor) or "Stockwerk" (storey) to mean the one at the very top
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen in der obersten Etage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live on the top floor.

definitions.note: often used for opinions, reporting, or assessments.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen bei der Bewertung objektiv bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to remain objective in the evaluation.

definitions.native: is incumbent on, is the responsibility of
definitions.note: Formal/official wording, usually used with dative (e.g. „Es obliegt mir …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es obliegt der Stadt, die Straßen zu reparieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is the city’s responsibility to repair the streets.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe spazieren, obwohl es regnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going for a walk although it’s raining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möchtest du Tee oder Kaffee?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like tea or coffee?

definitions.note: Can also mean "open" in a figurative sense (e.g., open-minded, open about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist offen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is open.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „lassen“, „stehen“, „sagen“ (e.g. „die Tür offen lassen“ = to leave the door open).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lass bitte das Fenster offen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please leave the window open.

definitions.note: Often used when something seems clear from evidence or what you observe; it can also mean you’re making an assumption based on information you have.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat offenbar den Termin vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently, he forgot the appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bericht offenbart neue Details.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report reveals new details.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (e.g. feminine or plural, depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe eine offene Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see an open door.

definitions.note: Dative singular masculine/neuter form of "offen" (used after dative articles like "mit", "bei", "zu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit offenem Fenster ist es zu kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With an open window, it’s too cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schließe die offenen Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m closing the open windows.

definitions.note: past participle of „offenlassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Fenster offengelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the window open.

definitions.note: Often used with doors, windows, or options (e.g., keeping possibilities open).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte die Tür offenhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to keep the door open.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist offensichtlich, dass er nicht die Wahrheit sagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is obvious that he is not telling the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat offensichtlich den Termin vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He obviously forgot the appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die offizielle Version des Berichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the official version of the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ergebnisse sind noch nicht offiziell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The results are not official yet.

definitions.note: adjective form used with nouns (e.g., feminine singular or plural, depending on the noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die offizielle Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the official answer.

definitions.note: Adjective ending often used with feminine nouns (e.g., „die offizielle Einladung“) or in plural with „die“ (e.g., „die offizielleN Regeln“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die offizielle Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the official answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe oft nach der Arbeit spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often go for a walk after work.

definitions.note: Slightly more formal/literary than the very common "oft".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich oftmals über das Wetter beschwert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often complained about the weather.

definitions.note: used to show surprise, realization, disappointment, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oh, das habe ich nicht gewusst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh, I didn't know that.

definitions.note: Preposition that usually takes the accusative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke meinen Kaffee ohne Milch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink my coffee without milk.

definitions.note: Used in clauses like „ohne dass …“ or „ohne zu …“ (“without (that) … / without doing …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ging, ohne dass er sich verabschiedete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left without saying goodbye.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollte ohnehin heute zu Hause bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to stay at home today anyway.

definitions.note: Often used with "werden" (to become) or "sein" (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall war er ohnmächtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was unconscious.

definitions.note: Past tense form of "ohrfeigen"; usually implies a slap across the cheek.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ohrfeigte ihn vor allen Leuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slapped him in the face in front of everyone.

definitions.note: An interjection used to express worry, dismay, or regret (often mildly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oje, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh no, I forgot my key.

definitions.note: Common in spoken and informal German; can also be used as an adverb ("Das ist ok.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alles ist ok.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is okay.

definitions.note: Commonly used in informal speech and texting; also written as „OK“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ok, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: OK, I’ll be there in a moment.

definitions.note: Often used informally as an adjective to mean something is acceptable or fine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist es für dich okay, wenn wir um acht anfangen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is it okay for you if we start at eight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Okay, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, I'll come in a moment.

definitions.native: “one” (English for “one”; used in German especially in product names, slogans, or casual Denglisch)
definitions.note: Not standard German; appears as an English word in otherwise German contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir noch one Minute geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me one more minute?

definitions.note: Used as part of an official name; in German it’s typically kept in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir gestern eine Xbox one gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I bought an Xbox One.

definitions.native: “the one” / the chosen one (as a title in English within German texts)
definitions.note: Often used in quotes or as a nickname/title; stylistic/English usage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle nennen ihn nur one, weil er immer gewinnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone just calls him “one” because he always wins.

definitions.note: Often used unchanged in German, especially for internet-related things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Abend online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll be online this evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm online right now.

definitions.note: Usually used for medical surgery (someone is operated on: „jemanden operieren“; the surgeon operates: „operieren“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt muss sie morgen operieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor has to operate on her tomorrow.

definitions.note: medical context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt operiert den Patienten am Knie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor operates on the patient’s knee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen opfern ihre Freizeit für die Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people sacrifice their free time for work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum opferst du so viel Zeit für dieses Projekt?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you sacrificing so much time for this project?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er opferte viel Zeit für das Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sacrificed a lot of time for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin optimistisch, dass alles gut wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m optimistic that everything will turn out well.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „optisch“; used before a noun (e.g. „optische Täuschung“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine optische Täuschung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an optical illusion.

definitions.note: As a color adjective, it often stays the same (especially after „sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jacke ist orange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jacket is orange.

definitions.note: adjective ending; used before a noun (e.g., with a definite article: die orangefarbene …)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die orangefarbene Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the orange-colored jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Zimmer ist heute wirklich ordentlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your room is really tidy today.

definitions.note: Often used to describe appropriate behavior or something done in a correct way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte benimm dich ordentlich im Unterricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please behave properly in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte räum dein Zimmer ordentlich auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tidy up your room properly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine ordentliche Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a tidy apartment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keinen ordentlichen Stift.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have a proper pen.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone/something as well-behaved or respectable (not just physically tidy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein ordentlicher Schüler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a well-behaved student.

definitions.native: to arrange; to put in order; to sort
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ordnen die Bücher nach Themen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrange the books by topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde den Ausflug morgen organisieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will organize the trip tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er organisiert das Treffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He organizes the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Fest ist gut organisiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party is well organized.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr gut organisiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very well organized.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall war er völlig orientierungslos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was completely disoriented.

definitions.note: Often used for copies, translations, or adaptations that closely follow the original.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Übersetzung ist sehr originalgetreu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The translation is very faithful to the original.

definitions.note: often used for finding the position of something (e.g., a signal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei konnte das Handy-Signal orten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were able to locate the phone signal.

definitions.note: Interjection often used as a signal that something is finished (e.g., after a task or in a game).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Okay, over!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, over!

definitions.note: Used with plural nouns, often with "ein" (ein paar = a few).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein paar Fragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a few questions.

definitions.note: colloquial; often written as “ein paar Mal”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war schon paarmal dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've been there a few times already.

definitions.note: Often used as part of the phrase „ein paarmal“ (= „ein paar Mal“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war schon ein paarmal dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already been there a few times.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial (often used instead of „packe!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pack das bitte in deinen Rucksack.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put that in your backpack, please.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "packen" ("ich packe" = "I pack").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich packe meinen Koffer für die Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pack my suitcase for the trip.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „aus“ (e.g. „Wir packen … aus.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir packen die Kisten aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We unpack the boxes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute meinen Koffer packen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pack my suitcase today.

definitions.note: Often used for grabbing something quickly or firmly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst mich nicht so fest packen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You mustn't grab me that hard.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Packst du bitte die Tasche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you pack the bag, please?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „auspacken“; in a main clause it appears as „packt … aus“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er packt den Koffer aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He unpacks the suitcase.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er packt seinen Koffer für die Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He packs his suitcase for the trip.

definitions.note: Simple past of the separable verb „auspacken“; the prefix often goes to the end of the sentence (… packte … aus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie packte den Koffer aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She unpacked the suitcase.

definitions.note: simple past of „einpacken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie packte die Kleidung in den Koffer ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She packed the clothes into the suitcase.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "packen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich packte meine Tasche für die Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I packed my bag for the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Prozesse laufen parallel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two processes run in parallel.

definitions.note: Often used as a predicate adjective: „bereit/parat sein“ = to be ready.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bist du parat?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you ready?

definitions.note: Often used as a polite way to ask someone to repeat what they said, or when you want to get past someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pardon, können Sie das bitte wiederholen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, could you please repeat that?

definitions.note: first-person singular present (ich) of „parken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich parke das Auto vor dem Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I park the car in front of the house.

definitions.note: usually used for vehicles (e.g., cars)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier darfst du nicht parken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re not allowed to park here.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "parken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er parkt das Auto vor dem Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He parks the car in front of the house.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "parken"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern parkte ich vor dem Supermarkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I parked in front of the supermarket.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative of „aufpassen“, usually used with „auf“ (e.g. „Pass auf!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, da kommt ein Auto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, a car is coming!

definitions.note: Usually used with the separable prefix „auf“: „Ich passe auf.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich passe auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m paying attention.

definitions.note: Often used to say something fits (size) or suits/matches (goes well).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich passe nicht in diese Hose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t fit into these pants.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „auf“ (aufpassen): „passen … auf“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Passen Sie auf, es ist rutschig!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, it’s slippery!

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „auf“ (aufpassen): „passen … auf“ + accusative object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir passen heute Abend auf die Kinder auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking after the kids this evening.

definitions.note: Often used with “zu” or “in” (e.g., “zu mir”, “in die Tasche”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schuhe passen mir gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes fit me well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein passendes Geschenk für sie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a suitable gift for her.

definitions.note: Form of „passend“ used before a noun (e.g., „eine passende …“, „passende …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine passende Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a suitable solution.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was wird passieren, wenn wir zu spät kommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What will happen if we arrive too late?

definitions.note: often with an object: an jemandem / an etwas passieren
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sehen das Museum, wenn wir daran passieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We see the museum when we pass by it.

definitions.note: common in travel/controls: die Kontrolle passieren
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich konnte die Sicherheitskontrolle schnell passieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was able to get through security quickly.

definitions.note: Often used in questions like „Was ist passiert?“ = “What happened?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was ist passiert?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What happened?

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "passieren"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern passierte etwas Seltsames.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday something strange happened.

definitions.note: From the verb „anpassen“; it’s often used with a direct object (what is being adjusted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er passt den Plan an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He adjusts the plan.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufpassen“ (the „auf“ often goes to the end of the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er passt im Unterricht gut auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pays attention well in class.

definitions.note: Often used to say something fits (size) or works/works for you (plans).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jacke passt mir gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jacket fits me well.

definitions.note: Simple past of „passen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jacke passte mir nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jacket didn’t fit me.

definitions.note: In German, it often means “melodramatic” or “overly sentimental,” not “moving” in a positive sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine pathetische Rede hat viele im Publikum genervt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His melodramatic speech annoyed many people in the audience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat pausenlos gearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He worked nonstop.

definitions.note: relating to the Pacific (Ocean)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Inseln liegen im pazifischen Ozean.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many islands are located in the Pacific Ocean.

definitions.note: Old spelling of the imperative "Pass!" (from "aufpassen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Paß auf, da kommt ein Fahrrad!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, a bicycle is coming!

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufpassen“; in a full sentence the prefix often appears at the end (… „paßt … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er paßt im Straßenverkehr immer gut auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always pays close attention in traffic.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "passen"; also commonly written "passt" (new spelling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jacke paßt mir gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jacket fits me well.

definitions.note: Often used as an exclamation (usually written with a capital letter: “Pech!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pech! Jetzt hat es angefangen zu regnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bad luck! Now it’s started to rain.

definitions.note: Often used for situations, mistakes, or behavior that causes embarrassment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war mir total peinlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was totally embarrassing for me.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is awkward or embarrassing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war mir peinlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was embarrassing for me.

definitions.note: In modern German, peinlich usually means “embarrassing/awkward” (it may look related to English “pain,” but that’s not the common meaning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine peinliche Situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an embarrassing situation.

definitions.note: Sound effect for a sudden loud noise (e.g., a shot or explosion); often used in comics or jokingly in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Und dann: Peng! war die Tür zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: And then: Bang! the door slammed shut.

definitions.note: informal, colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute früh pennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sleep early today.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like delivery, transport, or communication methods (e.g., per E-Mail, per Post).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schicke dir die Unterlagen per E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll send you the documents by email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist perfekt für mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is perfect for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das passt perfekt zu dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That suits you perfectly.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine singular or with plural nouns (e.g., after “die”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die perfekte Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the perfect solution.

definitions.note: adjective inflection (masculine accusative singular or plural in some contexts)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche den perfekten Moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for the perfect moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein perfektes Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a perfect gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist permanent geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is permanently closed.

definitions.note: Often used for things relating to a person, or for face-to-face contact (e.g., „persönlich sprechen“).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to discuss that with you in person.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne ihn persönlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know him personally.

definitions.note: adjective inflected form (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist meine persönliche Meinung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my personal opinion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen persönlichen Brief bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I received a personal letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr pessimistisch und erwartet immer das Schlimmste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very pessimistic and always expects the worst.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal imperative (command), like “Pfeif!” = “Whistle!”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann sehr laut pfeifen.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird whistles every morning in front of the window.

definitions.note: first-person singular present tense ("I plant")

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planting tomatoes in the garden tomorrow.

definitions.note: usually used for putting plants (e.g., flowers, trees) into the ground
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir pflanzen im Garten Tomaten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We plant tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.note: present tense (ihr) or 3rd person singular (er/sie/es)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er pflanzt Tomaten im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He plants tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „pflanzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr pflanzte sie einen Baum im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year she planted a tree in the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr pflanzten wir Tomaten im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year we planted tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for caring for a person (e.g., in nursing/caregiving).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie pflegen ihre Großmutter zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take care of their grandmother at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir pflegen gute Kontakte zu unseren Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We maintain good contact with our neighbors.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She takes care of her sick mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher pflegte er jeden Sonntag seine Großmutter zu besuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past, he used to visit his grandmother every Sunday.

definitions.note: Usually used for picking fruit, flowers, or similar things by hand.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pick a flower.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „pflücken“.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She picks a flower in the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „pflücken“, often used for picking flowers or fruit by hand

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She picked a rose in the garden.

definitions.note: An exclamation of strong disgust or disapproval.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yuck, that stinks!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert war phänomenal!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was phenomenal!

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re having a picnic in the park today.

definitions.note: Often describes someone who is very particular about small details (e.g., cleanliness or how things are done).

definitions.note: adjective form (inflected), e.g. before a feminine noun

definitions.note: vulgar/very informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss pissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pee.

definitions.note: Often used for something that keeps worrying or afflicting someone over time (e.g., fears, worries, an illness).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This worry has been bothering him for weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m planning a trip to Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir planen eine Reise nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re planning a trip to Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug fährt heute planmäßig ab.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "planen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was planst du für das Wochenende?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you planning for the weekend?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er plant eine Reise nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He plans a trip to Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „planen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich plante eine Reise nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planned a trip to Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Reifen ist platt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tire is flat.

definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Arbeit bin ich total platt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I'm totally exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder spielen mit einem platten Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are playing with a flat ball.

definitions.note: Often used for things like balloons, bubbles, or pipes bursting.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon can pop at any time.

definitions.note: Often used with clothing or seams: "Die Naht kann platzen."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich mich bücke, kann die Naht an der Hose platzen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ballon platzt!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon pops!

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „platzen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ballon platzte plötzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon suddenly burst.

definitions.note: usually means talking in a relaxed, informal way

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We chat a little longer at the café.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean someone has no money; also used for companies meaning insolvent.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll have the salad, plus a soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich fing es an zu regnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly it started to rain.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a feminine noun or (in some cases) a plural noun
