definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sudden change surprised everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hatte einen plötzlichen Schmerz im Rücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had a sudden pain in his back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein plötzlicher Regen überraschte uns.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A sudden rain shower surprised us.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts like war, riots, or burglary (taking things by force or illegally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Sturm begannen einige Leute, die verlassenen Häuser zu plündern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, some people began to loot the abandoned houses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er poliert die Schuhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He polishes the shoes.

definitions.note: adjective form used with feminine singular nouns (nominative/accusative) and with plural nouns in all cases in many common patterns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind politische Themen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are political topics.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak inflection form (often after articles like „den/die/das“ or demonstratives like „diesen“), e.g. masculine accusative or plural dative/genitive depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir diskutieren den politischen Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are discussing the political plan.

definitions.note: Used with a neuter singular noun (or as a nominalized adjective), e.g., „ein politisches Thema“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein politisches Thema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a political topic.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with feminine nouns or in some plural contexts, depending on the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne die polnische Sprache.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning the Polish language.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sänger ist in Deutschland sehr populär.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The singer is very popular in Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht ist positiv.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news is positive.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “in a positive way” or “favorably,” especially with verbs like klingen (to sound) or reagieren (to react).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das klingt positiv.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That sounds positive.

definitions.note: adjective ending (-e), e.g. after a definite article (die/der/das).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine positive Einstellung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a positive attitude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen eine pragmatische Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a pragmatic solution.

definitions.note: Often used with "mit" to say what someone is boasting about ("mit etwas prahlen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er prahlt mit seinem neuen Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He brags about his new car.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ + dative to say what someone is bragging about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er prahlte mit seinem neuen Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bragged about his new car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine praktische Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a practical solution.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Supermarkt ist praktisch um die Ecke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supermarket is conveniently just around the corner.

definitions.note: Often also used to mean "conveniently" or "usefully" in everyday German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Praktisch kann ich heute nicht kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Practically speaking, I can’t come today.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine accusative or plural (e.g., after "einen" or "die")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche einen praktischen Rucksack für die Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a practical backpack for the trip.

definitions.note: simple past of "prallen"; often used with "gegen" (against) or "auf" (into/onto)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball prallte gegen die Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball bounced off the wall.

definitions.note: Often used in a religious context (e.g., a pastor in church); can also be used figuratively for moralizing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Pfarrer muss jeden Sonntag predigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pastor has to preach every Sunday.

definitions.native: to reveal, to disclose, to give away (information/secret)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will nicht preisgeben, wo er das Geld versteckt hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't want to reveal where he hid the money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel ist sauber und preiswert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is clean and good value (inexpensive).

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist prima!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That's great!

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist prima!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s great!

definitions.note: Often used as an enthusiastic reaction, like “great!” or “awesome!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prima, dann können wir jetzt losgehen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Great, then we can head off now!

definitions.note: Often used to mean “in one’s private life” (not at work / not official).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich telefoniere lieber privat als im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer to make phone calls privately rather than in the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine private Angelegenheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a private matter.

definitions.note: Used here as an adjective with a weak ending (-en), e.g., after a definite article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schreibt einen privaten Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is writing a private letter.

definitions.note: Used in measurements and rates (e.g., euros per person, kilometers per hour).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kostet zehn Euro pro Person.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That costs ten euros per person.

definitions.note: Used to express being in favor of something, often in “pro und contra”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin pro Umweltschutz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in favor of environmental protection.

definitions.note: often used for theater, music, or dance rehearsals
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen heute Abend proben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to rehearse this evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen die neue Software erst proben, bevor wir sie benutzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to test the new software first before we use it.

definitions.note: informal command (du-imperative) of „probieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Probier das neue Eis!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try the new ice cream!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (or imperative, informal) of "probieren".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich probiere das neue Rezept heute aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying out the new recipe today.

definitions.note: Often used with "etwas probieren" = to try something (also: to taste something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute ein neues Rezept probieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to try a new recipe today.

definitions.note: Often used with food/drink meaning “tries/tastes (something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er probiert den Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries the cake.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „probieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich probierte die Suppe und fügte dann Salz hinzu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried the soup and then added salt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Lösung ist problematisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This solution is problematic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma produziert Elektroautos in Deutschland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company produces electric cars in Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film wurde in Berlin produziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The film was produced in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wirkt in dem Gespräch sehr professionell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She seems very professional in the conversation.

definitions.note: adjective; this form is used with a noun (e.g., after an article) in feminine singular or in plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine professionelle Ausbildung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a professional education/training.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "professionell".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein neuer Lebenslauf sieht professioneller aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your new résumé looks more professional.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute lange programmieren, um das Projekt fertigzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to program for a long time today to finish the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Software ist bereits programmiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The software is already programmed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er programmiert jeden Tag eine Stunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He programs for an hour every day.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used as a loanword, especially in phrases like „Alles pronto!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bist du pronto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you ready?

definitions.note: said when raising glasses for a toast
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prost! Auf deine Gesundheit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cheers! To your health!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen protestieren gegen die neuen Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people are protesting against the new rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er protestiert gegen die neuen Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He protests against the new rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er protestierte gegen die neuen Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He protested against the new rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Studierenden protestierten gegen die neuen Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students protested against the new rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will mich nicht beleidigen, er will mich nur provozieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't want to insult me; he just wants to provoke me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er provoziert mich ständig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He provokes me all the time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schloss ist prächtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle is splendid.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a neuter noun (e.g., with “ein …es” or “das …e”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sehen ein prächtiges Schloss am Fluss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We see a magnificent castle by the river.

definitions.note: Often used for giving a talk or showing something (e.g., results, a product) to an audience.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute werde ich unsere Ergebnisse präsentieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I will present our results.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sei präzise und gib mir die genaue Uhrzeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be precise and tell me the exact time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte erklären Sie das präzise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please explain that precisely.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I"); also used as the informal (du) imperative: "Check!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich prüfe die Antwort noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I check the answer once more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Antworten noch einmal prüfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to check the answers one more time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte prüfen Sie die Angaben in diesem Formular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please verify the information in this form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Techniker wird die Maschine morgen prüfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The technician will inspect the machine tomorrow.

definitions.note: often used for oral or written exams
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin wird die Klasse am Freitag prüfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher will test the class on Friday.

definitions.note: Often used for hitting someone repeatedly, including in a fight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jungen fangen an, sich auf dem Schulhof zu prügeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys start to fight (beat each other up) in the schoolyard.

definitions.note: used to ask someone to be quiet
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pscht! Das Baby schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shh! The baby is sleeping.

definitions.note: Used to get someone’s attention quietly (like a hush or whisper).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pst, komm mal her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Psst, come here for a moment!

definitions.note: Usually describes a person in a mildly humorous or somewhat informal way; it can be sensitive depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der kleine Junge ist ein bisschen pummelig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The little boy is a bit chubby.

definitions.note: This form is the informal (du) imperative of "putzen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Putz bitte deine Schuhe, bevor du reinkommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please clean your shoes before you come in.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "putzen" (ich putze).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich putze heute die Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cleaning the kitchen today.

definitions.note: Often used for cleaning rooms/surfaces; also common with teeth (Zähne putzen) and shoes (Schuhe putzen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute die Küche putzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to clean the kitchen today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „putzen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er putzt die Küche nach dem Abendessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cleans the kitchen after dinner.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "putzen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern putzte ich die Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I cleaned the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sei morgen pünktlich um 8 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be on time tomorrow at 8 o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug kommt heute pünktlich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train arrives on time today.

definitions.note: usually used for ducks/frogs, or for a person speaking in an annoying/nasal way
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Enten quaken am Teich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ducks are quacking at the pond.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist qualifiziert für diese Stelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is qualified for this position.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe quasi keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have practically no time.

definitions.note: Used to reject what someone just said (like “That’s nonsense!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quatsch! Das stimmt nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nonsense! That’s not true.

definitions.note: informal/colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich quatsch kurz mit meiner Nachbarin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chat briefly with my neighbor.

definitions.note: informal; often means talking casually (sometimes a bit too much or about nothing important)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir quatschen nach der Arbeit noch ein bisschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We chat for a bit after work.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum quatschst du so lange mit ihm?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you chatting with him for so long?

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du quatschst doch!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're talking nonsense!

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is positioned or moving across/through something (e.g., across the street).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen quer über die Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking across the street.

definitions.note: Often used for things lying or placed at an angle rather than straight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stuhl steht quer im Raum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair is standing crosswise in the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür kann manchmal richtig quietschen, wenn ich sie öffne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door can sometimes really squeak when I open it.

definitions.note: used as an adjective (present participle) describing something that squeaks
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto fuhr mit quietschenden Reifen um die Kurve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car went around the curve with squealing tires.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „mit jemandem quitt sein“ (to be even with someone) or „quitt sein“ after paying a debt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jetzt sind wir quitt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Now we're even.

definitions.note: Simple past of „quellen“; often used for liquids or something swelling up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus der Wunde quoll Blut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Blood welled up from the wound.

definitions.note: Often used for causing someone (or yourself) severe emotional or physical suffering.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gedanke kann ihn die ganze Nacht quälen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thought can torment him all night.

definitions.note: 2nd-person singular informal (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum quälst du dich so sehr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you tormenting yourself so much?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „quälen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm quält ihn jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise torments him every day.

definitions.note: Simple past form of "quälen" (to torment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm quälte ihn die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise tormented him all night.

definitions.native: to ride a bike, to cycle
definitions.note: Often used with the separable prefix form: „Ich fahre Rad.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Wochenende gehe ich gern radfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the weekend I like to go cycling.

definitions.note: past participle of „radfahren“, used with „sein“ (e.g. „ich bin … radgefahren“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern zur Schule radgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cycled to school yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something ingeniously designed or done in a subtle, skillful way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine raffinierte Lösung für das Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a clever solution to the problem.

definitions.note: Often used for putting a picture or photo into a frame.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir rahmen das Foto ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We frame the photo.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used as a shortened form of „heran/dran“ in phrases like „Komm ran!“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm ran, ich zeige es dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come over, I’ll show it to you.

definitions.note: Often used as a directional particle with verbs (e.g. ran gehen/ran kommen) meaning movement closer to something/someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm ran!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come over here! / Come closer!

definitions.native: completely full, filled to the brim
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas ist randvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is completely full.

definitions.native: to approach, to go up to
definitions.note: Often used with "an" (e.g. "an jemanden/etwas rangehen"); fairly informal/colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht an den Hund rangehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to go up to the dog.

definitions.native: to tackle, to deal with (a task/problem)
definitions.note: Often used with "an" (e.g. "an eine Aufgabe rangehen"); fairly informal/colloquial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Problem jetzt ruhig und systematisch rangehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to tackle the problem calmly and systematically now.

definitions.note: simple past of "rennen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rannte nach Hause, weil es regnete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ran home because it was raining.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural (they) and also polite form (you)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie rannten schnell zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They ran quickly to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte rapide antworten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please answer quickly?

definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem starken Kaffee war ich wieder rappelvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the strong coffee, I was wide awake again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine ziemlich rare Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a pretty strange idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte rasch kommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come quickly, please?

definitions.note: Often implies going very fast (sometimes dangerously), e.g. in a car.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto kann rasen, wenn die Straße frei ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car can speed when the road is clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war rasend vor Wut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was furious with anger.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something moving extremely fast (e.g., a car, a train).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein rasendes Auto fuhr an uns vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A speeding car drove past us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sahen den rasenden Zug vorbeifahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw the speeding train go past.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present: “I shave” (also used as a polite command: “shave!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rasiere mich jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shave every morning.

definitions.note: often used reflexively: sich rasieren = to shave (oneself)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich jeden Morgen rasieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to shave every morning.

definitions.note: can be used with a direct object (e.g., a client or an area of hair)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Friseur wird den Kunden rasieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The barber will shave the customer.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "rasieren".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum rasierst du dich heute nicht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you shave today?

definitions.note: Used for the verb "rasieren" (to shave); depending on context, "rasiert" can be present tense (he/she shaves) or past participle (shaved).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rasiert sich jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shaves every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist heute rasiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is clean-shaven today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rasierte sich jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shaved every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der langen Fahrt rast du kurz an der Raststätte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long drive, you take a short break at the rest stop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto raste durch die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car sped through the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rastete kurz am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rested briefly by the lake.

definitions.note: Often used like “I guess …”. (Not the same as English “to rate”.)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll guess: You’re tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rate dir, früher ins Bett zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advise you to go to bed earlier.

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the dative + „zu“ + infinitive: „Ich rate dir, ...“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir nur raten, früher ins Bett zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All I can do is advise you to go to bed earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du raten, wie alt sie ist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you guess how old she is?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ratet die Antwort richtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He guesses the answer correctly.

definitions.note: Often used with “jemandem (zu etwas) raten” = to advise someone (to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ratet ihm, früher zu schlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She advises him to sleep earlier.

definitions.note: Often used with "Es ist ratsam, ..." ("It is advisable to ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist ratsam, früh zu buchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is advisable to book early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wand ist rau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wall is rough.

definitions.note: Often used for taking things by force (e.g., in a robbery); more formal than everyday “stehlen” (“to steal”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Täter wollte der Frau die Handtasche rauben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrator wanted to rob the woman of her handbag.

definitions.note: Can also be used figuratively to mean “takes away” (e.g., time, sleep).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb raubt Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief steals money.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „rauben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er raubte der alten Frau die Handtasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He robbed the old woman of her handbag.

definitions.note: As a verb form of „rauchen“; can mean smoking cigarettes or producing smoke (e.g., a chimney).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Küche rauch es.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s smoke in the kitchen.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I smoke").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rauche nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't smoke.

definitions.note: Usually refers to smoking cigarettes or other tobacco products.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will nicht rauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to smoke.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rauchst du hier drinnen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you smoke in here?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er raucht jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He smokes every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „rauchen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rauchte früher jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He smoked every day in the past.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der raue Wind macht meine Haut trocken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The harsh wind makes my skin dry.

definitions.note: Colloquial form of "herauf/hinauf"; often used with verbs of movement (e.g., raufgehen, raufkommen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm rauf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come up!

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often interchangeable with "hinauf" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm rauf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come up!

definitions.note: often used for rough fighting or scuffling (e.g., kids or animals)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jungs raufen sich auf dem Schulhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys are fighting on the schoolyard.

definitions.note: colloquial for „hinaufgehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir raufgehen die Treppe zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go up the stairs together.

definitions.note: often used with things like prices or temperatures
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn die Nachfrage steigt, können die Preise raufgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When demand rises, prices can go up.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; short for „heraus“/„hinaus“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte raus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go out!

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often means “outside” or “(go/get) out!” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Raus aus dem Zimmer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Out of the room!

definitions.note: Colloquial form of „heraus“; often used with verbs like „gehen/kommen“ (to go/come out) or as an imperative: „Raus!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh raus und spiel im Garten!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go out and play in the garden!

definitions.note: colloquial short form of „heraus“; often used as a separable particle (e.g., „rausgehen“) or in commands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh raus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go out!

definitions.note: colloquial for „herausbekommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will rausbekommen, warum er nicht kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to find out why he isn’t coming.

definitions.note: often used with stains/dirt: „einen Fleck rausbekommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Fleck aus dem T-Shirt rausbekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get the stain out of the T-shirt.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „herausfinden“; separable verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch rausfinden, wann der Zug abfährt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still need to find out when the train leaves.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball ist aus dem Fenster rausgeflogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball flew out of the window.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean someone was forced to leave (e.g., from a club, school, or job).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist aus der Schule rausgeflogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got kicked out of school.

definitions.note: colloquial form of „herausgefunden“ (past participle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es rausgefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found it out.

definitions.note: Colloquial form; from "rausgehen" (= "to go out").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schon rausgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has already gone out.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often interchangeable with „hinausgehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss kurz rausgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go outside for a moment.

definitions.note: past participle of „rausholen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Schlüssel aus der Tasche rausgeholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the key out of my pocket.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present of „rausgehen“; separable verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum rausgehst du so früh?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you going out so early?

definitions.note: Past participle of "rauskommen"; often used with "sein" (e.g., "ist rausgekommen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze ist endlich rausgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat finally came out.

definitions.note: Used for results or information becoming known.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende ist alles anders rausgekommen als geplant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, everything turned out differently than planned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Katze rausgelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I let the cat out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Namen extra rausgelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I deliberately left out the name.

definitions.note: Colloquial; can also mean “fired” (from a job).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Türsteher hat ihn rausgeschmissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bouncer kicked him out.

definitions.note: Often used informally; can also mean “fired” from a job, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde rausgeschmissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got kicked out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde aus der Bar rausgeworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was thrown out of the bar.

definitions.note: Separable verb: rausholen → holt ... raus.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte den Müll rausholen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please take out the trash?

definitions.note: informal for „herauskommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du kurz rauskommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come out for a moment?

definitions.note: used when talking about how something ends up/result
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende kann es ganz anders rauskommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end it can turn out completely differently.

definitions.note: Colloquial for „herauskommst“ (from „herauskommen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du nach der Pause wieder rauskommst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming back out again after the break?

definitions.native: turn out, come out (as a result)
definitions.note: Often used to talk about how something ends up or what the result is.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass du gut rauskommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope things turn out well for you.

definitions.note: Often used for results or what you discover (“it turns out that …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende rauskommt, dass wir uns geirrt haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, it turns out that we were wrong.

definitions.note: informal; separable verb (raus- + kriegen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will rauskriegen, warum der Zug so spät ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to find out why the train is so late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst den Hund rauslassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You may let the dog out.

definitions.note: Often used with emotions like Ärger (anger) or Frust (frustration).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meinen Ärger rauslassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to vent my anger.

definitions.native: to throw out; to kick out
definitions.note: informal; often means forcing someone to leave a place (e.g., a bar, a club, an apartment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Türsteher wird ihn aus dem Club rausschmeißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bouncer will throw him out of the club.

definitions.native: to throw out; to kick out (someone); to discard (something)
definitions.note: Colloquial; used for forcing someone to leave (e.g., a bar/apartment) or throwing something away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Türsteher hat ihn rauswerfen lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bouncer had him thrown out.

definitions.note: Often used with separable word order in a sentence (e.g., „Ich ziehe den Stecker raus.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du den Stecker rausziehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pull out the plug?

definitions.note: colloquial for „herauszugehen“; used with „zu“ (e.g., after verbs like „Lust haben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Lust, rauszugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel like going out.

definitions.native: to take out, to get out
definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of the separable verb „rausholen“ (e.g. „versuchen, ... rauszuholen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Handy aus der Tasche rauszuholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to take the phone out of my pocket.

definitions.native: to get out, to come out
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, heute früher rauszukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to get out earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative (to react to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie reagieren Sie auf die Nachricht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you react to the news?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reagiert sofort auf die Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reacts immediately to the message.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „reagieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reagierte sofort auf die Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He reacted immediately to the message.

definitions.note: Used mostly in formal/academic contexts; in everyday speech, "echt" is often used instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein reales Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a real problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen eine reale Lösung finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to find a real solution.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective "real" (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein Problem mit realen Folgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a problem with real consequences.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Plan ist realistisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your plan is realistic.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present of "rechnen" (also used after "ich" is omitted, e.g. in instructions or notes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rechne jeden Monat meine Ausgaben aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I calculate my expenses every month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das im Kopf rechnen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you calculate that in your head?

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ (e.g., „mit etwas rechnen“ = to expect something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen mit einer Verspätung rechnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to expect a delay.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie rechnet die Kosten schnell aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She quickly calculates the costs.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ (to count on/expect something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rechnet mit dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s counting on you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rechnete die Gesamtkosten aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He calculated the total cost.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In Deutschland ist das Recht für alle gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Germany, the law is the same for everyone.

definitions.note: Also used in expressions like „das Recht haben, …“ = “to have the right to …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast das Recht, deine Meinung zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have the right to say your opinion.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the phrase „Recht haben“ (“to be right”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast recht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are right.

definitions.note: Often used as an intensifier meaning “quite/pretty” (e.g., “recht gut” = “quite good”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist recht teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s quite expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die rechte Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the right (correct) answer.

definitions.note: Used for things on the right side, especially in phrases like „die rechte Hand“ (the right hand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich halte deine rechte Hand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m holding your right hand.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „recht“, used before a noun (e.g., after „den“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hebt den rechten Arm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He raises his right arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein rechter Arm tut weh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right arm hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie kannst du so ein Verhalten rechtfertigen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How can you justify such behavior?

definitions.native: to the right, on the right
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Apotheke ist gleich rechts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pharmacy is right on the right.

definitions.note: Describes a person’s moral character; slightly old-fashioned/formal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist ein rechtschaffener Mensch und hilft immer, wenn jemand sie braucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an upright, honest person and always helps when someone needs her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte komm rechtzeitig zum Unterricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come to class on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich red nur kurz mit dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m just talking to you briefly.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of "reden" ("I talk").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rede jetzt mit meiner Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m talking to my teacher now.

definitions.note: Often used with "mit" (to talk with someone) or "über" (to talk about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir reden später darüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll talk about it later.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of "reden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du redest sehr schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You talk very fast.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "reden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er redet jeden Tag mit seiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He talks with his sister every day.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „reden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern redete ich mit meiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I talked with my sister.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „reden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir redeten gestern lange über die Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked for a long time yesterday about the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr redselig und erzählt gern Geschichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very talkative and likes to tell stories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Kosten reduzieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to reduce the costs.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (e.g., “reduced price”), even though it comes from the verb “reduzieren”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Produkt ist heute reduziert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product is reduced today.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative form (short for "rege"), usually with a reflexive pronoun ("dich").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reg dich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move!

definitions.note: Often used to describe lots of activity (e.g., "rege Betriebsamkeit", "reger Verkehr").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dem Markt ging es heute rege zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The market was bustling today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe regelmäßig ins Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the gym regularly.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or technical contexts (e.g., laws, rules, systems).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gesetze regeln den Umgang mit persönlichen Daten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Laws regulate how personal data is handled.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that something is extreme or surprising; often with a negative tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist regelrecht unfair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really unfair.

definitions.note: Most commonly used reflexively: „sich regen“ = to stir/move (often in the negative: „sich nicht regen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich nicht regen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to move.

definitions.note: Often used for governments or monarchs; also used more generally for being in power (e.g., a party).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit 2021 regieren die Parteien in einer Koalition zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since 2021, the parties have governed together in a coalition.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der König regiert das Land seit zehn Jahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king has ruled the country for ten years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma ist in Deutschland registriert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is registered in Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, ich regle das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, I’ll take care of it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich regle die Temperatur auf 20 Grad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I regulate the temperature to 20 degrees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen soll es stark regnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s supposed to rain heavily tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es regnerisch, also nehme ich einen Schirm mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s rainy, so I’m taking an umbrella with me.

definitions.note: Used both literally for weather and figuratively (e.g., when something “rains down”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute regnet es den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining all day today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern regnete es den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it rained all day.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular form; in everyday German, people usually say “es regnet” (“it’s raining”), so “du regst” is rare and mostly poetic or playful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Spiel bist du die Wolke: Heute regst du über dem Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the game you are the cloud: today you rain over the forest.

definitions.note: From the verb „aufregen“; often used as „sich aufregen“ = to get upset.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das regt mich auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That annoys me.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: „sich regen“ = to move/stir (e.g. „Nichts regt sich.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Wald regt sich nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nothing is moving in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst den Fleck mit Seife reiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to rub the stain with soap.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr reich und hat ein großes Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very rich and has a big house.

definitions.note: colloquial shortened form of „reiche“ (dropping the final -e), often in spoken German or informal writing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich reich dir das Salz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll pass you the salt.

definitions.note: adjective with an ending (e.g., before a noun: „reiche Leute“ = “rich people”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat reiche Eltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has rich parents.

definitions.note: Often used with an object plus a person in the dative (e.g., „jemandem etwas reichen“ = to hand/pass someone something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich reiche dir das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hand you the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Familie ist sehr reichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His family is very rich.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Geld muss reichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The money has to be enough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte das Salz reichen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please pass me the salt?

definitions.note: comparative form of „reich“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist reicher als sein Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is richer than his brother.

definitions.note: inflected form of „reich“ (e.g., before a masculine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein reicher Mann wohnt hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A rich man lives here.

definitions.note: Can also mean “abundant” in some contexts (e.g., „ein reiches Angebot“ = “a wide/abundant selection”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein reiches Land.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a rich country.

definitions.note: Often means “more than enough.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben reichlich Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have plenty of time.

definitions.note: Often used to say there is more than enough of something (e.g., time, food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben reichlich Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have plenty of time.

definitions.note: superlative form of „reich“ (rich)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist der reichste Mann in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is the richest man in the city.

definitions.note: superlative form of "reich"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die reichsten Menschen der Welt leben nicht alle im gleichen Land.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The richest people in the world do not all live in the same country.

definitions.note: From the verb "ausreichen"; often used with "nicht" ("das reicht nicht" = "that’s not enough").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Geld reicht nicht aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The money isn’t enough.

definitions.note: Often used impersonally with „Es reicht.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Geld reicht nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The money isn’t enough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch reicht bis zur Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table reaches all the way to the wall.

definitions.note: Usually used with a direct object: „jemandem etwas reichen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reicht mir das Salz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hands me the salt.

definitions.note: Simple past of the separable verb „einreichen“; often used with the prefix at the end: „reichte … ein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie reichte den Antrag gestern ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She submitted the application yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „reichen“; commonly used in writing and narratives. Depending on context, it can mean to reach or to hand/pass something to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reichte ihr das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He handed her the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bananen sind schon reif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bananas are already ripe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wasser ist rein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is pure.

definitions.note: often used with verbs of motion (e.g. "Komm rein!" = "Come in!")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte rein!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come in!

definitions.note: colloquial interjection used to tell someone to enter (often said from inside a room).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: „Rein!“, ruft sie von innen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “Come in!” she calls from inside.

definitions.note: Often used as a directional particle meaning “in(to)” (especially in spoken German), e.g. with verbs of motion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm rein!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come in!

definitions.note: Colloquial for "hereinbringen"; often used with something being carried into a room or building.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Taschen reinbringen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring the bags inside?

definitions.note: Often used before a feminine noun (e.g., „reine Luft“ = “clean air”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier gibt es reine Luft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is clean air here.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "rein" used before a noun (e.g., with der/einen/keinen, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen reinen Zucker für das Rezept.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need pure sugar for the recipe.

definitions.note: Often used before a masculine noun (e.g. „ein reiner Zufall“ = “a pure coincidence”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein reiner Zufall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a pure coincidence.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „rein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Wasser ist reiner als das aus dem Fluss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This water is purer than the one from the river.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a neuter noun (or as a nominalized adjective in neuter), typically after an article/demonstrative (e.g., „ein reines …“, „dieses reines …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist reines Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is pure water.

definitions.note: Colloquial form of „hineingefahren“ (past participle of „reinfahren“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist in die Garage reingefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drove into the garage.

definitions.native: fell for it, got taken in
definitions.note: Commonly used with "auf" (e.g. "auf jemanden/etwas reingefallen" = to be fooled by someone/something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin auf den Trick reingefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell for the trick.

definitions.note: Past participle of "reingehen"; typically used with "sein" in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schon reingegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has already gone in.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech instead of the more formal „hineingehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist kalt draußen; lass uns reingehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold outside; let’s go inside.

definitions.note: Past participle of the separable verb „reinkommen“ (to come in/enter). Often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern Abend spät reingekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came in late last night.

definitions.note: past participle of "reinlassen" (often used with "haben" or in the passive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Türsteher hat uns nicht reingelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bouncer didn’t let us in.

definitions.note: past participle; used with haben/sein (Perfekt) or in passive
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Schlüssel in die Tasche reingelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the key in my pocket.

definitions.note: informal; often used like: jemanden reinlegen
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich reingelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tricked me.

definitions.note: Colloquial past participle of „reintun“ (standard: „hineingetan“ / „hineingetan“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Schlüssel in die Tasche reingetan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the key in my pocket.

definitions.note: Often used for bringing something from outside into a house/building; separable verb (e.g., „Ich hole die Wäsche rein.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Stühle reinholen, es regnet gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to bring the chairs in; it’s going to rain soon.

definitions.note: Common in contexts like sports, races, or progress (reducing a lead).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Läuferin kann die Spitze noch reinholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The runner can still catch up to the leader.

definitions.note: often used for cleaning something thoroughly or as a task (e.g., cleaning a room, device, or surface)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute die Küche reinigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to clean the kitchen today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reinigt das Badezimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cleans the bathroom.

definitions.note: Colloquial; formed with the particle „rein“ (= in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich reinkommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I come in?

definitions.note: often used informally for entering a room or building
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reinkommt und sagt nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes in and doesn’t say anything.

definitions.note: Colloquial for „hereinlassen“ (to let someone/something inside).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mich bitte reinlassen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please let me in?

definitions.native: to put in, to place inside
definitions.note: often used in everyday speech as a separable verb: „leg ... rein“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst den Brief hier reinlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can put the letter in here.

definitions.note: colloquial; usually with a person as the object (e.g. „jemanden reinlegen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lasse mich nicht reinlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not going to let myself be tricked.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „die reinste + noun“ to mean something is completely/absolutely that thing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die reinste Wahrheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the pure truth.

definitions.note: Common in expressions like „das reinste Chaos“ meaning ‘utter/complete chaos’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Sturm war es das reinste Chaos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, it was utter chaos.

definitions.native: to come in, to get in
definitions.note: Infinitive with „zu“ of „reinkommen“; often used after verbs like „versuchen“, „hoffen“, „schaffen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, reinzukommen, aber die Tür ist abgeschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to come in, but the door is locked.

definitions.native: to put in, to place inside
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergessen, den Schlüssel wieder reinzulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot to put the key back in.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used with a person as the object (jemanden reinlegen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat versucht, mich reinzulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to trick me.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I travel").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer reise ich nach Österreich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer I travel to Austria.

definitions.native: ready to travel, ready to leave
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind reisefertig und warten nur noch auf das Taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re ready to travel and are just waiting for the taxi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen nach Berlin reisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will travel to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.note: often implies taking a journey (vacation or business)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir möchten im Sommer durch Italien reisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to go on a trip through Italy in the summer.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „reisen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reist morgen nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He travels to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "reisen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr reiste ich nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I traveled to Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „reisen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzten Sommer reisten wir nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last summer we traveled to Berlin.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "reiten" ("I ride").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich reite jeden Sonntag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ride every Sunday.

definitions.note: Used especially for riding a horse (not for riding a bike).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann gut reiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can ride (a horse) well.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du reitest heute zum Stall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re riding to the stable today.

definitions.note: Usually used for riding a horse; for riding a bicycle you’d normally use „fährt“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie reitet jeden Samstag im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She rides every Saturday in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mücken können meine Haut reizen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mosquitoes can irritate my skin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Angebot kann mich reizen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The offer can tempt me / appeal to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein reizendes kleines Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a charming little café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rauch reizt meine Augen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke irritates my eyes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Idee reizt mich, aber ich habe keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The idea tempts me, but I don’t have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm reizte ihn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise irritated him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen reizte mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake tempted me.

definitions.note: Informal command (imperative, du-form) of „reißen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reiß das Papier nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t tear the paper!

definitions.note: General verb for tearing/ripping something (often suddenly or forcefully).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Papier aus Versehen gerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accidentally tore the paper.

definitions.native: to tear off, to rip off
definitions.note: With objects being removed by tearing (often with a preposition like „von“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das Etikett von der Flasche gerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tore the label off the bottle.

definitions.native: to tear open, to rip open
definitions.note: Often used for opening something by tearing (e.g., a package).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat das Paket mit bloßen Händen gerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tore the package open with her bare hands.

definitions.note: Figurative/extended use: a sudden, strong pull (e.g., on an arm, on the wheel).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat plötzlich an der Leine gerissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog suddenly yanked on the leash.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „reißen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Papier reißt leicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The paper tears easily.

definitions.note: Often used to soften a statement (meaning “fairly” or “rather”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aufgabe ist relativ einfach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The task is relatively easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Informationen sind für die Prüfung relevant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is relevant for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Großeltern sind sehr religiös.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are very religious.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a noun (weak/mixed declension), e.g. after an article like „die“ or „eine“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die religiöse Zeremonie beginnt um zehn Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The religious ceremony starts at ten o’clock.

definitions.note: informal singular command (imperative, addressing one person: du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Renn schnell nach Hause!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Run home quickly!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich renne jeden Morgen zum Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I run to the bus every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht mehr rennen, weil ich müde bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't run anymore because I'm tired.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "rennen" (used with "du")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du rennst jeden Morgen zum Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You run to the bus every morning.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „rennen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund rennt schnell nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog runs quickly home.

definitions.note: Usually means improving/refreshing the interior (painting, new flooring, etc.); for bigger structural work, Germans often say "sanieren".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir renovieren die Wohnung im Sommer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re renovating the apartment in the summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die Küche renoviert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We renovated the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr renovierte ich die Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I renovated the kitchen.

definitions.note: informal (du) command form of „reparieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reparier bitte den Computer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please repair the computer!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich repariere mein Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I repair my bike.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mein Fahrrad reparieren?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you repair my bike?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er repariert sein Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He repairs his bicycle.

definitions.note: simple past form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er reparierte das Fahrrad gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He repaired the bicycle yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for reserving a table, hotel room, seat, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte einen Tisch für zwei Personen reservieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to reserve a table for two people.

definitions.note: Often used for tables, seats, rooms, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist für 19 Uhr reserviert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is reserved for 7 p.m.

definitions.note: Often used for people (not very open or talkative) or for something booked in advance (e.g., a seat or table).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist am Anfang etwas reserviert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a bit reserved at first.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich respektiere deine Meinung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I respect your opinion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten die Regeln respektieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should respect the rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er respektiert die Meinung seiner Kollegin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He respects his colleague’s opinion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war respektlos von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was disrespectful of you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spricht respektvoll mit ihren Lehrern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks respectfully to her teachers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich respektvoll mit deiner Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak respectfully to your teacher.

definitions.note: Used attributively before a noun (with a definite article or similar), often meaning “the rest of the …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den restlichen Kuchen gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate the remaining cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist restlos aufgegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake has been eaten completely.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rette das Kind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rescue the child.

definitions.note: often used for saving someone from danger or preventing something bad from happening
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Feuerwehr will die Katze aus dem brennenden Haus retten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire department wants to rescue the cat from the burning house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du rettest die Katze aus dem Baum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You rescue the cat from the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund rettet das Kind aus dem Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog rescues the child from the water.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "retten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund rettete das Kind aus dem Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog rescued the child from the water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neue Technik ist wirklich revolutionär.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new technology is truly revolutionary.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something into the right position (e.g., straightening a picture).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich richte das Bild gerade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I straighten the picture.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition like "auf" (to aim at) or "nach" (to be guided by).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir richten die Kamera auf das Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We aim the camera at the house.

definitions.note: Used in a legal context (e.g. "über jemanden richten" = to judge someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Gericht kann über schwere Verbrechen richten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A court can judge serious crimes.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" (at/onto), e.g. "auf etwas richten" = to aim/direct at something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er richtet die Kamera auf das Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He aims the camera at the house.

definitions.note: simple past of „richten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er richtete die Kamera auf das Gebäude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He aimed the camera at the building.

definitions.note: simple past of „richten“ (in a legal context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gericht richtete ihn wegen Betrugs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The court judged him for fraud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Antwort ist richtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is correct.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist richtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is correct.

definitions.note: Used as a short reaction to confirm that something is correct.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Richtig! Das ist die richtige Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Right! That is the correct answer.
