definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun; which ending it has depends on gender/case and the article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die richtige Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the correct answer.

definitions.note: inflected form of "richtig" (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne den richtigen Weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the right way.

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adjective „richtig“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Antwort ist richtiger als meine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is more correct than mine.

definitions.note: Adjective ending (strong or mixed declension) used with a neuter noun (e.g., "ein richtiges ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein richtiges Wort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a correct word.

definitions.native: to correct, to set the record straight
definitions.note: Often used for correcting a false statement or misunderstanding.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das richtigstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to correct that / set the record straight.

definitions.note: Used especially in spoken German, signs, and headlines as a preposition-like word (often without an article), e.g. „Richtung Berlin“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir fahren Richtung Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re driving towards Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past of „reiben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rieb mir die Hände, weil mir kalt war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rubbed my hands because I was cold.

definitions.note: simple past of „reiben“ (for food, e.g. cheese)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rieb Käse über die Pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grated cheese over the pasta.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rieche Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I smell coffee.

definitions.note: Can mean either to perceive a smell (with your nose) or to have/give off a smell, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich riechen Rauch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I smell smoke.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of „riechen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du riechst nach Rauch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You smell like smoke.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „riechen“ (can be neutral “smells” or “smells bad” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen riecht gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food smells good.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „rufen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rief laut um Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouted loudly for help.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „rufen“ for „wir/sie/Sie“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie riefen ihre Freunde an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They called their friends.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used like a prefix before a noun (e.g. „riesen Spaß“) and usually without adjective endings
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten riesen Spaß auf der Party.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had huge fun at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist riesengroß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is enormous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist riesig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is huge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt ist in den letzten Jahren riesig gewachsen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city has grown enormously in the last few years.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine riesige Überraschung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a huge surprise.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (often in dative plural with -en, or in other declined forms depending on the article/case)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen in einem riesigen Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a huge house.

definitions.note: adjective in masculine nominative singular (or also used as a form with an indefinite article/possessive in the same case)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein riesiger Hund steht vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A huge dog is standing in front of the door.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with neuter singular nouns (e.g., ein riesiges Haus)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ein riesiges Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a huge problem.

definitions.note: simple past of „raten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er riet die richtige Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He guessed the correct answer.

definitions.note: simple past of „raten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich riet ihr, früher zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I advised her to leave earlier.

definitions.note: Used to mean that something is everywhere around something (not related to English “rings” as jewelry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rings um das Haus stehen Bäume.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are trees all around the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist riskant, bei Nebel so schnell zu fahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s risky to drive that fast in fog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist riskanter als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is riskier than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will kein Geld riskieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to risk any money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er riskiert alles für diesen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He risks everything for this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er riskierte alles für diesen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He risked everything for this job.

definitions.note: Simple past of the separable verb „aufreißen“; the prefix „auf“ often appears later in the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er riss das Fenster auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tore the window open.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „reißen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er riss das Papier in zwei Teile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tore the paper into two pieces.

definitions.note: simple past of „reiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ritt gestern zum Bauernhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rode to the farm yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past of „riechen“ (used especially in writing; in speech often „hat ... gerochen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern roch es in der Küche nach Rauch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it smelled like smoke in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse den Fisch roh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat the fish raw.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse keine rohe Zwiebel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't eat raw onion.

definitions.note: Dative singular masculine/neuter or genitive plural form of „roh“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er isst Sushi mit rohem Fisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He eats sushi with raw fish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sehen den Ball über den Boden rollen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children watch the ball roll across the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball rollt in den Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball rolls into the garden.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „rollen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball rollte langsam die Straße hinunter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball rolled slowly down the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein romantischer Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a romantic evening.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (declined), e.g. before a feminine noun or plural noun depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine romantische Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a romantic night.

definitions.note: comparative form of "romantisch"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Restaurant ist abends romantischer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant is more romantic in the evening.

definitions.note: Often used without ending (indeclinable), especially in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine rosa Jacke gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a pink jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Apfel ist rot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apple is red.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective (e.g., with feminine or plural nouns, or after a determiner)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag die rote Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the red jacket.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine/neuter nouns in certain cases (e.g., der rote Apfel / den roten Apfel)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den roten Apfel auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the red apple on the table.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine nominative singular (e.g., ein roter Apfel) or feminine/genitive/dative singular (e.g., mit roter Farbe) depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein roter Apfel ist süß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A red apple is sweet.

definitions.note: attributive form used with a neuter noun (e.g., ein rotes Auto)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein rotes Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a red car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir rudern jeden Samstag auf dem See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We row on the lake every Saturday.

definitions.note: third-person singular present (he/she/it), or second-person plural present (you all)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rudert jeden Morgen auf dem Fluss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rows on the river every morning.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative (command), e.g. “Ruf mich an!” = “Call me!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ruf mich später an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call me later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich später an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you later.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufen dich später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I call you later.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "rufen" (du-Form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rufst du mich später an?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you call me later?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "rufen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ruft seine Freundin an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He calls his girlfriend.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection (often as a command), especially to tell people to stop talking or calm down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ruhe, bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Quiet, please!

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present of „ruhen“ (“I rest”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ruhe mich nach der Arbeit aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rest after work.

definitions.note: Often used for resting, being at rest, or lying still (e.g., things or people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Sonntag ruhen wir uns aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sunday we rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sei ruhig und hör mir zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be calm and listen to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich ruhig, das Baby schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak quietly; the baby is sleeping.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine nouns or with plural nouns (e.g., after der/die/eine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine ruhige Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a quiet street.

definitions.note: adjective ending (e.g., accusative masculine/neuter singular or dative plural), depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir suchen einen ruhigen Platz im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for a calm spot in the park.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „ruhig“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es ruhiger als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is calmer than yesterday.

definitions.note: Adjective in neuter singular (strong or mixed declension), e.g. before an indefinite article or with no article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte ein ruhiges Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a quiet room.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular ("du") form of "ruhen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du ruhst dich nach der Arbeit aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You rest after work.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "ruhen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch ruht auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book rests on the table.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „ausruhen“; often used with the separable prefix „aus“ (e.g. „ruhte … aus“) and sometimes reflexively („sich ausruhen“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Wanderung ruhte er sich eine Stunde aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the hike, he rested for an hour.

definitions.note: Often used about finances, plans, or reputations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die hohen Kosten könnten das Unternehmen ruinieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The high costs could ruin the company.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of being financially or emotionally “wrecked.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall war das Auto völlig ruiniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the car was completely ruined.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean physically exhausted or worn out (not just destroyed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der langen Wanderung war ich völlig ruiniert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long hike, I was completely exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fehler ruinierte den ganzen Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mistake ruined the whole evening.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion or activity (e.g., rumlaufen, rumsitzen) to mean moving or being around without a specific purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er läuft den ganzen Tag rum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He walks around all day.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „herum“; often used with verbs (e.g. „rumlaufen“, „rumschauen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaue nur rum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm just looking around.

definitions.note: Informal; often implies moving around without a clear purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde den ganzen Tag in der Stadt rumlaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will walk around in the city all day.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often implies wasting time or being idle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können nicht den ganzen Tag rumsitzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can't sit around all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist rund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is round.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war rund zwei Stunden unterwegs.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was out for about two hours.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German; often used instead of "herunter"/"hinunter".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte runter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come downstairs!

definitions.note: Often used informally in spoken German to mean “down” or “downwards,” e.g., telling someone to go or move down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm runter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come down!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs as a separable particle (e.g. runtergehen = to go down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte die Treppe runter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go down the stairs!

definitions.note: Past participle of "runterfallen"; used with "sein" in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas ist runtergefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass fell down.

definitions.note: Commonly used for going down stairs/elevator, or for something decreasing (e.g., prices, temperature).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen die Treppe runtergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going down the stairs.

definitions.native: to bring down, to take down
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Kiste runterholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to bring the box down.

definitions.note: Colloquial (more formal: „herunterladen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die App runterholen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you download the app?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du kurz runterkommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come down for a moment?

definitions.note: adjective form used with a feminine noun (or plural without article), depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne die russische Sprache.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning the Russian language.

definitions.note: adjective form used after a definite article or certain determiners (weak declension), e.g. „den russischen …“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne den russischen Schauspieler aus dem Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the Russian actor from the movie.

definitions.note: adjective in masculine nominative singular (or feminine genitive/dative singular)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein russischer Film läuft heute Abend im Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Russian movie is playing at the cinema tonight.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative: “Rutsch!” = “Slide/Move over!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rutsch bitte ein Stück zur Seite!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please slide a bit to the side!

definitions.note: Used for sliding on a surface (ice, a floor) or for moving downward unintentionally; also for going down a playground slide.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind muss auf dem nassen Boden aufpassen, damit es nicht rutschen kann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has to be careful on the wet floor so that it doesn’t slip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorsicht, die Straße ist rutschig!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful, the road is slippery!

definitions.note: simple past of "ausrutschen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dem nassen Boden rutschte er aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slipped on the wet floor.

definitions.note: simple past of "rutschen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rutschte auf dem nassen Boden aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slipped on the wet floor.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun (sich rächen = to take revenge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will seinen Bruder rächen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to avenge his brother.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative of „aufräumen“ (used to tell one person to tidy/clean something up)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Räum bitte dein Zimmer auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tidy up your room!

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative of „räumen“; often used with „auf“ (e.g. „aufräumen“ = to tidy up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Räum bitte dein Zimmer auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tidy up your room!

definitions.native: to clear, to empty, to tidy up
definitions.note: Often used with places/areas (e.g., a room, a table) meaning to clear them; also used for clearing away snow.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte den Tisch räumen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please clear the table?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufräumen“; in the present tense the prefix often goes to the end of the sentence (… räumt … auf).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er räumt sein Zimmer auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tidies up his room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er räumt die Küche nach dem Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tidies up the kitchen after eating.

definitions.note: simple past of „aufräumen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern räumte ich mein Zimmer auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I tidied up my room.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „räumen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er räumte sein Zimmer auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tidied up his room.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich räuspern“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er räusperte sich, bevor er anfing zu sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cleared his throat before he started speaking.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a masculine noun in nominative singular (e.g., „römischer Kaiser“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein römischer Kaiser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a Roman emperor.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of movement (e.g., rübergehen = go over).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du nachher rüber?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming over later?

definitions.note: Commonly used with verbs like gehen/kommen/fahren to mean crossing to the other side; often colloquial for hinüber/herüber.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du nachher rüber?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming over later?

definitions.note: Commonly used in spoken German; can mean coming to someone’s place or coming over to the other side.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du später rüberkommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come over later?

definitions.note: Often used for moving something a little (e.g., furniture), or moving closer/over: „ein Stück nach links/rechts rücken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Tisch ein bisschen nach links rücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to move the table a little to the left.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war rücksichtslos und hat niemandem zugehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was ruthless and didn’t listen to anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke, dass du so rücksichtsvoll bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for being so considerate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stuhl rückt näher an den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair moves closer to the table.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „rücken“; often used with „ein Stück“/„näher“ to mean moving something slightly (e.g., a chair).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rückte den Stuhl näher an den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moved the chair closer to the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh bitte rückwärts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please walk backwards.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rühr die Suppe gut um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stir the soup well.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command), often used in warnings like "Rühr das nicht an!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rühr das nicht an!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t touch that!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of "rühren"; also used as the imperative "stir!" (informal, to one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rühre die Suppe langsam um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stir the soup slowly.

definitions.note: Often used with liquids or mixtures (e.g., soup, sauce, batter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte rühren Sie die Suppe um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stir the soup.

definitions.note: often used for stirring food or liquids
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rührt die Suppe auf dem Herd.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stirs the soup on the stove.

definitions.note: used when something affects someone emotionally
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Geschichte rührt sie zu Tränen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The story moves her to tears.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rührte die Suppe langsam um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stirred the soup slowly.

definitions.note: Often used for being emotionally affected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Geschichte rührte mich sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The story moved me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigung, ich musste rülpsen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I had to burp.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "rülpen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er rülpste nach dem Essen laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He burped loudly after eating.

definitions.note: Colloquial/dialectal short form of „das“ (neuter definite article), used especially in spoken German (often in southern Germany/Austria/Switzerland).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir s Buch geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me the book?

definitions.note: informal spoken contraction of „es“ (often written with an apostrophe as „'s“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: S regnet heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining today.

definitions.note: Often a bit old-fashioned or literary; also used in fixed phrases like "sachte, sachte".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fahr sachte, die Straße ist glatt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Drive gently; the road is slippery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Pfirsiche sind sehr saftig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The peaches are very juicy.

definitions.note: Informal command form (imperative) of "sagen" addressed to one person (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sag bitte die Wahrheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell the truth.

definitions.note: Not related to the English word “sage” (a wise person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sage dir später Bescheid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll let you know later.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (etwas sagen) or with an indirect object (jemandem etwas sagen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dazu nichts sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't say anything about that.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean something is extremely good or impressive; literally related to “legend” (Sage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert war sagenhaft!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was amazing!

definitions.note: colloquial spelling of “sag’s” (= “sag es”); common in speech/texting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du es weißt, sags mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you know it, tell me.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „sagen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was sagst du dazu?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you say to that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, dass er morgen kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says that he is coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix "ab" elsewhere in the sentence (from "absagen": "sagte ... ab").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagte das Treffen ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He canceled the meeting.

definitions.note: simple past of „sagen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sagte, dass sie keine Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She said that she doesn’t have time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „sagen“ for „we/you (plural)/they“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sagten, dass sie später kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They said that they would come later.

definitions.note: simple past (du-form) of "sagen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du sagtest, du hättest keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You said you didn’t have time.

definitions.note: past tense (preterite), 2nd person plural (ihr) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr sagtet, dass ihr morgen kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You said that you’re coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: simple past of „ansehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sah sich den Film gestern Abend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watched the movie yesterday evening.

definitions.note: Past tense form of the separable verb „aufsehen“; often used with the prefix separated (e.g. „sah … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sah zu mir auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked up at me.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „aussehen“ (e.g. „sah … aus“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sah müde aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked tired.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix of „einsehen“ (e.g., „sah … ein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sah meinen Fehler ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I realized my mistake.

definitions.note: simple past of „fernsehen“; usually used with the separable part „fern“ (e.g., „sah fern“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern Abend sah ich fern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I watched TV.

definitions.note: Simple past of „sehen“ (used mainly in writing and storytelling).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sah ihn gestern im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him yesterday in the park.

definitions.note: simple past of „umsehen“ (often used as „sah sich um“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sah sich im Zimmer um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked around the room.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb "zusehen" (often with "zu": "sah ... zu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sah ihm beim Kochen zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched him while he was cooking.

definitions.note: simple past of „ansehen“ (they/you all looked at)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern sahen wir einen Film an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we watched a movie.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb "aussehen"; in the sentence, "aus" typically comes at the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sahen müde aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They looked tired.

definitions.note: Simple past of „fernsehen“ (to watch TV).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern Abend sahen wir einen Film im Fernsehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday evening we watched a movie on TV.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sahen den Film gestern Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They saw the movie last night.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "zusehen" (plural: we/they); often used with "zu" separated, e.g. "Wir sahen zu."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sahen zu, wie die Kinder im Park spielten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched as the children played in the park.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person singular of "aussehen" (du sahst).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du sahst heute müde aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You looked tired today.

definitions.note: simple past (du-form) of „sehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du sahst gestern einen Hund im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You saw a dog in the park yesterday.

definitions.note: Informal greeting; also used to say goodbye (like “bye”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salut, wie geht’s?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi, how are you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe ist zu salzig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is too salty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute Pilze sammeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to collect mushrooms today.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of „sammeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sammelt Briefmarken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He collects stamps.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „sammeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sammelte im Herbst Pilze im Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He collected mushrooms in the forest in autumn.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural or polite “Sie” form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sammelten im Park alte Flaschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They collected old bottles in the park.

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sammle Briefmarken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I collect stamps.

definitions.note: often used to talk about something that happens regularly on Saturdays
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Samstags gehen wir oft einkaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Saturdays we often go shopping.

definitions.note: Used after a person’s name in Japanese (often written with a hyphen: -san). In German it’s mainly used when talking about Japanese people/culture.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern mit Tanaka-san gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spoke with Mr. Tanaka yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind ist heute ganz sanft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind is very gentle today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schließ die Tür sanft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please close the door gently.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine sanfte Stimme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a gentle voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag den sanften Wind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the gentle wind.

definitions.note: comparative form of „sanft“ (more gentle/soft)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sprich sanfter mit mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak more gently with me.

definitions.note: simple past of „singen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern sang er ein Lied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he sang a song.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „singen“ (used e.g. with „wir/sie/Sie“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sangen ein Lied am Lagerfeuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sang a song at the campfire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff sank in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship sank during the night.

definitions.note: Used after eating; often with „sein“ (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin satt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm full.

definitions.note: Often used for both cleanliness and doing something neatly/correctly (e.g., “sauber arbeiten”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Küche ist wieder sauber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is clean again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schreib bitte sauber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please write neatly.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „sauber“, used before a noun (e.g., feminine singular or plural with an ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte eine saubere Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a clean kitchen.

definitions.note: inflected form of „sauber“, often used before a masculine noun (e.g. „ein sauberer …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein sauberer Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a clean table.

definitions.note: comparative form of „sauber“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Tisch ist sauberer als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This table is cleaner than the other one.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter noun in nominative or accusative (e.g., „ein sauberes Zimmer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen ein sauberes Handtuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a clean towel.

definitions.note: past participle of "saubermachen" (used with auxiliaries like "haben" in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Küche saubergemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cleaned the kitchen.

definitions.note: This is the 'zu' infinitive form (used after certain verbs/phrases, similar to 'to' in English: 'to clean').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit, das Zimmer sauberzumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time to clean the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Milch ist sauer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The milk is sour.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "auf" + accusative (e.g., "sauer auf jemanden sein").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin sauer auf dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm mad at you.

definitions.note: Colloquial and often crude; typically used for heavy drinking (especially alcohol), and also commonly used for animals drinking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat gestern Abend wieder viel saufen müssen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to booze a lot again last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby kann schon kräftig saugen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby can already suck strongly.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „saugen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby saugte am Daumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby sucked its thumb.

definitions.note: simple past of „sitzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern saß ich im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I sat in the park.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „sitzen“ for „we/you(pl)/they“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie saßen den ganzen Abend am Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sat at the table all evening.

definitions.note: Often used as an interjection to express regret or disappointment (e.g., “Schade!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schade, dass du heute nicht kommen kannst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's too bad that you can't come today.

definitions.note: Used to express disappointment or sympathy; often said as a short reaction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oh nein, das ist schade!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Oh no, that's too bad!

definitions.note: Often used with dative: „jemandem/etwas schaden“ (to harm someone/something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rauchen kann der Gesundheit schaden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoking can harm your health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rauchen schadet der Gesundheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoking harms your health.

definitions.native: do it, get it done, manage it
definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (command) of „schaffen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schaff das bitte bis morgen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please get that done by tomorrow!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaffe heute etwas Neues.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I create something new.

definitions.note: Often used like: „Ich schaffe das.“ = “I can do it / I’ll manage.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, ich schaffe das allein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, I can do it alone.

definitions.native: to manage (to do something), to make it
definitions.note: Common in spoken German: „Ich schaffe das!“ = “I can do it / I’ll manage.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das allein schaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will manage that on my own.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Künstler will ein neues Werk schaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The artist wants to create a new work.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "schaffen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du schaffst das schon!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’ll manage that!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie schafft ein neues Kunstwerk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She creates a new artwork.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schafft es nicht allein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can’t manage it alone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie schaffte ein neues Logo für die Firma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She created a new logo for the company.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like “es” (e.g. “Ich schaffte es ...”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaffte es nicht, den Zug zu erwischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t manage to catch the train.

definitions.note: Informal singular (du) imperative of "schalten" (a command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schalt das Licht aus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the light!

definitions.note: Often used with the separable prefixes „ein-“ (on) and „aus-“ (off), e.g. „einschalten/ ausschalten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schalte das Licht aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turn off the light.

definitions.note: Often used with devices, lights, or settings; commonly with prefixes like einschalten (turn on) and ausschalten (turn off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Licht schalten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please switch the light on/off?

definitions.note: Often used with devices; e.g., „das Licht schalten“ = switch the light on/off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaltet das Licht aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He switches the light off.

definitions.note: simple past of "ausschalten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaltete das Licht aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned off the light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaltete das Licht ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned on the light.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schalten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaltete das Licht aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He switched off the light.

definitions.note: Also used for food that is spicy/hot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Messer ist sehr scharf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knife is very sharp.

definitions.note: Used for food (chili heat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe ist zu scharf für mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is too spicy for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe ist sehr scharf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is very spicy.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „sehen“ or „stellen“ (e.g. „scharf sehen“, „scharf stellen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Brille kann ich nicht scharf sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without glasses, I can’t see clearly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine scharfe Klinge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a sharp blade.

definitions.note: Often used for food (e.g., scharfe Soße).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie bestellt eine scharfe Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She orders a spicy soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich probiere den scharfen Senf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying the spicy mustard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein scharfes Messer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a sharp knife.

definitions.note: Used for food with a lot of heat (e.g., chili).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte heute etwas Scharfes essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to eat something spicy today.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal/colloquial form of „schaue“; also common as an imperative („Schau!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schau dir das an!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at that!

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command (imperative) meaning “look!” (to one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schau mal, da drüben ist ein Hund!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look, there’s a dog over there!

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anschauen“; in a main clause the prefix „an“ often comes at the end (e.g. „ich schaue … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaue mir den Film an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m watching the movie.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich schaue).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaue aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I look out the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir schauen einen Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re watching a movie.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition, e.g. „schauen auf/zu/nach“ (look at/toward/for).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir schauen einen Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re watching a movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaufelt den Schnee von der Einfahrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shovels the snow off the driveway.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "anschauen"; often used with "dir/mir/uns" for "look at" (e.g., "Du schaust dir ... an").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du schaust mich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look at me.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present of "schauen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du schaust heute sehr müde aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look very tired today.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anschauen“; in many sentences the prefix „an“ appears later (e.g. „schaut … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaut sich den Film an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watches the movie.

definitions.note: Often used with „fern“ (e.g. „schaut fern“) to mean “watches TV”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaut jeden Abend fern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watches TV every evening.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "schauen"; also the formal (Sie) imperative: "Schaut!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaut aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks out the window.

definitions.note: Simple past of „anschauen“; often used with the separable prefix: „schaute … an“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaute mich lange an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked at me for a long time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schauen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaute aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked out the window.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „zuschauen“; the prefix „zu“ often comes at the end (e.g., „schaute … zu“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaute dem Spiel zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the game.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anschauen“; in a sentence the prefix usually comes at the end (… schauten … an).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir schauten den Film zusammen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watched the movie together.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie schauten einen Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They watched a movie.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively with "sich" when talking about a couple getting divorced (e.g. "sich scheiden lassen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen sich scheiden lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to get divorced.

definitions.note: Often used when something seems true based on what you see or know, but may not actually be true.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scheinbar hat er die E-Mail nicht bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently he didn’t get the email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich scheine heute müde zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I seem to be tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich scheine mit der Taschenlampe auf den Weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shine the flashlight on the path.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen wird die Sonne wieder scheinen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow the sun will shine again.

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ + infinitive (e.g., „Er scheint müde zu sein“ = He seems to be tired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann müde scheinen, obwohl er genug geschlafen hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can seem tired even though he has slept enough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist scheinheilig und sagt etwas anderes, als er wirklich denkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is hypocritical and says something different from what he really thinks.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du scheinst müde zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seem to be tired.

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ + infinitive: „scheint zu …“ = „seems to …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es scheint heute sehr kalt zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It seems to be very cold today.

definitions.note: Can mean “to shine” literally (e.g., the sun, a light).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne scheint am Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun shines in the morning.

definitions.note: Vulgar/impolite; often used as an exclamation (same as “Scheiße!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scheisse, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit, I forgot my key!

definitions.note: often used for plans, attempts, or projects that don’t succeed
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan kann scheitern, wenn wir zu spät anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan can fail if we start too late.

definitions.note: simple past of „scheitern“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan scheiterte am Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan failed because of the money.

definitions.note: Vulgar/impolite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So ein Scheiß!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such crap!

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar; used to show strong annoyance (often before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses scheiß Wetter macht mich verrückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This shitty weather is driving me crazy.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/impolite; used to express anger, annoyance, or frustration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scheiß, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit, I forgot my key!

definitions.note: Vulgar/strong language; 2nd person singular informal (du) imperative of "scheißen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scheiß nicht auf den Boden!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t shit on the floor!

definitions.note: vulgar; often used informally to mean “this sucks / this is terrible.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist scheiße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s shit. / That sucks.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/impolite slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist scheiße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s shitty.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/strong slang; used to express that something is really bad or that you feel very bad.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir geht’s scheiße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel like shit.

definitions.note: Vulgar; used as an exclamation to show anger, frustration, or surprise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scheiße, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit, I forgot my key!

definitions.note: Vulgar/offensive language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich Angst habe, scheiße ich manchmal auf alles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I'm scared, I sometimes don't care about anything.

definitions.native: I don't care, couldn't care less
definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar; can sound rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist das scheißegal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't care about that.

definitions.note: Very vulgar; avoid in polite conversation. Often used as an insult or in expressions like “Scheiß-…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss scheißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to shit.

definitions.note: Vulgar/offensive; also used figuratively in insults (e.g., to say someone/something is terrible).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er scheißt auf die Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t give a shit about the rules.

definitions.note: Vulgar/strong language; used to express anger, frustration, or surprise.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Scheiûe! Ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit! I forgot my key.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (to “du”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schenk mir bitte dein altes Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please give me your old book.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (to “du”), used especially for drinks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schenk uns bitte noch ein Glas Wasser ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pour us another glass of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schenke dir ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving you a book as a gift.

definitions.note: Often used with “ein”: „jemandem etwas einschenken“ = to pour someone something to drink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schenke dir ein Glas Wasser ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m pouring you a glass of water.

definitions.note: Used when you give something as a present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dir zum Geburtstag ein Buch schenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give you a book for your birthday.

definitions.note: Used when you give something as a present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was schenkst du deiner Schwester zum Geburtstag?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you giving your sister for her birthday?

definitions.note: Used for giving something as a present; also commonly used in the phrase "jemandem etwas schenken" (to give someone something as a gift).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schenkt ihr ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gives her a book as a gift.

definitions.note: Past tense form of the separable verb "einschenken" (often used with drinks); the prefix "ein" can appear later in the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schenkte mir ein Glas Wasser ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He poured me a glass of water.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schenken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schenkte ihr zum Geburtstag ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave her a book for her birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Frühling scher ich das Schaf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring I shear the sheep.

definitions.note: Often used for cutting hair or shearing animals (e.g., sheep).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Frühling hilft der Schäfer, die Schafe zu scheren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the shepherd helps to shear the sheep.

definitions.note: Common in negative phrases like „Das schert mich nicht.“ (= I don't care / That doesn't bother me).

definitions.note: comparative form of „schlau“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Bruder ist schlauer als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is smarter than I am.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum schläfst du so lange?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you sleeping so long?

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „einschlafen“; the particle „ein“ often appears elsewhere in the sentence (e.g., „Er schläft ein.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby schläft endlich ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby finally falls asleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby schläft schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is already sleeping.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of "schlagen" (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum schlägst du gegen die Tür?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you hitting the door?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "schlagen"; also used with time to mean "(the clock) strikes".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schlägt den Ball mit dem Schläger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hits the ball with the racket.

definitions.note: Often used for quickly putting on or taking off clothes/shoes, or slipping quietly into/out of a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann schnell in meine Schuhe schlüpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can quickly slip into my shoes.

definitions.note: Used for young animals (especially birds) coming out of an egg.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Frühling können die Küken aus den Eiern schlüpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In spring, the chicks can hatch from the eggs.

definitions.note: Simple past of „schlüpfen“; often used with „aus“ (to slip out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze schlüpfte schnell aus der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat quickly slipped out through the door.

definitions.note: Simple past of „schlüpfen“; used for birds/reptiles coming out of an egg.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus dem Ei schlüpfte ein kleines Küken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A little chick hatched from the egg.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „schlürfen“ (often used in writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schlürfte die Suppe laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slurped the soup loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe ist wirklich schmackhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is really tasty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist hier sehr schmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is very narrow here.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a noun (e.g., after der/die/das, ein/eine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe durch die schmale Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m walking through the narrow door.

definitions.note: used as an inflected form of the adjective „schmal“ (e.g., before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch die schmalen Gassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking through the narrow alleys.

definitions.note: Used to describe how something tastes: „Es schmeckt (gut/schlecht/nach …)“; also: „Mir schmeckt …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe wird gut schmecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup will taste good.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „schmecken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe schmeckt sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup tastes very good.

definitions.note: Simple past of „schmecken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe schmeckte sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup tasted very good.

definitions.note: Used for flattering a person (often to gain an advantage), and also for something that is flattering (e.g., clothing, colors).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, seiner Chefin zu schmeicheln, weil er eine Beförderung will.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to flatter his boss because he wants a promotion.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German as (1) the informal imperative to one person (“Schmeiß …!”) and (2) a colloquial shortened form of “schmeiße” (“ich schmeiß …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schmeiß das bitte weg!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw that away, please!

definitions.note: Often informal; frequently implies throwing with force or carelessly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will den Ball zu mir schmeißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to throw the ball to me.

definitions.native: to kick out, to throw out
definitions.note: Informal; often used for removing someone (e.g., from a place, a group, a job).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef will ihn aus der Firma schmeißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss wants to kick him out of the company.

definitions.note: Colloquial/informal for "wirft"; also used in some contexts for "to dump/throw away".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schmeißt den Ball zu mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He throws the ball to me.

definitions.note: Can be used both intransitively (something melts) and transitively (to melt something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer kann das Eis schnell schmelzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, the ice can melt quickly.

definitions.note: often used about body parts or pain (e.g., „Meine Zähne schmerzen.“ / „Es schmerzt.“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Beine können nach dem Lauf schmerzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My legs can hurt after the run.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Verletzung am Knie ist sehr schmerzhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The injury on my knee is very painful.

definitions.note: used for physical pain; can also be used for emotional pain in contexts like "Das schmerzt."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Rücken schmerzt seit gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My back has been hurting since yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "schmerzen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Rücken schmerzte den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My back hurt all day.

definitions.note: Often used both literally (metal) and figuratively (plans, alliances).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schmied muss das Eisen sorgfältig schmieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blacksmith must forge the iron carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schokolade schmilzt in der Sonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate melts in the sun.

definitions.native: to put on makeup, to apply makeup
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jeden Morgen schminken sich viele Menschen vor der Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning many people put on makeup before work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie schminkt sich jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She puts on makeup every morning.

definitions.note: Colloquial past tense of „schmeißen“ (to throw).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schmiss den Ball zu dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the ball to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schmollt, weil er nicht mitkommen darf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sulks because he isn’t allowed to come along.

definitions.note: simple past of „schmelzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schokolade schmolz in der Sonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chocolate melted in the sun.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schuhe sind schmutzig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are dirty.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with some nouns (e.g., feminine singular or plural, depending on the sentence)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ziehe die schmutzige Jacke aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take off the dirty jacket.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in declension (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wasche mir die schmutzigen Hände.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my dirty hands.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a neuter singular noun (e.g., „ein schmutziges Auto“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein schmutziges Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a dirty car.

definitions.note: Often used in a rather formal or literary style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde schmählich im Stich gelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was shamefully abandoned.

definitions.note: Commonly used as an imperative, often with a reflexive pronoun: „Schnall dich an!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schnall dich an, wir fahren los!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Buckle up, we’re leaving!

definitions.native: to buckle, to fasten (with a buckle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schnallen Sie den Gürtel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please buckle the belt.

definitions.note: Colloquial, often used in the negative ("Ich schnall’s nicht.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schnallen es einfach nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just don’t get it.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (du) of „schnappen“; often used with „dir“ (e.g., „Schnapp dir …!“ = „Grab …!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schnapp dir deinen Rucksack und komm!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grab your backpack and come!

definitions.note: Can be used for something snapping shut or making a snapping sound.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schnapp die Dose zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Snap the can shut.

definitions.native: to snap (bite quickly), to lunge and bite
definitions.note: Often used for a quick, sudden bite or snapping movement (e.g., a dog snapping).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund kann nach Fremden schnappen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog can snap at strangers.

definitions.note: Colloquial for quickly getting/obtaining something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich musste das Handy schnell schnappen, bevor es runterfiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to quickly grab the phone before it fell.

definitions.native: to catch (a cold), to come down with something
definitions.note: Common with illnesses, especially "eine Erkältung schnappen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf der Reise habe ich eine Erkältung geschnappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the trip I caught a cold.

definitions.note: Often used with „nach“ to mean “snap at” (e.g., an animal snapping at something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund schnappt nach dem Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog snaps at the ball.

definitions.note: Often used with „sich“: „sich etwas schnappen“ = to grab something quickly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schnappt sich das Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grabs the phone.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schnappen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund schnappte nach dem Ball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog snapped at the ball.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schnarche manchmal nachts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sometimes snore at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht schlafen, weil ich schnarchen höre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't sleep because I hear snoring.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schnarcht jede Nacht sehr laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He snores very loudly every night.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "schnarchen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schnarchte die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He snored all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Berge sind im Winter schneebedeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mountains are snow-covered in winter.

definitions.note: common in spoken German (esp. southern) as a shortened form of „schneide“; also used as the informal (du) imperative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schneid das Brot in Scheiben!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cut the bread into slices!

definitions.note: Depending on context, this can mean “I cut” (present tense) or “cut!” (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schneide das Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut the bread.

definitions.note: Often used with a knife or scissors; also used for cutting hair.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Brot morgen schneiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will cut the bread tomorrow.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "schneiden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schneidet das Brot mit einem Messer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cuts the bread with a knife.

definitions.note: Used mainly about the weather; it usually takes "es" as the subject ("Es kann schneien.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Winter kann es oft schneien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter it can often snow.

definitions.note: Used about the weather; often with "es": "Es schneit."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute schneit es den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is snowing all day.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schneien“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern schneite es den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it snowed all day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist sehr schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is very fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er läuft schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He runs fast.

definitions.note: Used as an urgent call to do something faster (like “hurry!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schnell, komm her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Quick, come here!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine schnelle Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a quick decision.

definitions.note: adjective form used with certain endings (e.g., after “der/die/das”, “den”, “dem”, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir nehmen den schnellen Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking the fast train.

definitions.note: comparative form of „schnell“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte schneller sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak faster?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte schneller sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please speak faster?

definitions.note: Adjective form (neuter nominative/accusative singular) used before a noun, e.g. „ein schnelles Auto“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein schnelles Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a fast car.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schnell“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die schnellste Läuferin im Team.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the fastest runner on the team.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schnell“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der schnellsten Weg nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the fastest way home.

definitions.note: simple past of „schneiden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schnitt das Brot in Scheiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cut the bread into slices.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schieben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schob den Stuhl an den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushed the chair up to the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solche Nachrichten können viele Menschen schockieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such news can shock many people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht war wirklich schockierend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was really shocking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht schockiert mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news shocks me.

definitions.note: often used with "sein" (to be shocked)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin wirklich schockiert über die Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really shocked about the news.

definitions.note: Simple past of „schockieren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das schockierte mich sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That shocked me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe schon gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already ate.
