definitions.note: Often used to reassure someone (e.g. in “Schon gut!” = “It’s okay!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schon gut, kein Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s okay, no problem.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “don’t worry, it’ll happen soon”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be right there.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es schon gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already did it.

definitions.note: Often used to reassure or soften a statement (like “don’t worry, it’ll be fine” / “it’s okay now”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, das wird schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, it’ll be fine.

definitions.note: often used in the sense of treating something or someone gently or carefully (e.g., not damaging or overusing)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schonen Sie die Pflanzen im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please spare the plants in the garden.

definitions.note: Colloquial spelling of „schon mal“; used to mean that something happened before (often: ‘already’ in questions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warst du schonmal in Berlin?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you ever been to Berlin before?

definitions.note: simple past of "schießen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schoss den Ball ins Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shot the ball into the goal.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „schießen“ (e.g., wir/sie schossen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten schossen in die Luft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers shot into the air.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine nouns in nominative singular (and also with neuter nouns after an article like „ein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein schottischer Whisky ist oft rauchig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A Scottish whisky is often smoky.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „schrauben“; often used in written narration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schraubte das Regal an die Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He screwed the shelf to the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein schrecklicher Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a terrible accident.

definitions.note: Often used as an intensifier meaning "very" (e.g., "schrecklich nett" = "very nice").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es tut mir schrecklich leid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm terribly sorry.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with feminine singular nouns (e.g., „eine schreckliche Nacht“) or with plural nouns in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine schreckliche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a terrible idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen schrecklichen Fehler gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a terrible mistake.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective ending (e.g., with a neuter noun like „ein schreckliches Ereignis“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein schreckliches Erlebnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a terrible experience.

definitions.note: Often used as a shortened/colloquial form of "ich schreie" ("I scream/shout").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schrei nicht, ich rede nur laut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not shouting; I’m just talking loudly.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular): used to tell one person you address as “du” to write.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schreib mir bitte eine Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write me a message, please.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of "schreiben" ("I write").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schreibe dir eine Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m writing you a message.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir morgen einen Brief schreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will write you a letter tomorrow.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "schreiben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du schreibst heute einen Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re writing a letter today.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of „schreiben“ (er/sie/es schreibt)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schreibt eine E-Mail an seine Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He writes an email to his mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schreie nicht; ich habe nur Angst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not screaming; I’m just scared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht so laut schreien!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t scream so loudly!

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „schreien“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum schreist du so laut?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you shouting so loudly?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "schreien".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schreit, weil er wütend ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouts because he is angry.

definitions.note: Simple past of „schreien“ (ich/er/sie/es).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schrie laut nach Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shouted loudly for help.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schreiben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern schrieb ich eine E-Mail an meine Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I wrote an email to my girlfriend.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „schreiben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie schrieben gestern einen langen Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wrote a long letter yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schreien“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder schrien vor Angst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children screamed with fear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte geben Sie Ihre Beschwerde schriftlich ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please submit your complaint in writing.

definitions.note: Simple past of "schreiten" (a more formal/literary word for walking/stepping).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schritt schweigend durch den Flur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He strode through the hallway in silence.

definitions.note: Often used for a person's manner or tone (speaking in an unfriendly, brusque way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer war schroff zu mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher was blunt with me.

definitions.note: Often used for cleaning something thoroughly (e.g., floors, pots).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Boden in der Küche schrubben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to scrub the kitchen floor.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schrubben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schrubbte den Boden mit einer Bürste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He scrubbed the floor with a brush.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Bild hängt schräg an der Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The picture is hanging crookedly on the wall.

definitions.note: Often used informally to describe something or someone as strange in a slightly negative or humorous way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Idee klingt irgendwie schräg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His idea sounds kind of weird.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Häng das Bild bitte etwas schräg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please hang the picture a bit at an angle.

definitions.note: Often used informally to describe a person, situation, or comment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist irgendwie schräg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s kind of weird.

definitions.note: Often implies a small push, sometimes in a slightly rude or careless way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schubsen Sie mich nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t push me!

definitions.note: Simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „schubsen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schubste mich aus Versehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushed me by accident.

definitions.note: Simple past of "schaffen" (used especially in writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schuf ein neues Logo für die Firma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He created a new logo for the company.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" (e.g., "schuld sein" = "to be to blame").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nicht schuld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's not my fault.

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the dative (e.g., „dir“) to say who you owe something to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schulde dir noch zehn Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still owe you ten euros.

definitions.note: Used for owing money or owing someone something (e.g., a favor, an explanation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dir noch 50 Euro schulden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still owe you 50 euros.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du schuldest mir noch fünf Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You still owe me five euros.

definitions.note: used for owing money or something to someone
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schuldet mir noch zehn Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He still owes me ten euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schuldete mir zehn Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He owed me ten euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nicht schuldig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is not guilty.

definitions.note: Often used with a specific amount or object: "jemandem etwas schuldig sein" = to owe someone something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin dir noch 10 Euro schuldig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still owe you 10 euros.

definitions.note: Often used for cheating in games, sports, or on tests/exams.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will bei der Prüfung nicht schummeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't want to cheat on the exam.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "schummeln"; often used for cheating in school/tests or in games.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schummelte bei der Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cheated on the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Krankheit fühle ich mich noch schwach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the illness, I still feel weak.

definitions.note: Declined form of the adjective „schwach“ used before a noun (e.g., feminine singular or plural, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat eine schwache Stimme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a weak voice.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „schwach“ (e.g., after „den/einen“ or in certain genitive contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den schwachen Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the weak man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein schwacher Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a weak man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern schwamm ich im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I swam in the lake.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schwimmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzten Sommer schwammen wir jeden Tag im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last summer we swam in the lake every day.

definitions.note: simple past of "schwingen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schild schwang im Wind hin und her.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sign swung back and forth in the wind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist schwanger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is pregnant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze ist schwarz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is black.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist ganz schwarz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is completely black.

definitions.note: inflected form of „schwarz“ used before a noun (e.g., feminine or plural, depending on the sentence)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die schwarze Katze schläft auf dem Sofa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The black cat is sleeping on the couch.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „schwarz“, used before a noun (e.g., after „einen“, „die“, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage einen schwarzen Mantel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing a black coat.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine nouns (e.g., „ein schwarzer …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein schwarzer Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a black dog.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter noun (e.g., „ein schwarzes Auto“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ein schwarzes Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see a black car.

definitions.note: Often used for photos/films or images without color.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag schwarzweiß Fotos lieber als bunte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like black-and-white photos more than colorful ones.

definitions.note: Used for something suspended or moving lightly in the air; also figuratively for something being “up in the air,” unresolved, or uncertain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Über der Stadt kann man einen Ballon schweben sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Above the city you can see a balloon floating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ballon schwebt über der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon is floating over the city.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schweben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Ballon schwebte über dem Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A balloon floated over the park.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal, to one person) of „schweigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schweig bitte einen Moment!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be quiet for a moment!

definitions.native: to be silent; to keep quiet
definitions.note: Often implies deliberately not speaking or keeping something unspoken.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte schweigen Sie jetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be quiet now.

definitions.note: Often used like an adverb or adjective (present participle of „schweigen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hörte schweigend zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He listened silently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie saßen schweigend am Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sat at the table silently.

definitions.note: Describes a person who doesn’t talk much.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr schweigsam und sagt nur wenig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very quiet and says only a little.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „schweigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum schweigst du plötzlich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you suddenly silent?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "schweigen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schweigt, weil er nichts sagen will.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is silent because he doesn’t want to say anything.

definitions.note: Often capitalized when used directly before a noun (e.g., „Schweizer Schokolade“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag Schweizer Schokolade.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Swiss chocolate.

definitions.note: Often used with "in" + dative (e.g., "in Erinnerungen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie schwelgten in Erinnerungen an ihre Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They indulged in memories of their trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Kiste ist schwer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This box is heavy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutsch ist nicht schwer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: German isn't difficult.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it describes how something is done (e.g., „Es ist schwer zu …“ = „It’s hard to …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist schwer, heute einen Parkplatz zu finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to find a parking spot today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage eine schwere Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m carrying a heavy bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine schwere Aufgabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a difficult task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage einen schweren Koffer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m carrying a heavy suitcase.

definitions.note: Often used with abstract nouns (e.g., mistake, decision, times) to mean serious/severe rather than physical weight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat einen schweren Fehler gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a serious mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Tasche ist schwerer als die andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is heavier than the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deutsch ist schwerer als Englisch für mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: German is more difficult than English for me.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter noun (or as a nominalized adjective) in certain cases; here: “schweres” = “heavy” describing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein schweres Paket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a heavy package.

definitions.note: Can describe tasks, situations, or times as not easy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat ein schweres Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a difficult problem.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative person: „Es fällt mir schwer …“ = “It’s hard for me …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wird mir schwerfallen, so früh aufzustehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will be difficult for me to get up so early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Opa ist schwerhörig, aber er trägt ein Hörgerät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandpa is hard of hearing, but he wears a hearing aid.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schwer“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die schwerste Aufgabe im Test.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the hardest task on the test.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schwer“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der schwerste Koffer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the heaviest suitcase.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schwer“ (used with plural nouns or in certain cases/endings)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die schwersten Aufgaben im Test.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the hardest tasks on the test.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schwer“ (weight)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die schwersten Kisten im Lager.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the heaviest boxes in the warehouse.

definitions.note: often used for problems, consequences, mistakes, or accusations
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hatte schwerwiegende Folgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That had serious consequences.

definitions.native: to find it difficult (to do something)
definitions.note: Used with a person in the dative (e.g., „Es fällt mir schwer, …“ / „Deutsch fällt mir schwer.“). The infinitive is „schwerzufallen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wird mir schwerzufallen, Deutsch zu sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will be difficult for me to speak German.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „schweigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schwieg, als ich ihn fragte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was silent when I asked him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Prüfung war schwierig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam was difficult.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article/context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine schwierige Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a difficult question.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a noun in some cases (e.g., masculine accusative, feminine dative/genitive, plural genitive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen schwierigen Test.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a difficult test.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Aufgabe ist schwieriger als die letzte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This task is more difficult than the last one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein schwieriges Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a difficult problem.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schwierig“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die schwierigste Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the most difficult question.

definitions.note: superlative form (often used with an article: „die schwierigsten …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die schwierigsten Fragen im Test.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the most difficult questions on the test.

definitions.note: Used as an informal command to one person (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schwimm nicht so weit raus!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t swim out so far!

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present subjunctive I (also used as a polite/dated 1st-person singular form in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich Zeit habe, schwimme ich jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I have time, I swim every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann sehr gut schwimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can swim very well.

definitions.note: present participle; often used like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind kommt schwimmend ans Ufer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child comes to the shore swimming.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (used with “du”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schwimmst du heute im See?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you swimming in the lake today?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „schwimmen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schwimmt jeden Morgen im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swims in the lake every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist schwindelig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel dizzy.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of "schwinden"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Hoffnung schwindet jeden Tag ein bisschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hope diminishes a little bit every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist schwindlig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel dizzy.

definitions.note: informal (du) imperative form of „schwingen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schwing das Seil höher!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Swing the rope higher!

definitions.note: Often used for something moving back and forth (like an arm, rope, or a pendulum).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das Seil schnell schwingen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can swing the rope quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schwitze, weil es so heiß ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sweating because it’s so hot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich Sport mache, schwitzen meine Hände schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I exercise, my hands sweat quickly.

definitions.note: More formal/clinical synonym of "to sweat".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei Fieber kann der Körper stark schwitzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With a fever, the body can perspire heavily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schwitzt sehr schnell, wenn es warm ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sweats very quickly when it is warm.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schwitzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Lauf schwitzte er sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the run, he sweated a lot.

definitions.note: simple past of „schwören“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schwor, die Wahrheit zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He swore to tell the truth.

definitions.note: Used mainly for men; can be used as a general term for homosexual. Can sound rude if used as an insult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schwul und lebt mit seinem Freund zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is gay and lives with his boyfriend.

definitions.note: Describes a male who is homosexual; can be used more generally, but in German it most often refers to men.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat einen schwulen Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a gay friend.

definitions.note: comparative form of „schwach“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein rechter Arm ist schwächer als mein linker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right arm is weaker than my left.

definitions.note: comparative form of „schwach“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Grippe bin ich noch schwächer als vorher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the flu, I’m even weaker than before.

definitions.note: Informal; usually means skipping school/classes on purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird heute schwänzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s going to skip (class/school) today.

definitions.note: Usually means skipping school or class on purpose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schwänzt heute die Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is skipping school today.

definitions.note: Colloquial short form of „schwöre“ (1st person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schwör, das stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swear, that’s true.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present ("I swear").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schwöre, ich habe nichts damit zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swear I have nothing to do with it.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" (to swear by) or "dass" (to swear that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde schwören, dass ich die Wahrheit sage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will swear that I am telling the truth.

definitions.note: “du” form (2nd person singular, informal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du schwörst, dass du morgen kommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You swear that you’re coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually used for weather/air that feels heavy and unpleasant because of high humidity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es draußen richtig schwül.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s really muggy outside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zu viel Zucker ist schädlich für die Zähne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Too much sugar is harmful to your teeth.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular): used to tell one person to peel something, e.g. in recipes or instructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schäl die Kartoffeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Peel the potatoes.

definitions.note: Often used with fruits/vegetables (peel) and sometimes with things like peas or nuts (shell).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schäle eine Kartoffel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I peel a potato.

definitions.note: Used for removing the skin/peel from fruit, vegetables, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Kartoffeln schälen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please peel the potatoes?

definitions.note: used for peeling fruit/vegetables (removing the skin)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schält eine Kartoffel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He peels a potato.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "schälen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schälte die Kartoffeln für das Abendessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He peeled the potatoes for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command with a reflexive pronoun (e.g. „Schäm dich!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schäm dich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be ashamed of yourself!

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present of „sich schämen“ (reflexive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schäme mich für meinen Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am ashamed of my mistake.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich schämen (to be ashamed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mich schämen, wenn ich das noch einmal tue.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will be ashamed if I do that again.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form of "sich schämen"; used with the reflexive pronoun (dich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum schämst du dich?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you ashamed?

definitions.note: Used with the reflexive pronoun: sich schämen (e.g., „Er schämt sich.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schämt sich für seinen Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is ashamed of his mistake.

definitions.note: Past tense form of the reflexive verb „sich schämen“ (usually used with „mich/dich/sich …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schämte mich für meinen Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was ashamed of my mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Messer schärfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to sharpen the knife.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schärfte das Messer vor dem Kochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sharpened the knife before cooking.

definitions.note: Often used like “I guess…” to give an approximate number or an opinion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schätze, dass er in zehn Minuten da ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guess that he’ll be here in ten minutes.

definitions.note: Used to say you value someone or something (similar to “appreciate”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schätze deine Hilfe sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciate your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Kosten auf etwa 500 Euro schätzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will estimate the costs at about 500 euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schätzen deine Hilfe sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciate your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schätzt den Preis auf hundert Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He estimates the price at one hundred euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie schätzt deine Hilfe sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She really appreciates your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schätzte, dass wir noch zehn Minuten brauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I estimated that we would need another ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schätzte ihre Hilfe sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He valued her help a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter ist heute schön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is nice today.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it describes how something is done (not a person or thing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte schön erklären?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you explain that nicely, please?

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to react positively (like “Nice!” or “Great!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schön! Dann können wir anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Great! Then we can start.

definitions.note: Form of „schön“ used with a noun (declined adjective), e.g. after „eine“, „die“, „meine“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine schöne Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a beautiful city.

definitions.note: inflected form of „schön“, typically used before a noun (e.g. „einen schönen Tag“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünsche dir einen schönen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you a nice day.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "schön"; also used (before a noun) with masculine nominative singular, or with feminine nominative/accusative singular and neuter nominative/accusative singular after an article (e.g., "ein schöner Tag", "eine schönere Stadt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Park ist schöner als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This park is more beautiful than the other one.

definitions.note: comparative form of „schön“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern die schönere Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like the nicer jacket.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "schön"; used with neuter nouns (e.g., "ein schöneres ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein schöneres Kleid gekauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a more beautiful dress.

definitions.note: Neuter nominative/accusative singular form of "schön" (often used before a noun, e.g. "ein schönes ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein schönes Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a beautiful gift.

definitions.note: superlative form of „schön“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der schönste Tag des Jahres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the most beautiful day of the year.

definitions.note: superlative form of "schön"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir waren in den schönsten Städten Deutschlands.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were in the most beautiful cities in Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss Wasser aus dem Eimer schöpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to scoop water out of the bucket.

definitions.native: to gain, to draw (e.g., courage, strength)
definitions.note: Often used with abstract nouns like „Mut“ (courage) or „Kraft“ (strength), e.g. „Mut schöpfen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Gespräch versucht sie, Mut zu schöpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the conversation, she tries to gain courage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr schüchtern und spricht kaum in der Gruppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very shy and hardly speaks in the group.

definitions.note: comparative form of "schüchtern"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schüchterner als sein Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is shyer than his brother.

definitions.note: Often used with an accusative object: jemanden/etwas schütteln (to shake someone/something). Also used reflexively: sich schütteln (to shiver/shake).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss die Flasche vor dem Öffnen schütteln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has to shake the bottle before opening it.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „schütteln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schüttelte den Kopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shook his head.

definitions.note: Often used for pouring something in larger amounts (e.g., water, sand) rather than carefully pouring a small amount.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Wasser in die Flasche schütten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will pour the water into the bottle.

definitions.note: Usually used for pouring a lot of something (often a liquid, but also things like sand or salt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schüttet Wasser in das Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pours water into the glass.

definitions.note: Also commonly used about heavy rain: „Es schüttete.“ = „It was pouring (with rain).“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schüttete Wasser ins Glas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He poured water into the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schütze meine Augen mit einer Sonnenbrille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I protect my eyes with sunglasses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Umwelt schützen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to protect the environment.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „schützen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Helm schützt deinen Kopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The helmet protects your head.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "schützen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Helm schützte meinen Kopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The helmet protected my head.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe sechs Äpfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have six apples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin sechzehn Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am sixteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin sechzig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am sixty years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir wird auf dem Boot schnell seekrank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get seasick quickly on the boat.

definitions.note: Used for boats/ships that are safe and fit for use at sea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Boot ist seetüchtig und kann die Überfahrt machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat is seaworthy and can make the crossing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir segeln morgen über den See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re sailing across the lake tomorrow.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „segeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzten Sommer segelte er über die Ostsee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last summer he sailed across the Baltic Sea.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present ("I bless") or imperative ("bless!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich segne euch im Namen Gottes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bless you in God's name.

definitions.note: Often used in religious or formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Priester will die Kinder segnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The priest wants to bless the children.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present: "ich seh" is a common colloquial short form of "ich sehe".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich seh dich nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't see you.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ansehen“; in the present tense the prefix often splits off (e.g. „Ich sehe dich an.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe mir den Film heute Abend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to watch the movie tonight.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „fernsehen“; it’s often used with „fern“ (e.g. „Ich sehe fern.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe heute Abend fern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m watching TV tonight.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of „sehen“ (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den Bus schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can already see the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich nicht sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t see you.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „aussehen“ (e.g. „Sie sehen … aus.“ = “You/they look …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sehen heute müde aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look tired today.

definitions.note: Also appears in the separable verb „fernsehen“ (= to watch TV).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can see you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dich sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can see you.

definitions.note: Used as part of the separable verb „zusehen“ (e.g., „Wir sehen zu.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sehen zu, wie er das Abendessen kocht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We watch as he cooks dinner.

definitions.note: Often used for places, sights, or films (e.g., „ein sehenswerter Film“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Altstadt ist wirklich sehenswert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old town is really worth seeing.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich sehnen nach + dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehne mich nach dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I long for you.

definitions.note: Past tense form of "sich sehnen" (to long for); usually used with "sich" and often "nach".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sehnte sich nach ihrem Zuhause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She longed for her home.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich sehnen (nach)“ = to long for, to yearn for.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sehnten sich nach ihrem Zuhause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They longed for their home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist sehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is very good.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ansehen“; the prefix „an“ often goes to the end of the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr seht euch den Film heute Abend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) are watching the movie tonight.

definitions.note: Form used with the separable prefix „fern“: „ihr seht fern“ = you (plural) watch TV.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seht ihr heute Abend fern?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you (all) watching TV tonight?

definitions.note: 2nd person plural present (you all see)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seht ihr den Hund dort?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you all see the dog over there?

definitions.note: imperative, 2nd person plural (Look! / Look, everyone!)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seht mal, wie schön der Sonnenuntergang ist!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look, how beautiful the sunset is!

definitions.note: Used with the separable particle „zu“ (zusehen): „ihr seht … zu“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seht ihr dem Spiel zu?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you watching the game?

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form of „sein“, often used in reported speech (indirect statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er sei müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he is tired.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form of „sein“, often used in reported/indirect speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagte, er sei gestern sehr spät nach Hause gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said he had come home very late yesterday.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative of „sein“ (used to tell one person to be/do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei bitte leise!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be quiet!

definitions.note: Often used literally (water) or figuratively for ideas/entertainment that lack depth.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fluss ist hier sehr seicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river is very shallow here.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural form of „sein“ (used with „ihr“ = you all). Also used as an auxiliary in the perfect tense with some verbs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr seid nach Hause gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have gone home.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) present form of „sein“; also used as an auxiliary in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr seid gestern früh nach Hause gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You went home early yesterday.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form of "sein" used mainly in reported speech (indirect speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, sie seien müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says they are tired.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form of „sein“, often used in reported/indirect speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sagte, sie seien müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She said they were tired.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form of „sein“, used especially in reported/indirect speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, du seiest krank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says you are sick.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I (subjunctive I), 2nd person plural of „sein“, often used in reported speech or formal/older style.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ihr seiet schon zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says you are already at home.

definitions.note: Also used as an auxiliary to form the perfect tense with some verbs (often movement or change of state).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er muss gestern zu Hause gewesen sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He must have been at home yesterday.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner used with masculine or neuter nouns (e.g., sein Vater, sein Buch). Not to be confused with the verb “sein” (“to be”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist sein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is his book.

definitions.note: Also used as an auxiliary verb to form the perfect tense with some verbs (especially movement/change of state).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist schön, ein Kind zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s nice to be a child.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner; used before feminine singular nouns and all plural nouns (masculine/neuter singular is usually "sein").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sucht seine Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s looking for his keys.

definitions.note: possessive form of „sein“ used with feminine singular nouns (e.g., „seine Mutter“) and with plural nouns (e.g., „seine Schlüssel“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sucht seine Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is looking for his keys.

definitions.note: Dative masculine/neuter singular form of the possessive determiner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe seinem Bruder das Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving the book to his brother.

definitions.note: Form of the possessive determiner „sein“; used before a masculine accusative singular noun (e.g., „seinen Hund“) or a dative plural noun (e.g., „seinen Kindern“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie besucht seinen Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is visiting his father.

definitions.note: possessive form of „sein“ used before a masculine noun in the accusative (and also in some plural/dative uses, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe seinen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see his dog.

definitions.note: Genitive form of the personal pronoun „er“; in everyday German this form is relatively rare and is often replaced by other constructions (e.g. „ihn/ihm“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gedachten seiner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We remembered him.

definitions.note: feminine dative or genitive form of the possessive determiner „sein“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe seiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help his sister.

definitions.note: a declined form of the possessive pronoun/determiner „sein“ (used with certain cases and genders, e.g. „wegen seiner Arbeit“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen seiner Arbeit kommt er heute später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of his work, he is coming later today.

definitions.note: Genitive singular masculine or neuter form of the possessive determiner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen seines Unfalls kommt er heute nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of his accident, he isn’t coming today.

definitions.native: because of him, for his sake
definitions.note: Refers to a male person; often used with the genitive (sometimes with the dative in spoken German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seinetwegen sind wir zu spät gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of him, we arrived late.

definitions.note: Colloquial/nonstandard shortened form of the genitive singular (masc./neut.) of the possessive pronoun "sein"; in standard German you usually see "seines".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen seins Handys hat er den Bus verpasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of his phone, he missed the bus.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form of „sein“, often used in reported speech or formal/written language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass du gesund seist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that you are healthy.

definitions.note: Used with the dative; for ongoing time periods up to now ("seit" + time point = since; "seit" + duration = for).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne seit 2020 in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have lived in Berlin since 2020.

definitions.note: Used with a point in time or an event to say something has been true from then until now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne seit 2020 in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've lived in Berlin since 2020.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn seitdem nicht mehr gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I haven't seen him since then.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a clause about a point in the past (similar to “seit” + time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seitdem ich hier wohne, fahre ich mit dem Fahrrad zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ever since I’ve lived here, I bike to work.

definitions.note: Introduces a subordinate clause (often with verb at the end) to say something started at that time and continues up to now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seitdem ich hier wohne, fühle ich mich sicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ever since I’ve lived here, I’ve felt safe.

definitions.note: Used to talk about something that started in the past and continues up to now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn 2020 kennengelernt, und seitdem habe ich ihn nicht mehr gesehen; seither schreibe ich ihm nur noch Nachrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met him in 2020, and I haven’t seen him since then; ever since, I’ve only been texting him.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to ask someone to wait briefly (often said as: „Sekunde!“ or „Eine Sekunde!“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sekunde, ich komme gleich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One second, I’ll be right there!

definitions.note: Used after a definite article or a demonstrative (e.g. der/die/das, dieser) and inflected; means “the same (one)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen im selben Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in the same house.

definitions.native: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves
definitions.note: Colloquial variant of "selbst"; often used for emphasis (“... myself/yourself/etc.”) and as “even”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das habe ich selber gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did that myself.

definitions.note: Often used to add emphasis, similar to "selbst".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sogar er hat es selber nicht gewusst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even he didn't know it himself.

definitions.native: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves
definitions.note: Means “(one)self” for emphasis; often interchangeable with "selbst" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mache das lieber selber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d rather do that myself.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis, similar to “myself/yourself/himself,” or “even.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das selbst gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did that myself.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize something surprising or unexpected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selbst Kinder verstehen das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even children understand that.

definitions.native: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves
definitions.note: Used for emphasis (“… myself/yourself/etc.”) or as “even.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es selbst gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did it myself.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that something is surprising or includes an extreme case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selbst Kinder verstehen das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even children understand that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr selbstbewusst und sagt klar, was sie will.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very confident and clearly says what she wants.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a feminine noun or before a plural noun (e.g., with "die")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse heute die selbstgemachte Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m eating the homemade soup today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wirkt sehr selbstsicher, obwohl sie nervös ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She seems very confident even though she is nervous.

definitions.note: Often used as a short answer meaning “sure” or “certainly.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selbstverständlich helfe ich dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of course I’ll help you.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite, confident way to say something is obvious or assured.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Selbstverständlich helfe ich dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Of course I'll help you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das selbständig machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can do that independently.

definitions.note: Often used in a poetic/old-fashioned way; also used about someone who has died (like “the late …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Konzert war sie selig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, she was blissful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe ihn nur selten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only see him rarely.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe selten ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rarely go to the cinema.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine singular nouns (e.g. eine seltene Krankheit) or with plural nouns (e.g. seltene Tiere), depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine seltene Krankheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a rare disease.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak declension (e.g., after a definite article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den seltenen Vogel im Park gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw the rare bird in the park.

definitions.note: comparative form of "selten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schnee ist hier seltener als früher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Snow is rarer here than it used to be.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit dem Umzug sehen wir uns seltener.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since the move, we see each other less often.

definitions.note: Used here as an adjective with a neuter noun (e.g., “ein seltenes Tier”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Zoo haben wir ein seltenes Tier gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the zoo we saw a rare animal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein seltsamer Geruch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a strange smell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich heute seltsam verhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He behaved strangely today.

definitions.note: Used here as an adjective ending (e.g., before a noun): „seltsame …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine seltsame Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a strange story.

definitions.note: adjective in a declined form (e.g., after der/die/das, ein/eine, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern einen seltsamen Anruf bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a strange call yesterday.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "seltsam"; used to compare two things ("more strange/odd").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das wird immer seltsamer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is getting stranger and stranger.

definitions.note: Neuter form used with an indefinite article or without an article (e.g., „ein seltsames Geräusch“, „seltsames Wetter“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein seltsames Geräusch gehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a strange noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sende dir die E-Mail später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll send you the email later.

definitions.note: Often used for sending messages, emails, or data; for parcels, learners also commonly see "schicken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte die Adresse senden?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please send me the address?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sendet mir eine E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sends me an email.

definitions.note: Used for TV/radio stations and live streams.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sender sendet heute ein Fußballspiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The channel is broadcasting a soccer match today.

definitions.note: Transitive: you lower something (for “sink” by itself, German usually uses „sinken“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich senke die Lautstärke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turn down the volume.

definitions.note: often used for lowering something physically or reducing a value (e.g., prices, costs, taxes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma will die Preise senken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to lower the prices.

definitions.note: simple past of "senken" (to lower)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er senkte den Blick und sagte nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lowered his gaze and didn’t say anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert war sensationell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was sensational.

definitions.note: Often used about people’s feelings or reactions; it can also describe something delicate that needs careful handling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr sensibel und wird schnell verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very sensitive and gets hurt easily.

definitions.note: Often implies being overly emotional.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film ist sehr sentimental.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is very sentimental.

definitions.note: Often used for people, companies, or sources you can trust.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine seriöse Firma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a reputable company.

definitions.note: Often used for serving food or drinks (e.g., in a restaurant).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kellner muss das Essen servieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter has to serve the food.

definitions.note: also used for serving food/drinks in a restaurant
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kellner serviert das Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter serves the food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kellner servierte uns das Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waiter served us the food.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative of „aufsetzen“ (with „auf“ at the end), e.g. „Setz … auf!“; also a common shortened form of „setze“ in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Setz bitte deine Brille auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put on your glasses!

definitions.note: Usually used with the separable prefix: „setz … ein!“ (from „einsetzen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Setz die SIM-Karte ins Handy ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the SIM card into the phone.

definitions.note: Commonly used as the informal imperative of „setzen“ (often used when speaking to one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Setz das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the glass on the table.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „setz dich“ as an informal imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Setz dich bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sit down.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich). Also used in informal commands (du): “Setze …!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich setze das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the glass on the table.

definitions.native: to put, to place, to set
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Glas auf den Tisch setzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will put the glass on the table.

definitions.native: to put; to place; to set (something somewhere)
definitions.note: Transitive: to put/place/set something somewhere (often with a location or prepositional phrase).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich setzen das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the glass on the table.

definitions.native: to set (a rule/limit/price/goal); to establish; to impose
definitions.note: Used for setting/establishing abstract things like rules, limits, prices, goals, deadlines.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir setzen eine klare Grenze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We set a clear boundary.

definitions.native: to deploy; to use; to employ (resources/people)
definitions.note: Common in contexts like staff allocation or using tools/resources: „Personal/Technik einsetzen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma setzen erfahrene Techniker ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company deploys experienced technicians.

definitions.note: From the separable verb "aufsetzen"; in the present tense, "auf" often goes to the end of the clause (e.g., "Er setzt ... auf.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er setzt seine Brille auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts on his glasses.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „durchsetzen“; in main clauses the prefix often appears at the end (e.g. „setzt … durch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei setzt das Gesetz durch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police enforce the law.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „einsetzen“; in a sentence the prefix often appears at the end (… setzt … ein).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er setzt den Computer für die Arbeit ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He uses the computer for work.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "setzen" (also used as the formal "you" form: "Sie setzen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er setzt das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts the glass on the table.

definitions.note: Simple past of the separable verb „absetzen“ (often used with the prefix „ab“ at the end of the clause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er setzte den Koffer ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put the suitcase down.

definitions.note: Past tense form of „aufsetzen“; often used with hats, glasses, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich setzte meine Brille auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my glasses.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „einsetzen“; in simple past the prefix often comes at the end (e.g., „setzte … ein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt setzte ein neues Medikament ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor used a new medication.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „fortsetzen“ (often with „fort“ later in the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er setzte das Gespräch fort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He continued the conversation.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of "setzen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich setzte das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the glass on the table.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "setzen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir setzten die Tasche auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put the bag on the table.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "seufzen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er seufzte leise und schaute aus dem Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sighed quietly and looked out the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sexuelle Belästigung ist verboten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sexual harassment is forbidden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fühlen sich sexuell angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They feel sexually attracted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kleid sieht sehr sexy aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dress looks very sexy.

definitions.note: informal; expresses annoyance, frustration, or surprise
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Shit, ich habe den Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Shit, I forgot the key!

definitions.note: Common in everyday German; often implies shopping for fun (like “go shopping”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Samstag gehen wir in der Stadt shoppen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Saturday we’re going shopping in the city.

definitions.note: Reflexive pronoun used with many verbs; it refers back to the subject (also used with formal “Sie” = “yourself/yourselves”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wäscht sich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He washes himself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier ist es sicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s safe here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bist du sicher?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you sure?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kommst du morgen? – Sicher!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming tomorrow? – Sure!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind sicher zu Hause angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived home safely.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to agree or confirm something (often like “sure” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —Kommst du morgen? —Sicher!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Are you coming tomorrow? —Sure!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine sichere Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a safe street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine sichere Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a certain answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche einen sicheren Ort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for a safe place.

definitions.note: comparative form of „sicher“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit Helm ist Radfahren sicherer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cycling is safer with a helmet.

definitions.note: comparative form of „sicher“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mir jetzt sicherer, dass es klappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m more certain now that it will work.

definitions.native: make sure; be on the safe side
definitions.note: Often used with „dass …“ to mean checking or confirming something to avoid a mistake.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will sichergehen, dass ich die Tür abgeschlossen habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to make sure that I locked the door.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong assumption or emphasis (similar to “probably” in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt sicherlich morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will surely come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for physically securing something (e.g., with a lock or rope) or making sure something is safe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sichern Sie die Tür, bevor Sie gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please secure the door before you go.

definitions.note: Common in tech contexts for saving or backing up files/data.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meine Dateien sichern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to save/back up my files.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mond ist heute Nacht sehr gut sichtbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The moon is very clearly visible tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war sichtlich nervös.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was visibly nervous.

definitions.note: 3rd-person singular (female) subject pronoun; when capitalized as „Sie“, it usually means formal „you“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute sagt sie nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today she doesn’t say anything.

definitions.note: 3rd-person plural subject pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen kommen sie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they are coming.

definitions.note: Object pronoun (often accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe sie jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see her every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe sieben Äpfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have seven apples.

definitions.note: adjective form; often used with feminine nouns (e.g., „die siebte Woche“) or as an ordinal number
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist der siebte Januar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is the seventh of January.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin siebzehn Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am seventeen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Oma ist siebzig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma is seventy years old.

definitions.note: often used for winning in a competition, match, or war
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Mannschaft wird siegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team will win.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mannschaft ging siegreich vom Platz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team left the field victorious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Mannschaft siegt heute klar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team wins clearly today.

definitions.note: Simple past form of "siegen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mannschaft siegte mit 2:1.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team won 2–1.

definitions.note: informal singular command (imperative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sieh dir das mal an!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a look at that!

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative (du-form) of „sehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sieh mal, da drüben!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look over there!

definitions.note: imperative (formal singular) and also 3rd person singular present subjunctive of "sehen"; often used in writing like “see …” (e.g., references: „siehe Seite 10“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siehe Seite 10.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See page 10.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ansehen“; it often appears with „an“ at the end of the clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du siehst das Bild an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look at the picture.

definitions.note: Used with separable verb „aussehen“; often with an adjective: „Du siehst müde aus.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du siehst heute sehr glücklich aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look very happy today.

definitions.note: Used with the subject „du“ (2nd person singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du siehst das Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You see the problem.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siehst du den Hund dort?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you see the dog over there?

definitions.note: Colloquial spoken form of “siehst du”; often used to point something out or to mean “see?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siehste, ich hab’s dir doch gesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You see, I told you so.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „ansehen“; in a main clause the prefix often goes to the end (e.g. „sieht … an“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sieht sich den Film heute Abend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is watching the movie tonight.

definitions.note: Used with separable prefix verbs like „aussehen“; e.g., „Sieht gut aus.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sieht gut aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That looks good.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „fernsehen“; it’s usually used with „fern“ (e.g. „sieht fern“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sieht jeden Abend fern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He watches TV every evening.
