definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „sehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sieht den Hund im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sees the dog in the park.

definitions.note: Adjective form (weak inflection), used before a noun with a determiner (e.g. der/die/das, ein/eine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage die silberne Uhr jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wear the silver watch every day.

definitions.note: Often a bit negative: “too simple” or “not very intelligent.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aufgabe ist ziemlich simpel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The task is pretty simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Programm simuliert den Verkehr in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The program simulates traffic in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Türen sind geschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doors are closed.

definitions.note: Imperative (du-form): used to tell one person to sing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sing bitte leiser!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sing more quietly, please!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "singen" (ich singe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich singe jeden Morgen unter der Dusche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sing every morning in the shower.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte heute Abend singen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sing this evening.

definitions.note: Often used in everyday speech; can also imply “not in a relationship.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist seit einem Jahr single.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been single for a year.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Singst du gern im Chor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you like to sing in the choir?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie singt jeden Morgen unter der Dusche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sings every morning in the shower.

definitions.note: Often used for things decreasing in level, amount, or value (e.g., water level, prices, temperatures).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff kann im Sturm sinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship can sink in the storm.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (from the verb „sinken“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sehen die sinkende Sonne am Horizont.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We see the sinking sun on the horizon.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „sinken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff sinkt schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship is sinking quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Plan weiterzumachen ist sinnlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Continuing without a plan is pointless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne einen Plan herumzulaufen ist sinnlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Walking around without a plan is pointless.

definitions.note: imperative (command form), often used when telling a dog to sit
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sitz! Und bleib.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit! And stay.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich sitze)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sitze am Fenster und lese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sit by the window and read.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte hier sitzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to sit here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde jetzt hier sitzen und ein Buch lesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to sit here now and read a book.

definitions.note: past participle of "sitzenlassen"; often used when someone is left behind somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat mich einfach im Restaurant sitzengelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She just left me sitting in the restaurant.

definitions.note: In school contexts, "jemanden sitzenlassen" means not letting a student pass to the next grade/class.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer hat ihn am Ende des Jahres sitzengelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher failed him (and made him repeat the year) at the end of the school year.

definitions.note: Often used when you leave someone waiting or alone (e.g., you go away without them).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte lass mich nicht sitzenlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t leave me behind.

definitions.native: to fail (a student), to make (a student) repeat a grade
definitions.note: Used in a school context: the teacher decides the student doesn’t pass and must repeat the year/class.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du nicht genug lernst, kann dich die Schule sitzenlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t study enough, the school can fail you (and make you repeat the grade).

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "sitzen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sitzt am Fenster und liest ein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is sitting by the window and reading a book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin skeptisch, ob das wirklich klappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m skeptical about whether that will really work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef war skrupellos und entließ die Mitarbeiter ohne Vorwarnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss was unscrupulous and fired the employees without warning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach es so, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do it like this, please.

definitions.note: Used to intensify an adjective or adverb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum bist du so müde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you so tired?

definitions.note: Used as a determiner before a noun, often with "ein" (e.g. "so ein ...") to mean "such a ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So ein Auto hätte ich auch gern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a car like that too.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to start a new point, move things along, or signal that something is settled/finished (often with a short pause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So, jetzt gehen wir nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well then, now we’re going home.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a subordinate clause; the verb goes to the end of that clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sobald ich Zeit habe, rufe ich dich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As soon as I have time, I'll call you.

definitions.note: Introduces a subordinate clause and often expresses a result or consequence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche langsam, sodass du mich gut verstehen kannst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak slowly so that you can understand me well.

definitions.note: Often used for something that happened very recently (more formal than “gerade”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe soeben eine E-Mail bekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just got an email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm coming right away.

definitions.note: Used before a feminine noun (or as the plural form without an article), e.g. „die sofortige Antwort“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen eine sofortige Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an immediate answer.

definitions.note: used before a noun (inflected form of the adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen eine sofortigen Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an immediate answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe sogar meinen Schlüssel vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I even forgot my key.

definitions.note: Slightly formal/literary; common in writing and announcements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme sogleich zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be right back.

definitions.note: introduces a time condition; often used with a verb at the end of the clause (e.g., „Solange du hier bist, …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solange du hier bist, bin ich ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As long as you are here, I’m calm.

definitions.note: Introduces a time/condition clause; the verb goes to the end of the subordinate clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst hier bleiben, solange du willst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can stay here as long as you want.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „solch ein/so ein“ with a noun (e.g., „solch ein Tag“ = “such a day”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas habe ich noch nie gesehen, und solch ein Chaos auch nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never seen anything like that, and such chaos neither.

definitions.note: Often used as "solch ein/solche" before a noun; can sound a bit formal in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe solch ein Problem noch nie gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have never seen such a problem before.

definitions.note: Plural or feminine singular form (often used before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche solche Schuhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for such shoes.

definitions.note: Used with plural nouns (or with feminine singular in nominative/accusative) as a demonstrative determiner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solche Fragen sind wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such questions are important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne solche Leute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know such people.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter form of "solch"; often used with a noun (e.g., "mit solchem ...")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit solchem Wetter bleiben wir lieber zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With such weather, we'd rather stay at home.

definitions.note: Used with strong/mixed adjective endings depending on the article; here it’s the inflected form (e.g., dative masculine/neuter after "mit").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit solchen Problemen habe ich nicht gerechnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t expect such problems.

definitions.note: inflected form of the determiner "solch" (used before a noun; the ending changes with case/gender/number)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit solchen Problemen habe ich nicht gerechnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't expect problems like that.

definitions.note: Declined form of "solcher"; used before a noun (often in phrases like "solchen Leuten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit solchen Leuten möchte ich nicht arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to work with such people.

definitions.note: Used as a determiner; this form is typically masculine nominative (e.g., „solcher Mann“) or masculine/neuter genitive (e.g., „wegen solcher Probleme“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solcher Lärm macht mich verrückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Such noise drives me crazy.

definitions.note: Often used with a noun (e.g., „solches Wetter“) or on its own to refer back to something mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas hatte ich noch nie gesehen, aber so etwas wie solches Wetter ist wirklich selten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had never seen anything like that before, but weather like this is really rare.

definitions.note: Often used for something reliable or well-built; can also describe finances or arguments (e.g., a “solide Grundlage”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist sehr solide.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is very solid.

definitions.note: Often used to express obligation or what someone says/claims is the case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er soll morgen kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is supposed to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often expresses an obligation or expectation (“is supposed to”) rather than personal advice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er soll morgen früh hier sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is supposed to be here tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „sollen“; often used to report what is expected or said (like “is said to”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er soll heute länger arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is supposed to work longer today.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I of "sollen"; often used in reported speech (what someone says is supposed to be the case).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich solle heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says I should go home earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used to express an obligation/expectation (usually weaker than müssen). Can also be used to report what someone says ("is said to").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollen um acht Uhr da sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re supposed to be there at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of the modal verb "sollen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du sollst deine Hausaufgaben machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are supposed to do your homework.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (“you all”) of "sollen" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr sollt jetzt leise sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You all should be quiet now.

definitions.note: Often expresses advice (“should”) or an expected obligation/plan (“was supposed to”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sollte mehr Gemüse essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I should eat more vegetables.

definitions.note: Often used to give advice or make a polite suggestion (subjunctive II of „sollen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du solltest mehr schlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should sleep more.

definitions.note: Often used to give advice or make a polite suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten jetzt gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should go now.

definitions.note: Often used to express a recommendation or obligation; depending on context it can also mean “were supposed to.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should leave earlier.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form of "sollen"; often used for polite advice or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du solltest mehr Wasser trinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should drink more water.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) past subjunctive form of "sollen"; often used for advice or polite suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du solltest mehr schlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should sleep more.

definitions.note: Second person plural (ihr) simple past / subjunctive II form; often used for advice or polite suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr solltet mehr Wasser trinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should drink more water.

definitions.note: Common in more formal writing and speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnete den ganzen Tag, somit blieben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained all day, so we stayed at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wirklich sonderbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is really strange.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich heute sonderbar verhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He behaved strangely today.

definitions.note: Often used in negatives to mean “not particularly / not especially.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde den Film nicht sonderlich gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't find the movie particularly good.

definitions.note: Used after a negation (e.g., „nicht“, „kein-“), to correct or replace what was just negated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist nicht mein Auto, sondern das von Anna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That isn’t my car, but rather Anna’s.

definitions.note: Loanword from English; common in everyday German, especially for pop/rock music.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag diesen Song sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es sonnig und warm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is sunny and warm.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak inflection form (e.g., after a definite article like "den")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir genießen den sonnigen Tag im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re enjoying the sunny day in the park.

definitions.note: Adjective in comparative form (more sunny).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es sonniger als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is sunnier than yesterday.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively with „sich“: „sich sonnen“ = to sunbathe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sonnt sich im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is sunbathing in the garden.

definitions.note: used to mean something happens regularly on Sundays
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sonntags schlafe ich länger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sundays I sleep longer.

definitions.note: means “every Sunday” (habitually/regularly), not “this Sunday.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sonntags schlafen wir oft lange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sundays, we often sleep in.

definitions.note: refers to something that happens regularly every Sunday
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sonntags gehen wir oft spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sundays we often go for a walk.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich sonnen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern sonnte ich mich im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I sunbathed in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beeil dich, sonst verpassen wir den Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hurry up, otherwise we’ll miss the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sonst geht es mir gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apart from that, I’m doing well.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative with a reflexive pronoun: „Sorg dich nicht!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sorg dich nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry!

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative: „Sorg dafür, dass …“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sorg bitte dafür, dass die Tür zu ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please make sure the door is closed.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "sorgen" (ich sorge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sorge mich um dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worry about you.

definitions.note: Common patterns: „für (etw./jdn.) sorgen“ = take care of (sth./sb.); „dafür sorgen, dass …“ = make sure that …
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sorge dafür, dass alles klappt, und ich werde dafür sorgen, dass wir pünktlich ankommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I make sure that everything works out, and I will make sure that we arrive on time.

definitions.note: Often reflexive: „sich um etw./jdn. sorgen“ = worry about sth./sb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sorge mich um dich, weil du so spät nach Hause kommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worry about you because you come home so late.

definitions.note: „für etw./jdn. sorgen“ can mean to look after someone or to provide what is needed
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sorgen für ihre Kinder und sorgen dafür, dass genug zu essen da ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take care of their children and make sure there is enough to eat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte lies den Vertrag sorgfältig durch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please read through the contract carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte lies den Vertrag sorgfältiger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please read the contract more carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Urlaub fühle ich mich sorglos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On vacation I feel carefree.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of "sorgen" (du). Often used with "dich" ("sich sorgen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du sorgst dich zu viel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You worry too much.

definitions.note: Used with "für" for taking care of/providing for someone or something: "sorgt für ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sorgt für seine Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes care of his family.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „sorgen“ in the sense of „to worry“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sorgte sich um seine Tochter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He worried about his daughter.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „sorgen“ in the sense of „to take care of / ensure“ (often with „für“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sorgte für das Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took care of the food.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German as an English loanword; used to apologize or to get someone's attention (like “excuse me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sorry, das war mein Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, that was my mistake.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “as much/many as that,” and in phrases like „so viel wie möglich“ (“as much as possible”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht soviel Geld dabei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have that much money with me.

definitions.note: Means “this much/that much; so much/so many.” Also commonly written as two words (“so viel”), but here the examples use the spelling “soviel” exactly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht soviel Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have so much time.

definitions.note: Used to refer to an amount or number; often appears in phrases like „so viel wie …“ (“as much as …”) or „so viel(e) …“ (“so many …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nicht soviel Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have that much time.

definitions.native: something like that, such a thing
definitions.note: colloquial; short for "so etwas"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sowas habe ich noch nie gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've never seen anything like that.

definitions.native: something like that, that kind of thing
definitions.note: colloquial contraction of "so etwas".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sowas habe ich noch nie gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never seen anything like that before.

definitions.native: something like that; a thing like that
definitions.note: colloquial; often used to express surprise or disapproval
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sowas habe ich noch nie gesehen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never seen anything like that!

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „soweit ich weiß“ (“as far as I know”) or „soweit möglich“ (“as far as possible”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soweit ich weiß, kommt er morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As far as I know, he's coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: Can refer to progress up to now (often with „bis jetzt“ implied).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soweit ist alles gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: So far, everything is good.

definitions.note: Often introduces a clause meaning “as far as / insofar as” (e.g., “as far as I know”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soweit ich weiß, kommt er morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As far as I know, he’s coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to link two items; similar to “und” but emphasizes addition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe Brot sowie Käse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m buying bread as well as cheese.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme sowieso zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to be late anyway.

definitions.note: Usually used with „als (auch)“: „sowohl … als (auch) …“ = „both … and …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche sowohl Deutsch als auch Englisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak both German and English.

definitions.note: Usually used with „als/auch“: „sowohl … als auch …“ (= both … and …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spricht sowohl Deutsch als auch Englisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks both German and English.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a feminine noun (or with plural nouns when preceded by a definite article, e.g. die sozialen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie macht soziale Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She does social work.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with masculine accusative, feminine dative/genitive, or plural (all cases)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen mehr sozialen Wohnungsbau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more social housing.

definitions.native: so to speak, as it were
definitions.note: Used to soften or qualify what you just said, similar to “kind of” or “in a manner of speaking.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sozusagen mein Chef.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is, so to speak, my boss.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with feminine singular or plural nouns, depending on the article and case)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne spanische Wörter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Spanish words.

definitions.note: adjective in the masculine nominative singular form (often used before a masculine noun, e.g. "spanischer Wein")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein spanischer Wein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a Spanish wine.

definitions.note: Often used for making something taut (e.g., a rope, a string, a bow).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Seil spannen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tighten the rope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich spannend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really exciting.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with neuter singular nouns (e.g., "ein spannendes Buch").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese gerade ein spannendes Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reading an exciting book right now.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (du-form): used to tell one person to save or conserve something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spar dein Geld!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Save your money!

definitions.note: Often used with money or resources; not the same as English “to spare” (= übrig haben/verschonen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spare jeden Monat Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I save money every month.

definitions.note: Often used with "Geld" (money) or "für" (for) to say what you're saving for.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mehr Geld sparen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to save more money.

definitions.note: Often used about spending, using resources, or consumption (e.g., electricity, water).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen sparsam mit Wasser umgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to use water sparingly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spart jeden Monat Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He saves money every month.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „sparen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr sparte ich genug Geld für ein neues Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I saved enough money for a new bike.

definitions.native: go for a walk, take a walk
definitions.note: Often used with „gehen“: „spazieren gehen“ = to go for a walk.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen nach dem Essen spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go for a walk after the meal.

definitions.native: gone for a walk, gone strolling
definitions.note: Past participle, used with „sein“ in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin nach dem Abendessen spazierengegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went for a walk after dinner.

definitions.native: go for a walk, take a walk
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen nach dem Abendessen spazierengehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go for a walk after dinner.

definitions.note: Often used for saving files/data (e.g., on a computer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, die Datei zu speichern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to save the file.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sonnenuntergang war spektakulär.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sunset was spectacular.

definitions.native: to donate, to give (as a donation)
definitions.note: Often used with money, blood, or goods given to a cause or organization.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Leute spenden Geld für das Tierheim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people donate money to the animal shelter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spendet jeden Monat Geld an eine Hilfsorganisation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He donates money to a charity every month.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "spenden"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spendete Geld für das Tierheim.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He donated money to the animal shelter.

definitions.note: Often used for blocking access (e.g., roads, accounts, cards).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei muss die Straße sperren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have to block off the street.

definitions.note: Often used for things that are awkward to handle or transport because of their size or shape.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schrank ist zu sperrig für das kleine Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wardrobe is too bulky for the small car.

definitions.note: Often used with objects like doors, streets, or accounts (e.g., to lock a door or block a road/account).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sicherheitsdienst sperrt die Tür ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The security service locks the door.

definitions.note: This form is the inflected adjective (e.g., before a noun: „eine spezielle Frage“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine spezielle Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a special question.

definitions.note: Used here with neuter nouns (e.g., „ein spezielles Angebot“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein spezielles Angebot nur für heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a special offer just for today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der See spiegelt die Berge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lake reflects the mountains.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of „spielen“ (used with „ich“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spiel heute Abend mit meinen Freunden Karten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m playing cards with my friends tonight.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of "spielen" ("I play").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spiele heute Abend Fußball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play soccer tonight.

definitions.note: Used for playing games or sports, and for playing an instrument.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder spielen im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are playing in the park.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form) of „spielen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spielst du heute Abend Fußball?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you playing soccer tonight?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "spielen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spielt jeden Abend Fußball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He plays soccer every evening.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „spielen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern spielte ich mit meinem Bruder im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I played with my brother in the park.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "spielen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern spielten wir im Park Fußball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we played soccer in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern spieltest du Fußball im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you played soccer in the park.

definitions.note: often used for spinning thread/yarn; also used for spiders spinning webs
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spinnen können Netze spinnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spiders can spin webs.

definitions.native: to be crazy, to be out of your mind
definitions.note: informal/colloquial (e.g. said to someone: „Du spinnst!“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du solltest nicht gleich spinnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn’t go crazy right away.

definitions.native: are you crazy?, are you nuts?
definitions.note: Commonly used as an informal exclamation (often in questions like „Spinnst du?“) meaning someone is acting crazy or unreasonable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spinnst du? Das ist viel zu gefährlich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you crazy? That’s way too dangerous!

definitions.note: Literal meaning (e.g., spinning wool/thread).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spinnst du heute wieder Wolle?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you spinning wool again today?

definitions.native: are you crazy?, are you out of your mind?
definitions.note: Common colloquial use, often as an exclamation: “Spinnst du?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spinnst du? Das ist viel zu gefährlich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you crazy? That’s far too dangerous!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Spinne spinnt ein Netz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The spider spins a web.

definitions.note: Colloquial; used to say someone is acting crazy or being ridiculous.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spinnt, wenn er denkt, das klappt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s crazy if he thinks that will work.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum spionierst du mir nach?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you spying on me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorsicht, das ist eine spitze Nadel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful, that’s a sharp needle.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Idee ist spitze!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your idea is great!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spitzte den Bleistift.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sharpened the pencil.

definitions.native: spontaneous, on the spur of the moment
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben spontan beschlossen, heute Abend essen zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided spontaneously to go out to eat tonight.

definitions.native: spontaneously, on the spur of the moment
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben spontan beschlossen, ins Kino zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We decided spontaneously to go to the cinema.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr sportlich und geht dreimal pro Woche joggen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very athletic and goes jogging three times a week.

definitions.note: simple past of "sprechen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern sprach ich lange mit meiner Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I spoke with my teacher for a long time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „sprechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sprachen gestern lange über den Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spoke for a long time about the movie yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for being so surprised, shocked, or moved that you can’t speak.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als ich die Nachricht hörte, war ich sprachlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I heard the news, I was speechless.

definitions.note: simple past of „springen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Katze sprang auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat jumped onto the table.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „springen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern sprangen die Kinder über die Pfütze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday the children jumped over the puddle.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense (ich spreche).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche ein bisschen Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak a little German.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann gut Deutsch sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can speak German well.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural present ("you" plural/informal: you all) of "sprechen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr sprecht sehr leise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) speak very quietly.

definitions.note: Often used for explosives or deliberately destroying something (e.g., a bridge, a safe).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei musste die Tür sprengen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police had to blow up (blast open) the door.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular “du” command) of „sprechen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sprich bitte langsamer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak more slowly.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (used with "du")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sprichst du Englisch?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you speak English?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "sprechen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spricht sehr gut Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He speaks German very well.

definitions.note: informal singular (du) imperative of „springen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spring nicht von der Mauer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t jump off the wall!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich springe) or imperative (springe!) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich springe über die Pfütze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I jump over the puddle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder springen über die Pfütze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children jump over the puddle.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „springen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum springst du so hoch?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you jumping so high?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "springen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund springt über den Zaun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog jumps over the fence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gärtner spritzt Wasser auf die Blumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gardener sprays water on the flowers.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „spritzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlauch spritzte Wasser in alle Richtungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hose sprayed water in all directions.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of „sprechen“, often used for hypotheticals or polite phrasing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spräche mit ihm, wenn ich Zeit hätte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would speak with him if I had time.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spuck nicht auf den Boden!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t spit on the floor!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht auf den Boden spucken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t spit on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spuckte auf den Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spat on the ground.

definitions.note: Usually used about ghosts; more commonly you’ll see it as “es spukt” (“it’s haunted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nachts spuke ich im alten Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, I haunt the old house.

definitions.note: Used for ghosts or spooky things (e.g., a place is haunted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dem alten Haus spukt es nachts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old house is haunted at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb verschwand spurlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief disappeared without a trace.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase "sich sputen" (= to hurry up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen uns sputen, sonst verpassen wir den Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to hurry up, otherwise we’ll miss the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist schon spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s already late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute spät nach Hause gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got home late today.

definitions.note: Weak adjective ending: used after a definite article or similar (e.g., der/die/das).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns am späten Nachmittag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet in the late afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll come later.

definitions.native: at the latest, no later than
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst spätestens um 18 Uhr zu Hause sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to be home by 6 p.m. at the latest.

definitions.note: Often used for rinsing or for doing the dishes (e.g., "Geschirr spülen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss nach dem Essen die Teller spülen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to wash the plates after the meal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spült die Teller nach dem Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rinses the plates after the meal.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „spülen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spülte das Geschirr nach dem Abendessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rinsed the dishes after dinner.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (du) of „spüren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Spür mal, wie warm die Sonne ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Feel how warm the sun is.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "spüren" (ich spüre).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spüre den Wind im Gesicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel the wind on my face.

definitions.note: often used for physically or emotionally noticing something (sometimes more subtle than "fühlen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spüre den Wind auf meiner Haut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel the wind on my skin.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "spüren".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du spürst die Kälte im Wind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You feel the cold in the wind.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "spüren".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er spürt den kalten Wind im Gesicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels the cold wind on his face.

definitions.note: Simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „spüren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spürte die kalte Luft im Raum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt the cold air in the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch ist stabil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is stable.

definitions.note: simple past form of „stechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Biene stach mich in den Arm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bee stung me in the arm.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „stehlen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stahl gestern ein Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stole a bicycle yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) plural form of „stehlen“ (e.g., „wir/sie stahlen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stahlen das Fahrrad vor dem Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They stole the bicycle in front of the house.

definitions.note: Often used with „aus“ (from a place) or „von“ (from a family/background).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stamme aus Kanada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from Canada.

definitions.note: Often used with „aus“ (from) or „von“ (from).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stamme aus Deutschland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come from Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stammt aus Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes from Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „stammen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stammte aus Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came from Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wütend stampfte er mit dem Fuß auf den Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Angry, he stomped his foot on the floor.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "aufstehen"; often used with the separable prefix "auf" at the end of the clause
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stand um sechs Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got up at six o’clock.

definitions.note: simple past of „stehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern stand ich lange an der Haltestelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I stood at the bus stop for a long time.

definitions.note: Simple past form used with the separable verb „aufstehen“ (the „auf“ usually comes later in the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir standen um sechs Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got up at six o’clock.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „stehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie standen vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They stood in front of the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr standet gestern lange vor dem Museum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stood in front of the museum for a long time yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie blieb auch in schwierigen Zeiten standhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She remained steadfast even in difficult times.

definitions.note: simple past of „stinken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Regen stank die Mülltonne besonders stark.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, the trash can stank especially badly.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „sterben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er starb gestern im Krankenhaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He died yesterday in the hospital.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 3rd-person plural of „sterben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen starben in diesem Krieg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people died in this war.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist stark genug, um die Kiste zu tragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is strong enough to carry the box.

definitions.note: Often used to describe the intensity or degree of something (e.g., it’s raining heavily).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnet heute stark.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining heavily today.

definitions.note: inflected form of “stark”, typically used before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine starke Frau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a strong woman.

definitions.note: inflected form of "stark" (used with some noun endings, e.g., after "ein"/"der")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke morgens einen starken Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink a strong coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: used before a masculine noun (e.g. „ein starker Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein starker Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a strong man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein starkes Bier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a strong beer.

definitions.note: Often used with „an“ + accusative: „jemanden/etwas anstarren“ = to stare at someone/something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum starren wir uns so lange an?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are we staring at each other for so long?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist manchmal sehr starrköpfig und hört nicht auf Ratschläge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is sometimes very stubborn and doesn't listen to advice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum starrst du mich so an?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you staring at me like that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er starrt mich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stares at me.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of "anstarren"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er starrte mich die ganze Zeit an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stared at me the whole time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er starrte mich lange an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stared at me for a long time.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) plural of „starren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie starrten ihn lange an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They stared at him for a long time.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense ("I start")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich starte den Computer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I start the computer.

definitions.note: Often used for starting a machine, vehicle, program, or an activity (e.g., a course or project).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir starten das Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We start the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film startet um 20 Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie starts at 8 p.m.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „starten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Pilot startete das Flugzeug um sieben Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pilot started the airplane at seven o’clock.

definitions.native: ready to start, ready to go
definitions.note: Often used for people, teams, or machines when they’re prepared to begin.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind startklar und können losfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re ready to go and can set off.

definitions.note: Often used with sein/werden to say that soldiers, police, or units are based in a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Soldaten sind in der Stadt stationiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers are stationed in the city.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive in formal German (instead des Kaffees), but often with dative in everyday speech (statt dem Kaffee).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke heute Tee statt Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m drinking tea instead of coffee.

definitions.note: Often used with a noun/pronoun (usually with genitive in formal German, but commonly with dative in everyday speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke heute Tee statt Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m drinking tea instead of coffee.

definitions.note: Used to introduce an alternative (often followed by “dass” or a zu-infinitive: “statt dass …”, “statt zu …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Statt dass wir ausgehen, bleiben wir heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Instead of going out, we're staying at home today.

definitions.note: Refers to doing/choosing something in place of something else mentioned or implied.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe heute nicht ins Fitnessstudio; ich mache stattdessen einen Spaziergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not going to the gym today; I’m going for a walk instead.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert wird morgen Abend stattfinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert will take place tomorrow evening.

definitions.note: Used especially for scheduled or organized events; 3rd person singular present of „stattfinden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert stattfindet morgen im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert takes place tomorrow in the park.

definitions.note: past participle of "stattfinden"; used with "haben" (e.g., "hat stattgefunden")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Treffen hat gestern stattgefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting took place yesterday.

definitions.note: Used mainly in formal/legal contexts (e.g., courts, official decisions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dem Antrag wurde stattgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The request was granted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das alte Klavier ist staubbedeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old piano is covered in dust.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dachboden ist sehr staubig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The attic is very dusty.

definitions.note: often used for insects like bees or wasps
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bienen können stechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bees can sting.

definitions.note: used for something sharp (e.g., a needle, knife, thorn)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorsicht, die Nadel kann stechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful, the needle can prick.

definitions.note: Often used with "in" (e.g., "etwas in etwas stecken" = to put/stick something into something). As a standalone form, "steck" is commonly used as the informal imperative (du-form) of "stecken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Steck den Schlüssel in die Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the key in your pocket.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative (command). It can also mean “plug in,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Steck den Schlüssel ins Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the key in the lock.

definitions.note: Often used with a direction phrase like „in + Akkusativ“ to say you put something into something (e.g., a pocket, bag, or socket).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stecke den Schlüssel in die Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the key in my pocket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst den Schlüssel ins Schloss stecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to put the key into the lock.

definitions.note: Often used with places like traffic: im Stau stecken.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir scheinen im Stau zu stecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We seem to be stuck in traffic.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "stecken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du steckst den Schlüssel in die Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put the key in your pocket.

definitions.note: Often used to say something is located in something (e.g. a key in a lock).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel steckt im Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key is in the lock.

definitions.note: Used with an object: someone puts/sticks something into something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie steckt den Brief in den Umschlag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She puts the letter into the envelope.

definitions.note: simple past of "stecken" (intransitive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlüssel steckte im Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The key was stuck in the lock.

definitions.note: simple past of "stecken" (transitive)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich steckte den Brief in den Umschlag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the letter in the envelope.

definitions.note: Often used with a thing + „in“ (e.g., „den Schlüssel in die Tasche“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir steckten den Schlüssel in die Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put the key in the pocket.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase „im Stau stecken“ = to be stuck in traffic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Autos steckten im Stau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cars were stuck in traffic.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative form of "aufstehen"; often used in the phrase "Steh auf!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Steh auf, wir müssen los!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get up, we have to go!

definitions.note: informal singular imperative of „stehen“; often used with „auf“: „Steh auf!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Steh bitte auf!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stand up!

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufstehen“; in the present tense the prefix often comes at the end (e.g., „ich stehe ... auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stehe jeden Tag um sieben Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get up every day at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present of "stehen" ("ich stehe" = "I stand" / "I am standing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stehe an der Bushaltestelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am standing at the bus stop.

definitions.note: Used with the separable-prefix verb „aufstehen“; in many sentences „auf“ appears at the end (e.g., „wir stehen ... auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir stehen jeden Tag um sechs Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We get up every day at six o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht lange stehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand for long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht lange stehen, also setze ich mich gleich hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand for long, so I'll sit down right away.

definitions.native: to stop (moving); to come to a standstill
definitions.note: Often used for people/vehicles that were moving and then stop.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als die Ampel auf Gelb sprang, musste ich plötzlich stehenbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the light turned yellow, I suddenly had to stop.

definitions.native: to remain standing; to stay where you are (standing)
definitions.note: Used when someone is asked not to move from a spot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte stehenbleiben und auf den nächsten Bus warten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stay where you are and wait for the next bus.

definitions.note: Past participle of „stehenbleiben“, often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist stehengeblieben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus ist plötzlich stehengeblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus suddenly stopped.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man sollte nicht stehlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One should not steal.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du-form). In the separable verb "aufstehen" (to get up/stand up), the prefix often goes to the end: "Du stehst auf."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du stehst um sieben Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You get up at seven o'clock.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „stehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum stehst du hier?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you standing here?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „aufstehen“; in main clauses it’s split: „steht … auf“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er steht jeden Morgen um sechs Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets up every morning at six o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er steht vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is standing in front of the door.

definitions.note: Often used for buildings/objects to say where something is.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel steht am Meer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel is located by the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem langen Flug war mein Nacken ganz steif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the long flight, my neck was completely stiff.

definitions.note: Most commonly used as the informal singular imperative of „steigen“ (e.g., telling one person to climb or get on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Steig auf den Hügel!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Climb up the hill!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich steige auf den Berg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I climb the mountain.

definitions.note: Often used with "in" or "ein" (e.g. "in den Bus", "einsteigen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich steige in den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get on the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis ist hoch, also steige ich nicht höher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price is high, so I don’t go higher.

definitions.native: to climb, to rise, to go up
definitions.note: Often used with "in" + accusative for getting into a vehicle (e.g., "in den Bus steigen" = to get on the bus).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Temperaturen steigen im Sommer oft sehr schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Temperatures often rise very quickly in summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Produktion steigern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to increase production.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present of "steigen" (du-Form). Often used with prepositions like "auf" (climb onto) or "in" (get into).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du steigst in den Bus ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You get on the bus.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "steigen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rauch steigt in den Himmel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke rises into the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Weg ist hier sehr steil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The path is very steep here.

definitions.note: Used attributively before a noun (weak declension), e.g. after a definite article like "den".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind den steilen Weg hinaufgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked up the steep path.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal imperative (command) of „stellen“ (to set/put something somewhere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stell das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the glass on the table.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „vor“ (e.g., „stell … vor“); often the imperative singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stell dich bitte vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please introduce yourself.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „vor“ (e.g., „stell dir vor …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stell dir vor, wir gewinnen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagine we win!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stelle das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the glass on the table.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix: „jemanden vorstellen“ → e.g., „Ich stelle dich vor.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stelle meinen Freund vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I introduce my friend.

definitions.note: Often used as „sich (etwas) vorstellen“ (to imagine something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stelle mir das vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagine that.

definitions.note: Often used for placing something in an upright/standing position; also common in fixed phrases like „eine Frage stellen“ (= to ask a question).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte stellen Sie die Flasche auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put the bottle on the table.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „stellen“ (you put/place/set).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du stellst die Tasse auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put the cup on the table.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „stellen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stellt das Glas auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts the glass on the table.

definitions.note: Used with „eine Frage“ (to ask a question). 3rd person singular present of „stellen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stellt eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asks a question.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „stellen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stellte die Flasche auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put the bottle on the table.

definitions.note: used with „eine Frage“: „eine Frage stellen“ = to ask a question
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stellte eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asked a question.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „stellen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stellten die Stühle an die Wand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put the chairs against the wall.

definitions.note: simple past of „stemmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stemmte sich gegen die Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She braced herself against the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sterbe vor Hunger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dying of hunger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen sterben jedes Jahr an dieser Krankheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people die from this illness every year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alle Menschen sind sterblich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All people are mortal.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used for places, containers, or events that are extremely crowded.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus war sternhagelvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus was completely packed.

definitions.note: Slightly formal; common in written German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist stets pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is always punctual.

definitions.note: Often used for directing a vehicle/ship/plane, and more generally for controlling or regulating something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Pilot muss das Flugzeug bei starkem Wind vorsichtig steuern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pilot has to steer the airplane carefully in strong wind.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "stechen"; also used for pain like an insect bite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mückenstich sticht noch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mosquito bite still stings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Boden ist stickig, weil Saft darauf verschüttet wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floor is sticky because juice was spilled on it.

definitions.note: simple past of „einsteigen“ (often used with „in“: „stieg in“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stieg in den Bus und fuhr nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got on the bus and went home.

definitions.note: simple past of „steigen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rauch stieg schnell in die Luft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke rose quickly into the air.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stiegen auf den Berg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They climbed the mountain.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „stehlen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stiehlt ein Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He steals a bicycle.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „stoßen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stieß im Dunkeln gegen den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bumped into the table in the dark.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „stoßen“, often used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir stießen im Dunkeln gegen den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bumped into the table in the dark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist hier ganz still.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s completely quiet here.

definitions.note: Often means something is continuing ("still"), or emphasizes that something happens despite something else ("still").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte immer noch; er ist noch still.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still waiting; he’s still quiet.

definitions.note: Can describe doing something without noise or movement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sei still, das Baby schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be quiet; the baby is sleeping.

definitions.note: Used to tell someone (often children) to be quiet or keep still.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Still! Das Baby schläft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Quiet! The baby is sleeping.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (attributive). Don’t confuse with English “still” meaning “yet” (German: „noch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gingen durch eine stille Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked through a quiet street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie möchte ihr Baby stillen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to breastfeed her baby.

definitions.native: to satisfy, to quench (e.g., hunger, thirst)
definitions.note: Often used with "Hunger" or "Durst".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, seinen Durst zu stillen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is trying to quench his thirst.

definitions.note: Often used as an instruction (e.g., to a child or animal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte stillhalten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please stay still?

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ (e.g., „Ich stimme zu.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stimme dir zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree with you.

definitions.note: Used with the separable verb „zustimmen“ (e.g. „Ich stimme dir zu.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stimme dir zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree with you.

definitions.note: used when something (facts, numbers, a story, etc.) is correct or matches reality
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zahlen müssen stimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The numbers have to be correct.

definitions.note: often used with "für" (for) or "gegen" (against)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen für den Vorschlag stimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to vote for the proposal.

definitions.note: used for tuning musical instruments
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Gitarre stimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tune the guitar.

definitions.note: Used with "zu" (e.g., "jemandem/etwas zustimmen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stimmst du mir zu?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you agree with me?

definitions.note: Often used with a musical instrument (e.g., "die Gitarre stimmen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stimmst du die Gitarre?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you tuning the guitar?

definitions.note: Often used on its own: „Das stimmt.“ = “That’s right.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das stimmt nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s not correct.

definitions.note: Often used with „es“: „Das stimmt“ = “That’s right/That’s correct.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das stimmte nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That wasn’t correct.

definitions.note: Past tense, plural (and also polite "Sie") of "stimmen" in the sense of being in agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir stimmten dem Plan zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agreed to the plan.

definitions.note: Often also used informally to express strong disapproval (e.g., “Das stinkt!” = “That stinks!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Müll kann furchtbar stinken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trash can stink terribly.

definitions.note: Informal/emphatic; often sounds a bit rude or judgmental.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sind stinkreich und können sich jedes Auto leisten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are filthy rich and can afford any car.

definitions.note: informal; very strong emphasis (like “mad as hell”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war stinksauer, als er wieder zu spät kam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was furious when he was late again.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du stinkst nach Rauch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stink of smoke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Müll stinkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trash stinks.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative form of „sterben“.
