definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stirb nicht, bitte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t die, please!

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "sterben" (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du so schnell fährst, stirbst du noch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you drive that fast, you might die.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "sterben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Wasser stirbt die Pflanze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, the plant dies.

definitions.note: Used for emphasis; often with „es ist …“ or „stockdunkel sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Wald war es stockdunkel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the forest it was pitch-dark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stolpere oft auf unebenem Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often trip on uneven ground.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "stolpern"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stolperte über den Stein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tripped over the stone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin stolz auf dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m proud of you.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective ending (e.g., masculine nominative: „ein stolzer Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein stolzer Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a proud father.

definitions.note: Can also be the comparative form of „stolz“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute stolzer als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am prouder today than yesterday.

definitions.native: to stuff, to cram (something into something)
definitions.note: To fill something tightly by pushing material into it (e.g., a bag, pillow, mouth).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie muss den Koffer schnell stopfen, damit alles hineinpasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to stuff the suitcase quickly so that everything fits.

definitions.native: to plug, to stop up (an opening)
definitions.note: To block an opening or hole so nothing can pass through (e.g., a drain, crack, ear).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will den Abfluss mit einem Tuch stopfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to plug the drain with a cloth.

definitions.native: to darn, to mend (holes in fabric)
definitions.note: Common with clothing, especially socks: repairing holes by filling/stitching them.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Oma kann Socken stopfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma can darn socks.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "stopfen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stopfte das Loch mit Papier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stuffed the hole with paper.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation/command to tell someone to stop doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Stopp, hör auf damit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop, quit doing that!

definitions.note: Common colloquial short form of „stoppe“ (from „stoppen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warte kurz, ich stopp das Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a second, I’ll stop the car.

definitions.note: Often used for vehicles/machines or processes; for people, „aufhören“ is also very common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fahrer muss den Bus an der nächsten Haltestelle stoppen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The driver has to stop the bus at the next stop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus stoppt hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stops here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stottert, wenn er nervös ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stutters when he is nervous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigung, ich stoße dich nicht mit Absicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I’m not bumping into you on purpose.

definitions.note: often with an object; can also be used with a direction (e.g., in/gegen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Tür kräftig stoßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will push the door hard.

definitions.native: to bump into; to knock against
definitions.note: often with „gegen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Dunkeln kann man leicht gegen den Tisch stoßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the dark you can easily bump into the table.

definitions.note: a small push to get someone’s attention
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte stoßen Sie mich an, wenn der Zug ankommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please nudge me when the train arrives.

definitions.note: common with sounds (e.g., einen Schrei/einen Seufzer)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie musste einen Schrei stoßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She had to let out a scream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer will die Schüler nicht strafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher doesn't want to punish the students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne kann heute den ganzen Tag strahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun can shine all day today.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a bright glow (light, colors) or a very happy-looking smile.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat strahlende Augen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has radiant eyes.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „strahlen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne strahlte den ganzen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun shone all day.

definitions.note: Often used with: „nach“ + dative (e.g., „nach Erfolg streben“ = to strive for success).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen streben nach Erfolg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people strive for success.

definitions.note: Often used with "nach" + dative ("to strive for") or "zu" + dative ("to aspire to").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie strebt nach Erfolg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She strives for success.

definitions.note: Often used without the ending -e in informal speech (e.g., “ich streck …” instead of “ich strecke …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich streck die Beine aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stretch out my legs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Aufstehen muss ich mich strecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After getting up, I have to stretch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er streckte die Arme aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stretched out his arms.

definitions.note: Often used for gently petting an animal or caressing a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will die Katze streicheln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to pet the cat.

definitions.note: simple past of "streicheln"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie streichelte die Katze ganz vorsichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She petted the cat very gently.

definitions.note: often used for painting a wall or room with a brush or roller
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Zimmer streichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to paint the room.

definitions.note: used for removing something from a list, plan, or text
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten den letzten Punkt streichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should cross out (cancel) the last item.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er streicht die Wand weiß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He paints the wall white.

definitions.note: Often used for removing something from a list, schedule, or text.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie streicht den Termin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cancels the appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er streicht die Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pets the cat.

definitions.note: Often used for lightly touching something by accident while moving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beim Vorbeigehen kann es passieren, dass du jemanden mit dem Arm streifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As you walk past, it can happen that you brush someone with your arm.

definitions.note: Usually used with „mit“ (to argue with someone) or „über“ (to argue about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich streite oft mit meinem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often argue with my brother.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" ("sich streiten" = to argue/quarrel with each other).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir streiten oft über Kleinigkeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We often argue about little things.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "streiten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum streitest du immer mit deinem Bruder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you always argue with your brother?

definitions.note: often used with „mit“ + dative: „streitet mit jemandem“ = argues with someone
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er streitet oft mit seinem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often argues with his brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unser Lehrer ist sehr streng.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our teacher is very strict.

definitions.note: Often used with rules or requirements; also common in set phrases like „streng geheim“ (“top secret”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier ist das Rauchen streng verboten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoking is strictly forbidden here.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with feminine nouns (e.g., „eine strenge Lehrerin“) or as a plural form with „die“ (e.g., „die strengen Regeln“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Lehrerin ist sehr strenge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our teacher is very strict.

definitions.note: comparative form of "streng"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unser neuer Lehrer ist strenger als der alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our new teacher is stricter than the old one.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: sich anstrengen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er strengt sich in der Schule sehr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries very hard at school.

definitions.note: Simple past form of (sich) anstrengen; often used in writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich strengte mich an, alles zu verstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried hard to understand everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Woche vor der Prüfung war wirklich stressig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The week before the exam was really stressful.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (declension), e.g. before a noun like „eine stressige Woche“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hatte eine stressige Woche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a stressful week.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of „streuen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er streute Salz auf den Gehweg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sprinkled salt on the sidewalk.

definitions.note: simple past of „streichen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich strich das falsche Wort durch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I crossed out the wrong word.

definitions.note: simple past of „streichen“ (often with paint, using a brush or roller)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er strich die Wand weiß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He painted the wall white.

definitions.note: Not related to English “strike”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stricke einen Schal für meine Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m knitting a scarf for my sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Oma stricken jeden Winter warme Socken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma knits warm socks every winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie strickt einen Pullover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is knitting a sweater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen uns strikt an die Regeln halten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to stick strictly to the rules.

definitions.note: simple past of „abstreiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stritt die Vorwürfe ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He denied the accusations.

definitions.note: simple past of „streiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stritt mit seinem Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He argued with his brother.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „streiten“; used with plural subjects (we/you/they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stritten sich über das Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They argued about the money.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „streiten“; used with plural subjects (we/you/they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Teams stritten bis zum Schluss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two teams fought until the end.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „strömen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fluss strömte schnell nach dem starken Regen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river flowed quickly after the heavy rain.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich studiere Informatik an der Uni.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study computer science at the university.

definitions.note: Used especially for studying at a university or college.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde in Berlin studieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will study in Berlin.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (used with "du").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Studierst du heute Abend für die Prüfung?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you studying for the exam tonight?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er studiert Medizin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He studies medicine.

definitions.note: past participle, often used with "hat" (has) in the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat in Berlin studiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studied in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie studierte drei Jahre in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She studied in Berlin for three years.

definitions.note: Often used for people who cannot speak (“mute”), but also for things (e.g., a phone) that are set to make no sound (“silent”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Nachricht war er stumm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, he was speechless.

definitions.note: Used for things with no sharp edge/point; can also describe a dull sound or sensation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Messer ist stumpf und schneidet nicht mehr gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knife is blunt and doesn’t cut well anymore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben stundenlang gewartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We waited for hours.

definitions.note: often used for something done or paid in hourly units (e.g., hourly work)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie arbeitet stundenweise in einem Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works in a café by the hour.

definitions.note: Often used for people or animals that don’t want to do what they’re told.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Esel ist stur und bleibt stehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The donkey is stubborn and stays put.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mehr ich ihn bitte, desto sturer wird er.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The more I ask him, the more stubborn he becomes.

definitions.note: informal/colloquial and strongly emphatic
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war nach der Party sturzbetrunken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was extremely drunk after the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ständig am Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is constantly on his phone.

definitions.note: Adjective in masculine nominative or masculine/neuter genitive form, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein ständiger Besucher unseres Cafés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a constant visitor to our café.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Regelmäßiges Training kann die Muskeln stärken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Regular training can strengthen the muscles.

definitions.note: comparative form of „stark“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute fühle ich mich stärker als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I feel stronger than yesterday.

definitions.note: comparative form of „stark“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute stärker als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am stronger today than yesterday.

definitions.note: superlative form of „stark“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die stärkste Mannschaft der Liga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the strongest team in the league.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stöhnt vor Schmerzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He groans in pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stöhnte vor Schmerz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He groaned in pain.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „nicht stören“ (“do not disturb”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigung, störe ich gerade?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, am I disturbing you right now?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht stören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please do not disturb.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "stören".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du störst mich gerade beim Lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're disturbing me while I'm studying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es stört mich, wenn du so laut bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It bothers me when you are so loud.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „stören“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm störte mich beim Lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise bothered me while I was studying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stößt die Tür auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushes the door open.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of "stehen", used for hypotheticals and polite/indirect statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne den Wind stünde die Kerze noch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without the wind, the candle would still be standing.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form (used for hypotheticals/conditional statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Wasser stürbe die Pflanze schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, the plant would die quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es an der Küste sehr stürmisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s very stormy on the coast.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „stürmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er stürmte aus dem Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stormed out of the room.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „stürmen“ for „wir/sie/Sie“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fans stürmten nach dem Spiel auf das Feld.

definitions.note: feminine form of the adjective (used before a feminine noun, e.g. „eine tiefe …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine tiefe Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a deep pocket.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „tief“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen durch den tiefen Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk through the deep forest.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „tief“ (deep/low).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der See ist hier tiefer als dort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lake is deeper here than there.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Taucher schwamm tiefer, weil er etwas auf dem Meeresboden sah.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The diver swam deeper because he saw something on the seabed.

definitions.note: superlative form of „tief“ (deep)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der tiefste Punkt im See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the deepest point in the lake.

definitions.note: superlative form of „tief“ (e.g. „am tiefsten“ = deepest)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der See ist an dieser Stelle am tiefsten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lake is deepest at this spot.

definitions.note: Often used for debts (e.g., a loan or mortgage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich tilge jeden Monat einen Teil meines Kredits.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pay off part of my loan every month.

definitions.note: Often used for typing on a keyboard or phone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich tippen eine Nachricht auf meinem Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m typing a message on my phone.

definitions.note: Interjection used to express resignation, uncertainty, or a reluctant acceptance (often like “oh well”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tja, da kann man nichts machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, there’s nothing you can do about that.

definitions.note: Often used for children playing very loudly and energetically, or for storms/violence "raging."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder toben im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are romping in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm tobt schon die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm has been raging all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Eltern sind sehr tolerant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents are very tolerant.

definitions.note: Informal; very common in spoken German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war toll!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was great!

definitions.note: Common in spoken German to express enthusiasm.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist toll!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s awesome!

definitions.note: Used to express enthusiasm or approval (often like “awesome!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Toll, das hast du geschafft!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Great, you did it!

definitions.note: Adjective form of "toll"; often used informally to express enthusiasm.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine tolle Idee!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a great idea!

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective used before a noun (e.g., after "einen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten einen tollen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a great day.

definitions.note: Informal/common in spoken German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein toller Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a great movie.

definitions.note: Often used to express that something is getting out of control or surprising.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm wird immer toller.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise is getting crazier and crazier.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a neuter noun (often after an article like „ein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein tolles Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a great present.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen war top.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was great.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vogel ist tot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird is dead.

definitions.note: informal; common in spoken German
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin total müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m totally tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine totale Überraschung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a total surprise.

definitions.note: Adjective in masculine nominative singular (or genitive singular, or plural dative) form of "total".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein totaler Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a total mistake.

definitions.note: Adjective form of „tot“ used before a noun (e.g., feminine singular or plural, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Da liegt eine tote Katze auf der Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a dead cat lying in the street.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „tot“ (e.g., plural or after certain articles/prepositions)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben die toten Fische aus dem Teich geholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took the dead fish out of the pond.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a masculine noun (e.g., „ein toter Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein toter Vogel liegt auf der Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A dead bird is lying on the street.

definitions.note: Colloquial exaggeration meaning you laughed very hard.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich über den Witz totgelacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I laughed myself to death at the joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er drohte, ihn totzuschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threatened to beat him to death.

definitions.note: simple past of "treffen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich traf gestern meine Freundin in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met my friend in town yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past of "treffen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball traf das Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball hit the window.

definitions.note: simple past of „treffen“ (used with wir/ihr/sie/Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir trafen uns gestern im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We met yesterday in the park.

definitions.note: simple past of „treffen“ (used with wir/ihr/sie/Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bälle trafen das Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balls hit the window.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command) of "tragen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trag bitte den Koffer ins Auto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please carry the suitcase into the car!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of "tragen" ("I carry / I wear").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage heute eine Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing a jacket today.

definitions.note: Commonly used for carrying something (often on/with your body or in your hands) or wearing clothing/accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Tasche nach Hause tragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to carry the bag home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unfall war tragisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accident was tragic.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with a noun (e.g., after “eine”, “die”, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine tragische Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a tragic story.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in declined form (e.g., with a masculine accusative noun or a plural dative noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir erinnern uns an den tragischen Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We remember the tragic accident.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "tragen" (er/sie/es).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er tragt heute eine Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is wearing a jacket today.

definitions.note: 1st person singular (I)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trainiere dreimal pro Woche im Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I train three times a week at the gym.

definitions.native: to train; to work out; to practice (a skill)
definitions.note: Common for sports/fitness and for practicing skills; also used in the sense of coaching/training someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde für den Marathon trainieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to train for the marathon.

definitions.note: Used with a direct object when you train a person/team/animal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Trainer wird die Mannschaft diese Woche intensiver trainieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coach will train the team more intensely this week.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du trainierst heute Abend im Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You train at the gym this evening.

definitions.note: present tense (he/she/it); can also be a past participle depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trainiert jeden Morgen im Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He trains at the gym every morning.

definitions.note: simple past form of „trinken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern trank ich Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I drank coffee.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „trinken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Spiel tranken wir zusammen ein Bier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the game, we drank a beer together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Kisten morgen in die neue Wohnung transportieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to transport the boxes to the new apartment tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der LKW transportiert die Möbel in die neue Wohnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck transports the furniture to the new apartment.

definitions.note: Simple past of „auftreten“; often used with the separable prefix „auf“ (e.g., „trat … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich trat sie vor der Tür auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly she appeared in front of the door.

definitions.note: Simple past of „auftreten“; often used with the separable prefix „auf“ (e.g., „trat … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Während der Reise trat ein Problem auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the trip, a problem occurred.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „eintreten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trat leise in das Zimmer ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She quietly entered the room.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „eintreten“ (often used for events or situations)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück trat kein Problem ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, no problem occurred.

definitions.note: simple past of "treten"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trat dir auf den Fuß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stepped on your foot.

definitions.note: Past tense form used with the separable verb „zurücktreten“ (e.g. „trat … zurück“), often about resigning from a job or office.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Minister trat gestern zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The minister stepped down yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite), plural of „treten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie traten ins Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They stepped into the room.

definitions.note: informal; common in Austria and southern Germany
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie tratscht gern über die Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She likes to gossip about the neighbors.

definitions.note: Commonly used without the ending -e in spoken German ("ich trau" = "ich traue").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trau dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" (e.g., "ich trau mich" = "ich traue mich").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trau mich nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t dare.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (e.g. „Ich traue dir.“ = “I trust you.”). Not related to English “true.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich traue dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative person: jemandem trauen = to trust someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst mir trauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can trust me.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich trauen = to dare (to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich trauen, das zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to dare to say that.

definitions.note: Often used with „um“ + accusative: „um jemanden trauern“ = to mourn someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie werden lange um ihren Vater trauern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will mourn their father for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ausblick von hier ist traumhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view from here is dreamlike.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute traurig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am sad today.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (declension), e.g. after an article like „eine“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine traurige Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a sad story.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (attributive form), e.g. after words like "den/einen/keinen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den traurigen Jungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the sad boy.

definitions.note: Comparative form of the adjective „traurig“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute bin ich trauriger als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I am sadder than yesterday.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "traurig" used before a neuter noun (e.g., "ein trauriges ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein trauriges Lied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a sad song.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das waren die traurigsten Tage meines Lebens.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those were the saddest days of my life.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß, dass du mir traust.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know that you trust me.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object (e.g. jemandem trauen = to trust someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er traut ihm nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t trust him.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich trauen (to dare).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie traut sich, die Lehrerin zu fragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dares to ask the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich traute ihm nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't trust him.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive form: sich trauen (to dare).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie traute sich, vor allen zu sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dared to speak in front of everyone.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "treffen" (ich treffe = I meet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich treffe heute Abend meine Freunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm meeting my friends this evening.

definitions.note: Used for meeting people (planned or by arrangement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich treffe heute meine Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m meeting my friend today.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (ihr) form of "treffen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trefft ihr euch heute Abend?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you meeting up tonight?

definitions.note: Often used with "Sport" ("Sport treiben" = to do sports/exercise).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich treibe jeden Morgen Sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do sports/exercise every morning.

definitions.note: Used for forcing something to move (e.g., wind, water, or an external force).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind treibe das Boot ans Ufer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind drives the boat to the shore.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase „Sport treiben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute Sport treiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to do sports today.

definitions.note: Often used for forces like wind or water moving something along.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind kann das Boot ans Ufer treiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind can drive the boat to the shore.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "treiben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum treibst du so viel Sport?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you do so much sport?

definitions.note: Often used with objects like "Sport" (do sport) or "Handel" (do trade), or with "es" as a dummy subject (e.g., "Was treibt dich hierher?" = what brings you here?).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er treibt viel Sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He does a lot of sport.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" ("sich trennen") to mean "to break up" or "to separate" (as a couple).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir trennen den Müll nach Papier, Glas und Plastik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We separate the trash into paper, glass, and plastic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trennt den Müll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He separates the trash.

definitions.note: Can also mean “broke up” when talking about a relationship.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trennte das Papier in zwei Teile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She separated the paper into two parts.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "trennen" for "we/you(pl)/they"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie trennten sich nach dem Streit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They separated after the argument.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trete vorsichtig auf den nassen Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I step carefully onto the wet ground.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trete den Ball ins Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kick the ball into the goal.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „ein-“ (eintreten): „treten … ein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte treten Sie ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come in.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" + accusative (e.g. "auf etwas treten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht auf das Gras treten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t step on the grass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann den Ball sehr weit treten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can kick the ball very far.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr tretet den Ball ins Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You kick the ball into the goal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist seiner Freundin treu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is loyal to his girlfriend.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „bleiben“ (to remain) or „sein“ (to be) to express loyalty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er bleibt ihr treu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He remains faithful to her.

definitions.note: Often describes someone who stays committed to a person, friend, team, etc. Can look like English “true,” but usually means “loyal/faithful.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich danke meinen treuen Freunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thank my loyal friends.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „treiben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind trieb das Boot ans Ufer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind drove the boat to the shore.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „treiben“, often used with „Sport“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trieb jeden Morgen Sport.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did sports every morning.

definitions.note: informal singular command (to one person: du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Triff mich morgen im Café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Meet me tomorrow at the café.

definitions.note: informal singular command (to one person: du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Triff den Ball mit dem Schläger!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hit the ball with the racket!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du triffst heute deine Freunde im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You meet your friends in the park today.

definitions.note: Often used for hitting a target (e.g., in sports or games).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du triffst den Ball mit dem Fuß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You hit the ball with your foot.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "treffen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trifft seine Freunde nach der Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He meets his friends after work.

definitions.note: Also used for hitting a target (literal or figurative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ball trifft das Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball hits the window.

definitions.note: informal imperative (command) to one person: “Drink!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trink bitte mehr Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please drink more water.

definitions.note: colloquial short form of “ich trinke” (often without the -e).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trink keinen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t drink coffee.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present tense of „trinken“ (used with „ich“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke jeden Morgen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink coffee every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinken Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink water.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "trinken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du trinkst heute nur Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re only drinking water today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "trinken".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trinkt jeden Morgen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drinks coffee every morning.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „auftreten“; often used with „auf“ (e.g., „tritt … auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Problem tritt heute wieder auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem occurs again today.

definitions.note: from the verb „eintreten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er tritt ins Zimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He enters the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er tritt auf den Fuß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He steps on the foot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie tritt den Ball ins Tor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kicks the ball into the goal.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of "treten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du trittst auf das Pedal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You step on the pedal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wäsche ist schon trocken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The laundry is already dry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die trockene Luft macht meine Haut spröde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dry air makes my skin chapped.

definitions.note: neuter singular adjective ending (e.g., before a neuter noun like "Brot")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich esse trockenes Brot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I eat dry bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trockne meine Hände mit einem Handtuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dry my hands with a towel.

definitions.note: Can be used both intransitively (to become dry) and transitively (to dry something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lasse die Wäsche auf dem Balkon trocknen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I let the laundry dry on the balcony.

definitions.note: third-person singular present of "trocknen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wäsche trocknet draußen in der Sonne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The laundry dries outside in the sun.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „trocknen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trocknete die Wäsche auf dem Balkon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dried the laundry on the balcony.

definitions.note: simple past of "trommeln"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trommelte den Rhythmus mit den Fingern auf den Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drummed the rhythm on the table with his fingers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wasserhahn tropft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The faucet is dripping.

definitions.note: Used with the genitive in formal German; in everyday speech it’s often followed by the dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trotz des Regens gehen wir spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the rain, we’re going for a walk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat geregnet, aber wir sind trotzdem spazieren gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained, but we still went for a walk.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the dative ("trotzen + Dativ").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie muss dem Sturm trotzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to withstand the storm.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „tragen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trug eine schwere Tasche nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He carried a heavy bag home.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „tragen“ (wir/sie/Sie).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir trugen die Kisten in die Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We carried the boxes into the kitchen.

definitions.note: often implies being slow or lacking energy/motivation
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute zu träge, um aufzuräumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m too lazy to tidy up.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "tragen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du trägst heute eine Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re wearing a jacket today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of "tragen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du trägst die Kiste nach oben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You carry the box upstairs.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „tragen“; also used for “to bear/support” (e.g., costs or weight) in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er trägt jeden Tag eine Brille.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wears glasses every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Regen tränkte meine Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain soaked my jacket.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular imperative (“Dream!”). It can also be a colloquial shortened form of “ich träume” (“I dream”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Träum süß!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dream sweetly!

definitions.note: present tense: “I dream” (can also be used as an imperative “dream!”, depending on context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich träume oft von einer Reise ans Meer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often dream about a trip to the sea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute Nacht träumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will dream tonight.

definitions.note: 2nd-person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Träumst du manchmal von fliegen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you sometimes dream about flying?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „träumen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er träumt von einem Haus am Meer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dreams of a house by the sea.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „träumen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzte Nacht träumte ich von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night I dreamed about you.

definitions.note: Often used when someone is being slow and wasting time (e.g., when you want them to hurry up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf zu trödeln, wir müssen los!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop dawdling, we have to go!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, sie zu trösten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to comfort her.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „trösten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie tröstete das Kind nach dem Sturz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She comforted the child after the fall.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Okay, ich muss los — tschüs!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, I have to go — bye!

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Okay, ich muss los — tschüss!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Okay, I have to go — bye!

definitions.note: Colloquial form of standard German „tue“ (1st person singular of „tun“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich tu das später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll do that later.

definitions.note: Singular imperative of "tun" (used to tell one person to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu das bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please do that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich tue mein Bestes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I do my best.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das heute tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do that today.

definitions.note: often implies whispering secretly, especially about someone nearby
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Während der Rede tuschelten die Schüler in der letzten Reihe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the speech, the students in the last row whispered.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of "tun".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was tust du gerade?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing right now?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „tun“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er tut so, als wüsste er nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pretends as if he doesn’t know anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist typisch für Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is typical for Berlin.

definitions.note: comparative form of "typisch" (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein typischer Fall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a more typical case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mache täglich einen Spaziergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go for a walk every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke täglich zwei Tassen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink two cups of coffee every day.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of "tun", used for hypothetical/conditional situations or polite suggestions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich täte das, wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would do that if I had more time.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II plural ("wir/sie/Sie täten"); used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir täten das sofort, wenn wir mehr Zeit hätten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would do that right away if we had more time.

definitions.note: Second person singular (du), subjunctive II (Konjunktiv II), used for hypothetical situations or polite phrasing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du mehr Zeit hättest, tätest du das sicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had more time, you would definitely do that.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive II), 2nd person plural (ihr).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ihr mehr Zeit hättet, tätet ihr öfter kochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had more time, you would cook more often.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g. beruflich tätig = employed/working in a profession).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist als Lehrerin tätig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She works as a teacher.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts for transactions (e.g., a payment, purchase, transfer, investment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir tätigen heute eine Überweisung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are making a bank transfer today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mir einen kleinen Stern auf den Arm tätowieren lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to have a small star tattooed on my arm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst mich nicht täuschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not deceive me.

definitions.note: Often used with “jemanden täuschen” (to deceive someone) or reflexively “sich täuschen” (to be mistaken).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will mich täuschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to deceive me.

definitions.note: Used reflexively: “sich täuschen”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mich täuschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I might be mistaken.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "täuschen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er täuschte seine Freunde mit einer erfundenen Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deceived his friends with a made-up story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kann tödlich sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That can be deadly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde tödlich verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was fatally injured.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine tödliche Krankheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a deadly disease.

definitions.note: Rather formal/old-fashioned; can sound judgmental.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wäre töricht, jetzt aufzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It would be foolish to give up now.

definitions.note: Describes an action/idea as unwise; somewhat old-fashioned or formal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine törichte Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a foolish idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich töte keine Tiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't kill animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man darf keine Tiere töten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One must not kill animals.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum tötest du die Spinne?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you killing the spider?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Täter tötet das Opfer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrator kills the victim.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „töten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann tötete die Schlange im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man killed the snake in the garden.

definitions.note: Used as a hesitation sound while thinking or searching for words.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ähm, uh, ich weiß nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Um, uh, I don't know.

definitions.note: Used with the accusative; often indicates movement around something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen um den See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk around the lake.

definitions.note: Used with the accusative for clock times.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs beginnt um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course starts at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Often used as a separable verb particle (e.g. sich umsehen = to look around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schaue mich um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I look around.

definitions.note: Used with the accusative (e.g., um den Park).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir laufen um den Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking around the park.

definitions.note: Used when telling time (e.g., um drei Uhr).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug kommt um 8 Uhr an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train arrives at 8 o’clock.

definitions.native: in order to, so as to
definitions.note: Used in the purpose construction „um … zu“ + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne Deutsch, um in Deutschland zu arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning German in order to work in Germany.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I hug") or imperative ("hug!", informal singular), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm her, ich umarme dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, I’ll hug you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will ihre Freundin zum Abschied umarmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to hug her friend goodbye.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie umarmt ihre Freundin zur Begrüßung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She hugs her friend to say hello.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „umarmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er umarmte seine Freundin zum Abschied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hugged his girlfriend goodbye.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 1st/3rd person plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als wir uns verabschiedeten, umarmten wir uns lange.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we said goodbye, we hugged for a long time.

definitions.note: often implies killing intentionally; can also be used informally to mean “to wear someone out” in some contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will ihn umbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to kill him.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du ihn umbringst, kommst du ins Gefängnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you kill him, you’ll go to prison.

definitions.note: In main clauses, the prefix often separates: „bringt … um“. The combined form „umbringt“ is common in subordinate clauses (e.g. with „dass“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaube, dass er ihn umbringt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think that he is killing him.

definitions.native: to turn around, to turn over
definitions.note: Often used with a separable prefix: Ich drehe mich um. / Ich drehe das Buch um.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du dich bitte umdrehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn around?

definitions.note: This meaning is usually the inseparable verb (stress on the second part: umFAHren).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, dass du niemanden umfahren kannst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful that you don’t run anyone over.

definitions.native: to drive around, to go around (avoid)
definitions.note: This meaning is usually the separable verb (stress on the first part: UMfahren).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Baustelle umfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to drive around the construction site.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Vase ist vom Tisch umfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vase fell off the table.

definitions.note: used when a person loses consciousness (often briefly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir war schwindlig, und ich bin fast umfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt dizzy, and I almost fainted.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (er/sie/es umfasst).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis umfasst Frühstück und WLAN.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price includes breakfast and Wi‑Fi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Garten ist von einer hohen Mauer umgeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden is surrounded by a high wall.

definitions.note: past participle of "umbringen"; often used in the perfect tense with "haben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat den Täter gestern festgenommen, weil er einen Mann umgebracht hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the perpetrator yesterday because he killed a man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Bild ist umgedreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The picture is turned around.

definitions.note: Past participle of the separable verb „umfahren“ (to run someone/something over).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Radfahrer umgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ran over the cyclist.

definitions.note: past participle of „umfallen“; commonly used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Baum ist im Sturm umgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tree fell over in the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind hat den Mülleimer umgehauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind knocked over the trash can.

definitions.note: Colloquial, used to mean someone is very impressed or amazed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert hat mich umgehauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert really blew me away.

definitions.note: Often used with "mit": "mit etwas/jemandem umgehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kann gut mit Stress umgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She can handle stress well.

definitions.native: to avoid, to bypass, to go around
definitions.note: Can mean avoiding a rule/problem or physically going around an obstacle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Stau umgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to bypass the traffic jam.

definitions.native: to spread, to be going around
definitions.note: Also used for rumors, news, or illnesses; commonly phrased as "(etwas) umgehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Schule kann ein Gerücht schnell umgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At school, a rumor can spread quickly.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., emails, announcements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte antworten Sie umgehend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please reply immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hilfst mir, und ich helfe dir umgekehrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You help me, and I help you the other way around.

definitions.note: Attributive form of „umgekehrt“ (used before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gingen den umgekehrte Weg zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went back the opposite way.

definitions.note: Often used for an unnatural, sudden, or accidental death; typically used with the auxiliary verb "sein" ("ist umgekommen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dem Unfall ist ein Mann umgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A man died in the accident.

definitions.note: Often used with things like a switch or lever: „den Schalter/Hebel umlegen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Lichtschalter umgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He flipped the light switch.

definitions.note: Common in formal contexts (e.g., costs): „Kosten auf jemanden umlegen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kosten werden auf die Mieter umgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The costs are passed on to the tenants.

definitions.note: Often used when something is knocked over by force (e.g., wind).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Baum wurde vom Wind umgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tree was knocked down by the wind.

definitions.note: Past participle of "umsetzen"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben den Plan umgesetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We implemented the plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Möbel wurden umgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The furniture was rearranged.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of "umziehen" with "sein" when talking about moving to a new home/place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind letztes Jahr nach Hamburg umgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We moved to Hamburg last year.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of "umziehen" with "haben" (often with "sich") when talking about changing clothes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich nach dem Sport schnell umgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed quickly after спорт.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „umgeben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Gartenzaun umgibt das Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden fence surrounds the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, dass du die Vase nicht umhauen wirst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful you won’t knock the vase over.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Boxer kann seinen Gegner mit einem Schlag umhauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boxer can knock his opponent out with one punch.

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Konzert kann mich total umhauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert can really blow me away.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“, „laufen“, „schauen“ to mean moving or looking around (e.g. „umhergehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder laufen im Park umher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are running around in the park.

definitions.note: Used almost only in the phrase „nicht umhin können“ (= can’t avoid / can’t help doing something), usually with „zu“ + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich konnte nicht umhin, zu lachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn’t help laughing.

definitions.native: to turn around, to turn back
definitions.note: Often used when you go back the way you came; separable verb (e.g. „Wir kehren um.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen umkehren, der Weg ist gesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to turn back; the path is blocked.

definitions.note: Used for changing order or direction (e.g. reversing a sequence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man kann die Reihenfolge umkehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can reverse the order.

definitions.note: Often used for dying in an accident, disaster, or other tragic event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dem Unfall sind drei Menschen umkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Three people died in the accident.

definitions.note: Usually used with a direct object (something that is being orbited/circled): etw. umkreisen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mond kann die Erde in etwa 27 Tagen umkreisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The moon can orbit the Earth in about 27 days.

definitions.native: to put on (around), to wrap around
definitions.note: Often used with an object: sich etwas umlegen (e.g., a scarf around your neck).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mir den Schal umlegen, es ist kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to put on my scarf; it’s cold.

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial, especially in phrases like jemanden umlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei will den Täter lebend fassen und ihn nicht umlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police want to catch the perpetrator alive and not kill him.

definitions.native: puts on, puts around (e.g. a scarf)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zieht die Jacke an und umlegt den Schal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He puts on the jacket and puts the scarf around (his neck).

definitions.note: Contraction of "um das" or "um die" (colloquial/commonly used in speech and informal writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen ums Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk around the house.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich umschauen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mich umschauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to look around.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as „sich umsehen“ (= to look around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe mich im Laden um und kann mich nicht entscheiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I look around in the store and can’t decide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Plan umsetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to implement the plan.

definitions.note: Used in comparisons, often with "je ... desto/umso ..." ("the ... the ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Je mehr ich übe, umso besser werde ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The more I practice, the better I get.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eintritt ist heute umsonst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suche war umsonst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The search was in vain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eintritt ist heute umsonst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe umsonst auf den Bus gewartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited for the bus in vain.

definitions.note: Used especially for switching from one train/bus/tram/plane to another during a trip.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss in Frankfurt umsteigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change trains in Frankfurt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei umstellt das Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police surround the house.

definitions.note: often used for moving things (like furniture) into a different position
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie umstellt die Möbel im Wohnzimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She rearranges the furniture in the living room.

definitions.native: to change (someone’s) mind; to persuade (someone) to reconsider
definitions.note: Often used with an object in the accusative (jdn. umstimmen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, ihn umstimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to change his mind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Plan ist sehr umstritten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new plan is very controversial.

definitions.note: Often used for exchanging something you bought (e.g., in a store), like exchanging it for a different size or getting a replacement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte das T-Shirt umtauschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to exchange the T-shirt.

definitions.native: to knock over, to tip over
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind kann den Baum umwerfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind can knock the tree over.

definitions.note: Often used for a very positive, impressive effect (e.g., appearance, performance, impression).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kleid sieht umwerfend aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dress looks stunning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kleid sieht umwerfend aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dress looks stunning.

definitions.native: to move (house), to move (to a new place)
definitions.note: Used for changing where you live (moving apartments/houses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen nächsten Monat nach Berlin umziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to move to Berlin next month.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich umziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich schnell umziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change clothes quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt ist umzingelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is surrounded.

definitions.note: Infinitive with "zu" (used after certain verbs, e.g., "versuchen", "vergessen", "vorhaben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat versucht, die Fliege umzubringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to kill the fly.

definitions.note: Used as a "zu"-infinitive (e.g., after verbs like lernen, versuchen, anfangen); commonly with "mit" + dative ("mit Stress umgehen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne, besser mit Stress umzugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning to deal with stress better.

definitions.note: As a "zu"-infinitive, often implies intentionally finding a way around something (e.g., rules, restrictions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, mit den Regeln so umzugehen, dass er sie praktisch umzugehen lernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to handle the rules in such a way that he effectively learns to get around them.

definitions.native: to turn back, to turn around
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen umzukehren, weil der Weg gesperrt ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to turn back because the path is blocked.
