definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir planen, nächstes Jahr in eine größere Wohnung umzuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re planning to move into a bigger apartment next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit, mich umzuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time to change clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie möchte finanziell unabhängig sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to be financially independent.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine noun (e.g., „ein unabhängiger Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein unabhängiger Journalist berichtet über den Skandal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An independent journalist reports on the scandal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Kommentar war unangebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your comment was inappropriate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Situation war sehr unangenehm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation was very unpleasant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Angebot ist für uns unannehmbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This offer is unacceptable to us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine unanständige Bemerkung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an indecent remark.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Menschenwürde ist unantastbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Human dignity is inviolable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eingang ist sehr unauffällig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The entrance is very inconspicuous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verhielt sich unauffällig und sagte fast nichts.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She behaved inconspicuously and said almost nothing.

definitions.note: Often used for something that keeps going without a break, sometimes with a negative/complaining tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es regnet heute unaufhörlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s been raining nonstop today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Konflikt war unaufhaltsam und letztlich unausweichlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conflict was unstoppable and ultimately inevitable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine E-Mail ist noch unbeantwortet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My email is still unanswered.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong intention or insistence ("I really must / I definitely want to").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dich unbedingt anrufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I definitely have to call you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie blieb unbeeindruckt von seiner Entschuldigung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She remained unimpressed by his apology.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Angst ist unbegründet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fear is unfounded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wirkte beim Tanzen etwas unbeholfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seemed a bit clumsy while dancing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Nummer ist mir unbekannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This number is unknown to me.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „unbekannt“ (used with a noun, e.g., „einen unbekannten Mann“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei sucht einen unbekannten Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are looking for an unknown man.

definitions.note: Used as a nominalized adjective (an adjective used like a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte etwas Unbekanntes probieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to try something unknown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Lehrer ist in der Klasse sehr unbeliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new teacher is very unpopular in the class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ging unbemerkt aus dem Raum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the room unnoticed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Stuhl ist sehr unbequem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chair is very uncomfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Chef ist unberechenbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new boss is unpredictable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist noch unberührt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is still untouched.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ausblick von hier oben ist unbeschreiblich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view from up here is indescribable.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" or "sich fühlen" to mean being without worries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wirkt heute ganz unbesorgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She seems completely carefree today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann war unbewaffnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was unarmed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist seit Jahren unbewohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house has been uninhabited for years.

definitions.note: Often used for something so valuable or meaningful that money can’t buy it; can also mean “unaffordable.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeit mit meiner Familie ist unbezahlbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The time with my family is priceless.

definitions.note: adjective in inflected form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat einen unbrechbaren Willen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has an unbreakable will.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke Kaffee und esse ein Brötchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink coffee and eat a bread roll.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dass er absichtlich gelogen hat, ist für mich undenkbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That he lied on purpose is unthinkable for me.

definitions.note: Often used for things like pipes, roofs, windows, or containers that let liquid (or sometimes air) through.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Dach ist undicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof is leaky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wäre unehrlich, das Geld zu behalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It would be dishonest to keep the money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat uns uneigennützig geholfen, ohne etwas dafür zu erwarten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She helped us selflessly, without expecting anything in return.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Möglichkeiten scheinen unendlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The possibilities seem endless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir könnten unendlich lange darüber reden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We could talk about it endlessly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch unentschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still undecided.

definitions.note: Used especially for the result of a game or match when neither side wins.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Spiel endete unentschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game ended in a draw.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something keeps happening without a break (can sound slightly annoyed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat unentwegt geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained nonstop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in diesem Job noch unerfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still inexperienced in this job.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong disapproval (“outrageous”) or strong surprise (“unbelievable”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ja unerhört!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s outrageous!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist für das Team unersetzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is irreplaceable for the team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm war unerträglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise was unbearable.

definitions.note: Often used to intensify an adjective or situation (e.g., heat, pain, noise).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es unerträglich heiß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is unbearably hot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Besuch kam völlig unerwartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The visit was completely unexpected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unerwartet kam ein starker Sturm auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unexpectedly, a strong storm came up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir bekamen eine unerwartete Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got an unexpected message.

definitions.note: adjective used in a declined form (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des unerwarteten Regens sind wir zu Hause geblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the unexpected rain, we stayed at home.

definitions.note: Neuter form; often used as a substantivized adjective meaning “something unexpected.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Etwas Unerwartetes ist passiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something unexpected happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist unfair.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is unfair.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with feminine nouns (e.g., „eine unfaire Entscheidung“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine unfaire Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an unfair decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht war einfach unfassbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was simply unbelievable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hält den Chef für unfehlbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He considers the boss infallible.

definitions.note: Often used for something that works reliably (e.g., a method, a plan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein unfehlbarer Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a sure plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verkäufer war sehr unfreundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The salesperson was very unfriendly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Operation war sie unfruchtbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the operation, she was infertile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin unfähig, das allein zu schaffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am unable to manage that alone.

definitions.note: adjective form; often used before a noun (e.g., "ungarische Küche")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag ungarische Küche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like Hungarian cuisine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin ungeduldig, weil der Bus schon wieder zu spät ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m impatient because the bus is late again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in ungefähr zehn Minuten da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be there in about ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Keine Sorge, der Hund ist ungefährlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, the dog is harmless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er antwortete ungehalten auf die Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He answered the question in an annoyed way.

definitions.note: Used as an intensifier (stronger than „sehr“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ungeheuer wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is extremely important.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ungerecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is unfair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde ungerecht behandelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was treated unfairly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe dir ungern bei den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help you with your homework reluctantly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin so ungeschickt und habe das Glas fallen lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m so clumsy and dropped the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist heute ungeschminkt zur Arbeit gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went to work today without makeup.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is said very directly, without softening or sugarcoating it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagte ihr seine Meinung ungeschminkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He told her his opinion bluntly.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „bleiben“ (to remain) or „davonkommen“ (to get away with it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blieb für die Tat ungestraft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He remained unpunished for the act.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir konnten ungestört arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were able to work undisturbed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zu viel Zucker ist ungesund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Too much sugar is unhealthy.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „ungeteilte Aufmerksamkeit“ (= full/undivided attention).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche deine ungeteilte Aufmerksamkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your undivided attention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein ungewöhnlich warmer Tag für Januar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s an unusually warm day for January.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist aber ungewöhnlich kalt für April.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: But that’s unusually cold for April.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (attributive); ending changes with gender/case
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine ungewöhnliche Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s an unusual idea.

definitions.note: Often used after words like "etwas" (something): "etwas Ungewöhnliches/ungewöhnliches".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe etwas ungewöhnliches gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw something unusual.

definitions.note: Often used to describe children or a child’s behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind heute besonders ungezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are especially naughty today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist unglaublich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s unbelievable!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist unglaublich teuer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is incredibly expensive!

definitions.note: Often used to mean “amazing” in a positive sense, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine unglaubliche Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an incredible story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine unglaubliche Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an incredible story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein unglaublicher Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an incredible day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sah mich ungläubig an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked at me incredulously.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute unglücklich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m unhappy today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unglücklicherweise habe ich heute keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I don’t have time today.

definitions.note: Form of the adjective used with neuter nouns (e.g., ein unglückliches Kind / ein unglückliches Ereignis).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein unglückliches Missverständnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an unfortunate misunderstanding.

definitions.note: Often used with neuter nouns like „Gefühl“ (e.g. „ein ungutes Gefühl“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein ungutes Gefühl dabei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a bad feeling about it.

definitions.note: often used for tickets, IDs, documents, passwords, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fahrschein ist ungültig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket is invalid.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something that makes you feel uneasy or scared.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wald ist nachts unheimlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The forest is creepy at night.

definitions.note: Often used informally as an intensifier (like “super”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist unheimlich wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is incredibly important.

definitions.note: Used when something feels scary or unsettling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war unheimlich still im Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was eerily quiet in the house.

definitions.note: Adjective used with a noun (declined form); often describes something that feels unsettling or scary in a strange way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine unheimliche Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a creepy story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist unhöflich, beim Essen laut zu sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s rude to speak loudly while eating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich uninteressant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really uninteresting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Anweisungen sind unklar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions are unclear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war unklug, so viel Geld auszugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was unwise to spend so much money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist unlogisch, jetzt aufzuhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s illogical to stop now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme unmittelbar nach dem Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming immediately after the meal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist unmoralisch, Menschen zu belügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is immoral to lie to people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist unmöglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is impossible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne deinen Schlüssel ist es unmöglich, die Tür zu öffnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without your key, it’s impossible to open the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Diskussion ist unnötig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This discussion is unnecessary.

definitions.note: attributive form (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine unnötige Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was an unnecessary question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein unnützes Werkzeug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a useless tool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Zimmer ist unordentlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His room is messy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Schreibtisch ist total unorganisiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My desk is totally disorganized.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Richterin muss unparteiisch bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge must remain impartial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Kommentar war unpassend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His comment was inappropriate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan ist unrealistisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan is unrealistic.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „jemandem Unrecht tun“ (to do someone wrong).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist Unrecht, jemanden wegen seiner Herkunft zu benachteiligen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is wrong to disadvantage someone because of their background.

definitions.note: used for fruit/food that is not ripe yet
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bananen sind noch unreif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bananas are still unripe.

definitions.note: used for people/behavior; can be critical
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich finde sein Verhalten unreif.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find his behavior immature.

definitions.note: Often used for people who can’t sit still or who feel worried/uneasy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin unruhig und kann nicht einschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m restless and can’t fall asleep.

definitions.note: 1st-person plural object/reflexive pronoun (accusative or dative), used with verbs like „sich waschen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir waschen uns jeden Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wash ourselves every morning.

definitions.note: object pronoun in the accusative or dative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du uns helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help us?

definitions.note: object form of „wir“ (can be accusative or dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du uns helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you help us?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Angebot ist unschlagbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This offer is unbeatable.

definitions.note: often used about not having made a decision yet
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch unschlüssig, ob ich mitkommen soll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m still undecided about whether I should come along.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist unschuldig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is innocent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war nur eine unschuldige Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was just an innocent question.

definitions.note: Often used as a milder/more neutral way to say something is not nice to look at, compared with „hässlich“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Farbe an der Wand ist leider etwas unschön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, the color on the wall is a bit unattractive.

definitions.note: possessive determiner (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unser Haus ist alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our house is old.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner/pronoun for “we” (1st person plural).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our car is parked in front of the house.

definitions.note: Possessive determiner form used before feminine singular nouns and before plural nouns (it changes form to match the noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Freunde kommen heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our friends are coming today.

definitions.note: Used with feminine singular nouns (nominative/accusative) and with plural nouns (nominative/accusative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Freunde kommen heute Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our friends are coming this evening.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter singular form of "unser"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe unserem Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help our neighbor.

definitions.note: Used with masculine accusative singular nouns or dative plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich besuche unseren Freund heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m visiting our friend today.

definitions.note: genitive singular feminine form of „unser“ (e.g., „unserer Mutter“ = of our mother)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen unserer Verspätung kommen wir zu spät, und deswegen warten alle auf unserer Gruppe, obwohl es unserer Schuld nicht allein ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of our delay we are arriving late, and that’s why everyone is waiting for our group, although it isn’t our fault alone.

definitions.note: genitive singular (masculine/neuter) or dative singular (feminine) form of „unser“

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of our delay, we missed the train.

definitions.note: genitive singular (masculine or neuter) form of the possessive determiner
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen unseres Autos kommen wir zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of our car, we’re arriving late.

definitions.note: Genitive singular (masculine/neuter) or genitive plural form of „unser“; used to show possession.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen unseres Wetters bleiben wir heute zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of our weather, we're staying at home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mir unsicher, ob ich morgen Zeit habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not sure whether I’ll have time tomorrow.

definitions.note: often about a person’s feelings or confidence
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie fühlt sich in der neuen Klasse unsicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels insecure in the new class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gas ist unsichtbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The gas is invisible.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of the adjective „unsichtbar“ (e.g., used before a noun with certain articles/determiners).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir suchen den unsichtbaren Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are looking for the invisible man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff galt als unsinkbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship was considered unsinkable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In vielen Geschichten sind die Götter unsterblich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In many stories, the gods are immortal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schuhe stehen unten im Flur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are downstairs in the hallway.

definitions.note: Takes dative for location (where?) and accusative for direction/movement (where to?).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund schläft unter dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is sleeping under the table.

definitions.note: Often used as a preposition with the dative (location) or accusative (movement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund liegt unter dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is lying under the table.

definitions.note: simple past of „unterbrechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer unterbrach den Schüler mitten im Satz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher interrupted the student in the middle of the sentence.

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I interrupt") of "unterbrechen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigung, ich unterbreche dich nur kurz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I’m just interrupting you briefly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigung, ich möchte Sie kurz unterbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I'd like to interrupt you briefly.

definitions.note: Often used for stopping an activity (e.g., a trip, a project) for a while.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir mussten die Reise wegen des Sturms unterbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to stop the trip because of the storm.

definitions.note: often means finding someone a place to stay (temporarily or permanently)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Gäste für zwei Nächte unterbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to accommodate the guests for two nights.

definitions.note: used for putting something somewhere so it fits (e.g., in a bag, drawer, or room)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Koffer nicht im Auto unterbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t fit the suitcase in the car.

definitions.note: past participle of "unterbrechen"; also commonly used as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sitzung wurde unterbrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting was interrupted.

definitions.note: Often used for suppressing feelings, opinions, protests, or symptoms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, seine Wut zu unterdrücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to suppress his anger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regierung unterdrückt die Presse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government suppresses the press.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Regierung unterdrückte die Proteste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government suppressed the protests.

definitions.native: among each other, between one another
definitions.note: used when multiple people/things are interacting with each other within a group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder helfen sich untereinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children help each other.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „unter“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Café ist im unteren Stockwerk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The café is on the lower floor.

definitions.note: Often used to say where someone is staying (e.g., in a hotel) or where something is placed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind in einem Hotel untergebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are accommodated (staying) in a hotel.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Boot ist gestern im Sturm untergegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat sank in the storm yesterday.

definitions.note: Used with the sun (and sometimes the moon) meaning it went below the horizon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne ist schon untergegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun has already set.

definitions.native: to sink; to go under (e.g., a ship)
definitions.note: Common for ships or objects going beneath the surface; also used figuratively for failing or being ruined.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff wird im Sturm untergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship will sink in the storm.

definitions.note: For the sun: *Die Sonne geht unter* is common; here phrased with *untergehen* to match the exact word form requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne wird heute um acht Uhr untergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun will set today at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Simple past of "untergehen"; often used for ships (sinking) or the sun (setting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff unterging in wenigen Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship sank within a few minutes.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive); often used in hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn das Boot ein Leck hätte, unterginge es schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the boat had a leak, it would sink quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich unterhalte die Gäste mit Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entertain the guests with music.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich unterhalten (e.g., „Ich unterhalte mich mit …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich unterhalte mich mit meiner Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I chat with my girlfriend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dich ein bisschen unterhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to entertain you a little.

definitions.native: to maintain, to keep (something) in good condition
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Haus gut unterhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to maintain the house well.

definitions.native: to have a conversation, to chat
definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich unterhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können uns nach dem Essen unterhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can chat after the meal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr unterhaltet die Gäste mit Musik und Spielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You entertain the guests with music and games.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich unterhalten = to talk/chat (with each other).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr unterhaltet euch über eure Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You talk about your trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war sehr unterhaltsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was very entertaining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Clown unterhielt die Kinder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The clown entertained the children.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of paying for someone’s living costs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterhielt seine Familie allein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He supported his family by himself.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf der Party unterhielten sie die Gäste mit Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the party they entertained the guests with music.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" ("sich unterhalten") to mean "to talk/chat."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterhält die Gäste mit Witzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He entertains the guests with jokes.

definitions.note: Can mean paying for someone/something or keeping something in good condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie unterhält ihre Familie allein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supports her family on her own.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of the adjective (used with a noun), e.g. after an article or other determiner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Forscher erkunden einen unterirdischen Tunnel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The researchers are exploring an underground tunnel.

definitions.native: find somewhere to stay, find accommodation
definitions.note: Often used when you need a place to sleep for the night (e.g., in a hotel, with friends, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen heute Nacht irgendwo unterkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to find somewhere to stay tonight.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal/written German to mean you deliberately stop doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich unterlasse weitere Kommentare.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I refrain from making further comments.

definitions.native: to refrain (from), to stop (doing), to desist
definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts; common in the phrase „etwas unterlassen“ = to refrain from doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte unterlassen Sie das Rauchen im Gebäude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please refrain from smoking in the building.

definitions.native: to happen (by mistake), to slip in (as an error)
definitions.note: Often used with a mistake: „Mir ist ein Fehler unterlaufen.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist ein Fehler unterlaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a mistake. (A mistake happened to me.)

definitions.note: Used for rules/laws/decisions that someone tries to bypass.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, das Gesetz zu unterlaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is trying to circumvent the law.

definitions.note: Often used with rules, laws, or conditions (e.g. „der Steuerpflicht unterliegen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Produkt unterliegt strengen Sicherheitsregeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product is subject to strict safety rules.

definitions.note: Used in competitions or comparisons (often with „gegen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Mannschaft unterliegt gegen Ende knapp.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team narrowly loses near the end.

definitions.note: Contraction of „unter dem“ or „unter der“ (e.g. dative after a fixed location).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unterm Tisch liegt eine Katze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a cat under the table.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „unternehmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unternahm eine lange Reise durch Deutschland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He undertook a long trip through Germany.

definitions.note: Often used for planned actions or activities (e.g., a trip, a project, an attempt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir unternehmen morgen einen Ausflug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going on a trip tomorrow.

definitions.note: past participle of „unternehmen“; often used with „haben“ to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern viel unternommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did a lot yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used with „ich“: „ich unterrichte …“ (“I teach …”). It can also be an imperative form (“teach!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich unterrichte Deutsch an einer Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I teach German at a school.

definitions.note: Often used for teaching a subject/class (e.g., in a school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird Deutsch an einer Schule unterrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will teach German at a school.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du unterrichtest heute Mathe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re teaching math today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Frau Keller unterrichtet heute Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mrs. Keller teaches German today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „unterrichten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterrichtete Deutsch an der Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He taught German at the school.

definitions.note: contraction of „unter das“ (colloquial/written with apostrophe: „unter’s“); used before a neuter singular noun with „das“ in the accusative, often with motion/direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lege das Buch unters Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book under the bed.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts and on signs (e.g. rules, warnings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Betreten ist untersagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Entry is forbidden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann die beiden Stimmen kaum unterscheiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can hardly distinguish the two voices.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterscheidet zwischen Arbeit und Freizeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He distinguishes between work and leisure time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Antworten sind unterschiedlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two answers are different.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about multiple kinds or types of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Klasse sprechen wir über unterschiedliche Themen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class we talk about various topics.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Antworten sind unterschiedlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two answers are different.

definitions.note: adjective ending used with plural nouns or with feminine singular nouns (depending on the article/case)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben unterschiedliche Meinungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have different opinions.

definitions.note: Used as the informal (du) imperative of „unterschreiben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unterschreib bitte hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sign here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich unterschreibe den Vertrag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sign the contract.

definitions.note: usually means to sign (your name) on a document
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Vertrag noch unterschreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to sign the contract.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unterschreibst du bitte hier?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you sign here, please?

definitions.note: often used with an object: etwas unterschreiben = to sign something (e.g., a contract)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterschreibt den Vertrag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He signs the contract.

definitions.note: simple past of „unterschreiben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterschrieb den Vertrag sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He signed the contract right away.

definitions.note: past participle of „unterschreiben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Vertrag schon unterschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already signed the contract.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Leute unterschätzen, wie lange die Aufgabe dauert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people underestimate how long the task takes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterschätzt die Aufgabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He underestimates the task.

definitions.note: Often used with a person + an accusation: „jemandem etwas unterstellen“ = to say/assume someone did something (often unfairly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dir nichts unterstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to accuse you of anything.

definitions.native: to store/park (under cover), to put in a safe place
definitions.note: Often used for vehicles/bikes, meaning to put them somewhere protected (e.g., a garage, shed, basement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir können die Fahrräder im Keller unterstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can store/park the bicycles in the basement.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of „unterstützen“ (ich unterstütze).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich unterstütze dich bei deinen Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I support you with your homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mich bitte unterstützen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please support/help me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie unterstützt ihren Bruder bei den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supports her brother with his homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie unterstützte ihre Freundin beim Umzug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supported her friend with the move.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Freunde unterstützten ihn in dieser schweren Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many friends supported him during that difficult time.

definitions.note: Used for medical examinations (a doctor examining a patient) and for investigating facts, causes, or problems.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt wird den Patienten gründlich untersuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor will examine the patient thoroughly.

definitions.note: Also used as the past participle: "examined, investigated" (e.g., "hat untersucht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt untersucht den Patienten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examines the patient.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt untersuchte den Patienten gründlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examined the patient thoroughly.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural or formal “you” (Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärztinnen untersuchten die Patientinnen gründlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors examined the patients thoroughly.

definitions.note: Often used with "in" + accusative: "in drei Teile unterteilt" = "divided into three parts".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bericht unterteilt das Thema in drei Kapitel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report divides the topic into three chapters.

definitions.native: on the way, on the go
definitions.note: often used to say you are traveling somewhere or out and about
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade unterwegs zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m on my way to work right now.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (or imperative) of „unterzeichnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich unterzeichne den Vertrag heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sign the contract today.

definitions.note: Often used for signing official documents (contracts, forms, letters).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte unterzeichnen Sie dieses Formular.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sign this form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterzeichnet den Vertrag heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He signs the contract today.

definitions.note: past participle, often used with "hat" (has) or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag ist bereits unterzeichnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract is already signed.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of „unterzeichnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er unterzeichnete den Vertrag gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He signed the contract yesterday.

definitions.note: Most commonly used reflexively: sich (einer Sache) unterziehen = to undergo / submit to something (often something unpleasant, like an operation or test).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich einer Operation unterziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to undergo an operation.

definitions.note: Past participle of „unterziehen“; often used in passive („wurde … unterzogen“) or reflexive („sich einer Prüfung unterziehen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde einer Operation unterzogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He underwent an operation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Boot droht unterzugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat is in danger of sinking.

definitions.note: Used especially for the sun going below the horizon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sonne beginnt unterzugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sun is starting to set.

definitions.note: Often used about being unfaithful to a partner; can also mean disloyal to a person or cause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war seiner Frau untreu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was unfaithful to his wife.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der schlechten Nachricht war sie untröstlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the bad news, she was inconsolable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat die ganze Nacht ununterbrochen geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained continuously all night without stopping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war unverantwortlich, so schnell im Regen zu fahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was irresponsible to drive so fast in the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist unverheiratet und lebt allein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is unmarried and lives alone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist in eine unverheiratete Frau verliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is in love with an unmarried woman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall blieb er unverletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was uninjured.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stau war unvermeidlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic jam was unavoidable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist unvernünftig, so viel Geld für etwas Unnötiges auszugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s unreasonable to spend so much money on something unnecessary.

definitions.note: Often used for doors, windows, bags, etc. (i.e., not secured with a lock).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür war unverschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door was unlocked.

definitions.note: Describes a person who is friendly and not reserved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr unverschlossen und spricht gern mit neuen Leuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very open and likes talking to new people.

definitions.note: Often used as a strong criticism (about behavior, words, or demands).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist unverschämt!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s shameless!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein unverschämter Kunde hat die Verkäuferin angeschrien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A shameless customer yelled at the saleswoman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist unverschämter als sein Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is more shameless than his brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück kamen alle Passagiere unversehrt an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, all the passengers arrived unharmed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir lassen nichts unversucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We leave nothing untried.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese beiden Themen sind unverwandt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These two topics are unrelated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Held ist unverwundbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hero is invulnerable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war wirklich unverzeihlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was truly unforgivable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Handy ist für viele Menschen unverzichtbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A cellphone is indispensable for many people.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or official contexts (e.g., instructions, letters).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte melden Sie den Schaden unverzüglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please report the damage immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Plan bleibt unverändert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan stays unchanged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Formular ist unvollständig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The form is incomplete.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war auf die Frage völlig unvorbereitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was completely unprepared for the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Richterin blieb unvoreingenommen und hörte sich beide Seiten an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge remained unbiased and listened to both sides.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war sehr unvorsichtig von dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was very careless of you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schmerz war unvorstellbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pain was unimaginable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kosten sind unvorstellbar hoch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The costs are unimaginably high.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist unwahrscheinlich, dass es heute noch regnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s unlikely that it will rain again today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist unwahrscheinlich, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s unlikely that he’ll come today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist unwichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is unimportant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich musste unwillkürlich lachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to laugh involuntarily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht sah unwirklich aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light looked unreal.

definitions.note: Often implies not knowing something (sometimes innocently; can also sound critical depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war unwissend über die neuen Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was unaware of the new rules.

definitions.note: often used for feeling slightly ill (e.g., nauseous or not quite right)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist heute unwohl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel unwell today.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „sich fühlen“ or „sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist heute unwohl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't feel well today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Freunde sind unzertrennlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two friends are inseparable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin unzufrieden mit dem Ergebnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am dissatisfied with the result.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist unzuverlässig und kommt oft zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is unreliable and often arrives late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unzählige Menschen kamen zu dem Konzert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Countless people came to the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unzählige Menschen kamen zu dem Konzert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Countless people came to the concert.

definitions.note: Often used informally to emphasize that something feels extremely old (not necessarily historically ancient).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Handy ist uralt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This phone is really old.

definitions.note: Emphatic form of "alt" (old); often implies something has existed for a very long time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine uralte Tradition.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an ancient tradition.

definitions.note: Informal; "ur-" is a colloquial intensifier meaning "really/very."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war urkomisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was super funny.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ursprünglich wollte ich heute zu Hause bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Originally, I wanted to stay home today.

definitions.note: Often used with „über“ + accusative (to judge about/on something) or „nach“ + dative (to judge according to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man sollte nicht über andere urteilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn't judge others.

definitions.note: Colloquial/regional form of „aus“, used especially in phrases like „Licht us“ (= the light is off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Licht ist us.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is off.

definitions.note: Often used with sein to mean you have made plans to meet someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind um acht Uhr verabredet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have arranged to meet at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: often used with “sein” to mean you have plans/an appointment with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind um acht Uhr verabredet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have plans to meet at eight o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verabscheue Lügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I detest lies.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present (he/she/it) of „verabscheuen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verabscheut Lügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He despises lies.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun: „sich verabschieden“ = “to say goodbye / to take leave”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verabschiede mich jetzt von euch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m saying goodbye to you now.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich verabschieden = to say goodbye (and leave).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich verabschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to say goodbye (and leave).

definitions.note: This form can also be the past participle (used with an auxiliary like „hat/ist … verabschiedet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verabschiedet sich von seinen Freunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says goodbye to his friends.

definitions.note: Past participle form (used with an auxiliary like „hat/ist … verabschiedet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat sich am Bahnhof verabschiedet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She said goodbye at the train station.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive „sich verabschieden (von)“ = to say goodbye (to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verabschiedete sich von ihren Freunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She said goodbye to her friends.

definitions.native: passed, adopted (e.g., a law or resolution)
definitions.note: Common in formal/political contexts: „ein Gesetz/eine Resolution verabschieden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bundestag verabschiedete das Gesetz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Parliament passed the law.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verachte seine Lügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I despise his lies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann es nicht verstehen, warum manche Menschen andere verachten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t understand why some people despise others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verachtet Lügen und Betrug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He despises lies and deception.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verachtete mich für meine Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He despised me for my decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Software ist veraltet und sollte aktualisiert werden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This software is outdated and should be updated.

definitions.note: often used with „zu“ (e.g. „jemanden dazu veranlassen, etwas zu tun“ = to cause/prompt someone to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat ihn dazu veranlasst, früher nach Hause zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That caused him to go home earlier.

definitions.note: Used for events like parties, meetings, concerts, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir veranstalten morgen ein kleines Fest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re organizing a small party tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used for arranging an event (e.g., a party, concert, festival).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt veranstaltet am Samstag ein Festival.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is organizing a festival on Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann nicht verantworten, dass Kinder ohne Aufsicht schwimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't be responsible for children swimming without supervision.

definitions.note: Can mean being responsible for something/someone (für) or being in charge (für).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin für das Projekt verantwortlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am responsible for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es war verantwortungslos, so schnell zu fahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was irresponsible to drive so fast.

definitions.note: Often used for processing materials, food, or information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma muss die Daten schnell verarbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company has to process the data quickly.

definitions.native: to cope with, to work through (something)
definitions.note: Often used for emotions or difficult experiences (e.g., grief, stress).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie versucht, den Verlust zu verarbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is trying to cope with the loss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma hat die Daten verarbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company processed the data.

definitions.native: to mess with (someone), to tease (someone), to kid (someone)
definitions.note: Informal/vulgar; can be insulting. Often used like “Du verarschst mich!” = “You’re messing with me / You’re kidding me!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf, mich zu verarschen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop messing with me!

definitions.native: are you kidding (me)?, are you messing with (me)?
definitions.note: Slang and vulgar; can be rude/offensive depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verarschst mich doch, oder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re kidding me, right?

definitions.native: messed with, made fun of, fooled
definitions.note: Informal and often vulgar; can mean to prank/tease someone or to deceive them.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verarscht mich doch!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’ve got to be kidding me!

definitions.note: Past participle of „verbannen“; often used in passive or with „sein“ (e.g., „ist verbannt worden / ist verbannt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schriftsteller wurde aus dem Land verbannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The writer was banished from the country.

definitions.note: simple past of „verbergen“ (to hide, conceal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verbarg den Schlüssel unter der Matte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hid the key under the mat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, seine Gefühle zu verbergen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to hide his feelings.

definitions.note: Often used as “ich verbessere …” (I improve …); it can also be used as an informal command: “Verbessere das!” (Improve that!).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verbessere mein Deutsch jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I improve my German every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mein Deutsch verbessern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to improve my German.

definitions.note: Often used as the 3rd person singular present form (e.g., er/sie/es verbessert).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verbessert sein Deutsch jeden Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He improves his German every day.

definitions.note: Often used as the past participle (e.g., in passive or with haben/sein).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Programm wurde verbessert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The program was improved.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich verbeugen = to bow (oneself), e.g., as a polite gesture.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Vorstellung verbeugen sich die Schauspieler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the performance, the actors bow.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich verbeugen“ = to bow (e.g., as a greeting or out of respect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Konzert verbeugte sich der Pianist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the concert, the pianist bowed.

definitions.native: to bend out of shape, to warp
definitions.note: Often implies bending something the wrong way so it’s no longer straight or in its proper shape.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst den Draht nicht verbiegen, sonst bricht er.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not bend the wire out of shape, otherwise it will break.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I forbid").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verbiete dir, hier zu rauchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forbid you to smoke here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Eltern verbieten mir, so spät auszugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents forbid me to go out so late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verbinde mein Handy mit dem WLAN.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I connect my phone to the Wi‑Fi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Kabel kann den Computer mit dem Monitor verbinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cable can connect the computer to the monitor.

definitions.note: In the medical sense: to wrap a wound with a bandage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt muss die Wunde verbinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor has to bandage the wound.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug verbindet Berlin mit Hamburg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train connects Berlin with Hamburg.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „verbergen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum verbirgst du die Wahrheit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you hiding the truth?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „verbergen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verbirgt den Schlüssel unter dem Blumentopf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hides the key under the flowerpot.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the fixed phrase „Ich verbitte mir (das)!“ to strongly reject or refuse something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verbitte mir diesen Ton!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won't tolerate that tone!

definitions.note: often used for colors, light, photos, or memories becoming less strong
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Farbe kann in der Sonne verblassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The color can fade in the sun.

definitions.note: often used for colors, photos, text, memories, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Foto verblasst mit der Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo fades over time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nach dem Unfall verblutet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bled to death after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Ergebnis war wirklich verblüffend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The result was really astonishing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er konnte verblüffend gut singen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He could sing astonishingly well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war völlig verblüfft, als er plötzlich vor der Tür stand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was completely astonished when he suddenly showed up at the door.

definitions.note: Often used for something that got bent out of shape.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Nagel ist verbogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nail is bent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eingang ist verborgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The entrance is hidden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben eine verborgene Tür hinter dem Regal gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found a hidden door behind the bookshelf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Rauchen ist hier verboten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoking is forbidden here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hier ist das Rauchen verboten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Smoking is forbidden here.

definitions.note: past participle of "verbringen"; commonly used with time (e.g., a day, vacation)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den ganzen Tag zu Hause verbracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent the whole day at home.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "verbringen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzten Sommer verbrachte ich zwei Wochen in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last summer I spent two weeks in Berlin.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "verbringen" for "wir/sie/Sie".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verbrachten den ganzen Tag am Strand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spent the whole day at the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen ist verbrannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food is burnt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen ist verbrannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food is burnt.

definitions.note: Simple past form (Präteritum) of „verbrennen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Feuer verbrannte das Papier schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire burned the paper quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verbrannten das Holz im Ofen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They burned the wood in the stove.

definitions.note: Often used for resources like energy, electricity, fuel, time, money, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verbrauchen zu viel Strom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We use up too much electricity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verbraucht viel Strom.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He uses up a lot of electricity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ganze Wasser ist schon verbraucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the water has already been used up.

definitions.note: Often used for spreading information, news, or rumors.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeitung wird die Nachricht schnell verbreiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper will spread the news quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma verbreitet die Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company spreads the news.

definitions.note: past participle, often used with "haben" or "sich haben" (e.g., "hat sich verbreitet").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gerücht hat sich schnell verbreitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rumor spread quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Meinung ist in vielen Ländern weit verbreitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This opinion is widespread in many countries.

definitions.note: simple past form of „verbreiten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeitung verbreitete die Nachricht schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper spread the news quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachrichten verbreiteten sich schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news spread quickly.

definitions.note: This is the verb stem used in forms like “verbrenne” (I burn) or the imperative “Verbrenn …!” (Burn …!).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verbrenn den Brief nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t burn the letter!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I) of "verbrennen"; also used like an imperative in recipes/instructions (e.g., "Man verbrenne …" = "Burn …").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man verbrenne den Müll nicht im Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t burn the trash in the garden.

definitions.note: Often used for burning something completely (e.g., trash) or for something being consumed by fire. (Be careful: the participle is usually *verbrannt*, but this example is forced to include the exact form *verbrennen*.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dem Brand konnte man das ganze Haus verbrennen sehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the fire, you could see the whole house burning up.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du so nah am Feuer stehst, verbrennst du dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you stand so close to the fire, you burn yourself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Holz verbrennt schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wood burns quickly.

definitions.note: Used with time (and often also with an object like time, a vacation, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verbringe das Wochenende bei meinen Eltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm spending the weekend at my parents' place.

definitions.note: Commonly used with time periods (z.B. den Tag, die Woche) to say how/where you spend time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verbringen das Wochenende bei meinen Eltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re spending the weekend at my parents’ place.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „verbringen“ (you spend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie verbringst du deine Freizeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you spend your free time?

definitions.note: Used for spending time (and sometimes spending money).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verbringt den Sommer bei seinen Großeltern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spends the summer with his grandparents.

definitions.note: Past participle of „verbrechen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was hast du verbrochen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What have you done (wrong)?

definitions.note: past participle of „verbinden“; often used with „sein“ to mean “to be connected”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit dem Internet verbunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am connected to the internet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Geräte sind verbunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two devices are connected.

definitions.note: Often used as a swear word or intensifier (like “damn!” / “damn it!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verdammt, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn, I forgot my key!

definitions.note: Often used as a swear word or as a strong intensifier (like “damn” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der verdammte Regen hört nicht auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The damned rain won’t stop.

definitions.note: Often used to add strong emphasis; can sound rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist verdammt schwer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is damn hard.

definitions.note: An exclamation expressing anger, annoyance, or frustration; can be considered rude.
