definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verdammt, ich habe meinen Schlüssel vergessen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn, I forgot my key!

definitions.note: Strong, rude language; used to express anger/annoyance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese verdammte Tür klemmt ständig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This damned door keeps getting stuck.

definitions.note: Often used as a swear word or to show strong annoyance; can sound rude or offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese verdammte Tür klemmt schon wieder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This damned door is stuck again.

definitions.note: Strong, often rude/angry emphasis (like “damn” / “bloody” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese verdammte Tür geht nicht auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This damned door won’t open.

definitions.note: Very strong and rude; used for swearing/complaining.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo sind meine verdammten Schlüssel?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are my damn keys?

definitions.note: Often used as a swear word to express anger or frustration; can sound rude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den verdammten Schlüssel verloren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost the damned key.

definitions.note: Often used as a swear word to express anger or frustration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein verdammter Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a damned day.

definitions.note: Strong/vulgar language; often used as an intensifier to show anger or frustration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein verdammter Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a damn mistake.

definitions.note: strong language; used to express anger or frustration
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verdammtes Glück, schon wieder verloren!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damned luck, lost again!

definitions.note: Often used with an object (someone you owe thanks to) and/or with "dass" + clause or "etwas" (something you owe to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verdanke dir viel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I owe you a lot.

definitions.note: Often used with a thing or person you owe something to (e.g., „jemandem etwas verdanken“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diesen Erfolg verdankst du harter Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You owe this success to hard work.

definitions.note: Often used with dative: „etwas jemandem verdanken“ = to owe something to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seinen Erfolg verdankt er seiner Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He owes his success to his family.

definitions.note: Often used for people/things kept secret, e.g. in police contexts: „verdeckter Ermittler“ = undercover detective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein verdeckter Ermittler arbeitet in der Bar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An undercover investigator is working in the bar.

definitions.note: Often used for food going bad (spoiling) or for ruining plans, mood, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Milch ist im Kühlschrank verderben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The milk is spoiling in the fridge.

definitions.note: Colloquial spelling/pronunciation of „verdiene“ (e.g., „ich verdien …“); also used as the (informal) „du“ imperative: „Verdien …!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verdien nicht viel Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't earn much money.

definitions.note: Colloquial spelling/pronunciation of „verdiene“; also used as the (informal) „du“ imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verdien dir erst das Vertrauen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Earn their trust first!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense of „verdienen“ (ich verdiene).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verdiene nicht genug Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t earn enough money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mehr Geld verdienen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to earn more money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wirst es verdienen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will deserve it / You will have earned it.

definitions.note: second-person singular present (du-form) of "verdienen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verdienst viel Geld in deinem neuen Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You earn a lot of money in your new job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verdient viel Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He earns a lot of money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verdient eine Pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deserves a break.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum); can refer to earning money or income
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr verdiente sie nicht viel Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year she didn’t earn much money.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum); used when someone deserves praise, punishment, success, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach so viel Arbeit verdiente er eine Pause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After so much work, he deserved a break.

definitions.note: Can also mean "doubled" depending on context (present vs. past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma verdoppelt ihren Umsatz in zwei Jahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company doubles its revenue in two years.

definitions.note: Often used for food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Milch ist verdorben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The milk has gone bad.

definitions.note: Used to describe a person's character or behavior.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein verdorbener Mensch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a corrupt person.

definitions.note: Often used for food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Milch ist verdorben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The milk has gone bad.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person’s character or morals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist durch Macht verdorben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been corrupted by power.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kabel ist verdreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cable is twisted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schlauch ist verdreht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hose is twisted.

definitions.note: Often used informally to describe an unusual person or idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine verdrehte Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a weird idea.

definitions.note: Often used for removing someone/something from a place or position, sometimes in a figurative sense (e.g., in the market).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Neue Apps können ältere Programme vom Markt verdrängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: New apps can push older programs out of the market.

definitions.note: Common with feelings, thoughts, or memories that someone tries not to think about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie versucht, die Erinnerung an den Unfall zu verdrängen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tries to suppress the memory of the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der neue Chef verdrängt die alte Managerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new boss pushes out (displaces) the old manager.

definitions.note: Often used for unpleasant thoughts, feelings, or memories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verdrängt ihre Angst und lächelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She represses her fear and smiles.

definitions.note: Colloquial; often used for eating something quickly (past participle of "verdrücken").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das ganze Sandwich in fünf Minuten verdrückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wolfed down the whole sandwich in five minutes.

definitions.note: Informal and often rude; used as a command telling someone to go away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verdufte endlich!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get lost already!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Himmel verdunkelte sich plötzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sky suddenly darkened.

definitions.note: often used to describe being momentarily confused or surprised
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaute mich verdutzt an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked at me, bewildered.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann wirkt verdächtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man seems suspicious.

definitions.note: Often used with a person as the object, and the thing/crime with „wegen“ or „etwas zu tun“ (e.g. „jemanden verdächtigen, etwas getan zu haben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei beginnt, ihn zu verdächtigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are starting to suspect him.

definitions.note: Usually used with a direct object (accusative): jemanden verdächtigen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verdächtigst ihn ohne Beweise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You suspect him without evidence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei verdächtigt ihn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police suspect him.

definitions.note: often used as a past participle in passive constructions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird verdächtigt, Geld gestohlen zu haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is suspected of having stolen money.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of suspecting someone of a crime or wrongdoing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei verdächtigte ihn, das Fahrrad gestohlen zu haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police suspected him of having stolen the bicycle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verehrt seine Großmutter sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He really admires his grandmother.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite form of address (e.g. „Sehr verehrte Damen und Herren …“ = “Dear/Esteemed Ladies and Gentlemen …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sehr verehrte Frau Müller, vielen Dank für Ihre Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Ms. Müller, thank you very much for your message.

definitions.note: Used in formal address (especially in letters/speeches), often with titles like Frau/Herr.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sehr verehrte Frau Müller, vielen Dank für Ihre Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Mrs. Müller, thank you very much for your message.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite form of address (especially in letters/speeches), similar to “dear/esteemed”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verehrter Herr Müller, vielen Dank für Ihre Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Mr. Müller, thank you very much for your message.

definitions.note: Often used with "einen Termin" (an appointment) or "etwas" + "vereinbaren" (agree on something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir vereinbaren einen Termin für nächste Woche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrange an appointment for next week.

definitions.note: Past participle of „vereinbaren“; it can also be the 3rd-person singular present form (“agrees/arranges”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben einen Termin für morgen vereinbart.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arranged an appointment for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen unsere Kräfte vereinen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to unite our forces.

definitions.note: past participle of „vereinen“ (often used with „haben“: „etw. vereinen“ = to unite/join something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie haben ihre Kräfte vereint.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They united their strengths.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Spiel waren die Fans vereint.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the game, the fans were united.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist vereist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is icy.

definitions.native: to proceed, to act (according to a rule/plan)
definitions.note: Often used with "so" or "nach" (e.g., "so verfahren", "nach dem Plan verfahren").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In diesem Fall müssen wir so verfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this case we have to proceed like this.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: "sich verfahren".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mich nicht verfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to get lost (while driving).

definitions.note: often used for buildings or things that are not maintained
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das alte Haus beginnt zu verfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old house is starting to decay.

definitions.native: to fall prey to, to become addicted to
definitions.note: often used with dative: jemandem/etwas verfallen
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist dem Alkohol verfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell prey to alcohol (he became addicted to alcohol).

definitions.note: Often used for writing something more formal (e.g., an email, a text, an essay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch eine E-Mail verfassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to write an email.

definitions.note: Often used for writing or composing texts (e.g., reports, articles, letters).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verfasst einen Artikel für die Zeitung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She writes an article for the newspaper.

definitions.note: often used for food or organic material that has gone bad
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Apfel ist schon verfault.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apple is already rotten.

definitions.note: Often used for missing a physical target or failing to meet a goal/deadline.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird das Ziel knapp verfehlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will narrowly miss the target.

definitions.note: Often used with a target/goal (das Ziel) or in the phrase „den Punkt verfehlen“ (to miss the point).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verfehlt das Ziel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He misses the target.

definitions.note: Simple past form; often used for missing a target, goal, or opportunity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verfehlte das Ziel knapp.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He narrowly missed the target.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/strong profanity; often used to express anger or frustration.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese verfickte Sache geht mir auf die Nerven.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This fucking thing is getting on my nerves.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/strong language; often used as an intensifier.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo sind meine verfickten Schlüssel?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are my fucking keys?

definitions.note: Very vulgar and offensive; used as an intensifier or insult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein verfickter Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a fucking mistake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das alte Haus verfiel nach dem Sturm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old house fell into ruin after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verflucht sein schlechtes Glück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He curses his bad luck.

definitions.note: Often used as a swear word or to express annoyance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein verfluchter Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a cursed/damned mistake.

definitions.note: Common in spoken German to intensify an adjective or statement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist verflucht schwer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is damn hard.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to show anger, frustration, or annoyance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verflucht! Ich habe den Schlüssel vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn! I forgot the key.

definitions.note: Often used colloquially to express anger or frustration (like an annoyed swear/insult).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser verfluchte Computer funktioniert nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This damned computer isn’t working.

definitions.note: Often used to express annoyance (like “damn” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche den verfluchten Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for the damned key.

definitions.note: Often used as an angry exclamation (strong language), like “damn …!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verfluchter Regen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Damn rain!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Schon wieder Regen – verfluchtes Wetter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rain again—damned weather!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verfolge die Nachrichten jeden Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I follow the news every evening.

definitions.note: Often used for following someone/something (physically or in an investigation) or tracking progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei muss den Verdächtigen verfolgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have to track the suspect.

definitions.note: Used for goals, plans, or interests (not necessarily physical movement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will ein klares Ziel verfolgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to pursue a clear goal.

definitions.note: Often used for following someone/something in order to catch them (e.g., police chasing a suspect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei verfolgt den Verdächtigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are chasing the suspect.

definitions.note: Often used in the passive to describe people being treated unfairly and harmed because of who they are or what they believe.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird wegen seiner Religion verfolgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is persecuted because of his religion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund verfolgte die Katze bis zum Garten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chased the cat all the way to the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Regime verfolgte politische Gegner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The regime persecuted political opponents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sind noch Tickets verfügbar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are there still tickets available?

definitions.native: to have (at one’s disposal), to have available
definitions.note: Often used with „über“ („verfügen über“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann heute nicht kommen, weil ich nicht über genug Zeit verfügen kann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t come today because I don’t have enough time available.

definitions.note: Formal/official usage (e.g., by a judge or authority).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Richter kann eine Geldstrafe verfügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge can order a fine.

definitions.note: Often used with "über" + accusative: "über etwas verfügen" = to have something available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Hotel verfügt über einen Pool.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel has a pool.

definitions.note: Often used in a romantic/sexual sense; can also mean to tempt someone into doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versuchte, sie zu verführen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to seduce her.

definitions.note: Often used in a romantic/sexual sense, but it can also mean enticing someone into doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verführt sie mit schönen Worten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seduces her with beautiful words.

definitions.note: Simple past of "vergeben"; often used for handing out or awarding (e.g., points, grades, prizes, appointments).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer vergab zehn Punkte für die richtige Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher awarded ten points for the correct answer.

definitions.note: Often used about time (e.g., last week/month/year).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im vergangenen Jahr war ich oft in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the past year, I was often in Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used with time words (e.g. „vergangene Woche“ = last/past week).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergangene Woche war ich krank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last week I was sick.

definitions.note: Used attributively before a noun (with an ending), often in phrases like „im vergangenen Jahr“ = “last year.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im vergangenen Jahr war ich in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I was in Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used before a neuter noun (e.g., „vergangenes Jahr“ = “last year”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich denke nicht gern an vergangenes Leid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like to think about past suffering.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „vergessen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vergaß deinen Namen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot your name.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vergebe dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgive you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir vergeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can forgive you.

definitions.note: Often used for assigning or awarding something (e.g., a contract, tasks, appointments, tickets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma will den Auftrag an ein kleines Team vergeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to award the contract to a small team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn vergebens angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called him in vain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben ihn vergeblich angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We called him in vain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vergeblich versucht, dich zu erreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried in vain to reach you.

definitions.note: Often used about time passing (e.g., Minuten, Stunden, Jahre).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeit kann schnell vergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time can pass quickly.

definitions.note: As a reflexive verb: „sich vergehen an + Dativ“ = to wrong/assault someone (incl. sexual assault, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich an dem Kind vergangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He assaulted the child.

definitions.note: often used when talking about time
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeit vergeht schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time passes quickly.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I) of „vergessen“; often used in indirect speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er vergesse den Termin nie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he never forgets the appointment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe gestern meinen Schlüssel zu Hause vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I forgot my key at home yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute total vergesslich und habe meinen Schlüssel schon wieder vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m totally forgetful and I’ve forgotten my key again.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) present tense; also used as a polite imperative meaning “(please) don’t forget …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr vergesst immer eure Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always forget your keys.

definitions.note: Often used for wasting time, money, or opportunities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird seine Zeit vergeuden, wenn er den ganzen Tag am Handy ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will waste his time if he is on his phone all day.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular informal (du) present tense of „vergeuden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du vergeudest deine Zeit mit sinnlosen Videos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re wasting your time on pointless videos.

definitions.note: Often used as the 3rd-person singular present tense form (he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vergeudet sein Geld für unnötige Dinge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wastes his money on unnecessary things.

definitions.note: Can also be the past participle (used with 'hat/ist').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat keine Zeit vergeudet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She didn’t waste any time.

definitions.note: Very serious and sensitive term.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde beschuldigt, eine Frau zu vergewaltigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was accused of raping a woman.

definitions.note: Sensitive/violent term; refers to sexual assault.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wurde vergewaltigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was raped.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich vergewissern (to make sure/ascertain for yourself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vergewissere mich, dass die Tür abgeschlossen ist, bevor ich gehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I make sure that the door is locked before I leave.

definitions.note: Old spelling of „vergesst“ (modern: ss). Used with „ihr“ (you plural) in the present tense and also as an imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr vergeßt immer eure Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always forget your keys.

definitions.note: Command form (du-imperative) of "vergeben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte vergib mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please forgive me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie vergibt ihm den Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She forgives him for the mistake.

definitions.note: Often used for awarding prizes or assigning something (like a contract or an appointment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Jury vergibt den ersten Preis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jury awards the first prize.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man wollte ihn vergiften.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wanted to poison him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen ist vergiftet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food is poisoned.

definitions.note: Be careful: German "Gift" means "poison" (not an English "gift").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen war vergiftet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was poisoned.

definitions.note: Often used about time (e.g., how quickly time passes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeit verging schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time passed quickly.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „vergehen“ (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stunden vergingen wie im Flug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hours passed by as if in a flash.

definitions.note: informal singular command (du-imperative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss deinen Regenschirm nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget your umbrella!

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „vergessen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vergisst oft seinen Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often forgets his key.

definitions.note: informal singular command (du)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiß nicht, den Schlüssel mitzunehmen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to take the key with you!

definitions.note: third-person singular present tense of "vergessen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vergißt oft seinen Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often forgets his key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Angebote sind preislich gut vergleichbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two offers are very comparable in terms of price.

definitions.note: Can mean “I compare” (present tense) or “compare!” (informal singular imperative), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vergleiche die Preise online.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I compare the prices online.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Preise in zwei Geschäften vergleichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will compare the prices in two stores.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "vergleichen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vergleicht die Preise im Internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He compares the prices on the internet.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „vergleichen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verglich die Preise im Internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He compared the prices online.

definitions.note: Past participle of „vergleichen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat … verglichen“) or in phrases like „verglichen mit“ = „compared to“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Preise verglichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I compared the prices.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective meaning someone is in a good mood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind vergnügt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are cheerful.

definitions.note: Often used with something hidden/covered in the ground (literally or figuratively).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat den Knochen im Garten vergraben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog buried the bone in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Bild bitte vergrößern?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you enlarge the picture, please?

definitions.note: Very strong admiration; treating someone almost like a god.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vergöttert seine Tochter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He adores his daughter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vergöttert seine Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He adores his girlfriend.

definitions.note: Used especially for police/legal arrests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei wird den Verdächtigen verhaften.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police will arrest the suspect.

definitions.note: past participle of "verhaften"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde gestern von der Polizei verhaftet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was arrested by the police yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann ist verhaftet und wartet auf seinen Anwalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man is arrested and is waiting for his lawyer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei verhaftete den Mann am Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the man at the train station.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich verhalten“ = to behave.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst dich in der Schule besser verhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to behave better at school.

definitions.note: Often used with "über" + accusative (about) or "mit" + dative (with).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verhandeln mit dem Vermieter über die Miete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are negotiating with the landlord about the rent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verhandelt mit dem Verkäufer über den Preis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She negotiates with the seller about the price.

definitions.note: Usually used for wounds/injuries healing (closing up) over time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde kann gut verheilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound can heal well.

definitions.note: often used for wounds/injuries after healing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wunde ist gut verheilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wound has healed well.

definitions.native: to keep secret; to conceal (from someone)
definitions.note: Used when someone deliberately hides information or a fact from another person; often with a dative person (jemandem) and an accusative thing (etwas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will seiner Freundin die Wahrheit verheimlichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to keep the truth from his girlfriend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum verheimlichst du mir das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you hiding that from me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verheimlicht die Wahrheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hides the truth.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective with „sein“ (e.g. „Sie ist verheiratet.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Schwester ist verheiratet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is married.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist seit fünf Jahren verheiratet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been married for five years.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „verheiratet“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine verheiratete Frau.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a married woman.

definitions.note: masculine form (e.g., before a noun like "Mann")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein verheirateter Mann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a married man.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist verhext.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is bewitched.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to mean someone seems under a spell (e.g., strongly fascinated).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaut sie an, als wäre er verhext.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looks at her as if he were bewitched.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Unfall verhindern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to prevent the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das verhindert Unfälle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That prevents accidents.

definitions.note: Often used for dying from lack of food; for being very hungry without dying, German more often uses „verhungern vor Hunger“ or „am Verhungern sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Hilfe könnten viele Menschen verhungern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without help, many people could starve to death.

definitions.note: Past participle of "verhungern"; often used with "sein" (e.g., "ist verhungert").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Hilfe wäre er verhungert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without help, he would have starved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das verhungerte Kind braucht sofort Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The starved child needs help immediately.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „verhungern“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Hilfe verhungerte er im Winter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without help, he starved in the winter.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), plural or formal (Sie) form of "verhungern".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Krieg verhungerten viele Menschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the war, many people starved.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: sich verhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verhält sich heute sehr ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is behaving very calmly today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wohnung ist verhältnismäßig günstig für diese Gegend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment is relatively cheap for this area.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich verhalten = to behave/act (e.g., „Du verhältst dich …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verhältst dich heute sehr höflich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re behaving very politely today.

definitions.note: Often used in official contexts (e.g., police/legal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei wird den Zeugen morgen verhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police will interrogate the witness tomorrow.

definitions.note: Can be the 3rd-person singular present tense form of „verhören“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizist verhört den Zeugen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer interrogates the witness.

definitions.note: Can also be the past participle of „verhören“ (often used in the passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Verdächtige wurde verhört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect was interrogated.

definitions.native: to get lost, to lose one's way
definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich verirren.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mich hier leicht verirren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can easily get lost here.

definitions.note: often used like an adjective meaning “lost/astray” (e.g., a lost person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich verirrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got lost.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „verirren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verirrte mich im Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got lost in the forest.

definitions.note: Often used when installing or connecting cables in a building, device, or system.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Büro noch verkabeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still need to wire up the office.

definitions.note: first-person singular present (ich) or imperative (du) of „verkaufen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verkaufe mein altes Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sell my old bike.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mein Auto verkaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sell my car.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum verkaufst du dein Fahrrad?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you selling your bike?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verkauft sein Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sells his car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist schon verkauft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is already sold.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „verkaufen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verkaufte sein Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sold his car.

definitions.note: Used with „mit“ to mean spending time with certain people (e.g. „mit Freunden verkehren“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verkehrt oft mit seinen Kollegen nach der Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often socializes with his colleagues after work.

definitions.note: Often used when something is the opposite of what it should be (e.g., clothes on the wrong way, the wrong direction).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast das T-Shirt verkehrt herum angezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put the T-shirt on the wrong way around.

definitions.note: Usually means to sue someone (e.g., in court).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will die Firma verklagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to sue the company.

definitions.note: past participle of „verklagen“ (to sue); often used in passive constructions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vermieter wird wegen Betrugs verklagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The landlord is being sued for fraud.

definitions.note: Often used with "als" to say what someone is dressed up as (e.g., "als Pirat").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist als Pirat verkleidet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is dressed up as a pirate.

definitions.note: Often used with „als“ + role/costume (e.g., „als Pirat“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist als Pirat verkleidet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is disguised as a pirate.

definitions.note: Often used with sein: „in jdn. verknallt sein“ (colloquial).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin total in ihn verknallt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a huge crush on him.

definitions.native: to fall into ruin, to become run-down
definitions.note: Often used to describe a place or thing that has been neglected and is in poor condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist völlig verkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house has completely fallen into disrepair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das verkompliziert alles nur.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That just complicates everything.

definitions.note: Often used for dealing with something difficult (bad news, stress, a shock).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann die schlechte Nachricht kaum verkraften.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can barely cope with the bad news.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister verkündete die neuen Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor announced the new rules.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., "etwas verlangen") or with "von" (e.g., "etwas von jemandem verlangen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wird mehr Einsatz von uns verlangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will demand more commitment from us.

definitions.note: Often used with "nach" (e.g., "nach etwas verlangen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manchmal kann ich nur nach Ruhe verlangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes all I can do is long for peace and quiet.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verlangst zu viel von mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You demand too much from me.

definitions.note: Often used with an object in the accusative (e.g., etwas verlangt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer verlangt Ruhe im Klassenzimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher demands quiet in the classroom.

definitions.note: Common with „nach“ (e.g., nach etwas verlangt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach einem Urlaub verlangt er schon seit Wochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has been longing for a vacation for weeks.

definitions.note: Past tense (simple past) form of „verlangen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kunde verlangte sein Geld zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The customer demanded his money back.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural or formal "you"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kunden verlangten ihr Geld zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The customers demanded their money back.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative of "verlassen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verlass bitte das Zimmer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please leave the room!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich) or imperative (du) of „verlassen“; can mean leaving a place or leaving/abandoning a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verlasse jetzt das Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm leaving the house now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus ist verlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is abandoned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Haus verlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben eine verlassene Fabrik gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw an abandoned factory.

definitions.note: Describes something that has been left behind; this is a declined (inflected) form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind an den verlassenen Häusern vorbeigelaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked past the abandoned houses.

definitions.note: 2nd-person plural form (ihr) in the present tense; can also be the plural imperative (“leave!”) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr verlasst das Haus um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You leave the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich verlaufen = to get lost (by taking a wrong turn).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich in der Stadt verlaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got lost in the city.

definitions.note: Often used to describe how an event went (e.g., gut/schlecht verlaufen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gespräch ist besser verlaufen als erwartet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conversation went better than expected.

definitions.note: Often used in impersonal constructions like „Es verlautet, dass …“ or after „lassen“ (e.g. „etwas verlauten lassen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma lässt verlauten, dass sie nächste Woche neue Produkte vorstellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company announces (has it announced) that it will present new products next week.

definitions.note: Past participle of „verleben“, used with „haben“ in the perfect tense, especially about spending a period of time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein schönes Wochenende in Berlin verlebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent a nice weekend in Berlin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade ein bisschen verlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m a little embarrassed right now.

definitions.native: to misplace, to lose (by putting it somewhere and forgetting)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich darf meine Schlüssel nicht immer verlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must not keep misplacing my keys.

definitions.native: to postpone, to reschedule (to a different time/place)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Treffen verlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to postpone/reschedule the meeting.

definitions.note: past participle of "verlegen" (to relocate/move something to another place)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma hat ihren Sitz nach Berlin verlegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company relocated its headquarters to Berlin.

definitions.note: past participle of "verlegen" (used for books/newspapers being published by a publisher)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Buch wird von einem kleinen Verlag verlegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is published by a small publishing house.

definitions.note: Often used for lending something out (e.g., a library lending books).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir dein Buch für einen Tag verleihen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you lend me your book for one day?

definitions.native: to award, to confer (e.g., a prize, a title)
definitions.note: Used with things like prizes, honors, titles, or degrees.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Universität wird ihm einen Ehrendoktortitel verleihen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The university will award him an honorary doctorate.

definitions.note: can mean lending something temporarily, or awarding/confering something (e.g., a prize or a title); context decides
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verleiht mir sein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lends me his book.

definitions.note: used for giving someone something like a prize, title, or honor
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Universität verleiht ihm den Doktortitel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The university confers the doctoral title on him.

definitions.note: Often used to mean you lost a skill over time (e.g., a language or an activity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Französisch fast verlernt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve almost forgotten my French.

definitions.native: to read aloud, to read out
definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., announcements, meetings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sprecher wird die Namen der Gewinner verlesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The speaker will read out the names of the winners.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich verlesen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich verlesen und die Zahl falsch verstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I misread and misunderstood the number.

definitions.note: Often used for physical injury; also used figuratively for emotional hurt (e.g., feelings, pride).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann sich leicht verletzen, wenn er ohne Helm fährt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can injure himself easily if he rides without a helmet.

definitions.note: Used in formal/legal contexts: e.g., ein Gesetz/eine Pflicht/die Privatsphäre/die Menschenrechte verletzen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wer diese Regeln missachtet, kann das Gesetz verletzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Anyone who disregards these rules can violate the law.

definitions.note: Common with objects like jemanden, Gefühle, Stolz, Ehre.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollte dich nicht verletzen, aber deine Worte haben mich verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t want to hurt you, but your words hurt me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Operation war sie sehr verletzlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the operation, she was very vulnerable.

definitions.note: usually about a physical injury
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist am Bein verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is injured in his leg.

definitions.note: about feelings (emotionally hurt)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist verletzt, weil du nicht gekommen bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is hurt because you didn’t come.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist am Bein verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is injured in his leg.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist am Bein verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is injured in his leg.

definitions.note: Can describe physical injury or hurt feelings.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall ist er am Bein verletzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, his leg is injured.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „verletzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verletzte sich beim Fußball.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He injured himself playing soccer.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective before a noun (e.g., „eine verletzte Person“ = “an injured person”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rettungswagen bringt eine verletzte Person ins Krankenhaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ambulance is taking an injured person to the hospital.

definitions.note: Used as a declined adjective (often from the participle of „verletzen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sanitäter versorgten die verletzten Menschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The paramedics treated the injured people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verleumdet seine Kollegin, obwohl er keine Beweise hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slanders his coworker even though he has no evidence.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich in jemanden verlieben“ = to fall in love with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mich in ihn verlieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will fall in love with him.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g. „Ich bin verliebt“) and frequently with „in + Akkusativ“ (e.g. „in dich“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in dich verliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in love with you.

definitions.note: Often used with „in + Akk.“ (e.g. „in ihn/sie“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin in dich verliebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in love with you.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich verlieben (e.g., „Ich verliebte mich …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verliebte mich in sie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell in love with her.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: sich verlieben (to fall in love).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verliebten sich im Urlaub.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fell in love on vacation.

definitions.note: simple past of „verlaufen“ (often used to talk about how an event went)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gespräch verlief gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conversation went well.

definitions.note: simple past of „verlaufen“ (used for routes or liquids)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße verlief am Fluss entlang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road ran along the river.

definitions.note: Often used with prizes, medals, titles, or honors.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis wurde ihr gestern verliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prize was awarded to her yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for items that are loaned out (e.g., by a library or rental service).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir wurde für die Reise ein Auto verliehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A car was loaned to me for the trip.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (du-form), often used in negative commands: „Verlier nicht …“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verlier nicht die Schlüssel!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't lose the keys!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present subjunctive I (Konjunktiv I) of „verlieren“; also used as an imperative (formal „ich“-form) in instructions like recipes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er verliere oft seine Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he often loses his keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will meine Schlüssel nicht verlieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to lose my keys.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „verlieren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du den Schlüssel verlierst, kommst du nicht rein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you lose the key, you won’t be able to get in.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „verlieren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verliert oft seine Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often loses his keys.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „verlassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verließ das Haus um sieben Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left the house at seven o'clock.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „verlassen“ (used with plural subjects like „we/they“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verließen das Haus um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the house at eight o’clock.

definitions.note: used about being engaged to be married
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sind seit einem Jahr verlobt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been engaged for a year.

definitions.note: used especially with „sein“ (e.g., „Ich bin verlobt.“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist seit einem Jahr verlobt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been engaged for a year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Angebot ist verlockend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The offer is tempting.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person’s behavior, statements, or attitude as deceitful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine verlogenen Ausreden haben niemanden überzeugt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His lying excuses didn’t convince anyone.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „verlieren“; commonly used in writing and narratives.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verlor gestern meinen Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost my key yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „verlieren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Schlüssel verloren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost my key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Schlüssel ist verloren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My key is lost.

definitions.note: Declined form of the adjective (used before a noun, e.g. with feminine singular or plural nouns depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche meine verlorene Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for my lost jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir suchten den verlorenen Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We looked for the lost key.

definitions.note: often used for things that have gone missing (e.g., keys, documents)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat die verlorengegangenen Ausweise gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found the lost ID cards.

definitions.note: Often used for extending time periods (e.g., a contract, a deadline, a visa).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Frist verlängern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to extend the deadline.

definitions.note: present tense form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs verlängert sich um eine Woche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course is extended by a week.

definitions.note: past participle form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Öffnungszeiten sind verlängert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The opening hours have been extended.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine verlässliche Kollegin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a reliable colleague.

definitions.note: comparative form of „verlässig“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Auto ist verlässlicher als das alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car is more reliable than the old one.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „verlassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verlässt heute früher das Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He leaves the office earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used to describe the course/route of something (e.g., a road) or how something proceeds.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße verläuft am Fluss entlang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road runs along the river.

definitions.note: Often used for how a route, line, river, or a process proceeds.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fluss verläuft durch die Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river runs through the city.

definitions.note: Alternative spelling: „verlässlich“ (more common in modern German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr verläßlich und hält immer ihr Wort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very reliable and always keeps her word.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/literary; often used with "zu" + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vermag das nicht zu verstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can’t understand that.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal; often used in writing. Usually followed by an infinitive (e.g., „vermag zu …“ / „vermag … zu …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vermag das Problem allein zu lösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can solve the problem on his own.

definitions.note: colloquial
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will die Prüfung nicht vermasseln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to mess up the exam.

definitions.note: Often used for numbers/amounts (increase) or for living things (multiply/reproduce).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen die Anzahl der Pflanzen im Garten vermehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to increase the number of plants in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zahl der Fälle hat sich vermehrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The number of cases has increased.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich) or imperative (du) of „vermeiden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vermeide heute Zucker.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I avoid sugar today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, Zucker zu vermeiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to avoid sugar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vermied den Blickkontakt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He avoided eye contact.

definitions.native: to rent out, to lease out
definitions.note: Means the owner/landlord rents something to someone else (the opposite of "mieten" = to rent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will seine Wohnung an eine Studentin vermieten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to rent out his apartment to a student.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vermietet sein Zimmer an Studenten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rents out his room to students.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective to mean something is already rented (not available).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wohnung ist schon vermietet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment is already rented out.

definitions.note: Used with an object (often a person or thing) that you miss.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vermisse dich sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I miss you a lot.

definitions.note: Used for missing a person/thing (feeling their absence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vermisse meine Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I miss my family.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „vermissen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vermisst seine Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He misses his family.

definitions.note: Often used in passive constructions (e.g., „wird vermisst“ = „is missing“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind wird seit gestern vermisst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has been missing since yesterday.

definitions.note: often used about a person who has been reported missing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit gestern wird die Frau vermisst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman has been missing since yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vermisste dich sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed you a lot.

definitions.note: often used about people who have disappeared and are being searched for ("missing persons")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei sucht nach den vermissten Kindern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are searching for the missing children.

definitions.note: Often used for arranging contacts, services, jobs, or deals between people/parties.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Agentur kann Wohnungen an Studierende vermitteln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The agency can broker apartments for students.

definitions.note: Used for passing on information or explaining/teaching something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer kann den Stoff sehr klar vermitteln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher can convey the material very clearly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie vermittelt zwischen den beiden Streitenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She mediates between the two people who are arguing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer vermittelt den Stoff verständlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher explains the material in an understandable way.

definitions.note: Old spelling; today usually written as „vermisst“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vermißt seine Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He misses his family.

definitions.note: Often used to express an educated guess (similar to “I guess” or “I suppose”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vermute, dass er heute zu spät kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suspect that he’ll be late today.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce an educated guess (e.g., “Ich vermute, dass …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vermute, dass der Zug Verspätung hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suspect that the train is delayed.

definitions.note: Often used to express an educated guess (like “I suspect/assume”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vermutet, dass er heute zu spät kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I suspect that he’ll be late today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie vermutete, dass er schon zu Hause war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suspected that he was already at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt vermutlich morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will probably come tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vernachlässigt seine Hausaufgaben oft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often neglects his homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat ihre Gesundheit lange vernachlässigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She neglected her health for a long time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vernachlässigte seine Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He neglected his homework.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich verneigen“ = to bow (e.g., in greeting or to show respect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende der Rede verneigte er sich vor dem Publikum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the speech, he bowed to the audience.

definitions.note: Often used for complete destruction (including in figurative contexts, e.g., “to crush/ruin”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Feuer kann ein ganzes Dorf vernichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A fire can destroy an entire village.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Feuer vernichtet das ganze Dorf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire destroys the whole village.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Feuer vernichtete das Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire destroyed the house.

definitions.note: Often sounds formal or literary, especially in the phrase „davon vernommen“ (= heard about it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe davon vernommen, dass du umziehst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard that you’re moving.

definitions.note: Used in police/legal contexts (to question a witness or suspect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zeuge wurde von der Polizei vernommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witness was questioned by the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine vernünftige Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a reasonable decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten vernünftig handeln und zuerst darüber reden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should act sensibly and talk about it first.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine vernünftige Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a reasonable decision.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective (used with a noun, e.g., after an article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen einen vernünftigen Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a reasonable plan.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „vernünftig“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dein Vorschlag ist vernünftiger als meiner.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your suggestion is more reasonable than mine.

definitions.note: Often used after words like „etwas“ or „nichts“ to mean “something/nothing reasonable.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten etwas Vernünftiges essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should eat something sensible.

definitions.note: Most commonly used as the 1st-person singular present (ich verpacke).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verpacke das Geschenk für dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wrapping the present for you.

definitions.native: to pack; to package; to wrap (for transport/sale)
definitions.note: Used for putting something into packaging (box, bag, wrapping) for transport, storage, or sale.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Geschenk in Papier verpacken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will wrap the present in paper.

definitions.note: Often used for missing a bus/train, an appointment, or an opportunity; also used for failing to achieve something (e.g., a goal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verpasse den Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I miss the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will den Zug nicht verpassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to miss the train.

definitions.note: Often used for missing an appointment, train/bus/flight, or an opportunity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Zug verpasst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed the train.

definitions.note: simple past of „verpassen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verpasste den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed the bus.

definitions.note: Older spelling of modern German „verpasst“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Zug verpaßt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed the train.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used when someone tells on another person to an authority figure
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verpetzt mich bei der Lehrerin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He snitches on me to the teacher.

definitions.note: colloquial: to tell on someone (often to the police)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird seinen Freund bei der Polizei verpfeifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will snitch on his friend to the police.

definitions.note: used especially in sports when a referee whistles something (often incorrectly)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Schiedsrichter kann einen Elfmeter verpfeifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The referee can wrongly award a penalty kick.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used with someone being reported to an authority (e.g., the police)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich bei der Polizei verpfiffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ratted me out to the police.

definitions.note: Often used with "zu" + infinitive: "verpflichtet, etwas zu tun".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin verpflichtet, die Regeln einzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am obliged to follow the rules.

definitions.note: Often used for putting an object (or rights/property) up as collateral to get money or secure a loan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er musste seine Uhr verpfänden, um die Miete zu bezahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to pawn his watch to pay the rent.

definitions.native: to get lost, to piss off (go away)
definitions.note: Very informal and rude/vulgar; usually used reflexively: sich verpissen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich jetzt verpissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get out of here now.

definitions.note: very informal and vulgar slang; often used as an insult (similar to “piss off / get the hell out of here”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verpisst sich, bevor die Polizei kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes off before the police arrive.

definitions.note: Informal; implies physical violence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will ihn verprügeln, weil sie sich gestritten haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to beat him up because they argued.

definitions.note: past participle of „verprügeln“; commonly used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat ihn verprügelt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat ihn auf dem Schulhof verprügelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He beat him up in the schoolyard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verrate dich nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won’t betray you.

definitions.note: Often used for giving away a secret or information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verrate dir mein Geheimnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll tell you my secret.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seinen Freund verraten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He betrayed his friend.

definitions.native: to reveal, to give away (a secret)
definitions.note: Often used about revealing a secret or unintentionally giving something away (e.g., feelings).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte verraten Sie niemandem mein Geheimnis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t tell anyone my secret.

definitions.note: colloquial and often rude; also used for machines/devices meaning “stops working”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy verreckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone dies (stops working).

definitions.native: I leave (to travel), I go away (on a trip)
definitions.note: Used when leaving somewhere to go on a trip/journey, often with a destination.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen verreise ich nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m leaving for Berlin.

definitions.native: to go away (on a trip), to travel away
definitions.note: Often implies leaving home for a trip, frequently for vacation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verreisen nächste Woche nach Italien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going away to Italy next week.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to mean someone is away on a trip.
