definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Chefin ist diese Woche verreist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss is away traveling this week.

definitions.note: Used especially to say someone is not at home because they are traveling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Frau Müller ist diese Woche verreist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Mrs. Müller is away traveling this week.

definitions.note: Often used for tasks, duties, or work in a somewhat formal tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute noch einige Aufgaben verrichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to carry out a few tasks today.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal; often used for duties or tasks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verrichtet seine Arbeit sehr sorgfältig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He does his work very carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist verriegelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is locked.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „verraten“; it can mean betraying someone or giving away a secret.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verriet das Geheimnis nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He didn’t reveal the secret.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verrät seinen besten Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He betrays his best friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Blick verrät, dass er müde ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His look reveals that he is tired.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verrätst dein Geheimnis nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t betray your secret.

definitions.note: Often used when something is moved slightly from its original position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte verrücken Sie den Stuhl ein bisschen nach links.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please move the chair a little to the left.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean something is very unusual or wild; can be insulting if used about a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist verrückt!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s crazy!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine verrückte Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a crazy idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat einen verrückten Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a crazy plan.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "verrückt"; can be informal and may sound rude depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Film ist noch verrückter als der letzte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This movie is even crazier than the last one.

definitions.note: Used as a nominalized adjective meaning a person; context decides gender/number (e.g., "ein Verrückter").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Verrückter hat an die Tür geklopft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A crazy person knocked on the door.

definitions.note: General: to fail at a task, under pressure, or to not meet expectations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann nicht versagen, weil er sehr gut vorbereitet ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can’t fail because he is very well prepared.

definitions.native: to break down / to stop working
definitions.note: Used for systems, machines, body parts, or functions that no longer work properly (formal/technical).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn die Technik versagen sollte, gibt es einen Notfallplan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the technology should fail, there is an emergency plan.

definitions.native: to let someone down / to fail someone
definitions.note: Can mean not giving help or support when expected (often in formal contexts: someone is failed by an institution/system).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Staat darf seine Bürger in einer Krise nicht versagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The state must not fail its citizens in a crisis.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Motor versagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The engine fails.

definitions.note: Often used for people, machines, or body parts that stop working (e.g., “Das Gerät versagte.” = “The device failed.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Prüfung versagte er völlig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the exam, he failed completely.

definitions.note: past participle of „versammeln“; often used with „sein“ (e.g., „Die Leute sind versammelt.“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schülerinnen und Schüler sind in der Aula versammelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are gathered in the auditorium.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schüler sind in der Aula versammelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are gathered in the auditorium.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „versammeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer versammelte die Klasse vor der Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher gathered the class in front of the door.

definitions.note: simple past of "versinken"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff versank in der Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship sank during the night.

definitions.note: often used with "in" + dative (e.g., "in Gedanken")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versank in Gedanken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He became absorbed in thought.

definitions.native: to mess up, to screw up, to ruin
definitions.note: Informal/colloquial; can sound a bit crude.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dir den Abend nicht versauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to ruin your evening.

definitions.note: informal; can be rude depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast alles versaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You messed everything up.

definitions.note: often used about jokes or thoughts; informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Witz ist versaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The joke is dirty.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object: jemandem etwas verschaffen = to get/obtain something for someone (often with some effort).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte einen Termin beim Arzt verschaffen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please get me an appointment with the doctor?

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object + direct object (e.g., jemandem etwas verschaffen = to get/procure something for someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verschafft sich einen Überblick über die Lage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gets an overview of the situation.

definitions.note: Used when you give something to someone for free, as a present.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Buch an meine Freundin verschenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to give the book to my friend as a gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund hat die Katzen verscheucht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog chased the cats away.

definitions.note: Often used for sending items (e.g., packages, letters), especially by mail or delivery service.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verschicken das Paket morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll ship the package tomorrow.

definitions.note: past participle of „verschicken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Paket gestern verschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent the package yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for appointments, meetings, or events (putting them to a later time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen das Treffen auf nächste Woche verschieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to postpone the meeting until next week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Meinungen sind verschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The opinions are different.

definitions.note: Used attributively before a noun (e.g., „verschiedene Bücher“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben verschiedene Ideen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have different ideas.

definitions.note: adjective ending used in declined forms (e.g., after an article or in plural/dative contexts)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben mit verschiedenen Leuten gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spoke with different people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kulturen verschiedener Länder sind spannend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cultures of different countries are fascinating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will morgen nicht verschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to oversleep tomorrow.

definitions.native: to get lost, to end up (somewhere by chance)
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich verschlagen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben uns im Wald verschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got lost in the forest.

definitions.note: Used for injuries where something gets knocked out/loose.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Beim Sturz hat er sich einen Zahn verschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the fall, he knocked out a tooth.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive "sich verschlechtern" = "get worse" (e.g., "Die Situation verschlechtert sich").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neue Maßnahme könnte die Lage weiter verschlechtern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new measure could worsen the situation further.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter verschlechtert sich am Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather gets worse in the evening.

definitions.note: Past participle, often used with "hat"/"ist" in the perfect tense (e.g., "hat sich verschlechtert").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Zustand hat sich deutlich verschlechtert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His condition has gotten noticeably worse.

definitions.note: Often used in passive constructions for someone being taken away against their will.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Journalist wurde in der Nacht verschleppt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was abducted during the night.

definitions.note: Used when something (like a task, project, or decision) is unnecessarily postponed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Entscheidung wurde monatelang verschleppt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision was delayed for months.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „verschlafen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verschlief den Wecker und kam zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I overslept the alarm and arrived late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Behandlung verschlimmert sich die Infektion schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without treatment, the infection quickly gets worse.

definitions.note: Can also be used figuratively for things like time, money, or fire (e.g. 'costs a lot', 'engulfs').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund verschlingt sein Futter in zwei Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog devours its food in two minutes.

definitions.note: simple past of „verschließen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verschloss die Tür und ging weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He locked the door and left.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist verschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is closed.

definitions.note: Describes a person who doesn’t show feelings easily or doesn’t talk much.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wirkt sehr verschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seems very reserved.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind verschluckt die Tablette.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child swallows the tablet.

definitions.note: Often used with weather/nature as the subject (e.g., wind, storm): to drive/blow something to a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind verschlug das Boot ans Ufer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind blew the boat to the shore.

definitions.note: Common in the expression "Es verschlug mir die Sprache."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht verschlug mir die Sprache.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news left me speechless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schlange hat die Maus verschlungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snake devoured (swallowed) the mouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fluss ist verschmutzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river is polluted.

definitions.note: simple past of "verschieben"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des Regens verschob er das Spiel auf morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the rain, he postponed the game until tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Termin wurde verschoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The appointment was postponed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Datei wurde in einen anderen Ordner verschoben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The file was moved into another folder.

definitions.note: Often used in contexts where a person or thing has been missing for a long time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wanderer gilt seit drei Tagen als verschollen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hiker has been considered missing for three days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verschone dich dieses Mal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll spare you this time.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (someone) and sometimes with „vor“ + noun: „jemanden vor etwas verschonen“ = to spare someone from something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich vor weiteren Fragen verschonen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to spare you any more questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verschont seinen Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spares his brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Glück wurde das Dorf vom Sturm verschont.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, the village was spared by the storm.

definitions.note: Used especially for medicine ("etwas verschreiben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt hat mir ein Antibiotikum verschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed me an antibiotic.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" ("sich verschreiben") when you write something wrong by mistake.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mich beim Namen verschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote the name incorrectly.

definitions.note: Often used with "die Arme" to mean crossing/folding your arms in front of your chest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verschränkte die Arme und schwieg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He folded his arms and stayed silent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Studierende sind nach dem Studium verschuldet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many students are in debt after their studies.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „verschwinden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich verschwand die Katze unter dem Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly the cat disappeared under the bed.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "verschwinden"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich verschwanden die Wolken, und die Sonne kam heraus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly the clouds disappeared, and the sun came out.

definitions.native: to conceal, to keep quiet about
definitions.note: Often used for intentionally not mentioning something (to withhold information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seiner Frau die Wahrheit verschweigen wollen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to conceal the truth from his wife.

definitions.note: Used as the 1st person singular present ("I waste") or as a command to one person ("waste!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verschwende keine Zeit mit unnötigen Meetings.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t waste any time on unnecessary meetings.

definitions.note: Often used for wasting money, time, or resources (especially by using them carelessly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er darf sein Geld nicht verschwenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He must not waste his money.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verschwendest deine Zeit mit diesem Spiel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're wasting your time with this game.

definitions.note: Used as a conjugated form of "verschwenden" (to waste).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verschwendet sein Geld für unnötige Dinge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wastes his money on unnecessary things.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular): a command to one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verschwinde bitte aus meinem Zimmer!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go away from my room, please!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Plötzlich musste der Mann in der Menge verschwinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly the man had to disappear into the crowd.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum verschwindest du einfach, ohne etwas zu sagen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you just disappear without saying anything?

definitions.note: third-person singular present tense of "verschwinden"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Fleck verschwindet nach dem Waschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stain disappears after washing.

definitions.note: past participle often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist verschwunden“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Schlüssel ist verschwunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My key has disappeared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Schlüssel ist verschwunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My key has disappeared.

definitions.native: related by marriage, related through in-laws
definitions.note: Used when two people/families are connected through marriage (in-laws).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind verschwägert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re related by marriage.

definitions.note: past participle of „verschütten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Kaffee verschüttet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spilled coffee.

definitions.note: often used for people/objects covered by something like rubble or snow
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arbeiter wurde unter den Trümmern verschüttet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The worker was buried under the rubble.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verschüttete den Kaffee auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spilled the coffee on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe versehentlich die falsche Datei gelöscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accidentally deleted the wrong file.

definitions.note: Often used for sending goods, packages, or mail (e.g., by a company or online shop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versenden die Bestellung morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll send out the order tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past participle of „versenken“; often used for sinking a ship/boat (or more generally lowering/submerging something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das U-Boot hat das Schiff versenkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The submarine sank the ship.

definitions.note: Often used as the past participle meaning someone/something caused another thing (e.g., a ship) to sink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das U-Boot hat das Schiff versenkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The submarine sank the ship.

definitions.note: Often used when someone is moved to a different position, department, or location (e.g., by an employer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma wird ihn nach Berlin versetzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company will transfer him to Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used for transferring someone (e.g., an employee) to a different location or department.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma versetzt ihn nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company transfers him to Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used for being moved to a different job location or position (e.g., by an employer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma versetzte ihn nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company transferred him to Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive dative: „Ich versichere dir …“ = “I assure you …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versichere dir, dass ich morgen pünktlich bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assure you that I will be on time tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g. jemanden/etwas versichern) in the sense of taking out insurance for someone/something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mein Auto versichern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to insure my car.

definitions.note: Used to tell someone firmly that something is true (e.g. jemandem etwas versichern).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dich versichern, dass ich die Wahrheit sage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to assure you that I’m telling the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto ist versichert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is insured.

definitions.note: Often used with a person as the object (e.g., jemanden versichern), meaning to state something confidently to make them feel sure.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versicherte mir, dass alles in Ordnung war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He assured me that everything was fine.

definitions.note: Used in the sense of arranging insurance coverage (e.g., ein Auto versichern).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie versicherte ihr Auto im letzten Jahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She insured her car last year.

definitions.note: Used when something like a river, spring, or source of help/ideas stops flowing/producing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Sommer versiegt der Bach oft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, the stream often dries up.

definitions.native: to take care of, to provide for
definitions.note: Often used for looking after people/animals or ensuring someone has what they need (e.g., food, supplies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich um meine Großmutter kümmern und sie versorgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to look after my grandmother and take care of her.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“ + dative for supplying something (e.g., a city) with something (e.g., water).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt muss die Haushalte mit Wasser versorgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city has to supply households with water.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone has what they need (e.g., food, care, support).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind gut versorgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are well provided for.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder sind gut versorgt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are well taken care of.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versorgte die Gäste mit Essen und Getränken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He supplied the guests with food and drinks.

definitions.note: Past participle of „verspielen“; often used with things like a lead, advantage, or chance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seinen Vorsprung verspielt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He squandered his lead.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verspottet seinen Freund vor allen anderen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He mocks his friend in front of everyone else.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „versprechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versprach mir, morgen anzurufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He promised me that he would call tomorrow.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verspreche dir, dass ich morgen anrufe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I promise you that I’ll call tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir etwas versprechen: Ich rufe dich morgen an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will promise you something: I’ll call you tomorrow.

definitions.note: often 2nd person plural present tense (ihr)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr versprecht mir, pünktlich zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You promise me to be on time.

definitions.note: can also be the informal plural imperative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versprecht mir, dass ihr vorsichtig seid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Promise me that you’re careful.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative: used to tell one person to promise something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versprich mir, dass du morgen anrufst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Promise me that you’ll call tomorrow.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du versprichst mir, dass du morgen anrufst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You promise me that you’ll call tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verspricht, morgen pünktlich zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He promises to be on time tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe es dir versprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I promised you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist versprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is promised.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: „ich verspäte mich“ = “I’m late.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verspäte mich heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm late today.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: sich verspäten = to be late / to be delayed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mich heute wahrscheinlich verspäten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will probably be late today.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g. „Der Zug ist verspätet.“) to say something/someone is running late.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist heute verspätet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is delayed today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist verspätet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is late.

definitions.note: Often used with "sich" to mean “was late” (e.g. "Der Zug verspätete sich").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug verspätete sich um zehn Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train was delayed by ten minutes.

definitions.note: Often used for noticing an internal feeling (e.g., hunger, pain, relief), sometimes in a slightly formal tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verspüre keinen Hunger.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t feel hungry.

definitions.note: Often used for noticing/feeling something (especially an emotion, pain, or desire).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verspürte plötzlich Angst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She suddenly felt fear.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „verstehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verstand die Frage nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't understand the question.

definitions.note: past participle of „verstehen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „Ich habe verstanden.“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich verstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood you.

definitions.note: past tense (simple past) form of "versterben"; formal/official, used especially in announcements or reports
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Autor verstarb im Jahr 2005.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The author died in 2005.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versteck dich hinter dem Baum!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hide behind the tree!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verstecke den Schlüssel unter der Matte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hide the key under the mat.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum versteckst du das Buch unter dem Bett?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you hiding the book under the bed?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versteckt den Schlüssel unter der Matte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hides the key under the mat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Café ist in einer kleinen Seitenstraße versteckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The café is hidden on a small side street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versteckte den Schlüssel unter der Fußmatte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hid the key under the doormat.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal singular command (short for „verstehe!“) or as a colloquial short form of „verstehe“ (“I understand”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versteh mich bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please understand me.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I understand").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verstehe die Frage nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't understand the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann das nicht verstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't understand that.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form of "verstehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verstehst du die Frage?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand the question?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "verstehen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versteht die Frage nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn't understand the question.

definitions.note: Often used literally for fossils/wood; can also be used figuratively to mean emotionally rigid or stiff.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Holz ist im Laufe der Zeit versteinert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wood became petrified over time.

definitions.native: to adjust, to set (e.g. a clock)
definitions.note: Often used for setting/adjusting a device, especially a clock or watch.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Uhr verstellen, weil wir in einer anderen Zeitzone sind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to adjust the clock because we’re in a different time zone.

definitions.native: to pretend, to put on an act
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich verstellen = to pretend (to be different than you are).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst dich nicht verstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t have to pretend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verstellt die Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He adjusts the clock.

definitions.note: Often used with Stimme (voice) or Verhalten (behavior).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verstellt ihre Stimme am Telefon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She disguises her voice on the phone.

definitions.note: used especially for musical instruments
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Gitarre ist verstimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My guitar is out of tune.

definitions.note: describes someone’s mood
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist heute etwas verstimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s a bit upset today.

definitions.note: often used for a blocked nose or a clogged drain/pipe
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Nase ist verstopft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My nose is blocked.

definitions.note: Often used as a more formal or polite way to say someone died.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Großvater ist 2020 verstorben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather died in 2020.

definitions.note: Formal/polite way to say someone has died; often used in obituaries and official contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben über die verstorbene Nachbarin gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked about the deceased neighbor.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective to describe someone who has died (often in formal contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gedenken der verstorbenen Angehörigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We remember the deceased relatives.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst nicht gegen die Regeln verstoßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not break the rules.

definitions.note: Often used for rejecting someone from a family or community.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Familie hat gedroht, ihn zu verstoßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His family threatened to disown him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Unterlagen liegen verstreut auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents are scattered on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute bin ich etwas verstreut und vergesse dauernd Dinge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm a bit absent-minded and keep forgetting things.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als sie das hörte, verstummte sie sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When she heard that, she fell silent immediately.

definitions.note: Often used for notifying authorities (e.g., die Polizei verständigen). It does not simply mean “to understand” (that’s verstehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Polizei verständigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to notify the police.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: jemanden verständigen = to notify someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat uns sofort verständigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police notified us immediately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deine Erklärung war sehr verständlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your explanation was very understandable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er war verständlicherweise enttäuscht, als der Flug abgesagt wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was understandably disappointed when the flight was canceled.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meine Chefin ist sehr verständnisvoll, wenn jemand krank ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss is very understanding when someone is sick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Brücke verstärken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to reinforce the bridge.

definitions.note: Used for sound/signals (e.g., music, radio, an effect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Musik bitte verstärken?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn up the music?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wind verstärkt sich am Nachmittag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind intensifies in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who seems unsettled or confused after something unpleasant or shocking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall war er völlig verstört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was completely shaken.

definitions.note: Often used with "gegen" + accusative (e.g. "gegen das Gesetz").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verstößt gegen die Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He violates the rules.

definitions.note: Used when a person is rejected by their family or community (e.g. "Die Familie verstößt ihn").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Familie verstößt ihn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His family disowns him.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive), used for hypotheticals/polite phrasing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verstünde das besser, wenn du es mir noch einmal erklären würdest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would understand that better if you explained it to me one more time.

definitions.note: From the verb „versuchen“ (to try).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuch, das heute noch zu machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to do that today.

definitions.note: can mean either “I try” or “(you) try” depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, jeden Tag ein bisschen Deutsch zu lernen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to learn a little German every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuchen, heute früher nach Hause zu kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to get home earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used with „zu“ + infinitive (e.g., „versuchen, etwas zu machen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, das Problem zu lösen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re attempting to solve the problem.

definitions.note: Colloquial contraction of the imperative „versuch’s“ (= „versuch es“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Versuchs noch mal!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Try it again!

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "versuchen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du versuchst, pünktlich zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You try to be on time.

definitions.note: Commonly used as the 3rd person singular present tense of „versuchen“ (he/she/it tries).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, pünktlich zu sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to be on time.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ and an infinitive clause: „Ich bin versucht, …“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin versucht, das zu kaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m tempted to buy that.

definitions.note: Simple past form of "versuchen" (used with ich/er/sie/es).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versuchte, die Tür zu öffnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to open the door.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchten, den Zug noch zu erreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We tried to still catch the train.

definitions.note: Past participle of „versinken“. Can also be used figuratively to mean “lost/deeply absorbed (in thought)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schiff ist im Meer versunken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship has sunk in the sea.

definitions.note: Can also be used as the past participle meaning “missed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versäumt den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He misses the bus.

definitions.note: often used for meetings, sessions, or court proceedings
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Sitzung wird auf nächste Woche vertagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting is postponed until next week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verteidige meine Meinung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I defend my opinion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen unsere Stadt verteidigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to defend our city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verteidigt seinen Freund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He defends his friend.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "verteidigen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verteidigte seine Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He defended his girlfriend.

definitions.note: Used for handing out or distributing items, information, or tasks among multiple people/places; separable verb: verteilt, verteilte, hat verteilt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer muss die Arbeitsblätter an die Schüler verteilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher has to distribute the worksheets to the students.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin verteilt die Arbeitsblätter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher hands out the worksheets.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective in German (e.g., "Die Aufgaben sind verteilt.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aufgaben sind gleichmäßig verteilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tasks are distributed evenly.

definitions.note: often used with „in“ + dative (e.g. „vertieft in ein Buch“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist vertieft in sein Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is absorbed in his book.

definitions.note: often used to describe learning or discussion (e.g. „vertiefte Kenntnisse“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben eine vertiefte Diskussion geführt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had an in-depth discussion.

definitions.native: to tolerate, to put up with
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Lärm nicht vertragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't tolerate the noise.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about whether your body can handle a food or drink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann keine Milch vertragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't digest milk / My body can't handle milk.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „vertreten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vertrat seine Kollegin im Meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He represented his colleague in the meeting.

definitions.note: Commonly used as the informal singular imperative (“Trust!”), and also as the 1st/3rd person singular present subjunctive (“that I/he/she trust”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vertrau mir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Trust me!

definitions.note: From the separable verb „anvertrauen“; in a sentence the prefix „an“ often comes at the end (e.g. „Ich vertraue … an.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vertraue dir meine Schlüssel an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entrust you with my keys.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I trust") or imperative ("trust!") depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vertraue dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust you.

definitions.note: Common patterns: „jemandem vertrauen“ (to trust someone), „auf etwas vertrauen“ (to rely on something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dir vertrauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to trust you.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“: „auf etwas vertrauen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir vertrauen auf deine Erfahrung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We rely on your experience.

definitions.native: to confide (in someone) / to entrust (something to someone)
definitions.note: In some contexts it can imply confiding or entrusting, depending on what follows in the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst mir vertrauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can trust me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr vertrauenswürdig und hält ihr Wort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very trustworthy and keeps her word.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Informationen sind vertraulich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is confidential.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum vertraust du mir nicht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you trust me?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vertraut dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He trusts you.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object: jemandem vertrauen = to trust someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vertraut mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He trusts me.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit + dative“: „mit etwas vertraut“ = familiar with something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit dieser Software nicht vertraut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not familiar with this software.

definitions.note: Describes a person or relationship you know well and feel you can trust.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist eine vertraute Kollegin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a trusted colleague.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of the separable verb „anvertrauen“; often used with „an“ at the end of the clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vertraute ihm mein Geheimnis an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I entrusted him with my secret.

definitions.native: to chase away, to drive away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Mücken vertreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to chase the mosquitoes away.

definitions.note: often used for companies selling/distributing products
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma will diese Software in Europa vertreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company wants to sell/distribute this software in Europe.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm vertreibt die Vögel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise drives the birds away.

definitions.note: Often used for companies selling or distributing products.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma vertreibt Software in Europa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company sells/distributes software in Europe.

definitions.native: represent, stand in for (fill in for)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute vertrete ich meine Kollegin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m filling in for my colleague.

definitions.note: also commonly: to stand in for someone (e.g., at work)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute muss ich meine Kollegin vertreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I have to cover for my colleague.

definitions.note: often used reflexively: sich den Fuß/Knöchel vertreten
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich den Fuß vertreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sprained his foot.

definitions.note: past participle of „vertreiben“; often used in passive or perfect tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen wurden aus ihrer Heimat vertrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people were driven out of their homeland.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" (e.g., "ist verunglückt"); can imply a serious accident.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern auf dem Heimweg verunglückt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had an accident yesterday on the way home.

definitions.note: Often used for problems, damage, or costs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm kann große Schäden verursachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm can cause major damage.

definitions.note: past participle of „verursachen“; often used with „hat“ (e.g. „hat … verursacht“) or as an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm hat große Schäden verursacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm caused major damage.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm verursachte große Schäden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm caused major damage.

definitions.note: Used in legal contexts (court decisions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gericht wird ihn verurteilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The court will convict/sentence him.

definitions.note: Often used for expressing moral or political disapproval.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen verurteilen die Gewalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people condemn the violence.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts, typically in the passive (e.g. „wurde … verurteilt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde zu zwei Jahren Haft verurteilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sentenced to two years in prison.

definitions.note: Used when someone/something is publicly criticized as wrong or unacceptable (often in the passive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gewalt wird von vielen Menschen verurteilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The violence is condemned by many people.

definitions.note: Often used with „in“ + accusative: „etwas in etwas verwandeln“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zauberer kann einen Frosch in einen Prinzen verwandeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wizard can transform a frog into a prince.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (you transform / you turn into).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du verwandelst Wasser in Eis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You turn water into ice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zauberer verwandelt den Frosch in einen Prinzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wizard turns the frog into a prince.

definitions.note: simple past form of „verwandeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Hexe verwandelte den Prinzen in einen Frosch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The witch transformed the prince into a frog.

definitions.note: Often used with „mit“: „mit jemandem verwandt sein“ = to be related to someone (by family).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit Anna verwandt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m related to Anna.

definitions.note: Colloquial; means secretly fitted with microphones/recording devices.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Büro ist verwantzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The office is bugged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verwechsele oft die Namen der beiden Brüder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often mix up the two brothers' names.

definitions.native: to mix up, to confuse (one thing/person with another)
definitions.note: Often used with “mit” (e.g., „A mit B verwechseln“ = to confuse A with B).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann manchmal Namen verwechseln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can sometimes mix up names.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verwechselt die Namen oft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often mixes up the names.

definitions.note: past participle (used with "haben" in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Termin verwechselt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mixed up the appointment.

definitions.note: simple past form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verwechselte seinen Bruder mit ihm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I mistook his brother for him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein verwegener Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a daring plan.

definitions.note: Often used with an object; common patterns include „etwas verweigern“ and „jemandem etwas verweigern“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird die Hilfe verweigern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will refuse the help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verweigert die Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He refuses the help.

definitions.note: Often used in a slightly formal sense of staying somewhere for a while.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir verweilen noch eine Weile im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stay in the park for a little while longer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Blume ist schon verwelkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flower has already wilted.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich) or imperative (du) of "verwenden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verwende für die Suppe frisches Gemüse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I use fresh vegetables for the soup.

definitions.note: often used for using something for a particular purpose
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde diese App jeden Tag verwenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will use this app every day.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wofür verwendest du dieses Werkzeug?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you use this tool for?

definitions.note: Often means "used" in the sense of "utilized" (e.g., used for a purpose).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Material wird oft in der Küche verwendet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This material is often used in the kitchen.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "verwenden"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verwendete für den Kuchen nur frische Eier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She used only fresh eggs for the cake.

definitions.note: Often used with „in + Akkusativ“ (e.g. „in einen Skandal verwickelt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist in einen Skandal verwickelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is involved in a scandal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Geschichte ist ziemlich verwickelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The story is pretty complicated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine verwickelte Situation.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a complicated situation.

definitions.note: Often used with „in“ to say someone is involved in something (e.g. a conflict or a scandal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist in einen Streit verwickelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is involved in an argument.

definitions.native: to realize, to make (something) come true
definitions.note: Often used with goals, dreams, plans, or ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will ihren Traum verwirklichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to make her dream come true.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verwirklicht ihren Traum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She realizes her dream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seinen Plan verwirklicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has realized his plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die vielen Regeln verwirren mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The many rules confuse me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die vielen Regeln sind wirklich verwirrend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The many rules are really confusing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine verwirrende Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a confusing question.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective or past participle (e.g., with „sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin verwirrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am confused.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das verwirrt mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That confuses me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gerade total verwirrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m totally confused right now.

definitions.note: describes someone whose spouse has died
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit drei Jahren ist sie verwitwet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been widowed for three years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vorschlag wurde vom Vorstand verworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The proposal was rejected by the board.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schwer verwundet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is badly wounded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Soldat ist verwundet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldier is wounded.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich verwählen“ = to dial the wrong number.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entschuldigung, ich habe mich verwählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I dialed the wrong number.

definitions.native: to pamper; to spoil (in a positive, indulgent way)
definitions.note: Used when you treat someone especially well with extra comfort, attention, or treats.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dich heute so richtig verwöhnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to really pamper you today.

definitions.note: Usually describes a child or person who is used to getting what they want because they have been indulged a lot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind ist sehr verwöhnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is very spoiled.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who is treated very well (e.g., with comfort or luxury).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Urlaub fühle ich mich richtig verwöhnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On vacation I feel really pampered.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das verwöhnte Kind will alles sofort haben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The spoiled child wants to have everything right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm hat die Küste verwüstet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm devastated the coast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verzehrt einen Apfel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He eats an apple.

definitions.note: Singular informal imperative of „verzeihen“; often used as an apology (like “sorry” or “excuse me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verzeih mir bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please forgive me.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite apology or to get someone’s attention (like “excuse me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verzeihe mir bitte, ich habe es vergessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please forgive me, I forgot it.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object in the dative (jemandem verzeihen = to forgive someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir verzeihen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you forgive me?

definitions.note: Used when speaking to one person (informal “du” form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verzeihst du mir, dass ich zu spät bin?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you forgive me for being late?

definitions.note: Used with the informal plural “ihr” (you all) and also as the plural imperative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verzeiht mir bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please forgive me.

definitions.note: Polite; often used to apologize or to get someone’s attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verzeihung, können Sie mir helfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, can you help me?

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative: „auf etwas verzichten“ = to do without something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich verzichte heute auf Süßigkeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving up sweets today.

definitions.native: to do without, to give up
definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative: „auf etwas verzichten“ = to do without / give up something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute auf Süßigkeiten verzichten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to do without sweets today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er verzieh ihr den Fehler.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forgave her for the mistake.

definitions.note: Often used for things like smoke/fog (e.g. „Der Rauch verzieht sich.“) or in the reflexive form „sich verziehen“ meaning to leave/clear off.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Rauch verzieh nach ein paar Minuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smoke dissipated after a few minutes.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich verziehen“ (e.g., wood, metal, paper).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Holz kann sich verziehen, wenn es nass wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wood can warp when it gets wet.

definitions.native: to pull a face, to grimace
definitions.note: Common with „das Gesicht verziehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann das Gesicht verziehen, weil es so sauer schmeckt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can pull a face because it tastes so sour.

definitions.note: Meaning: to raise too indulgently.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Großeltern verziehen die Kinder ein bisschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grandparents spoil the children a little.

definitions.note: Often used about raising children (to spoil a child).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie verzieht ihren Sohn total.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She totally spoils her son.

definitions.note: Used when something loses its shape (e.g., wood, metal, fabric).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durch die Feuchtigkeit verzieht sich das Holz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the moisture, the wood warps.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war verzweifelt und wusste nicht, was sie tun sollte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was desperate and didn’t know what to do.

definitions.note: often implies being in despair or feeling hopeless
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er suchte verzweifelt nach seinem Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He desperately looked for his phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen unsere Strategie verändern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to change our strategy.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective meaning “changed/altered,” or as the 3rd-person singular present tense of the verb „verändern“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat alles verändert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That changed everything.

definitions.note: simple past form of "verändern"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich veränderte den Text ein bisschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I changed the text a little bit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind war verängstigt und wollte nicht allein bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child was scared and didn’t want to stay alone.

definitions.note: Often used meaning to make someone (feel) angry or irritated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich nicht verärgern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to upset you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das verärgert mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That annoys me.

definitions.note: Often used for a person’s (slight to moderate) irritated mood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin verärgert über die Verspätung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed about the delay.

definitions.note: Past tense form of "verärgern" (to annoy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die laute Musik verärgerte die Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loud music annoyed the neighbors.

definitions.note: Used for making something public (e.g., an article, book, photo, announcement, or results).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeitung wird den Artikel morgen veröffentlichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper will publish the article tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used for making something public (e.g., an article, book, announcement) and is also used for publishing something online.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zeitung veröffentlicht heute einen neuen Artikel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The newspaper publishes a new article today.

definitions.note: Past participle of "verüben"; commonly used with crimes or wrongdoing (e.g., "ein Verbrechen verüben").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat die Tat allein verübt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed the act alone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Handy vibriert in meiner Tasche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone vibrates in my pocket.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs and adjectives/adverbs (e.g., „viel lernen“, „viel besser“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lerne viel für die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study a lot for the exam.

definitions.note: Used with uncountable nouns (= much) and plural countable nouns (= many).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe viel Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of time.

definitions.note: Often used with uncountable nouns or in general statements (e.g., „viel Wasser“, „viel zu tun“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute viel zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot to do today.

definitions.note: Used with plural (countable) nouns; for uncountable nouns you usually use „viel“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Menschen sprechen Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people speak German.

definitions.note: Used with plural nouns (or as a pronoun referring to a plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Leute haben heute frei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people have the day off today.

definitions.note: dative plural form of the determiner „viel“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe vielen Leuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help many people.

definitions.note: Dative plural form of "viel"/"viele" (often used with plural nouns, e.g. "mit vielen Freunden").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe vielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help many (people).

definitions.note: Used with plural nouns (often in the dative case, e.g. after certain prepositions like "mit").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche mit vielen Freunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m talking with many friends.

definitions.note: Genitive form of "viel" (often used in more formal/written German).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Ideen scheitern an vieler Kritik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many ideas fail because of a lot of criticism.

definitions.note: Neuter singular form used as a pronoun meaning “a lot/much (of it)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vieles ist heute anders als früher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A lot is different today than in the past.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vielleicht komme ich morgen vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maybe I'll stop by tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used as an intensifier in set phrases like “vielmals danke” (“many thanks”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vielmals danke für deine Hilfe!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many thanks for your help!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das klingt sehr vielversprechend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That sounds very promising.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein vielversprechender Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a promising plan.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe vier Brüder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have four brothers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war schon viermal in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already been to Berlin four times.

definitions.note: ordinal number; form used with feminine nouns (and sometimes with plural nouns in certain case endings)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wohnt in der vierten Etage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives on the fourth floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne im vierten Stock.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live on the fourth floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein vierter Versuch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a fourth attempt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin vierundzwanzig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twenty-four years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin vierzehn Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fourteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dieses Jahr vierzig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m turning forty this year.

definitions.note: Used as a cheer or chant, often before a person or country (e.g., “Viva …!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viva die Freiheit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Long live freedom!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Flasche ist voll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bottle is full.

definitions.note: Often used about places that have a lot of people (e.g., "Der Bus ist voll.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus ist heute Morgen voll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is crowded this morning.

definitions.note: Often used with the genitive in more formal/fixed expressions (e.g. „voll des Lobes“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist voll des Lobes für seine Kollegin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is full of praise for his colleague.

definitions.note: colloquial/informal; often used to emphasize an adjective (e.g. „voll schön“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist voll schön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really nice.

definitions.note: past participle of „vollbringen“; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist vollbracht“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Werk ist vollbracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The work is accomplished.

definitions.note: Often used for something important or difficult; sounds a bit formal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will heute etwas Großes vollbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to accomplish something great today.

definitions.note: attributive form of "voll" (used before a noun, e.g. with "eine", "die")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte eine volle Tasse Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a full cup of coffee.

definitions.note: dative masculine or neuter (often after a preposition like „mit“ or „zu“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Schüssel ist mit vollem Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bowl is filled with full water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen vollen Teller.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a full plate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie vollendet das Bild heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She finishes the picture today.

definitions.note: comparative form of "voll" (full)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas ist voller als vorher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is fuller than before.

definitions.note: Used as a preposition with the genitive (often replaced by dative in everyday speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Garten ist voller Blumen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden is full of flowers.

definitions.note: Used like a preposition, usually with the genitive (common in phrases like „ein … voller …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Glas voller Wasser steht auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A glass full of water is on the table.

definitions.note: inflected form of „voll“, used with a neuter singular noun (e.g. „ein volles Glas“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ein volles Glas Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a full glass of water.

definitions.note: Used mainly for people who have reached the legal age (often 18 in Germany).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In Deutschland ist man mit 18 Jahren volljährig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Germany, you are of legal age at 18.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine vollkommen normale Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a completely normal question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist vollkommen in Ordnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is completely fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein vollkommener Idiot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a complete idiot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Formular vollständig ausgefüllt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filled out the form completely.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die vollständigen Unterlagen dabei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the complete documents with me.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „vollständig“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Liste ist vollständiger als die alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This list is more complete than the old one.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal contexts (e.g., for actions, decisions, reforms).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei vollzog den Haftbefehl am frühen Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police carried out the arrest warrant early in the morning.

definitions.note: contraction of „von dem“ (dative masculine/neuter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme vom Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from the train station.

definitions.note: Takes the dative case; often contracts to "vom" (= von dem).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme von der Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming from work.

definitions.note: Takes the dative case; used to show association/possession or who something is by.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein Foto von meiner Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a photo of my sister.

definitions.native: from each other, apart (from each other)
definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „lernen“, „trennen“, „unterscheiden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Kinder lernen viel voneinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two children learn a lot from each other.

definitions.note: Usually followed by the dative case in time expressions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich stehe vor sechs Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get up before six o’clock.

definitions.note: For places, it’s a two-way preposition: dative for location (no movement), accusative for direction (movement).
