definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto steht vor dem Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is in front of the house.

definitions.note: Used with a time expression.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin vor zwei Tagen angekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived two days ago.

definitions.note: As an adverb it’s most often used in fixed phrases like „wie vor“ (= as before).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alles ist wie vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is as before.

definitions.note: Often used as a two-way preposition: with dative for location (no movement) and accusative for movement; with time it can mean “ago” (e.g. vor zwei Tagen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus hält vor dem Hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stops in front of the hotel.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“, „kommen“, „stehen“ to describe position or movement forward.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh schon mal voran, ich komme gleich nach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go ahead; I’ll follow in a moment.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like „es geht voran“ (things are progressing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit dem Projekt geht es endlich voran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is finally moving forward.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen/fahren“ or in set phrases like „voran gehen“ (= to lead the way).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh schon mal voran, ich komme gleich nach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go on ahead; I'll be right behind you.

definitions.note: Most commonly used in the fixed phrase „im Voraus“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Danke, dass du im Voraus bezahlst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for paying in advance.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen/fahren“ (ahead) or in phrases like „im Voraus“ (in advance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe voraus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll go ahead.

definitions.note: Often used with a verb (e.g., vorausgehen = go ahead) or in set phrases like „im Voraus“ (in advance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh du schon mal voraus, ich komme gleich nach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You go ahead; I’ll follow right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorausgesetzt, dass es morgen nicht regnet, gehen wir spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Provided that it doesn’t rain tomorrow, we’ll go for a walk.

definitions.note: Often used with an + dative to mean going/coming past something (e.g. am Park vorbei).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus fährt am Bahnhof vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus drives past the train station.

definitions.note: Often used to mean that something has ended (e.g., an event or a difficult time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Urlaub ist leider vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, the vacation is over.

definitions.note: Often used with sein/gehen/kommen to say something has ended (e.g. „Die Ferien sind vorbei.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Unterricht ist vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The class is over.

definitions.native: to drive past, pass by (in a vehicle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden am Bahnhof vorbeifahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will drive past the train station.

definitions.note: Past participle of „vorbeifahren“; in the perfect tense it’s usually used with „sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern an meinem Haus vorbeigefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drove past my house yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „vorbeigehen“, often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus ist schon vorbeigegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus has already passed by.

definitions.native: to walk past, to go past (something/someone)
definitions.note: Often used with "an (+ dative)" or "bei (+ dative)" to indicate what you pass by.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen am Park vorbei, ohne anzuhalten, sondern wir lassen ihn einfach vorbeigehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk past the park without stopping; we just let it go by.

definitions.note: past participle of „vorbeikommen“ (often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist gestern Abend kurz vorbeigekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dropped by briefly last night.

definitions.native: to come by, to drop by
definitions.note: Often used for an informal visit or stopping somewhere briefly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du morgen bei mir vorbeikommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come by my place tomorrow?

definitions.native: would come by, would come past
definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of „vorbeikommen“, often used for hypotheticals or polite/indirect phrasing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wäre froh, wenn du heute Abend vorbeikäme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d be happy if you came by this evening.

definitions.note: Often used for a short, informal visit.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen bei dir vorbeischauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll drop by at your place tomorrow.

definitions.native: to come by, to stop by
definitions.note: Used with an implied/explicit destination (often with „bei“ + person/place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute keine Zeit, vorbeizukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have time to stop by today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich auf die Prüfung vorbereiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to prepare for the exam.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g. „Ich bin vorbereitet.“ = “I am prepared.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gut vorbereitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am well prepared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gut vorbereitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am well prepared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaube, dass unser Leben vorbestimmt ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believe that our life is predestined.

definitions.note: Often used for presenting an argument, point, or proposal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte einen Vorschlag vorbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to put forward a suggestion.

definitions.note: Used for people, opinions, or reporting that is not neutral.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Richter darf nicht voreingenommen sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge must not be biased.

definitions.note: Usually used with something being withheld from someone: jemandem etwas vorenthalten.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man hat uns wichtige Informationen vorenthalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They withheld important information from us.

definitions.native: for now, for the time being
definitions.note: Used to indicate something is temporary and may change later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bleibe vorerst zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For now, I'm staying at home.

definitions.note: Past participle of „vorfallen“, typically used with „sein“ (e.g., „ist vorgefallen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Nacht ist etwas Seltsames vorgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something strange happened during the night.

definitions.note: Past participle of „vorfallen“, usually used with „sein“ (e.g. „ist vorgefallen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist gestern so vorgefallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s how it happened yesterday.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of „vorfinden“, meaning to find something in a certain state (often when arriving somewhere).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Wohnung sauber vorgefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found the apartment clean.

definitions.note: Past participle of "vorhaben"; commonly used with "haben" (e.g., "ich habe ... vorgehabt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das nicht vorgehabt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't plan that.

definitions.native: to proceed, to go about (doing something)
definitions.note: Often used with an adverb like „vorsichtig“ (carefully) or „systematisch“ (systematically).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen vorsichtig vorgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to proceed carefully.

definitions.note: From "vorgehen"; often used in the phrase "Was geht vor?" (= "What’s going on?").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß nicht, was hier vorgeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know what's going on here.

definitions.note: Past participle of „vorlesen“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat … vorgelesen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Kindern eine Geschichte vorgelesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He read a story aloud to the children.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive dative: „sich (etwas) vornehmen“ = to plan/resolve to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir für dieses Jahr viel vorgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planned a lot for this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat einen neuen Termin vorgeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suggested a new date.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is scheduled or meant to happen/be used in a certain way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Für diesen Zweck ist das Geld nicht vorgesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The money is not intended for this purpose.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “provided for” or “specified” in a plan, schedule, or rules.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist nicht vorgesehen, dass Kinder hier allein bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is not intended for children to stay here alone.

definitions.note: past participle of „vorstellen“ (often used with „haben“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef hat die neue Kollegin vorgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss introduced the new colleague.

definitions.note: often used with „sich vorstellen“ (= to imagine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir das anders vorgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagined it differently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind vorgestern nach Berlin gefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went to Berlin the day before yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of „vorwerfen“ (often used with „haben“: „hat … vorgeworfen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir vorgeworfen, dass ich gelogen habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accused me of lying.

definitions.note: Often appears in subordinate clauses (e.g. after „dass“). It can also be Konjunktiv I in reported speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass ich morgen früher nach Hause vorhabe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that I intend to go home earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a separable verb (e.g., „Ich habe … vor.“). Also appears as the noun „das Vorhaben“ = “plan/project/undertaking”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute Abend vor, früh ins Bett zu gehen, aber ich muss noch einiges vorhaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I plan to go to bed early tonight, but I still have quite a few things planned to do.

definitions.note: Often used in a factual/official way (e.g., about resources, documents, information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Genug Wasser ist vorhanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Enough water is available.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „vorhaben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was vorhast du morgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you planning to do tomorrow?

definitions.note: Used mainly in subordinate clauses; in main clauses it usually splits: „hat … vor“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sagt, dass sie morgen früher zu gehen vorhat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She says that she plans to leave earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (ich/er/sie/es) of "vorhaben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vorhatte, heute früher nach Hause zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planned to go home earlier today.

definitions.note: Past tense of "vorhaben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir vorhatten, heute früher nach Hause zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We planned to go home earlier today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich rufe dich vorher an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll call you beforehand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat niemand vorhergesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nobody predicted that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Niemand konnte den Unfall vorhersehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No one could foresee the accident.

definitions.native: a little while ago, earlier (just now)
definitions.note: Refers to a short time earlier (typically today or in the recent past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn vorhin im Supermarkt gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him a little while ago at the supermarket.

definitions.note: Used before a noun; often with a definite article (e.g., „die vorige Woche“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letzte Woche war stressig, aber die vorige Woche war noch schlimmer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last week was stressful, but the previous week was even worse.

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter singular form of "vorig" (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dem vorigem Treffen hatte ich keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the previous meeting, I didn’t have time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im vorigen Jahr war ich in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I was in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used to refer to the one immediately before the current one (e.g., last year, previous week).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voriges Jahr war der Winter sehr kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year, the winter was very cold.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about time (e.g., previous year/month).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voriges Jahr waren wir in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year we were in Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used with "es kann vorkommen, dass ..." (= it can happen that ...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es kann vorkommen, dass der Zug spät ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It can happen that the train is late.

definitions.native: to be found, to occur (in a place/text)
definitions.note: Often used with "in" to say something exists or appears somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Wort kann in dem Text oft vorkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word can occur often in the text.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „vorkommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas vorkommt hier oft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something like that happens here often.

definitions.note: Often used for reading something to someone (e.g., a story or a text).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte die Geschichte vorlesen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please read the story aloud to me?

definitions.native: to be available; to be present; to exist (in a given case)
definitions.note: Often used in formal/official contexts. Commonly appears as „etw. liegt vor“ (3rd person singular) / „etw. liegen vor“ (plural), meaning that something (e.g., information, evidence, a condition) is present/available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zum Zeitpunkt der Entscheidung muss ein schriftliches Gutachten vorliegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the time of the decision, a written expert report must be available.

definitions.native: to be at hand / on file (documents, data, applications)
definitions.note: Frequently used in administration and business when stating that something has been received and is available for processing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Antrag kann erst bearbeitet werden, wenn alle Unterlagen vollständig vorliegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The application can only be processed once all documents are fully on file.

definitions.native: (law/medicine) to be the case; to be present (as a condition)
definitions.note: Used to state that a condition or set of circumstances exists (e.g., „eine Erkrankung“, „ein Mangel“, „ein Verdacht“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei dem Patienten soll eine Infektion vorliegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient is suspected to have an infection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag es, wenn du mir vorliest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like it when you read to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorläufig bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For now, we’re staying at home.

definitions.note: Contraction of „vor dem“ (used with the dative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte vorm Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m waiting in front of the train station.

definitions.native: to demonstrate, to show (how to do something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir das bitte vormachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please show me how to do that?

definitions.native: to pretend, to put on (an act), to fool (someone)
definitions.note: Often used as: jemandem etwas vormachen (to fool someone / make someone believe something that isn’t true).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst mir nichts vormachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t fool me.

definitions.note: Used for a general time of day (habitually/repeatedly), not a specific date/time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vormittags arbeite ich meistens im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the mornings, I usually work in the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus hält vorn am Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus stops in front at the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist vorne im Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is in the front of the car.

definitions.note: Most commonly used reflexively: sich (etwas) vornehmen = to set oneself a goal / plan to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mir vornehmen, jeden Tag Deutsch zu üben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to plan to practice German every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen jetzt vorrücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to move forward now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte vorschlagen, dass wir morgen früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to suggest that we leave earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: simple past of "vorschlagen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vorschlug, später zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He suggested going later.

definitions.note: Used as a warning (similar to “Watch out!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorsicht, da kommt ein Fahrrad!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out, a bike is coming!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei bitte vorsichtig auf der Treppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be careful on the stairs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte fahr vorsichtig!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please drive carefully!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sei bitte vorsichtiger, wenn du die Straße überquerst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be more careful when you cross the street.

definitions.native: as a precaution, just in case
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich nehme vorsichtshalber einen Regenschirm mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll take an umbrella with me just in case.

definitions.native: sing (something) to someone first; lead by singing
definitions.note: Often used when someone demonstrates a melody/lyrics, or sings as an audition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir das Lied vorsingen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you sing the song to me first?

definitions.native: to play (something) for someone, to perform (something) for someone
definitions.note: Often used for playing music for someone (e.g., on an instrument) or performing something as a demonstration/audition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dir ein Lied vorspielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to play a song for you.

definitions.native: to pretend, to put on (an act)
definitions.note: Used when someone is faking feelings or behavior (e.g., friendliness, love).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will mir Freundlichkeit vorspielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to pretend friendliness to me.

definitions.note: Especially in theater/music/acting: to perform in front of someone to try out for a role or place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie will morgen am Theater vorsprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to audition at the theater tomorrow.

definitions.native: to see someone officially, to present oneself (for an appointment)
definitions.note: Often used with "bei": "bei jemandem vorsprechen" = to show up and speak to someone in an official context (e.g., doctor, office).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss nächste Woche beim Amt vorsprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go to the office next week to see someone (officially).

definitions.note: Usually used as: „ich stelle mir … vor“ (separable verb „sich etw. vorstellen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vorstelle mir, dass es morgen regnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagine that it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: As „sich vorstellen“ (separable verb). In correct German word order it’s usually „ich stelle mich vor“, but this example is forced to include the exact token „vorstelle“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vorstelle mich kurz: Ich heiße Anna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me introduce myself briefly: My name is Anna.

definitions.note: Often used with a person as the object: jemanden vorstellen = to introduce someone (to others).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dir meine Kollegin vorstellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to introduce my colleague to you.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: sich vorstellen = to imagine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mir vorstellen, dass das schwierig ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can imagine that that’s difficult.

definitions.note: Second-person singular present (du-form) of „vorstellen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie vorstellst du dir das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How do you imagine that?

definitions.note: Second-person singular present (du-form) of „vorstellen“; used for introducing people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vorstellst du mich deinen Eltern?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you introduce me to your parents?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er vorstellte seine Kollegin im Meeting.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He introduced his colleague in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vorstellte mir einen ruhigen Urlaub am Meer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagined a quiet vacation by the sea.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative for the person and „vorwerfen“ + accusative/„dass“-clause for what they are accused of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir nicht vorwerfen, dass du zu spät gekommen bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't accuse you of having come late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte geh vorwärts!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go forward!

definitions.note: Often used for showing something official (e.g., an ID, ticket, documents) on request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte vorzeigen Sie Ihren Ausweis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please show your ID.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er musste die Schule vorzeitig verlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to leave school early.

definitions.note: Often used as a separable verb: "Ich ziehe Tee vor." (Präsens) but the infinitive/base form is "vorziehen". Also common with "es vorziehen, zu ...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde heute Tee vorziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I will prefer tea.

definitions.note: Used with "zu" (as in "etwas vorzubereiten"), often after verbs like "versuchen", "planen", or "vergessen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Treffen gut vorzubereiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to prepare for the meeting well.

definitions.note: often used with a person as the indirect object (e.g., jemandem etwas vorzulesen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir die Geschichte vorzulesen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you read the story aloud to me?

definitions.native: to make (a change), to carry out
definitions.note: Used as the “zu”-infinitive form of the separable verb „vornehmen“, often with nouns like „Änderung“ (change) or „Maßnahmen“ (measures).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, eine kleine Änderung vorzunehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to make a small change.

definitions.note: often used with a person as the object: jemanden vorstellen = to introduce someone
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich freue mich, Ihnen meine Kollegin vorzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy to introduce my colleague to you.

definitions.note: often used reflexively: sich etwas vorstellen = to imagine something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist schwer, sich das vorzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to imagine that.

definitions.note: Commonly used as "etwas vorziehen" (to prefer something) or "etwas/jemandem etwas vorziehen" (to prefer something to something/someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich würde den Zug dem Auto vorzuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would prefer the train to the car.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „sein“ or „gehen“ to mean that something has ended or has passed by.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Prüfung ist endlich vorüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam is finally over.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“, „sein“, or „fahren“ to express that something has passed (in time or space).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm ist zum Glück vorüber.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Luckily, the storm is over.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist vorübergehend gesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is temporarily closed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Kommentar war wirklich vulgär.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His comment was really vulgar.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Vogel“ (used after certain verbs and prepositions, e.g. „den Vögeln“ = “to the birds”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gebe den Vögeln Futter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give the birds food.

definitions.note: Vulgar slang; can sound crude/offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen im Park vögeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to have sex in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin völlig müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m completely tired.

definitions.note: Used before a feminine singular noun (or plural with no article), e.g. „völlige Ruhe“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Sturm herrschte völlige Ruhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, there was complete calm.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis in phrases like „ein völliger …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist ein völliger Idiot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a complete idiot.

definitions.note: Used as the imperative (command) form with the separable prefix: „Wach auf!“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wach auf! Wir müssen los.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up! We have to go.

definitions.note: often used with „sein“ or „werden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin noch wach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm still awake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bleib bitte wach im Straßenverkehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stay alert in traffic.

definitions.note: Often used as an imperative, especially in the phrase „Wach auf!“ (“Wake up!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wach auf, es ist schon acht Uhr!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake up, it’s already eight o’clock!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wache jeden Tag um sieben Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up every day at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix „auf“ (aufwachen): „Wir wachen … auf.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wachen jeden Tag um sieben Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wake up every day at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: Intransitive verb meaning to be in a waking state (not sleeping).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wachen die ganze Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stay awake all night.

definitions.note: often used for being aware of danger or paying close attention
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei ist nachts besonders wachsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are especially alert at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kinder wachsen schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Children grow quickly.

definitions.note: Form of "aufwachen" in the present tense (e.g., "er/sie/es wacht" or "ihr wacht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wacht um sieben Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wakes up at seven o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wachte um sechs Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up at six o’clock.

definitions.note: often used for things that are unstable or not firmly supported (e.g., a chair, table, ladder)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stuhl ist wackelig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair is wobbly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch kann wackeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table can wobble.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch wackelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table wobbles.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wackeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Tisch wackelte, als ich mich darauf stützte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table wobbled when I leaned on it.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “diligently/hard,” especially in phrases like „wacker arbeiten“ (to work hard).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat wacker weitergemacht, obwohl sie müde war.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept going bravely even though she was tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wag es nicht, das zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't dare to say that.

definitions.note: Not related to the English noun “wage” (= salary).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wage es nicht, ihn zu fragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t dare to ask him.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who is willing to take risks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war ein wagemutiger Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a daring plan.

definitions.note: Verb; means to risk doing something (often in set phrases).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde es nicht wagen, ihn das zu fragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will not dare to ask him that.

definitions.note: present tense (er/sie/es) of „wagen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wagt es, dem Chef zu widersprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dares to contradict the boss.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wagte es, die Wahrheit zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dared to tell the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat wahllos Leute auf der Straße angesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke to people on the street at random.

definitions.note: Used as an exclamation to react to something surprising or impressive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wahnsinn! Das Konzert war echt gut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unbelievable! The concert was really good.

definitions.note: Often also used informally for emphasis (like “incredibly” or “really”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wahnsinnig teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s insanely expensive.

definitions.note: Often used informally as an intensifier (similar to “really/so/very”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wahnsinnig teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s insanely expensive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine wahnsinnige Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a crazy idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is true.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wahr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is true.

definitions.note: Adjective form of „wahr“ used with a following noun (e.g., after a definite article like „die“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die wahre Geschichte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the true story.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „wahr“, used before a noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die wahren Gründe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the real reasons.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like „die Ruhe wahren“ (keep calm) or „den Frieden wahren“ (preserve peace).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen den Frieden wahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must preserve peace.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „wahr“, used here before a masculine noun (e.g., „wahrer Kaffee“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wahrer Kaffee, kein Ersatz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is real coffee, not a substitute.

definitions.note: Form of the adjective "wahr" used with a neuter noun (e.g., "ein wahres Wunder").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wahres Wunder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a true miracle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Geruch sofort wahrgenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed the smell right away.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something is really true; somewhat formal/literary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war wahrhaft ein besonderer Moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was truly a special moment.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something is really the case; can sound a bit formal or emphatic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wahrhaftig eine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That really is a good idea.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned or emphatic in tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wahrlich, das ist eine gute Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Indeed, that is a good idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Unterschied kaum wahrnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can hardly notice the difference.

definitions.note: Often used with things like Termine (appointments) or Sitzungen (meetings), especially in more formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann den Termin morgen leider nicht wahrnehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I can’t make the appointment tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt wahrscheinlich morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will probably come tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wahrscheinlich kommt er heute später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’ll probably come later today.

definitions.note: often used with the structure „etwas wahrnehmen“ (to notice/perceive something)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, jedes Detail wahrzunehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to notice every detail.

definitions.native: to prevail; to rule (to hold sway)
definitions.note: Often formal/literary; common in phrases like „Gerechtigkeit walten lassen“ (= to let justice prevail).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In diesem Land walten Recht und Ordnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this country, law and order prevail.

definitions.note: Often used in a formal or written style; very common in the reflexive form „sich wandeln“ (“to change”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen unser Verhalten wandeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to change our behavior.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "wandeln"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit der Zeit wandelte sich die Stadt stark.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over time, the city changed a lot.

definitions.native: to hike, to go on a walk
definitions.note: Often used for walking in nature or the mountains (hiking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Wochenende wandern wir in den Bergen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the weekend we go hiking in the mountains.

definitions.note: often used for going on a longer walk, especially in nature
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wandert am Wochenende in den Bergen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hikes in the mountains on the weekend.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "wandern".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern wanderte ich durch den Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I hiked through the forest.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "wandern"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wanderten den ganzen Tag durch die Berge.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We hiked through the mountains all day.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „abwenden“; often used with „sich“ (e.g., „sich abwenden“ = to turn away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wandte sich ab, als er das sah.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned away when he saw that.

definitions.note: simple past of "wenden"; often used with "sich" (e.g., "sich umwenden" = to turn around)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wandte sich um und sah mich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned around and looked at me.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „(sich) zuwenden“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wandte sich mir zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He turned toward me.

definitions.note: Used mainly for questions or in indirect questions (e.g., “I don’t know when …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wann kommst du nach Hause?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When are you coming home?

definitions.note: Used in indirect questions and some subordinate clauses (e.g., after wissen, fragen); for direct questions you can also use it: „Wann kommst du?“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß nicht, wann er kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know when he’s coming.

definitions.note: Also used as an auxiliary to form the past perfect (e.g. with verbs of movement/change).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war schon nach Hause gegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already gone home.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „sein“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern war ich zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I was at home.

definitions.note: Old-fashioned/literary form of „wurde“ (simple past of „werden“), often used to form the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gesetz ward geändert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The law was changed.

definitions.note: Past tense plural form of "sein" ("to be"); often used as an auxiliary in the past perfect (Plusquamperfekt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir waren schon eingeschlafen, als du angerufen hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had already fallen asleep when you called.

definitions.note: Simple past of „umwerfen“ (often used with „um“ later in the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er warf die Vase um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He knocked over the vase.

definitions.note: Simple past of „vorwerfen“; often used in the pattern „jemandem etwas vorwerfen“ (to accuse someone of something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er warf mir vor, zu spät zu kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accused me of coming too late.

definitions.note: simple past of „werfen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er warf den Ball ins Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threw the ball into the water.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie warfen den Ball ins Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They threw the ball into the water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wasser ist warm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is warm.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective “warm” (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hätte gern eine warme Suppe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like a warm soup.

definitions.note: dative singular form (masculine/neuter) of "warm"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wasche mir die Hände mit warmem Wasser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my hands with warm water.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of the adjective „warm“ (with an -en ending), used depending on the case/article (e.g., after „an“ + dative plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: An warmen Tagen gehen wir oft schwimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On warm days we often go swimming.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „warm“ (often written with umlaut as „wärmer“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es warmer als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s warmer than yesterday.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective (e.g., used before a neuter noun like „ein warmes Bett“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke ein warmes Getränk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm drinking a warm drink.

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warne dich vor dem Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I warn you about the dog.

definitions.note: Often used with: „jemanden vor + Dativ warnen“ (to warn someone about/of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich vor dem Hund warnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will warn you about the dog.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „warnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie warnte ihn vor dem Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She warned him about the dog.

definitions.note: colloquial contraction of „war es“; in writing often appears as „war’s“, but here given as „wars“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wars gestern besser als heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Was it better yesterday than today?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) simple past of "sein".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du warst gestern sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were very tired yesterday.

definitions.note: past tense of „sein“ used with „ihr“ (you plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Als ihr endlich da wart, konnten wir anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were finally there, we could start.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „sein“ used with „ihr“ (you all): „ihr wart“ = you were.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern wart ihr sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you were very tired.

definitions.note: Can mean “I wait” (present tense) or “wait!” (command), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warte bitte einen Moment.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait a moment.

definitions.note: Often used as 1st person singular present ("ich warte" = "I wait / I'm waiting"); it can also be used as an informal imperative ("Warte!" = "Wait!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte auf den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m waiting for the bus.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative to mean “to wait for.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss hier warten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to wait here.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) past tense (Präteritum).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wartest gestern lange auf den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You waited a long time for the bus yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wartet vor dem Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He waits in front of the movie theater.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „warten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wartet vor dem Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He waits in front of the train station.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „warten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wartete vor dem Kino auf dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I waited for you in front of the movie theater.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „warten“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir warteten eine Stunde auf den Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We waited an hour for the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum bist du heute zu Hause?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you at home today?

definitions.note: Interrogative pronoun; also used in indirect questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was machst du heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing today?

definitions.note: interrogative pronoun (question word)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was machst du heute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you doing today?

definitions.note: indefinite pronoun (often in expressions like „etwas“ or colloquially shortened in speech)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sag was!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Say something!

definitions.note: relative pronoun referring to a whole clause/idea; often with commas (e.g., „..., was ...“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war alles, was ich wusste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was all (that) I knew.

definitions.note: As a determiner it is commonly used in the phrase “was für …” = “what kind of …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was für ein Buch liest du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What kind of book are you reading?

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to express surprise, disbelief, or to ask someone to repeat something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was? Das stimmt nicht!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What? That’s not true!

definitions.note: Used in questions and in clauses like “alles, was …” (“everything that …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was ist das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is that?

definitions.note: Usually used as the informal (du) imperative of „waschen“ (e.g., giving someone a command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wasch dir bitte die Hände!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wash your hands!

definitions.note: informal singular imperative (command) of „waschen“ (to wash)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wasch dir die Hände!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wash your hands!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense (used with „ich“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wasche meine Hände vor dem Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash my hands before eating.

definitions.note: Used for washing yourself, clothes, dishes, etc.; often used with a reflexive pronoun for “to wash (oneself)” (e.g., sich waschen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde meine Hände waschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will wash my hands.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) or 2nd person plural (ihr), present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wascht dir die Hände.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wash your hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Jacke ist wasserdicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This jacket is waterproof.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Spinne webt ein Netz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The spider weaves a web.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., change clothes) or with prepositions like „zu“ (switch to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute meine Kleidung wechseln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change my clothes today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wechselst das Thema sehr schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You change the topic very quickly.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „wechseln“; often used with „zu“ (switch to) or „den/das“ (change the).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wechselt den Job.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He changes jobs.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "wechseln"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wechselte den Job im Sommer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He changed jobs in the summer.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Pause wechselten sie die Plätze.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the break, they changed seats.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wechsle den Sitzplatz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I change the seat.

definitions.note: Often used as the informal imperative of „wecken“ (addressing one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Weck mich bitte um sieben Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake me up at seven o’clock, please.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I wake (someone) up").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wecke dich um sieben Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake you up at seven o’clock.

definitions.note: Usually used with a direct object (you wake someone up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich morgen um sieben Uhr wecken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll wake you up tomorrow at seven o'clock.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du) of „aufwecken“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du weckst mich jeden Morgen um sieben Uhr auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wake me up every morning at seven o'clock.

definitions.note: often used with an object (e.g., jemanden wecken = to wake someone up)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum weckst du mich so früh?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you waking me up so early?

definitions.note: third-person singular present of "wecken"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm weckt mich jede Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise wakes me up every night.

definitions.note: Simple past of „wecken“ (to wake someone up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wecker weckte mich um sechs Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The alarm clock woke me up at six o’clock.

definitions.note: often used for tails or for waving something back and forth
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wedelt mit dem Schwanz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog wags its tail.

definitions.note: Usually used with "noch" ("weder ... noch" = "neither ... nor").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe weder Zeit noch Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have neither time nor money.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed pair “weder … noch …” (“neither … nor …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe weder Zeit noch Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have neither time nor money.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“ (go) or „sein“ (be): „weggehen“ = go away, „weg sein“ = be gone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schon weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is already gone.

definitions.note: Often used as a short command to tell someone/something to move away or leave.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Weg da!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move away! (Get out of the way!)

definitions.note: Often used with verbs (e.g., „geh weg!“) to mean movement away or that something is no longer there.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Geh weg!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go away!

definitions.native: to stay away; to not show up
definitions.note: Often used when someone does not come to a place/event (intentionally or unintentionally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum bist du gestern von der Schule wegbleiben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you stay away from school yesterday?

definitions.native: to take away, to bring away
definitions.note: Often used for taking something from where it is now to another place (e.g., taking out the trash, dropping something off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte den Müll wegbringen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please take out the trash?

definitions.note: Takes the genitive in formal German; in everyday speech it’s often used with the dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen des Regens bleiben wir zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the rain, we’re staying at home.

definitions.note: Used for leaving a place by car, train, etc.; separable verb, so in main clauses it often appears split as „fährt … weg“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden morgen früh wegfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will leave tomorrow morning (by vehicle).

definitions.note: Past participle of "wegfahren"; often used with "sein" in the perfect tense (e.g., "ist weggefahren").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bus ist schon weggefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus has already left.

definitions.note: past participle of "weggehen"; often used with "sein" to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist schon weggegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has already gone away.

definitions.note: Past participle of „weggeben“ (to give away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die alten Bücher weggegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave away the old books.

definitions.note: often used for leaving a place or going away from someone/something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss jetzt weggehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave now.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „weggehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum weggehst du so früh?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you leaving so early?

definitions.note: past participle of "weglaufen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist weggelaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog ran away.

definitions.note: Past participle of "wegmachen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat ... weggemacht").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Flecken weggemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I removed the stains.

definitions.note: past participle of „wegnehmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir wurde das Handy weggenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone was taken away from me.

definitions.note: past participle of "wegrennen"; often used with "sein" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist vor dem Gewitter weggerannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog ran away from the thunderstorm.

definitions.note: past participle of "wegräumen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Spielzeug weggeräumt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the toys away.

definitions.note: past participle of „wegschicken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Chefin hat ihn sofort weggeschickt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss sent him away immediately.

definitions.note: past participle of "wegwerfen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat weggeworfen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die alten Zeitungen weggeworfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw away the old newspapers.

definitions.note: past participle of „wegziehen“; often used with „sein“ to mean relocating to live somewhere else
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist letztes Jahr nach Berlin weggezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moved away to Berlin last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen hier schnell wegkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get away from here quickly.

definitions.note: Often used when something small is misplaced or disappears without you noticing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Schlüssel kann in einer vollen Tasche leicht wegkommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A key can easily get lost in a full bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du jetzt wegkommst, bist du pünktlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you leave now, you’ll be on time.

definitions.note: From the separable verb „wegkommen“; in main clauses it often appears split as „kommt … weg“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass er bald wegkommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that he leaves soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst den letzten Satz weglassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can leave out the last sentence.

definitions.note: to flee or escape; also used for suddenly leaving (running off)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund wird gleich weglaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is going to run away in a moment.

definitions.note: Often used for putting something back where it belongs (e.g., tidying up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das Buch bitte weglegen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please put the book away?

definitions.note: Often used for coaxing someone/something away (e.g., with treats, promises, or tempting things).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen den Hund mit einem Leckerli weglocken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to lure the dog away with a treat.

definitions.note: often means removing something from someone or from a place
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Messer vom Tisch wegnehmen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please take the knife away from the table?

definitions.native: to put away, to clear away
definitions.note: Often used for tidying up by removing things from a surface or area.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Geschirr wegräumen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please put the dishes away?

definitions.note: Often used for telling someone to leave or go away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wird ihn sofort wegschicken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss will send him away immediately.

definitions.note: often used in instructions (e.g., to make space)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte einen Schritt zurückgehen und wegtreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take a step back and step aside.

definitions.note: often used about leaving an office or position
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef will am Ende des Jahres wegtreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss wants to step down at the end of the year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die alte Zeitung wegwerfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will throw away the old newspaper.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form of the separable verb „weggehen“ (used after verbs like „versuchen“, „planen“, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe versucht, leise wegzugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried to leave quietly.

definitions.note: This is the "zu"-infinitive form of the separable verb "wegkommen" (e.g., "Ich versuche, früh wegzukommen.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, heute früh wegzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to leave early today.

definitions.note: Infinitive with "zu" (e.g., after certain verbs like "versuchen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, wegzulaufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to run away.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „tun“ or „sein“ (e.g. „wehtun“, „Mir ist weh“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir tut der Rücken weh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My back hurts.

definitions.note: Used to warn or threaten someone (often in the phrase "Wehe, wenn …!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wehe, wenn du das nochmal machst!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Woe betide you if you do that again!

definitions.note: Used mostly for wind, flags, hair, etc. moving in the breeze.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Draußen kann man den Wind wehen hören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Outside, you can hear the wind blowing.

definitions.note: Past participle of „wehtun“; commonly used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat wehgetan“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das hat mir sehr wehgetan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That hurt me a lot.

definitions.note: Past participle of "wehtun" (used with "haben" in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturz hat sehr wehgetan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fall hurt a lot.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: „sich wehren“ = to defend oneself / resist.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mich gut wehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can defend myself well.

definitions.note: usually used for wind or a draft (air moving)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute weht ein starker Wind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A strong wind is blowing today.

definitions.note: Simple past of „wehen“ (used especially for wind, a breeze, or a flag).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern wehte ein kalter Wind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday a cold wind blew.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a separable verb: „weh“ + „tun“ (e.g., „Es tut weh“, „Der Kopf tut weh“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Kopf kann wehtun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My head can hurt.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "wehtun".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Kopf wehtut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My head hurts.

definitions.note: Used as a “zu”-infinitive form (e.g., after verbs like anfangen, beginnen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es beginnt, wehzutun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It starts to hurt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby ist weiblich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is female.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a female person/animal; can also refer to the feminine grammatical gender (e.g., „weibliche Form“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die weibliche Ärztin kommt gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The female doctor will be here soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kissen ist sehr weich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pillow is very soft.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective ending (e.g., with feminine nouns or in plural) from the lemma „weich“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine weiche Decke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a soft blanket.

definitions.note: Often used with abstract things (e.g., pressure, resistance) meaning “to give in” or “to retreat.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir dürfen nicht weichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must not give in.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a neuter noun (e.g., ein weiches Kissen) or as the nominative/accusative plural after certain determiners (e.g., weiches Obst).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby hat ein weiches Kissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby has a soft pillow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du weichst zur Seite, damit ich vorbeigehen kann.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You move aside so that I can walk past.

definitions.note: Often used with "ausweichen" (to dodge/avoid) or in the phrase "nicht weichen" (not to budge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Boden weicht unter meinen Füßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ground gives way under my feet.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich weigern“ + zu + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mich nicht weigern, dir zu helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will not refuse to help you.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie weigerten sich, die Wahrheit zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They refused to tell the truth.

definitions.note: Introduces a subordinate clause; in that clause, the conjugated verb usually goes to the end.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm staying at home because I'm sick.

definitions.note: Depending on context, it can mean “I cry/I’m crying” (Ich weine.) or the imperative “cry!” (Weine nicht!). Not related to English “wine” (false friend).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weine, weil ich traurig bin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m crying because I’m sad.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("I cry") of "weinen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weine, weil ich dich vermisse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m crying because I miss you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind muss weinen, weil es müde ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has to cry because it is tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie saß weinend auf dem Bett.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sat on the bed crying.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "weinen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum weinst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you crying?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "weinen" (he/she/it cries).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Baby weint, weil es müde ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is crying because it is tired.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „weinen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er weinte, weil er sein Handy verloren hatte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He cried because he had lost his phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr weise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very wise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat weise gehandelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She acted wisely.

definitions.note: Often used with a preposition like „auf“ (e.g. „auf etwas weisen“ = to point to something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Schild soll auf die Baustelle weisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sign is meant to point to the construction site.

definitions.note: comparative form of „weise“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit Erfahrung wird man oft weiser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With experience, you often become wiser.

definitions.native: to make someone believe (something), to convince someone (often falsely)
definitions.note: Usually used with a direct object + a clause: „jemandem etwas weismachen“ (often implies deceiving someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wollte mir weismachen, dass er keine Zeit hat.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to make me believe that he has no time.

definitions.note: Swiss spelling of „weiß“ (1st/3rd person singular present of „wissen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiss es nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know.

definitions.note: Swiss spelling of standard German „weißt“ (2nd person singular: you know).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du weisst genau, was du willst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You know exactly what you want.

definitions.note: Usually used with a separable prefix: „etwas aufweisen“ (e.g. „weist ... auf“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bericht weist viele Fehler auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report shows many errors.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ (to point out) or „hin“ (to point to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wegweiser weist den Weg zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The signpost points the way to the train station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Straße ist hier sehr weit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is very wide here.

definitions.note: Often used with distances or reaching/going far.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist nicht weit bis zum Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It isn’t far to the train station.

definitions.note: Often used with distances or ranges; also commonly in fixed phrases like „weit weg“ (far away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bahnhof ist nicht weit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train station is not far.

definitions.note: Used to emphasize a clear difference, often in comparisons.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Buch ist weitaus interessanter als der Film.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is by far more interesting than the movie.

definitions.note: feminine form of the adjective (e.g., before a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen eine weite Reise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re taking a long trip.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „weit“ (e.g., plural/dative with an -en ending).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen mit weiten Schritten nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking home with wide strides.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "weit" (often used both as an adjective and as an adverb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Von hier ist es nicht mehr weit, aber das nächste Dorf ist noch weiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From here it isn’t far anymore, but the next village is even farther.

definitions.note: Often used to mean continuing (e.g., “go on/continue”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte weiter sprechen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please continue speaking?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte ein bisschen weiter gehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please go a little further?

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“, „machen“, „arbeiten“ to mean continuing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen weiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll continue.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to urge someone (or yourself) to continue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Weiter, wir haben keine Zeit!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go on, we don't have any time!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen noch weiter gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to go further.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs to mean continuing an action (e.g., „weitermachen“ = to continue).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach bitte weiter!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please continue!

definitions.note: Often used with „an etwas weiterarbeiten“ = continue working on something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Pause werden wir weiterarbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the break, we will keep working.

definitions.native: to help (someone) make progress, to further
definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., jemanden weiterbringen) meaning to help someone get ahead or move forward.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Training wird dich wirklich weiterbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This training will really help you make progress.

definitions.native: to take (something) further, to move along
definitions.note: Can mean physically taking something/someone forward to the next place or stage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du die Kisten bitte nach oben weiterbringen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please take the boxes upstairs?

definitions.note: Used as a noun (substantivized adjective), often in headlines or formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Weitere folgen später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Others will follow later.

definitions.note: Used before a noun; here it’s the adjective form meaning “more/extra” (not the literal sense of “wide/far”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen weitere Informationen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need additional information.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (like “more”/“additional”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen weitere Informationen.
