definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need further information.

definitions.note: Used before a noun; this form is common in phrases like „weitere Informationen“ (additional information).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche weitere Informationen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need additional information.

definitions.note: Often used like a noun meaning “the others / the remaining/additional ones” (a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne die weiteren nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know the others.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (inflected form of „weiter“), often in plural phrases like „keine weiteren …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen keine weiteren Informationen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t need any further information.

definitions.note: Often used for continuing a trip in a vehicle (car, bus, train, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen jetzt weiterfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to continue driving now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Informationen weitergegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed on the information.

definitions.note: Used for continuing an activity, conversation, or process; also literally ‘to keep walking/going’.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Pause werden wir mit der Präsentation weitergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the break, we will continue with the presentation.

definitions.note: used when something (a process, event, story, etc.) continues
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass es morgen weitergeht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it continues tomorrow.

definitions.note: past participle of „weitermachen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben nach der Pause weitergemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We continued after the break.

definitions.note: Often used in customer service (e.g., a clerk asking if they can help you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kann ich Ihnen weiterhelfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I help you further?

definitions.note: Often used for something that remains the same and is expected to continue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich arbeite weiterhin im Homeoffice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still work from home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trotz der Niederlage will die Mannschaft weiterkämpfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the defeat, the team wants to keep fighting.

definitions.note: Often used about continuing to live after a difficult event, or about something continuing to exist.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Unfall musste er lernen, weiterleben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he had to learn to keep living.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen jetzt weitermachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to continue now.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "weitermachen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er weitermacht, auch wenn es schwierig ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He continues even when it is difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte noch ein bisschen weiterreden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to keep talking a little longer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin müde und möchte weiterschlafen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m tired and want to keep sleeping.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen nach der Pause weiterspielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to keep playing after the break.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte weitersprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to continue speaking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du hier nichts findest, musst du weitersuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t find anything here, you have to keep searching.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Mittagessen wollen wir weiterziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After lunch we want to move on.

definitions.note: This is the "zu" infinitive form, often used after another verb (e.g. versuchen, planen, vergessen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, trotz des Regens weiterzugehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to keep going despite the rain.

definitions.note: Infinitive with "zu" (used after certain verbs like anfangen, versuchen, aufhören, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, weiterzumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to continue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto ist weiß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is white.

definitions.note: From the verb "wissen" (to know). Not to be confused with "weiß" meaning "white" (adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß das nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know that.

definitions.note: Present tense form of „wissen“: ich/er/sie/es weiß.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß nicht, wo er ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know where he is.

definitions.note: Inflected form of "weiß"; used before a noun (e.g., feminine or plural, depending on the context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trage eine weiße Bluse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing a white blouse.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective „weiß“ (used before a noun, e.g. with an article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich sehe den weißen Hund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I see the white dog.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective "weiß" (e.g., before a masculine noun: "ein weißer ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein weißer Hund läuft im Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A white dog is running in the park.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "weiß" (used with "als": "weißer als ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieser Schnee ist weißer als der Schnee von gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This snow is whiter than yesterday’s snow.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a neuter singular noun (or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe ein weißes T-Shirt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm buying a white T-shirt.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "wissen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du weißt das schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already know that.

definitions.note: This appears to be a nonstandard/mistyped spelling of „weiß“ (1st/3rd person singular present of „wissen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiá es.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know it.

definitions.note: Nonstandard/dialect form of the verb „wissen“ (standard German would use a form like „weiß/weißt“ depending on the subject).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du weiát das schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already know that.

definitions.note: Non-standard/rare spelling; likely an archaic or mistaken form related to „weiß“ (from „wissen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiû es nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know.

definitions.note: Archaic/older form of modern German „weißt/weiß“ (from „wissen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du weiût es schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already know it.

definitions.note: Used mainly in exclamations; sounds formal or old-fashioned in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welch ein Glück, dass du da bist!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What luck that you’re here!

definitions.note: Often used in questions; can also sound formal/old-fashioned compared to "welche(r/s)" in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welch ein Buch liest du gerade?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What book are you reading right now?

definitions.note: Used as a determiner before a noun; this form agrees with the noun’s gender/case/number.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welche Farbe magst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which color do you like?

definitions.note: feminine singular or plural form of „welcher“ (also used in questions and relative clauses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welche Jacke gefällt dir besser?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which jacket do you like better?

definitions.note: feminine singular or plural form (e.g., “which one/which ones” depending on context)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welche Jacke möchtest du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which jacket would you like?

definitions.note: dative masculine or dative neuter form of "welch"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit welchem Bus fährst du zur Schule?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which bus do you take to school?

definitions.note: dative masculine/neuter singular form of „welcher“ (used after a preposition or as an indirect object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit welchem Bus fährst du zur Schule?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which bus are you taking to school?

definitions.note: Dative singular form of "welcher"; used after dative-taking verbs or prepositions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit welchem Bus fährst du nach Hause?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which bus are you taking home?

definitions.note: masculine accusative singular (also used as dative plural) form of "welch".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welchen Film möchtest du sehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which movie would you like to watch?

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular or dative plural form of “welcher”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welchen Film willst du sehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which movie do you want to see?

definitions.note: accusative masculine singular or dative plural form of „welcher“ (used like “which”/“what” in questions or relative clauses)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welchen Film möchtest du sehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which movie would you like to see?

definitions.note: Used like a question word or relative determiner; changes ending for gender/case (here: masculine nominative singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welcher Film gefällt dir am besten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which movie do you like best?

definitions.note: Often used like a question word; changes form for gender/case (welcher/welche/welches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welcher Film gefällt dir am besten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which movie do you like best?

definitions.note: Interrogative/relative pronoun; often used before a noun with endings that match the noun’s gender/case (e.g., welcher, welche, welches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welcher Film gefällt dir am besten?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which movie do you like best?

definitions.note: neuter singular form of "welch" (used with neuter nouns; also used as a standalone pronoun in questions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welches Buch liest du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which book are you reading?

definitions.note: Neuter singular form of „welcher“ (used with neuter nouns, e.g. „welches Buch?“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welches Buch liest du gerade?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which book are you reading right now?

definitions.note: Neuter form of "welcher"; used with neuter nouns (e.g., "welches Buch?")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Welches Buch liest du gerade?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which book are you reading right now?

definitions.note: Adjective (masculine nominative singular) of „weltlich“; often used in contrast to religious/church contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein weltlicher Herrscher hatte damals großen Einfluss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A secular ruler had great influence back then.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Unternehmen ist weltweit bekannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is known worldwide.

definitions.note: dative form of "wer" (used for the indirect object: "to whom?")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wem gehört dieses Buch?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who does this book belong to?

definitions.note: accusative form of "wer" (who); used for the direct object
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wen siehst du dort?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whom do you see there?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wende das Blatt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turn the page.

definitions.note: Often used for changing direction (e.g., a car turning around).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man darf hier nicht wenden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re not allowed to make a U-turn here.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wendest das Auto an der Kreuzung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You turn the car around at the intersection.

definitions.note: Often used for turning around or changing course (literally or figuratively).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wendet sich um.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turns around.

definitions.note: Used as a noun, often with an article (e.g., „das Wenige“ = the little that there is/that one has).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit dem Wenigen, das wir haben, müssen wir auskommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get by with the little that we have.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich schlafe wenig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sleep little.

definitions.note: Used with uncountable nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe wenig Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have little time.

definitions.note: Used with countable plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben nur wenig Freunde hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have only a few friends here.

definitions.note: Often used with uncountable nouns (e.g., wenig Zeit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute wenig Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have little time today.

definitions.note: Often used with countable plural nouns (e.g., wenige Leute).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es sind nur wenige Leute da.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are only a few people there.

definitions.note: used with plural countable nouns (declined form of „wenig“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nur wenige Freunde in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have only a few friends in the city.

definitions.note: Used with plural countable nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe nur wenige Freunde in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have only a few friends in the city.

definitions.note: plural form; used for people or things
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nur wenige kommen heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Only a few are coming today.

definitions.note: Used with plural nouns; often appears in dative plural after prepositions (e.g., mit, von, zu).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe mit wenigen Freunden ins Kino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the cinema with a few friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute weniger Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have less time today.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "wenig"; use "less" with uncountable nouns and "fewer" with countable nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe weniger Zeit als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have less time than yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du wenigstens anrufen, wenn du später kommst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you at least call if you're coming later?

definitions.note: Used to introduce a condition. (German „wenn“ can also mean “when” in some contexts.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du Zeit hast, komm vorbei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have time, come by.

definitions.note: Often used for present/future or repeated events; for a one-time event in the past, German usually uses „als“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich nach Hause komme, rufe ich dich an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I get home, I’ll call you.

definitions.note: More formal than "obwohl".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenngleich es kalt ist, gehen wir spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Although it is cold, we are going for a walk.

definitions.note: Used to ask about a person (subject); can also be used in relative clauses meaning “the one who”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wer ist das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who is that?

definitions.note: colloquial/spoken short form of „werde“ (from „werden“), used as an auxiliary to form the future tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werd morgen zu Hause sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will be at home tomorrow.

definitions.note: colloquial/contracted form of „werde“ (1st person singular of „werden“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werd später kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll come later.

definitions.note: colloquial/contracted form of „werde“ (1st person singular of „werden“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werd langsam müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm slowly getting tired.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to form the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen abgeholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am being picked up tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I become tired.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary verb to form the future tense (often with an infinitive at the end).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will work tomorrow.

definitions.note: used with a past participle to form the passive (something is/gets done)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fenster müssen heute geputzt werden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows have to be cleaned today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte Arzt werden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to become a doctor.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive to talk about the future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Morgen werden wir arbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will work.

definitions.note: Used to form the passive voice with a past participle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Brief wird heute werden geschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter is being written today.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form the future (with an infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr werdet morgen kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form the passive (with a past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr werdet morgen abgeholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are being picked up tomorrow.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werfe den Ball zu dir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I throw the ball to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden den Ball gleich werfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will throw the ball in a moment.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural form: “you (all) throw” (also used as the plural command “throw!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum werft ihr den Ball so weit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you (all) throwing the ball so far?

definitions.note: Used with a noun or pronoun in the genitive (e.g., „das ist es wert“ = „it’s worth it“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist es wert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s worth it.

definitions.note: Used in formal/old-fashioned direct address (e.g., in letters or speeches), often with a title like "Herr".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Werter Herr Schmidt, ich habe eine Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear Mr. Schmidt, I have a question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich in meinem Team wertgeschätzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel appreciated in my team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses alte Papier ist wertlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This old paper is worthless.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Gemälde ist sehr wertvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This painting is very valuable.

definitions.note: Often used for things like time, experiences, or activities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kurs war für mich sehr wertvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The course was very worthwhile for me.

definitions.note: adjective ending; often used before a noun (e.g., „wertvolle Zeit“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine wertvolle Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a valuable idea.

definitions.note: Comparative form of „wertvoll“; used before masculine nouns with an indefinite article (e.g., „ein wertvoller …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wertvoller Ring als der andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a more valuable ring than the other one.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wertvolles Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a valuable gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neue Methode ist wesentlich schneller als die alte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new method is significantly faster than the old one.

definitions.note: often used in questions; can also mean “for that reason” when referring back to something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Weshalb bist du heute nicht in der Schule?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why aren’t you at school today?

definitions.note: Genitive question word; used to ask who something belongs to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wessen Jacke ist das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whose jacket is that?

definitions.note: Genitive question word/relative pronoun used to ask about or refer to possession.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wessen Tasche ist das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whose bag is that?

definitions.note: Describes direction or location; often used with verbs like „liegen“ (to be located) or „fahren“ (to travel).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ort liegt westlich von Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town is west of Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used to refer back to a reason just mentioned (similar to “deshalb/darum”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hat stark geregnet, weswegen das Spiel abgesagt wurde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It rained heavily, which is why the game was cancelled.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "wetten" (ich wette).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wette, dass er heute zu spät kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bet that he’ll be late today.

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" + accusative (to bet on something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen auf Deutschland wetten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to bet on Germany.

definitions.note: English interjection sometimes used in German (often to show surprise or to tell someone/something to stop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Whoa, das war knapp!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whoa, that was close!

definitions.note: simple past of „weichen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Nebel wich langsam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fog slowly gave way.

definitions.note: very vulgar, slang
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde gefeuert, weil er im Büro wichsen wollte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was fired because he wanted to masturbate in the office.

definitions.note: old-fashioned; used especially for shoes
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er musste seine Schuhe wichsen, damit sie glänzen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He had to polish his shoes (with wax) so that they shine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wichtiger Termin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an important appointment.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a noun (e.g., after der/die/das/ein/eine)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine wichtige Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an important question.

definitions.note: This is the declined form of the adjective "wichtig" (used before a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die wichtigen Dokumente finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to find the important documents.

definitions.note: comparative form of "wichtig"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wichtiger als das Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is more important than the money.

definitions.note: Often used as a nominalized adjective meaning “something important.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dir etwas Wichtiges sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tell you something important.

definitions.note: superlative form of „wichtig“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist das wichtigste Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the most important problem.

definitions.note: superlative form of „wichtig“; often used with a definite article (e.g., „die wichtigsten …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die wichtigsten Regeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the most important rules.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wickeln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wickelte das Geschenk in buntes Papier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrapped the present in colorful paper.

definitions.note: Formal/literary; often used in set phrases (e.g., „wider Erwarten“ = contrary to expectations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wider das Gesetz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is against the law.

definitions.note: Usually used with a dative object (e.g., jemandem) for something that happens to someone, often unexpectedly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas Schlimmes ist ihm noch nie widerfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something that terrible has never happened to him before.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Geruch ist widerlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The smell is disgusting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein widerliches Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is disgusting food.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive pronoun + dative: sich (Dat.) widersetzen = to resist/defy someone or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er widersetzen sich dem Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He resists the plan.

definitions.note: simple past of „widersprechen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er widersprach dem Lehrer im Unterricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He contradicted the teacher in class.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative: jemandem widersprechen = to contradict/disagree with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dir widersprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to disagree with you.

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the dative: „jemandem widersprechen“ = to contradict/disagree with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er widerspricht dem Lehrer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He contradicts the teacher.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative (jdm./etw. widerstehen = to resist someone/something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann der Schokolade nicht widerstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t resist chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nickte widerstrebend und ging mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He nodded reluctantly and came along.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er half ihr widerwillig bei den Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He helped her with the homework reluctantly.

definitions.note: First-person singular present of "widmen" (ich widme). Often used with "jemandem/etwas" (dative) or "etwas" (accusative), e.g. "jemandem etwas widmen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich widme dir dieses Lied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dedicate this song to you.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative for the recipient and a phrase with „zu“ for the purpose (e.g. „jemandem etwas widmen“, „sich einer Sache widmen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte dieses Buch meiner Mutter widmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to dedicate this book to my mother.

definitions.note: Often used with “sich” (sich widmen = to devote oneself) or with dative + accusative (jemandem etwas widmen = to dedicate something to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er widmet das Buch seiner Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dedicates the book to his mother.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „widmen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er widmete das Buch seiner Mutter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He dedicated the book to his mother.

definitions.note: Often used in questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie heißt du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s your name?

definitions.note: Used to make comparisons ("like") or to mean "as" in phrases such as "as a...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist wie sein Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is like his father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie heißt du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What’s your name? (Literally: How are you called?)

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist wie sein Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is like his father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie geht es dir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you?

definitions.note: Used for comparisons (often with "so ... wie").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist so groß wie sein Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is as tall as his father.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie geht es dir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you?

definitions.note: Used to compare things or introduce examples ("like").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist so groß wie sein Bruder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is as tall as his brother.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a subordinate clause describing manner or comparison (often with „so … wie“ = “as … as”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mach es, wie ich es dir gezeigt habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do it the way I showed you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte wiederholen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you repeat that, please?

definitions.note: Often used with verbs meaning to return (e.g., kommen, gehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme morgen wieder nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m coming back home tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often means “again” (repetition). In separable verbs it can also mean “back” in the sense of “return” (e.g., zurückkommen/wiederkommen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte wiederholen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you repeat that, please?

definitions.note: past participle of „wiedererkennen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn sofort wiedererkannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I recognized him again immediately.

definitions.native: recognize (again); recognize as the same person/thing as before
definitions.note: Used for recognizing someone or something you have seen/heard/experienced before.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann ihn sofort wiedererkennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can recognize him immediately.

definitions.note: Often used for finding something you lost, or meeting/finding someone again after a while.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann meine Schlüssel nicht wiederfinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t find my keys again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Reise konnte sie die Freude am Lesen wiederfinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, she was able to rediscover the joy of reading.

definitions.note: Often used in a religious or spiritual sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der Krise fühlte er sich wie wiedergeboren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the crisis, he felt reborn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meinen Schlüssel wiedergefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my key again.

definitions.note: Colloquial for „wiederbekommen“ (past participle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mein Geld wiedergekriegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got my money back.

definitions.note: Past participle of „wiedersehen“, usually used with „haben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn gestern wiedergesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw him again yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister wurde wiedergewählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor was re-elected.

definitions.note: Often used for compensating for a mistake, damage, or loss.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde meinen Fehler wiedergutmachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will make up for my mistake.

definitions.native: to have back, to get back
definitions.note: Often used when you want something returned to you.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mein Buch wiederhaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to have my book back.

definitions.note: past participle of „wiederherstellen“; often used with „sein/haben“ or like an adjective
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Internetverbindung ist wiederhergestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The internet connection has been restored.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wiederhole die Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I repeat the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du das bitte wiederholen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please repeat that?

definitions.note: present tense form (e.g., he/she/it repeats)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wiederholt die Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He repeats the question.

definitions.note: past participle form (used with haben; can also be used like an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Wort mehrmals wiederholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I repeated the word several times.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich wiederholt angerufen, aber ich konnte nicht rangehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He called me repeatedly, but I couldn't answer.

definitions.note: Separable verb: ich komme wieder, du kommst wieder, er/sie/es kommt wieder; Präteritum: kam wieder; Perfekt: ist wiedergekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du morgen wiederkommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come back tomorrow?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wann wiederkommst du nach Hause?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When are you coming back home?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „wiederkommen“; in a main clause it often splits: „Er kommt wieder.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich freue mich, dass er morgen wiederkommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m happy that he’s coming back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form (often used in reported speech or formal/written style).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hofft, dass ich dich bald wiedersehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hopes that I will see you again soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden uns morgen wiedersehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will see each other again tomorrow.

definitions.note: This is the infinitive with "zu" (e.g., after certain verbs like "versuchen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, morgen wiederzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to come back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used as a "zu"-infinitive (e.g., after verbs like freuen, hoffen, versuchen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich freue mich, dich bald wiederzusehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking forward to seeing you again soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wiege das Paket.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I weigh the package.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Paket wiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to weigh the package.

definitions.note: Used for gently moving someone (often a baby) back and forth, e.g. in your arms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie kann das Baby gut wiegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She can rock the baby well.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie viel wiegst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much do you weigh?

definitions.note: Present tense (er/sie/es) of „wiegen“ in the sense of having a certain weight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Koffer wiegt zehn Kilo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suitcase weighs ten kilos.

definitions.note: Present tense (er/sie/es) of „wiegen“ in the sense of gently moving back and forth (e.g., a baby) to calm them.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mutter wiegt das Baby im Arm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mother rocks the baby in her arms.

definitions.note: Often used with a separable particle like „ab“ or with „zurück“ (e.g., „wies … ab“, „wies … zurück“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wies den Vorschlag zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss rejected the suggestion.

definitions.note: Simple past form of „anweisen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef wies mich an, den Bericht zu schreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss instructed me to write the report.

definitions.note: simple past of „weisen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wies auf den Fehler hin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pointed out the mistake.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „weisen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lehrerin wies auf den Fehler hin, und die Schüler wiesen ihn auch sofort nach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher pointed out the mistake, and the students also proved it right away.

definitions.note: Often used in spoken German; similar to "warum".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wieso bist du heute so spät?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you so late today?

definitions.note: Used in questions (and indirect questions) to ask about quantity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wieviel kostet das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does that cost?

definitions.note: Used in questions to ask about an amount (uncountable) or number (countable).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wieviel kostet das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does that cost?

definitions.note: Used to ask about quantity. In standard spelling it is usually written as two words ("wie viel" / "wie viele"), but here the headword is given as "wieviel"; the example below keeps the exact form "wieviel" as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wieviel kostet das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does that cost?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wievielmal warst du schon in Berlin?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many times have you been to Berlin?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist heute ganz wild.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is completely wild today.

definitions.note: Often used informally to describe someone or something behaving in an uncontrolled, overly excited way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf der Party ging es wild zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Things got pretty crazy at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er gestikuliert wild mit den Händen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gestures wildly with his hands.

definitions.note: adjective form of "wild"; often used before a noun (e.g., "wilde Tiere") or as a weak ending after "der/die/das".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der wilde Hund rennt durch den Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wild dog runs through the park.

definitions.note: adjective ending used before a masculine noun in the accusative case (e.g., „einen wilden …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sehen einen wilden Hund im Wald.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We see a wild dog in the forest.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective ending (e.g., masculine nominative singular before a noun: „ein wilder …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein wilder Hund läuft durch den Park.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A wild dog is running through the park.

definitions.note: Modal verb used with another verb in the infinitive (often at the end of the sentence).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to go home earlier today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "wollen" ("to want (to)").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will heute zu Hause bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wants to stay at home today.

definitions.note: Used in the fixed phrase „um … willen“ and takes the genitive; sounds formal/old-fashioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Um des Friedens willen sollten wir leiser sein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For the sake of peace, we should be quieter.

definitions.note: Mostly used in the formal phrase „willens sein, (etwas) zu …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin willens, dir zu helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am willing to help you.

definitions.note: Past tense form of „einwilligen“, often used with „in“ + accusative (e.g. „in etwas einwilligen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er willigte in den Vertrag ein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He agreed to the contract.

definitions.note: Often used with „ein“ (willigte ein = agreed/consented).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er willigte ein und unterschrieb den Vertrag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He agreed and signed the contract.

definitions.note: Often used as a greeting or to make someone feel welcome; also used in the phrase „Willkommen in …“ (“Welcome to …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Willkommen in Berlin!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Welcome to Berlin!

definitions.note: used to greet someone or to make them feel welcome
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Willkommen in Berlin!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Welcome to Berlin!

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „wollen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Willst du einen Kaffee?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a coffee?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present of "wollen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Willst du mit mir ins Kino gehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to go to the movies with me?

definitions.note: Often used with „von“ + dative: „Es wimmelt von …“ = “It’s teeming with …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Stadt wimmelt es von Touristen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is teeming with tourists.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es sehr windig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is very windy.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „winken“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er winkte uns zum Abschied.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He waved goodbye to us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Wohnung ist winzig, aber sehr gemütlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apartment is tiny, but very cozy.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (attributive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sahen eine winzige Spinne in der Ecke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a tiny spider in the corner.

definitions.note: Form: neuter nominative/accusative singular of the adjective "winzig" (used with a neuter noun, often after an article like "ein").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wohnen in einem winziges Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live in a tiny house.

definitions.note: 1st-person plural pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with an infinitive to talk about the future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird morgen kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the present passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus wird gebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is being built.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "werden"; also commonly used as an auxiliary to form the passive or the future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He becomes tired.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with an infinitive to talk about the future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wird morgen regnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperative (command) form used with du.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wirf den Ball zu mir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw the ball to me!

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "werfen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum wirfst du den Ball so weit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you throwing the ball so far?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "werfen" (er/sie/es).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wirft den Ball zu mir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He throws the ball to me.

definitions.native: to have an effect, to work
definitions.note: Often used as “wirken” = to have an effect/influence, and “auf + Akk.” = to affect (someone/something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Medikament kann schnell wirken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The medicine can take effect quickly.

definitions.note: Used to describe the impression something/someone gives (often with an adjective: „Er kann müde wirken.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann heute sehr müde wirken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can seem very tired today.

definitions.note: used to emphasize that something is real/true; in questions it can express surprise (“really?”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist das wirklich wahr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is that really true?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die wirkliche Welt, nicht ein Traum.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the real world, not a dream.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kenne den wirklichen Grund.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know the real reason.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wirkst heute sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seem very tired today.

definitions.note: Often used with an adjective (e.g., „wirkt müde“ = „seems tired“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wirkt heute sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seems very tired today.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "wirken"; commonly used in written German to describe impressions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wirkte müde, aber er ging trotzdem zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He seemed tired, but he still went to work.

definitions.note: Often used with an adjective to describe an impression (e.g., „müde wirken“ = to seem tired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wirkten sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They seemed very tired.

definitions.note: Often used for medicine or measures that produce a result.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Medizin wirkte sofort, aber die Tabletten wirkten erst nach einer Stunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The medicine worked immediately, but the tablets only had an effect after an hour.

definitions.note: Simple past (du-form) of "wirken"; often used meaning "to have an effect" or "to seem" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wirktest heute sehr ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seemed very calm today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wirktet gestern sehr müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You seemed very tired yesterday.

definitions.note: often used for things like measures, methods, speeches, or remedies that have a strong effect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die neue Methode ist sehr wirkungsvoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new method is very effective.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form; used both as a main verb meaning “become” and as an auxiliary to form the future tense or the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wirst morgen früh aufstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will get up tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: adjective form (e.g., before a noun) of wirtschaftlich
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die wirtschaftliche Lage ist im Moment schwierig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The economic situation is difficult at the moment.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal singular command (imperative), like “Wisch den Tisch ab!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wisch bitte den Tisch ab!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wipe the table off!

definitions.note: Often used with something like "(den Tisch) wischen" = to wipe (the table).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute den Tisch wischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to wipe the table today.

definitions.note: Commonly used for touchscreen gestures.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst nach links wischen, um das Foto zu wechseln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can swipe left to change the photo.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wischen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wischte den Tisch nach dem Essen ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wiped down the table after eating.

definitions.note: Often Konjunktiv I (subjunctive I), used in indirect/reported speech (e.g. „er sagt, er wisse …“). It can also be an imperative („Wisse!“ = “Know!”), but that use is uncommon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er wisse es nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he doesn't know it.

definitions.note: Used for knowing facts or information (compare: „kennen“ = know someone/something personally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will es wissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to know.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wissenschaftlich bewiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That has been scientifically proven.

definitions.note: adjective form used before a noun (attributive); agrees with the noun it describes
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie liest wissenschaftliche Artikel über Klima und Gesundheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reads scientific articles about climate and health.

definitions.note: This is an inflected form of the adjective (e.g., used after “die/der/das”, “einen”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich lese einen wissenschaftlichen Artikel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reading a scientific article.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) form of "wissen" (present tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wisst ihr, wo der Bahnhof ist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you know where the train station is?

definitions.native: to scent, to smell, to sense
definitions.note: Often used for animals (especially dogs) sensing a smell or danger; can also mean to suspect something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund kann die Angst wittern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog can scent the fear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war wirklich witzig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was really funny.

definitions.note: Old spelling (pre-1996). Today it’s usually written “wisst”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wißt doch, wo er wohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You know where he lives, don’t you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo wohnst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you live?

definitions.note: Also used to introduce a relative clause (like “where” in “the place where…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich weiß nicht, wo er wohnt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know where he lives.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Können wir uns woanders treffen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can we meet somewhere else?

definitions.note: Used with motion/direction (answering “where to?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen jetzt woandershin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going somewhere else now.

definitions.note: Used to refer back to what was just mentioned; often means “in which” or “where,” and can also introduce an additional detail (“whereby/and in the process”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine Aufgabe, wobei du viel Geduld brauchst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a task where you need a lot of patience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war wochenlang krank.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was sick for weeks.

definitions.note: Used in questions to ask what something happens by/through (the cause or means).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wodurch ist das Fenster kaputtgegangen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How did the window break?

definitions.note: Used in questions to ask the purpose or intended use of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wofür ist dieser Schlüssel?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is this key for?

definitions.note: Used in questions meaning “against what?” and also as a conjunction meaning “whereas/while (in contrast)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wogegen protestieren die Leute?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are the people protesting against?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich trinke Kaffee, wogegen sie lieber Tee trinkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I drink coffee, whereas she prefers tea.

definitions.note: Used in questions to ask about origin or where something comes from.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Woher kommst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are you from?

definitions.note: Used to ask about a destination or direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wohin fährst du morgen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are you going tomorrow?

definitions.note: Often used to describe how someone feels (especially in the phrase „sich wohl fühlen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich fühle mich heute nicht wohl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t feel well today.

definitions.note: Often used as a modal particle to show an assumption/guess.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt wohl später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’ll probably come later.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to describe how someone feels (e.g., „mir ist wohl“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist heute nicht wohl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t feel well today.

definitions.note: Often used to express an assumption or guess.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt wohl später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’ll probably come later.

definitions.note: Somewhat old-fashioned; often used after an illness to say someone is doing well again.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach einer Woche war er wieder wohlauf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a week, he was well again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Lied ist in Deutschland wohlbekannt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This song is well-known in Germany.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kommt aus einer wohlhabenden Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes from a wealthy family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Stadt baut mehr Wohnungen, damit nicht nur die wohlhabenden Menschen hier leben können.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city is building more apartments so that not only wealthy people can live here.

definitions.note: Usually used to describe a person who has a lot of money.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein wohlhabender Mann lebt in diesem Viertel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A wealthy man lives in this neighborhood.

definitions.note: Informal singular imperative of "wohnen" (a command/request to one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wohn bei uns, wenn du in der Stadt bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Live with us when you’re in the city.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present of "wohnen" ("I live").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in Berlin.

definitions.note: Used for living somewhere (having your home there).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne in Berlin, aber meine Schwester wohnt in Hamburg; wir wohnen trotzdem oft zusammen im Sommer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in Berlin, but my sister lives in Hamburg; we still often live together in the summer.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular informal (du) form of "wohnen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wo wohnst du jetzt?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you live now?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „wohnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "wohnen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr wohnte ich in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year I lived in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wohnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Früher wohnten wir in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We used to live in Berlin.

definitions.note: Colloquial/dialectal shortened form of forms of "wollen" (often written with an apostrophe: "woll'").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich woll heute nicht rausgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to go out today.

definitions.note: Subjunctive I form of "wollen", often used in reported speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er wolle morgen früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he wants to leave earlier tomorrow.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv I form, mainly used in reported speech (especially in news or formal writing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagte, er wolle nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said he wanted to go home.

definitions.note: Used as a modal (auxiliary) verb; it’s followed by an infinitive (usually at the end of the clause).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollen heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to go home earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used with another verb in the infinitive: „Ich will gehen.“ = “I want to go.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will wollen, dass du heute Abend zu Hause bleibst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to want you to stay at home tonight.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural (ihr) form; also used for polite address in some dialects/older usage.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wollt ihr heute ins Kino gehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you (all) want to go to the cinema today?

definitions.note: Past tense form of „wollen“ (to want).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wollt gestern früher nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (plural) wanted to go home earlier yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollte heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to go home earlier today.

definitions.note: Often used to sound more polite or less direct than “will”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollte Sie kurz etwas fragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to ask you something quickly.

definitions.note: simple past of „wollen“ (to want)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wollte heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to go home earlier today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „wollen“; often used in writing and storytelling
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollten heute früh losfahren, aber es hat geregnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wanted to leave early today, but it rained.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wollen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollten heute ins Kino gehen, aber es regnet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wanted to go to the cinema today, but it’s raining.

definitions.note: Past tense form of the modal verb „wollen“; often used for polite requests (like „would like to“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollten heute früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wanted to go home earlier today.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du), simple past of the auxiliary verb "wollen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wolltest gestern früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wanted to go home earlier yesterday.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular, simple past (du-form) of "wollen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wolltest gestern früher nach Hause gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wanted to go home earlier yesterday.

definitions.note: 2nd person plural simple past (ihr) of „wollen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wolltet heute früher gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) wanted to leave earlier today.

definitions.note: second person plural (ihr), simple past
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wolltet gestern ins Kino gehen, aber es war zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You all wanted to go to the cinema yesterday, but it was too late.

definitions.note: Used in questions and relative clauses; it refers to the thing/instrument you use to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Womit schreibst du den Brief?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you writing the letter with?

definitions.note: Used to introduce a relative clause, referring back to something mentioned before.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist der Stift, womit ich immer schreibe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the pen with which I always write.

definitions.note: Often used when the speaker considers something plausible and sometimes (slightly) undesirable or surprising; can also mean “even/actually (might)” in warnings (e.g., “womöglich noch …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Womöglich kommt er heute später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He might possibly come later today.

definitions.native: what for, what after, according to what
definitions.note: Used in questions and relative clauses; often used with verbs like „suchen“ (look for) or „sich richten“ (to be guided by).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wonach suchst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you looking for?

definitions.note: Used with verbs/adjectives that take the preposition "an" (e.g., denken an, arbeiten an) in a question or relative clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Woran denkst du gerade?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you thinking about right now?

definitions.note: Often used in questions and relative clauses, referring back to something and meaning “on what/what for.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Worauf wartest du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you waiting for?

definitions.note: Used to ask about the material or origin of something; often introduces an indirect question after verbs like „wissen“ (to know).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Woraus ist der Tisch gemacht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the table made of?

definitions.note: Past participle of „werden“ used mainly to form the passive voice (often with „sein“), e.g. „ist ... worden“ = „has been ...“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag ist gestern unterschrieben worden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract was signed yesterday.

definitions.note: Used in questions; refers to being inside something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Worin liegt das Problem?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the problem? (Literally: In what does the problem lie?)

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist sehr wortgewandt und kann ihre Meinung klar ausdrücken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very eloquent and can express her opinion clearly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie stand wortlos in der Tür und sah ihn an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She stood in the doorway without a word and looked at him.

definitions.native: what ... about, what ... for, what ... around (i.e., the issue/topic)
definitions.note: Used to ask about the topic/issue someone is talking about (often in questions like „Worum geht es?“ = “What is it about?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Worum geht es in dem Film?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is the movie about?

definitions.note: Used in questions and relative clauses; refers to a thing/idea (not a person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Worüber sprecht ihr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you talking about?

definitions.note: Used in questions and relative clauses; refers back to something previously mentioned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wovon sprichst du?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you talking about?

definitions.note: Used in questions and relative clauses with verbs/adjectives that take "vor" (e.g., Angst haben vor, warnen vor).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wovor hast du Angst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you afraid of?

definitions.note: Expresses surprise, admiration, or amazement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wow, das ist wirklich beeindruckend!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, that is really impressive!

definitions.note: Used to ask about purpose or usefulness; can also mean “why” in the sense of “to what end?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wozu brauchst du das?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you need that for?

definitions.note: simple past of „aufwachsen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wuchs in Berlin auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grew up in Berlin.

definitions.note: simple past of „wachsen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind wuchs sehr schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child grew very quickly.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „wachsen“ for „we/they“ (and polite „you“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder wuchsen sehr schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children grew very quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Urlaub war wunderbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vacation was wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wunderbar!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is wonderful!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Urlaub war wunderbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vacation was wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Urlaub war wunderbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vacation was wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen schmeckt wunderbar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food tastes wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine wunderbare Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wonderful idea.

definitions.note: Adjective form used with a noun (attributive), e.g. with feminine or plural nouns depending on the article.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine wunderbare Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a wonderful idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hatte einen wunderbaren Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a wonderful day.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine/neuter nouns in certain cases (e.g., accusative masculine, dative plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe einen wunderbaren Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a wonderful day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wunderbarer Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wonderful day.

definitions.note: This can be the comparative form of „wunderbar“ (often used with „als“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der zweite Film war wunderbarer als der erste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The second movie was more wonderful than the first.

definitions.note: comparative form of „wunderbar“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wunderbarer Tag für einen Spaziergang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a more wonderful day for a walk.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wunderbares Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wonderful gift.

definitions.note: Neuter nominative/accusative singular form (often used before a neuter noun or as a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wunderbares Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wonderful gift.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich wundern“ (e.g. „ich wundere mich“ = I’m surprised / I wonder).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wundere mich über seine Antwort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m surprised about his answer.

definitions.note: Used in constructions where something is surprising; often with a subject like „Es“ or „Das“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es würde mich wundern, wenn er pünktlich kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d be surprised if he arrives on time.

definitions.note: Very common as the reflexive verb „sich wundern“; expresses that you are surprised or puzzled.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann mich nur wundern über die hohen Preise.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All I can do is wonder at the high prices.

definitions.note: Common intensifier meaning “wonderfully/very beautiful.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sonnenuntergang ist wunderschön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sunset is beautiful.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize that something is especially beautiful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sonnenuntergang ist wunderschön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sunset is beautiful.

definitions.note: Stronger than just "schön" (beautiful).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sonnenuntergang ist wunderschön.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sunset is gorgeous.

definitions.note: Used before a noun; means “very beautiful.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine wunderschöne Aussicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a beautiful view.

definitions.note: inflected form of the adjective; often used before a noun (e.g., "wunderschöne Stadt")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine wunderschöne Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a beautiful city.

definitions.note: Form of the adjective used before a noun (attributive), e.g. with plural nouns like „die wunderschönen …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vielen Dank für die wunderschönen Blumen!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you very much for the beautiful flowers!

definitions.note: adjective ending used in declined forms (e.g., after a definite article or in certain case/gender/number contexts)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich danke dir für den wunderschönen Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for the wonderful evening.

definitions.note: Used as an inflected form before a noun (e.g., „ein wunderschöner …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wunderschöner Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wonderfully beautiful day.

definitions.note: Used before a neuter singular noun (e.g. ein wunderschönes Bild) or after words like etwas/nichts/viel (e.g. etwas Wunderschönes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wunderschönes Bild.
