definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a beautiful picture.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used with a neuter singular noun (e.g., "ein wunderschönes Haus").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wunderschönes Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a beautiful present.

definitions.note: Often used like: „Das wundert mich.“ (= “That surprises me.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wundert mich, dass du schon fertig bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It surprises me that you’re already finished.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Urlaub war wundervoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vacation was wonderful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Urlaub war wundervoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The vacation was wonderful.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (inflected form of the adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir hatten einen wundervollen Tag am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a wonderful day at the lake.

definitions.note: Adjective ending used before a noun (e.g., feminine or plural, depending on the article).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine wundervolle Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a wonderful idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich danke dir für den wundervollen Abend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for the wonderful evening.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein wundervoller Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a wonderful day.

definitions.note: Used as the simple past form of the auxiliary „werden“ to form the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag wurde unterschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract was signed.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „werden“ (ich/er/sie/es wurde). Often also used as an auxiliary to form the passive in the simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde letztes Jahr Vater.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He became a father last year.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the passive in the simple past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Auto wurde gestern repariert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car was repaired yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past of the auxiliary "werden"; used to form the passive in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fenster wurden gestern geputzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows were cleaned yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „werden“ (often used with plural subjects or formal „you“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wurden plötzlich sehr ruhig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They suddenly became very quiet.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary to form the passive in the simple past (Präteritum).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Fenster wurden gestern geputzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The windows were cleaned yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (du-form) of the auxiliary verb „werden“; also used to form the passive in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wurdest gestern sehr schnell müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You got very tired very quickly yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person plural (“you all”); used as an auxiliary to form the passive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wurdet sofort informiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were informed immediately.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „waschen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern wusch ich meine Hände vor dem Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I washed my hands before eating.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) plural form of „waschen“ (e.g., „wir/sie wuschen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern wuschen wir die Wäsche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we washed the laundry.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „wissen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wusste nicht, dass du heute kommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t know that you were coming today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wissen“; used for „we/you/they knew“ (and formal „you knew“) depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wussten das nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We didn't know that.

definitions.note: Second-person singular simple past of "wissen" (du-Form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wusstest du schon, dass der Kurs heute ausfällt?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you already know that the class is canceled today?

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 2nd person plural (ihr) of „wissen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wusstet es gestern schon.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You already knew it yesterday.

definitions.note: Past tense form of „wissen“; spelling „wusste“ is also common in modern German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wußte nicht, dass du heute kommst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t know that you were coming today.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural (they) or formal ‘you’ (Sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wußten nicht, dass der Zug ausfällt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They didn't know that the train was cancelled.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular, simple past (du-Form) of "wissen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wußtest das schon seit gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You knew that already since yesterday.

definitions.note: Old spelling of „wusstet“ (simple past, 2nd person plural: „you (all) knew“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr wußtet nicht, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You didn’t know that he was coming today.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of "wachsen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Pflanze wächst schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plant grows quickly.

definitions.note: First-person singular present ("I ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wähle ein blaues T‑Shirt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I choose a blue T-shirt.

definitions.note: First-person singular present ("I ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wähle morgen bei der Wahl.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I vote tomorrow in the election.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du kannst zwischen Tee und Kaffee wählen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose between tea and coffee.

definitions.note: Used for elections or decisions in a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Sonntag wählen wir einen neuen Bürgermeister.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sunday we’re voting for a new mayor.

definitions.note: Often used about someone who is hard to please (e.g., about food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr wählerisch beim Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very picky about food.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of „wählen“ (used with „du“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wählst heute ein blaues T‑Shirt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You choose a blue T-shirt today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wählt ein neues Handy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He chooses a new phone.

definitions.note: Used in the context of elections or voting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wählt morgen im Rathaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She votes tomorrow at city hall.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "wählen"; can mean choosing or voting depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wählte den roten Pullover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She chose the red sweater.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wählen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wählten ein anderes Restaurant.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They chose a different restaurant.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „wählen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Letztes Jahr wählten wir einen neuen Bürgermeister.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year we voted for a new mayor.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/old-fashioned; often suggests a mistaken belief.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wähnte sich in Sicherheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He thought he was safe.

definitions.note: Usually takes the genitive case (especially in formal German); in everyday speech it’s often used with the dative.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Während des Films hat er nicht gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the movie, he didn’t speak.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a simultaneous action or situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Während ich koche, hört sie Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While I’m cooking, she listens to music.

definitions.note: Introduces a subordinate clause (verb goes to the end).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Während ich koche, hört er Musik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: While I’m cooking, he listens to music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film währt zwei Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie lasts two hours.

definitions.note: colloquial short form of „wäre“ (subjunctive II of „sein“); often used as an auxiliary in conditional/perfect forms
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wär früher gekommen, aber ich hatte keinen Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have come earlier, but I didn't have a bus.

definitions.note: Subjunctive II form of „sein“; used for hypotheticals/conditions (and often for polite phrasing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, wäre ich öfter hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, I would be here more often.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) of "sein"; used for hypotheticals and polite/indirect statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, wären wir öfter zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, we would be together more often.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) subjunctive II / conditional form of „sein“; often used in „wenn …“ or to express hypotheticals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du hier wärest, wäre alles einfacher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you were here, everything would be easier.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form of "sein" used with "ihr" (you all), often in hypothetical/if-clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ihr mehr Zeit wäret, könntet ihr öfter reisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you had more time, you could travel more often.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wärme die Suppe auf.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heat up the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Suppe in der Mikrowelle wärmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will warm up the soup in the microwave.

definitions.note: comparative form of „warm“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Heute ist es wärmer als gestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it is warmer than yesterday.

definitions.note: Comparative form of "warm"; used before a noun or as a predicative adjective depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche eine wärmere Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a warmer jacket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Suppe wärmt schnell.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup warms up quickly.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „wärmen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wärmte die Suppe in der Mikrowelle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He warmed the soup in the microwave.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) of „sein“, used in hypothetical or polite statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du hier wärst, wäre alles leichter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you were here, everything would be easier.

definitions.note: Archaic/poetic form (instead of modern „wäret“); used with „sein“ in the subjunctive (e.g., „wenn ihr … wärt“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ihr früher da wärt, könnten wir anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you were here earlier, we could start.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of "waschen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du wäschst dir die Hände vor dem Essen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wash your hands before eating.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „waschen“ (to wash).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wäscht sich die Hände.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He washes his hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns wöchentlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We meet weekly.

definitions.note: Common colloquial short form of „wünsche“ (often used with „ich“: „Ich wünsch …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünsch dir einen schönen Tag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you a nice day.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., „dir“) to express good wishes; can also be used more formally to mean “would like” (e.g., „Ich wünsche einen Kaffee.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünsche dir alles Gute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you all the best.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünsche dir alles Gute, und ich möchte dir außerdem wünschen, dass du gesund bleibst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you all the best, and I would also like to wish that you stay healthy.

definitions.note: Often used to sound polite, especially in stores or restaurants.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was wünschen Sie? — Ich wünsche einen Kaffee, bitte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would you like? — I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was wünschst du dir zum Geburtstag?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you wish for your birthday?

definitions.note: third-person singular (he/she/it) of „wünschen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wünscht sich ein neues Fahrrad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wishes for a new bike.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „wünschen“; also used in polite requests (e.g. „Ich wünschte …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wünschte, ich hätte mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wished I had more time.

definitions.note: Used with an infinitive in Konjunktiv II (subjunctive II), e.g. „würde gehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich würd dir helfen, aber ich hab keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would help you, but I don’t have time.

definitions.note: Used to form the conditional or polite requests (Konjunktiv II of „werden“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich würde gern kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to come.

definitions.note: Used as the subjunctive (Konjunktiv II) form of the auxiliary "werden" to express hypothetical situations or polite requests; often used with an infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir würden gern kommen, aber wir haben keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like to come, but we don’t have time.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular subjunctive (Konjunktiv II) of "werden", used for hypotheticals/conditionals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was würdest du tun, wenn du mehr Zeit hättest?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What would you do if you had more time?

definitions.note: second-person plural (ihr) subjunctive II form of the auxiliary „werden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr würdet morgen länger bleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You would stay longer tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie blieb auch in dieser schwierigen Situation würdevoll.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She remained dignified even in this difficult situation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist dieser Auszeichnung würdig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is worthy of this award.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er blieb auch in der Krise würdig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He remained dignified even in the crisis.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) of "wissen"; often used for hypotheticals or polite statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn ich die Antwort wüsste, würde ich sie dir sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I knew the answer, I would tell you.

definitions.note: Subjunctive II or simple past (plural) of "wissen"; used for unreal/conditional situations or as past tense for "we/you/they".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn wir das früher wüssten, würden wir anders entscheiden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we knew that earlier, we would decide differently.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II (subjunctive) form, often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., with „wenn“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du das wüsstest, würdest du anders handeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you knew that, you would act differently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin wütend auf dich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m angry at you.

definitions.note: Often used like an adverb to describe how someone looks/speaks/acts (e.g., „jemanden wütend ansehen“ = to look at someone angrily).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er schaute mich wütend an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He looked at me angrily.

definitions.note: Konjunktiv II form of "wissen"; used for hypothetical situations, polite statements, or reported uncertainty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wüßte gern, ob du morgen Zeit hast.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d like to know whether you have time tomorrow.

definitions.note: Informal; common in spoken German and in casual writing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yeah, das stimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yeah, that's right.

definitions.note: Informal, mostly used in texting/online chat; the standard German word is "ja".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yes, ich komme gleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yes, I’m coming right away.

definitions.note: Informal greeting or attention-getter.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo, wie geht’s?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yo, how’s it going?

definitions.note: English pronoun sometimes used in German (e.g., in ads, slogans, or informal mixed-language speech); in standard German you would use „du“ (singular informal) or „Sie“ (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hey you, komm mal her!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hey you, come here for a moment!

definitions.note: Used to emphasize that something happens suddenly or very quickly; often in the phrase “und zack …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Und zack, war er weg!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: And just like that, he was gone!

definitions.note: Often a colloquial short form of „zahle“ (especially in speech/writing like texts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zahl das heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll pay that today.

definitions.note: Often a colloquial short form of „zähle“ (from „zählen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zahl bis zehn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I count to ten.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zahle heute mit Karte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m paying by card today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss heute die Miete zahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pay the rent today.

definitions.note: Commonly used before a plural noun; often implies a relatively large number.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gab zahlreiche Gründe, warum sie nicht kommen konnte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were numerous reasons why she couldn’t come.

definitions.note: Used as a determiner/adjective before a noun; often in more formal written German.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zahlreiche Menschen warten vor dem Gebäude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Numerous people are waiting in front of the building.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense (du).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du zahlst heute die Rechnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You pay the bill today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zahlt die Rechnung sofort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pays the bill right away.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „zahlen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zahlte gestern die Rechnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I paid the bill yesterday.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „zahlen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir zahlten gestern die Rechnung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We paid the bill yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for animals; can also describe a person who is very timid or not rebellious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund ist ganz zahm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is completely tame.

definitions.note: Often used for petty or frequent arguments; somewhat old-fashioned compared to "streiten".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder zanken sich schon wieder um das Spielzeug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are quarreling again about the toy.

definitions.note: Often used for restless, nervous movement, especially by children.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind kann nicht still sitzen und muss die ganze Zeit zappeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child can’t sit still and has to fidget the whole time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Haut des Babys ist ganz zart.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby's skin is very tender.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Wald sieht im Winter wirklich zauberhaft aus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The forest looks really magical in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine zauberhafte Nacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was a magical night.

definitions.note: Often used for doing magic like a magician; can also be used figuratively for creating something seemingly effortlessly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zauberer kann auf der Bühne zaubern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The magician can do magic on stage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe zehn Euro dabei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have ten euros with me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich zehnmal angerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called you ten times.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dieser Stadt leben zehntausend Menschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ten thousand people live in this city.

definitions.note: ordinal number (used for dates, order, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns am zehnten Januar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re meeting on the tenth of January.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zeichne ein Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I draw a house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann gut zeichnen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can draw well.

definitions.note: Used for signing a document (e.g., a contract).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte zeichnen Sie den Vertrag hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please sign the contract here.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du zeichnest ein Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are drawing a house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind zeichnet ein Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child draws a house.

definitions.note: Commonly used with documents, letters, or contracts (e.g., „einen Vertrag zeichnen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zeichnet den Vertrag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He signs the contract.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „zeichnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zeichnete ein Haus auf das Papier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drew a house on the paper.

definitions.note: Imperative (informal singular): used when telling one person you address as “du” to show something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zeig mir bitte dein Foto!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Show me your photo, please!

definitions.note: 1st person singular present tense ("I show")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zeige dir das Foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I show you the photo.

definitions.note: imperative (informal singular): "show!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zeige mir bitte das Foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please show me the photo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir das Foto zeigen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me the photo?

definitions.note: Often used with "auf" (e.g., "auf etwas zeigen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kann auf der Karte auf den Fluss zeigen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He can point to the river on the map.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present (du-form) of „zeigen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zeigst du mir bitte, wo die Haltestelle ist?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please show me where the stop is?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "zeigen" (er/sie/es zeigt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer zeigt ein Bild.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher shows a picture.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „zeigen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zeigte mir ein Foto von seiner Familie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He showed me a photo of his family.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "zeigen"; usually means "they showed" (or formal "you showed") depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie zeigten mir den Weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They showed me the way.

definitions.note: Often used like “rechtzeitig” to mean arriving/being done early enough (not late).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte zeitig nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come home in time (early enough).

definitions.note: Often used to mean something is possible or limited with regard to timing/scheduling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zeitlich passt es mir am besten am Freitag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Timewise, Friday works best for me.

definitions.note: Often used to mean something happens for a limited period or intermittently (not continuously).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen der Bauarbeiten war die Straße zeitweise gesperrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the construction work, the road was temporarily closed.

definitions.note: usually means camping in a tent
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir zelten am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re camping by the lake.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „zelten“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zeltet am See.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He camps by the lake.

definitions.note: simple past of „zerbrechen“ (to break, shatter)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas zerbrach auf dem Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass broke on the floor.

definitions.note: Usually refers to breaking something into pieces (often accidentally or by force).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Glas nicht zerbrechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will not break the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas ist sehr zerbrechlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is very fragile.

definitions.note: Often used for something breaking unintentionally (e.g., glass, a plate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du das Glas fallen lässt, zerbricht es.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you drop the glass, it breaks.

definitions.note: past participle of „zerbrechen“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas ist zerbrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is broken.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (it’s originally the past participle of „zerbrechen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Glas ist zerbrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund zerfetzt das Kissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog tears the pillow to pieces.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kissen ist zerfetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pillow is torn to pieces.

definitions.note: Often used for acids, rust, or insects damaging something; can also be used figuratively (e.g., worry eating at you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Säure kann das Metall zerfressen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The acid can corrode the metal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zerlegt den Motor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He takes the engine apart.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., with "sein" in the perfect or as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Motor ist schon zerlegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The engine has already been taken apart.

definitions.note: Often implies squeezing with force so something gets flattened, burst, or damaged.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pass auf, dass du die Beeren nicht zerquetschen wirst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful that you won’t crush the berries.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tomate ist in der Tasche zerquetscht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tomato is crushed in the bag.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird den Brief in zwei Stücke zerreißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will tear the letter into two pieces.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present tense of „zerreißen“; can be used literally (tear/rip something) or figuratively (tear something apart).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hund zerreißt das Spielzeug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog tears the toy apart.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „zerreißen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zerriss den Brief.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tore up the letter.

definitions.note: Can also be used figuratively for a person meaning emotionally torn or conflicted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Hemd ist zerrissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shirt is torn.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (it’s the past participle of „zerreißen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Papier ist zerrissen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The paper is torn.

definitions.native: to smash, to break into pieces
definitions.note: Often implies breaking something violently (e.g., by hitting it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das Glas zerschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He smashed the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute etwas zerstreut und vergesse ständig meinen Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm a bit absent-minded and I keep forgetting my key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bücher liegen zerstreut auf dem Boden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are scattered on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte sei vorsichtig, damit ich nichts zerstöre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be careful so that I don’t destroy anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm kann viele Häuser zerstören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm can destroy many houses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm hat das Dach zerstört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm destroyed the roof.

definitions.note: often used like a past participle (as an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Sturm war das Dach völlig zerstört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the roof was completely destroyed.

definitions.note: simple past form of "zerstören"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm zerstörte das Dach.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm destroyed the roof.

definitions.note: Past participle of "zerstückeln"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat ... zerstückelt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei hat die Beweise zerstückelt gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found the evidence chopped up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst die Blumen nicht zertreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not trample the flowers.

definitions.note: informal singular command (du imperative) of „ziehen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zieh bitte an der Tür!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pull on the door!

definitions.note: Used with the separable prefix: "vorziehen" → "Ich ziehe ... vor."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ziehe Tee vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer tea.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich). Also used in the polite imperative: Ziehe(n) Sie …
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ziehe die Tür zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pull the door shut.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (ich). Also used in the polite imperative: Ziehe(n) Sie …
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ziehe nächste Woche nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m moving to Berlin next week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte an der Tür ziehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please pull on the door?

definitions.note: Often used with “umziehen” for moving to a new home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nächste Woche ziehen wir nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next week we’re moving to Berlin.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form of „ziehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ziehst du bitte die Tür zu?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Could you please pull the door shut?

definitions.note: From the separable verb „vorziehen“ (e.g. „Er zieht X vor.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie zieht Tee vor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prefers tea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zieht den Wagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pulls the cart.

definitions.note: Often used with „auf“ + accusative (e.g., „auf das Ziel zielen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss auf die Scheibe zielen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to aim at the target.

definitions.note: often used with „auf“ (+ accusative): „auf etwas/jemanden zielen“ = to aim at someone/something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zielt auf die Mitte der Scheibe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He aims at the center of the target.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "zielen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Junge zielte auf die Dose.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy aimed at the can.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “rather” in the sense of “to a pretty high degree.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ziemlich teuer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s quite expensive.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize a noun (e.g., „eine ziemliche …“ = “quite a …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das war eine ziemliche Überraschung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was quite a surprise.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine noun (e.g., „ein ziemlicher …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein ziemlicher Aufwand.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s quite a lot of effort.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss diese Quelle in meiner Arbeit zitieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to cite this source in my paper.

definitions.note: Can also be used as the past participle meaning “quoted/cited.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zitiert einen Satz aus dem Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He quotes a sentence from the book.

definitions.note: Often used for shaking from cold, fear, or nervousness.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss vor Kälte zittern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tremble from the cold.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum zitterst du so sehr?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you shivering so much?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor Angst zittert er am ganzen Körper.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Out of fear, he trembles all over.

definitions.note: Simple past of "zittern".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor Kälte zitterte er am ganzen Körper.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He trembled all over from the cold.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural of „zittern“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vor Angst zitterten sie am ganzen Körper.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They trembled all over with fear.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „ziehen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zog die Tür langsam zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He slowly pulled the door shut.

definitions.note: Past tense of the separable verb „zurückziehen“; „zurück“ often goes to the end of the sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zog seine Bewerbung zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He withdrew his application.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "ziehen" (used with plural subjects like "wir"/"sie")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie zogen den schweren Koffer die Treppe hoch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They pulled the heavy suitcase up the stairs.

definitions.note: Stronger than "ärgerlich" (annoyed); sounds fairly formal/serious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war zornig, weil er sie belogen hatte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was angry because he had lied to her.

definitions.note: Used before an adjective or adverb to mean “too” (more than desired/possible).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kaffee ist zu heiß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is too hot.

definitions.note: Preposition used with the dative, often for going to a person or a specific place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe zu meinem Arzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to my doctor.

definitions.note: Used before an adjective or adverb to say something is more than desired or acceptable.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist heute zu kalt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s too cold today.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase „etwas ist zu“ (= something is closed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door is closed.

definitions.note: used before an infinitive (often after another verb)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, früher zu kommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to come earlier.

definitions.note: used before adjectives/adverbs to mean ‘too (much)’
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kaffee ist zu heiß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coffee is too hot.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce the very first point or step.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zuallererst müssen wir die wichtigsten Fragen klären.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First of all, we have to clarify the most important questions.

definitions.note: Often used for preparing food (e.g., meals, dishes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde das Abendessen zubereiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will prepare dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Essen ist frisch zubereitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food is freshly prepared.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Auge zuckte kurz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His eye twitched briefly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe keine Zeit, und zudem bin ich müde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time, and moreover I’m tired.

definitions.note: used for reciprocal relationships or movement between two or more people/things
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sind sehr freundlich zueinander.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are very friendly to each other.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen zuerst die Hausaufgaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First we do the homework.

definitions.note: Usually follows the noun/pronoun it refers to and is used with the dative case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Polizei zufolge war es ein Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the police, it was an accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit dem Ergebnis zufrieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m satisfied with the result.

definitions.note: Inflected form of the adjective „zufrieden“ (used before a noun, e.g. after „den“, „die“, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie sprach mit den zufriedenen Kunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spoke with the satisfied customers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Ergebnis ist zufriedenstellend, aber nicht perfekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The result is satisfactory, but not perfect.

definitions.note: This is the zu-infinitive form of „zufriedenstellen“, often used in constructions like „um … zufriedenzustellen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich arbeite länger, um den Kunden zufriedenzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work longer to satisfy the customer.

definitions.note: used as a „zu“-infinitive form (e.g., after another verb: „versuchen, ... zu“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, alle Kunden zufriedenzustellen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to satisfy all customers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn zufällig im Supermarkt getroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into him by chance at the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zufälligerweise habe ich ihn gestern im Supermarkt getroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By chance, I ran into him at the supermarket yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like "etwas hinzufügen" (= to add something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte noch etwas hinzufügen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to add something else.

definitions.note: often used to admit something (sometimes reluctantly), e.g. after „Ich muss …“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss zugeben, dass ich einen Fehler gemacht habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to admit that I made a mistake.

definitions.note: common in cooking instructions
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, am Ende etwas Salz zuzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to add a little salt at the end.

definitions.note: Used mainly with time expressions (e.g., den Tag/Abend) meaning “to spend” time somewhere or doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den ganzen Tag im Park zugebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I spent the whole day in the park.

definitions.note: Often used for lakes/ponds (frozen over) or for things like doors/locks (frozen shut).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der See ist komplett zugefroren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lake is completely frozen over.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe der Suppe Salz zugefügt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I added salt to the soup.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zugeben“, often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat … zugegeben“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat den Fehler zugegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He admitted the mistake.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a concession (like “I admit…”), especially at the start of a sentence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zugegeben, ich habe einen Fehler gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admittedly, I made a mistake.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal; often used in phrases like „anwesend/zugegen sein“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei der Sitzung waren alle Mitglieder zugegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All members were present at the meeting.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal; often used with „sein“ (e.g. „zugegen sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bei der Sitzung war auch der Bürgermeister zugegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor was also present at the meeting.

definitions.note: past participle of „zuhören“ (often used with „haben“: „hat zugehört“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir aufmerksam zugehört.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He listened to me attentively.

definitions.note: often used for things that are officially permitted (e.g., medicines, vehicles, products)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Medikament ist in Deutschland zugelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The medicine is approved in Germany.

definitions.note: Often used about gaining weight.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe in den letzten Monaten ein paar Kilo zugelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve put on a few kilos in the last few months.

definitions.note: Often used as „sich etwas zulegen“ = to get/acquire something for yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat sich ein neues Fahrrad zugelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got herself a new bike.

definitions.note: past participle of „zumachen“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Fenster zugemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I closed the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe in letzter Zeit zugenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve gained weight lately.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Preise haben stark zugenommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prices have increased a lot.

definitions.note: often used as a past participle (e.g. with „haben“) or like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Gemüse schon zugerichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already prepared the vegetables.

definitions.note: informal; used when someone is hurt or looks badly damaged after an attack or accident.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde übel zugerichtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was badly beaten up.

definitions.note: Often used when someone has officially agreed/confirmed something (e.g., help or attendance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mir seine Hilfe zugesagt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He promised me his help.

definitions.note: past participle of "zuschauen"; often used with "haben" (Perfekt): "hat zugeschaut"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dem Spiel zugeschaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watched the game.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zuschlagen“, often used for doors/windows closing with force.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Tür ist zugeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door has slammed shut.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative person/thing: „etwas wird jemandem zugeschrieben“ = something is attributed to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Erfolg wurde der ganzen Mannschaft zugeschrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The success was attributed to the whole team.

definitions.note: past participle of "zusehen"; often used with "haben" in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe beim Spiel nur zugesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only watched the game.

definitions.note: Past participle of "zustellen"; often used for mail/parcels being delivered (and also in passive perfect tenses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Paket wurde heute zugestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package was delivered today.

definitions.note: past participle of "zustimmen" (often used with "haben")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dem Plan zugestimmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agreed to the plan.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „etwas ist jemandem zugestoßen“ meaning something (usually bad) happened to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Was ist dir zugestoßen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What happened to you?

definitions.note: Usually used with dative: jemandem/etwas zugetan sein.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin meiner Schwester sehr zugetan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very fond of my sister.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zuteilen“, often used with „werden“ or „bekommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jeder Mitarbeiter bekommt eine Aufgabe zugeteilt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Each employee is assigned a task.

definitions.note: Often used with "sein" to say someone has moved to a place (e.g. "nach Berlin zugezogen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin letztes Jahr nach Hamburg zugezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I moved to Hamburg last year.

definitions.note: Often used for curtains/blinds (e.g. "Die Vorhänge sind zugezogen.").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Vorhänge sind schon zugezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The curtains are already drawn.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal writing; it can also mean “also/at the same time” when adding a second point.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er arbeitet und studiert zugleich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works and studies at the same time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin müde und zugleich glücklich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am tired and at the same time happy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Dieb will nach meiner Tasche zugreifen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief wants to grab my bag.

definitions.note: Common when offering food: „Greif zu!“ (imperative of zugreifen)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte zugreifen und nimm dir ein Stück Kuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please help yourself and take a piece of cake.

definitions.note: Usually used in the fixed verb phrase „zugrunde gehen“ (to be ruined, to go under).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele kleine Läden gehen durch die hohen Mieten zugrunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many small shops are ruined because of the high rents.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like "zugrunde gehen" (to go under/perish) or "zugrunde richten" (to ruin).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ohne Wasser gehen die Pflanzen zugrunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, the plants perish.

definitions.note: Often used for places, information, or people (meaning approachable/open).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Eingang ist barrierefrei und gut zugänglich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The entrance is barrier-free and easily accessible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin heute Abend zuhause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m at home this evening.

definitions.note: Usually used with the dative: jemandem zuhören = to listen to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir aufmerksam zuhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will listen to you attentively.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „zuhören“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum zuhörst du mir nicht?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why aren’t you listening to me?

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of "zuhören".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zuhört mir immer aufmerksam.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always listens to me attentively.

definitions.native: to approach, to come up to
definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „auf jemanden zukommen“ (to approach someone, e.g., to talk or propose something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss nächste Woche auf dich zukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to come to you (approach you) next week.

definitions.native: to be coming up (for someone), to be due (for someone)
definitions.note: Common with things like costs or work: „Auf jemanden zukommen“ + noun (e.g., Kosten, Arbeit, Aufgaben).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf dich werden keine zusätzlichen Kosten zukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No additional costs will come up for you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die zukünftigen Kosten genau planen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to plan the future costs carefully.

definitions.note: Often used for formally allowing something (e.g., an action, a person, a vehicle, an application).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lehrer wird keine Handys im Unterricht zulassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher will not allow any phones in class.

definitions.note: Very often used reflexively: „sich (etwas) zulegen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde mir ein neues Fahrrad zulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to get myself a new bike.

definitions.note: Often used with „Tempo“ or in the phrase „eine Schippe zulegen“ (= speed up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen beim Tempo zulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to speed up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn zuletzt im Sommer gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I last saw him in the summer.

definitions.note: Used after the noun or pronoun it refers to (postposition), usually with the dative: „meiner Mutter zuliebe“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Meiner Schwester zuliebe komme ich mit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For my sister’s sake, I’m coming along.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef zulässt keine privaten Telefonate im Büro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss doesn’t allow personal phone calls in the office.

definitions.note: Contraction of „zu dem“ (used before masculine/neuter nouns in the dative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe zum Arzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the doctor.

definitions.note: Often used for closing something like a door, window, or lid; can also mean “to close up” (e.g., a shop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Fenster zumachen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please close the window?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe zumindest versucht, dir zu helfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At least I tried to help you.

definitions.note: Mostly used in fixed expressions like „jemandem ist (nicht) zumute“ to say how someone feels.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist heute nicht zumute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not in the mood today.

definitions.note: Mostly used in fixed phrases like „zunichte machen“ (to thwart/undo) or „zunichte werden/gehen“ (to come to nothing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Sturm hat unsere Pläne zunichte gemacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm ruined our plans.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zunächst trinken wir einen Kaffee, und dann gehen wir zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First we’ll have a coffee, and then we’ll go to work.

definitions.note: contraction of „zu der“ (used with feminine singular nouns in the dative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe zur Schule.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to school.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „kommen“, „finden“, or „weisen“ to mean doing something the right way or arriving at the right place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin mit der Karte schnell zurechtgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I managed quickly with the map.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „kommen“ (to get along), „finden“ (to figure out), or „weisen“ (to reprimand/set straight).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit der neuen Software komme ich noch nicht zurecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still can’t get along with the new software.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin allein gut zurechtgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I managed well on my own.

definitions.native: to cope, to manage, to get by
definitions.note: Commonly used with "mit" + dative to mean "to cope/get along with" someone/something. The verb is separable: present tense often appears as "... komme ... zurecht".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich komme mit dem Stress nicht zurecht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t cope with the stress.

definitions.native: to cope, to manage, to get by
definitions.note: Often used with "mit" + dative to mean "to get along with" someone/something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mit dem Stress zurechtzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm trying to cope with the stress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zurzeit arbeite ich von zu Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the moment, I’m working from home.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion or return (e.g., zurückkommen, zurückgehen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Komm bitte zurück!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come back!

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like „gehen“, „kommen“, „geben“ to mean returning or giving back.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe jetzt zurück nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going back home now.

definitions.note: Often used for getting something returned to you (e.g., money, an item, or a reply).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte mein Geld zurückbekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get my money back.

definitions.native: to stay behind, to remain behind
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss hier zurückbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to stay behind here.

definitions.native: to fall behind, to lag behind
definitions.note: Often used about progress, development, or being behind others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir dürfen in der Schule nicht zurückbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must not fall behind at school.

definitions.note: Often used when you physically take something back to a place or person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir das Buch morgen zurückbringen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring the book back to me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Often used for things you can rotate, like a knob, dial, or screw.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du den Knopf bitte wieder zurückdrehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please turn the knob back again?

definitions.note: Common with volume, heat, or similar settings controlled by a knob/dial.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte zurückdrehen Sie die Musik ein bisschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn the music down a bit.

definitions.note: Often used for going back to a place by car/train/etc.; separable verb (e.g. "Ich fahre zurück").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen morgen früh nach Berlin zurückfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to drive back to Berlin tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir bitte das Buch zurückgeben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please give me back the book?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Zug ist eine Tasche zurückgeblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A bag was left behind on the train.

definitions.note: When used about people, it can be insulting/offensive (similar to calling someone “mentally retarded”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Deutsch ist im Vergleich zu den anderen etwas zurückgeblieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Compared to the others, his German is a bit behind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch zurückgebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I brought the book back.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zurückfahren“ (often with „sein“ in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind gestern Abend spät zurückgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drove back late last night.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zurückfahren“ (often with „haben“ when meaning to reverse a car).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat das Auto ein Stück zurückgefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He backed the car up a bit.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zurückgehen“ (usually used with „sein“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist nach Berlin zurückgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He went back to Berlin.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zurückgehen“ (usually used with „sein“), used for numbers/levels going down.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Zahl der Besucher ist stark zurückgegangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The number of visitors has decreased significantly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch gestern zurückgegeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I returned the book yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Chef hat einen Teil meines Gehalts zurückgehalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss withheld part of my salary.

definitions.note: Often used for going back to a place or returning to an earlier state or topic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen jetzt zurückgehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to go back now.

definitions.note: past participle of „zurückkehren“; often used with „sein“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist gestern spät nach Hause zurückgekehrt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She returned home late yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of „zurückkommen“ (used with „sein“ in the perfect tense)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin gestern spät zurückgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I came back late yesterday.

definitions.note: past participle of "zurücklassen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat seine Tasche im Zug zurückgelassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He left his bag behind on the train.

definitions.note: Often used with distances (e.g., kilometers) in the perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben heute 10 Kilometer zurückgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We covered 10 kilometers today.

definitions.note: Used for returning an object to where it was before.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch wieder zurückgelegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book back again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dich später zurückgerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I called you back later.

definitions.note: Often used for product recalls or calling someone back to a place/job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hersteller hat das Produkt zurückgerufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The manufacturer recalled the product.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Termin wurde zurückgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The appointment was postponed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Buch wieder ins Regal zurückgestellt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the book back on the shelf.

definitions.note: Often used about leaving an official position or job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Minister ist gestern zurückgetreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The minister resigned yesterday.

definitions.note: Can be used literally (physically moving backward).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin einen Schritt zurückgetreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stepped back one step.

definitions.note: past participle of „zurückzahlen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe dir das Geld schon zurückgezahlt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already paid you back the money.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive verb „sich zurückziehen“ (to withdraw, retreat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat sich nach dem Streit zurückgezogen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He withdrew after the argument.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir das Buch morgen zurückgibst?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me the book back tomorrow?

definitions.native: to get back, to have back
definitions.note: often used when you want something returned to you (money, items, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will mein Geld zurückhaben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want my money back.

definitions.note: Often used for holding someone/something back physically or emotionally, or for not revealing information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann meine Wut kaum zurückhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can hardly hold back my anger.

definitions.note: Often describes someone’s personality (not very outgoing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist am Anfang etwas zurückhaltend, aber sehr freundlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a bit reserved at first, but very friendly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Buch aus der Bibliothek zurückholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to bring the book back from the library.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "zurückkommen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zurückkam spät nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He came back home late.

definitions.note: often used for returning to a place or situation; slightly more formal than „zurückkommen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden morgen nach Berlin zurückkehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will return to Berlin tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zurückkehrt jeden Abend nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He returns home every evening.

definitions.note: Simple past (3rd person singular) of „zurückkehren“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zurückkehrte spät in der Nacht nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He returned home late at night.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of „zurückkommen“; often used in reported speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, er hoffe, dass ich bald zurückkomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says he hopes that I come back soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wann wirst du zurückkommen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When will you come back?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wann zurückkommst du nach Hause?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When are you coming back home?

definitions.note: third-person singular present tense of „zurückkommen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zurückkommt morgen nach Hause.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes back home tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for leaving something (or someone) behind when you go away.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich musste meinen Koffer am Bahnhof zurücklassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had to leave my suitcase behind at the train station.

definitions.note: Used for calling someone again (e.g., returning a phone call).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dich später zurückrufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will call you back later.

definitions.note: Often used for returning items (e.g., products) to a shop or sender.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Paket zurückschicken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to send the package back.

definitions.note: often used for physically hitting back or fighting back; can also mean to retaliate
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er will nicht zurückschlagen, obwohl er wütend ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doesn’t want to hit back, even though he’s angry.

definitions.note: often used for literally stepping back or backing away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte treten Sie einen Schritt zurück und dann zurücktreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please step back one step and then step back.

definitions.note: often used for resigning from an office or position
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Minister will zurücktreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The minister wants to resign.

definitions.note: Used for paying back money you borrowed or returning money someone paid you (e.g., a refund).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das Geld nächste Woche zurückzahlen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pay back the money next week.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., ein Angebot zurückziehen) or reflexively as „sich zurückziehen“ = to withdraw/retreat.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bank wird das Angebot zurückziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bank will withdraw the offer.

definitions.note: Also used in military/strategic contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der General ließ die Truppen zurückziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The general had the troops pulled back.

definitions.note: Reflexive: „sich zurückziehen“ = to retreat from a situation or to keep to oneself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Streit wollte sie sich zurückziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the argument, she wanted to withdraw.

definitions.native: to get back, to receive back
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, mein Geld zurückzubekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to get my money back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Buch morgen zurückzubringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to bring the book back tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, meine Tränen zurückzuhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to hold back my tears.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, mein Paket zurückzuholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to get my package back.

definitions.note: often used with „nach“ (return to a place) or „zu“ (return to a person/organization).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, bald nach Hause zurückzukehren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to return home soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, bald zurückzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to come back soon.

definitions.note: Often used about leaving a position (e.g., in politics, a job, an office).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Minister hat angekündigt, zurückzutreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The minister announced that he would step down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie bat ihn, einen Schritt zurückzutreten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She asked him to step back.

definitions.native: to trace back, to track back
definitions.note: Often used for tracing something to its origin (e.g., a source, cause, or where something came from).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei versucht, die Telefonnummer zurückzuverfolgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are trying to trace the phone number back.

definitions.note: Also used in expressions meaning “in total” (e.g. “zusammen 10 Euro”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir lernen zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We study together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wohnen zusammen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen eng zusammenarbeiten, um das Projekt rechtzeitig abzuschließen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to work closely together to finish the project on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten auch in schwierigen Zeiten zusammenbleiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should stay together even in difficult times.

definitions.note: Past participle of „zusammenarbeiten“ (often used with „haben“ in the present perfect).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben letztes Jahr an einem Projekt zusammengearbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We worked together on a project last year.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to describe someone collapsing (physically) or breaking down (emotionally).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Mann ist plötzlich zusammengebrochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man suddenly collapsed.

definitions.note: Past participle of "zusammenleben"; commonly used with "haben" (e.g., "Sie haben zusammengelebt").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben drei Jahre zusammengelebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We lived together for three years.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person who has been attacked (e.g., with "werden/sein").
