definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde auf dem Heimweg zusammengeschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was beaten up on the way home.

definitions.note: often used about people supporting each other
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In schweren Zeiten müssen wir zusammenhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In hard times we have to stick together.

definitions.note: used about things staying connected or being kept together
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Klammer muss die Papiere zusammenhalten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The clip has to hold the papers together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wollen nach dem Studium zusammenleben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to live together after college.

definitions.native: to pull yourself together, to get a grip (on yourself)
definitions.note: Usually used reflexively: „sich zusammenreißen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss mich jetzt zusammenreißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to pull myself together now.

definitions.native: to tear up, to rip apart
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht den Zettel zusammenreißen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t tear up the note.

definitions.native: to put together, combine; to pool
definitions.note: Separable verb (e.g. "Wir tun das Geld zusammen"). Often used for pooling money or resources.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen unser Geld zusammentun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to pool our money.

definitions.note: zu-infinitive form (used with modal verbs or constructions like "versuchen", "um ... zu").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir versuchen, besser zusammenzuarbeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re trying to work together better.

definitions.note: often used for watching an activity or event (watching what’s happening) rather than watching TV
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir schauen dem Spiel zu, wir wollen nur zuschauen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are watching the game; we just want to watch.

definitions.note: Often used with doors, windows, lids, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht die Tür zuschlagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t slam the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wollte zuschlagen, aber sie hielt ihn zurück.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to hit (someone), but she held him back.

definitions.note: Often used with „(jemandem) bei (etwas) zusehen“ (= watch someone doing something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich mag es, den Kindern beim Spielen zuzusehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like watching the children play.

definitions.note: Common with „zusehen, dass …“ (= make sure that …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du musst zusehen, dass du pünktlich bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to make sure you’re on time.

definitions.note: Mostly used in fixed phrases like „zustande kommen“ (to come about) or „zustande bringen“ (to bring about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag kommt zustande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract comes about.

definitions.note: Mostly used in fixed expressions like „zustande kommen“ (to come about) and „zustande bringen“ (to bring about).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Vertrag ist zustande gekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The contract came about.

definitions.note: Often used for rights, money, or things someone should receive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dir steht eine Entschädigung zu, aber er glaubt, dass sie ihm zusteht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are entitled to compensation, but he thinks it is due to him.

definitions.note: Often used with „jemandem“ (dative) and/or „etwas“: to agree with someone / to agree to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kann dir in diesem Punkt zustimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can agree with you on this point.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er nickte zustimmend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He nodded in agreement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte nicht die Tür zustoßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t slam the door shut.

definitions.note: Often used like: „Jemandem stößt etwas zu“ (something happens to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: So etwas kann jedem zustoßen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Something like that can happen to anyone.

definitions.note: often used with „für“ to say what someone is responsible for
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Frau Keller ist für die Anmeldung zuständig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ms. Keller is responsible for the registration.

definitions.note: Used for something (often unexpected or negative) that happens to someone: „jemandem zustößt“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich hoffe, dass dir nichts Schlimmes zustößt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope nothing bad happens to you.

definitions.note: attributive form of the adjective (used before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen zusätzliche Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need additional time.

definitions.note: Often used when the noun is left out (a nominalized adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Möchten Sie noch etwas Zusätzliches bestellen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like to order something extra?

definitions.note: Usually used in fixed phrases like „jdm. etw. zuteilwerden“ (= to be granted/assigned to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihm wurde große Anerkennung zuteil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was given great recognition.

definitions.note: Often used to emphasize strong feelings, convictions, or effects.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin zutiefst traurig über das, was passiert ist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am deeply sad about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr zuverlässig und hält immer sein Wort.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very reliable and always keeps his word.

definitions.note: Often used about expectations for the future (e.g., about plans, results, or developments).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin zuversichtlich, dass wir eine Lösung finden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m confident that we’ll find a solution.

definitions.note: Often written as one word when it means “too much/many.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe heute zuviel gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate too much today.

definitions.note: Used to say the amount is more than necessary; can refer to uncountable (too much) or plural countable nouns (too many).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du trinkst zuviel Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You drink too much coffee.

definitions.note: Used to say there is more than is good or needed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du trinkst zuviel Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You drink too much coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast zuviel Zucker in den Kaffee getan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put too much sugar in the coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn schon zuvor gesehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had seen him before.

definitions.note: Often used with a dative object: jemandem zuvorkommen = to anticipate someone / do something before they can.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin dir mit der Antwort zuvorgekommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I anticipated you with the answer.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s polite, helpful manner (e.g., service staff).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Mitarbeiterin war sehr zuvorkommend und hat mir sofort geholfen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employee was very courteous and helped me right away.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal/literary; in everyday speech, "manchmal" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zuweilen gehe ich nach der Arbeit noch spazieren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I go for a walk after work.

definitions.note: Most commonly used in fixed expressions like „jemandem zuwider sein“ (to be unpleasant/repugnant to someone) or „etwas zuwiderhandeln“ (to act against something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mir zuwider.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is against my wishes.

definitions.native: to pull shut, to close (by pulling)
definitions.note: often used for doors, windows, curtains, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte zuzuziehen die Tür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please pull the door shut.

definitions.native: to move to (a place), to move in
definitions.note: often used with a destination (e.g., „nach Berlin“) and with „sein“ in the past: „Er ist ... zugezogen.“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist letztes Jahr nach Hamburg zuzuziehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moved to Hamburg last year.

definitions.note: Used with another verb ("zu" + infinitive), often after verbs like "versuchen", "vergessen", "haben", etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, das Abendessen zuzubereiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to prepare dinner.

definitions.note: Infinitive with „zu“ (e.g., after another verb: „Ich versuche, … zuzubinden.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, meine Schuhe zuzubinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to tie my shoes.

definitions.note: Used as the zu-infinitive form (e.g., after certain verbs or expressions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, den Fehler zuzugeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tries to admit the mistake.

definitions.note: Used as a “zu”-infinitive (e.g., after another verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, dir zuzuhören.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to listen to you.

definitions.native: to add (something extra), to put in
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe beschlossen, noch etwas Geld zuzulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I decided to add a bit more money.

definitions.native: to save up (money), to put aside
definitions.note: Often used with money: Geld zulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, jeden Monat etwas Geld zuzulegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I try to put aside some money every month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vergiss nicht, die Tür zuzuzumachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t forget to close the door.

definitions.note: Often used in the pattern: „etwas ist jemandem (Dat.) zuzuschreiben“ = something is attributable to someone/something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Erfolg ist dem Team zuzuschreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The success is attributable to the team.

definitions.note: Infinitive with "zu" (often used after another verb, e.g. "Es ist schwer, zuzusehen.")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist schwer, zuzusehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to watch.

definitions.native: to agree (to something / to do something)
definitions.note: Infinitive form often used with a modal/auxiliary or in infinitive constructions (e.g., „Ich habe zugestimmt …“, „Er bat mich, zuzustimmen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin bereit, dem Vorschlag zuzustimmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am ready to agree to the proposal.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „zwingen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zwang mich, zu gehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He forced me to go.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of "zwingen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie zwangen ihn, die Wahrheit zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They forced him to tell the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin zwanzig Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twenty years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In dieser Stadt leben zwanzigtausend Menschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Twenty thousand people live in this city.

definitions.note: Often used in the pattern „zwar … aber …“ to mean “although …” / “it’s true that … but …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist zwar müde, aber er arbeitet weiter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is indeed tired, but he keeps working.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ist zwecklos, darüber zu streiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s pointless to argue about it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe zwei Schwestern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two sisters.

definitions.native: two and a half, two point five
definitions.note: Often used with units of measure (time, weight, distance, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich warte seit zweieinhalb Stunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been waiting for two and a half hours.

definitions.note: Used in more formal German as the genitive form of "zwei" (often meaning “of two”), especially after certain prepositions like "wegen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen zweier Fehler mussten wir noch einmal anfangen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of two mistakes, we had to start again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Erklärung ist zweifelhaft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His explanation is doubtful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist zweifellos die beste Lösung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is undoubtedly the best solution.

definitions.note: Often used with „an“ + dative (e.g., „an etwas zweifeln“ = to doubt something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Man kann an seiner Ehrlichkeit zweifeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: One can doubt his honesty.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular informal (du) present tense of „zweifeln“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du zweifelst an dir, aber du schaffst das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You doubt yourself, but you can do it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zweifelt an der Wahrheit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He doubts the truth.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present; also used in the expression „ich zweifle daran, dass …“ (= I doubt that …).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zweifle daran, dass er heute kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I doubt that he’s coming today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das kostet zweihundert Euro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That costs two hundred euros.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war schon zweimal in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already been to Berlin twice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unsere Schule ist zweisprachig, und wir haben Unterricht auf Deutsch und Englisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our school is bilingual, and we have classes in German and English.

definitions.note: Used to say someone/something is in 2nd place (e.g., in a race or ranking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist beim Rennen zweit geworden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came second in the race.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Haus wurde im Jahr zweitausend gebaut.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house was built in the year two thousand.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (usually with an article), often referring to the person or thing in second place (feminine form, e.g. „die Zweite“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist die Zweite im Rennen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is second in the race.

definitions.note: used as an ordinal number (e.g., "the second" or "second" in a sequence)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist meine zweite Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my second question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die zweite Seite.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the second page.

definitions.note: Used with feminine nouns or as a nominalized form (e.g., 'die Zweite' = the second one/woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist meine zweite Frage.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my second question.

definitions.note: ordinal number (2nd); inflected form of „zweit“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne im zweiten Stock.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live on the second floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich wohne im zweiten Stock.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live on the second floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mein zweiter Tag hier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my second day here.

definitions.note: ordinal number; masculine nominative singular form (e.g., before a masculine noun like „Zug“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zweiter Zug kommt später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Second train comes later.

definitions.note: used here with a neuter noun (e.g., „das zweite Buch“ = “the second book”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist mein zweites Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my second book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Berlin ist die zweitgrößte Stadt in Deutschland.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Berlin is the second-largest city in Germany.

definitions.note: Often used to describe people, places, or deals that seem dishonest or not trustworthy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei beobachtet eine zwielichtige Gestalt vor dem Haus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are watching a shady figure in front of the house.

definitions.note: informal singular imperative of „zwingen“ (a command to one person)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zwing ihn nicht dazu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t force him to do it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zwinge dich nicht, mitzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not forcing you to come along.

definitions.note: Often used with "zu" + infinitive (e.g., "jemanden zwingen, etwas zu tun" = to force someone to do something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Niemand kann dich zwingen, das zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: No one can force you to do that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du zwingst mich, die Wahrheit zu sagen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You force me to tell the truth.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „zwingen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zeitplan zwingt uns, uns zu beeilen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The schedule forces us to hurry.

definitions.note: past tense (simple past) of "zwinkern"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zwinkerte mir zu.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He winked at me.

definitions.note: Used with the dative for location (where?) and with the accusative for direction/movement (where to?).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Stift liegt zwischen dem Buch und dem Heft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pen is lying between the book and the notebook.

definitions.note: Used especially for birds (and sometimes jokingly for people chatting in a high voice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Vögel zwitschern schon früh am Morgen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The birds are chirping early in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin zwölf Jahre alt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twelve years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ist sehr zynisch und macht oft Witze über ernste Themen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very cynical and often makes jokes about serious topics.

definitions.note: Often describes something physically hard to break or chew; also used for people who keep going despite difficulties.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Fleisch ist ziemlich zäh.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meat is pretty tough.

definitions.note: Commonly used as the informal singular imperative of „zählen“ (e.g., telling one person to count).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zähl bis zehn!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Count to ten!

definitions.note: Informal/colloquial imperative form of „zählen“ (du-form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zähl bitte bis zehn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Count to ten, please.

definitions.note: first-person singular present of „zählen“ (ich zähle)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zähle bis zehn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I count to ten.

definitions.note: Can also mean “to matter” in phrases like „Das zählt.“ (“That counts.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bis zehn zählen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you count to ten?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du zählst bis zehn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You count to ten.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zählt das Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He counts the money.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like „Das zählt!“ or „Am Ende zählt nur …“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Am Ende zählt nur, dass du gesund bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, only that you are healthy matters.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of "zählen"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gestern zählte ich das Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I counted the money.

definitions.note: Often used for taming animals; can also be used figuratively (e.g., to tame fears or impulses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Trainer versucht, das wilde Pferd zu zähmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trainer is trying to tame the wild horse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er streichelt die Katze zärtlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He strokes the cat tenderly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde nicht zögern, dich anzurufen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won’t hesitate to call you.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum zögerst du so lange?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you hesitating for so long?

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "zögern".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zögerte einen Moment, bevor er antwortete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hesitated for a moment before he answered.

definitions.note: Often used for animals (breeding) and plants (cultivating/raising).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie züchten Hunde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They breed dogs.

definitions.note: Used for breeding/raising animals; also commonly used for cultivating plants.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er züchtet Pferde auf dem Bauernhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He breeds horses on the farm.

definitions.note: Simple past form of "zücken"; often used for quickly pulling something (like a phone, weapon, or ID) out of a pocket or bag.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zückte sein Handy und machte ein Foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pulled out his phone and took a photo.

definitions.note: Often used figuratively: to control your feelings, behavior, or spending.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss meine Wut zügeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to rein in my anger.

definitions.note: Often used to mean doing something efficiently without wasting time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen zügig losfahren, sonst kommen wir zu spät.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to leave quickly, otherwise we'll arrive too late.

definitions.note: First-person singular present of "zünden" ("I light/ignite"); also used as an imperative "light!" (informal, to one person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich zünde die Kerze an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I light the candle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir wollen die Kerzen zünden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to light the candles.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Täter wollten die Bombe zünden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The perpetrators wanted to detonate the bomb.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zündet eine Kerze an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lights a candle.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „anzünden“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zündete die Kerze an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lit the candle.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of "zünden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er zündete eine Kerze an.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lit a candle.

definitions.note: Diminutive of „Affe“; often sounds cute or affectionate.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Zoo hat das Äffchen eine Banane gegessen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the zoo, the little monkey ate a banana.

definitions.note: Male person from Egypt; the feminine form is „Ägypterin“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Nachbar ist Ägypter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Egyptian.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „oder Ähnliches“ (= or something like that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du schon mal etwas Ähnliches erlebt?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you ever experienced something similar?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zwischen den beiden Fotos gibt es eine große Ähnlichkeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a strong similarity between the two photos.

definitions.note: Nominalized adjective meaning “the older one(s)”; often used to refer to elderly/older people in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ältere brauchen oft mehr Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Older people often need more time.

definitions.note: Plural form (often used with articles like „den“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten mehr mit den Älteren sprechen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should talk more with older people.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (often with an article), e.g. „die Älteste“ = the oldest (female person) / the eldest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Älteste in der Familie wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The oldest person in the family lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: Plural form of "Älteste" (older/oldest people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sprechen mit den Ältesten des Dorfes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are talking with the elders of the village.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir brauchen eine Änderung am Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a change to the plan.

definitions.note: Plural of „Änderung“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen noch ein paar Änderungen am Plan machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We still need to make a few changes to the plan.

definitions.note: Plural of "Angst".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Kinder haben nachts Ängste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many children have fears at night.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Angst“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie spricht offen über ihre Ängsten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks openly about her fears.

definitions.note: Plural of "Apfel".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich kaufe Äpfel im Supermarkt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy apples at the supermarket.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Apfel“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Kuchen ist mit Äpfeln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is with apples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mit dem neuen Trainer begann eine erfolgreiche Ära für den Verein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the new coach, a successful era began for the club.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe Ärger mit meinem Nachbarn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having trouble with my neighbor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ärmel von meiner Jacke ist zu lang.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sleeve of my jacket is too long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind mit der Fähre über den Ärmelkanal gefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took the ferry across the English Channel.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (superlative of „arm“ = poor), usually with an article like „der/die/das Ärmste“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ärmste hat kein Geld.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poorest one has no money.

definitions.note: Plural of the vulgar/slang noun “Arsch”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hör auf, euch wie Ärsche zu benehmen – da drüben sind Kinder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop behaving like asses—there are children over there.

definitions.note: plural of „Arzt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärzte arbeiten im Krankenhaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors work in the hospital.

definitions.note: dative plural of „Arzt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich vertraue den Ärzten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I trust the doctors.

definitions.note: Female form of Arzt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärztin untersucht mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (female) doctor examines me.

definitions.note: plural of „Ärztin“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Ärztinnen arbeiten heute im Krankenhaus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The female doctors are working at the hospital today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er achtet auf sein Äußeres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pays attention to his appearance.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „die Öffentlichkeit“ (“the public”) or „in der Öffentlichkeit“ (“in public”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Öffentlichkeit hat ein Recht auf Informationen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The public has a right to information.

definitions.note: as a noun, it refers to the act/process of opening something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Öffnen der Tür war schwierig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Opening the door was difficult.

definitions.note: Can mean an opening (a gap/hole) or the act/event of opening (e.g., a store opening).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Öffnung ist zu klein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The opening is too small.

definitions.note: Usually uncountable; can also mean cooking oil or motor oil depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche Öl zum Kochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need oil for cooking.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a car engine oil filter.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss den Ölfilter wechseln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change the oil filter.

definitions.note: Often used for engine oil in a car.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Ölstand ist zu niedrig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The oil level is too low.

definitions.note: usually refers to changing the engine oil in a vehicle
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss morgen einen Ölwechsel machen lassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get an oil change tomorrow.

definitions.note: Male form; the female form is "Österreicherin".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Nachbar ist Österreicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Austrian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er kämpft gegen das Übel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fights against evil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Übel ist, dass wir zu spät sind.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The problem is that we are too late.

definitions.note: Nominalized verb (used like a noun), often with an article: „das Üben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durch das Üben werde ich besser.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By practicing, I get better.

definitions.note: Often used for changes to a text, plan, or draft.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bericht braucht noch eine Überarbeitung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report still needs a revision.

definitions.note: Refers to being overworked (too much work), often in the sense of exhaustion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wegen Überarbeitung war sie völlig erschöpft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of overwork, she was completely exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche einen Überblick über die wichtigsten Punkte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need an overview of the most important points.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural: Überbrückungskabel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hast du Überbrückungskabel im Auto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have jumper cables in the car?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wurde wegen einer Überdosis ins Krankenhaus gebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was taken to the hospital because of an overdose.

definitions.note: Often used for agreement between people (e.g., in opinion) or a match between things (e.g., results and expectations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zwischen uns herrscht Übereinstimmung über den Plan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is agreement between us about the plan.

definitions.note: Often used for a sudden attack or a robbery (e.g., a mugging).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem Überfall rief sie sofort die Polizei.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the attack/robbery, she called the police right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es gibt hier einen Überfluss an Lebensmitteln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is an abundance of food here.

definitions.note: Often used for officially giving something to someone (e.g., keys, documents, a position).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Übergabe der Schlüssel findet morgen statt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The handover of the keys will take place tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Arzt sagt, dass ich Übergewicht habe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor says that I am overweight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sein Überleben hing von der schnellen Hilfe ab.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His survival depended on quick help.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning “survivor(s)” (the exact meaning depends on context, e.g., singular or plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Überlebenden wurden schnell in Sicherheit gebracht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The survivors were quickly brought to safety.

definitions.note: This form is often used in the dative plural (e.g. after "mit", "zu", "helfen").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir halfen den Überlebenden nach dem Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We helped the survivors after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach kurzer Überlegung habe ich mich dafür entschieden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a short consideration, I decided to do it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Überprüfung der Daten hat einen Fehler gefunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The check of the data found an error.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Party war eine große Überraschung für ihn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party was a big surprise for him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Auf der Party gab es viele Überraschungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many surprises at the party.

definitions.note: Plural of "Überschrift".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Überschriften in der Zeitung sind heute sehr groß.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The headlines in the newspaper are very big today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem starken Regen gab es eine Überschwemmung in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the heavy rain, there was a flood in the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach den starken Regenfällen gab es Überschwemmungen in vielen Städten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the heavy rainfall, there were floods in many cities.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like „aus Übersee“ (from overseas) or „nach Übersee“ (to overseas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Waren kommen aus Übersee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many goods come from overseas.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (nominalized verb).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Übersetzen braucht Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Translating takes time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Übersetzer arbeitet an einem neuen Buch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The translator is working on a new book.

definitions.note: Refers specifically to a woman; the gender-neutral/plural forms are different.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Übersetzerin übersetzt den Text ins Englische.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (female) translator translates the text into English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du mir die englische Übersetzung geben?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you give me the English translation?

definitions.note: plural of „Übersetzung“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Übersetzungen schon fertig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already have the translations finished.

definitions.note: Plural form; used for extra hours worked beyond regular working time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss diese Woche viele Überstunden machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to work a lot of overtime this week.

definitions.note: Often used for official or systematic watching/monitoring (e.g., by police, cameras, or authorities).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Überwachung der Straße erfolgt durch Kameras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The surveillance of the street is done by cameras.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Überwachungskamera hängt über der Eingangstür.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The surveillance camera is hanging above the front door.

definitions.note: Often used for a strongly held belief or firm opinion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aus Überzeugung esse ich kein Fleisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Out of conviction, I don't eat meat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihre Überzeugungen sind ihr sehr wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her beliefs are very important to her.

definitions.note: Often used as "das Übliche" (meaning "the usual").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie immer nehme ich das Übliche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As always, I’ll have the usual.

definitions.note: Often used as a nominalized adjective: „das Übliche“ = “the usual (thing)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen heute das Übliche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re doing the usual thing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen eine Übung für die Prüfung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re doing an exercise for the exam.

definitions.note: Plural of „Übung“; often used for practice tasks (e.g., in class or a workbook) or training exercises.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir machen heute Übungen zur Grammatik.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re doing grammar exercises today.

definitions.note: A hesitation sound used when you’re thinking or searching for words in speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Äh, wie heißt du nochmal?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Um, what’s your name again?

definitions.note: Filler sound used when hesitating or thinking what to say.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ähm, ich weiß nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Um, I don't know.

definitions.note: Used as a filler sound when hesitating or thinking.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ähm, ich glaube, ich habe meinen Schlüssel verloren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Um, I think I lost my key.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative: jemandem ähneln = to resemble someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er wird seinem Vater immer mehr ähneln.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He will resemble his father more and more.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du ähnelst deiner Mutter sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You resemble your mother a lot.

definitions.note: Used with dative (jemandem/etwas ähneln).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ähnelt seinem Vater sehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He resembles his father a lot.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „ähneln“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Gebäude ähnelte einem Schloss.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building resembled a castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die beiden Bilder sind sich sehr ähnlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two pictures are very similar.

definitions.note: Often used with "wie" (e.g., "ähnlich wie" = "similar to").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir denken ähnlich über das Problem.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We think similarly about the problem.

definitions.note: adjective form used with a noun (attributive); often after an article or determiner
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe eine ähnliche Jacke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a similar jacket.

definitions.note: adjective form used with masculine/neuter singular (weak or mixed declension) or with plural (strong declension), depending on the article/case
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich suche einen ähnlichen Mantel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a similar coat.

definitions.note: comparative form of ähnlich
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Kleid ist ähnlicher als das andere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dress is more similar than the other one.

definitions.note: comparative form of „alt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Bruder ist älter als ich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is older than me.

definitions.note: Comparative form used before a noun (attributive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich helfe meiner älteren Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I help my older sister.

definitions.note: comparative form (inflected) of „alt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich spreche oft mit älteren Leuten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often talk with older people.

definitions.note: superlative form of „alt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist meine älteste Schwester.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my oldest sister.

definitions.note: superlative form of „alt“ (old)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das sind die ältesten Häuser in der Stadt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those are the oldest houses in the city.

definitions.note: superlative form of „alt“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein ältester Bruder wohnt in Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My oldest brother lives in Berlin.

definitions.note: first-person singular present ("I change") or imperative ("change!") depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ändere das Passwort jetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m changing the password now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich möchte das Passwort ändern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like to change the password.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „ändern“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum änderst du deine Meinung so oft?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you change your mind so often?

definitions.note: third-person singular present (er/sie/es) of „ändern“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er ändert seine Meinung oft.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He often changes his mind.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of „ändern“ (ich/er/sie/es änderte).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er änderte seine Meinung nach dem Gespräch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He changed his mind after the conversation.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural ("they" or "you all")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie änderten den Plan in letzter Minute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They changed the plan at the last minute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Kind ist nachts oft ängstlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child is often anxious at night.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively with „mich“ (e.g., „ich ärgere mich“ = I’m annoyed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich ärgere mich über den Lärm.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed about the noise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist wirklich ärgerlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s really annoying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es wird ihn immer ärgern, wenn der Bus zu spät kommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It will always annoy him when the bus comes too late.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular present tense of "ärgern" (you annoy/irritate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du ärgerst mich mit deinen ständigen Unterbrechungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You annoy me with your constant interruptions.

definitions.note: 3rd person singular present of „ärgern“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Lärm ärgert mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise annoys me.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „ärgern“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das laute Handy ärgerte mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loud phone annoyed me.

definitions.note: Often used with nouns to mean “medical/doctor’s,” e.g., ärztliche Untersuchung (medical exam), ärztliche Hilfe (medical help).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche ärztliche Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need medical help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Säure ist ätzend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The acid is corrosive.

definitions.note: Informal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Wetter ist heute echt ätzend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather is really awful today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die äußere Tür ist verschlossen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The outer door is locked.

definitions.note: Often used with an object like „eine Meinung“ (an opinion), or reflexive as „sich äußern“ = to express oneself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie wird ihre Meinung klar äußern.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will clearly express her opinion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist äußerst wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is extremely important.

definitions.note: Often used as a superlative with a definite article (e.g., „die äußerste …“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist die äußerste Ecke des Zimmers.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is the outermost corner of the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Film war total öde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was totally boring.

definitions.note: Often used for empty, bleak places or landscapes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Landschaft hier ist im Winter oft öde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The landscape here is often desolate in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine öffentliche Veranstaltung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a public event.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister hat sich öffentlich entschuldigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor apologized publicly.

definitions.note: Adjective inflected form; used with feminine singular nouns or in some plural forms depending on case.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine öffentliche Veranstaltung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a public event.

definitions.note: Inflected form of „öffentlich“, used before a noun (e.g. after „den/die/das“). Not the same as English “official”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich benutze oft den öffentlichen Verkehr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I often use public transportation.

definitions.note: Neuter nominative/accusative singular form of „öffentlich“ (often used before a neuter noun like „Gebäude“, „Verkehr“, „Interesse“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist ein öffentliches Gebäude.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is a public building.

definitions.note: often used as an imperative (command) or as the 1st-person singular present tense form (“I open”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Öffne bitte das Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please open the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte das Fenster öffnen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please open the window?

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Öffnest du bitte das Fenster?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you open the window, please?

definitions.note: third-person singular present of "öffnen" ("to open")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er öffnet das Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He opens the window.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „öffnen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er öffnete das Fenster.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He opened the window.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „öffnen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie öffneten die Tür um acht Uhr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They opened the door at eight o’clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit dem Umzug sehen wir uns öfter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since the move, we see each other more often.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich gehe jetzt öfter ins Fitnessstudio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the gym more often now.

definitions.note: comparative form of „oft“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seit ich in Berlin wohne, fahre ich öfters mit der U-Bahn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since I’ve lived in Berlin, I take the subway more often.

definitions.note: adjective in the weak declension (e.g., after a definite article)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir haben mit der örtlichen Polizei gesprochen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We spoke with the local police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Dorf liegt östlich von Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The village is east of Berlin.

definitions.note: First-person singular present subjunctive (Konjunktiv I) of „üben“, often used in reported speech or set phrases like „ich übe, dass …“ is rare; more common is „ich übe“ (indicative) meaning “I practice.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er sagt, ich übe jeden Tag Klavier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He says I practice the piano every day.

definitions.note: Often used for illness (feeling sick), smells, or behavior; can also mean "evil" in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist übel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel sick.

definitions.note: Often used informally to intensify something negative (similar to “really/seriously” in phrases like “übel aussehen”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mir ist übel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel sick.

definitions.note: Used for practicing a skill or rehearsing something (e.g., language, music, sports, a talk).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich üben jeden Tag Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I practice German every day.

definitions.note: As a preposition: with dative for location (where something is), with accusative for motion (where something goes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lampe hängt über dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp hangs over the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sprechen über das Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are talking about the weather.

definitions.note: Often used with the dative when describing location (e.g., above something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Lampe hängt über dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp hangs above the table.

definitions.note: Often used with the accusative when describing movement (e.g., across something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir gehen über die Straße.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re walking across the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe überall gesucht, aber ich finde meine Schlüssel nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked everywhere, but I can’t find my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Im Urlaub sind wir mit dem Bus überallhin gefahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On vacation we went everywhere by bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe den Text überarbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I revised the text.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective to mean exhausted from working too much.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der stressigen Woche bin ich total überarbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the stressful week, I’m totally overworked.

definitions.note: often used for texts, documents, plans, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die überarbeitete Version ist viel verständlicher.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The revised version is much easier to understand.

definitions.note: used to describe a person who has worked too much
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach der stressigen Woche bin ich völlig überarbeitet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the stressful week, I’m completely overworked.

definitions.note: Rather formal/emphatic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist überaus wichtig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is extremely important.

definitions.native: to have an overview (of), to take in, to grasp
definitions.note: Often used for understanding something as a whole or seeing it all at once (literally or figuratively).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Von hier aus kann man die ganze Stadt überblicken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From here you can take in the whole city.

definitions.note: simple past form of „überbringen“ (used for bringing/delivering a message, news, greetings, etc.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überbrachte ihr die Nachricht persönlich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He delivered the news to her in person.

definitions.note: Often used for bringing news, greetings, or a message (can sound a bit formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich soll dir herzliche Grüße von Anna überbringen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m supposed to pass on warm greetings to you from Anna.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss das noch einmal überdenken.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to rethink that one more time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überdenkt seine Entscheidung noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He rethinks his decision once more.

definitions.note: Often used with „etwas + Genitiv“ (e.g. „des Wartens“), and in modern speech also with „von + Dativ“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin des Wartens überdrüssig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m tired of waiting.

definitions.note: Commonly used with verbs like „stimmen“ or „sein“: „übereinstimmen/überein sein“ = to agree/match.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sind uns in diesem Punkt überein.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We agree on this point.

definitions.native: on top of each other, over each other
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Bücher liegen übereinander auf dem Tisch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The books are lying on top of each other on the table.

definitions.note: Often used for accidents (e.g., a car runs over a person/animal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ein Auto hat den Hund überfahren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A car ran over the dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir überfahren die Brücke.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We drive over the bridge.

definitions.note: Often used for a sudden attack with the intent to rob someone (e.g., in the street).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Zwei Männer wollten ihn nachts auf dem Heimweg überfallen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Two men wanted to mug him at night on his way home.

definitions.note: Can be used when you approach someone suddenly or interrupt them unexpectedly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich nicht überfallen, aber hast du kurz Zeit?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to catch you off guard, but do you have a moment?

definitions.note: simple past of „überfliegen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das Flugzeug überflog die Stadt in großer Höhe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The airplane flew over the city at a great altitude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Bemerkung war völlig überflüssig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That remark was completely unnecessary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Zug ist heute Morgen überfüllt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is overcrowded this morning.

definitions.note: Used before a noun (adjective ending -en), e.g. after 'den', 'die', 'mit', etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir saßen in einem überfüllten Bus.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were sitting on a packed bus.

definitions.note: Simple past form of "übergeben".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er übergab ihr den Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He handed her the key.

definitions.native: hand over, pass on, give (to someone)
definitions.note: Often used for giving something to another person; can also be used in formal contexts (e.g., handing over documents, responsibility).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich übergebe dir jetzt die Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m handing you the keys now.

definitions.note: often used for giving something to someone officially or formally (e.g., documents, keys, responsibility)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss dir die Schlüssel übergeben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to hand you the keys.

definitions.native: to ignore, to overlook; to pass over (someone)
definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (jemanden übergehen = to ignore someone / pass someone over, e.g. for a promotion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Warum willst du mich immer übergehen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you always want to ignore me / pass me over?

definitions.note: In this sense it can mean going across something (e.g. a street).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sollten die Straße nur an der Ampel übergehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We should cross the street only at the traffic light.

definitions.note: colloquial; often used in a joking or mildly critical way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du bist doch völlig übergeschnappt!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re completely crazy!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mein Onkel ist übergewichtig, aber er versucht, mehr Sport zu machen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is overweight, but he’s trying to do more exercise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er übergibt mir den Schlüssel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hands me the key.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie war überglücklich, als sie die Nachricht hörte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was overjoyed when she heard the news.

definitions.note: Often used in negatives and questions to emphasize “any/ever.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe überhaupt keine Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have no time at all.

definitions.note: Often used in traffic (passing another vehicle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der LKW wird das Auto auf der Autobahn überholen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck will overtake (pass) the car on the highway.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überholt ein langsames Auto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He passes a slow car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat mich überholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She passed me.

definitions.note: Often used to describe ideas, methods, or technology that are no longer up to date.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Software ist überholt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This software is outdated.

definitions.note: Often used for passing another vehicle (e.g., on the road).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich überholte den LKW auf der Autobahn.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I passed the truck on the highway.

definitions.note: Used when improving or modernizing something (a system, a plan, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma überholte das alte System.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company overhauled the old system.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative of „überlassen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Überlass das mir!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave that to me!

definitions.note: often used with a person in the dative (e.g. dir/ihm/ihr) to mean leaving a task or decision to someone
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich überlasse dir die Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll leave the decision to you.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase „jemandem etwas überlassen“ (to leave something to someone / leave it up to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Entscheidung ist dir überlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The decision is up to you.

definitions.note: Often used with a person in the dative: jemandem etwas überlassen = to leave/hand something over to someone. Can also mean to leave something to someone’s discretion (e.g., Das überlasse ich dir.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir meinen Platz überlassen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll give you my seat.

definitions.note: Used with ihr: “you (plural) leave/entrust … (to someone)”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ihr überlasst mir die Entscheidung.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You (all) leave the decision to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manche Menschen überleben schwere Unfälle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some people survive serious accidents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wenn du vorsichtig bist, überlebst du das.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re careful, you’ll survive that.

definitions.note: Can be present tense (3rd person singular) or past participle, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überlebt den Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He survives the accident.

definitions.note: Past participle form, often used with "hat" (has).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat den Unfall überlebt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has survived the accident.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „überleben“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überlebte den Unfall.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He survived the accident.

definitions.note: Informal imperative (du-form) of „überlegen“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Überleg dir das gut, bevor du entscheidest.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Think about that carefully before you decide.

definitions.note: often used with „dir“ (überleg dir …) for “think about it / consider …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich überlege, ob ich heute Abend ausgehe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm thinking about whether I'm going out tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Überlege bitte gut, bevor du etwas sagst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please think carefully before you say something.

definitions.note: Often used with dative: jemandem überlegen = superior to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie ist ihm im Schach überlegen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is superior to him at chess.

definitions.note: Often used when you need time to decide what to do (e.g., „Ich muss überlegen.“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss noch überlegen, ob ich mitkomme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I still have to think about whether I’m coming along.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du überlegst noch, ob du mitkommen willst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You're still thinking about whether you want to come along.

definitions.note: Often used with „nach“ (to think about) or „es sich überlegen“ (to think something over).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überlegt noch, ob er mitkommt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s still thinking about whether he’s coming along.

definitions.note: Past participle form (used e.g. with „haben“ in the perfect tense).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe mir das gut überlegt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought it over carefully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich überlegte lange, bevor ich antwortete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I thought about it for a long time before I answered.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), plural (e.g., wir/sie)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir überlegten lange, ob wir umziehen sollten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We considered for a long time whether we should move.

definitions.note: Simple past of „überlassen“; often used with a dative person and an accusative thing (e.g. „jemandem etwas überlassen“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überließ mir seinen Platz im Zug.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me his seat on the train.

definitions.native: to outsmart, to outwit, to trick
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er versucht, mich zu überlisten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s trying to outsmart me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat mich überlistet und die Schlüssel genommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He outwitted me and took the keys.

definitions.note: Often used for sending information/data or officially forwarding documents/messages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bitte übermitteln Sie mir die Details per E-Mail.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please send me the details by email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Daten wurden übermittelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The data was transmitted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Übermorgen fahren wir nach Berlin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The day after tomorrow we’re going to Berlin.

definitions.note: Often used for children or animals when they’re very lively and a bit uncontrolled; can also imply being a little reckless.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Kinder waren nach dem Geburtstag ganz übermütig.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were completely overexcited after the birthday party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich übernachte heute bei meiner Freundin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m staying overnight at my friend’s place today.

definitions.native: to stay overnight, to spend the night
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir übernachten heute in einem kleinen Hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re staying overnight in a small hotel today.

definitions.note: Past participle of „übernachten“; often used with „haben“ (e.g., „hat übernachtet“).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat im Hotel übernachtet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stayed overnight at the hotel.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), used with “wir/ihr/Sie” or “sie” (they)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie übernachteten in einem kleinen Hotel am Bahnhof.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They spent the night in a small hotel by the train station.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) of "übernehmen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie übernahm die Leitung des Teams.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took over the leadership of the team.

definitions.note: adjective; here in the declined form (e.g., before a noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie glaubt an übernatürliche Kräfte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She believes in supernatural powers.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present ("ich übernehme").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich übernehme morgen die Schicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking over the shift tomorrow.

definitions.note: Common for taking over a job/task/role, a company, or responsibility from someone else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde morgen die Schicht übernehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take over the shift tomorrow.

definitions.native: to assume (responsibility); to take responsibility for
definitions.note: Used with responsibility, costs, guarantees, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde die Verantwortung übernehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will assume responsibility.

definitions.note: Used for adopting a term, method, habit, or approach.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viele Firmen übernehmen neue Begriffe aus dem Englischen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many companies adopt new terms from English.

definitions.note: Used especially with costs/expenses in formal contexts (e.g., insurance, employer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Versicherung wird die Kosten übernehmen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The insurance will cover the costs.

definitions.note: Informal (du) imperative form: a command/request to one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Übernimm bitte die Leitung für heute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take over the leadership for today.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (du) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du übernimmst die Verantwortung für das Projekt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You take on responsibility for the project.

definitions.note: Often used with tasks, roles, or responsibility (e.g., a job, a shift, costs).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie übernimmt morgen die Schicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She takes over the shift tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Firma hat den Konkurrenten übernommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company took over the competitor.

definitions.note: Often used for adopting an idea, method, or custom from someone else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Methode von meiner Kollegin übernommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I adopted the method from my colleague.

definitions.native: the week after next, the next but one
definitions.note: Used mainly when talking about dates/time (e.g., days or weeks) further away than “nächsten”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns übernächsten Montag.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet the Monday after next.

definitions.note: 1st person singular present (or imperative) of „überprüfen“, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich überprüfe die Adresse noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll check the address one more time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du bitte die Rechnung überprüfen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you please check the bill?

definitions.note: present tense (3rd person singular) of „überprüfen“; often used for verifying or reviewing something
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überprüft die Daten noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He checks the data again.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „überprüfen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich überprüfte die E-Mail-Adresse noch einmal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the email address one more time.

definitions.note: 1st-person singular present ("I cross").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich überquere die Straße bei Grün.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cross the street when the light is green.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a street, a river).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir müssen die Straße überqueren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to cross the street.

definitions.note: second-person singular (du) form of „überqueren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du überquerst die Straße an der Ampel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You cross the street at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Present tense form (er/sie/es überquert).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überquert die Straße bei Grün.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He crosses the street when the light is green.

definitions.note: Past participle, used with "haben" (hat überquert).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie hat die Brücke überquert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She crossed the bridge.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „überqueren“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überquerte die Straße bei Grün.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He crossed the street when the light was green.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum), 3rd person plural (they)
