definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie überquerten die Straße bei Grün.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They crossed the street when the light was green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich will dich morgen überraschen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to surprise you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht war überraschend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news was surprising.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Überraschend hatte er heute schon Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Surprisingly, he already had time today.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective/participle meaning someone feels surprised.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin überrascht, dass du schon hier bist.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m surprised that you’re already here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin überrascht über die Nachricht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m surprised about the news.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) form of „überraschen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Nachricht überraschte mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news surprised me.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum); used with wir/sie/Sie
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie überraschten mich mit einem Geschenk.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You surprised me with a gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich glaube, ich habe gestern überreagiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think I overreacted yesterday.

definitions.note: From the verb „überreden“; this form is also the imperative (informal singular) and the 1st/3rd person singular present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Überrede ihn nicht, das zu tun.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't persuade him to do that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde ihn überreden, mitzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will persuade him to come along.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe ihn überredet, mitzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I persuaded him to come along.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie überredete ihn, mitzukommen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She talked him into coming along.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., presenting an award, a document, or a gift).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bürgermeister wird der Gewinnerin die Urkunde überreichen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mayor will present the certificate to the winner.

definitions.note: simple past (Präteritum) of „überreichen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Direktor überreichte der Gewinnerin den Preis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The principal presented the prize to the winner.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ to describe how someone feels after an unexpected situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich war von der Frage völlig überrumpelt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was completely caught off guard by the question.

definitions.note: contraction of "über das" or "über(s)" + accusative
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir sprechen übers Wetter.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We're talking about the weather.

definitions.note: Often used for crossing a boundary/limit (literal or figurative), e.g. a border, a line, a speed limit, or a time limit.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du darfst die Geschwindigkeitsbegrenzung nicht überschreiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must not exceed the speed limit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du hast das Tempolimit überschritten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You exceeded the speed limit.

definitions.note: often used for crossing a border or a line (literal or figurative)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Grenze wurde überschritten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The border was crossed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nach dem starken Regen ist die Straße überschwemmt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the heavy rain, the street is flooded.

definitions.note: Often used for very enthusiastic praise or emotional reactions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie lobte ihn überschwenglich für seine Hilfe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She praised him effusively for his help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überschätzt seine Fähigkeiten.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He overestimates his abilities.

definitions.note: past participle; often used in the passive or perfect tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Gefahr wird oft überschätzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The danger is often overestimated.

definitions.note: Often means you didn’t notice something; it can look like English “oversee,” but the usual meaning is different.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe deinen Anruf übersehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I missed your call.

definitions.note: Most often: 1st person singular present ("I translate").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich übersetze den Text ins Englische.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I translate the text into English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Kannst du diesen Satz ins Englische übersetzen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you translate this sentence into English?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie übersetzt den Brief ins Englische.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She translates the letter into English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Text ist schon übersetzt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The text is already translated.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) form of „übersetzen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er übersetzte den Text ins Englische.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He translated the text into English.

definitions.note: past participle of „überspringen“; often used with „haben“ in the Perfekt
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Kapitel übersprungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I skipped the chapter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe die Operation gut überstanden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got through the operation well.

definitions.note: Often used for difficult situations (e.g., illness, crises, hard times).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir werden diese Krise überstehen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will get through this crisis.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Preis übersteigt mein Budget.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price exceeds my budget.

definitions.note: Often used for transferring data, money, rights, or responsibilities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich muss die Datei auf meinen Computer übertragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to transfer the file to my computer.

definitions.note: Often used in a figurative sense (e.g., applying an idea or meaning to another situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Diese Regel lässt sich nicht auf alle Fälle übertragen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This rule can't be applied to all cases.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense ("I exaggerate"). Often used as an imperative: "Don’t exaggerate!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich übertreibe nicht, das ist wirklich passiert.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not exaggerating; that really happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du solltest nicht übertreiben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn’t exaggerate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du übertreibst total, so schlimm ist es nicht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re totally exaggerating; it’s not that bad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er übertreibt immer, wenn er Geschichten erzählt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always exaggerates when he tells stories.

definitions.note: Simple past (Präteritum) form of „übertreiben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich übertrieb ein bisschen, als ich die Geschichte erzählte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exaggerated a bit when I told the story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist übertrieben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s exaggerated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dieses Ergebnis übertrifft unsere Erwartungen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This result surpasses our expectations.

definitions.note: past participle of "übertreffen"; often used with "haben" (e.g., "hat übertroffen")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat alle Erwartungen übertroffen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He surpassed all expectations.

definitions.note: Often used for watching something/someone to make sure rules are followed or to ensure safety/security.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Polizei wird den Verkehr auf der Autobahn überwachen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police will monitor the traffic on the highway.

definitions.note: Past participle of „überwachen“; often used with „werden/sein“ in passive or perfect forms.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Bereich wird rund um die Uhr überwacht.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The area is monitored around the clock.

definitions.note: Most commonly used for transferring money via a bank.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich werde dir das Geld morgen überweisen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will transfer the money to you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In diesem Kurs sprechen wir überwiegend Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this course we speak mostly German.

definitions.note: Often used for a bank transfer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe das Geld überwiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I transferred the money.

definitions.note: Often used when a doctor sends a patient to a specialist.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Der Hausarzt hat mich zum Spezialisten überwiesen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family doctor referred me to the specialist.

definitions.note: Often used for overcoming a difficulty, obstacle, or fear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sie muss ihre Angst überwinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has to overcome her fear.

definitions.note: Commonly used for getting over a problem, setback, or disappointment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er konnte die Niederlage nicht überwinden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He couldn't get over the defeat.

definitions.note: past participle of „überwinden“; often used with „haben“ in the perfect tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich habe meine Angst überwunden.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have overcome my fear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die vielen Aufgaben überwältigen mich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The many tasks overwhelm me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Die Aussicht vom Berggipfel war überwältigend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The view from the mountain peak was overwhelming.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin von der vielen Arbeit völlig überwältigt.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m completely overwhelmed by all the work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich versuche, meinen Freund zu überzeugen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m trying to convince my friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seine Argumente sind sehr überzeugend.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His arguments are very convincing.

definitions.note: Often used with „sein“ (e.g. „Ich bin überzeugt, dass …“ = “I’m convinced that …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin überzeugt, dass es heute regnen wird.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m convinced that it will rain today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich bin überzeugt, dass du das schaffst.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m convinced that you can do it.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite) of „überzeugen“
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er überzeugte mich, es noch einmal zu versuchen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He convinced me to try again.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun (attributive) or in set phrases like „üble Laune“ (bad mood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er hat heute eine üble Laune.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s in a bad mood today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Das ist eine üble Idee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That’s a terrible idea.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine noun in the accusative (e.g. "einen üblen ...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In der Küche gibt es einen üblen Geruch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a nasty smell in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: In Deutschland ist es üblich, Trinkgeld zu geben.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Germany, it’s customary to give a tip.

definitions.note: Adjective form used before a noun (e.g., with a feminine noun, plural, or after certain determiners).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns zur üblichen Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We meet at the usual time.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like „im üblichen Rahmen“ (within the usual limits).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wir treffen uns zur üblichen Zeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re meeting at the usual time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Üblicherweise fahre ich mit dem Bus zur Arbeit.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually take the bus to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ist noch Kuchen übrig?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Is there any cake left over?

definitions.note: Used to introduce an additional comment or side note.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Übrigens, ich komme morgen etwas später.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By the way, I’ll be a little later tomorrow.

definitions.note: 2nd person singular (du) present tense of „üben“.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Du übst jeden Tag Deutsch.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You practice German every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er übt jeden Tag Klavier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He practices the piano every day.

definitions.note: simple past (ich/er/sie/es); can also be subjunctive II (würde-Form alternative) in some contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Er übte jeden Tag Klavier.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He practiced the piano every day.

definitions.note: colloquial short form of “eine” (feminine nominative/accusative), often used in spoken German
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche ’ne Minute.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a minute.

definitions.note: colloquial spoken contraction of „einen“ (accusative masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ich brauche ’nen Kaffee.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a coffee.

definitions.note: colloquial contraction of „es“ (often in spoken German, e.g. „Wie geht’s?“)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Wie geht’s dir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you?
